title: Ajax 1v1 with Neutrals
instructions_setup: This drill is a 1v1 possession and dribbling challenge, incorporating 4   neutral bounce players positioned around the outside of a square grid. While only two central players compete directly in a 1v1 duel, the player   in possession effectively has support from four bounce players, turning it   into a 5v1 situation when using the bounce options. Bounce players are restricted to one-touch passes only, and can only be   used to retain or redirect possession—not to bypass the opponent entirely.   The focus remains on maintaining control, drawing out the defender, and   creating space to attack. The goal for either player is to dribble through one of their opponent’s   two gates (4 total gates—2 per player—positioned directly opposite each other   on the grid) to score a point.
coaching_notes: • Awareness & Angle Use: Players should constantly scan to recognize   when and where to use bounce players to escape pressure.     • 1v1 Decision-Making: Encourage creativity and deception—players should   combine with bounce passes to manipulate the defender before bursting toward   a gate.     • Bounce Player Role: Stress sharp, clean one-touch passing. They should   offer angled support, not just act as static walls.
progression_one: Add Touch Limit for Central Players:     Limit the central player in possession to 3 touches (or even 2) before they   must attempt to either use a bounce pass or attack a gate.     Focus: Increases tempo, improves ball control under pressure, and forces   quicker decisions.

title: Ajax 2 Phase Counter Attack
instructions_setup: This drill simulates counter-attacking play, focusing on quick transitions   and defensive recovery. The drill includes two phases, where the direction of   attack changes after the first phase. Set up a grid with two goals positioned opposite each other. Place one   coach or deeper player at either end of the grid to be used as a bounce pass.   Position two attackers and two defenders. The attackers and defenders begin   in the same positions. Attackers are working to score, while defenders focus   on defending and recovering. Phase 1 begins with a pass into a coach or deeper attacker. The coach or   attacker returns the pass, and the player delivers a cross into the box. The   two attackers break into the box, aiming to score from the cross. The two   defenders attempt to clear the cross and defend the box while recovering back   to their starting positions. Phase 2 starts when phase 1 is completed. Players reset and turn around. A   second ball is played into the grid, and the team now attack in the opposite   direction.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Attackers should burst into space immediately after   receiving the return pass, creating a fast counter-attacking move.     • Defensive Recovery: Defenders must quickly recover after clearing the   cross, ensuring they track back to defend the second goal.     • Communication: Attackers should communicate when making runs, and defenders   must communicate on who to track and when to clear the ball.     • Awareness of Changing Directions: Players should quickly adjust to the   new attacking direction after completing phase 1. The game requires a quick   mental shift and physical transition to the opposite goal.
progression_one: Add Extra Defender: Introduce an additional defender in phase 1, increasing the difficulty for   the attacking team. This forces attackers to work harder to create space and   finish under pressure. Focus: Enhances attacking and decision-making under defensive pressure,   improving both individual and team attack strategies.

title: Ajax 2v2 & Bouncers
instructions_setup: This drill is a 2v2 in the central zone, with 2 bounce players positioned   on either side of the grid (1 on each side). The players in possession can   use the bounce player who is positioned ahead of them on the line, creating a   3v2 advantage when in possession. The grid is marked with a dotted line across the middle, which restricts   teams from scoring in their own half. This encourages effective link-up play   and rewards teams out of possession for high pressing. To score, there are 4 mini-goals, 2 located at either end of the grid. The   bounce players will be positioned on the line between the mini-goals,   ensuring they can contribute to the play without being static.
coaching_notes: • Use of Bounce Players: The bounce players should be utilized   strategically to create overloads, allowing the team in possession to break   through defensive lines with quick passes.     • High Pressing: Encourage the defending team to press high up the pitch,   as they cannot score from their own half. This creates a reward system for   pressing and forces turnovers.     • Link-Up Play: Players in possession need to focus on quick, precise   passing to the bounce players and the teammates to create attacking   opportunities.     • Spacing and Movement: The attacking players should focus on maintaining   good width and depth in their movements to support both the ball carrier and   the bounce players effectively.
progression_one: Limit Bounce Player Touches: Restrict the bounce players to 1 or 2 touches, forcing the team in   possession to think quicker and maintain fluidity in their attacking   play. Focus: Increases tempo, helps develop quicker decision-making, and   encourages sharper passes between players.
progression_two: Defender Zone: Introduce a defender or neutral player who can enter the central zone to   disrupt the play or intercept passes, making it a more dynamic 2v3   scenario. Focus: Forces the attacking team to adjust their tactics and be more   creative with their passes, improving their ability to break down defenses   under pressure.

title: Ajax 3 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This is an unopposed finishing practice designed to develop combination play and movement across attacking positions. Players are divided into three stations: left wing, centre forward, and right wing.The drill begins with a finish from the centre forward, who receives a pass and shoots on goal. Immediately after shooting, the centre forward runs to the left wing station for phase two, where they combine with the left winger in a 1-2 passing sequence that ends with the left winger finishing on goal.In phase three, the centre forward then makes a long recovery run across to the right wing. There, they complete another 1-2 combination—this time with the right winger, who then delivers a cross into the box. The centre forward and left winger both attack the cross to complete the final phase of the finishing circuit.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Finish: Focus on clean, composed finishing in each phase. Players should be aiming for corners and adjusting their body shape for quick, controlled strikes.• Timing of Runs: Emphasize the importance of timing the run after the 1-2 passes and into the box during the crossing phase. Arriving too early or too late affects goal-scoring chances.• Movement Across Lines: The centre forward must demonstrate high work rate and intelligent movement between all three stations. This mirrors real match scenarios where strikers shift laterally.• Communication: Players should call for the ball during combinations and crosses, helping to organize runs and ensure clarity during each attacking phase.
progression_one: One-Touch Finish Requirement:Introduce a rule where players must finish with one touch on all shooting opportunities.Focus: Improves anticipation, positioning, and sharp execution under pressure.
progression_two: Passive Defenders in the Box:Add 1–2 passive defenders in the box for the final crossing phase to create pressure without going full-contact.Focus: Forces attacking players to time their movement more precisely and choose smarter finishing options while under light pressure.

title: Ajax Attacking Overloaded SSG
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 3v3 (+1 neutral) possession game in a central   zone, where both teams compete to complete 5 consecutive passes. Once a team   achieves this, they are allowed to play forward into one of their wide   attackers positioned on their attacking end. The drill is directional—each   team attacks opposite ends—mirroring realistic game scenarios. Once the ball is played into the wide area, a 3v2 attacking phase is   triggered. Additionally, one attacker and one defender from the central zone   are encouraged to break out and join the play, turning it into a potential   4v3 situation. This transition moment adds realism and challenges players to   react quickly in both attacking and defensive roles.
coaching_notes: • Retention with Purpose: Encourage quick, intelligent movement in the   central zone. Players should aim to create space and maintain tempo, knowing   their goal is to earn the opportunity to break out.     • Breaking Lines: When transitioning out of the central zone, players must   look to break lines with decisive passes into the wide attacker.     • Transition Awareness: Once the ball is played forward, players must   quickly recognize their new roles—whether it’s joining the attack or   recovering to defend.     • Overload Decision-Making: In the 4v3 phase, attackers should use the   overload intelligently, prioritizing quick combinations and exploiting   numerical advantages.
progression_one: Time Limit to Break Forward: Once 5 passes are completed, give the team 5 seconds to break forward and   find their wide attacker. Focus: Increases urgency and reinforces speed of thought and execution in   transition.

title: Ajax Build Up via Full Backs
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on encouraging build-up play through the full backs,   using one-third of the pitch to simulate the build-up zone. The setup   includes two mini goals positioned on either side in the wide full back areas—one   mini goal faces straight down the line, and the other is angled inward to   represent a typical pass into midfield. These target goals reflect the two   most common passing options available to a full back: a pass down the line or   an angled ball inside. The team in possession works to play out from the back, building through   their full backs to score into either of the two mini goals. The defending   team applies pressure high up the pitch. If they regain possession, they   immediately counter-attack toward a full-size central goal, simulating a   real-game turnover and transition moment.
coaching_notes: • Full Back Decision-Making: Encourage full backs to scan before receiving   and decide whether to play wide down the line or inside based on the pressure   and teammate positioning.     • Body Shape in Build-Up: Players should position themselves to receive in   a forward facing positiong, allowing forward momentum when playing through   the thirds.     • Press Resistance: Teach the back line and midfielders to remain composed   under pressure and support the full backs with angles for short   combinations.     • Counter-Pressing Reactions: When possession is lost, the build-up team   should instantly react to either win the ball back or delay the counter to   allow for recovery.
progression_one: Central Dribble End Line Option (Lower Value): Introduce a central end line directly opposite the build-up team's starting   area. If the build-up team is unable to play through the full backs, they can   now also score by dribbling across this central end line. However, this   option is worth fewer points than scoring into the mini goals in the wide   areas. Focus: Offers a secondary solution while reinforcing that the primary   objective remains playing through the full backs. This encourages players to   scan for wide options first but rewards intelligent recognition of space   centrally if the wide lanes are blocked.

title: Ajax Dribble & Shoot SSG
instructions_setup: This directional small-sided game encourages players to break lines through   either precise passing or progressive dribbling. Each team can score in two   different ways: by passing into a mini goal placed on one side of the end   line, or by dribbling through a set of poles located on the opposite side.   The layout creates decision-making moments by offering different scoring   types in different zones. Ideal for 4v4 to 7v7 formats, this setup promotes a variety of attacking   methods while keeping the game flowing. Players are encouraged to recognize   when to switch play and how to penetrate through the opposition either with   the ball at their feet or with a line-breaking pass.
coaching_notes: • Line-Breaking Decisions: Players must assess when to play through,   around, or over the opposition using dribbles or incisive passing.     • Switch of Play Awareness: Encourage quick transitions from one side of   the pitch to the other to unbalance the defense and create space to   attack.     • Weight and Timing of Passes: Precision and timing are essential when   targeting the mini goal. Passes should be sharp, accurate, and   well-weighted.     • Dribble Recognition: Players should recognize when the space opens up to   carry the ball forward through the poles—especially when defenders are   stretched or caught shifting.
progression_one: Bonus Point for Combo Play: Award an extra point if a team scores after switching play at least once   before the final action. Focus: Reinforces the habit of switching play and stretching the opposition   to create attacking space.
progression_two: Touch Limit in Middle Third: Restrict players to 2 touches in the central area of the pitch. Focus: Increases tempo and decision-making speed, encouraging early   recognition of line-breaking opportunities.

title: Ajax Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This simple yet effective conditioning drill involves players jogging the   short ends of the pitch—either behind or in front of the goals—and sprinting   diagonally from corner to corner across the longer sides. The design promotes   repeated high-intensity efforts with active recovery built into the   movement. The number of repetitions and sets should be determined by the coach based   on the intended physical outcomes, whether it be aerobic capacity, anaerobic   endurance, or recovery training.
coaching_notes: • Sprint Intent: Players must treat each diagonal sprint as a   match-representative effort—100% intensity and sharpness throughout.     • Controlled Recovery: Emphasize active recovery during the jogs. Players   should regulate breathing and prepare mentally for the next sprint.     • Body Mechanics: Focus on posture and efficient running technique—drive   arms, lift knees, and maintain forward body lean during sprints.     • Spacing & Flow: Ensure appropriate spacing between players to avoid   congestion and maintain rhythm across repetitions.
progression_one: Add Ball Carry During Jog: Players carry a ball during the jogging phase and perform quick touches or   footwork patterns as they move. Focus: Adds technical load during recovery and encourages focus and   coordination under fatigue.
progression_two: Timed Sprint Targets: Set time goals for each diagonal sprint (e.g., <7 seconds). Players must   hit the target or repeat the effort. Focus: Pushes maximal output while building competitive edge and   accountability.

title: Ajax Individual Mastery
instructions_setup: This technical mastery drill focuses on sharp one-touch passing and close   control using both feet. One player moves laterally through a series of five   cones spaced one yard apart, while the other acts as a stationary server from   a fixed central position. As the working player navigates through the cones, they play a short   one-touch return pass with the server at each cone—alternating feet as they   move. The emphasis is on rhythm, clean touches, and quick footwork,   simulating tight-space play and improving touch consistency under time and   spatial pressure.
coaching_notes: • Footwork & Body Shape: Players should stay light on their feet,   keeping a low center of gravity and adjusting body position to control the   ball efficiently off both feet.     • One-Touch Quality: Each pass should be clean and controlled—encourage   players to find a rhythm and maintain accuracy even as fatigue sets in.     • Awareness of Cone Position: Players should keep their eyes up between   passes to navigate the cones without relying solely on peripheral   vision.     • Consistency Over Speed: Prioritize the quality of execution first, then   gradually increase tempo as technique improves.
progression_one: Opposite Foot Only: The receiving player must alternate playing every ball with their   non-dominant foot. Focus: Builds confidence, coordination, and reliability on the weaker   side.
progression_two: Add a Trigger Cue: The server shouts either “left” or “right” just before the pass, and the   receiver must react and use the correct foot. Focus: Develops listening, cognitive reaction, and decision-making under   pressure.

title: Ajax Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill is built around a 5-pole setup—four poles forming a square and a fifth placed deeper in the center. Players work the ball around the square using a series of forward passes and 1-2 combinations. After each pass, players follow their pass to the next position, ensuring constant rotation and movement.The pattern is initially played in one direction. Once the ball completes a full circuit and returns to the starting point, the pattern is reversed, encouraging players to adjust their angles, timing, and awareness.
coaching_notes: • Body Shape Before Receiving: Encourage players to check their shoulder and open up to receive on the back foot, ready to pass forward.• Quality of Combinations: The 1-2 with the central player should be quick, sharp, and with minimal touches. Emphasize clean execution.• Timing of Pass: Players must recognize when to release the ball—especially when combining with the central player—ensuring the movement and pass are synchronized.• Weight of Pass: Passes should be firm but controlled, giving teammates the best possible chance to play forward without breaking stride.• Tempo & Rhythm: Maintain a consistent flow. Too slow and it loses intensity; too fast and the technique drops.• Follow Your Pass: Reinforce the habit of moving immediately after playing to simulate game-like transitions and movement off the ball.
progression_one: One-Touch Only:Restrict all passes to one touch around the grid.Focus: Increases tempo and demands higher technical execution and awareness of positioning.

title: Ajax Positional Rondo
instructions_setup: This advanced positional rondo is set across two vertically aligned zones, with 2 defenders in each zone. The team in possession is shaped in a 4-2-3-1 formation, minus the striker.A mannequin is placed between the two center backs to discourage square passes across the back line, which are often pressing triggers in real-game scenarios. Instead, players must find angles and disguise to play forward or diagonally.From the deeper midfield line (the "2" in 4-2-3-1), one player is allowed to enter the active grid as a pivot, creating overloads and supporting circulation. The focus is on clean positioning, timing, and purposeful possession.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness: Players must hold realistic positions to reflect their roles in a real 4-2-3-1 shape. Encourage correct distances and angles.• Avoiding Pressing Triggers: The mannequin acts as a visual cue to discourage predictable square passes—promote disguised passes or bounces instead.• Pivot Player Timing: The supporting midfielder should time their movement into the zone to receive under minimal pressure and help connect lines.• Scanning & Body Shape: Constant scanning is key. Players should receive side-on and prepare for their next action before the ball arrives.• Tempo & Rhythm of Play: The ball should move quickly but under control. Sharp passing with minimal unnecessary touches maintains intensity and realism.
progression_one: Live Press from Both Zones:Allow one defender from the opposite zone to press after a set number of passes (e.g., 4), forcing quicker decisions and testing positional structure.Focus: Increases pressing realism and encourages smart positioning to play through pressure.
progression_two: Limit Pivot Touches:Restrict the pivot player to two touches when entering the grid.Focus: Enhances scanning, anticipation, and quicker release under pressure.

title: Ajax Temporarily Overloaded
instructions_setup: In this possession-based drill, teams play 4v4 in two separate grids, each with players numbered 1 to 4. As the game progresses, the coach will randomly shout a number between 1 and 4. The player corresponding to the shouted number must quickly switch to the other grid, creating temporary imbalance in the game.This dynamic switch challenges the players to maintain or win possession while adjusting to a momentary numerical disadvantage or advantage. The quicker the players react to the switches, the more likely their team will keep control or win back possession.Each grid is surrounded by four mini-goals (eight total), and the defending team can score in any of these mini-goals when they win possession.
coaching_notes: • Reaction Speed & Awareness: Players must react quickly when their number is called. Quick decision-making will help them exploit or recover from the numerical shift.• Spacing & Positioning: With the unbalanced play, it’s essential to maintain good spacing to support teammates, allowing for easier passing options.• Transition Focus: Players must be sharp in transitioning between attack and defense. Encourage them to immediately capitalize on a numerical advantage or adjust to a disadvantage.• Communication: Since the teams are momentarily unbalanced, communication becomes crucial. Players must call for passes, identify new roles, and communicate quickly about defensive responsibilities.• Mini Goal Focus: The defending team should remain aggressive and focused on scoring into the mini-goals after winning possession, simulating quick counter-attacks.
progression_one: Forced Numerical Advantage:When the coach calls a number, the player switching grids must bring a teammate with them to create a numerical advantage (e.g., 5v4 for a short period).Focus: Encourages exploitation of numerical superiority and fosters tactical awareness in fast transitions.

title: Ajax Throw In Routine
instructions_setup: This throw-in routine focuses on attacking play in the final third. The drill involves two players working together, with one player acting as a blocker to create space for the second player to make a run into free space.The players begin by running closely together, with the first player blocking the defender marking the second player, allowing the second player to break free and run into the space. Once the attacker is in the free space, they should have a brief window to cross the ball into the box, ideally unopposed if the routine is executed correctly.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Run & Block: The key to this routine is the timing. The blocker must anticipate the right moment to obstruct the defender, giving the runner the necessary time and space.• Run into Free Space: The attacking player making the run should accelerate quickly into the free space and position themselves ideally to receive the cross.• Precision of Cross: The crosser must ensure the ball is delivered accurately and with pace, aiming for an area that maximizes scoring opportunities.• Communication: Effective communication between the two players is critical—make sure the blocker knows when to time the block and the runner knows when to expect the ball.• Quick Execution: Encourage players to keep the routine quick and fluid. The longer it takes, the more likely defenders will recover.
progression_one: Vary the Cross:Instead of always crossing the ball into the box, alternate between different types of crosses (e.g., low, driven, lofted) or have the runner take a shot on goal after receiving the ball.Focus: Enhances adaptability and decision-making for the player receiving the ball and allows for varied attacking options.

title: Anderlecht 1v1 Dribbling
instructions_setup: This 1v1 practice is a fast-paced dribbling and mastery exercise. Players compete in a 1v1 scenario, with the attacker aiming to beat the defender and play a pass to a teammate. Each successful dribble and pass earns the attacker a point. As the practice progresses, the central defender becomes more fatigued, placing greater emphasis on winning possession in the initial 1v1s. This encourages attacking players to take advantage of the defender’s fatigue as the session moves forward.
coaching_notes: • Deceptive Dribbling Techniques – Encourage attackers to use feints, body movements, and quick changes of direction to beat the defender. The quicker the attacker can execute these moves, the more successful they'll be in getting past the defender.• Attacking Pace & Timing – Players should focus on timing their runs and dribbles effectively to exploit the defender’s weaknesses. Emphasize the importance of a quick first touch to get past the defender early.• Defensive Positioning & Recovery – Defenders must focus on positioning themselves properly to stop the attacker’s progress. They should also work on their recovery speed to stay in the play, especially as fatigue sets in.• Quick Decision Making – Both attackers and defenders must make split-second decisions. Attackers should focus on creating space for their teammates once they have passed the ball, while defenders should make quick decisions on when to commit to a tackle.
progression_one: Introduce Time LimitsLimit the time for each 1v1 battle (e.g., 10 seconds per attempt). This will force the attacker to make quicker decisions and the defender to react more rapidly.Focus: Encourage rapid decision-making and movement, both for attackers and defenders.
progression_two: Add Multiple DefendersIntroduce more defenders in the same space, requiring attackers to beat multiple opponents. This will challenge players to maintain control under pressure and enhance their decision-making in tight situations.Focus: Improve ball control and dribbling under pressure while refining decision-making in crowded spaces.

title: Anderlecht 1v1 With & Without
instructions_setup: This 1v1 drill is set in a square grid where players are tasked with beating their opponent and making it through one of the two gates. Players start on opposite ends of the grid, directly facing each other.The drill is split into two parts:Without Ball: In the first phase, the attacker’s goal is to sprint through one of the gates without being tagged by the defender. The defender must tag the attacker before they reach the gate.With Ball: In the second phase, the attacker will now dribble the ball and attempt to get through one of the gates without being tackled by the defender.
coaching_notes: • Acceleration & Agility: The attacker must focus on explosive acceleration and sharp direction changes to evade the defender.• Defender Positioning: The defender should focus on keeping a good distance to make it difficult for the attacker to easily burst past them. Encourage the defender to use lateral movements to mirror the attacker’s position.• Timing of the Run: The attacker should time their sprint or dribble well, using feints and changes in direction to confuse the defender and create a clear path to the gate.• Ball Control (With Ball Phase): When dribbling, the attacker should focus on maintaining close control of the ball while keeping their head up to scan for the best opening.• Pressure Under Attack: Defenders should be encouraged to apply pressure without fouling, challenging the attacker to make decisions under pressure.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Implement a time limit (e.g., 5-10 seconds) for each attacker to get through the gate, increasing pressure and forcing quicker decisions.Focus: Increases the tempo of the drill, encouraging attackers to be decisive and confident in their movements.
progression_two: Add Extra Gates:Increase the number of gates, placing them at different angles, forcing the attacker to be more strategic in their approach to breaking through.Focus: Encourages variety in movement and decision-making, requiring the attacker to choose the best gate based on the defender’s positioning.

title: Anderlecht 2 Touch Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing drill allows players to get two different types of finish consecutively. For the first finish, the player must run forwards and take their first touch into the box before finishing while inside. For the second finish, the player will receive the ball inside the box, but their first touch must take them outside of the box. This drill helps players practice both quick finishing inside the box and finishing under pressure after a touch outside the box.
coaching_notes: • First Touch Into the Box – The player should focus on taking their first touch into the box with control and speed, setting up a clean strike at goal. The touch should be directed towards the goal to allow for a natural follow-up finish.• Finishing Technique – Encourage players to use a variety of finishing techniques (instep, side-foot, etc.) based on the type of ball they receive and their angle. They should focus on composure and accuracy, not just power.• Touch Out of the Box – When receiving the ball inside the box and taking the touch outside, the player must ensure they create enough space between themselves and the defender. This will require the player to control the ball with their feet while maintaining good balance.• Quick Decision-Making – Players should work on making quick decisions in this drill, deciding in real-time which finishing technique to use based on the positioning of the defender and the angle of the ball.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a defender who can apply pressure as the player makes their first touch. The defender can close down the space quickly, forcing the attacker to be quicker with their touch and finish.Focus: Increase the attacking player’s ability to finish under pressure while maintaining composure.
progression_two: Vary the Ball DeliveryThe coach can serve balls from different angles, forcing the player to adjust their positioning and decision-making with each touch. This will simulate real match scenarios.Focus: Improve adaptability to different ball deliveries and angles while finishing.

title: Anderlecht Attacking Patterns of Play
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical drill focuses on developing attacking patterns of play through a series of 3-player combinations. Players will work together to improve their understanding of timing, positioning, and movement in the attacking third. The drill emphasizes fluidity in the movement and communication between attackers, allowing them to develop chemistry and create well-rehearsed patterns that can be executed in match situations.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – Focus on the timing of the attackers’ runs, ensuring they move at the right moment to receive the ball and create space for each other. Encourage players to make dynamic and intelligent runs that provide multiple options for the player with the ball.• Fluid Combinations – The key to success in this drill is fluidity and quick passing. Encourage players to execute combinations with sharp, precise passes, and to continuously move into new positions to support the attack. Players should work together to create triangles, ensuring that all players have a clear passing option at any given time.• Communication and Understanding – Emphasize the importance of verbal and non-verbal communication between players. The combination play should be instinctive, so players should be aware of their teammates' positioning and movements. Develop their ability to anticipate each other's actions and play with awareness.• Attacking Intensity – Ensure players maintain high intensity in their movements and passing. While the drill is unopposed, players should treat it as if they are under match pressure, making fast, decisive decisions in their combinations.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender to the drill, making it more realistic by forcing the attackers to read the defender's positioning and make quicker decisions on their combinations. The defender will not actively try to win the ball but will apply light pressure to simulate game conditions.Focus: Improve decision-making and awareness under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Increase the Number of Players in the CombinationIncrease the number of players involved in the attacking combinations, turning it into a 4-player combination. This will challenge players to maintain fluidity and sharp passing while expanding the range of movements and patterns they can use.Focus: Develop more complex attacking patterns and fluidity in larger groups.

title: Anderlecht Build Up vs Unopposed Attack
instructions_setup: This build-up practice is designed for pre-match preparation, focusing on building play from the back and creating fluid attacking combinations. Play begins with the goalkeeper and 3 outfield players completing unopposed passing combinations to progress the ball. After a few successful combinations, the goalkeeper plays a long ball into the red midfield. Once the red team gains possession, they transition to an unopposed attacking phase, where they must use quick, fluid combination play to finish the attack.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up from the Back – Encourage the goalkeeper and defenders to make accurate and well-timed passes during the unopposed phase. The focus should be on making simple, effective passing combinations to create angles and space to progress the ball forward.• Timing and Precision – The transition to the red team should be sharp and focused, with precise passes from the goalkeeper. Players should be aware of their positioning to receive the long ball and make the next pass as quickly as possible to keep the rhythm of the play moving.• Combination Play – Once the red team gains possession, emphasize quick, fluid combination play to break down the opposition. Encourage players to use one-touches and off-the-ball movement to support each other and maintain attacking momentum.• Finishing the Attack – Ensure that the red team finishes the drill by attacking with purpose. Players should focus on creating and exploiting spaces, making decisive runs, and using accurate, well-weighted passes to set up a clear shot or goal-scoring opportunity.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce passive defenders to pressure the red team as they begin their attacking phase. This increases the difficulty and simulates a more realistic scenario where the attackers need to move quickly and create space under defensive pressure.Focus: Improve decision-making and accuracy in combination play under light defensive pressure.
progression_two: Time the AttackSet a time limit for the red team to complete the attack after winning possession from the goalkeeper’s long pass. This pushes the players to move quickly and make faster decisions, simulating game conditions where speed is crucial in the attacking phase.Focus: Increase the speed of play and decision-making in transition from defense to attack.

title: Anderlecht Corner Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed corner routine drill is designed to help players learn various corner delivery techniques and movements to create goal-scoring opportunities. The team will practice their set-piece routine with a focus on timing, spacing, and coordination. Players will position themselves according to the chosen routine (e.g., near post, far post, edge of the box, etc.) and work to execute the set play under minimal pressure.The corner taker will deliver the ball into the designated area, while the other players make runs to attack the ball or create space. The focus is on smooth, well-timed movements and effective ball delivery. The drill is unopposed, allowing the attacking team to concentrate on executing their routine to perfection.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Ensure that attacking players time their runs to the ball correctly. Whether it’s attacking the near post, far post, or edge of the box, the players should be well-timed in their movements to meet the delivery.• Movement to Create Space: Players should work on off-the-ball movement to pull defenders out of position, making it easier for teammates to get a clear shot at goal. Movement should be quick and dynamic, with players changing direction to create space in key areas.• Delivery Quality: Emphasize the importance of delivering the ball with the correct weight, pace, and accuracy. The corner taker must consistently place the ball into the designated area, whether it’s a driven cross, floated ball, or short corner.• Target Areas: Players should understand where to attack based on the type of delivery (e.g., near post, far post, or central). Each player should be aware of their role in relation to the ball's flight path and their teammates’ movements.• Communication: Encourage clear communication between the corner taker and attacking players. This ensures everyone knows when to make their run and where the ball will be delivered.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to lightly pressurize the attackers during the delivery and movement. The defenders should focus on tracking runs and challenging for the ball but not actively blocking or winning it.Focus: Develops the ability to execute corner routines while under light pressure, simulating more realistic game situations and forcing players to adjust their timing and runs.

title: Anderlecht Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: The drill begins with two attackers sprinting into the main rondo grid, where they face a 2v4 situation against four defenders. Their task is to win possession from the defenders.Once the two attackers win possession, they immediately sprint into two separate smaller grids (left and right). In these grids, the attackers are tasked with dispossessing a single ball carrier (one defender) before returning to the main rondo grid.
coaching_notes: • Pressure & Timing: Attackers must work in unison to apply pressure, with each player aiming to isolate a defender and win possession. Quick and precise pressing is key to forcing mistakes from the defenders.• Transition to Smaller Grids: Once possession is gained, the attackers need to transition quickly into the smaller grids. Speed and sharp direction changes are critical for putting the defenders under pressure.
progression_one: Add Extra Defenders:Increase the number of defenders in the smaller grids (e.g., 2 defenders per grid), making it more challenging for the attackers to regain possession.Focus: Encourages attackers to work together in tight spaces and find creative ways to break down a stronger defense.
progression_two: Time-Based Challenge:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 15 seconds) for attackers to regain possession and return to the main rondo grid. If they don’t win possession in time, they must restart the drill.Focus: Adds intensity and urgency, encouraging attackers to be quick and efficient in regaining possession and maintaining control under pressure.

title: Anderlecht One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This drill is designed for midfielders to practice switching play using a variety of passing techniques. The player will alternate between short, precise passes into a mini goal and longer, floated passes into a main goal. The exercise encourages vision, weight of pass, and accuracy in changing the point of attack effectively.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Head Up Awareness Before Passing – Scan the field constantly to identify the best passing options quickly and efficiently.• Vary Passing Technique to Suit Distance and Target – Use crisp, driven passes for short options and controlled lofted passes for longer switches.• Maintain Balanced Body Positioning for Accurate Delivery – Align body correctly to control pass direction and power across different distances.• Control Tempo and Decision-Making to Maximise Effectiveness – Choose when to speed up or slow down play depending on pressure and team shape.
progression_one: Increase Passing Speed and Reduce Decision TimeEncourage quicker passes and faster decisions to simulate game-like pressure and improve mental sharpness.Focus:Enhances quick thinking, passing accuracy, and the ability to switch play fluidly under time constraints.
progression_two: Introduce Passive Pressure from a DefenderAdd a passive defender to force tighter control and more precise passing under pressure.Focus:Develops composure, spatial awareness, and technical execution when switching play in contested situations.

title: Anderlecht Patterned Finishing
instructions_setup: In this unopposed attacking pattern and finishing drill, players are set up across five stations: two central midfielders (CM) and three attackers (left winger (LW), center forward (CF), and right winger (RW)).The drill begins with the players completing a series of predefined passing routines, focusing on movement, timing, and ball circulation. The attackers will then work in tandem with the central midfielders, receiving passes, and executing specific movements to create goal-scoring opportunities.The drill ends with a cross from either the left or right winger, followed by a finish from the center forward. Mannequins are strategically placed to help attackers visualize and anticipate the spaces they will need to play in during the game.
coaching_notes: • Movement Off the Ball: Encourage attackers to make dynamic runs, creating space for themselves and their teammates. The center forward should be aware of the angles of runs made by the wingers and adjust accordingly to receive the ball in dangerous positions.• Timing of Passes: Focus on the timing of the passes, ensuring that the ball is played to the feet or into space based on the run made by the attacker. Central midfielders must demonstrate good vision and awareness to play the correct pass.• Mannequin Use: The mannequins should be treated as defenders. Players must work on reading the space around the mannequins and making runs to avoid being blocked or closed down.• Finishing Technique: When finishing, encourage attackers to use the correct technique (inside foot for placement, laces for power), and focus on shooting quickly and accurately, especially when receiving crosses.• Communication: Communication between the wingers, center forward, and central midfielders is key to executing the passing routine smoothly and ensuring everyone is aware of their role in the pattern.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure:Introduce passive defenders in the central midfield or wide areas. The defenders will apply light pressure to force players to make quicker decisions and execute the passing patterns under slightly more challenging conditions.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and sharper ball control when under pressure.
progression_two: 2 Players Attacking the Box:When the left winger crosses from the left side, the right winger should now make a run to attack the back post, making it a two-player attacking presence in the box. This creates more options for the center forward, increasing the chances of a goal-scoring opportunity.Focus: Increases attacking options in the box, encouraging attackers to support each other and attack the cross from multiple angles.

title: Antwerp 3 Phase Attacking
instructions_setup: This attacking drill is designed on a third of the pitch, divided into three vertical zones: two wide zones and a central zone roughly the width of the penalty box. The drill challenges players to work through multiple phases, focusing on different attacking combinations and transitions to build fluid, coordinated attacks. It requires sharp decision-making, movement, and finishing under realistic pressure.The drill progresses through three phases: Phase 1 is a 2v2 attack in the central zone, where attackers aim to score in the main goal and defenders try to win possession cleanly to score in two mini goals on the opposite line. Phase 2 and 3 move into the wide zones, each featuring a 2v1 scenario with a cross delivered into the box for the central 2v2 players to finish. The drill develops attacking creativity, defensive reactions, and team coordination across all attacking thirds.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Quick, Sharp Passing and Movement – Players must maintain a high tempo and precise ball control to effectively break down defenders under pressure.• Emphasize Communication Between Attackers and Defenders – Verbal and visual cues are essential for anticipating passes and improving defensive positioning.• Focus on Timing Runs and Delivering Accurate Crosses – Attackers should time their runs to exploit space while crossers deliver quality service into the box consistently.• Train Defenders to Transition Quickly from Pressing to Counterattack – Defenders need to intercept cleanly and exploit the mini goals to capitalize on opposition mistakes.
progression_one: Increase Intensity and Reduce Time Allowed Per PhaseShorten the decision-making windows to force faster reactions, sharper technical execution, and enhanced physical conditioning.Focus: Enhances players’ ability to perform complex technical and tactical actions effectively under intense pressure and fatigue.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Player in Wide Zones to Create OverloadsIntroduce a neutral player supporting attackers in wide zones, increasing tactical complexity and encouraging creative combination play.Focus: Develops spatial awareness, quick interplay, and adaptability in dynamic, overloaded attacking situations.

title: Antwerp Build Up Into Wide
instructions_setup: This tactical possession drill focuses on building out from the back using full backs as key outlets during controlled pressure scenarios. The build-up team plays 6 + GK vs 4 pressing players within a third-pitch area, replicating realistic build-up conditions from a goal kick or deep restart. Each attack begins with the goalkeeper, and the objective is to progress play into mini goals positioned in wide zones.If the pressing team wins the ball, they launch an immediate counterattack toward a full-size goal. The exercise develops composure under pressure, full-back involvement, pressing intensity, and transition play in realistic game-like settings.
coaching_notes: • Goalkeeper Must Be Comfortable Playing Under PressureEncourage the GK to scan early and distribute calmly, helping the team play through pressure rather than going long too quickly.• Full Backs Should Offer Constant Width and TimingPosition wide and receive at angles, arriving just as the pass is played to maximize space and passing rhythm.• Centre Backs and Midfielders Must Create Support TrianglesOffer close-range passing lanes and rotate positions to help progress the ball through short, sharp combinations.• Pressing Players Must Stay Compact and Trigger TogetherApply collective pressure with coordinated cues, cutting off passing lanes and anticipating backward or sideways passes.
progression_one: Limit Goalkeeper to Two TouchesReduce the goalkeeper’s time on the ball to force quicker decisions under pressure and increase the overall tempo of the build-up play across the back line.Focus:Enhances speed of play, sharpens technical decision-making, and improves communication and composure in high-pressure situations.

title: Antwerp Central Build & Transition
instructions_setup: This central build-up drill is designed to enhance a team’s ability to play out from the back through tight, compact spaces. The playing area covers roughly 40 yards wide by 30 yards deep, focusing on the width of the penalty box plus an additional 12 yards. The build-up team consists of four outfield players plus the goalkeeper, who start each phase by playing out from the back against three aggressive pressing opponents. The objective for the build-up team is to dribble and pass their way through one of two designated gates positioned on either side of the top line of the grid.The drill replicates high-pressure scenarios, with the three pressing players aiming to win possession and immediately launch a quick counter-attack toward the main goal. This setup encourages quick decision-making, effective ball control, and composure under pressure while emphasizing spatial awareness in a condensed area. The goalkeeper plays a critical role in initiating play and helping the team progress the ball securely through the midfield.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Players to Stay Compact and Support Each Other Closely – Maintaining tight distances helps create passing options and protects the ball under pressure.• Focus on Quick, Accurate Ball Circulation – Emphasize sharp, well-weighted passes to move the ball efficiently through the pressing lines.• Guide Players to Use Dribbling to Break Lines When Appropriate – Controlled, purposeful dribbling can disrupt the press and open passing lanes.• Reinforce Communication and Scanning Off the Ball – Players must constantly scan for pressing threats and communicate to maintain shape and awareness.
progression_one: Increase the Intensity and Aggression of the Pressing PlayersMake the pressing team more active and quicker to close down space, forcing the build-up team to speed up their decision-making and execution.Focus:Enhances composure, speed of play, and technical accuracy under heightened physical and mental pressure.
progression_two: Introduce a Numerical Advantage for the Pressing TeamAdd an additional pressing player to create a 4v4+GK scenario, further increasing defensive pressure and forcing more precise ball control and tactical awareness.Focus:Develops sharper spatial awareness, quick transitions, and resilience in tight, competitive conditions.

title: Antwerp Finishing The Attack Centrally
instructions_setup: This finishing the attack centrally drill focuses on developing players’ ability to break through defensive lines and finish efficiently in tight central areas. The practice is set up in a compact 30 by 40-yard zone, divided into two main phases. Initially, two attackers work together to play the ball forward past two defensive players positioned on a fixed line acting as blockers or screeners. Once past this line, the ball is delivered into a second zone where three attackers face two defenders in a 3v2 attacking situation, encouraging quick decision-making and sharp finishing.If the blockers intercept or win the ball during the first phase, they immediately transition to attack against two defenders in a 2v2 scenario aiming to score in two mini goals. This drill challenges players to combine effective combination play, sharp attacking movement, and strong defensive reactions while maintaining high intensity throughout both attacking and defensive phases.
coaching_notes: Encourage Precise, Timed Passing to Break Defensive Lines – The initial two attackers must focus on well-weighted, accurate passes to bypass the blockers effectively.• Promote Sharp, Coordinated Movement From Attacking Players – Off-the-ball runs should create passing lanes and overloads in the 3v2 attacking phase for better scoring opportunities.• Stress Defensive Alertness and Quick Transitions – Defenders must stay alert to intercept passes and immediately transition to attack, maintaining intensity and focus.• Reinforce Composed, Accurate Finishing Under Pressure – Attacking players should remain calm to execute quality shots in tight scenarios with limited space.
progression_one: Add a Passive Third Defender in the Final Attacking ZoneIntroduce a passive defender to increase pressure on the 3v2 attackers, encouraging quicker decision-making and improved spatial awareness.Focus:Develops sharper attacking creativity, improved defensive communication, and better composure in tight central spaces.
progression_two: Reduce Allowed Touches for Attackers in Both PhasesLimit attackers to two touches per possession phase to increase tempo, forcing faster ball control and decision-making under pressure.Focus:Improves technical precision, quicker thinking, and dynamic attacking combinations in high-pressure environments.

title: Antwerp Fitness & Finish Rondo
instructions_setup: This fitness & rondo drill combines high-intensity pressing, quick transition play, and finishing in a dynamic, game-realistic setting. Two defenders enter a central rondo area from opposite ends of the pitch, working together in a 2v6 to regain possession. If they win the ball, they break out of the grid to finish into either of two full-size goals. If the six retain the ball for 12 passes, the defenders must sprint back to tag in the next pair.This drill tests defensive pressing, team possession under pressure, and quick-fire finishing actions while building fitness and mental sharpness.
coaching_notes: • Press Aggressively and Communicate ConstantlyWork as a pair to close passing lanes, press with intensity, and stay connected to force errors from the team in possession.• Transition with Purpose After Winning the BallReact instantly, drive toward goal at pace, and make decisive finishing choices to convert turnovers into goals.• Keep Possession with Tempo and Smart Support PlayFor the 6 players in possession, focus on sharp ball speed, clever movement, and intelligent angles to maintain rhythm under pressure.• Recover Quickly and Tag Teammates with SpeedIf unable to win the ball, defenders must switch mentality fast and sprint back to maintain the tempo of the practice and their physical output.
progression_one: Lower Pass Target to 8Reduce the number of passes required before the defenders rotate out to raise intensity and decision-making demands.Focus:Increases pressing urgency, sharpens reaction times, and challenges possession players to stay composed under quicker pressure.
progression_two: One-Touch Limit for Possession TeamIntroduce a one-touch condition for players in possession to add technical difficulty and test awareness and positioning.Focus:Improves technical sharpness, quick thinking, and spatial discipline when under extreme pressure in tight spaces.

title: Antwerp Isolated Wide Build Up
instructions_setup: This isolated wide build-up drill focuses on developing a team’s ability to build play through one side of the pitch, either the left or right flank, within a specifically defined area covering roughly one-third of the pitch height and half the pitch width. The setup mimics real-game scenarios where attacks are constructed through wide defensive channels. The build-up team consists of one goalkeeper and three outfield players, working together to progress the ball against two pressing opponents. Their main objective is to move the ball forward and score by passing into one of two mini goals placed in advanced wide positions, representing wide attacking outlets.The drill encourages players to use the width effectively, maintain possession under pressure, and make smart decisions to break through defensive lines on the designated flank. The restricted area challenges the team to be precise with passing, movement, and spatial awareness to successfully bypass the pressers and transition into attack.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Wide Positioning and Effective Use of Space – Encourage players to stretch the play and exploit the available width to create passing lanes and overloads.• Focus on Quick, Accurate Passing and Movement – Sharp ball circulation and off-the-ball runs are essential to outmaneuver pressing opponents in a tight channel.• Encourage Supportive Body Positioning to Facilitate Easy Receiving – Players should open their body to see the field and be ready to receive under pressure.• Reinforce Patience and Composure in Progressing the Ball – Players must resist rushing and maintain calmness to pick the best moment to advance the play.
progression_one: ncrease Pressure Intensity by Making Pressers More AggressiveEncourage the pressers to close down space faster and apply stronger pressure, forcing quicker decisions and more precise execution from the build-up team.Focus:Improves technical skill, decision-making speed, and composure under high-pressure wide build-up conditions.
progression_two: Limit the Number of Touches Allowed for Build-Up PlayersRestrict players to two or three touches per possession phase, increasing the challenge of quick ball control and accurate passing in tight spaces.Focus:Develops sharper ball control, quicker thinking, and efficient use of limited touches to maintain possession and progress play.

title: Antwerp Retention Rondo
instructions_setup: This dynamic rondo drill features two teams of six players each occupying adjacent 15x15 yard grids, creating a combined 15x30 yard playing area. Each grid is bordered by four mini goals, adding scoring opportunities to both sides of the practice. The drill emphasizes possession, pressing, and quick transitions between attack and defense, challenging players to stay mentally and physically sharp throughout.At the coach’s whistle, one team sends three players to press aggressively in the opposite grid, creating a 6v3 possession battle. The team with six players aims to complete eight consecutive passes to earn the right to score into any of their four mini goals. This sequence repeats with the coach feeding new balls until the pressing trio wins possession. Upon winning the ball, the pressing players sprint back to their own grid and immediately begin their own 6v3 possession phase with three players from the opposite team crossing over to press.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Sharp, Accurate Passing Under Pressure – Players must maintain composure and precision despite intense pressing to sustain possession.• Stress Quick Transitions Between Offense and Defense – Emphasize rapid reaction times for both pressing and retreating phases to keep the drill flowing.• Promote Communication and Awareness of Surroundings – Players should constantly scan the field, anticipate passes, and support teammates effectively.• Focus on Effective Pressing Angles and Team Shape – The three pressers must work cohesively to close down space and force turnovers efficiently.
progression_one: Increase Required Passes to Ten Before Scoring OpportunityRaising the pass completion target forces greater patience, technical skill, and teamwork under sustained pressure, increasing the physical and mental demands on players.Focus: Improves collective ball retention, tactical discipline, and mental resilience during longer, more challenging possession phases.
progression_two: Limit Touches Per Player to Two or FewerReducing touches accelerates decision-making speed, forces quicker technical execution, and increases intensity by putting players under tighter constraints in possession.Focus: Develops faster thinking, sharper ball control, and enhanced spatial awareness in high-pressure, fast-paced game scenarios.

title: Antwerp Technical Passing Activation
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill is designed to develop players’ ability to maintain possession, execute varied passing techniques, and make quick decisions in a tight space. Players work the ball around a square grid, focusing on sharp, accurate passes and smooth movement. After circulating the ball with different passing combinations—including back-foot receiving, 1-2s, and third-man runs—they complete a final pass into a mini goal to simulate a decisive attacking action. Players rotate positions following each pass to encourage constant involvement and positional awareness.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Accurate, Weighted Passing for Smooth Ball Circulation – Quality passes set the rhythm and create opportunities for teammates to receive under control.• Encourage Quick, Confident Movement Off the Ball – Players should anticipate their next position and move promptly after each pass to maintain fluidity.• Incorporate Variety in Passing Techniques and Angles – Use back-foot receiving, 1-2 combinations, and third-man runs to develop versatile technical skills and tactical understanding.• Maintain Communication and Scanning to Improve Awareness – Players must communicate and scan regularly to identify passing options and stay alert to the flow of play.
progression_one: Increase Passing Speed and Reduce Touches AllowedSpeed up the tempo and limit players to one or two touches to challenge technical execution and quick decision-making under pressure.Focus:Enhances sharpness, precision, and rapid reactions in tight, fast-paced passing sequences.

title: Apoel 2 Zone Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: In this two-zone attacking overload practice, play begins with a 2v2 in the first zone, supported by a neutral player positioned in a central lane. The attacking pair must work the ball effectively to progress play forward and combine with the neutral player before entering the second zone. Once progression is achieved, the neutral player joins the attack to create a 3v2 situation, where the attackers attempt to score into two mini goals. After the phase is completed, the neutral player resets to the central lane and the practice restarts in the opposite direction with new attackers.
coaching_notes: • Breaking Lines: Encourage attackers to recognise moments to play forward through the central lane with disguised, well-weighted passes.• Support and Angles: Focus on off-ball movement to create clear passing lanes, depth and width during the build-up phase.• Speed of Attack: Emphasise quick ball circulation and positive forward actions to exploit the overload before defenders can recover.• Decision-Making in the Final Zone: Coach attackers to select the best finishing option quickly under pressure, using the overload effectively.
progression_one: Limit Touches in the First Zone:Restrict players in the build-up zone to two touches, increasing tempo, sharper movement and quicker recognition of progression moments.Focus: Improves technical efficiency, scanning habits and speed of play under increased cognitive and physical pressure.
progression_two: Add a Recovery Defender:Allow an additional defender to recover into the second zone after progression, forcing attackers to execute faster and more decisively.Focus: Develops realism, finishing quality under pressure and improved decision-making when overloads are reduced.

title: Apoel 2v1 & Finishing
instructions_setup: In this 2v1 attacking practice, players begin from one of three designated starting zones - left, central or right. Two attackers combine to attack a single defender and attempt to score against the goalkeeper. Each repetition challenges players to recognise different angles, distances and defensive pictures depending on the starting zone. After every action, attackers rotate to a different zone to ensure exposure to varied attacking scenarios and decision-making moments.
coaching_notes: • Exploiting the Overload:Encourage attackers to recognise the 2v1 early, commit the defender decisively, manipulate their positioning and create clear passing or shooting lanes.• Timing and Angle of Support:Focus on supporting runs that arrive at the correct moment, distance and body shape to receive cleanly or finish first time.• Decision-Making in the Final Action:Reinforce choosing between passing or shooting based on defender body position, pressure distance and goalkeeper movement cues.• Attacking from Different Angles:Coach players to adjust approach speed, body orientation and touch selection depending on starting zone and angle to goal.
progression_one: Touch Limit for Attackers:Restrict attackers to two or three touches to increase speed of play, technical efficiency and attacking clarity.Focus:Improves tempo, first-touch quality, faster decision-making and composure when attacking in tight, time-pressured scenarios.
progression_two: Defender Recovery or Pressure Cue:Allow the defender to delay initially, then add a recovery run, pressing trigger or directional constraint.Focus:Adds realism, challenges attackers to act earlier and enhances execution against recovering or late-pressing defenders.

title: Apoel 4v4 & Countering
instructions_setup: In this 4v4 + counter-attacking practice, play begins with a coach serving the ball into a central area where four attackers attempt to score against four defenders. The attacking team looks to combine, penetrate and finish under pressure, while the defending team focuses on regaining possession with control. Upon winning the ball, the defenders must immediately play forward into a centre forward positioned in a central transition zone. This triggers a counter-attacking phase, where three attackers break forward to attack two recovering defenders in the opposite zone, creating a realistic transition moment from defence to attack.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Defensive Regains:Encourage defenders to win the ball with control, secure first contact and look forward immediately rather than clearing aimlessly.• Speed of Counter-Attack:Emphasise quick forward passes, aggressive forward running and minimal touches to exploit defensive imbalance after regaining possession.• Movement of the Centre Forward:Coach the centre forward to stay connected, show at the correct angle and link play efficiently during the transition moment.• Attacking Decision-Making on the Counter:Reinforce choosing when to pass, carry or finish based on defender recovery speed and numerical advantage.
progression_one: Time Limit on Counter Attack:Add a time constraint for the counter-attacking team to create a shot or finish quickly.Focus:Increases realism, sharpens attacking urgency and improves execution under intense transition pressure.

title: Apoel Build Up vs Countering
instructions_setup: In this build-up practice, a team of seven outfield players plus a goalkeeper attempt to build and progress possession against five pressing defenders. The possession team aims to retain the ball under pressure while looking to score into any of the four mini goals positioned ahead of them. The two full backs are locked outside the main grid and operate up and down the touchlines to support circulation and progression, while the number 10 is locked into a horizontal central zone at the top of the grid to provide advanced support between lines. If the five defenders regain possession, they must counter-attack quickly and attempt to score against the goalkeeper, reinforcing realistic transition moments.
coaching_notes: • Building with Patience and Purpose:Encourage the possession team to circulate the ball with composure, drawing pressure before exploiting spaces to progress play forward.• Use of Full Backs for Width:Coach full backs to provide consistent width, correct timing of support and forward passing options to stretch the defensive shape.• Role of the Number 10:Emphasise intelligent movement, scanning and positioning between lines to receive on the half-turn and connect attacks effectively.• Reaction on Defensive Regain:Reinforce immediate transition behaviours for defenders, attacking forward quickly and decisively upon winning possession.
progression_one: Touch Limit in Central Areas:Apply a two- or three-touch limit for central players to increase speed of circulation and decision-making.Focus:Improves tempo, sharper first-touch execution and faster recognition of forward progression opportunities under pressure.
progression_two: Directional Counter-Attack Constraint:Require defenders to score within a time limit or through a specific mini goal when possession is regained.Focus:Enhances transition realism, encourages vertical play and sharpens counter-attacking efficiency and awareness.

title: Apoel Counter & Recovery
instructions_setup: In this counter-attack and recovery practice, three attackers begin just below the halfway line and attack against two central defenders. The attacking team initially looks to exploit the temporary numerical advantage by progressing quickly and directly towards goal. Once the attackers cross a designated trigger line, two recovering full backs are allowed to sprint back from wide positions to support the defence, potentially creating a 4v3 advantage for the defending team. This forces the attackers to recognise moments to play with speed and purpose before the defensive recovery arrives, while defenders are challenged to delay, recover and protect central areas effectively.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Counter-Attack:Encourage attackers to recognise the overload early and attack with tempo, direct running and decisive actions.• Decision Making in Overloads:Coach players to identify when to pass, carry or finish quickly before defensive numbers recover.• Defensive Delay and Positioning:Emphasise the importance of delaying play, protecting central spaces and forcing attackers wide where possible.• Recovery Runs and Communication:Reinforce full backs sprinting with intensity, recovering inside positions and communicating clearly with central defenders.
progression_one: Limited Touches for Attackers:Introduce a touch restriction for attackers to increase speed of play and reduce over-dribbling.Focus:Improves quick decision-making, sharper execution and greater urgency during counter-attacking moments.
progression_two: Defensive Advantage Triggered Earlier:Allow recovering full backs to enter the practice sooner or from varied starting distances.Focus:Challenges attackers to recognise shrinking windows of opportunity and execute actions under increasing pressure.

title: Argentina 1v1 with Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This practice begins with short passing combinations between the attacker and defender. Once the attacker feels confident, they make the decision to initiate live opposed play by turning and dribbling through the grid. The defender, after the pass, must make a recovery run in the opposite direction to the attacker, aiming to recover into the box and stop the attack in a 1v1 scenario.
coaching_notes: • Effective Ball Mastery – The attacker should focus on using quick, sharp touches to maintain close control of the ball during the initial combination. The goal is to create separation and set up a favorable situation for the 1v1.• Timing the Attack – The attacker must make a decision on when to shift into live play, using the right moment to turn and accelerate away from the defender. Timing is key to catching the defender off guard.• Defender’s Recovery Run – The defender must focus on recovering quickly and getting into the box before the attacker can get through. Emphasize positioning, reading the attacker’s movements, and preventing them from creating space.• 1v1 Situation – Once live play begins, the defender should close down the attacker quickly, applying pressure while maintaining balance. The attacker needs to use quick changes of direction to beat the defender and finish effectively.
progression_one: Limited Touches for the AttackerLimit the attacker to 3 touches when they transition into the live 1v1. This increases the pressure on the attacker to make quicker decisions and execute under tighter constraints.Focus: Improve decision-making and ball control under pressure, while forcing the attacker to take faster, more decisive actions.
progression_two: Add Extra DefendersIntroduce a second defender who starts from a different angle to increase the difficulty of the 1v1. The attacker now has to deal with two defenders in the final phase of the drill.Focus: Improve the attacker’s ability to work under increased defensive pressure and create space, while refining dribbling and decision-making in a crowded environment.

title: Argentina Cutback SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is played with 4v4 teams and 4 neutral players positioned at the 4 corners of the grid, known as the 'cutback' zones. The objective is to score 1 goal to win the game. After each goal, the losing team will switch with the neutral players, ensuring that both teams get equal opportunities in different roles.The neutral players are restricted to 1 touch, and the team in possession is encouraged to use them to create goal-scoring chances through quick cutbacks, crosses, or switching the play. The attacking team should aim to exploit the neutral zones to stretch the defense, pull defenders out of position, and open up space for a final delivery into the box. The defenders will need to be aware of their positioning and try to prevent passes into the neutral zones by maintaining close coverage on their opponents.
coaching_notes: • Neutral Player Use: Encourage the team in possession to quickly switch the play to the neutral zones to unbalance the defense and create overloads in wide areas. The neutral players should be used to create wide angles and allow for an easier ball progression.• Cutback Awareness: Attackers need to time their runs into the box to coincide with the pass being played into the cutback zones. This will give them a chance to attack the goal from an unmarked position.• Defensive Positioning: Defenders should work to deny passes into the cutback zones and stay alert to the runners from the central areas. They need to make sure to track attackers running into the box and deny them a clean shot.• Speed of Play: Emphasize quick, clean passing to switch the play and create overloads in the wide areas. The attacking team should look to exploit the space in the cutback zones by moving the ball quickly and efficiently.
progression_one: Limit Attacking Team’s Touches:Limit the attacking team to two touches to increase the tempo of the game, improve decision-making under pressure, and force quick execution in the final third. This will also help players focus on creating quick attacking opportunities.

title: Argentina Headers & Volleys Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This is a fun and competitive warm-up practice where teams will compete head-to-head. Players from opposite teams will take turns running around the poles and attempting to score a header into the goal. Once they've completed their attacking phase, they must quickly transition to become the goalkeeper and attempt to stop the header from the next opposition player. This exercise encourages both attacking and defending skills while keeping the players engaged.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – Encourage players to time their runs well to meet the ball at the right moment for a successful header. The run should be dynamic, with players using their momentum to direct the ball into the goal.• Accuracy over Power – Stress the importance of accuracy when heading the ball, rather than focusing solely on power. Players should aim for specific areas of the goal to increase their chances of scoring.• Quick Transitions – Players must quickly switch from attacker to goalkeeper, so emphasize the importance of quick footwork and alertness when transitioning. This will help players stay sharp both in attack and defense.• Goalkeeping Fundamentals – As goalkeepers, players should focus on positioning, anticipating the header, and being proactive in moving to the ball. They need to react quickly and be ready to make a save with both hands or using their head to deflect the ball if necessary.
progression_one: Add a Second Phase to the AttackIntroduce a second attacking phase where players need to pass the ball to a teammate before they attempt to score a header, making the drill slightly more complex.Focus: Improve teamwork and passing accuracy before the header, as well as decision-making on when to attempt a header.
progression_two: Increase the Number of DefendersAdd another defender to challenge the attacking player. The defender should try to block the header or pressure the attacker to make the header more difficult.Focus: Improve players’ ability to score under pressure and sharpen defensive skills in aerial duels.

title: Argentina Line Breaking Technical
instructions_setup: This is a technical passing practice with three different variations that allows players to develop their ability to make line-breaking passes. The practice focuses on the timing, accuracy, and creativity required to break through defensive lines with passing. The variations include different types of passes and runs, ensuring players are able to execute a range of passes to penetrate the opposition's defense effectively.
coaching_notes: • Passing Technique – Encourage players to focus on the quality of their passes, making sure they are crisp, accurate, and well-weighted. Emphasize the importance of using both feet and the correct surface of the foot (instep, inside, outside) for different situations.• Timing of Runs – Players should time their runs to receive line-breaking passes effectively. They must stay onside and make runs that force defenders to make a decision, whether to press or drop off.• Vision & Awareness – Players need to develop awareness of where the space is and when to play the ball. They should constantly scan the field for potential passing lanes and be ready to deliver the ball at the right moment.• Quick Transition – Focus on the transition from defense to attack. The player passing the ball should be quick and decisive in playing through the lines, while the receiving player should be prepared to take advantage of the space immediately.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce defenders in specific zones to force the attacking team to make quicker and more accurate line-breaking passes. The defenders can react to the passes and challenge for possession.Focus: Increase pressure on the passer, ensuring quicker decision-making and improved passing accuracy under pressure.
progression_two: Incorporate Movement After PassingAfter making a line-breaking pass, players must immediately move into space to receive a return pass or support the next phase of play.Focus: Improve players' ability to pass and move, ensuring they are always a viable option to receive the ball or support the attack.

title: Argentina Multi-Directional SSG
instructions_setup: This small sided game begins with a 6v6+2 setup where teams play horizontally across the pitch, attacking two mini goals on either end. The two goalkeepers act as neutral players, supporting the team in possession to build and maintain control.Once a team scores in either of the mini goals, the coach immediately feeds a new ball vertically into the pitch to a player from the scoring team. All players must then transition and switch direction, now attacking and defending vertically, creating a dynamic two-phase game that mimics real-time transitions and encourages adaptability, organization, and quick thinking.
coaching_notes: • Neutral Player Use: Encourage the team in possession to utilize goalkeepers as bounce options to maintain width and recycle possession when under pressure.• Speed of Transition: Once a goal is scored, all players must immediately react, shifting shape and roles to prepare for the second phase of play.• Positional Awareness: Defenders should maintain compactness and communication during the switch to prevent overloads and disorganization.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Players must make fast decisions in both attack and defense during transitional moments, replicating the intensity of match scenarios.
progression_one: Limit Attacking Touches:Limit the number of touches for the attacking players (e.g., no more than two touches per player).
