This encourages quicker, more efficient ball movement and decision-making.Focus: Increases tempo and improves the attackers' ability to control the ball under pressure while making rapid decisions in tight spaces.

title: Argentina Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing pattern mixes short combinations in the initial phase with longer passes to switch the play. Two square grids, positioned roughly 20 meters apart, are set up. Players complete quick one- or two-touch passes inside one grid, then switch the play with a longer diagonal pass to the opposite grid. Once the ball arrives, the same combination and switch sequence continues.
coaching_notes: • Short Passing Quality: Emphasize sharp, accurate passing during the combination phase. Players should focus on keeping the ball on the ground and playing with proper weight and direction.• Scanning and Timing: Players should scan before receiving and play their pass at the right time to maintain rhythm and avoid rushed decisions.• Body Shape: Encourage open body positions to receive on the back foot and play forward quickly, especially when preparing for the switch.• Weight and Accuracy of Long Passes: Switches of play must be well-timed and struck with precision to allow a smooth transition between grids.• Movement After Pass: Players must move purposefully after playing a pass to maintain angles and keep the tempo high.
progression_one: Add Passive Pressure:Place one passive defender in each grid to force players to adjust their position and stay alert during the short combination phase.Focus: Helps players improve decision-making and positioning under slight pressure while maintaining technical execution.

title: Argentina Transfer Rondo
instructions_setup: This is a high-intensity possession and transition game involving 8 players split into 4 teams of 2. The setup consists of two adjacent square grids. Two teams operate in the wide grids (one per side), one team positions on the outside acting as neutral link players, and one team defends across both grids.The objective for the 3 teams in possession is to circulate the ball from one side to the other using the neutral players and wide grids while evading the defending team’s pressure. If the defending pair win possession, they immediately look to score in either of the two mini-goals positioned back-to-back in the central channel between the grids. A successful goal allows them to swap roles with the team they dispossessed.
coaching_notes: • Defensive Communication: The defending team must communicate effectively to press as a unit and cut off passing lanes between grids.• Switching Tempo: Encourage quick switches across the grids to disorganize the defenders and find space on the opposite side.• Neutral Link Play: The neutral team must stay active and provide passing angles at all times, enabling smooth transitions between grids.• Ball Security: Teams in possession should focus on keeping the ball with minimal touches and clean, purposeful passes.• Immediate Transition: If possession is lost or won, players should transition quickly—either to attack the goal or reorganize defensively.
progression_one: Add a Touch Limit:Limit players in possession to two touches per sequence. This increases the difficulty and forces quicker decisions and sharper technical execution.Focus: Encourages faster play and sharper ball control while promoting quick decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to Score:Once the defenders win possession, they must score within 5 seconds. This simulates a fast counterattack under real match conditions.Focus: Improves speed of thought and execution during transition moments, helping players react instinctively in attacking situations.

title: Argentina Up, Back & Through
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing drill focuses on developing “up, back, and through” combinations to promote effective central penetration. Players are arranged with one central player and two outer players on either side of the grid.The ball begins with one of the deeper players, who plays into the an outer player (“up”), receives a layoff pass back (“back”), and then plays a forward pass through the poles into the opposite outer player (“through”). This pattern continues side to side, encouraging rhythm and movement.The initial wide passes are used to simulate drawing pressure from imaginary defenders, creating space centrally for the penetrating “through” pass. Players rotate positions after a set number of repetitions to ensure varied practice.
coaching_notes: • Weight & Timing: Ensure passes are properly weighted and timed to maintain rhythm and simulate match intensity.• Scanning & Awareness: Players should check shoulders before receiving to replicate game-realistic pressure recognition.• Communication: Encourage verbal and non-verbal cues to keep the drill flowing and realistic.• Tempo: Maintain a quick tempo to replicate game speed and decision-making.
progression_one: One-Touch Combinations:Challenge players to complete the entire “up, back, through” sequence using one-touch passing.Focus: Develops speed of play, sharper decision-making, and first-touch quality under time constraints.

title: Athens 2v2 Transitions
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to simulate transitional moments and counter-attacking opportunities. It begins with 2 defenders starting on the goal line, passing the ball back and forth while moving forward toward a line positioned 30 yards out from the goal. This line is 3 yards deeper than the attackers’ starting line.Once the ball reaches and is stopped on this line, both defenders must sprint around a designated pole placed wide of them. At the same moment, 2 attackers positioned higher up are triggered to burst forward and initiate a 2v2 counter-attack. The aim is for the attackers to capitalize on the defenders being momentarily off-balance and out of position.
coaching_notes: • Defender Recovery Shape: Emphasize quick reaction and correct recovery angles after rounding the pole to re-establish defensive shape under pressure.• Attacking Mentality: Attackers should focus on quick, direct play—using explosive movement and combination play to exploit the brief overload.• Timing the Trigger: Reinforce the importance of the ball being fully stopped on the line before triggering the attackers, to replicate game-like cues.• Sharp Execution: Players should aim for clean passing and good weight on the final ball to beat the recovering defenders efficiently.• Decision-Making: Encourage attackers to make quick decisions—whether to shoot, combine, or isolate a defender—based on how the defense recovers.
progression_one: Add a Third Attacker:Introduce a third attacker from a deeper position who arrives late into the attack to create a 3v2 scenario, simulating a midfield runner.Focus: Develops awareness, off-the-ball movement, and improves support play during transitions.
progression_two: Limit Touches on the Attack:Restrict attackers to a maximum of three touches per player before shooting. This increases the urgency of play and challenges decision-making speed.Focus: Enhances quick attacking combinations, encourages early shots, and replicates high-pressure moments in real games.

title: Athens Build, Create & Finish SSG
instructions_setup: This small sided game is designed to improve build-up play, chance creation, and clinical finishing. The field is divided into three vertical zones: a build-up zone, a central creation zone, and a finishing zone. Both teams are overloaded in their respective build-up zones, creating numerical superiority to encourage composed progression from the back.Play begins in the build-up zone, where teams aim to advance the ball into the central creation zone. Once in this zone, teams can either play directly into the finishing zone or use one of the two wide players, who are locked into channels on either side, to deliver a cross or stretch the play.Players from the central creation zone are allowed to advance into the finishing zone to create a 3v3 situation and increase goal-scoring opportunities.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Patience: Encourage calm and controlled play in the build-up zone, utilizing the numerical advantage to draw out opponents and find gaps.• Wide Option Utilization: Players should be alert to the use of wide players, recognizing moments to stretch the defense or create cutback/crossing chances.• Timing of Runs: Attackers entering the finishing zone must time their runs well to meet crosses or exploit gaps in the defensive line.• Switch of Play: Teach players to recognize when a direct central pass is blocked and encourage quick switches to wide areas to open up new angles.• Third-Man Movement: Reinforce intelligent off-the-ball movement from central players to support attacks and exploit overloads in the final third.
progression_one: Add Recovery Defenders:Allow one defender from the build-up zone and one from the central zone to recover and help in the finishing zone once the ball progresses.Focus: Develops transitional defending and challenges the attacking team to score in more realistic, crowded scenarios.

title: Athens Building into Midfield
instructions_setup: The drill begins with a 4v2 rondo inside a rectangular grid. The goalkeeper is positioned along the bottom line of the grid to simulate their involvement in the build-up phase from the back. The 4 outfield players work the ball around the 2 pressing defenders with a focus on maintaining possession and playing quickly under pressure.After completing a set number of passes (e.g., 4-6 passes), the team in possession must attempt a line-breaking forward pass into one of the mini goals positioned at angles ahead of the grid. These angled mini goals simulate central midfielders receiving the ball between the lines.The focus is on clean ball circulation, timing of the penetrating pass, and recognizing the right moment to break pressure.
coaching_notes: • Goalkeeper Involvement: Encourage the goalkeeper to play short, sharp passes and support as a constant outlet to switch the angle of attack.• Body Position: Players should receive on the half-turn to stay open to forward options and allow quicker progression when the moment comes.• Line-Breaking Decision-Making: Emphasize scanning and recognizing the moment to split defenders with a sharp pass into the angled mini goals.• Tempo of Possession: Maintain a quick rhythm in the rondo to unbalance the defenders and draw them out of shape before executing the killer pass.• Disguise & Weight of Pass: Reinforce the use of disguised passes and the proper weight to ensure the receiving ‘midfielder’ can take clean control.
progression_one: Defensive Transition to Goal:If the 2 defenders win possession during the rondo, they are allowed to break out and attempt to score in the main goal within a limited number of seconds (e.g., 5–7 seconds). The possession team must immediately transition to defend.Focus: Adds urgency and realism to the drill by rewarding defensive pressure and promoting quick transition reactions from both teams.

title: Barcelona 3 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This is an unopposed finishing practice designed to develop combination play and movement across attacking positions. Players are divided into three stations: left wing, centre forward, and right wing.The drill begins with a finish from the centre forward, who receives a pass and shoots on goal. Immediately after shooting, the centre forward runs to the left wing station for phase two, where they combine with the left winger in a 1-2 passing sequence that ends with the left winger finishing on goal.In phase three, the centre forward then makes a long recovery run across to the right wing. There, they complete another 1-2 combination—this time with the right winger, who then delivers a cross into the box. The centre forward and left winger both attack the cross to complete the final phase of the finishing circuit.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Finish: Focus on clean, composed finishing in each phase. Players should be aiming for corners and adjusting their body shape for quick, controlled strikes.• Timing of Runs: Emphasize the importance of timing the run after the 1-2 passes and into the box during the crossing phase. Arriving too early or too late affects goal-scoring chances.• Movement Across Lines: The centre forward must demonstrate high work rate and intelligent movement between all three stations. This mirrors real match scenarios where strikers shift laterally.• Communication: Players should call for the ball during combinations and crosses, helping to organize runs and ensure clarity during each attacking phase.
progression_one: One-Touch Finish Requirement:Introduce a rule where players must finish with one touch on all shooting opportunities.Focus: Improves anticipation, positioning, and sharp execution under pressure.
progression_two: Passive Defenders in the Box:Add 1–2 passive defenders in the box for the final crossing phase to create pressure without going full-contact.Focus: Forces attacking players to time their movement more precisely and choose smarter finishing options while under light pressure.

title: Barcelona Build Up & Counter
instructions_setup: The drill begins with a 2v1 build-up phase, replicating two center-backs facing pressure from a lone center forward. Play starts from the goal kick area, with the two defenders tasked with maintaining possession and progressing the ball upfield. Their objective is to successfully combine and score into one of two centrally placed mini goals located approximately 40 yards from the goal line.As soon as the mini goal is scored into (or the attempt ends), the same two defenders immediately transition into a 3v2 attacking phase. A third player joins to support the counter attack, while two defenders recover and attempt to stop the transition. The two mini goals remain active, and play continues with realistic flow and transitions.If the defending pair win possession during the 3v2 phase, they’re allowed to counterattack themselves—creating a 2v3 situation going the other way, placing them at an attacking disadvantage but simulating a realistic turnover moment.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Detail: Reinforce clean decision-making and composure under pressure during the initial 2v1 phase. Defenders should create angles and commit the pressing forward before releasing the ball.• Body Shape in Transition: Players must adjust quickly after completing the first phase, ensuring they adopt positive body positioning to exploit space in the counterattack.• Movement Coordination: Emphasize timing and coordinated runs from the third attacker entering the 3v2 to support and overload efficiently.• Recovery Runs: Defenders in phase 2 should focus on delaying the attack and maintaining balance while underloaded.• Quick Play Post-Turnover: Allow the counter-attacking team to play freely after regaining possession to encourage natural attacking patterns.
progression_one: Add a Passive Midfielder:Introduce a passive midfielder between the 2v1 and 3v2 zones who can be bypassed or used to link play before the attack begins.Focus: Encourages scanning and decision-making around midfield traffic, simulating game-realistic central pressure.
progression_two: Limit Transition Time:Allow only 5 seconds for the 3v2 counter to be completed once the transition begins.Focus: Increases urgency and sharpens decision-making during fast-break scenarios.

title: Barcelona Continuous 3v3's
instructions_setup: his continuous 3v3 game is played within a rectangular area that matches the width of the penalty box and extends 15 additional yards in depth. One team begins as the attackers, aiming to break down the defense and score into the main goal. The defending team, meanwhile, is tasked with winning possession and countering quickly by scoring into one of the two mini goals placed at the opposite end.Play is continuous and competitive. If the attacking team scores, they remain attackers. If the defending team wins possession and scores in either of the mini goals, they rotate roles and become the new attacking side. This structure reinforces transitions, quick decision-making, and intensity in both attack and defense.
coaching_notes: • Transition Focus: Reinforce the importance of quick reaction upon winning or losing possession. Players should switch mindsets rapidly to either exploit space or recover defensively.• Compact Defending: Defenders must stay organized and compact to force play into predictable areas and increase chances of regaining the ball.• Positive First Touch: Encourage attackers to take their first touch forward when receiving to accelerate the tempo and drive at defenders.• Counterattacking Urgency: When possession is won, players should immediately look for quick outlets and exploit disorganized opponents with sharp movements toward the mini goals.• End Product Under Pressure: Emphasize calm and composed finishes in both goals, with attackers under pressure to be clinical and defenders needing to convert fast breaks.
progression_one: Add Central Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player in the central area who plays for the team in possession, creating overloads and giving both teams an extra outlet.Focus: Promotes creative play, support movement, and intelligent use of overloads to break down compact defenses.

title: Barcelona Developing Build Up
instructions_setup: In this build-up drill, teams play 4v4 centrally within a rectangular grid. Four bounce players are positioned in the four corners of the grid, each within their own square. The team in possession aims to progress the ball from one corner to the next, simulating build-up play and replicating principles of quick ball circulation and line breaking passes or dribbles.The team in possession always enjoys an overload, playing 8v4, with the four bounce players acting as outlets to help maintain possession and switch the play across the grid. The focus is on fluid ball movement and creating space to transition the ball efficiently from one side to the other.
coaching_notes: • Bounce Player Use: Encourage players to use the bounce players to change the angle of attack and unbalance the defending team. These players should always be available for a quick pass and act as safe outlets.• Tempo of Play: Emphasize quick, clean passing to move the ball across the grid efficiently. The aim is to stretch the defense and quickly exploit the spaces created by overloads.• Spacing and Positioning: Players in possession should maintain good width and depth to stretch the defending team and create passing lanes for the bounce players.• Awareness and Communication: The team in possession must communicate well to quickly transition the ball across the grid and recognize when to switch the play to unbalance the defenders.• Defensive Shape: The defending team should focus on staying compact and cutting off passing lanes to the bounce players while pressing quickly once possession is lost.
progression_one: Limit Touches for the Team in Possession:Limit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2 touches per player) to force faster ball circulation and encourage quicker decision-making.Focus: Enhances passing speed, movement off the ball, and quick decision-making under pressure.

title: Barcelona Finishing & Attacking
instructions_setup: The exercise begins with two attackers working unopposed to execute short combination plays around the edge of the penalty area, leading to two separate finishing attempts on goal. The focus during this phase is on timing, movement, and clinical execution in front of goal.Immediately after both finishing attempts, the two attackers must quickly transition into defenders as they are challenged by a wave of three new attackers in a 3v2 scenario. This phase emphasizes defensive organization under pressure, recovery runs, and communication.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, sharp passing and creative movement during the unopposed finishing phase.• In the 3v2 transition, highlight defensive principles such as delaying, pressing triggers, and covering space effectively.• Rotate players frequently to ensure everyone experiences multiple repetitions both as attackers and defenders. This promotes well-rounded development and keeps intensity high throughout the session.
progression_one: Add Passive Defenders in the Finishing Phase:Introduce one or two passive defenders in the initial combination/finishing phase.Their job is to provide light pressure and take away space without actively winning the ball.Focus: Helps attackers improve scanning, decision-making, and quality of execution under mild pressure.
progression_two: Add a Target Goal or Counter Option for Defenders:Give the two defenders a small target goal or a counter line they can break after winning the ball.If they intercept or regain possession, they must try to counter quickly and score/pass into the target.Focus: Transition from defense to attack, encouraging game-realistic behavior.

title: Barcelona Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness drill replicates a recovery run. The attacker and defender start in separate channels, positioned horizontally to each other. On the coach's whistle, both players sprint toward a mini goal, with the defender tasked with preventing the attacker from scoring.The defender must close the gap and apply pressure, aiming to stop the attacker from getting a shot off, while the attacker attempts to quickly reach the mini goal and finish under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Starting Position: Ensure both players start in an athletic stance, ready to explode out of the channels on the coach’s whistle. This prepares them for the sprint and mimics a real game situation.• Defensive Sprinting: The defender must focus on closing down the attacker quickly, maintaining a low center of gravity to change direction efficiently, and positioning themselves to block the shot.• Attacker's Sprint: The attacker should focus on explosive acceleration out of the starting position, using quick, sharp movements to get to the mini goal before the defender closes them down.• Recovery Movement: Encourage both players to react quickly and recover properly after each sprint to prepare for the next repetition. Emphasize the importance of speed and agility in defensive situations.• Mental Focus: Players should stay mentally sharp and aware, focusing on the timing of their run and the attacker’s intentions.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender in a 2v1 situation, making it more challenging for the attacker to get a shot off.Focus: Encourages the attacker to be more creative and sharp with their decision-making while increasing the defender's ability to close down the space quickly and communicate with a teammate.

title: Barcelona Overloaded SSG
instructions_setup: This is a fast-paced 4v4+4 small-sided game, where 4 neutral players are positioned on the outside of the grid. These neutral players are limited to 1 touch and are used as bounce players to create space and facilitate goal-scoring opportunities. There are 2 neutral players positioned on each end of the grid, one on either side of the goals.The game begins with both teams playing 4v4 in the central area, with the goal of scoring 2 goals. The team that scores 2 goals first wins the game. The losing team will rotate with the neutral outside players, and the drill continues with fresh teams.
coaching_notes: • Neutral Player Use: Encourage the central players to use the outside neutral players to create overloads and break the defensive shape of the opposition. The 1-touch rule for the neutrals helps the ball move quickly and increases tempo.• Positioning of Neutrals: Neutrals should always be in positions that are effective in progressing the ball quickly, particularly by providing wide passing options and angles. They need to be aware of when to move to receive and support attacking play.• Passing & Movement: The players in the middle should focus on quick passing and off-the-ball movement to utilize the neutral players effectively. This movement will open up passing lanes and create space to attack the goal.• Defensive Organization: Defenders should work to close down the space between the neutral players and the attackers, denying easy passes and forcing turnovers. Communication between defenders and midfielders is key in tracking the neutral players’ movement.
progression_one: Neutral Players Become Attackers:Allow the neutral players to score into the main goal, encouraging them to actively participate in the attacking phase.Focus: Increases attacking options and encourages the central players to look for opportunities to incorporate the neutral players in goal-scoring situations. This enhances team dynamics and promotes fluid attacking play.
progression_two: Limit Neutral Player Touches:Reduce the number of touches the neutral players can take (e.g., 1 touch per player), forcing the central players to make quicker decisions and improve their timing of passes.Focus: Enhances ball circulation and decision-making speed under pressure while improving team coordination between the central and outside players.

title: Barcelona Passing Activation
instructions_setup: In this unopposed passing practice, the focus is on line-breaking forward passes. The drill setup consists of 3 players positioned at the top of the grid and 3 players at the bottom. Mannequins are placed in the center of the grid to create obstacles and simulate defenders.Players will work on progressing the ball diagonally, making passes up and down the grid. Each pass will be a line-breaking pass, with the ball moving horizontally with each pass as the players follow the ball. The movement from side to side will help to replicate the idea of breaking lines and shifting play to different areas of the field.
coaching_notes: • Line-Breaking Passes: Focus on playing forward, line-breaking passes to unbalance the defense. Players should be aware of the available passing lanes and execute passes that break the opposition’s lines.• Passing & Movement: Players must follow their passes and move into space after they release the ball. This encourages continuous movement, quick ball circulation, and timing of runs.• Mannequin Awareness: The mannequins in the center of the grid serve as static defenders, encouraging players to identify and pass through the correct lanes. Players should scan for the best possible passing option before making their move.• Tempo & Timing: Emphasize a quick tempo in passing and movement to ensure the ball reaches the desired area before defenders can react. Precision in passing is key, as well as timing to break the defensive lines effectively.
progression_one: Increase Mannequin Obstacles:Add more mannequins in the central area to increase the difficulty of passing lanes. This will force players to make quicker, more precise line-breaking passes under increased pressure.Focus: Develops the ability to read the game under pressure and improves passing accuracy in tight spaces while dealing with more obstacles.
progression_two: Introduce Defenders:Introduce 1 or 2 passive defenders in the central area. Players will now need to break lines while considering the positioning of defenders, forcing them to make quicker and more dynamic decisions when choosing when to pass and where to move.Focus: Increases the game realism and sharpens players’ decision-making in a more competitive context, improving their ability to break lines while under pressure from real opponents.

title: Barcelona Positional Possession
instructions_setup: Play begins with a 6v5 scenario in the central area, where one team is tasked with maintaining possession while the other looks to win the ball. If the team of 5 wins possession, the outside players become live, increasing the game to an 11v6, with the team of 5 combining with the 6 outside players to form a larger attacking team.The 6 outside players are positioned to replicate a traditional formation, with players positioned as a goalkeeper, right back, left back, right winger, left winger, and center forward. The players in the central area are expected to rotate positions to retain and progress possession effectively, simulating real game scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Rotation & Positional Awareness: Players in the central area should rotate their positions regularly to maintain fluidity in possession. Encourage them to be aware of the spacing between them and their teammates to support quick passing and create options for progression.• Outside Player Use: The outside players must be used strategically to progress the ball, offering wide options and switching the play. Players should focus on switching the ball quickly and utilizing the space provided by the wide players.• Defensive Pressure: The team of 6 should focus on applying effective pressure to win the ball. Encourage defenders to stay compact while trying to limit the options of the attacking team, closing down players who are in possession.• Possession Retention: Encourage quick passing, movement off the ball, and staying composed under pressure to maintain possession. Players must be ready to exploit the space provided by the outside players and create opportunities in the final third.
progression_one: Limit Attacking Touches:Limit the number of touches for the attacking players (e.g., no more than two touches per player) to increase the tempo and force quicker decision-making.Focus: Increases the speed of play and improves decision-making under pressure, encouraging the players to play with greater tempo and efficiency.

title: Barcelona Receiving Between Lines
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing scanning and decision-making before receiving the ball. The player starts facing the coach, who will pass the ball to them. Just before receiving, the player must check their shoulder. The player behind them will hold up either a red or blue cone, indicating through which gate the player must receive the ball.Once the ball is received, the player must pass through the respective gate (red or blue) before playing a pass into one of the mini goals. This drill challenges players to scan, evade pressure, and make quick decisions while moving the ball efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Scanning & Awareness: Emphasize the importance of scanning before receiving the ball to assess options and anticipate pressure. Players should make it a habit to check their shoulder before the ball arrives.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Encourage players to make quick decisions based on the information gathered during their scan. They need to act decisively, choosing the correct gate and preparing their body to receive the ball.• Ball Control: Players should focus on receiving the ball cleanly and with the right weight to allow for a smooth progression into the next phase of play. They should be prepared to execute a quick pass into the mini goals after passing through the gate.• Pressure Evasion: When scanning, players need to identify where the pressure is coming from and use body positioning and touch to evade defenders. Encourage using feints or fakes to throw off the defender before receiving.
progression_one: Add Pressure from Behind:Introduce a defender who will start behind the player receiving the ball. This defender will try to apply pressure as the player checks their shoulder and receives the ball, forcing them to react under pressure.Focus: Develops the player's ability to evade pressure while receiving, reinforcing the importance of body shape and touch in tight situations.
progression_two: Change the Direction of the Pass:Instead of always playing the ball into the same mini goal, vary the target goals. Players must scan to identify the correct goal after evading pressure.Focus: Enhances decision-making and awareness under pressure, as players will need to assess which mini goal is the best target after receiving the ball and making a quick move.

title: Barcelona Rondo to Attack
instructions_setup: The drill begins with a 4v2 rondo in the center of the pitch, with 3 attackers positioned on mannequins in the Left Wing (LW), Centre Forward (CF), and Right Wing (RW) positions. The team in possession (4 players) must complete a set number of passes (e.g., 4-6) before playing a forward ball to combine with the attackers.Once the ball is played forward, the 3 attackers (LW, CF, RW) attempt to score in an unopposed scenario. The focus is on the attackers timing their movements to receive the ball in space and finishing efficiently once they receive possession.
coaching_notes: • Rondo Passing Focus: Encourage quick, sharp passing in the rondo to move the defenders out of position and create space for the forwards. Players must focus on maintaining possession and recognizing when the pass should be played forward.• Forward Movement: Attackers (LW, CF, RW) must time their runs to receive the ball in space, ensuring they’re unopposed when the pass arrives. Encourage dynamic movement and anticipation of the forward pass.• Combination Play: Once the ball is played forward, attackers should combine with the ball carrier to break down the defense. Emphasize quick, one- or two-touch play to maintain momentum and unbalance the defense.• Finishing: The attackers should focus on finishing with composure, using different types of shots (e.g., driven, placed) based on the situation, and ensuring they are calm in front of goal.
progression_one: Introduce a Pressing Defender:After the initial pass forward, introduce one defender to apply light pressure on the attackers, forcing them to make quicker decisions under pressure.Focus: Develops the attackers' ability to finish under pressure and make fast decisions when combining with teammates.
progression_two: Limit Touches for the Attackers:Limit the number of touches the attackers can take when receiving the ball (e.g., no more than two touches). This forces quicker decision-making and improves the speed of play.Focus: Encourages attackers to play faster, making quicker passes and decisions while under pressure to execute combination play and finish efficiently.

title: Barcelona Technical & Transition
instructions_setup: The drill starts with a pass into a central player positioned at the top of the grid. The central player must receive the ball on the correct angle (e.g., receiving on the half-turn) before playing a forward pass into the mini goal.As soon as the central player takes their first touch, an attacker (starting at the bottom of the grid) begins running towards the second mini goal to receive the pass. The central player must then transition quickly after completing their pass to attempt to recover and stop the attacker from scoring in the mini goal.
coaching_notes: • Receiving on the Correct Angle: Ensure the central player receives the ball with the correct body position, enabling them to easily play a forward pass. Encourage players to always scan before receiving to identify potential passing lanes.• Timing of the Forward Pass: The player receiving the ball should quickly recognize the right moment to play a forward pass into the mini goal. Timing and weight of the pass are crucial for enabling the attacker to get a clean shot on goal.• Attacker's Timing & Movement: The attacker should time their run perfectly to meet the forward pass and finish under minimal pressure. The attacker must focus on keeping the run straight and explosive.• Defensive Transition: After making the forward pass, the central player must transition quickly into a defensive position to prevent the attacker from scoring in the mini goal. The focus is on recovering and applying defensive pressure in a timely manner.
progression_one: Add Extra Attacker:Introduce an additional attacker (e.g., 2 attackers) making runs toward the mini goal, creating a 2v1 situation against the recovering defender.Focus: Improves decision-making and defensive awareness when outnumbered, while also encouraging attackers to exploit overloads for better chances on goal.

title: Barcelona Tic Tac Toe Warm Up
instructions_setup: This high-energy warm-up involves two teams racing toward a large 9-square grid (3x3 setup) to play a game of tic-tac-toe using cones. Each team has three cones and must sprint from a designated starting point to place their cone in a square one at a time.Once all three cones are placed, players must continue sprinting to the grid to reposition their cones—one at a time—to try and form a line of three. The first team to create a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line wins the round.This warm-up encourages sharp thinking, explosive speed, and quick direction changes while building competitiveness and energy for the session ahead.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Starts: Emphasize quick acceleration off the mark. Players should react fast to the coach’s signal and focus on powerful first steps.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Encourage players to make smart, fast decisions about where to place or move cones, simulating in-game thinking speed.• Change of Direction: Reinforce efficient turning techniques and body control when transitioning between runs to and from the grid.• Team Communication: Promote verbal coordination between teammates to avoid overlapping moves and optimize cone positioning.• Competitiveness: Use the warm-up as an energy booster by emphasizing competition and intensity to get players mentally engaged.
progression_one: Reactive Start:Instead of starting on command, players begin in various reactive positions (lying down, facing away, or reacting to a clap or ball drop) before sprinting.Focus: Improves reaction speed and replicates unpredictable moments in a match environment.
progression_two: Add Ball Carrying:Players must dribble a ball to the grid before placing or adjusting a cone, then sprint back.Focus: Adds technical ball control to the physical and cognitive elements, reinforcing multitasking and composure under fatigue.

title: Bayern 2v2 & Double 1v1's
instructions_setup: This drill involves 3 live balls at all times, creating a dynamic and fast-paced environment. In the central zone, players will play a 2v2 attacking/defending scenario in an area the width of the penalty area, aiming to score in the larger central goal.In the 2 wider zones (full-back areas), players will engage in 1v1 situations, with the player in possession attempting to score into a mini goal.After each phase, the players from the 2 wider zones will move centrally to form the next 2v2, while the 2 players who were involved in the 2v2 now transition to the wider zones to play their 1v1s.
coaching_notes: • Dynamic Transitions: Encourage players to transition quickly between phases. The ability to shift from central play to wide play (and vice versa) will help improve their versatility and adaptability during matches.• 1v1 in Wide Areas: Focus on 1v1 defending techniques in the wider zones, encouraging defenders to show attackers down the line and apply pressure to win possession. For attackers, stress the importance of quick, decisive movements to beat their defender.• 2v2 in Central Zone: The 2v2 in the central zone should focus on communication, quick combinations, and exploiting overloads. Encourage attackers to play off each other, creating space and angles to break down the defense.• Finishing: Stress accuracy and composure when finishing, both in the central 2v2 and the 1v1 wide areas. Attackers should focus on shooting with precision, while defenders must work on closing down angles and preventing the shot.
progression_one: Add Neutral Player in the Central Zone:Introduce a neutral player in the central zone to create a 3v2 attacking advantage. The neutral player will always play for the team in possession.Focus: Enhances decision-making in overload situations, improves attacking combinations, and tests defensive positioning when outnumbered.
progression_two: Add a Second Attacker in the Wider Zones:Introduce a second defender in each of the 1v1 wide areas, turning it into a 2v1 scenario for the attacking player.Focus: Increases defensive pressure and encourages attackers to develop quick, effective decision-making when faced with double-team situations.

title: Bayern 2v2 Pressing
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing pressing and protecting forward passes. Players will pass the ball back and forth, while the pressing players are tasked with using the press and cover concept to prevent any of the 2 players in possession from breaking lines.Once a pass is made across the grid, the team that passed the ball must transition quickly and become the new pressing duo. The two pressing players must adopt a press-and-cover approach, moving in tandem to ensure they cover passing options and deny space. Importantly, the pressing players are not aiming to win the ball directly but are working on shadow play to develop their understanding of when and how to press effectively.
coaching_notes: • Press and Cover Concept: Encourage the pressing players to maintain a compact shape, with one player applying pressure to the ball while the other covers passing lanes. The covering player should ensure they remain in a position to intercept or block any potential forward passes.• Angle of Pressing: Emphasize the importance of the angle at which the pressing player approaches the ball. The pressing player should always angle their body in a way that forces the ball carrier into the cover player, preventing easy line breaks.• Communication: Players should communicate constantly, especially when transitioning from defending to pressing. Clear verbal cues and non-verbal signals (like hand gestures) will help improve coordination and prevent the attackers from exploiting any gaps.• Transition Speed: Stress the need for quick transitions between attacking and defending. As soon as the ball is passed, the team must quickly shift their mentality to pressing, ensuring there are no delays in the movement.• Pressing Without Winning the Ball: Reinforce the idea that the pressing players are not looking to win the ball immediately but to disrupt the offensive flow and force mistakes. The focus should be on positioning, timing, and working together to limit the attacking options.
progression_one: Pressing Team Wins the Ball to Score:Now allow the pressing team to score if they win possession. They can immediately transition and attack the goal or mini goal located on one end of the grid.Focus: Encourages the pressing team to not only disrupt possession but also to capitalize on their successful defensive actions by transitioning quickly into attack.

title: Bayern Corner Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed corner routine drill is designed to help players learn various corner delivery techniques and movements to create goal-scoring opportunities. The team will practice their set-piece routine with a focus on timing, spacing, and coordination. Players will position themselves according to the chosen routine (e.g., near post, far post, edge of the box, etc.) and work to execute the set play under minimal pressure.The corner taker will deliver the ball into the designated area, while the other players make runs to attack the ball or create space. The focus is on smooth, well-timed movements and effective ball delivery. The drill is unopposed, allowing the attacking team to concentrate on executing their routine to perfection.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Ensure that attacking players time their runs to the ball correctly. Whether it’s attacking the near post, far post, or edge of the box, the players should be well-timed in their movements to meet the delivery.• Movement to Create Space: Players should work on off-the-ball movement to pull defenders out of position, making it easier for teammates to get a clear shot at goal. Movement should be quick and dynamic, with players changing direction to create space in key areas.• Delivery Quality: Emphasize the importance of delivering the ball with the correct weight, pace, and accuracy. The corner taker must consistently place the ball into the designated area, whether it’s a driven cross, floated ball, or short corner.• Target Areas: Players should understand where to attack based on the type of delivery (e.g., near post, far post, or central). Each player should be aware of their role in relation to the ball's flight path and their teammates’ movements.• Communication: Encourage clear communication between the corner taker and attacking players. This ensures everyone knows when to make their run and where the ball will be delivered.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to lightly pressurize the attackers during the delivery and movement. The defenders should focus on tracking runs and challenging for the ball but not actively blocking or winning it.Focus: Develops the ability to execute corner routines while under light pressure, simulating more realistic game situations and forcing players to adjust their timing and runs.

title: Bayern Counter Press Rondo
instructions_setup: Play begins with 6 players in possession, attempting to retain the ball against 3 defenders in a defined area. The attacking team (6 players) works on maintaining possession through quick, short passes and movement. If the defending team (3 players) wins possession, they transition quickly and attempt to score in one of the 2 mini goals placed on either side of the grid.When possession is lost, the outside players from the team that was previously in possession must immediately counter-press, applying pressure to the defenders and attempting to regain the ball before the defenders can score. The goal of this practice is to develop the players' counter-pressing skills and improve their ability to react quickly after losing possession.
coaching_notes: • Counter-Pressing Immediately After Losing Possession: As soon as the attacking team loses possession, emphasize the importance of the outside players quickly transitioning into a counter-pressing role. They should move quickly to close down space and apply pressure to the ball carrier to regain possession.• Defensive Awareness: The 3 defenders must be sharp in recognizing when they win the ball and take advantage of the opportunity to score in the mini goals. Quick transitions to attack are crucial to exploit the unbalanced attacking team.• Shape and Compactness: Encourage the players to keep their shape, both in possession and during the counter-pressing phase. The defending team should work together to close off passing lanes and force the attackers into tight spaces, while the counter-pressing players should cover key areas quickly.• Quick Decision-Making: The players on the outside need to quickly assess the situation when possession is lost, deciding whether to press the ball or cover space. Quick decision-making in these moments is essential for effective counter-pressing.• Communication: Strong verbal communication is vital. The defending team and counter-pressing players need to be vocal, guiding each other through the press and ensuring no spaces are left open for the attackers to exploit.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Increase the number of defenders to 4, making it more challenging for the attacking team to retain possession. The defensive team should be rewarded for regaining possession and scoring in the mini goals.Focus: Develops defensive organization and the ability to regain possession under increased pressure, reinforcing the importance of counter-pressing after losing possession.
progression_two: Limit Attacking Touches:Limit the attacking players to a certain number of touches (e.g., 2 touches per player), forcing them to move the ball quicker and creating a more dynamic counter-pressing situation.Focus: Encourages quicker ball circulation from the attacking team, forcing the defending team to apply pressure more rapidly and transition effectively during the counter-pressing phase.

title: Bayern Counter with Recoveries
instructions_setup: Play begins with a pass from one of the 3 attacking players, who are positioned 15 yards outside the penalty area, into the 4th attacking player positioned on the edge of the penalty area. As soon as the initial pass is made, a 4v1 scenario is created, with 3 recovering defenders attempting to prevent a counter-attack and make it a 4v4 situation.The 3 defenders start 3 yards behind the attacking players and must work to recover quickly, covering key passing lanes and denying the attacking team the opportunity to finish. The attacking team looks to break the defensive lines and exploit the space, while the defenders are tasked with closing down the attacking players and creating numerical equality as quickly as possible.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition to Counter-Attack: The attacking team should immediately look to take advantage of the space and try to create an opportunity on goal. Emphasize the need for quick, decisive passing and movement to break the defensive line before the defenders can recover.• Defensive Recovery: The 3 defenders must quickly recover ground and communicate with each other to make it a 4v4 scenario. Their goal is to deny space to the attacking players and prevent them from getting a shot on goal. Focus on positioning, anticipation, and timing of recovery runs.• Speed and Timing of the Pass: The initial pass into the attacking player on the edge of the penalty area should be weighted properly, giving the receiving player the best chance to control the ball and progress forward. Timing is crucial to ensure the defenders can't get in front of the pass.• Defender Positioning: Defenders should aim to position themselves in a way that forces the attacking team into tighter areas, using their numbers to apply pressure. The recovering defenders must quickly close the gaps and work to create an overload, taking advantage of the numerical advantage once the ball is played to them.• Finishing Under Pressure: The attacking players must be composed in front of goal, focusing on finishing quickly and accurately under pressure from the defenders.
progression_one: 4v2 Attack with 3 Recovering Defenders:Start with 2 defenders positioned deeper in the defensive zone, creating a 4v2 attack for the attacking team. As the attacking team attempts to break forward, the 3 other defenders start recovering from a deeper position to make it a 4v5 scenario.Focus: Enhances attacking team’s ability to break down a defense with numerical superiority initially, while improving the defending team’s ability to recover and regain control under pressure.

title: Bayern Dribbling Square
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery and awareness drill, two players work within or around a square grid—one designated as the runner and the other as the chaser. The runner starts with the ball and attempts to evade the chaser, who must try to tag them while both players remain on the move.The runner can dribble freely in any direction around the square, while the chaser works to apply constant pressure. Both players are encouraged to scan frequently and react quickly to changes in movement. This creates a dynamic game-like situation that challenges both awareness and technical ball control under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Scanning & Awareness: Reinforce the importance of players scanning their surroundings constantly to anticipate changes in the chaser’s position.• Body Orientation: Encourage players to stay side-on and low to the ground to maximize balance and agility during changes of direction.• Ball Protection: The runner should use their body to shield the ball and utilize quick touches to change direction under pressure.• Chaser Footwork: The chaser should focus on quick, balanced footwork and closing down angles to cut off the runner’s escape routes.• Decision Making: Praise players for using feints, changes of pace, and misdirection to outsmart their opponent.
progression_one: Time Limit Challenge:Introduce a 10-second time limit for the runner to evade the chaser. If the chaser hasn't tagged the runner in that time, the runner scores a point.Focus: Increases intensity and urgency for both players, encouraging sharper movement and quicker decision-making.

title: Bayern Finishing from Knockdowns
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill begins with a central player playing a pass out wide to a winger. The winger receives the ball, cuts inside onto their stronger foot, and delivers a floated cross toward the back zone of the penalty area.Two attackers make timed runs into the box—one attacks the back zone to meet the cross and provide a knockdown, while the second attacker arrives centrally to finish first-time off the knockdown.Play alternates from both wings, and players should rotate through each role to ensure repetition of various attacking movements and finishing techniques.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Run: Emphasize the importance of the first attacker timing their arrival to meet the cross in stride without overrunning the ball.• Communication: Attackers should call for the knockdown and clearly signal where they want the ball delivered.• Winger’s Delivery: Focus on quality of the cross—encouraging floated deliveries into the back zone with enough hang time for attackers to adjust.• Finishing Technique: The second attacker should stay composed, adjusting body position to strike cleanly off the knockdown.
progression_one: Passive Defender on the Knockdown:Introduce a passive defender between the two attackers to simulate interference and force more accurate knockdowns and quick finishes.Focus: Sharpens decision-making and spatial awareness in tight areas under light pressure.
progression_two: Live Defender on the Cross:Add a live recovering defender who starts next to the winger and attempts to block or pressure the delivery.Focus: Replicates more game-realistic pressure on the cross and tests attackers’ ability to adapt their runs and finish under pressure.

title: Bayern One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 finishing drill helps players improve their first touch, awareness, and ability to finish quickly under changing conditions. The coach plays a pass to the player positioned just outside the penalty area. As the ball travels, the coach calls out one of three colour-coded gates. The player must take their first touch through the correct gate before finishing on goal, simulating real-time decision-making based on visual and verbal cues.
coaching_notes: • React Quickly to the Colour Cue From the Coach – Train your mind to instantly process instructions and adjust your body shape mid-movement.• Take a Purposeful First Touch Toward the Correct Gate – Drive the ball firmly but under control through the correct channel to set up the finish.• Adjust Body Angle to Finish From Varying Distances – Control your hips and feet positioning to strike cleanly from multiple angles after each gate.• Scan Early and Stay Balanced When Receiving – Prepare your body before the pass arrives to take clean, composed touches under pressure.
progression_one: Vary the Speed and Type of Coach PassUse slower passes, fast rollers, or slight bouncers to force players to adapt their receiving technique and timing before finishing.Focus:Improves touch control, finishing consistency, and adaptability under unpredictable delivery types.
progression_two: Introduce a Passive Defender Behind the GatesAdd a passive defender who shadows the gates after the coach’s call, increasing pressure and limiting space for execution.Focus:Develops composure, timing of touches, and the ability to make decisions in dynamic scenarios.

title: Bayern Overload & Wide Cross
instructions_setup: This two-phase attacking drill is designed to work on creating and finishing in overloaded situations. It begins with 2 defenders playing a pass into 3 attackers, triggering a 3v2 attacking phase toward goal. The attackers must use the overload to combine quickly and create a goalscoring opportunity.Once the first phase is complete, play immediately transitions into phase two. Two players in wide channels combine to deliver a cross into the box. At this point, a second 3v2 scenario becomes live inside the penalty area, with the same attacking trio aiming to convert the cross under pressure from the defenders.The drill promotes sharp attacking movement, intelligent positioning, and clinical finishing from different service types.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Play: Encourage attackers to exploit the overload quickly before the defenders can recover or delay.• Positioning in the Box: Attackers must time their runs into the box to avoid being static when the cross is delivered.• Variety of Combinations: Promote the use of wall passes, overlaps, and quick give-and-go's during both phases.• Wide Player Delivery: Crosses should vary—driven, floated, or cut-back—based on defender positioning and attacker runs.• Defensive Body Shape: Defenders should stay compact but ready to engage—encouraging attackers to be sharp in decision-making.
progression_one: Add a Recovering Defender:After the initial 3v2 phase begins, allow one recovering defender to join from behind the play, increasing defensive pressure and testing attackers’ decision-making.Focus: Enhances realism and encourages quicker, more decisive actions in overload scenarios.
progression_two: Aerial Finish Requirement:For the second phase, require at least one attacker to attempt an aerial finish from the cross.Focus: Trains timing, body control, and attacking headers or volleys from wide service under pressure.

title: Bayern Pass & Receiving
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing and receiving drill is designed to develop turning under pressure, awareness, and quick decision-making. Four players are positioned on the outside of a square grid, with one player working inside the central box. Two of the outside players start with a ball.Play begins with one ball being passed into the central player, who must check their shoulder, receive, turn, and play to another outside player. They then follow their pass and switch roles. The outside player who made the initial pass then enters the central box to repeat the process with the second ball, which has been played in from the opposite side.This creates a continuous flow, with two balls constantly in motion and players rotating in and out of the central box.
coaching_notes: • Scanning: Players must check their shoulder before receiving to create space and make better decisions.• Body Shape: Encourage players to receive on the half-turn to open up their options and keep the play moving fluidly.• Pass Timing & Weight: Emphasize well-timed, crisp passes that allow for quick turns and smooth transitions.• Communication: Players must constantly communicate to ensure clarity in movement and role switching.• Tempo: Keep intensity high to simulate match speed and demand constant alertness.
progression_one: One-Touch Requirement:Require players to play their pass out of the grid using one touch after receiving, if the body position and pass allow.Focus: Enhances quick decision-making, movement preparation, and first-touch quality.

title: Bayern SAQ & Warm Up
instructions_setup: This SAQ (Speed, Agility, Quickness) warm-up involves four players starting from different corners of a square grid. On the coach’s signal, all players sprint towards the center of the grid simultaneously.Once they reach the middle, the coach calls out either “clockwise” or “anti-clockwise,” prompting the players to quickly shuffle or sprint around the grid in that direction. At any moment, the coach can blow the whistle, signaling all players to return to their original starting positions as quickly as possible.This drill promotes reaction speed, coordination, and directional awareness.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Movement: Encourage players to stay light on their feet and use quick, short steps when changing direction.• Head Up: Players must keep their eyes on the coach at all times to react instantly to directional cues and the whistle.• Explosive First Step: Emphasize an aggressive first step both when moving toward the center and when returning to start.• Body Control: Focus on balance and control when rotating to avoid slipping or over-committing.• Communication: Optionally, have players call out the direction or their start position to keep mental focus sharp.
progression_one: Ball Carry:Each player carries a ball during the drill. When the whistle blows, they must dribble the ball back to their starting position.Focus: Enhances technical control under physical fatigue and directional changes.
progression_two: Competition Element:Make the return a race—first player back to their cone earns a point. Rotate starting cones after each round.Focus: Adds urgency, competition, and fun while sharpening reaction time.

title: Beijing 3rd Man Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up focuses on developing third-man combinations through repeated passing patterns that emphasise timing, accuracy and movement. Players work through a structured third-man action, where the ball is played through a supporting player before the third runner receives and finishes by passing into a mini goal. The emphasis is on clean execution, correct body shape and efficient ball circulation.The practice is mirrored across three identical areas, allowing multiple teams of four or more players to work simultaneously. Teams compete to complete the third-man pattern and score first, creating a race scenario that challenges players to balance technical precision with speed of execution. This competitive element increases intensity while maintaining a strong technical focus suitable for a session warm-up.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Third-Man Run:Emphasise the third player moving at the correct moment to receive on the move without disrupting rhythm, spacing or overall passing flow.• Weight and Accuracy of Pass:Encourage crisp, well-weighted passes that allow teammates to play forward smoothly, maintain tempo and execute the next action cleanly.• Body Shape to Play Forward:Coach players to receive side-on and open their body early to execute the third-man action efficiently with minimal touches.• Composure Under Competition:Reinforce staying calm, technically clean and focused despite competitive pressure, time constraints and the presence of racing teams.
progression_one: Two-Touch Maximum Throughout:Limit all players to two touches for every action, increasing speed, technical demand and decision-making pressure.Focus:Improves first-touch quality, passing accuracy and execution of third-man combinations under time constraints.
progression_two: Weaker-Foot Finish Into Mini Goal:Require the final pass or finish into the mini goal to be played using the weaker foot.Focus:Develops technical balance, confidence on both feet and accuracy when executing at speed and under pressure.

title: Beijing Attack Central & Counter
instructions_setup: This attacking and counter-attacking practice begins with a 4v3 inside a central grid positioned around the halfway line. The attacking team of four aims to combine effectively, exploit central spaces and create a scoring opportunity against the three defenders and the goalkeeper. The focus in this phase is on quick circulation, movement between lines and decisive actions in tight areas.If the defending team of three win possession, the practice immediately transitions into a counter-attacking phase. The defenders can break forward into a large open area between the halfway line and the main penalty box, attacking at speed and attempting to score. This creates a strong contrast between compact central attacking play and expansive counter-attacking moments, challenging both attacking and defensive transition behaviours.
coaching_notes: • Central Combination Quality:Encourage attackers to use quick, sharp combinations centrally to break defensive lines and create shooting opportunities.• Speed of Decision-Making:Reinforce recognising when to play one-touch, when to carry and when to finish under pressure.• Reaction on Turnover:Coach attackers to react instantly on loss, delaying the counter and protecting central spaces immediately.• Exploiting Space on the Counter:Emphasise direct running, positive first touches and early forward passes when counter-attacking into space.
progression_one: Touch Limit in the Central Grid:Apply a two- or three-touch limit in the central attacking phase to increase tempo and technical demand.Focus:Improves speed of play, sharper combinations and faster decision-making in congested central areas.
progression_two: Add a Recovering Defender:Allow one attacker to recover and defend during the counter-attacking phase after a short delay.Focus:Adds realism, challenges counter-attacking efficiency and improves defensive recovery and transition behaviour.

title: Beijing Attacking Transitions
instructions_setup: This attacking and counter-attacking practice begins with a 4v3 inside a central grid positioned around the halfway line. The attacking team of four aims to combine effectively, exploit central spaces and create a scoring opportunity against the three defenders and the goalkeeper. The focus in this phase is on quick circulation, movement between lines and decisive actions in tight areas.If the defending team of three win possession, the practice immediately transitions into a counter-attacking phase. The defenders can break forward into a large open area between the halfway line and the main penalty box, attacking at speed and attempting to score. This creates a strong contrast between compact central attacking play and expansive counter-attacking moments, challenging both attacking and defensive transition behaviours.
coaching_notes: • Composure in the 1v0 Finish:Encourage calm body shape, controlled touches and confident finishing despite the simplicity of the opening phase.• Immediate Transition Reaction:Reinforce instant mindset change from attacker to defender, reacting quickly and recovering with intensity and purpose.• Defending the 2v1:Coach the recovering defender to delay, protect central space and force attackers into predictable wide decisions.• Exploiting the Final Overload:Emphasise quick combinations, purposeful movement and decisive finishing to take advantage of the 3v2 situation.
progression_one: Time Limit on Each Phase:Introduce strict time limits for each attacking phase to increase tempo and reduce unnecessary delays.Focus:Improves attacking urgency, transition speed and execution under realistic time and fatigue pressure.

title: Beijing Breakout Rondo
instructions_setup: This breakout rondo begins with a 5v2 inside a central grid, where the possession team looks to circulate the ball with control and composure under pressure. The two defenders work together to screen passing lanes, press intelligently and force mistakes while the five focus on quick support, angles and ball speed.If the two defenders win possession, they immediately break out by playing to any of their six teammates positioned around the outside, triggering a transition into an 8v5 possession phase. The new possession team must manage the overload and retain control, while the team of five counter-presses to regain the ball. If the five win possession again, they can score into any of the four mini goals located on the outside of the grid, rewarding aggressive counter-pressing and rapid attacking intent.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Initial Possession:Encourage the five to circulate with purpose, maintain strong support angles, vary passing lanes and avoid forcing risky central passes under pressure.• Breakout Decision-Making:Coach defenders to recognise the moment to play forward quickly on regain, selecting the best outside option with speed and clarity.• Counter-Pressing Intensity:Reinforce immediate reaction from the five on loss, closing space aggressively, protecting central areas and forcing rushed decisions.• Managing the Overload:Emphasise calm ball circulation, constant scanning, patience and intelligent spacing from the eight to unbalance the pressing unit.
progression_one: Two-Touch Limit After Breakout:Apply a two-touch maximum for the 8v5 phase to increase tempo, raise technical demands and reduce dwelling on the ball.Focus:Improves first-touch quality, faster decision-making and cleaner circulation under numerical-advantage pressure and fatigue.
progression_two: Time-Limited Scoring Window for the Five:Give the five a short time window to score into mini goals after regaining possession.Focus:Encourages explosive counter-pressing reactions, quicker attacking actions and decisive end-product execution under realistic transition pressure.

title: Beijing Technical Triangle
instructions_setup: This technical passing warm-up focuses on developing third-man combinations within a simple triangular passing structure. Players circulate the ball with purpose, using supporting movements and well-timed runs to create third-man actions that allow play to continue fluidly. The emphasis is on clean technique, awareness of teammates and efficient movement to maintain rhythm.The practice encourages players to receive, pass and move continuously, following their actions to rotate positions and create new passing angles. By keeping the structure simple and unopposed, players can concentrate on first-touch quality, body shape and timing, making it an effective activation exercise before more complex game-based practices.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Third-Man Movement:Emphasise supporting players moving at the correct moment to receive on the move without slowing ball circulation.• Body Shape to Play Forward:Encourage players to receive side-on with an open body shape to see multiple passing options early.• Weight and Detail of Pass:Reinforce crisp, accurate passes that allow the next action to be played smoothly at tempo.• Movement After the Pass:Coach players to follow their pass with intent, rotate positions quickly and maintain constant passing angles.
progression_one: Coach Call to Change Direction:On the coach’s shout or signal, players must immediately change the direction of the passing pattern and reorganise the third-man combination.Focus:Improves scanning, communication, adaptability and speed of decision-making when patterns are disrupted unexpectedly.

title: Belgium Arriving Late SSG
instructions_setup: The game begins as a 4v4(+1) possession-based phase inside a central grid, with one neutral player acting as a floater to maintain tempo and overloads. Teams aim to complete a set number of consecutive passes (e.g., 5–6) before they are allowed to play out to one of the four wide players positioned on each side of the grid.Once the ball is played to a wide player, two attacking players can make late, timed runs into the box. At the same time, two designated defenders must recover quickly to apply pressure and prevent the goal, turning the practice into a live finishing scenario.
coaching_notes: • Patience in Possession: Encourage calm, composed play in the central zone to bait defenders and create openings.• Movement to Support: Players should constantly rotate and create angles to support the ball carrier and keep the possession fluid.• Late Runs: Highlight the importance of timing and delayed movements into the box to arrive unmarked and finish with quality.• Recovery Runs: Defenders must transition quickly from passive to active, focusing on recovering body shape and applying pressure.• Wide Player Awareness: Wide players must scan early to assess delivery options and execute quality final balls.
progression_one: Add a Target Goal for Central Possession:Instead of immediately playing wide after completing passes, teams must play a penetrating pass into a small central goal first before switching play.Focus: Reinforces the value of forward-thinking passes and adds variety to the build-up phase.

title: Belgium Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: The drill involves four players working at the same time in a continuous rotation. Each player starts by dribbling to and around the cone directly ahead of them. After completing the dribble, they must then pass the ball into the next player in line. The process repeats with players constantly moving and passing.The coach can vary the cones the players must initially dribble around and may also dictate which direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise) the players should work in, creating variation and challenge.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Control: Encourage players to keep close control while dribbling and focus on quick touches around the cone to maintain rhythm.• Passing Quality: Stress the importance of clean, accurate passing to the next player while maintaining good posture and balance.• Decision Making: Players should be aware of the situation ahead, using feints or changes of direction to improve their dribbling and engage the cone at the correct angle.• Body Shape: As players approach the cone, they should position their body to shield the ball, ensuring they can change direction quickly.
progression_one: Change of Direction Challenge:Players must now dribble to a cone, stop, and then change direction to complete the pass to the next player.Focus: Focuses on improving quick direction changes, agility, and turning under control.

title: Belgium Finishing from Wide
instructions_setup: In this unopposed attacking pattern and finishing drill, players are set up across five stations: two central midfielders (CM) and three attackers (left winger (LW), center forward (CF), and right winger (RW)).The drill begins with the players completing a series of predefined passing routines, focusing on movement, timing, and ball circulation. The attackers will then work in tandem with the central midfielders, receiving passes, and executing specific movements to create goal-scoring opportunities.The drill ends with a cross from either the left or right winger, followed by a finish from the center forward. Mannequins are strategically placed to help attackers visualize and anticipate the spaces they will need to play in during the game.
coaching_notes: • Movement Off the Ball: Encourage attackers to make dynamic runs, creating space for themselves and their teammates. The center forward should be aware of the angles of runs made by the wingers and adjust accordingly to receive the ball in dangerous positions.• Timing of Passes: Focus on the timing of the passes, ensuring that the ball is played to the feet or into space based on the run made by the attacker. Central midfielders must demonstrate good vision and awareness to play the correct pass.• Mannequin Use: The mannequins should be treated as defenders. Players must work on reading the space around the mannequins and making runs to avoid being blocked or closed down.• Finishing Technique: When finishing, encourage attackers to use the correct technique (inside foot for placement, laces for power), and focus on shooting quickly and accurately, especially when receiving crosses.• Communication: Communication between the wingers, center forward, and central midfielders is key to executing the passing routine smoothly and ensuring everyone is aware of their role in the pattern.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure:Introduce passive defenders in the central midfield or wide areas. The defenders will apply light pressure to force players to make quicker decisions and execute the passing patterns under slightly more challenging conditions.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and sharper ball control when under pressure.
progression_two: 2 Players Attacking the Box:When the left winger crosses from the left side, the right winger should now make a run to attack the back post, making it a two-player attacking presence in the box. This creates more options for the center forward, increasing the chances of a goal-scoring opportunity.Focus: Increases attacking options in the box, encouraging attackers to support each other and attack the cross from multiple angles.

title: Belgium Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: Players will sprint to and from the central cones, with the distance increasing on each rep. The drill starts with players jogging in the lead-up to the sprint zone and also after the sprint zone, ensuring they maintain a steady pace and control throughout.
coaching_notes: • Pacing: Encourage players to jog at a controlled pace before each sprint to ensure they can sustain the effort throughout the drill.• Sprinting Form: Focus on proper sprinting technique, with emphasis on arm movement, posture, and a quick turnover of legs.• Breathing Control: Remind players to control their breathing, especially as the distances increase with each rep, to ensure they maintain energy.• Recovery Phase: Ensure players understand the importance of recovery during the jogging phase to prepare for the next sprint.
progression_one: Add a Change of Direction:In each sprint, add a small change of direction at one of the cones (e.g., a quick pivot or 90-degree turn) before resuming the sprint. This simulates real-game situations where players often need to accelerate in different directions.Focus: Improves agility, change of direction, and acceleration.
progression_two: Sprint Backwards:For the final rep, players must sprint backwards to the central cone, and then jog back to their starting position.Focus: Develops overall speed and coordination while engaging different muscle groups in the sprint.

title: Belgium Penetration Patterns
instructions_setup: Play starts with 1 player positioned centrally, with 2 players on the outer central line (acting as wingers) and 4 mannequins or poles placed on the central line. The deeper central player serves as the starting point.The drill begins with a pass made from a deeper central position into the central player. This player then combines with the deeper player before playing a penetrative through ball between the mannequins or poles, allowing one of the outer wide players to run onto the ball. The play then mirrors with the higher central player, creating a back-and-forth flow from top to bottom.
coaching_notes: • Ball Movement: Emphasize quick and accurate passing to move the ball efficiently from one side to the other.• Timing of Runs: The wide players should time their runs perfectly to ensure they meet the through ball at the correct moment.• Through Ball Technique: Players must focus on playing a clean and weighted through ball that allows the wide player to continue their run without losing momentum.• Combination Play: Encourage fluid combinations between the central players to manipulate the defensive lines and open up passing lanes.• Scanning: The central player must always scan to recognize when to play the penetrating pass or make the combination.
progression_one: Increase the Pressure:Introduce 1 or 2 defenders in the central area who are tasked with putting pressure on the central players, forcing them to play quicker and under pressure.Focus: This progression adds pressure and helps players improve decision-making and passing under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Finishing Element:Once the wide player receives the ball after the through pass, they now attempt to finish the play by shooting at a goal or a mini-goal.Focus: The progression emphasizes converting attacking opportunities after the through ball and promotes quick transitions from midfield to attack.

title: Belgium Positioning & Build Up
