instructions_setup: This drill allows a defensive unit to work on their positioning and reactions. The coach will call out a color, and the 4 defenders will react using the press and cover principle to adjust their positioning. The defensive line should be compact and adjust to the coach's instructions.After 'x' number of reps, the coach serves a ball in behind the defensive line. The defenders must react to the ball and recover to prevent a counter-attack. Once they regain control of the ball, the defenders will build up play unopposed into one of the 2 mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Press & Cover: Emphasize the importance of the press and cover principle, where one defender presses the ball while the others provide cover to protect the space and prevent penetration.• Communication: Defenders must constantly communicate to ensure they maintain a solid, compact shape and are aware of each other's positioning.• Awareness: The defenders should constantly scan to identify threats, especially when adjusting to the coach's color calls.• Recovery: Once the ball is served in behind, defenders must quickly recover, track the ball, and transition from defense to attack.• Build-up Play: After recovering possession, defenders should focus on playing simple, clean passes as they progress the ball toward the mini goals.

title: Belgium Unopposed Finishing & 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with 2 unopposed finishes into 2 separate goals, positioned on a mini pitch resembling two 18-yard boxes with goals opposite each other. The 2 wide players combine before delivering a cross into the box for the attacker to finish.After completing the unopposed finishing phase, the coach serves the ball to one of the attackers. The attacker then plays out a 1v1 with a defender, followed by completing a second 1v1 with a second ball.
coaching_notes: • Finishing Technique: Focus on composure and accuracy during the unopposed finishing phase. Attackers should aim for placement rather than power when finishing.• Crossing: Encourage wide players to deliver precise, weighted crosses into the box. The delivery should cater to the attacking player's run and positioning.• 1v1 Decision Making: The attacker must quickly decide whether to dribble, perform a skill move, or shoot early. Encourage a calm but decisive approach.• Defender Positioning: Defenders should focus on closing down the angle and preventing the attacker from cutting inside or shooting at goal.• Timing of Runs: Attackers should time their runs well, arriving at the right moment to meet the cross or make an effective move in the 1v1 scenario.
progression_one: Add a Second Attacker:Introduce a second defender in the 1v1 phase, creating a 2v1 scenario for the attacker. This forces the attacker to make quicker decisions and enhances their ability to beat multiple defenders.Focus: Improves decision-making and ability to maintain control under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Challenge:Add a time challenge for the wide players to deliver a set number of accurate crosses within a given time frame. This increases the intensity and challenges both the quality and speed of the crosses.Focus: Enhances the decision-making speed of the wide players and increases the tempo of the attacking phase.

title: Belgrade 1v1 with Pressure Behind
instructions_setup: This 1v1 practice focuses on encouraging attackers to get ahead of defenders and receive the ball before turning and playing forwards. The attacker can receive the ball on either side, and they should be encouraged to vary their positioning to keep play unpredictable. Once they receive the ball, the attacker must aim to turn and take on the defender, ultimately attempting to score into either of the two mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Receiving the Ball – The attacker should focus on receiving the ball quickly and positioning their body to make an immediate turn, creating space between themselves and the defender. Varying the side from which they receive helps keep the defender off balance.• Creating Separation – Encourage attackers to use quick touches or feints to break away from the defender. The attacker should look to accelerate as soon as they turn, getting ahead of the defender to create space for a shot on goal.• Decision-Making – The attacker must quickly assess whether to take the defender on directly, pass, or shoot. They should focus on using the defender’s positioning to decide whether a dribble, feint, or quick shot is the best option.• Finishing Under Pressure – Attackers should be encouraged to shoot quickly when they have the opportunity, particularly when the defender is closing in. Shooting with composure, even under pressure, is key to being effective in this situation.
progression_one: Add More DefendersIntroduce a second defender who can apply light pressure from behind or the sides, forcing the attacker to make quicker decisions and moves.Focus: Increases the difficulty for the attacker, encouraging faster turns and sharper dribbling skills under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit for ScoringGive the attacker a set amount of time to beat the defender and score into one of the mini goals.Focus: Encourages quick thinking and decision-making, mimicking real-game scenarios where time and space are limited.

title: Belgrade 3v2 Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: This attacking the box practice starts with a wide combination before a cross into the box. Teams will take it in turns attacking the box 3v2 and are competing head-to-head to score the highest number of goals. The practice is timed, and the team with the most goals scored are the winners. Players will rotate throughout the practice and must fulfill all 3 positions of attacker, defender, and crosser.
coaching_notes: • Attacker Timing – The attacking players should focus on timing their runs into the box. They must make sure to arrive at the right moment to meet the cross and take the shot with composure.• Crossing Accuracy – The crosser must focus on delivering accurate and quality crosses into the box, ensuring the ball is played into dangerous areas for the attacking players to attack.• Defender Positioning – The defenders should focus on closing down the attackers quickly and making sure they are positioned between the ball and the goal. They should be aware of the attackers' movements and anticipate their runs.• Finishing Technique – The attackers need to be clinical in their finishing, working on different types of finishes, such as volleys, headers, or first-time shots, depending on the ball's delivery.
progression_one: Increase Attacking OverloadTo increase the intensity, allow the attacking team to have more players in the box, creating a greater numerical advantage and more opportunities for crosses and finishes.Focus: Creating space in the box and exploiting numerical superiority.
progression_two: Limit Touches for CrossersLimit the number of touches the crosser can take before delivering the ball. This forces quicker decision-making and sharper crosses.Focus: Quick decision-making and faster ball delivery to increase tempo.

title: Belgrade Build & Finishing
instructions_setup: This practice allows teams to develop their ability to build and progress play through central areas whilst under possession. Teams of 6 (+2 GK) will attempt to retain and progress play whilst under pressure from 2 pressing players. The team building must complete 3 passes before attempting to break lines into the next zone. If the pressing team wins possession, they can attack quickly into either main goal.
coaching_notes: • Ball Retention – The team in possession must focus on short, quick passes to retain possession while under pressure. Encouraging close control and scanning the field is key to maintaining possession and finding passing lanes.• Passing Patterns – Encourage players to focus on breaking the lines with well-timed passes after completing the required 3 passes. Players should aim to switch the ball or play forward passes to advance play into the next zone.• Pressing Team – The defending players should look to press aggressively and cut off passing lanes, forcing the building team into mistakes. Their main goal is to win the ball and exploit the transition by quickly counter-attacking.• Finishing in Transition – Once possession is won, the pressing team should focus on making a quick transition towards the goal, using the space created from the overloaded build-up phase to create a clear shot on goal.
progression_one: Increase Pressing PressureIncrease the number of pressing players from 2 to 3, forcing the team in possession to work even harder to break lines and progress through the zones.Focus: Improving decision-making under increased defensive pressure.
progression_two: Add a Goalkeeper for Each TeamIntroduce goalkeepers to both teams, which adds another level of challenge in the final transition phase. Teams must now focus on finishing under pressure with a goalkeeper present.Focus: Improving finishing under pressure and transitioning from build-up to attack.

title: Belgrade Finishing the Attack
instructions_setup: This practice begins with an unopposed pass played into a player positioned in the wide area, who will deliver a cross into the box. The centre forward and the inside forward (who didn’t play the initial pass) will attack the box in a 2v2 scenario against the defenders, aiming to score. The defending team consists of two central defenders and a recovering defensive midfielder, whose role is to prevent cutbacks to the inside forward and add an extra layer of realism to the scenario by challenging the attacking team with additional defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – The attacking players should time their runs into the box to meet the cross with momentum, ensuring they are in the right position to finish on the delivery.• Crossing Technique – The wide player must focus on delivering accurate and varied crosses, ranging from driven balls to floated deliveries, depending on the attacking players’ positioning.• Movement off the Ball – The centre forward and inside forward should communicate and move dynamically, creating angles and making intelligent runs to create space for themselves and the ball carrier.• Defensive Awareness – Defenders must track the attackers’ runs while positioning themselves to prevent cutbacks or early shots. The recovering defensive midfielder must act as a shield, disrupting the offensive flow.
progression_one: Restrict Passes Before CrossLimit the number of touches the wide player can take before crossing (e.g., one or two touches).Focus: Increases the speed of the attack and forces the wide player to make quicker decisions, simulating match conditions.
progression_two: Add an Extra AttackerIntroduce a third attacker into the box, creating a 3v2 attacking scenario.Focus: Challenges the defenders to maintain shape and communication, while providing more attacking options for the forwards to exploit.

title: Belgrade FUN Heading Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This drill involves a head-to-head (H2H) competition where teams take turns attacking and defending through headers. After an attacking player attempts to score with a header, they immediately transition to become the goalkeeper (GK) and try to stop the opposition from scoring their header.The transition between attacking and goalkeeping is continuous, and teams are rewarded with 1 point for every goal they score. This drill adds a competitive edge while also serving as an engaging heading warm-up.
coaching_notes: • Heading Technique: Emphasize proper heading form—players should focus on timing, accuracy, and direction to increase their chances of scoring.• Transition Speed: Encourage quick transitions between attack and defense, with players being alert and ready to react as soon as they switch roles.• Goalkeeper Positioning: When in goal, players must focus on positioning themselves effectively, staying on their toes, and reacting quickly to the incoming header.• Decision Making: Attackers must assess the goalkeeper's positioning and decide whether to go for a powerful header or a more controlled, precise attempt.
progression_one: Add a Timed Challenge:Set a time limit for each phase of the drill (e.g., 30 seconds per round). The team with the most goals at the end of the time limit wins.Focus: This progression encourages a faster tempo, increases intensity, and simulates the pressure of a game situation where speed and focus are crucial.

title: Belgrade One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to develop a defender’s ability to defend crosses under continuous physical demand. Positioned on a small-sided pitch with two full-sized goals at opposite ends, the defender will sprint from one goal to the other, defending crosses delivered from wide areas at each end. The drill emphasizes aerial defending, timing, and fitness through repeated high-intensity efforts across the length of the pitch.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Proper Positioning and Timing When Defending Crosses – Anticipate the flight of the ball to make effective clearances or interceptions.• Use Strong, Controlled Aerial Challenges – Win headers with power and precision while maintaining balance and body control.• Communicate Clearly with the Goalkeeper and Teammates – Organize the defensive area to cover key attacking threats during each cross.• Maintain High Intensity and Quick Recovery Between Sprints – Build the stamina to repeatedly track back and contest crosses without loss of concentration.
progression_one: Increase the Pace and Frequency of CrossesDeliver crosses more rapidly and consistently to raise physical demands and improve decision-making speed under fatigue.Focus:Builds aerobic fitness, defensive alertness, and quick reaction skills during continuous high-pressure defending.
progression_two: Add an Attacker to Challenge the DefenderIntroduce an active attacker making runs to increase the defender’s need to track runners and defend crosses with greater intensity.Focus:Enhances one-on-one defensive skills, spatial awareness, and the ability to win aerial duels under realistic pressure.

title: Belgrade Pass & Press
instructions_setup: This passing practice focuses on a pass and press scenario. Players are positioned at four points: North, South, East, and West, around a central area. The practice starts with one player making a forward pass to a teammate, after which they immediately press the receiving player, simulating game-like pressure.This drill is ideal as a warm-up, focusing on receiving the ball and playing under pressure while also improving the players' ability to react quickly to the ball and the opponent's movements.
coaching_notes: • Pass with Purpose: Players should focus on making accurate and purposeful passes to the receiving player, ensuring the ball is played with the correct weight and direction.• Pressing Technique: Emphasize the importance of pressing immediately after passing. The pressing player should close down the space quickly, staying on their toes and being ready to react to the ball.• Receiving Under Pressure: Encourage the receiving player to check their shoulder before receiving the ball, scanning the area to assess the pressure they are under. They should aim to control the ball and quickly make a decision, either passing or dribbling away from the defender.• Communication: Players should communicate verbally and non-verbally with their teammates, helping to organize the press and coordinate movements.
progression_one: Increase the Pressing Intensity:Allow the pressing players to close down the receiving player more aggressively, aiming to win the ball back in a shorter amount of time. This progression adds a level of intensity to simulate higher-pressure situations.Focus: This progression helps players refine their pressing skills, improving their ability to win the ball back quickly and apply relentless pressure in match situations.

title: Belgrade Technical Passing Warm Up
instructions_setup: This technical passing warm-up focuses on ball mastery, quick combinations, and vertical passing patterns. The practice is designed to be adaptable and can be set up in various grid formats depending on the number of players available. Players work through passing sequences that emphasize clean first touches, sharp movement, and speed of play. It serves as an ideal activation drill to prepare players for more complex possession or attacking patterns later in the session.
coaching_notes: • Body Position – Players should open their body to play forward quickly and receive on the back foot whenever possible.• Tempo – Emphasize sharp, game-like tempo in all passing and movement to simulate match conditions and improve rhythm.• Communication – Players must call for the ball and give clear cues to support quick, clean combinations.• Ball Mastery – Focus on quality of first touch and control under pressure, especially when receiving on the move.
progression_one: One-Touch Passing SequencesIntroduce one-touch restrictions in parts of the pattern to increase difficulty and test reaction speed.Focus: Enhances speed of play and challenges players to think ahead before receiving.
progression_two: Add Passive Defender in the GridPlace a passive defender inside the grid to encourage scanning and positional awareness.Focus: Promotes better decision-making and awareness under semi-opposed conditions.

title: Benfica 2v2 with Transitions
instructions_setup: This practice involves two mini-pitches placed side by side. Play starts with a 2v2 attack, where the attacking team attempts to beat the defending pair and score into the main goal. Once the attacking phase is complete, the two attacking players transition to the opposite side of the grid, where they now become defenders in another 2v2 scenario.The transitions between attacking and defending are continuous, which helps players develop quick decision-making and adaptability in different situations.If you don’t have two goalkeepers or main goals available for the session, you can substitute mini-goals in place of the main goals.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Focus: In the 2v2 attacking phase, encourage players to make quick decisions, using width and combination play to break down the defending team. Emphasize quick transitions from attack to defense.• Defensive Focus: Defenders should communicate and work together to maintain compactness and control space. They must focus on tracking runners and cutting off passing lanes.• Transition Play: The key to this drill is the rapid transition between attack and defense. Players should always be prepared to switch roles, maintaining focus and readiness as soon as the ball goes out of play or a goal is scored.• Compactness in Defense: In the defending phase, defenders should aim to close the space between them, making it difficult for the attacking team to find openings.
progression_one: Add Neutral Players:Introduce two neutral players who play on the attacking team. These players are positioned on the outside of the grid and can support the attack, creating a 4v2 when the attacking team has the ball.Focus: This progression enhances attacking options, increases width, and encourages the defending team to adjust to an overload situation.

title: Benfica Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This mastery drill allows wide players to practice their crossing technique into two different zones in the box.The drill starts with three wide players, each positioned on different sides of the field. The wide players will engage in a variety of combinations, such as overlaps, underlaps, and third-man runs, before delivering crosses into two target zones within the box.The two target areas are:Angled Mini Goal – Positioned near the penalty spot, replicating a cut-back cross.6-Yard Mini Goal – Positioned on the six-yard line, replicating a flashed cross across the face of goal.The wide players will rotate through these movements and focus on timing, accuracy, and the variety of crosses to be delivered into the appropriate target zones.
coaching_notes: • Crossing Technique: Emphasize the importance of delivering accurate crosses to the right zones, focusing on both pace and placement. Players should strike the ball cleanly to ensure consistency in their crosses.• Movement for Overlaps & Underlaps: Wide players should recognize when to execute an overlap (around the player) or underlap (inside the player) to create space and open up crossing angles.• Third-Man Run: The third-man runner should time their run into the box to be a target for the cross, ensuring they arrive just as the ball is delivered.• Timing & Positioning: Ensure wide players understand the importance of timing their runs and positioning themselves to be in the best spot for receiving or delivering a cross.
progression_one: Add Pressure on the Crossers:Introduce a defender or two to press the wide players as they prepare to cross. This will simulate pressure from opposition defenders and challenge the wide players to deliver the cross under pressure.Focus: This progression helps develop crossing under pressure and encourages players to be more aware of opposition movement as they deliver balls into the box.
progression_two: Introduce a Finishing Element:Introduce one or two attackers in the box to finish the crosses. This will encourage the wide players to focus on the quality of their delivery and the timing of their runs into the box.Focus: This progression focuses on the connection between the wide players' crosses and the attackers' movement in the box, improving both crossing accuracy and finishing technique.

title: Benfica Counter & Recover
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on quick attacking transitions and defending against a counter-attack. Play starts with a pass from the coach into any of the three attacking players positioned 40-50 yards from the goal line. The attacking players must then attack the main goal as quickly as possible, with three defenders behind them who are tasked with recovering and stopping the attack.The recovery defenders start 2 meters behind the attacking players and face away from the coach at the start. This positioning forces the defenders to react quickly to the counter-attack, simulating a real game situation where defenders must recover and apply pressure to prevent a goal.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Attack: Emphasize the importance of quick, direct attacking towards the goal, making sure the attackers take advantage of the space before defenders can recover.• Decision Making: Attackers should make quick decisions, whether to take on a defender, play a through ball, or take a shot on goal.• Defender Recovery: Recovery defenders should focus on their reaction time and positioning as they quickly transition from defense to attack. They need to close down space and apply pressure to disrupt the attackers' rhythm.• Communication: Both attackers and defenders should communicate throughout the drill. Attackers should talk about their intentions, and defenders should communicate when they are recovering and covering space.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player who can support the attack. This neutral player can pass or receive the ball to help create overloads for the attacking team, making the defenders' job harder and forcing quicker recovery decisions.Focus: This progression enhances attacking play and allows the attackers to utilize the extra player for more dynamic and varied attacks.
progression_two: Limit Attacker Touches:Limit the number of touches the attacking players can take (e.g., one or two touches maximum). This forces the attackers to play quicker and under more pressure, simulating the need to make fast decisions in a real counter-attack situation.Focus: This progression develops the attackers' ability to make quick, accurate decisions while under pressure, and reinforces the need for fast transitions in attack.

title: Benfica Finishing Overloaded
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on attacking under overload conditions and finishing under pressure. The field is set up in a 20-yard grid, split down the middle into two zones. In each zone, the attacking team has a 2v1 advantage. The goal for the attackers is to move the ball from the defensive zone into the attacking zone while maintaining possession, using their overload to create space and opportunities.Once the ball reaches the attacking zone, the two attackers must work together in sync to break down the lone defender and attempt to score. If either of the defending players wins possession, they are allowed to transition quickly and attack the main goal.
coaching_notes: • Overload Utilization: Emphasize how the attackers can use the overload to stretch the defense and create passing lanes. The players must communicate well and move off the ball to create options for the player with possession.• Sync and Timing: Attackers should time their movements to work in sync, making sure one player is drawing defenders while the other looks to exploit space or receive the ball for a shot on goal.• Defender Transition: Defenders should focus on winning the ball and then immediately transitioning to attack. The drill simulates real-game pressure where a loss of possession leads to an instant change in roles, requiring quick reactions.• Finishing Under Pressure: The attacking players must remain composed in front of goal, making quick decisions while under the pressure of a lone defender.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender into the attacking zone once the ball is played in. This adds more pressure to the attackers and challenges them to make quicker decisions and execute combination plays to break down the defense.Focus: This progression improves attacking combinations, quick decision-making, and finishing under increased defensive pressure.

title: Benfica Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: This conditioning rondo is designed to build fitness while also incorporating ball control and decision-making. The drill starts with two defenders sprinting into a grid, where they attempt to win the ball in a 2v4 rondo. The four attacking players will work to maintain possession by passing and moving in sync.Once the defenders touch the ball, both will split and move into smaller grids located to the left and right of the main grid. In these smaller grids, the defenders will now work in a 1v3 scenario, where they will again attempt to win possession of the ball from the attacking players.
coaching_notes: • Fitness & Intensity: Emphasize the high-intensity nature of the drill. Attackers must constantly move to offer passing options, while defenders should press aggressively to win the ball as quickly as possible.• Positioning: Attackers should focus on maintaining good positioning to facilitate quick ball movement and prevent defenders from closing down options too quickly.• Decision Making: Attackers must make quick decisions when receiving the ball, choosing the best option to pass or move based on the pressure from the defenders.• Transition: The defenders must be ready to transition immediately after winning the ball, quickly splitting into the smaller grids to challenge the attackers again. This teaches them to react to possession changes quickly and adjust to new situations.
progression_one: Increase the Size of the Smaller Grids:Enlarge the smaller grids where the defenders work in a 1v3. This gives the defenders a bit more space to cover, forcing them to work harder and be more strategic in how they win possession.Focus: This progression focuses on enhancing the defenders' ability to close down space efficiently while still requiring attackers to make quick decisions under increased defensive pressure.

title: Benfica One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 drill focuses on improving a player’s ability to receive the ball under control, execute effective dribbling skills to beat a mannequin defender, and finish accurately into a mini goal. The player continuously works back and forth, receiving passes from the coach, dribbling past mannequins on alternating sides, and scoring in opposite directions to develop rhythm, technical skill, and sharp finishing.
coaching_notes: • Control Your First Touch to Set Up the Skill Move – Ensure the ball is close and positioned to enable a confident, effective feint or dribble around the mannequin.• Use Quick, Explosive Footwork to Beat the Defender – Perform sharp skill moves with speed and precision to create separation from the mannequin.• Keep Your Head Up to Maintain Awareness of the Goal – Stay alert to the goal’s location while dribbling so you can adjust your approach for an accurate finish.• Focus on Composure and Accuracy When Finishing – Take a controlled, well-placed shot into the mini goal after beating the mannequin to build confidence and precision.
progression_one: Increase the Speed of Each RepReduce rest between repetitions and encourage faster dribbling and finishing to build stamina and decision-making under fatigue.Focus:Enhances dribbling speed, technical execution, and finishing accuracy under continuous physical and mental pressure.

title: Benfica Possession to Finish
instructions_setup: This practice is set up on half a pitch with an additional goal placed at the halfway line. The drill starts with a 4v4 central phase, with a joker player who can be used by the team in possession to create a 5v4 advantage. Both teams are required to complete a set number of successful passes (e.g., "x" passes) before switching the ball to one of the wide players.Once the ball is switched to a wide player, both teams transition into a 3v3 attacking phase in the box. Both teams can attack either end of the pitch, making this drill dynamic and focusing on both offensive and defensive transitions.
coaching_notes: • Ball Circulation: Stress the importance of quick, accurate passing and movement to create passing lanes and complete the required number of passes before switching to the wide players.• Wide Play: The wide players must be ready to receive the ball quickly, looking to attack space and create a crossing or cut-back opportunity into the box.• Decision Making: Attackers and defenders must make quick decisions in transition, deciding whether to press or drop back when the ball is switched to the wide player.• Defensive Shape: Defenders should be aware of their positioning as they move from a 4v4 to a 3v3 in the box. They need to track attacking runs and stay compact to prevent goal-scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Wide Area:Introduce a neutral defender in the wide areas who works with the attacking team to support the build-up play. This adds an extra layer of complexity to the wide phase of the drill.Focus: This progression helps players to develop their wide attacking play under pressure and improves their ability to create space and deliver effective crosses.

title: Benfica Warm Up & SAQ
instructions_setup: This SAQ and technical warm-up combines speed, agility, and finishing. Players must complete a pre-defined movement route through a series of poles or markers as quickly as possible. As they exit the final pole, they receive a pass from a teammate and attempt to score with a first-time finish.Immediately after their shot, the attacker switches roles with the passer, who now becomes the next runner. The drill continues in relay format. The first team to score a pre-determined number of goals is declared the winner, encouraging both speed and finishing quality.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Movement: Encourage quick footwork and sharp changes of direction around the poles to simulate in-game agility requirements.• Timing & Accuracy: Focus on the timing of the pass and the body shape of the attacker when receiving the ball for a first-time finish.• Quality of Finish: Players should remain composed under pressure and aim for accurate, placed finishes over power.• Communication: Players must communicate to time passes correctly and maintain the rhythm of the practice.• Competitive Edge: Remind players that the speed element should never come at the cost of poor technical execution.
progression_one: Add a 1v1 After the Shot:After the first-time shot, the attacker must immediately turn and defend in a short 1v1 duel against the next attacking runner.Focus: Improves recovery speed, transition awareness, and defensive agility.

title: Berlin 1-2 Passing Activation
instructions_setup: This passing activation drill focuses on quick combinations and technical execution. Players begin by playing a simple 1-2 (give-and-go) pass around a cone or mannequin. The receiving player continues their movement and finishes the move with a shot into a mini goal.The drill emphasizes fluidity in movement, timing of the combination, and accuracy in passing and finishing. It’s a perfect technical warm-up to activate players both physically and mentally at the start of a session.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Pass: Players should focus on releasing the return pass at the right moment to keep the combination smooth.• Body Shape: Encourage players to open their body when receiving to accelerate into the finish cleanly.• Communication: Verbal cues and eye contact are key to coordinating the combination play effectively.• Finishing Quality: Players should stay composed and focus on placing the shot accurately into the mini goal.• Tempo & Intensity: Reinforce the importance of sharp movement and crisp passing to simulate match-like rhythm.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender on the Return Pass:Introduce a passive defender positioned near the 1-2 return area. The attacking player must work around them before finishing.Focus: Adds realism and encourages better timing and spatial awareness.

title: Berlin Breaking Lines into 2v2
instructions_setup: This practice starts with 2 defenders dribbling towards the edge of the box before making a line-breaking pass into a mini goal. As soon as the defenders make the pass, 2 attacking players located centrally must attack quickly and attempt to score while the defending 2 are unbalanced and transitioning from the wide to central spaces. The defending 2 must react quickly, as if they've lost possession after their initial pass, and attempt to protect the central spaces and defend against the 2 attackers.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Line-Breaking Pass – The defenders must make the pass at the right moment to break the lines and set up the transition to attack. The timing is crucial for catching the defending team off guard before they can recover their defensive shape.• Quick Transition to Attack – The 2 attackers must react immediately to the line-breaking pass and move into the central space to exploit the defensive disorganization. Emphasize fast, decisive movement to create an attacking overload and maximize scoring opportunities.• Defending During Transition – Once the defenders make their pass and are unbalanced, they must recover quickly to protect the central spaces. Encourage defenders to focus on closing down the attackers, cutting off passing lanes, and preventing shots on goal.• Reaction to Loss of Possession – If the attacking team regains possession in the central areas, the defending team should quickly transition into a defensive shape and be ready to counter the threat from the attackers. Encourage quick reactions and communication during this moment of transition.
progression_one: Add a GoalkeeperIntroduce a goalkeeper to make the practice more realistic and improve the attacking players' finishing under pressure. This will also help the defending players adjust their positioning and decision-making when protecting the goal.Focus: Finishing under pressure and improving transition play from wide to central areas.
progression_two: Limit Passing Options for DefendersLimit the number of passes the defenders can make before transitioning. This forces them to make quicker decisions under pressure and will create a more intense transition for both the defending and attacking players.Focus: Quick decision-making, maintaining defensive balance, and exploiting attacking overloads.

title: Berlin Build Up Centrally
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on developing players’ ability to build up centrally using a single pivot player. Play always starts from the goalkeeper, and the attacking team must attempt to build play towards one of the two mini goals. The scoring system awards 1 point for a pass into a mini goal and 2 points if the pass into the mini goal comes from a combination involving the central end line player (acting as the pivot). If the defending team wins possession, they immediately counter-attack towards the main goal. Every goal scored in the main goal is worth 2 points.
coaching_notes: • Use of Pivot Player – The pivot player must be positioned centrally to link up play, receiving the ball and distributing it either back to the defenders or forward to progress the attack. Emphasize their role in maintaining possession and recycling the ball when necessary.• Building through the Midfield – Encourage players to play quick, accurate passes to break through the central midfield areas. The team in possession should aim to use the pivot player as the fulcrum for central progression.• Combination Play – Focus on quick combinations between players, especially around the central areas and the pivot player. Quick 1-2s or give-and-goes should be used to break through pressure and advance the ball.• Defensive Pressure & Transitions – When defending, players must quickly close down the pivot player and prevent easy distribution into the mini goals. On regaining possession, transition quickly to counter-attack into the main goal, capitalizing on the moment of overload.
progression_one: Introduce Defensive SupportAdd one additional defender to increase pressure on the build-up team and force more intricate play.Focus: Forces the build-up team to be more precise and creative when using the pivot player, enhancing their ability to play under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Time for ScoringIntroduce a time limit within which the attacking team must score into the mini goals or counter-attack to the main goal.Focus: Increases the intensity and encourages faster decision-making and quicker ball circulation to avoid stalling play.

title: Berlin Continuous 2v2
instructions_setup: This high-tempo 2v2 drill is played inside a square grid with goals on each of the four sides. Each pair of players occupies one side of the grid. Teams attack in pairs and immediately transition to defend against the next attacking team, creating a continuous rotation.The drill works in a clockwise pattern—once a 2v2 is completed, the next attacking team (positioned clockwise from the previous attackers) enters to face the new defenders. This format encourages intensity, quick decision-making, and sharp transitions between attacking and defending roles.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of reacting quickly from attack to defense, encouraging mental sharpness and urgency.• Communication: Teams must communicate constantly—both in and out of possession—to maintain shape and work together effectively.• Defensive Compactness: Defenders should stay close and support each other to reduce space and block shots or passes.• Attack with Purpose: Encourage attackers to combine quickly and be decisive with their efforts on goal.• Positional Awareness: Players must remain aware of the clockwise rotation and be ready to enter or exit the grid at the right time.
progression_one: Add Time Limit on Attacks:Each attacking team must shoot within 10 seconds of entering the grid. If they don’t, possession switches automatically.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and more urgency in attack.
progression_two: Introduce a Joker Player:Add a neutral player inside the grid who always plays with the team in possession to create a 3v2 situation.Focus: Promotes combination play and supports movement, while challenging defenders to cover more space.

title: Berlin Finish While Overloaded
instructions_setup: This finishing drill begins with a 3v1 situation in the first zone. The attacking player must progress the ball from the first zone to the second zone using two outer bounce players, creating the overload. Once the attacker reaches the second zone, they can combine with a teammate already positioned there to create a 2v1 and attempt to score. The goal is to finish quickly while under pressure from defenders.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: Encourage the attacking player to make quick decisions when using the outer bounce players to progress the ball.• Effective Use of Overload: The player with the ball in the first zone should use the overload effectively, drawing defenders and playing the ball to their teammate for a shooting opportunity.• Timing of Runs: The teammate in the second zone should focus on timing their run to create a clear 2v1 with the attacker and take the shot quickly.• Awareness in the Final Third: Stress the importance of being aware of defensive pressure and the best angle for a shot once the 2v1 situation is created.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure in First Zone:Increase the pressure on the attacker by adding an extra defender, turning the first zone into a 3v2 situation.Focus: This progression encourages the attacker to make faster decisions and use the overload more effectively.
progression_two: Limit Attack Time:Set a time limit for the attacker to progress the ball into the second zone (e.g., 10 seconds). If they fail to do so, the defending team wins possession.Focus: Promotes quick transitions and sharp decision-making in attack.

title: Berlin Fitness & 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 20-yard sprint race from the pole into the grid. The first player to arrive in the grid will receive a ball from the coach and play out a 1v1 scenario. If either of the players scores, they will be awarded 2 points. A bonus point is awarded for the reaction in transitions. Once the ball is dead, the first player to touch the pole in which both players started from will be awarded this bonus point.
coaching_notes: • Sprint and Reaction Time – Emphasize the importance of sprinting quickly into the grid and being the first to receive the ball. Players should focus on quick acceleration and strong sprinting mechanics to gain an advantage early in the 1v1 situation.• 1v1 Technique – During the 1v1 scenario, players should focus on maintaining good body positioning and using skill moves to beat their opponent. Encourage attackers to take defenders on with pace and creativity, while defenders should focus on staying balanced and forcing the attacker wide.• Transitioning Quickly – Encourage players to transition quickly when the ball is dead. Both players need to be aware of the transition moment and react fast to gain the bonus point. This helps build fitness, as well as focus on quick recoveries.• Scoring and Decision-Making – Remind players that the quicker they can finish their 1v1, the more likely they are to regain possession or score. Encourage decision-making that leads to a high percentage of goals, such as taking the shot early when the opportunity arises.
progression_one: Add Multiple DefendersAdd additional defenders to the grid, requiring the attacking player to beat more than one defender. This increases the difficulty and helps develop decision-making in 1v1 situations.Focus: Improving 1v1 finishing skills and defending under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Sprint DistanceIncrease the sprint distance to 30 yards to make the race more challenging. This will test the players’ endurance and acceleration over a longer distance, simulating more intense game situations.Focus: Improving stamina, speed, and 1v1 duels in a high-intensity scenario.

title: Berlin One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 technical practice is designed to improve a fullback’s decision-making, first touch, and passing execution in wide areas. The fullback begins each rep by taking a positive touch through a gate positioned in the wide zone to simulate receiving on the move. From there, they must scan and choose between two passing options: one mini goal positioned down the line (replicating a winger) and another located more centrally (replicating a number 9 dropping in). The goal is to play accurate, well-weighted passes that match the visual trigger.
coaching_notes: • Controlled First Touch Through the Gate – Use the inside of the foot to guide the ball smoothly through the gate with controlled weight and direction, preparing for the next action.• Head Up to Scan Before Passing – Lift your head immediately after the gate to assess which option is best, reacting to coach cues or visual triggers under minimal time.• Match Pass Type to Target – Use a driven pass down the line or a guided pass inside based on the angle, distance, and target zone for realism and precision.• Body Position on Release – Open up the body when playing wide and rotate hips for inside passes, maintaining balance to strike cleanly and consistently.

title: Berlin Rondo into Counter Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 4v2 rondo, where the 4 players in possession work to maintain the ball against 2 defenders. If the defending 2 win possession and can play a forward pass into the attacker outside the grid, they will be rewarded with a bonus point. If the defending team wins possession but the ball goes out of the grid, the coach will serve the ball into the attacker to restart the next phase.Once the ball is passed into the attacker, the defending 2 players from the grid must break out to create an attacking overload. They will have 10 seconds to complete the attack, focusing on quick transitions. As a progression, the number of attacking players can be increased, turning the attack into a 5v4 scenario, which encourages a more dynamic and varied attacking strategy.
coaching_notes: • Fast Transitions – Encourage defenders to quickly switch from defense to attack once they win possession. Speed is essential, so the defending players must be aware of the timing to break out and attack.• Communication – The attacking player must communicate clearly with the defenders to ensure they understand when and where to play the ball. Quick decision-making and effective passing will help maximize the attacking potential.• Effective Use of Overload – Once the defenders break out, they need to exploit the overload situation. Encourage quick passes, movement off the ball, and finding gaps in the defense to complete the attack.• Progressive Attack – As the game progresses and more players are added to the attacking phase, remind players to keep composure and work as a unit. The attackers should focus on teamwork and positioning to maximize the space created by the overload.
progression_one: Increase Attacking NumbersIntroduce more players into the attacking phase, creating a full defensive back 4, thus turning the game into a 5v4 attacking scenario. This progression allows for more complex decision-making and a greater emphasis on building attacks with numerical superiority.Focus: Build awareness of positioning and use of space in overload situations.
progression_two: Time Pressure on AttackersIntroduce a time limit for attackers to score once they receive the ball. This will add urgency and challenge the attackers to make quicker decisions. Focus on exploiting the overload situation and converting possession into goals within the time frame.Focus: Speed of thought and execution in attacking phases.

title: Berlin Rondo with Goalkeepers
instructions_setup: This practice starts with a 4v2 rondo in a small grid. After every 3 successful passes, an additional defender joins the rondo, progressing to a 4v3 and possibly even a 4v4 as pressure increases. If the defending team wins possession, they aim to score in one of the four mini goals located around the grid, which are protected by two goalkeepers. If the defending team regains possession and scores, they switch roles and become the possession team.
coaching_notes: • Passing Precision – Encourage quick, precise passes to maintain possession and avoid giving defenders opportunities to intercept or pressure the ball carrier.• Positional Awareness – Players should focus on maintaining good spacing to allow for passing options and ensure they’re always ready to support their teammates in possession.• Defensive Pressure – As the defenders increase in number, emphasize compactness and effective pressing. Defenders should read the attacking team’s movements and anticipate passing lanes.• Goalkeeper Support – The two goalkeepers must stay alert, helping protect the mini goals while coordinating with defenders to block or clear the ball when necessary.
progression_one: Limit Number of TouchesRestrict the number of touches players in possession can take (e.g., two touches maximum).Focus: Increases tempo and decision-making speed, simulating real-game pressure.
progression_two: Allow Defenders to ScoreAllow defending players to score in the mini goals if they win possession, giving them more incentive to press.Focus: Adds an extra layer of intensity to the drill and motivates defenders to be more aggressive and proactive in regaining the ball.

title: Berlin Switch to Finish the Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 3v2 rondo on one side of the pitch. After a set number of successful passes, the team in possession can switch to the opposite rondo grid through the defensive midfielder positioned in between the two rondo grids. If the 2 players out of possession win the ball, they must attempt to score into either of the mini goals located just outside the rondo grids.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: Encourage quick, precise passing and constant movement off the ball to maintain possession and create passing lanes.• Defensive Pressing: The defenders should focus on staying compact, pressing effectively, and trying to intercept the ball to transition quickly into attack.• Transition Awareness: Once possession is lost, both teams must transition quickly—either to attack or to regain possession.• Awareness of Space: Players must be aware of the space around them to make the most of the rondo’s overload and create passing opportunities.
progression_one: Add Attacking Phase:After every successful switch of play, the possession team will transition to a 3v3 attacking phase against defenders.Focus: This progression adds a dynamic attacking element to the drill, encouraging fluid transitions from possession to a real match situation.
progression_two: Add Defender Pressure on Switch:Once the team switches play, add an additional defender on the opposite grid, creating a 3v3 situation that the possession team must overcome.Focus: This progression increases the challenge and encourages the possession team to think quickly and execute effective combinations to maintain control and create scoring opportunities.

title: Bern 1v1 Into 2v2
instructions_setup: A coach and a defender start by passing the ball between each other just outside the penalty area. Two attackers are positioned around 10 yards to either side. At an unpredictable moment, the coach plays a pass into one of the attackers, triggering a 1v1 with the central defender.After this first 1v1 phase is complete—regardless of the outcome—the coach quickly serves a new ball to the second attacker. This starts a second phase, turning it into a 2v1 situation, with the two attackers now combining to beat the same recovering defender and score.
coaching_notes: • Defender Reaction Speed – The defender must stay alert during the passing phase and react immediately to the coach’s cue, closing down space quickly.• Attacker First Touch – The receiving attacker should take a strong, positive first touch forward to exploit the space and stay away from the defender’s recovery angle.• 2v1 Combination – In the second phase, attackers must make quick decisions on when to pass or drive, using overlaps, underlaps, or direct play based on defender positioning.• Support Angle and Timing – The second attacker should enter the play at speed, offering a clear passing lane and creating a 2v1 advantage before the defender can recover centrally.
progression_one: Add Second Defender After First ShotIntroduce a second defender who enters the field just as the second attacker receives their ball, turning the second phase into a 2v2 instead of a 2v1.Focus:Improves communication, speed of play, and decision-making under pressure as space and time are reduced rapidly in the second phase.
progression_two: Coach Calls “Freeze” to Delay Second BallBefore passing the second ball, the coach calls a quick “freeze” command (1–2 second delay) before serving, forcing attackers to stay focused and defenders to recover positioning.Focus:Enhances attacker concentration, timing of runs, and ability to read defender movements before executing combinations in tight, changing scenarios.

title: Bern 2v1 into Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: Play begins with a 2v1 attacking scenario just outside the penalty area. The two attackers aim to combine and beat the single defender to score. Immediately after the initial attack is completed—regardless of outcome—the same two attackers remain active and reposition around the penalty area.A second ball is then served from a wide area into the box, turning the exercise into a second-phase 2v1, where the same defender recovers and attempts to deal with the cross. This drill focuses on attacking transitions, movement, and decision-making across two distinct phases of play.
coaching_notes: • First Phase Decision-Making – Attackers should assess whether to combine quickly or isolate the 1v1 opportunity based on defender positioning and body shape.• Supporting Angles – The second attacker must provide good depth or diagonal angles to receive a return pass or break the defensive line.• Second Phase Reactions – Encourage attackers to stay alert and adjust their position immediately after the first action to prepare for the incoming cross.• Cross Timing and Delivery – Wide players must deliver the second ball with accurate weight and timing to match attacking runs and create clear finishing chances.
progression_one: Passive Wide Pressure on CrosserIntroduce a passive wide defender who applies light pressure to the wide player before the second cross, adding realism without disrupting delivery.Focus:Encourages quicker decision-making from wide areas, realistic delivery timing, and urgency in attacker positioning for the second ball.

title: Bern Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: A striker receives a pass while positioned ahead of a recovering defender who starts 3 yards behind them. As the ball is played in, the attacker must take a positive first touch and drive toward goal to maintain their advantage and create a 1v1 opportunity with the goalkeeper. The defender applies immediate recovery pressure, forcing the attacker to protect the ball and make quick, decisive movements to finish.
coaching_notes: • First Touch Direction – Attackers must take their first touch forward and away from the defender to maximize space and retain the 1v1 advantage.• Awareness of Pressure – Encourage players to scan before receiving to recognize the defender’s position and adjust their touch accordingly.• Finishing Under Pressure – Emphasize calm, early decision-making in front of goal, aiming for quick, composed finishes before the defender can recover.• Defender Recovery Intensity – Defenders should apply full-speed recovery pressure, pushing attackers to execute at match tempo.
progression_one: Angle the Defender’s Starting PositionHave the defender start from a slight angle (left or right) to vary the attacker’s decision on touch direction and finishing side, creating different recovery angles and challenges.Focus:Improves the striker’s ability to read defensive pressure, adjust movement, and select the optimal route to goal.
progression_two: Add a Second Attacker for a 2v1 OptionIntroduce a supporting attacker on the opposite side to create the option of a pass or shot in the 1v1 situation, forcing the striker to make quicker passing vs shooting decisions under pressure.Focus:Encourages awareness, decision-making, and combination play while navigating live pressure and dynamic defensive scenarios.

title: Betis 3 Phase 3v3
instructions_setup: This is a dynamic 3-phase attacking drill where two teams will play 3v3. The drill begins with one of the 3 balls in play, and the attacking team looks to maintain possession and create scoring opportunities until the ball goes dead, either through a goal, out of bounds, or a turnover. The ball is then switched, and the attacking team must immediately adapt to the next phase. This continues through three phases, with each phase lasting until the ball is dead.After completing the third phase, the attacking players will switch out with another set of 3 attackers. The drill emphasizes maintaining attacking intensity, quick decision-making, and seamless transitions between phases. It challenges players to continuously think ahead, stay sharp, and work together to break down the defense while being ready for the next attacking opportunity.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Encourage players to transition quickly between phases, maintaining high tempo and quick decision-making to create attacking opportunities.• Awareness of Space: Attackers should focus on creating space for themselves and teammates while looking for opportunities to exploit gaps in the defense.• Ball Movement: Encourage the attacking team to move the ball quickly and combine effectively, making sure not to hold on to the ball for too long.• Defensive Responsibility: Defenders s
progression_one: Add Restriction on Passing:Introduce a restriction where each player can only make a maximum of two passes before they must shoot or attempt to create a scoring opportunity.Focus: This progression emphasizes quicker decision-making, faster ball movement, and encourages players to be more decisive in attack.
progression_two: Add a Defender in Each Phase:In each phase, add one additional defender to create a 3v4 or 3v5 scenario. The attackers must still attempt to score with the added defensive pressure.Focus: This progression challenges the attackers to think more creatively and work together to break down a higher defensive line.

title: Betis 4v4 SSG + Goalkeepers
instructions_setup: This 4v4 directional small-sided game encourages quick, fluid combinations and 1v1/2v2 attacking situations before players score into one of two mini goals. Each team is assigned a goalkeeper who operates along the central line, responsible for protecting both mini goals. The game is fast-paced and requires players to quickly adjust to the goalkeeper’s positioning, often resulting in rapid switches of play to create scoring opportunities. The goalkeepers’ presence challenges players to think on their feet and adjust their attacking decisions.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations – Encourage players to focus on quick, sharp combinations to break through defensive lines and create space for goal-scoring opportunities.• Awareness of Goalkeeper Positioning – Players must constantly scan the goalkeeper’s position on the line to adjust their approach and find space to shoot or create an angle for the pass.• Attacking Variety – Players should explore both 1v1 and 2v2 attacking situations, testing different strategies to break down the defensive setup.• Defensive Tracking – Defenders should stay alert to both the ball and the movement of attacking players, ensuring they close down space while maintaining awareness of the goalkeeper’s position.
progression_one: Limit Time to ScoreSet a time limit for each attacking phase (e.g., 10 seconds to attempt a shot on goal).Focus: Increases the urgency of decision-making and tests players' ability to create chances under pressure.
progression_two: Introduce Additional DefendersAdd an extra defender to one team, creating a 4v3 scenario.Focus: Enhances defensive organization and challenges the attacking team to work through numerical disadvantage while considering the goalkeeper's influence.

title: Betis Attacking Corner Routine #2
instructions_setup: This unopposed corner routine drill is designed to help players learn various corner delivery techniques and movements to create goal-scoring opportunities. The team will practice their set-piece routine with a focus on timing, spacing, and coordination. Players will position themselves according to the chosen routine (e.g., near post, far post, edge of the box, etc.) and work to execute the set play under minimal pressure.The corner taker will deliver the ball into the designated area, while the other players make runs to attack the ball or create space. The focus is on smooth, well-timed movements and effective ball delivery. The drill is unopposed, allowing the attacking team to concentrate on executing their routine to perfection.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Ensure that attacking players time their runs to the ball correctly. Whether it’s attacking the near post, far post, or edge of the box, the players should be well-timed in their movements to meet the delivery.• Movement to Create Space: Players should work on off-the-ball movement to pull defenders out of position, making it easier for teammates to get a clear shot at goal. Movement should be quick and dynamic, with players changing direction to create space in key areas.• Delivery Quality: Emphasize the importance of delivering the ball with the correct weight, pace, and accuracy. The corner taker must consistently place the ball into the designated area, whether it’s a driven cross, floated ball, or short corner.• Target Areas: Players should understand where to attack based on the type of delivery (e.g., near post, far post, or central). Each player should be aware of their role in relation to the ball's flight path and their teammates’ movements.• Communication: Encourage clear communication between the corner taker and attacking players. This ensures everyone knows when to make their run and where the ball will be delivered.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to lightly pressurize the attackers during the delivery and movement. The defenders should focus on tracking runs and challenging for the ball but not actively blocking or winning it.Focus: Develops the ability to execute corner routines while under light pressure, simulating more realistic game situations and forcing players to adjust their timing and runs.

title: Betis Finishing the Attack Centrally
instructions_setup: This practice is split into 2 zones. In the first zone, the attacking team will play a 2v1 and must attempt to progress the ball to the 3 forward players. If successful, the attacking 3 will play out a 3v3 attack in the second zone. If the defending team wins the ball in either of the 2 zones, they can counter-attack into one of the 2 mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Zone 1 – Progressing the BallThe attacking team should focus on quick, accurate passing to break down the defending 1v1 and progress the ball forward. The player receiving the ball should always look to make the most of the space and create options for the ball carrier by making intelligent runs into advanced positions.• Zone 2 – 3v3 AttackOnce the ball has been successfully progressed into the 3 attacking players, they must now play out a 3v3 attack. The attacking players should focus on quick combinations, using the numerical advantage to overload the defenders and create goal-scoring opportunities. Movement off the ball is key for creating space and options for the ball carrier.• Defensive TransitionIf the defenders win possession in either zone, they should immediately look to transition and attack into one of the 2 mini goals. The defending players should be alert and prepared to exploit the situation, focusing on quick ball recovery and transitioning into the attacking phase as quickly as possible.
progression_one: Add a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit for the attacking team to progress the ball and score in the 3v3. This encourages quick decision-making and high-intensity play.Focus: This progression emphasizes urgency and fast-paced attacking combinations.
progression_two: Rotate Attacking RolesAfter each rep, rotate the attacking players between the 2v1 and 3v3 phases. This ensures that every player gets an opportunity to both attack and defend in different scenarios.Focus: This progression builds versatility in players and helps them develop both attacking and defensive skills.

title: Betis Free Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed free kick routine drill is designed to help players rehearse and refine various attacking free kick patterns from wide or central areas. The team will focus on the key components of a successful set-piece routine including delivery, movement, and timing. Players will position themselves according to the selected routine (e.g., near post runs, edge of the box setups, far post overloads) and execute planned movements without opposition.The free kick taker will deliver the ball into a designated area, aiming for the appropriate target zone based on the play design. Meanwhile, attacking players will make synchronized runs to either meet the delivery or create decoy movements to free up teammates. This unopposed format allows the team to work on precise timing and technical execution without the distraction of defenders.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing & Synchronization:Attackers must time their runs perfectly in relation to the free kick taker’s delivery. Runs should be coordinated so that the ball is met at the optimal point, with staggered timing to create different attacking options.• Varied Movements:Players should rehearse a variety of runs including curved runs, late arrivals at the far post, and quick darts into central zones. Decoy runs and quick direction changes are essential to unsettle defenders in real match scenarios.• Delivery Execution:The free kick taker should focus on consistent and accurate delivery, using different techniques such as whipped, floated, or driven balls based on the routine. The quality of the ball into the target area is crucial to the success of the routine.• Role Clarity:Ensure every player knows their specific job in the routine — whether it’s to attack the ball, screen a defender, make a decoy run, or be in position for a second ball. Clarity in roles improves execution and reduces hesitation.• Communication:Strong verbal and non-verbal communication is essential between the free kick taker and the runners. Agreed cues or signals should trigger the movement so that everyone is synced to the delivery.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to lightly mark the runners and challenge aerially. Their role is to track movements and apply mild resistance without aggressively disrupting play.Focus: This adds realism and forces the attacking team to fine-tune timing and positioning under game-like conditions while still maintaining the structure of the routine.

title: Betis Mastery into 1v1
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery drill, players will dribble unopposed towards a mannequin, using any piece of skill to maneuver past it. Once they have successfully passed the mannequin, the practice becomes opposed, and the attacker must attempt to score into one of the two mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Skill Execution: Encourage players to use a variety of skills to beat the mannequin, focusing on fluid, controlled movements with the ball.• Close Control: Players should maintain close control of the ball while dribbling to ensure they can quickly react to any changes in defensive pressure.• Decision-Making: Once the ball becomes opposed, players must make quick decisions about when and where to shoot, considering the positioning of the defenders and mini goals.• Defensive Pressure: The defender should focus on applying pressure to prevent the attacker from getting a clear shot on goal, while trying to force mistakes or recover possession.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for how long the attacker has to beat the mannequin and score. If they don’t manage to score within the time limit, possession switches.Focus: This progression encourages the attacker to make quicker decisions and increases urgency to score.
progression_two: Add Extra Defenders:Increase the defensive pressure by adding an additional defender once the attacker has passed the mannequin.Focus: This progression challenges the attacker to think more creatively and work harder to create space to score under increased pressure.

title: Betis Possession Transfer
instructions_setup: This 3v1 transfer rondo involves 3 teams of 2 players plus 1 neutral player. Play starts with a 2v1 in one grid, with the neutral player creating a 3v1 situation for the team in possession. The players in possession must make 3 passes before attempting to transfer the ball across the grids.The neutral player can travel freely across both grids, ensuring the team in possession is always playing a 3v1. If either of the 2 defenders wins possession, they switch with the 2 players who lost possession, continuing the drill without interruption.
coaching_notes: • Ball Movement: Encourage quick and accurate passing, ensuring that the team in possession maintains control while looking for opportunities to transfer the ball efficiently.• Use of Neutral Player: The neutral player should be used to create overloads and facilitate quick ball movement between grids, helping the team maintain possession.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders should work together to apply pressure and anticipate passing lanes, aiming to win the ball and force a switch.• Awareness of Space: Players in possession should remain aware of the entire playing area and use the neutral player to stretch the defense, creating more passing options.
progression_one: Add Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for each transfer. The team in possession must complete the transfer within 10-15 seconds, or possession automatically switches.Focus: This progression encourages quicker decision-making and faster ball movement, putting pressure on the team to execute under time constraints.
progression_two: Restrict Pass Types:Restrict the type of passes that can be made (e.g., only one-touch or no long passes).Focus: This progression emphasizes passing precision and forces players to think creatively while still maintaining control and tempo in the drill.

title: Betis Warm Up & SAQ
instructions_setup: In this warm-up drill, players must sprint towards a central station and stay on their toes while waiting for the coach to call either yellow or blue. On the coach’s call, players must react quickly and sprint around the called-out colour (either a mannequin or pole) before sprinting to the end.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions: Encourage players to stay focused and react as quickly as possible when the coach calls the colour, promoting agility and sharp decision-making.• Staying on Toes: Players should maintain a ready, athletic position, staying on their toes to ensure they can accelerate quickly in any direction.• Controlled Sprinting: Players should focus on sprinting with control, ensuring they can stop and change direction quickly without losing balance or speed.• Anticipation: Encourage players to anticipate the coach’s call and be mentally prepared to react instantly.
progression_one: Add Multiple Colour Calls:Instead of calling only one colour, the coach can call two or three colours in sequence, and players must react accordingly to each call.Focus: This progression challenges players to stay alert and develop quicker reaction times, adding a layer of complexity to the drill.
progression_two: Add Competitive Element:Make the drill competitive by timing how fast players can complete the sequence or by having them race against one another to the end.Focus: This progression increases intensity and adds an element of competition, helping to improve both speed and motivation during warm-ups.

title: Birmingham 2 Touch Finishing Game
instructions_setup: This 2-touch finishing challenge is a fun and competitive activity designed for forwards. A coach or server positioned behind the goal will chip a ball to the edge of the box. Teams of 2 will take turns, with each player in the team allowed one touch. The first player must stop or set the ball, and the second player should finish. Players are rewarded with points for each goal, and the coach can vary the type of ball (high, low, or driven) to add complexity and challenge.
coaching_notes: • First Touch: The first player should focus on controlling or setting the ball effectively, preparing it for a clean finish from the second player.• Finishing Technique: The second player should focus on precise and powerful finishing, ensuring they direct the ball on target with the right technique (e.g., inside of the foot, laces).• Timing and Communication: Players should communicate clearly to ensure smooth transitions between touches and to time the set-up and finish effectively.• Adaptability: Encourage players to adjust to different types of balls (high, low, driven) and develop their ability to finish in various situations.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce one defender who can try to intercept the pass or block the shot. The attacking team must complete the 2-touch sequence while dealing with defensive pressure.Focus: This progression challenges players to finish under pressure, improving composure and decision-making in tight situations.

title: Birmingham Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: In this mastery drill, 2 teams of 3 players will be in possession, while the final team of 3 is classified as the catchers. On the coach's whistle, all the attackers must dribble from one corner to any of the other 3 corners while the catchers attempt to win possession of the ball.If the catchers win possession, they will switch places with the team that lost the ball, keeping the drill dynamic and competitive.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Technique: Players should focus on using different dribbling techniques, such as changes of direction, speed, and close control, to evade the catchers.• Spatial Awareness: Attackers must be aware of their positioning and the positioning of the catchers, choosing the best corner to dribble to for maximum safety.• Defensive Pressure: Catchers should work together to press and intercept, using teamwork to force attackers into mistakes or regain possession.• Composure: Attackers should stay calm under pressure, using their dribbling skills and vision to maintain possession while moving to a new corner.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 30 seconds) for the attackers to make it to a corner. If they don’t successfully reach a corner within the time, they switch roles with the catchers.Focus: This progression increases urgency and encourages quicker decision-making and dribbling in tight situations.

title: Birmingham Countering Outnumbered
instructions_setup: Play starts with 2 unopposed finishes. Once the second finish is complete, one attacker, who starts on the left side of the penalty area, must quickly attack horizontally across the penalty area and attempt to score into one of the two mini goals. The two original shooters then transition to defend against the single attacker.The single attacker will be outnumbered (1v2), so it’s crucial that they attack as quickly as possible while the defenders are momentarily unbalanced and disorganized.
coaching_notes: • Quick Attack: The single attacker should focus on attacking at pace, using the brief window of defensive disorganization to create a clear shooting opportunity.• Defensive Transition: The two defending players must quickly regain their shape and communicate to cover the attacking player, ensuring they close down any potential shooting angles.• Finishing under Pressure: Attackers should focus on being clinical with their finish, taking advantage of the imbalance created by the fast transition.• Timing and Decision-Making: The defending players should work on their timing and decision-making, making sure to balance pressure with control to avoid leaving too much space for the attacker.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Attacker:Introduce a neutral attacker to join the attacking side, creating a 2v2 situation. This will force the defenders to communicate and work together to cover both attackers.Focus: This progression challenges defenders to work more closely and forces the attacking team to make quick, coordinated decisions to create scoring opportunities.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 10 seconds) for the attackers to score, forcing them to act with more urgency and take quicker shots on goal.Focus: This progression encourages faster decision-making and execution, creating a sense of urgency to exploit defensive disorganization.

title: Birmingham Midfield Build Up
instructions_setup: This build-up practice encourages a midfield 3 to maintain a well-structured shape, enabling smooth progression of the ball. The practice area is a large square divided into 4 separate zones.The midfield 3 must each occupy a different grid and use quick movements and rotations to receive the ball and progress it into the attacker. This encourages fluidity and positional awareness while promoting efficient ball circulation.If any of the defenders win possession, they can counter-attack towards the main goal. The defenders who began the practice unopposed will then enter live play, transitioning into the defensive phase.
coaching_notes: • Movement and Rotation: The midfield 3 should focus on making dynamic, well-timed movements to create passing options, ensuring they remain fluid and unpredictable for the opposition.• Positional Awareness: Each midfielder should be aware of their positioning relative to the other two midfielders and the attackers, ensuring that they provide support and options in every phase of the build-up.• Quick Passing: Encourage players to move the ball quickly and decisively, using short, sharp passes to maintain tempo and avoid defensive pressure.• Defensive Transition: If possession is lost, the team must quickly switch to defensive mode, with the defenders joining the live play to apply pressure and prevent a counter-attack.
progression_one: Restrict Pass Types:Restrict the midfielders to using only one-touch passes to increase speed and improve decision-making under pressure.Focus: This progression forces faster thinking and sharper execution, enhancing the midfielders' ability to progress the ball quickly while under pressure.

title: Birmingham Multi-Directional 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass from one player to another horizontally across the grid. The player receiving the ball can choose which goal they attack, as there are two goals inside a small grid (a mini version of a pitch). However, they can only attack in the direction of their first touch.This drill focuses on quick decision-making and precise control while encouraging attacking players to use their first touch to shape their play towards the goal they intend to attack.
