coaching_notes: • First Touch Control: The player receiving the ball should focus on taking a good first touch, directing it towards their chosen goal while also positioning themselves for an immediate attack.• Attacking with Purpose: Encourage the receiver to attack with intent, aiming to be decisive and direct in their approach to the goal they are facing.• Defender Pressure: The defender should stay on their toes, ready to react to the receiver’s movement, trying to anticipate and intercept the attacker’s next move.• Decision-Making: Emphasize the importance of making quick decisions on whether to attack, pass, or use skills to bypass the defender based on the first touch.
progression_one: Allow Two Touches:Allow the receiving player to take two touches before being locked into a direction. This will give the attacker more freedom to use deception skills (like feints or quick changes of direction) to evade the defender.Focus: This progression allows attackers to create more space and apply more creativity in their movement, challenging them to beat the defender using skillful dribbling.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 5 seconds) for the receiving player to make their move, forcing them to act quickly and apply more urgency in their decision-making.Focus: This progression encourages quick thinking and faster decision-making, improving the attacking player’s ability to perform under pressure.

title: Birmingham Narrow Overloads
instructions_setup: This practice involves 4 teams of 2 players each. The small-sided game starts 2v2, with both teams attempting to score into single mini goals placed on a narrow pitch.When in possession, teams can use the 2 bounce players ahead of them to connect and combine in order to create goal-scoring opportunities. The pitch also features end zones located 5 yards from either end, where players must be within to shoot. This restriction prevents players from shooting from anywhere, encouraging forward combination play and more structured attacking moves.
coaching_notes: • Use of Bounce Players: Teams should focus on using the bounce players effectively to create passing triangles and quick combinations that break down the defensive team.• Positioning in End Zones: Encourage players to move into the end zones with purpose, ensuring that they time their runs to receive the ball in a dangerous shooting position.• Combination Play: The focus should be on quick, purposeful passing and movement to break down defensive lines and open up space for a shot on goal.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should be vigilant and position themselves to cut off passing lanes to the bounce players, while also being ready to press quickly when possession is lost.
progression_one: Restrict Passing Zones:Limit the passing options of the attacking team by defining specific areas (e.g., half of the pitch) where they can pass the ball. This forces teams to be more creative and precise in their combination play.Focus: This progression encourages better decision-making and more purposeful movement, improving attacking creativity under pressure.

title: Birmingham One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This unopposed 1-to-1 finishing practice is designed to improve a centre forward’s decision-making, body positioning, and ability to finish quickly. The player receives a central pass just outside the penalty area, with a mannequin placed ahead to simulate a defender. The coach, positioned just behind the mannequin, will step to one side to close the space. The forward must scan early, take their first touch into the opposite space, and finish with minimal delay.
coaching_notes: • Scan Early Before Receiving – Constantly check the coach’s position before and during the pass to make a quick decision, identifying available space and pressure cues.• Positive First Touch – Take the first touch into space away from pressure, setting up the finish cleanly and quickly, while avoiding contact with the mannequin or passive defender.• Use Body to Protect – Angle your body to shield the ball when shifting left or right around the mannequin, creating separation and denying recovery runs.• Clinical Finishing – Hit the target with intent, using various surfaces depending on angle and distance from goal, focusing on accuracy before power to increase success rate.

title: Birmingham Rondo to Attacking Patterns
instructions_setup: This drill begins opposed and transitions into an unopposed attacking phase. Play starts with a 4v2 rondo in the center circle, where after 'x' number of successful passes, the attacking team can break out and complete an unopposed attacking phase.The attacking phase should consist of various combinations between the fullback and winger before delivering the ball into the number 9. The fullback and winger should focus on overlapping and underlapping runs to create space and confusion for the defenders, providing multiple options for a final pass.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing in the Rondo: The attacking team should focus on quick, sharp passes to maintain possession and create opportunities for the breakout phase.• Overlapping Runs: The fullback should look to overlap the winger, creating width and pulling defenders out of position. The winger can then use this extra space to receive the ball in more dangerous areas.• Underlapping Runs: The winger should also be prepared to underlap the fullback, making runs inside the fullback to receive the ball in a more central position. This can be especially effective when the defending team is focused on stopping the fullback’s overlapping run.• Combination Play: Encourage quick combination play between the fullback, winger, and the number 9 to break down the defensive line. The key is fluid movement and constant communication to create space for effective crosses or passes into the striker.• Attacking Final Phase: Once the ball is delivered to the number 9, they should focus on finishing with composure, using the space created by the fullback and winger’s movement.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Attacking Phase:Introduce one defender into the attacking phase to create a 3v2 situation, forcing the attacking players to work harder on their combinations and movements to outnumber the defense.Focus: This progression improves the attacking team’s ability to create and exploit space under pressure, while also encouraging effective decision-making in final-third situations.
progression_two: Add a Second Number 9:Introduce a second number 9 to the attacking phase, allowing for more varied attacking options and combinations. This creates more space for the winger and fullback to work with and provides more opportunities to finish the attack.Focus: This progression promotes the use of dynamic runs and combination play between the two strikers, encouraging more movement off the ball and increased options in the final third.

title: Blackpool Finishing From Underlaps
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on creating goalscoring opportunities from underlapping runs. The drill is designed to help players develop the ability to time and execute underlapping runs, typically by a midfield player or wide attacker, to exploit space between the full-back and center-backs (often referred to as the half-space). Players should work on both the timing of these runs and the ability to finish once the ball is delivered into the space.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Underlapping Runs – The key to successful underlapping runs is timing. Players making the underlap must time their runs to arrive in the half-space just as the ball is played, ensuring they can receive and finish quickly. Encourage players to look for opportunities where they can cut inside or attack the goal with their underlap.• Receiving the Ball in the Half-Space – Players should focus on receiving the ball in the half-space and preparing to take a shot or make a quick decision on how to finish. Encourage players to receive with their outside foot to allow for quicker control and a smoother transition to shooting.• Finishing Under Pressure – Once the ball is played into the underlapping runner, encourage them to finish with composure, aiming for the far post or the corners. Players should be reminded to stay calm under pressure and make the most of the opportunity to score.• Wide Player's Role – The player on the outside (the one playing the ball into the underlapping run) should focus on accurate passing. They need to deliver the ball into the space with precision, ensuring it’s easy for the underlapping player to receive and finish.
progression_one: Add a Defender to Press the FinisherIntroduce a passive defender to pressure the player making the underlapping run and the player finishing the attack. This encourages the attacker to finish quickly and with composure under pressure.Focus:Helps improve finishing under pressure and enhances decision-making in real game-like scenarios.
progression_two: Increase the Number of Underlapping RunsExpand the practice by allowing multiple players to make underlapping runs during the same attacking phase, thus creating more options for the ball carrier. Players should focus on identifying the best possible option for a pass, either to the underlap or another attacker.Focus:Increases attacking options, improves timing of underlapping runs, and encourages the ball carrier to make quicker decisions based on the available attacking options.

title: Blackpool Finishing into 1v1s
instructions_setup: In this high-tempo attacking practice, two players begin by dribbling toward the center, each going around their designated pole before finishing on goal unopposed. Immediately after their finishes, both players transition into defenders for a new phase, where two more players enter to attack in two simultaneous 1v1 scenarios. The practice flows in rotations, giving all players multiple reps focusing on finishing, transition speed, and both attacking and defending in 1v1 situations.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Starts – Players should focus on a sharp, controlled dribble around the pole and immediately look to finish with pace and accuracy. Encourage variety in finishing (low driven, placed, or powerful shots).• Transition Speed – After finishing, players must instantly shift into a defensive mindset. Quick reactions and defensive positioning are key to delaying or stopping the oncoming 1v1 attacker.• 1v1 Defending – Emphasize defensive footwork, body shape, and staying on the attacker’s inside shoulder. Defenders should aim to delay and force attackers away from goal.• 1v1 Attacking – Encourage attackers to be direct, creative, and decisive. Use body feints, quick changes of direction, and speed to beat the defender and finish.
progression_one: Competitive ScorekeepingAward points for successful finishes in both phases (initial unopposed and 1v1). Keep score between pairs or teams.Focus:Adds a competitive edge, encouraging quality finishing and intensity in both attacking and defensive efforts.
progression_two: Add a Passive Recovery DefenderAfter the unopposed finish, have the original shooter track back into the 1v1 zone as a recovering defender to create pressure from behind.Focus:Simulates real-game moments where attackers must finish under recovering pressure, and defenders learn to delay and recover from disadvantageous positions.

title: Blackpool Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: In this finishing drill, the striker begins by making a movement to either the left or right pole, as determined by the coach or server. As the striker makes this movement, a defender, who starts behind the server, begins to recover and apply pressure on the attacker. Once the attacker receives the pass, they must quickly turn and attack the goal to finish, while being closely pressured by the recovering defender.This drill works on both the striker's movement off the ball, their ability to finish under pressure, and their decision-making when closing down the goal.
coaching_notes: • Off-the-Ball Movement: Encourage the striker to make a sharp and purposeful movement towards the poles to create space for themselves. This movement should be explosive, allowing them to receive the ball in a favorable position to attack the goal.• Receiving Under Pressure: The striker must focus on controlling the ball efficiently despite pressure from the defender. Remind them to receive with their body open and prepare to shoot quickly, minimizing time on the ball.• Finishing Under Pressure: The striker should maintain composure when shooting under pressure. Encourage them to focus on placement over power and aim for the far corners of the goal to increase the likelihood of scoring.• Defender's Pressure: The recovering defender should apply pressure, forcing the striker to make a decision quickly. The attacker should be prepared to adjust their finish based on the defender's positioning.
progression_one: Increase Defender Pressure:Start the defender closer to the attacker, reducing the time and space for the striker to finish. This progression encourages the striker to be even more decisive in their movement and finishing.Focus: This will increase the challenge of finishing under pressure, simulating real match conditions where defenders are constantly closing down the attacker.
progression_two: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender who arrives shortly after the first. The attackers will now need to make quicker decisions and may need to look for a different finishing option.Focus: This progression replicates a more intense match situation where attackers are under more pressure from multiple defenders, improving their ability to handle stress and execute a quality finish.

title: Blackpool Positional Rondo
instructions_setup: In this positional rondo, the possession team plays 4v2 in the ball-sided grid and aims to maintain possession while looking to switch play continuously. Outside the grid, two players work back and forth between themselves. Once the ball inside the grid has been transferred, one of the outside players will transition into the grid to support the ball. The focus is on maintaining balance in possession and ensuring that transitions between grids are quick and efficient.
coaching_notes: • Positional AwarenessEncourage the possession team to maintain good positional balance at all times. Players should ensure they are always in a position to receive the ball and help with the switching of play. Make sure the player on the ball has options to pass to, while others move into space to support.• Quick TransitionsWhen the ball is switched to the outside, encourage the outside players to transition quickly into the grid. The speed of transition is key to ensuring the possession team can maintain the flow of the drill and keep the opposition defending. Timing and sharpness in movement are vital for keeping the rhythm of the practice.• Ball Movement and Switching PlayIn the ball-sided grid, stress the importance of quick, accurate passes to maintain possession while also looking for opportunities to switch play. The players inside should focus on quick ball circulation, looking to exploit space and create gaps for the outside players to transition in.• Defensive Pressure and Spatial AwarenessFor the defending players, their goal is to apply pressure and force mistakes in the ball-sided grid. They must work hard to close down passing lanes and force the possession team to make quick decisions. Encourage defenders to stay compact, working together to limit passing options.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession TeamLimit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2 touches maximum) to increase the speed of play and force quicker decisions.Focus: This progression encourages quicker ball movement and increases the intensity of the practice. It also helps the players focus on efficient passing and quick transitions.
progression_two: Add More DefendersIncrease the number of defenders in the central grid (e.g., 4v2 becomes 4v3).Focus: This will force the possession team to adapt, using better movement and switching to break down a stronger defensive presence. It simulates playing against a more structured opposition and improves decision-making under pressure.

title: Bournemouth 4 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on a mixture of unopposed and opposed finishing. The first 2 phases involve unopposed finishes, allowing players to focus on technique and timing. In the final 2 phases, a defender joins the practice, making the finishing scenarios opposed. The drill is designed to replicate real-game finishing situations, starting with basic techniques and progressing to more challenging, defended opportunities.
coaching_notes: • Technique in Unopposed PhasesDuring the unopposed phases, emphasize clean technique, including proper body positioning and striking technique. Encourage players to focus on accuracy and composure, especially when finishing inside the box. The lack of defensive pressure should allow them to work on their first touch and finish with precision.• Composure Under PressureOnce the defender joins in the final 2 phases, remind players to maintain composure when finishing under pressure. The defender will force them to make quicker decisions, so encourage players to focus on staying calm and making decisive, confident strikes on goal.• Creating Space for the FinishEncourage attackers to work on creating space between themselves and the defender. In the opposed phases, players should be aware of their positioning and look to make quick, intelligent movements to create space for a clean shot. This could be through feints, quick changes of direction, or timed runs into open areas.• Finishing from Various AnglesSince the defender will provide different types of pressure in the opposed phases, encourage players to adjust their finishing technique based on the angle and distance from goal. Whether they’re finishing a cross, cutting inside, or taking a shot from a tight angle, players should practice various finishing methods such as driven shots, chips, and first-time finishes.
progression_one: Add More DefendersAfter completing the original drill with one defender, progress to adding another defender or having the defender pressure the player from different angles (e.g., from the side or behind).Focus: This progression simulates more complex game situations, where attackers must deal with multiple defenders and adjust their approach accordingly.
progression_two: Limit Time to FinishIn the opposed phases, introduce a time limit (e.g., 3-5 seconds) for players to take a shot after receiving the ball.Focus: This progression increases the intensity of the practice, encouraging players to make quick decisions and focus on rapid execution under pressure.

title: Bucharest 2 Way Countering
instructions_setup: This dynamic counter-attacking practice begins in a central zone where three attacking players attempt to break defensive lines and play through to three teammates positioned on the opposite side. Between them are three defenders who aim to screen, intercept, and win possession. If the defenders win the ball, they immediately counter-attack toward the main goal, supported by wide players who join the attack quickly.Once this first counter is underway, the coach will immediately play a second ball into the opposite direction for the remaining players to launch their own counter-attack. This creates two simultaneous, rapid transitions, emphasizing speed of thought, recovery runs, and attacking intent from both teams.
coaching_notes: • Encourage fast ball movement and sharp passing through central areas – Players should focus on tempo and timing when trying to break defensive lines cleanly.• Highlight the positioning and body shape of screening defenders – Defenders must angle themselves properly to read passes and cut off central lanes effectively.• Promote explosive forward runs during the counter attack – Players must transition with urgency and support wide quickly to overload the defending side.• Emphasize scanning and reaction speed as play flips directions – All players must stay alert and react instantly when the second ball is introduced.
progression_one: Limit players to two-touch in central build-upRestrict the three central attackers to two touches each when attempting to break lines to increase the challenge and speed of play.Focus: Promotes sharper decision-making, quicker passing, and greater spatial awareness under time pressure.

title: Bucharest Build Up & Progression
instructions_setup: This build-up practice takes place inside a 30x50 yard grid divided into three horizontal zones. The possession team consists of two goalkeepers and five outfield players (7 total) who work together to maintain possession against five pressing defenders. The defenders are restricted so only one defender may occupy the central zone at any time, encouraging the possession team to switch play quickly between zones.By moving the ball across the three zones, the possession team can create numerical overloads in the central zone, exploiting the limited defensive presence there. This setup encourages smart switching, quick ball circulation, and exploiting space to retain control under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Encourage constant scanning and awareness to identify moments when the central zone is lightly defended – Players should exploit these overloads by switching play quickly and accurately.• Promote crisp, accurate passing and fast decision-making under pressure – Maintaining high tempo prevents defenders from recovering and reorganizing their shape effectively.• Stress the importance of support and movement off the ball to create multiple passing options across all zones – Active positioning is key to retain possession and manipulate defenders.• Remind defenders to coordinate pressing intensity while respecting the one-player limit in the central zone – This forces the possession team to be patient and creative with their ball circulation.
progression_one: Add a time limit for possession switches between zonesRequire the possession team to switch play between zones within a certain number of seconds to increase tempo and decision-making speed.Focus: Improves quick thinking, speed of execution, and pressure handling in tight spaces.
progression_two: Allow two defenders in the central zoneIncrease central defensive pressure by permitting two defenders in the central zone, forcing the possession team to find alternative ways to create overloads.Focus: Encourages more creative movement and passing options to break down increased defensive pressure.

title: Bucharest Central Breakout to Attack
instructions_setup: This central breakout practice is set inside a 15x15 yard grid where four players, including a goalkeeper, work together to progress the ball out from a tight central area. The main goal is to move the ball efficiently from this starting zone into the attacking final third, emphasizing quick combination play and effective positioning to break through the opponent’s initial defensive pressure.Once the ball is successfully played into the final third, the players immediately transition into a 3v3 attacking scenario where they look to create scoring opportunities. This drill develops quick decision-making, tight control under pressure, and seamless transition from build-up play to attack.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp, accurate passing and quick movement to break defensive lines in tight spaces – Players should focus on timing their runs and supporting the ball carrier effectively.• Encourage communication and awareness of available passing options to maintain possession under pressure – Constant scanning helps anticipate defensive pressure and identify breakthroughs.• Promote quick transitions from possession to attack once the ball enters the final third – Players must switch mindset instantly to capitalize on attacking opportunities.• Highlight the importance of positioning to create passing lanes and exploit defensive weaknesses – Effective spacing opens up more attacking options in the 3v3 phase.
progression_one: Limit players to two touches in the breakout phaseRestrict players to a maximum of two touches when moving the ball inside the starting grid to speed up play and improve technical control.Focus: Encourages sharper control, quicker passing, and improved ball mastery under pressure.

title: Bucharest Diagonal Penetration Patterns
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill involves two players working simultaneously around a marked grid, focusing specifically on diagonal passing patterns. Players aim to improve their ability to execute sharp, accurate diagonal passes that break lines and create forward momentum. The drill emphasizes body positioning, timing, and first-touch control to enable effective diagonal penetration through the opposition’s defensive shape.As the players move around the grid, they work on receiving the ball on the move and playing incisive diagonal passes to each other, simulating the quick changes of direction and space exploitation needed in match situations. The drill encourages quick decision-making, smooth transitions, and precision to help develop dynamic passing combinations.
coaching_notes: • Focus on proper body orientation to facilitate quick diagonal passes – Players should open up their hips to see passing lanes clearly and prepare for the next immediate action.• Emphasize crisp, well-weighted passes that penetrate lines effectively – Accurate passing speed and direction are crucial for consistently breaking defensive shapes cleanly.• Promote sharp first touches to control and direct the ball into attacking spaces – A quality first touch allows players to maintain flow and create immediate penetration opportunities.• Encourage constant scanning and communication to anticipate partner’s movements – Awareness helps players time passes and off-the-ball runs for maximum effectiveness and tempo.
progression_one: Limit touches to one or two per playerRestricting players to one or two touches increases the tempo and demands sharper control and passing, further developing quick thinking and technical proficiency under time constraints.Focus: Enhances speed of play and sharpens technical execution during fast diagonal passing sequences.

title: Bucharest Finishing Into 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with two players from opposite teams running into a small-sided grid, each completing an unopposed finish on one of the two goals guarded by two goalkeepers. After both players have taken their unopposed shots, a new ball is introduced, triggering a live 1v1 battle in the same grid. This drill combines finishing practice with a quick transition to competitive defensive and attacking play.The drill develops finishing under minimal pressure before immediately challenging players with a fast-paced, high-intensity 1v1 duel. It emphasizes composure in front of goal as well as sharp reaction and dribbling skills under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Focus on clean, composed finishing technique in the unopposed phase – Players should prioritize accuracy and confident shot selection before pressure is applied.• Encourage quick transition from finishing to immediate defensive or attacking mindset – Players must shift focus rapidly to adapt to the 1v1 challenge.• Stress the importance of sharp first touches and controlled ball manipulation in the 1v1 – Effective ball control is key to gaining advantage in tight duels.• Promote intense body positioning and timing in the 1v1 phase – Players should use proper stance and quick reactions to win duels and create scoring chances.
progression_one: Limit the 1v1 phase to two touches maximum per playerRestrict touches to increase speed of play and technical precision, forcing quicker dribbling decisions and more efficient attacking movements.Focus: Develops sharper control and faster decision-making during pressured offensive situations.

title: Bucharest Overlaps & Underlaps
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical drill focuses on wingers and full backs working together in wide areas. Two players combine using a variety of overlap and underlap runs to create space and crossing opportunities. The drill emphasizes timing, sharp passing, and effective movement off the ball to break down imaginary defensive setups on the flank.After completing their combinations, the wide players deliver crosses into the penalty area targeting one of two mini goals. These finishing zones replicate the typical positions forwards occupy, helping players develop accuracy and decision-making when delivering crosses under realistic attacking scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Focus on sharp, well-timed overlaps and underlaps – Players should coordinate runs closely to create clear crossing lanes and confuse defenders effectively.• Encourage crisp, accurate passing with proper weight and timing – Effective ball delivery supports smooth attacking combinations in wide areas consistently.• Promote quality first-time crossing to the targeted mini goals – Crosses should be precise and aimed at zones where forwards typically finish efficiently.• Emphasize communication and awareness between winger and full back – Verbal and non-verbal cues improve synchronization and timing of runs significantly.
progression_one: Add a passive defender to the wide areaIntroduce a passive defender to increase pressure on combinations, encouraging quicker decision-making and sharper execution. This also helps players adapt to mild defensive resistance while maintaining technical control.Focus: Develops technical skills under mild defensive pressure and improves movement timing and awareness.
progression_two: Limit players to one or two touches during combinationsRestrict touches to increase tempo and enhance first-time passing and movement. This forces players to think faster and improves their ability to execute precise technical actions under speed.Focus: Promotes quicker play, better control, and heightened awareness in tight spaces with faster decision-making.

title: Bucharest Reactions & 1v1
instructions_setup: This reactive 1v1 drill begins with two players sprinting into a grid facing each other. The attacking player must quickly decide to sprint left or right to collect one of two balls placed in those directions. Using body feints and deceptive movement, the attacker aims to create separation from the defender before reaching the chosen ball.Once the attacker has possession, the 1v1 phase is live and they must use their skills and speed to beat the defender and score into one of two mini goals positioned behind them. This drill sharpens reaction time, decision-making, and quick attacking transitions under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize explosive starts and quick reaction to the coach’s signal – Players must develop sharp responsiveness to sudden changes in direction and decision-making.• Encourage use of body feints and deceptive footwork to create separation – Attacking players should focus on misdirecting the defender to gain space effectively.• Stress maintaining control of the ball during the initial sprint and transition – Smooth ball control ensures the attacker can capitalize on the created separation quickly.• Promote quick decision-making and composure when choosing which ball to sprint towards – Players need to make fast, confident choices under pressure to succeed in this drill.
progression_one: Restrict attacker to one or two touches after collecting the ballLimit touches to force quicker decision-making and more precise execution during the 1v1 attacking phase, simulating higher pressure scenarios.Focus: Develops sharper technical skills and faster attacking decisions under pressure.

title: Bucharest Transfer & Score Rondo
instructions_setup: This transfer rondo takes place in a 15x30 yard grid divided into two 15x15 yard zones. One team plays 4+1 versus 4 in one zone, working on quick, precise passing and possession. After completing a set number of passes, the team in possession can either dribble or pass to the opposite, currently empty zone. In that zone, they can attack and score into two mini goals, emphasizing speed and accuracy in transferring play.Once the ball is successfully transferred and scored on one side, the game restarts there and the team attempts to switch back across to the original side, encouraging rapid transitions, spatial awareness, and quick decision-making in switching play effectively.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, sharp passing to maintain tempo and pressure on defenders – Rapid ball movement forces defenders to constantly adjust their positioning and shape effectively.• Stress the importance of accurate and timely transfers between zones – Precise passing or dribbling exploits space efficiently and creates scoring chances effectively.• Promote good communication and scanning before switching play – Players must anticipate teammates’ runs and be ready to receive the ball under pressure.• Remind players to keep high intensity and speed during transitions – Fast switches disrupt defensive shape and increase attacking opportunities significantly.
progression_one: Add passive defenders in the receiving zone before transferIntroduce one or two passive defenders in the receiving zone to increase difficulty, forcing players to make sharper decisions and more precise transfers under pressure.Focus: Improves passing accuracy, decision-making speed, and composure when under mild defensive pressure consistently.
progression_two: Limit touches to two per playerRestrict the possession team to a maximum of two touches each, speeding up play and demanding faster control and sharper passing.Focus: Enhances technical ability, quick thinking, and sharper execution in high-tempo, pressured situations.

title: Burton Albion 3rd Man Passing
instructions_setup: In this passing practice, the side players will alternate continuously to play 3rd man passing combinations while making short, sharp movements to and from the outer cones. The focus is on quick, dynamic movement and timing of the passes to keep the ball moving quickly and effectively.
coaching_notes: • Timing of MovementPlayers must time their movements well to receive the ball in space. Encourage the side players to make angled runs, timing their movement to meet the pass at the right moment and position. They should always be thinking one step ahead, anticipating the next pass.• Quick and Accurate PassingThe emphasis is on quick, sharp passes. Encourage players to play with accuracy and pace, making sure each pass is directed to a teammate’s feet or space. The third man pass should be delivered with enough pace to allow the next player to continue the move without hesitation.• Use of SpacePlayers should be aware of the space around them and use it effectively. The movement should not just be about running to the cone, but rather about creating space, both for themselves and their teammates. Proper use of space will allow for easier third man combinations and better flow in the practice.• Transition Between Attacking and Defending RolesAs players alternate positions, they need to transition quickly between attacking and defensive mindsets. After a pass or combination, players should be ready to switch roles, either by pressing or supporting in different areas, ensuring fluid transitions within the practice.
progression_one: Increase Passing DistanceAllow the side players to pass over a longer distance or to a player farther away to develop their ability to execute third man combinations in a more expansive scenario.Focus: This progression works on both passing technique over longer distances and better spatial awareness.
progression_two: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender who can close down space or make interceptions, forcing the attackers to be quicker and more precise with their passes.Focus: This progression adds a defensive challenge, helping players improve under pressure and develop decision-making skills.

title: Burton Albion 5v5+2 Possession
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice focuses on maintaining possession while encouraging quick transitions both in attack and defense. The attacking team (possessing team) aims to accumulate as many passes as possible, earning 1 point for every ‘X’ number of passes completed (e.g., 5 passes, 7 passes). During possession, the 2 neutral players join the attacking team to create a 7v5 phase.The defending team must work to regain possession and then score into any of the 4 mini goals, promoting a counter-pressing mindset from the attacking team if possession is lost. Once possession changes hands, the neutral players transition to the defending team to help in scoring and applying pressure on the new attacking team.
coaching_notes: • Possession Focus – Encourage the team in possession to focus on quick passing and movement to break down the defense. The neutral players should add numerical superiority, providing passing options and ensuring fluidity in the attack. The possession team should look to use the width of the grid and make quick, decisive passes to maintain control.• Quick Transitions – The defending team should be encouraged to counter-attack quickly once they win possession, aiming to score in one of the mini goals. The attacking team should focus on counter-pressing immediately when they lose possession, working to regain the ball as soon as possible to prevent a quick counter from the defenders.• Neutral Players’ Role – The neutral players play a key role in both phases. In attack, they should help to maintain possession and provide support for their team. When possession changes, they immediately transition to help the defending team and increase their numbers in the pressing and attacking phase.• Defensive Shape – The defending team should maintain compactness and focus on anticipating passes to break up the play. They need to be quick in closing down passing lanes and not allow the possession team to make too many consecutive passes. Once they win the ball, their aim is to transition quickly into attack.
progression_one: Limit the Number of TouchesLimit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches per player) to encourage quicker passing and decision-making. This will increase the pace of the game and encourage quicker transitions.Focus:Improves the speed of play, encouraging players to think and act faster under pressure.
progression_two: Add Scoring Zones for the Possession TeamTo encourage the attacking team to play forward and not just focus on possession, add scoring zones where they can score points if they successfully pass the ball into certain areas or mini-goals. This incentivizes the attacking team to progress the ball and create goal-scoring opportunities, rather than just completing passes.Focus:Adds a goal-scoring element to possession play, making it more game-like and encouraging the attacking team to move the ball forward more effectively.

title: Burton Albion Breakout Rondo
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on maintaining possession and transitioning between possession and pressure phases. Play starts with a 4v2 rondo in an 8x8 grid. The two defending players work to regain possession and then pass the ball out of the 8x8 grid into a larger area. Once the ball is successfully played out of the smaller grid, the second phase begins: an 8v4 rondo inside the larger area. The team in possession aims to complete a specific number of successful passes (X amount) during the 8v4 phase before the practice restarts.The four players who transition from in-possession to out-of-possession must now work together to win the ball back within the X amount of passes to score points.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions – The key to success in this drill is the speed of transition. The defenders need to quickly shift from pressing in the 8x8 grid to pressing in the larger area. Likewise, the attackers need to maintain possession under pressure and quickly make decisions to exploit space once they have regained the ball.• Communication – Encourage constant verbal communication between players, both in terms of organizing the defensive press and making sure the attacking team is aware of the number of passes needed to complete the phase. Players should be in constant motion, scanning the field for passing options and potential pressure.• Possession Under Pressure – The players in possession during the 8v4 phase should focus on quick passing and movement off the ball to maintain possession and increase the chance of completing the designated number of passes. The attacking team should also look to exploit any gaps in the defending team’s shape.• Defensive Shape and Pressure – The four defenders in the larger area must stay compact and press intelligently. Encourage them to anticipate passes, close down passing lanes, and be aggressive in winning the ball back. If the defenders win the ball, they should look to immediately transition into attack by passing the ball to the designated area (outside the larger grid).
progression_one: Limit the Number of Touches for AttackersLimit the number of touches each player can take in the 8v4 phase (e.g., 2 touches). This forces the attacking team to make quicker decisions and increases the tempo of the practice.Focus:Improves speed of play and decision-making, encouraging attackers to think and pass quickly under pressure.
progression_two: Add Scoring Opportunities for AttackersAdd small mini-goals or cones inside the larger area that the attackers can aim to pass the ball through after completing the X amount of passes. This adds a goal-scoring aspect to the possession phase and provides more focus for the attacking team.Focus:Increases the attacking team’s motivation to complete successful passes while also simulating real game situations where the focus is not just maintaining possession but also progressing the ball forward.

title: Burton Albion Crossing Repetition
instructions_setup: In this drill, the team works on switching play from side to side across the attacking third to create space and unbalance the defense. After a series of quick, precise passes to shift the ball horizontally, the winger receives the ball in space without immediate pressure and delivers a cross.The winger’s target options include two mini goals: one positioned at the front post and another in the cut-back zone, encouraging varied crossing angles and quick, decisive finishing. Additionally, there is a larger goal placed deeper in the box for clipped or lofted crosses aimed behind the defensive line.The drill focuses on effective ball circulation, creating quality crossing opportunities, and precise delivery to different attacking zones.
coaching_notes: • Effective Switching – Encourage quick, accurate switches of play with crisp passing to exploit space and unbalance defenders, forcing them to shift rapidly.• Winger’s Crossing Decision – Teach wingers to assess teammate movement and positioning carefully, choosing between front post, cut-back, or deeper clipped crosses depending on the defensive shape.• Timing of Runs – Attackers must time their runs intelligently, arriving just ahead or alongside the cross to maximize goal-scoring chances.• Crossing Technique – Focus on delivering a variety of crosses—driven, clipped, and low—each matched to the run and positioning of attackers for optimal finish quality.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure on WingerIntroduce a defender applying realistic, light pressure on the winger to simulate game intensity, forcing quicker decisions and encouraging improved composure under pressure.Focus:Enhances crossing accuracy, decision-making speed, and calmness under increasing defensive challenges.
progression_two: Limit Number of Passes Before CrossRestrict the attacking team to a maximum of three passes before the winger delivers the cross, encouraging faster ball circulation and quicker attacking transitions.Focus:Develops rapid playmaking skills, increases urgency, and improves ability to create quality chances under time constraints.

title: Burton Albion Finishing into 1v1
instructions_setup: This dynamic attacking practice focuses on quick transitions, finishing, and 1v1 play. Two players start by dribbling a ball each toward two designated poles. Upon reaching the poles, each player leaves their ball beside it, then quickly switches direction to collect the other player’s ball. One player attacks the goal immediately for an unopposed finish. The second player dribbles around a top mini goal before re-entering the area to create a 1v1 situation against the original attacker, who now transitions into a defender.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Transition – Encourage players to execute the switch and collect the new ball at speed. A quick transition helps simulate game-like reactions and maximizes pressure on the defender.• Composure in Finishing – The initial attacker should focus on taking a controlled first touch and executing a clean finish under no pressure.• 1v1 Attacking – Attackers must be direct, use feints or body movement, and recognize the defender’s body position to either go around or cut inside.• Defensive Recovery – After finishing, the first attacker must quickly switch mindsets and recover into a defensive shape. Emphasize speed, positioning, and delaying the attacker rather than diving in.
progression_one: Timed Finish WindowAdd a time constraint for the unopposed finish (e.g., must shoot within 3 seconds of collecting the ball).Focus:Develops urgency, quick decision-making, and improves players’ ability to finish under time pressure.
progression_two: Live Pressure During FinishThe second player no longer goes around the mini goal and instead closes the attacker immediately after the switch, turning the initial finish into a pressured 1v1 from the start.Focus:Increases intensity and challenges both attackers and defenders to react quickly and execute under pressure from the beginning of the sequence.Let me know if you’d like a quick visual diagram to go with this, or if you want all the Week 61 drills compiled into a single session outline!

title: Burton Albion Finishing into Attacking 3v2
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on both finishing and defending in attacking 3v2 situations. The drill begins with two attackers receiving a pass and having a maximum of 2 touches: the first touch to control the ball and the second touch to finish the attack. After the two finishes are complete, the two attackers will quickly transition to defense, where they will work together to defend against a 3v2 attack from the opposing team.
coaching_notes: • Finishing Under Pressure – The attackers should focus on completing the finish with two controlled touches. The first touch should be precise to set up the second, ensuring that they can finish with accuracy under game-like pressure.• Quick Transition to Defend – After completing the finishing phase, attackers must immediately transition to defense, shifting from an attacking to a defensive mindset. Emphasize quick decision-making to close down space and mark attacking players effectively.• Defending 3v2 – Defenders must communicate and work together to cover the attacking players. Focus on positioning, tracking runs, and deciding when to engage the ball carrier and when to cover the passing lanes.• Shooting with Composure – Attackers should remain calm and composed when finishing, focusing on placing the ball in the corners or aiming for the near or far post. The goal is to develop the ability to finish under pressure with limited touches.
progression_one: Add a Defender in the Finishing PhaseIntroduce a passive defender to apply light pressure during the finishing phase, forcing attackers to make quicker decisions and improve their ability to finish under slightly more pressure.Focus:Increases the intensity of the finishing phase and encourages attackers to handle defensive pressure while making quick decisions.
progression_two: Increase the Speed of TransitionReduce the time attackers have to transition from attack to defense. For example, once the finishing phase is complete, give the attackers only a few seconds to get into their defensive positions. This will create a sense of urgency and mimic game-like transitions.Focus:Improves fitness, mental focus, and the ability to transition quickly between attack and defense.

title: Burton Albion Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: In this finishing practice, play starts with a chipped pass into a deeper player. From this initial pass, the attackers will work in a 2v1 scenario, aiming to create space and generate a goal-scoring opportunity. The defender will apply pressure to the ball carrier, while the line of mannequins acts as an offside line, restricting attacking options and increasing the difficulty of the pass and run combination.The mannequins simulate defensive pressure by marking a line that attackers must navigate carefully. The timing of runs and the weight of the pass are critical to successfully breaking the defensive line and finishing under pressure. This practice challenges both the attackers' and defenders' decision-making, timing, and ability to perform under match-like conditions.
coaching_notes: • Attacker Runs – Attackers should focus on timing their runs to avoid running into the mannequins or being caught offside. Their runs must be dynamic and decisive, using the space behind the defender or around the mannequins to create opportunities for a goal.• Weight of Pass – The player providing the pass must focus on the weight and timing to ensure the attacking player can receive the ball without being closed down by the defender. The pass should be perfectly timed to meet the attacker as they make their run, allowing them to take a clean touch and finish.• Finishing Under Pressure – Once the ball is played to the attacker, they should finish quickly and calmly under pressure. Encourage players to focus on composure and accuracy rather than trying to finish too quickly or with too much power. The goal is to place the ball in a corner or finish with a well-timed touch.• Defender’s Role – The single defender should focus on pressuring the ball carrier while trying to anticipate the attacker’s movements and force them into a less advantageous position. The defender must also pay attention to covering the space created by the mannequins and adjusting their positioning accordingly.
progression_one: Add a Second DefenderIntroduce a second defender to the drill, creating a more challenging situation for the attackers. This will require them to move the ball quicker and be more precise with their passing and decision-making. The attackers will need to think fast to create space and exploit the overload.Focus:Improves attackers' ability to exploit space and finish in higher-pressure situations with multiple defenders.
progression_two: Vary the Type of FinishEncourage players to vary the type of finish based on the situation. This could include driven shots, chips, or volleys depending on the timing of the run and where the ball is played. This progression will help attackers to develop a more diverse set of finishing techniques and the ability to adapt to different types of chances.Focus:Develops versatility in finishing and decision-making based on the type of pass and pressure faced.

title: Burton Albion Receive in Pockets & Finishing
instructions_setup: In this attacking practice, one of the three attacking players drops between the lines to receive a ball from one of the outer coaches. Once the first touch is made, play becomes live, and a 3v2 attack will unfold. This practice is multi-sided, meaning two attacks can play out at once, or they can play alternatively in a head-to-head format. The focus is on receiving the ball in pockets of space, quick decision-making, and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Between the LinesEncourage the attacking players to drop into the space between the lines, keeping their body open to the ball and scanning for both the ball and the defenders around them. The first touch should be sharp and directed into space to set up a quick attack. Teach players to create space for themselves by using intelligent movement and not standing still.• Quick Transition to AttackOnce the ball is received, the attacking player should quickly transition into a 3v2 attacking situation. Players should aim to play quickly to exploit the numerical advantage and finish the attack efficiently. Encourage players to make quick passes, look for a combination play, and finish under pressure to improve speed of play.• Decision-Making in 3v2In a 3v2 situation, the attacking team should focus on making the correct decisions based on the defenders’ positioning. If one defender is committed to pressing, players should be encouraged to exploit the space left open. The attacker on the ball should be decisive, whether to take on the defender, play a quick pass, or look for an immediate shot on goal.• Finishing Under PressureOnce the ball is played into the attacking players, they should focus on finishing quickly and efficiently. They must be aware of the pressure from the defending players and make sure they finish accurately, using the correct technique for the situation. Encourage calm and composed finishing in front of goal, whether it's a first-time shot or a controlled finish.
progression_one: Add Pressure to Receiving PlayerIntroduce a passive defender to apply pressure on the receiving player as soon as they take their first touch.Focus: This progression forces the receiving player to handle pressure, improve their first touch under pressure, and make quicker decisions on the ball.
progression_two: Limit Touches for AttackersLimit the number of touches the attacking players can take (e.g., 2 touches maximum).Focus: This will increase the intensity of the practice and improve the attacking players' ability to make quick decisions, improve ball control, and execute quick passes in tight spaces.

title: Cambridge 3-2 Build Up Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical practice focuses on rehearsing three different build-up variations using a 3-2 shape with a box midfield. The setup allows players to work through structured movement patterns and passing sequences that mirror real-game situations where teams build from the back using three defenders and two central midfielders. The aim is to increase familiarity with positional roles, movement timing, and the types of combinations used to progress the ball through thirds in a controlled, predictable way.
coaching_notes: • Positional Discipline – Players must maintain their roles within the 3-2 structure, understanding how their positioning supports ball progression and team shape retention.• Timing of Movement – Midfielders should coordinate their movement in sync with the ball to arrive into pockets of space as the pass is played, not before.• Weight and Direction of Pass – All passes must be played with the appropriate pace and direction to allow for fluid combinations and support the intended rhythm of each pattern.• Scanning and Detail – Encourage players to scan before receiving and to provide quality detail on passes, such as body shape, foot selection, and pass timing.
progression_one: Add Passive Pressing TriggersIntroduce passive defenders who apply light pressure to guide the build-up in specific directions.Focus: Encourages players to read pressure cues and adjust positioning and decisions accordingly.
progression_two: Apply Time Constraints to Each PatternSet a time limit to complete each build-up sequence from start to finish.Focus: Develops tempo, urgency, and decision-making under realistic match tempo conditions.

title: Cambridge 3-D-3 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 3D3 formation down into specific zones where the possession team will play 4v2. The team in possession must move the ball from grid to grid, with the 2 outer grids offering larger space and the central grid offering lesser space, replicating a tight and congested midfield zone.
coaching_notes: • Ball Movement and Quick Passing – Players in the possession team should focus on moving the ball quickly between the grids. Emphasize one- or two-touch passing to maintain a fast tempo and avoid being closed down by the defenders.• Awareness of Space – Players must always be aware of their position relative to the space in each grid. When transitioning from the outer grids to the central grid, players need to adjust their positioning to deal with the increased pressure in the tighter space.• Defender Positioning and Pressuring – The defending players must remain compact and work together to close down passing lanes and limit the space available to the attacking team. Communication is key to maintaining defensive shape and ensuring the possession team doesn’t break through.• Transition and Counter-Pressing – Once the defending team wins possession, they should focus on transitioning quickly into an attacking mindset, using the outer grids to exploit space and counter-attack. Encourage immediate pressure to prevent the attacking team from regaining the ball.
progression_one: Increase Pressing IntensityAllow the defending team to add an additional player after every successful pass made by the possession team (4v3, 4v4, etc.). This progression will increase the defensive pressure and force the attacking team to adjust their passing and positioning.Focus: This progression tests the possession team’s ability to deal with changing defensive numbers and to find solutions under more pressure.
progression_two: Add Target ZonesAdd mini-goals or target zones at the edge of the grid, where the possession team must pass the ball into before completing the transition.Focus: This progression encourages the possession team to focus on passing accuracy and precise movement when transitioning between the grids, ensuring that each pass leads to a productive outcome.

title: Cambridge 3v2 With Attacking Sprints
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass from the defenders into one of the three attacking players. Upon receiving the ball, the attacking players must attack 3v2 and attempt to score into the goal.If the attacking team scores, the defending 2 must sprint up and back down through the two gates located on either side of the pitch. If the attacking 3 fail to score, they must sprint down and back up through the same two gates.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Speed and Decision Making – The attacking players should focus on quick decision-making, utilizing the overload to exploit the 3v2 advantage. Encourage direct runs towards goal, mixing up their approach between dribbling and passing to break down the defenders.• Defensive Compactness and Communication – The defending team must communicate and maintain a compact shape while defending the 3v2 overload. They should work together to funnel attackers towards less dangerous areas and reduce goal-scoring opportunities.• Transition to Sprints – After each attack, emphasize the importance of quickly transitioning into the sprints. Players should push themselves to recover quickly, whether they are attacking or defending, as the sprinting component adds an additional layer of physicality and intensity to the drill.• Restoring Positional Balance – When the defenders fail to stop the attack, they must be quick to recover, sprinting through the gates before immediately returning to defensive positions. Similarly, if the attacking team doesn’t score, they must transition quickly into defense for the next rep.
progression_one: Add Time LimitSet a time limit for each attacking phase, encouraging the attacking players to complete their 3v2 and shoot on goal within a set time frame (e.g., 10 seconds).Focus: This progression emphasizes speed in the attack and quick decision-making, as well as time management for the attacking team.
progression_two: Switch Attacking and Defensive RolesAfter a set number of repetitions or once one team has scored a certain amount, switch the attacking and defending roles to ensure all players engage in both attacking and defensive situations.Focus: This progression provides balanced practice for all players, ensuring they develop skills in both attacking and defending while maintaining high-intensity sprints.

title: Cambridge Attacking Corner Routine #1
instructions_setup: This unopposed corner routine drill is designed to help players learn various corner delivery techniques and movements to create goal-scoring opportunities. The team will practice their set-piece routine with a focus on timing, spacing, and coordination. Players will position themselves according to the chosen routine (e.g., near post, far post, edge of the box, etc.) and work to execute the set play under minimal pressure.The corner taker will deliver the ball into the designated area, while the other players make runs to attack the ball or create space. The focus is on smooth, well-timed movements and effective ball delivery. The drill is unopposed, allowing the attacking team to concentrate on executing their routine to perfection.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Ensure that attacking players time their runs to the ball correctly. Whether it’s attacking the near post, far post, or edge of the box, the players should be well-timed in their movements to meet the delivery.• Movement to Create Space: Players should work on off-the-ball movement to pull defenders out of position, making it easier for teammates to get a clear shot at goal. Movement should be quick and dynamic, with players changing direction to create space in key areas.• Delivery Quality: Emphasize the importance of delivering the ball with the correct weight, pace, and accuracy. The corner taker must consistently place the ball into the designated area, whether it’s a driven cross, floated ball, or short corner.• Target Areas: Players should understand where to attack based on the type of delivery (e.g., near post, far post, or central). Each player should be aware of their role in relation to the ball's flight path and their teammates’ movements.• Communication: Encourage clear communication between the corner taker and attacking players. This ensures everyone knows when to make their run and where the ball will be delivered.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to lightly pressurize the attackers during the delivery and movement. The defenders should focus on tracking runs and challenging for the ball but not actively blocking or winning it.Focus: Develops the ability to execute corner routines while under light pressure, simulating more realistic game situations and forcing players to adjust their timing and runs.

title: Cambridge Attacking in Wide Areas
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass from deep into a wide grid where players are matched up 2v2. The player who played the original pass must move into the grid at speed to create a 3v2 scenario. In this scenario, the attacking players attempt to progress the play before crossing into the box for an unopposed attacker. If the defending 2 win possession, they should attempt to score in the goals positioned towards the center of the field. If the defending 2 score, the attacking 3 players must complete a sprint to replicate a moment of transition.
coaching_notes: • Quick Entry into Wide Areas – The player who plays the initial pass into the wide grid should move quickly to join the grid and create the 3v2 scenario. Emphasize the importance of timing to ensure that they enter the grid at the right moment to support the attack and create overloads.• Attacking Combinations – Encourage the attacking players to combine quickly in the 3v2 scenario, focusing on making sharp, accurate passes and creating space for each other. This will allow them to progress the ball towards the box with speed and precision.• Crossing and Finishing – Once the play progresses into the final third, the attacker must focus on delivering an accurate, early cross into the box for the unopposed attacker. The receiver should time their run to meet the cross and finish efficiently.• Defending and Transitioning – When the defending 2 win possession, they must transition quickly to attack the central goals. Encourage defenders to act decisively and exploit the moment of transition to score, while attackers should respond by sprinting to mimic a game-like counterattack.
progression_one: Add a Second DefenderIntroduce a second defender in the central zone to make the defending team more balanced and give the attacking team a greater challenge. This will help develop their ability to break down defensive units with quick and precise passes.Focus: Creating overloads and maintaining control under pressure in wide areas.
progression_two: Time Limits on AttacksLimit the amount of time the attacking players have to score by introducing a countdown or a set number of passes (e.g., 3 passes) before they must cross. This will encourage faster play and improve decision-making under pressure.Focus: Enhancing attacking speed and decision-making while under time constraints.

title: Cambridge Overlap & 3rd Man Technical
instructions_setup: This technical passing warm-up allows players to develop multiple attacking patterns, including 3rd man combinations, overlapping runs, and underlapping runs. The drill encourages fluid movement and communication between players as they execute these attacking patterns to break defensive lines.
coaching_notes: • Fluid Movement – Players should focus on maintaining constant movement off the ball to create passing lanes and space for others. Overlapping and underlapping runs should be well-timed to avoid crowding the attacking area and to maximize options for the passer.• Timing of the 3rd Man Run – Players making the 3rd man run should focus on timing their movement to arrive in space at the right moment, allowing them to receive the ball with enough time to make a decisive action towards goal.• Pass Selection and Precision – The player in possession should be encouraged to make accurate passes into the path of the runner, whether it's for an overlap or a 3rd man combination. Precision in passing will ensure that the attacking players maintain momentum and create high-quality opportunities.• Anticipation and Communication – Encourage players to anticipate their teammates' movements, making sure they communicate with visual or verbal cues before executing the runs. This helps to ensure that overlaps and underlaps are effective and lead to productive attacking situations.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a passive defender who will apply pressure on the ball carrier, encouraging the attacking players to make quicker decisions and refine their timing. The defender should try to intercept or disrupt passes without fully committing to a tackle.Focus: This progression challenges players to maintain composure under pressure while still executing the planned attacking movements.
progression_two: Introduce a Target PlayerAdd a target player at the far end of the grid or zone, where the attacking players aim to deliver the final pass. This will allow the team to focus on completing the attacking patterns with a clear goal in mind, finishing the drill with a shot or cross.Focus: This will emphasize the importance of combining and overlapping runs with the ultimate goal of creating scoring chances through effective passes and finishes.

title: Celtic Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a dribble from the deepest central attacker, initiating a 4v3 attacking overload. The ball carrier passes to one of two wide players, triggering the attack. From that moment, four attackers (including the initial runner) play against three defenders in a dynamic attacking phase. The initial ball carrier is encouraged to continue their run as a supporting midfielder, either arriving late into the box or creating space with off-the-ball movement. The focus is on exploiting overloads through timing, positioning, and quick combinations.
coaching_notes: • Midfield Runner Timing – The initial ball carrier must time their support run effectively. Arriving too early can crowd space; arriving late can create the perfect cutback or shooting opportunity.• Width and Depth – Wide players should stay high and wide to stretch the back line and open passing channels. Central attackers must create depth by running behind or offering central support.• Clever Movement – Encourage attackers to use decoy runs, rotations, and diagonal movements to drag defenders out of position and create space for teammates.• Speed and Precision – The overload must be exploited quickly. Encourage quick ball movement, one-touch combinations, and decisive final actions (pass, cross, or shot).
progression_one: Recovering Midfielder DefenderAdd a recovering defender who joins from behind after the ball is played wide, potentially balancing the numbers to 4v4.Focus:Increases intensity and tests the attackers’ ability to recognize shifting overloads and adjust movement/timing accordingly.
progression_two: Directional Defending with Counter GoalAllow the defending team to counter into a mini goal if they win possession, forcing attackers to protect against transition and encouraging better structure in overload play.Focus:Develops attacking shape awareness, transition defense, and encourages purposeful possession with defensive cover in mind.

title: Celtic Hexagonal Possession
instructions_setup: In this possession-based practice, 7 players will attempt to keep possession of the ball against a defending team of 3 in a hexagonal-shaped grid with 4 mini goals positioned on the outside. The aim for the 7 players in possession is to accumulate 10 passes for a point.The defending team should attempt to break up play by intercepting or forcing errors from the attacking team. Should they win possession cleanly, they must attempt to score into any of the mini goals located around the outside of the grid. This encourages defenders to work on quick transitions and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: The players in possession should focus on quick, sharp passes to maintain possession and move the defenders around, creating space for new passing options.• Support and Angle of Support: Players should always offer support at the right angles, making sure they are available for a pass and keeping the ball moving fluidly to avoid being closed down.• Defensive Pressing: The defending team should work on coordinated pressing, closing passing lanes, and forcing the attacking team into tight situations to regain possession quickly.• Transitions to Attack: Once the defending team wins the ball, they should look to transition quickly, aiming to score in one of the mini goals as fast as possible. Defenders must stay focused and make quick decisions to capitalize on turnover situations.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Increase the number of defenders to 4, creating a 7v4 situation. This forces the attacking team to be more precise in their passing and more creative in finding space.Focus: This progression challenges the attacking players to move the ball even faster and be more dynamic in their positioning to break down a stronger defensive setup.

title: Chelsea 1v1 ATK & Transition
instructions_setup: Two goals and a goalkeeper are positioned to the north and west, creating a square-shaped field. Play starts with a 1v1 attacking situation, where the attacker’s objective is to beat the defender and score into the main goal. The defender’s job is to deny the attacking player a clear path to goal, working to win the ball back before the attacker can get a shot off. If the defender regains possession, they immediately switch roles and attempt to score into the mini-goal.After every phase, the roles switch, and the attacker transitions to defend against a new opponent from the opposite team. This encourages players to quickly adapt from attacking to defending, maintaining high intensity throughout the drill and improving both offensive and defensive decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Focus: The attacker should focus on quick, direct movements to get past the defender and create a goal-scoring opportunity. Use fakes, changes of direction, and pace to beat the defender.• Defending Focus: The defender should stay compact and control the attacker’s space by positioning themselves between the attacker and the goal. Focus on timing the tackle or interception to win the ball cleanly.• Transition Speed: When the attacker transitions to defense, they must do so quickly and with purpose. Transitioning between attacking and defending without hesitation keeps the drill dynamic and helps improve fitness and decision-making.• Mini Goal Awareness: If the defender wins possession, they should look to immediately transition to attack and finish in the mini-goal, using their newfound possession to take advantage of the open space.
progression_one: Add Time Limit on Attack:Introduce a time limit for each attacking phase (e.g., 20 seconds). If the attacker does not score within the time frame, the defender is awarded possession, and they attempt to score in the mini-goal.Focus: This progression adds urgency to the attacking play, forcing attackers to make quicker decisions and defenders to remain alert under pressure.

title: Chelsea 2v2 & Counter
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 2v2 in one of the wider boxes close to the halfway line. The objective is to score in the opposing team's mini-goal. If the attacking team scores, a new 2v2 begins in the opposite box. This format allows for fast-paced play and encourages both teams to work on their attacking and defending under pressure.Should the team out of possession win the ball during the 2v2, they must quickly break out of the box and transition into a 3v3 on half the pitch. This progression forces the defending team to quickly shift into defensive mode while also promoting counter-attacking play and tactical awareness in transitioning from small-sided games to larger field play.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of fast transitions, both when switching between attack and defense and when breaking out into the 3v3. Players must stay alert to capitalize on turnovers.• Compact Defending: When out of possession, defenders should focus on staying compact and denying space, making it harder for the attackers to break through and create a scoring opportunity.• Quick Decision-Making: Players should make quick decisions when transitioning to the 3v3 phase, taking advantage of numerical superiority or finding the right passing options.• Use of Width: Encourage players to use the full width of the field during the 3v3 phase, ensuring that the team with possession can stretch the defense and create space for attacking opportunities.
progression_one: Add Time Limit on Attacks:Introduce a time limit for each 2v2 phase (e.g., 20 seconds). If the attacking team doesn’t score within the allotted time, possession switches automatically.Focus: This progression forces attackers to make quicker decisions and increases the intensity of the play, making the drill more dynamic.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Player in 3v3:In the 3v3 phase, add a neutral player who always plays with the team in possession. This creates a 4v3 situation, helping improve combination play and quick passes in attack.Focus: This progression encourages players to work on their passing, movement, and combination play in a numerical advantage, while also testing the defenders’ ability to cover extra space.

title: Chelsea 3 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice is designed to develop attacking combinations and finishing techniques through three distinct phases. Each phase focuses on a different type of service and movement, helping attackers build confidence and consistency in front of goal.In Phase 1, a centre forward receives a through ball while running off the shoulder of the defender and finishes. Phase 2 involves a wide player delivering a cross into the box for two centre forwards making attacking runs. Phase 3 switches play to the opposite wing, where the winger cuts inside and delivers a floated cross into the two forwards, encouraging timing, movement, and aerial finishing.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Emphasize well-timed movements to stay onside and arrive in the right zones at the right moment.• Quality of Service: Wide players must focus on delivering accurate balls, whether driven, cut back, or floated.• Body Shape and Finishing Technique: Strikers should open up their body appropriately for different types of finishes—instep for placement or laces for power.• Communication: Attackers must coordinate and communicate when making runs to avoid overlapping and improve connection.
progression_one: Add Passive Defenders:Introduce a passive defender in each phase to add mild pressure, encouraging attackers to adjust positioning and decision-making under light opposition.Focus: Helps players develop composure and positioning when faced with defenders, without compromising the unopposed structure.
progression_two: Finish from Second Balls:After each initial finish, a coach or server plays a second ball into the box for a reactive finish, simulating rebounds or loose balls.Focus: Encourages quick reactions, second-phase attacking, and staying alert after the first action.

title: Chelsea Building Up Centrally
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on playing out from the back under pressure and encourages structured build-up play through central areas. The objective is for the team in possession to work the ball through the thirds and progress into one of the three mini goals positioned across the halfway line.The defending team looks to press high and regain possession. If they do, they initiate a counterattack using two wide players positioned in outer channels. This transition creates a 7v7 counterattacking scenario, promoting quick decision-making, spatial awareness, and the ability to exploit overloads.
coaching_notes: • Structured Build-Up: Encourage the use of positional play, with defenders and midfielders offering passing lanes and support angles.• Patience in Possession: Reinforce the importance of not forcing passes—look to draw the press and find the right moment to play through.• Counter-Press Reaction: Immediately upon losing possession, players should react and organize to prevent the counterattack.• Wide Support: The two wide players must time their involvement and provide quick, high-quality support during the counter phase.
progression_one: Limit Touches in Defensive Third:Restrict players in the defensive third to two touches to promote quicker decision-making and movement off the ball.Focus: Improves ball circulation speed and forces players to think ahead under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit on Counter Attacks:Once possession is won, the counterattacking team must attempt to score within 10 seconds.Focus: Encourages fast breaks, urgency, and efficiency during transitions.

title: Chelsea Continuous 3v3 SSG
instructions_setup: This 3v3 small-sided game is played across two horizontal mini-pitches, each with two mini goals (no goalkeepers required).
