Two games take place simultaneously while a third team waits in the central resting zone between the pitches.As soon as a goal is scored in either game, the scoring team immediately exits the pitch and the resting team replaces them, keeping the game flowing continuously. This dynamic format demands sharp awareness, quick reactions, and high intensity from all involved.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions: Encourage the resting team to stay alert and ready to join play instantly after a goal is scored.• High Tempo: Keep the games fast-paced with short, sharp actions and quick decision-making.• Awareness: Players must track both ongoing games and anticipate when they’ll need to enter the pitch.• Communication: Promote clear communication between teammates during transitions and while waiting.
progression_one: Add a 5-Second Entry Window:Once a goal is scored, the resting team has just five seconds to enter the pitch. If they’re not ready, the conceding team stays on.Focus: Increases focus, urgency, and readiness in transition.
progression_two: One-Touch Finish Rule:All goals must be scored with a one-touch finish to increase challenge and force creative play.Focus: Sharpens movement, timing, and final-third decision-making.

title: Chelsea Countering From Deep
instructions_setup: This unopposed attacking practice replicates a counter-attack from deep, focusing on speed, timing, and combination play in transition moments.    The sequence begins with a vertical forward pass played into a wide player, simulating the first action in a counter-attack. Upon receiving the ball, the wide player drives forward into space and delivers a cross into the box.    Meanwhile, three supporting attackers time their runs to enter the penalty area, aiming to finish from the cross. The attacking movements can be left open or based on pre-defined patterns to encourage coordination and role clarity.    This drill reinforces the principles of breaking quickly, stretching the pitch, and attacking with intent during transitions.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Transition: Emphasize sharpness and urgency from the initial pass to the final shot—players should recognize counter-attack opportunities and execute with minimal delay.    • Wide Play: The wide player must use positive first touches, attack space aggressively, and deliver with accuracy—whether by whipping across, cutting back, or flashing into danger zones.    • Timing of Runs: Attackers must stagger their runs to cover key zones (front post, penalty spot, far post), avoiding crowding and maximizing scoring angles.    • Combination Patterns: If using set routines, ensure players understand who initiates, who supports, and how to rotate within the movement.
progression_one: Opposed Finishing:Add 1–2 passive defenders in the box during the finishing phase to apply light pressure or block off obvious lanes.Focus: Encourages attackers to adapt their movements, positioning, and decision-making when defenders are present.

title: Chelsea Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness-based drill adds a competitive edge by turning high-intensity running into a race between two teams. Each team aims to complete a set number of successful runs before the opposition to win the round.Play begins with a dribble into the central zone, where the player leaves the ball and sprints to the top of the grid. After tagging the next teammate, that player sprints down, plays a first-time pass to the starting line, and repeats the sequence. It blends physical conditioning with technical sharpness.
coaching_notes: • Max Effort Runs: Emphasize full-speed efforts during sprints to maximize the conditioning benefit.• Quality First-Time Passing: Ensure the pass from the central zone is accurate and controlled, even under fatigue.• Sharp Transitions: Players should be quick to react once tagged to keep the tempo high.• Communication & Encouragement: Encourage teams to push each other and maintain intensity throughout.
progression_one: Use Weaker Foot for Passing:Players must complete the central pass using their weaker foot to enhance technical development.Focus: Builds confidence and ability on the weaker side under pressure.

title: Chelsea Fitness & Mastery
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery drill, an equal number of players start on the outside and inside of the grid. Outside players each begin with a ball, while the inside players begin without one, ready to receive and return with different techniques.Inside players must travel through the central zone before moving to a new outside player to engage in a new repetition. This constant movement encourages fitness, sharpness, and technical consistency. The drill is highly adaptable and can include volleys, half-volleys, headers, or one-touch passing depending on the focus.
coaching_notes: • High Tempo Movement: Inside players should move quickly between stations to maintain intensity.• Clean Technique: Emphasize sharp contact on all touches, particularly during first-time actions.• Body Positioning: Players must be balanced and on their toes when receiving, striking, or heading the ball.• Scanning and Awareness: Inside players should scan before moving to anticipate the next interaction.
progression_one: Add Competition Between Inside Players:Track the number of successful repetitions completed in a set time, creating a competitive edge.Focus: Increases intensity and focus under time pressure.

title: Chelsea Fitness Rondo
instructions_setup: This pressing-focused rondo begins with 2 defenders starting 10 yards outside the main grid, where they have 3 balls ready to play. To start, one of the defenders passes a ball into the grid to initiate a 2v6 rondo scenario. Immediately after the pass, both defenders sprint in to try and win possession.Once possession is won, the defenders must quickly exit the grid, return to their starting point, and play the next ball in to repeat the process. This cycle continues through all three balls and promotes high-intensity pressing, quick recovery, and transition play.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Entry: Defenders should sprint in with intensity and close angles quickly.• Team Coordination: The two pressing players must communicate and press as a unit to force mistakes.• Quick Reset: Emphasize a rapid transition back to starting position after each turnover.• Ball Speed and Movement: Possession players must move the ball quickly and stay spaced to maintain control.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession Players:Restrict possession players to 1 or 2 touches maximum to increase difficulty.Focus: Encourages quick decision-making and sharp passing under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Support Player Inside the Grid:Include a neutral player to support the possession team, creating a 7v2 and allowing more dynamic passing combinations.Focus: Teaches defenders how to press with cover and cut off options effectively.

title: Chelsea Handball Warm Up
instructions_setup: This handball-style possession game challenges players to move the ball quickly and accurately in order to score by receiving a pass inside the end zone. Players are not allowed to travel with the ball once in possession—they must pivot on one foot and find a teammate to pass to. This restriction helps develop ball control, awareness, and quick decision-making under pressure.To regain possession, defenders must intercept passes or block throws without making contact. The game flows continuously, promoting movement off the ball and intelligent positioning from attackers and defenders alike.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Movement: Encourage sharp, crisp passing with minimal time spent in possession to exploit gaps in the opposition’s defensive shape.• Off-the-Ball Movement: Players should constantly scan their surroundings and make intelligent, well-timed runs to create passing angles and options.• Pivoting Technique: Reinforce strong footwork and body balance when pivoting, allowing players to maintain control and stay composed under pressure.• Interceptions Over Tackles: Defenders must focus on positioning and timing to intercept cleanly, avoiding fouls while disrupting attacking flow.
progression_one: Correct Throw-In Technique Required:All passes must be delivered using the proper throw-in technique as seen in football (both hands, over the head, feet planted).Focus: Reinforces correct technique under pressure while simulating realistic match scenarios.
progression_two: Time Limit for Possession:Each player can only hold the ball for a maximum of 3 seconds before passing.Focus: Increases game tempo and forces quick thinking and rapid support play.

title: Chelsea Hexagonal Overload
instructions_setup: This possession practice focuses on creating and exploiting overloads in central areas of the pitch. When the blue team is in possession, they can use the 3 outside players to form a 6v4 overload, allowing for more passing options and space to build up play. The emphasis is on maintaining possession and finding the right opportunities to progress the ball forward.Once the white team wins possession, the focus shifts to retaining the ball in a 4v3 scenario in the central area. The white team must work together to keep the ball and break the opposition’s pressure while exploiting the overload in the middle of the pitch.
coaching_notes: • Creating Overloads: Encourage the attacking team to stretch the field and use the extra players on the outside to pull the defending team out of shape.• Quick Transitions: Upon winning possession, the defending team must transition quickly to ensure they can exploit the numerical advantage and retain possession in the central area.• Ball Movement and Support: Players should focus on quick, sharp passes and offer continuous support to maintain possession and prevent the opposition from closing down options.• Patience and Decision-Making: Emphasize patience in possession when overloaded, with players making intelligent decisions to either retain the ball or exploit gaps in the opposition’s defense.
progression_one: Restrict Space for Defenders:Place a marker in the central area to limit the space available for defenders, making it more challenging for them to regain possession.Focus: Increases pressure on defenders and encourages attackers to make quicker, more precise passes.

title: Chelsea One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: In this individual technical drill, the player begins by working on fast feet and first-touch control around a small area or cone setup. After a short period of sharp movement, the coach calls out a colour. The player must quickly react by sprinting to one of two coloured poles positioned on either side, collect a ball placed next to the pole, and finish on goal with minimal touches. This drill combines quick reactions, agility, ball mastery, and end-product under light pressure.
coaching_notes: • React Quickly to Cues – Encourage players to stay alert and explode toward the correct pole immediately after the colour call for realistic reaction training.• Sharp First Touch – Reinforce the importance of a positive first touch to set up an efficient strike without breaking stride or rhythm.• Controlled Speed – Players must balance sprint intensity with technical control when transitioning from footwork into the finishing action.• Quality Finishing – Emphasize clean, accurate strikes on goal, focusing on body shape, timing, and composure after high-speed movement.

title: Chelsea Overloaded Race
instructions_setup: This dynamic practice involves two teams of three players attacking in opposite directions on two different pitches. Each team’s goal is to outscore the opposing team in a fast-paced, 3v2 situation. The drill starts with an odd number of balls placed along the central line, and teams must use these balls to create attacking opportunities.As the game progresses, players are encouraged to balance speed and efficiency in their attacks—aiming to get as many attacks off as possible while also focusing on quality to maximize scoring chances. The drill concludes once all the balls have been played, promoting quick decision-making and teamwork under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of transitioning quickly from defense to attack in order to capitalize on numerical advantages and create more scoring opportunities.• Decision-Making: Players must make quick decisions on when to attack quickly versus when to slow down and organize, ensuring they take full advantage of the 3v2 overload.• Communication: Encourage constant verbal and non-verbal communication between attackers to create space, set up plays, and ensure effective movement off the ball.• Efficient Scoring: Players should focus on creating high-quality scoring chances through well-timed passes, runs, and positioning, making each attack count.
progression_one: Limited Touches:Players are restricted to two touches per player, forcing quicker decision-making and faster attacks.Focus: Increases game tempo and forces players to focus on quick, precise passing and decision-making.

title: Chelsea Y Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This Y passing pattern drill focuses on improving forward passing and receiving under pressure, with an emphasis on maintaining fluid movement and accuracy. The practice is set up with four poles or stations arranged in a Y shape, creating distinct passing lanes. Players follow their pass around the grid, ensuring they remain engaged and aware of their positioning throughout the drill.With multiple variations available, this drill can be adapted to work on different types of passing, including short, long, and driven passes. Players should aim to be sharp with their movements and passes, helping them develop quicker decision-making and better control of the ball.
coaching_notes: • Forward Passing: Encourage players to focus on moving the ball forward quickly, aiming for decisive passes that advance play rather than sideways or backwards.• Movement After Pass: Players must follow their pass immediately, moving into space and offering support to the next player, ensuring the drill flows smoothly.• Receiving Under Pressure: Stress the importance of receiving the ball with a controlled first touch, especially under pressure, to maintain possession and keep the tempo high.• Accuracy and Timing: Players should work on the precision of their passes and timing of their movements to create seamless connections between players, ensuring the drill progresses efficiently.
progression_one: Increase Speed and Touch Limit:Limit players to one or two touches per pass to increase the tempo of the drill and force players to think quickly and execute passes under time pressure.Focus: Improves decision-making and ball control while promoting faster, more dynamic passing combinations.

title: Copenhagen 1st Touch Technical
instructions_setup: In this drill, a defender initiates play by passing the ball to an attacker and immediately applies pressure. The attacker must then dribble through one of two designated gates while the defender simultaneously runs through one of the gates to close down space. This forces the attacker to take a precise, clean first touch away from the defender and towards the opposite gate to maintain possession and create space.This exercise improves first touch accuracy, decision-making under pressure, and close ball control. It encourages attackers to read the defender’s movement quickly and adapt their touch accordingly to evade pressure effectively.
coaching_notes: • Stress the importance of a sharp, controlled first touch away from pressure – This enables the attacker to maintain possession and create space quickly.• Encourage attackers to scan the field before receiving the pass – This improves awareness of gate positions and defender’s approach.• Remind defenders to time their approach carefully to force errors without fouling – Proper defensive timing increases pressure effectiveness and realism.• Emphasize body positioning and balance to allow quick changes of direction – Both attacker and defender benefit from strong stance and agility during the duel.
progression_one: Narrower GatesReduce the width of the gates to increase the difficulty of dribbling through and require more precise touches. This forces attackers to focus heavily on accuracy and close control to succeed.Focus: Enhance technical accuracy and quick decision-making under tighter spatial constraints, improving ball mastery under pressure.

title: Copenhagen 1v1 Warm Up Game
instructions_setup: This warm-up game challenges players to dribble from one end of the grid to the other while navigating two “danger zones” along the way. Each danger zone contains a single defender whose objective is to win the ball from the dribbler. If the defender succeeds, roles immediately switch— the dribbler becomes the defender, and the defender becomes the dribbler. This continuous challenge tests players’ dribbling under pressure and their ability to defend in tight spaces.The drill helps improve close control, quick decision-making, and defensive reactions in a dynamic and competitive environment. It also encourages players to maintain focus and composure while under threat from opponents.
coaching_notes: • Encourage players to use quick changes of direction and body feints – This helps evade defenders effectively and maintain forward momentum through danger zones.• Stress the importance of close ball control and shielding when under pressure – Players must protect the ball securely to avoid losing possession easily.• Remind defenders to anticipate dribbler’s moves and stay balanced in a low stance – This allows for quicker reactions and better chances of winning the ball cleanly.• Emphasize composure and decision-making to choose the best moments to accelerate – Players should balance speed with control for successful dribbles.
progression_one: Reduced Space in Danger ZonesShrink the size of the danger zones to increase defensive pressure and force sharper dribbling skills.Focus: Improve tight control and quick decision-making under intensified defensive pressure.
progression_two: Add Time Limit Per AttemptIntroduce a time limit for each dribble attempt to encourage faster, more decisive play while maintaining ball control.Focus: Develop speed of execution and composure under time constraints during attacking runs.

title: Copenhagen 3 Phase Finishing Wide
instructions_setup: This drill has three continuous unopposed phases to develop coordinated attacking play and finishing across key positions. The winger, attacking midfielder, and centre forward combine with quick passing and movement to create scoring chances. Each phase ensures every player receives the ball in a scoring position and takes a shot, promoting sharp timing and finishing.In Phase 1, the winger receives wide and passes or cuts back to the centre forward for a controlled finish. Phase 2 focuses on the attacking midfielder, who receives a pass after a quick combination, then drives forward to shoot unopposed. Phase 3 features the centre forward receiving a through ball to finish decisively. This setup lets players focus on technical execution, timing, and composure without defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize precise timing of runs to ensure each player receives the ball in an optimal scoring position, maximizing goal-scoring opportunities with intelligent movement and anticipation.• Stress the importance of accurate, weighted passes between the winger, attacking midfielder, and centre forward to maintain fluid attacking combinations and sharp transitions throughout the drill.• Encourage players to focus on first-touch control and quick decision-making to enhance the speed and quality of their finishing in all phases, fostering confidence in front of goal.• Reinforce the need for composure and technique in shooting, reminding players to aim for placement and power to increase scoring effectiveness under match-like conditions.
progression_one: Add Passive DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to apply light pressure during the finishing phases, encouraging players to improve composure and decision-making under mild defensive challenge. This encourages adapting to pressure while maintaining technical skills.Focus: Developing technical execution and finishing accuracy while adjusting to increased pressure and game realism.
progression_two: Increase Pace and IntensityIncrease the tempo of the drill, reducing rest time between phases to simulate match intensity and develop players’ fitness alongside technical skills. This tests stamina and decision-making under fatigue.Focus: Enhancing quick transitions, stamina, and maintaining finishing quality under fatigue and physical stress.

title: Copenhagen 4 Teams 2v2+4
instructions_setup: This drill takes place in a central grid where two teams compete in a 2v2 format, each aiming to score in their two mini goals located ahead. When a team is in possession, two neutral players positioned on the sides of the grid can join the attack, creating a 4v2 overload to help maintain possession and create scoring opportunities. These neutral players are limited to one touch and are not allowed to score, focusing their role on quick support and ball circulation.The main objective for the attacking team is to utilize the neutral players effectively to outplay the defenders, combining sharp passing and movement to break defensive lines. Defenders work to stay compact and communicate to resist pressure and regain possession as quickly as possible.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, accurate passing to exploit the overload – This helps maintain possession under pressure and creates better scoring chances through intelligent play.• Stress constant communication between teammates and neutral players – Good communication enhances positioning and anticipates passing options efficiently to maintain attacking flow.• Emphasize quick decision-making and use of one-touch play – Rapid choices prevent defenders from settling and increase attacking tempo effectively with purposeful intent.• Remind defenders to stay compact and anticipate passing lanes – This reduces space for attackers and forces errors during ball circulation with disciplined positioning.
progression_one: Limited Time PossessionIntroduce a time limit for each possession phase, encouraging faster play and sharper decision-making under game-like conditions.Focus: Increase tempo and precision under pressure during possession phases to simulate match intensity.

title: Copenhagen 4v2 Rondo Into SSG
instructions_setup: This practice starts with a 4v2 rondo on the outside of the grid where the possession team focuses on quick, accurate passing to maintain control. Once the team completes a set number of passes, they earn the right to transfer the ball into the main pitch, which measures approximately 36x40 yards. At this point, the possession players can run into the pitch themselves to join and begin a 6v6 attacking phase, encouraging smooth transitions from tight possession to open play.The main aim is to develop players’ ability to maintain composure and quick passing in tight spaces, then immediately apply those skills in a larger attacking scenario. Players must adjust from high-pressure rondo conditions to creating attacking opportunities in the more open small-sided game.
coaching_notes: • Encourage sharp, precise passing to maintain possession during the rondo – This builds technical control and decision-making speed essential for effective ball retention.• Stress communication and spatial awareness when transitioning between phases – Players must coordinate runs and positioning to exploit space and maintain attacking rhythm efficiently.• Emphasize quick decision-making to identify passing options in tight spaces – This helps break defensive pressure and maintain momentum heading into the SSG phase.• Remind players to stay alert and ready to switch mindset quickly – Smooth transitions between rondo and SSG improve game realism and tactical adaptability during play.
progression_one: Increased Pass RequirementIncrease the number of passes required to transition from the rondo to the SSG, challenging players to maintain longer possession sequences under pressure.Focus: Improve sustained ball control and patience during buildup to simulate real match possession demands.
progression_two: Defensive Pressure in RondoAdd a third defender to the rondo phase to intensify pressure, forcing quicker decisions and sharper ball control before transitioning.Focus: Enhance technical precision and composure when facing increased defensive pressure in tight spaces.

title: Copenhagen Counter With Fullback Recovery
instructions_setup: In this counter-attacking drill, play starts with a 2-3 pass combination between 4 attackers who then enter the live zone to attack 4v2 with the intention to score. Two extra defenders recover from wide areas (acting as recovering full backs) and attempt to restore balance by closing down space quickly.The drill develops rapid transition play, decision-making in numerical overloads, and defensive recovery runs. Players focus on quick passing, movement off the ball, and composure under pressure to exploit or deny scoring chances during fast breaks.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize quick, accurate passing to maintain attacking momentum – This helps players exploit gaps before defenders can recover and disrupt the attack effectively.• Stress effective communication and constant movement off the ball – Creating space and passing options is essential for breaking down defensive lines under pressure.• Encourage attackers to identify and exploit wide full backs’ positioning – Gaining numerical advantages forces defenders into difficult decisions and opens scoring chances.• Highlight the importance of defensive recovery runs by full backs – Attackers must anticipate these runs to adjust their timing and maintain attacking flow seamlessly.
progression_one: Increased Defensive PressureAdd one more defender to the live zone to create a 4v3 situation, increasing the defensive pressure and requiring faster decision-making.Focus: Improve quick passing accuracy and off-the-ball movement under higher defensive pressure.

title: Copenhagen Midfield 3 Link Up
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on a midfield trio working closely together to develop quick, precise 1-2 passing combinations. The three players continually rotate positions to simulate realistic midfield movement and support, aiming to break defensive lines. After completing a series of one-twos, the final player in the sequence drives forward to play a pass into a mini goal positioned at the end of the grid.The continuous flow encourages sharp passing, spatial awareness, and quick decision-making under moderate pressure, helping players improve their ability to maintain possession and create scoring opportunities through effective combination play.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp, accurate passing with the correct weight – This improves the speed of play and helps maintain fluid attacking momentum, especially during fast transitions.• Encourage players to communicate constantly and anticipate movements – Effective verbal and non-verbal cues enhance timing and coordination during one-twos, leading to better teamwork.• Stress the importance of body positioning to receive passes efficiently – Being open and balanced allows for quicker control and better passing angles, which helps maintain possession longer.• Reinforce quick movement after passing to create new passing lanes – Dynamic support play opens space and confuses defenders effectively, increasing attacking options.
progression_one: Add passive defendersIntroduce passive defenders applying light pressure on the midfield trio, encouraging quicker passing and sharper movement to maintain possession under increased challenge.Focus: Develop composure and speed of play under moderate defensive pressure, improving decision-making accuracy.
progression_two: Limit touches and increase paceRestrict players to a maximum of two touches per pass and increase the tempo of the drill, pushing players to improve control and decision-making speed in tight spaces.Focus: Enhance first-touch quality and quick decision-making in tight spaces, building confidence under pressure.

title: Copenhagen Wide Combo Into 3v2
instructions_setup: In this semi-opposed attacking practice, play starts with the ball moving from the central area out wide. A 2-player unopposed combination between the winger and full back takes place to build the attack. Once the ball is delivered into the box for the 3 attackers, the phase becomes opposed as 2 defenders actively try to protect the goal and defend the attackers.This drill focuses on quick, precise passing and combination play in wide areas, before transitioning into a realistic, pressured finishing scenario. It encourages attackers to time runs well and make effective decisions under defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize crisp, accurate passing in wide areas – This helps create space and opens opportunities before delivering into the penalty box effectively.• Encourage strong communication between winger and full back – Coordinated movement is key to creating effective overlaps and passing angles quickly.• Remind attackers to time runs and find pockets of space in the box – Movement off the ball is vital to beat defenders and create clear scoring chances.• Stress defenders’ positioning and anticipation inside the box – They must maintain compactness and focus on intercepting crosses or blocking shots decisively.
progression_one: Add defensive pressure earlierIntroduce a defender in the wide zone to pressure the winger and full back during their combination, increasing the challenge to maintain possession and execute the pass under pressure.Focus: Improve composure and quick decision-making under early pressure in build-up play situations.
progression_two: Limit attacking touchesRestrict attackers to a maximum of two touches once the ball enters the box, encouraging sharper finishing and faster decision-making under defensive pressure effectively.Focus: Enhance first-touch control and quick shot execution in tight, high-pressure situations consistently.

title: Coventry 1v1 Into Attacking Transitions
instructions_setup: This multi-phase attacking transition practice begins with a 1v1 duel toward two mini goals. Once the first phase concludes (either by a goal, ball out of play, or time limit), a second attacker joins in to create a 2v1 scenario against the original defender. After that attack is completed, an opposing attacker enters to form a final 2v2 phase, allowing for continuous play and multiple attacking/defensive transitions. The flow of the practice encourages players to adapt quickly and make effective decisions in evolving game situations.
coaching_notes: • 1v1 Attacking – Encourage creativity and quick decision-making. Players should use body feints, changes of pace, and clever touches to create separation and finish into either mini goal.• Transition to Overload – In the 2v1 phase, attackers should exploit the numerical advantage with sharp movement and precise passing. Look for quick combinations or isolating the defender 2v1.• 2v2 Phase Awareness – When the game shifts to 2v2, emphasize scanning and communication. Attackers must recognize when to combine and when to drive individually; defenders must work together to stay compact and cover.• Mental Transition – Players must be prepared to shift roles quickly—attacking one moment, defending the next. Reacting decisively during transitions is key to success in each phase.
progression_one: Time Limit for Each PhaseSet a short time limit (e.g., 5–6 seconds) for each attacking phase to encourage quicker decisions and more urgency in both attacking and defending.Focus:Promotes tempo, transition sharpness, and game-like speed of play.
progression_two: Directional Goals in Final PhaseReplace mini goals with a large goal and a goalkeeper in the 2v2 phase to create a more game-realistic finishing scenario.Focus:Improves finishing in tight spaces and requires greater precision and awareness in the final third.

title: Coventry 1v1 Race into 1v1 Attack
instructions_setup: This fast-paced, reaction-based attacking practice begins with a trigger from the coach, who calls out either "blue" or "red." Two players race to the corresponding ball placed on that side. The first player to reach the ball attacks and finishes unopposed. Immediately after, the second player retrieves the ball from the opposite side to initiate a 1v1 attack against the initial attacker, who now transitions into a defender. This two-phase setup promotes explosive movement, quick decision-making, and 1v1 attacking and defending skills.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Start – Encourage players to react instantly to the coach’s call. Quick acceleration and agility are key to gaining the advantage during the race.• Finishing with Speed and Control – The player who wins the race should focus on finishing with composure and purpose. A quick yet controlled shot is the aim.• 1v1 Attacking Mindset – The second phase emphasizes direct attacking. The ball carrier should use pace, dribbling skills, and body feints to beat the defender and score.• 1v1 Defensive Transition – After finishing, the first attacker must quickly recover into a compact defensive stance, aiming to delay, contain, or dispossess the oncoming attacker.
progression_one: Passive Defender in First PhaseAdd a passive defender during the unopposed finishing phase to add light pressure and simulate a more game-realistic shot decision.Focus:Improves composure and encourages attackers to recognize angles and timing under slight pressure.
progression_two: Both Players Compete for a Single BallInstead of calling a color, place one central ball and have both players race to win it and become the attacker. The winner attacks the goal; the loser immediately becomes the defender.Focus:Increases competition, decision-making under pressure, and reactions during transition moments.

title: Coventry 3v3 Attacking
instructions_setup: This attacking practice focuses on 3v3 attacking play with an emphasis on quick transitions and creating goal-scoring opportunities. The drill starts with both teams of 3 sprinting and switching sides. Once both teams are set, a 3v3 phase begins, where the attacking team aims to score into any of the two mini goals. If the defending team wins possession, they must dribble the ball to any of the 3 poles located directly ahead to complete the transition. Teams will swap roles throughout the practice to ensure multiple reps and high intensity.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Shape and Movement – Encourage the attacking team to spread out and create passing lanes, using quick passes and off-the-ball movement to break down the defense. Players should aim to combine and create space for each other in tight areas.• Quick Transitions – When possession changes, players must react quickly. The defending team should immediately look to exploit the counter-attack, dribbling to the poles as fast as possible. The attacking team must transition into defense and set up quickly to regain possession.• Decision-Making in Attack – Attackers should be encouraged to make quick decisions when they have the ball. They need to decide whether to shoot, pass, or dribble based on the positioning of defenders and teammates. Using a mix of low and high tempo play will keep the defenders guessing.• Defensive Shape – Defenders should focus on staying compact, closing down space, and applying pressure to the ball carrier. Encourage them to anticipate passes and block shooting lanes, while also staying aware of any potential runs from the attackers.
progression_one: Limit Touches for AttackersLimit the attackers to 2 touches (one for control and one for pass or finish). This will encourage quicker decision-making and increase the tempo of play, forcing players to move the ball faster and more efficiently.Focus:Increases the pace of the game and emphasizes quick ball movement in tight spaces.
progression_two: Add an Extra Defender for More ChallengeIntroduce an additional defender to make it a 4v3 in favor of the defending team. This will challenge the attackers to find creative ways to break down the defense, such as playing quicker combinations or using width to stretch the defense.Focus:Develops attacking creativity and the ability to break down overloaded defensive situations. Also reinforces defensive discipline when under increased pressure.

title: Coventry 5 Team Rondo
instructions_setup: In this 4v2 rondo practice, 5 teams of 2 players will attempt to retain possession and switch play after a minimum of 5 passes. The aim for the possession team is to keep the ball moving and find opportunities to switch the play to the opposite grid.The defending team (the 2 players in each grid) must press to win possession. If the defending team fails to win the ball and the attacking team successfully switches play, the attacking team must transition by passing into the next grid, continuing the sequence until the defenders win possession.If the defending team wins possession, they will switch places with the two players who lost the ball. The new defenders must sprint into the opposite grid to start their defensive phase. This ensures that all players experience both attacking and defending roles while also promoting high intensity and quick transitions.
coaching_notes: • Possession Awareness – The attacking teams should focus on quick passing and maintaining good positioning to ensure they retain possession. Players should move to support the ball carrier, creating passing angles and space for the ball to be played forward or switched quickly.• Switching Play – Encourage players to switch play quickly and decisively. This will test their ability to read the game and deliver accurate passes across different areas of the grid. Switching play is a vital skill in creating space and breaking defensive lines.• Defensive Pressure – The defending team must be proactive in their pressure. Encourage them to press in a coordinated manner, closing down passing lanes and forcing the attacking team to play at a higher tempo.• Transition Speed – After winning possession, defenders should transition quickly, sprinting into the next grid to begin their attacking phase. The attackers must also be quick to react, keeping the ball moving and preparing for defensive challenges.
progression_one: Add More GridsIntroduce additional grids in the practice to increase the size of the area the ball must be switched across. This will challenge players to cover more space and make longer passes. The defending team will also need to adjust their positioning to deal with the increased number of passing options.Focus:Improves spatial awareness and the ability to make longer, more accurate passes across a larger area.
progression_two: Restrict Number of TouchesLimit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2-touch or 1-touch passing) to increase the tempo and encourage faster decision-making. This restriction will force players to think quickly and rely on their first touch and vision to maintain possession.Focus:Increases passing speed, decision-making under pressure, and the ability to move the ball quickly while maintaining possession.

title: Coventry Counter Attack Half Pitch
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a forward pass from the center circle into a central forward who is being marked by 3 defenders from behind. Upon receiving the initial pass, a counter-attack phase is triggered. The attacking team consists of 6 players, while the defending team has 5 players, creating an overload for the attackers.The attackers are split into 3 players making forward runs from the center circle, and 2 defenders who are making recovery runs from the same position. The focus of this drill is on quick transition, utilizing numerical superiority in attack, and encouraging effective decision-making when transitioning from defense to offense.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: As soon as the central forward receives the ball, the attackers must transition quickly into a counter-attacking mindset. Encourage the attackers to make direct, forward runs, immediately exploiting the space left by the defenders.• Awareness and Timing: The players making forward runs from the center circle must time their movements well. They should focus on timing their runs to either drag defenders out of position or create space for themselves to receive a pass.• Decision-Making: The center forward, who is under pressure from 3 defenders, should quickly assess whether to lay the ball off to a teammate or take on the defenders. Encourage them to make decisions quickly, and utilize the overload in attack.• Defensive Recovery: The 2 defenders making recovery runs must work hard to close down the attackers. Their role is to stop the counter-attack by positioning themselves effectively and applying pressure to the ball carrier. They should communicate with each other to make the most of their numerical advantage.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Touches:Introduce a limit on the number of touches the attackers can take. This encourages quicker decision-making and improves ball control during fast transitions. For example, restrict each attacker to 2 touches or less.Focus: This progression focuses on increasing the tempo of the counter-attack, requiring the attackers to think and act faster under pressure.

title: Coventry SAQ Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This SAQ (Speed, Agility, and Quickness) practice can serve as both a warm-up or an arrival activity, depending on the context. As a warm-up, it is used in an uncompetitive manner to activate the players’ muscles and prepare them for the session. As an arrival activity, it becomes more competitive, with players engaging in a head-to-head race where they are rewarded for winning.The setup involves a series of cones or markers laid out in an area. Players will perform various speed, agility, and quickness drills, such as ladders, cone slaloms, or shuttle runs, designed to enhance footwork, coordination, and explosive movements.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Technique – Whether as a warm-up or competitive activity, the key is to emphasize proper form during each drill. For example, ensure players maintain a low center of gravity during shuttle runs and quick, light steps through the agility ladder.• Pacing and Intensity – Adjust the speed and intensity based on whether the activity is being used for activation or as a competitive race. For a warm-up, players should focus on controlled movements and gradually build intensity. In a competitive scenario, encourage players to push their limits but maintain proper technique.• Engagement and Motivation – If used as an arrival activity, encourage players to stay motivated by making the drills competitive. Keep the atmosphere fun and engaging, rewarding players for winning head-to-head races to build excitement and team camaraderie.• Movement Variety – Include a variety of movements in the drills (e.g., side steps, high knees, quick feet, backward runs) to ensure the warm-up is dynamic and activates different muscle groups.
progression_one: Time TrialsAdd a timing element where players race against the clock to complete the drills. This can be done individually or head-to-head. Players will try to beat their previous times or those of their peers.Focus:Encourages personal improvement and adds a fun competitive aspect to the activity. It also helps players focus on improving their speed and agility over time.
progression_two: Add Obstacles or ChallengesIntroduce additional obstacles, such as cones or hurdles, to increase the challenge. For example, players could perform cone dribbles, ladder drills, or short sprints around obstacles. The more varied the movements, the better the activation for the body.Focus:Enhances agility and coordination, making the warm-up more dynamic and effective for preparing players for high-intensity movements.

title: Coventry Technical Passing
instructions_setup: In this technical passing practice, players focus on key principles used in the build-up phase, such as penetration and movement. The practice begins with a bounce pass combination between players, helping them develop their passing accuracy and timing.Once the bounce pass combination is complete, the players will then play a line-breaking forward pass, simulating progression and breaking defensive lines in the build-up phase. This practice replicates real match situations, where quick, incisive passing can progress the play forward, bypassing defenders and moving the ball into more dangerous areas.
coaching_notes: • Penetration – Emphasize the importance of penetrating passes that break through the opposition's defensive lines. These passes should be executed with precision and timing to advance the play and create attacking opportunities.• Movement – Players should focus on dynamic movement after playing the initial pass. Encourage players to move into space to provide passing options and support for the player in possession. Timed runs into key areas should allow for better passing angles and options for the ball carrier.• Bounce Pass Combinations – The practice starts with bounce passes to help players develop their passing rhythm. Encourage players to focus on keeping the ball close and accurate when playing these combinations to ensure control and effective build-up play.• Forward Progression – After the bounce passes, the focus should shift to playing a forward pass that breaks lines. Encourage players to look for the best available options—whether it's a pass into space for a runner or a through ball splitting the defense. The goal is to create forward momentum and penetrate the defensive lines.• First Touch and Decision-Making – Players should work on their first touch to ensure they can control and pass quickly in tight spaces. Emphasize the importance of making quick decisions on when to pass and when to move into space to support the ball carrier.
progression_one: Add Pressure to the PassingIntroduce light defensive pressure after the bounce pass phase. This will require players to think quicker and make faster decisions when playing forward passes to break the lines. The defenders should pressure the passer without fully engaging to still allow for technical development.Focus:Helps players work on their decision-making under pressure and improve their ability to execute line-breaking passes in more realistic game situations.
progression_two: Add More Players for Movement and SupportAdd more players into the practice to replicate a larger build-up. For example, have two additional players in the center of the field that can either create passing lanes or support the ball carrier, adding more options for ball circulation and movement.Focus:Improves the ability to link up play and develop fluid build-up in tighter spaces, with increased support and options for the player in possession.

title: Coventry Warm Up Race
instructions_setup: In this FUN warm-up practice, players will compete head-to-head in a race to score into mini goals for points. Teams earn 1 point for a goal, but they will earn an additional point if they score the first goal, encouraging players to find a balance between speed and precision in their play.The practice begins with the coach calling out 2 numbers between 1 and 3. Each player must sprint to touch the two corresponding numbered poles in order, before progressing to the next phase, which involves a chip and finish into the mini goal. The objective is to score as quickly as possible, with the first team to score gaining the added bonus point.
coaching_notes: • Speed vs. Precision – The challenge is to balance speed with accuracy. While players want to move quickly to score, they must be careful to execute the chip and finish with precision to earn additional points. Encourage players to focus on quick decision-making while ensuring they maintain control of the ball.• Sprint Technique – Players should focus on explosive starts and quick direction changes when sprinting to the poles. This will help improve their acceleration and agility, which are essential for fast transitions in games.• Chip and Finish – In the final phase, players should be encouraged to chip the ball into the mini goal with a calm, controlled technique. Remind players that while speed is important, the finish should still be clean and effective.• Communication – Encourage players to communicate with each other, as this practice involves a lot of movement and quick decision-making. Clear instructions and feedback will help players stay on track during the drill.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a defender who will try to prevent the player from scoring by blocking the chip or challenging the finish. The defender can be positioned in front of the goal to add a bit more challenge to the attacking player’s finish.Focus:Improves finishing under pressure and the ability to handle defensive pressure while still executing the goal-scoring task.
progression_two: Add Multiple RoundsIncrease the intensity of the warm-up by introducing multiple rounds where players must perform the sprint and finish exercise more than once, switching between the two numbered poles. This will improve their endurance and ability to perform high-intensity tasks repeatedly.Focus:Helps players to maintain focus and energy throughout a warm-up or game situation.

title: Croatia 1st Touch Into Space
instructions_setup: This ball mastery drill focuses on encouraging players to take positive first touches into space, helping them improve their ability to control and accelerate with the ball. The setup consists of two balls being worked simultaneously around a square grid, with gates (poles) placed on both vertical sides of the square. Players must receive the ball and take a positive first touch through the poles before making a forward pass to the next player.The drill emphasizes the importance of quick decision-making and fluid movement. Players need to be aware of the space around them and aim to keep the ball moving quickly while maintaining control. This drill helps to develop technical skills like dribbling, passing, and ball control under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Positive First Touch: Encourage players to focus on taking the ball into space with their first touch, aiming to move the ball forward or into an area they can attack immediately.• Quick Passing: Players should aim to pass the ball quickly after their first touch, avoiding holding onto the ball for too long to maintain the drill's rhythm and tempo.• Body Positioning: Players should position their body to receive the ball in such a way that they can quickly open up their hips and drive the ball into space, ensuring smooth transitions.• Spatial Awareness: Encourage players to be aware of the surrounding space and anticipate the movement of both the ball and the other players, ensuring they are ready to make their next pass or move.

title: Croatia Technical Warm Up
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up focuses on improving passing accuracy and first touch under pressure. Players are placed around three poles arranged in a triangle. The objective is for players to use their first touch to move the ball to a new side of the triangle and their second touch to deliver a penetrative pass through the triangle to the opposite player.This drill encourages quick thinking, precise passing, and sharp first touches. Players need to be aware of their positioning relative to the poles and each other to ensure they can move the ball efficiently. The drill also builds passing accuracy under pressure, as players must maintain control while executing a quick pass.
coaching_notes: • First Touch Direction: Players should focus on using their first touch to direct the ball towards a new side of the triangle, ensuring it sets them up for a penetrative pass on their second touch.• Penetrative Passing: Encourage players to make their passes sharp and penetrative, aiming to break the defensive lines or move the ball forward, creating opportunities for their teammate to receive the ball.• Quick Decision-Making: Players need to make quick decisions on where to move and how to play the ball, helping develop fast thinking under pressure.• Body Positioning: Encourage players to position their bodies correctly so that they can receive the ball in a way that allows them to quickly play the ball to the next target, ensuring fluid movement through the triangle.

title: Donetsk Attacking into 1v1
instructions_setup: This is an unopposed finishing practice that transitions into an opposed 1v1. The first attacker must dribble at speed towards the goal and complete their finish. Meanwhile, a second attacker dribbles through a set of poles positioned horizontally along the edge of the box. After the second attacker completes the dribble through the poles, they attack the goal, and the first attacker must transition into a defensive position for a 1v1 scenario to defend the goal.
coaching_notes: • Unopposed Dribbling and Finishing – The first attacker should focus on dribbling at speed, controlling the ball effectively while preparing to finish under pressure. The aim is to develop control and accuracy in a dynamic situation.• Transitioning to Defense – Once the first attacker completes their finish, they must immediately transition into a defensive role, setting up for the 1v1. The focus should be on quick decision-making and using positioning to force the second attacker wide or into a less dangerous angle.• Timing and Acceleration – Both attackers need to focus on their timing. The second attacker must accelerate through the poles quickly, while the first attacker must move swiftly from attack to defense without losing focus.• Defending the 1v1 – The first attacker should use proper 1v1 defending techniques, staying low, watching the ball, and forcing the attacker into a less threatening position to make it harder for them to score.
progression_one: Add Pressure to the Dribbling PhaseIntroduce a defender to pressure the first attacker during their dribbling and finishing phase. This forces the first attacker to deal with pressure before transitioning to defense.Focus: Improve the attacking player’s ability to deal with pressure and finish under tight circumstances.
progression_two: Increase Defensive ChallengeIntroduce a second defender to assist in the 1v1 defending phase, making it a 2v1 scenario. This forces the attacking player to be more creative in their movements and decision-making when attacking the goal.Focus: Improve attacking player’s ability to recognize and exploit defensive overloads.

title: Donetsk Breaking Lines in Build Up
instructions_setup: This passing practice allows players to improve their line-breaking passing during the build-up phase. With two variations, players can work on breaking lines into midfield and also directly into the forward line using third-man combinations.
coaching_notes: • Breaking Lines Efficiently – Emphasize the importance of recognizing when and how to break defensive lines with passes, either into midfield or directly into the forward line. Players should focus on finding space and timing their runs for the ball.• Third-Man Combinations – Encourage players to use third-man runs to create options and space. The passer should always be aware of their teammate’s positioning and look to play a quick, incisive pass into the forward line.• Passing Accuracy – Focus on the accuracy and weight of the pass when breaking the lines. The ball should be played into space, allowing the receiving player to attack or progress play with minimal delay.• Movement Off the Ball – Ensure players are constantly moving to support the player in possession. Timing and positioning are key to making the best passing options available for the player in possession.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce one or two passive defenders to create pressure on the build-up play. The attackers must still focus on breaking the lines while managing the increased pressure.Focus: Improving decision-making and the ability to break lines under pressure.
progression_two: Speed Up the Build-UpReduce the time allowed to make passes in the build-up phase. This forces players to play quicker and encourages faster line-breaking passes and movement.Focus: Speeding up the decision-making process and execution of line-breaking passes.

title: Donetsk Close Range Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing practice allows players to develop their finishing ability from close range, specifically in and around the 6-yard box. Play starts with a 3-player combination before one forward attacks the space behind the mannequins in an attempt to get on the end of a cross.Once each phase is complete, the 3 players will rotate, ensuring all 3 players get high reps of crossing, setting, and finishing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions – Focus on the importance of reacting quickly to the cross and attacking the space in the 6-yard box. Players should be encouraged to time their runs to arrive at the perfect moment for a clean finish.• Finishing Techniques – Emphasize different finishing techniques based on the type of cross, such as volleys, headers, or side-foot finishes. Players should aim to place the ball with precision rather than just power.• Crossing Quality – Ensure that the player crossing the ball is focusing on delivery. The cross should be made with accuracy and pace, providing the attacker with the best opportunity to finish.• Positioning in the Box – Teach the attackers to always position themselves well in the 6-yard box, adjusting their runs depending on where the cross is coming from. Understanding where to be at the right time is crucial for finishing in tight spaces.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce a passive defender or two to apply light pressure on the attacking player. The attacker must still focus on timing their run and finishing under pressure.Focus: Developing the ability to finish when there’s light defensive pressure in tight spaces.
progression_two: Increase Cross VarietyVary the type of cross being delivered. Include low crosses, high balls, and floated deliveries to test the attacker’s ability to finish from different types of service.Focus: Adapting finishing techniques to different types of crosses and improving versatility in finishing from close range.

title: Donetsk Diagonal Passing
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on improving players' ability to receive and play forward passes while on the move. Players will start by running into the grid directly ahead of them to receive a pass as they arrive. Upon receiving the ball, the player should take a first touch either to the left or right before playing a diagonal pass forwards to a teammate.
coaching_notes: • Receiving on the Move – Players should focus on controlling the ball with the first touch, ensuring they are always moving in the direction of the pass. Encourage players to keep their body open and position themselves to receive the ball while maintaining momentum.• Quick Direction Change – Once the player has received the ball, they should quickly adjust their body position to either the left or right to create space and prepare for a diagonal pass. The key is to make the touch smooth and efficient.• Diagonal Passing Technique – When playing the diagonal pass, players should focus on using the inside of their foot to ensure accuracy and proper weight on the ball. The pass should be directed to the player’s movement, not just to the space.• Communication – Players should be encouraged to communicate with teammates before receiving the ball, ensuring they know where the pass will go and who is making the run.
progression_one: Increase the Passing DistanceAs the players become more comfortable, increase the distance between the player receiving the ball and the player making the pass. This forces players to adjust their technique and control over a longer distance.Focus: Develop the ability to control the ball under pressure and execute a longer, more precise diagonal pass.
progression_two: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a defender who applies pressure on the player receiving the ball. The attacker now has to receive and pass quickly while dealing with a defender attempting to intercept or block the pass.Focus: Improve the player’s ability to make quick decisions under pressure, focusing on both receiving and passing with minimal time and space.

title: Donetsk Double Phase 1v1
instructions_setup: This is a fun 1v1 practice where players begin by making an attacking pass into a teammate positioned on one side of the grid. After the pass, the player must transition to the opposite side of the grid to defend against an incoming attack. Players should swap roles throughout the practice to ensure everyone gets a chance to attack and defend. Scoring should be used to add a competitive edge to the drill.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Pass and Movement – The player making the pass should focus on delivering an accurate and weighted pass to their teammate. After the pass, they must quickly transition, sprinting across the grid to their defensive position.• Defending the 1v1 – Upon arriving at the defending side, the player should adopt a defensive stance, keeping their body between the ball and the goal. Emphasize quick decision-making and maintaining good positioning to challenge the attacker effectively.• Quick Transitions – Focus on the speed and fluidity of the transition between attacking and defending. The ability to switch between these roles quickly is key to the drill’s effectiveness.• Competitive Edge – To increase the intensity, players should keep track of the score and aim to win as many 1v1s as possible, using competition as a motivational tool.
progression_one: Add Time PressureIntroduce a time limit to each attacking and defending phase (e.g., 10 seconds). This forces players to make quicker decisions and encourages faster transitions.Focus: Improve the speed of transitions and the ability to make quick decisions under time pressure.
progression_two: Increase Defensive PressureAdd a second defender to the defending side of the grid, making it a 2v1 scenario. This increases the defensive challenge and forces the attacking player to be more creative and quick in their attacking phase.Focus: Develop the attacking player's ability to read the defensive setup and make faster, more effective decisions.

title: Donetsk Fun Bowling Warm Up
instructions_setup: This is a fun and competitive warm-up practice designed to get players moving and engaged. Teams of 3 players will run toward a set of cones arranged in a triangle. Each player must place their ball on one of the cones. Once all 3 players have successfully placed their ball on the cones, one player will use a final ball to knock all 3 balls off the cones, in a bowling-style game.To ensure the practice runs smoothly, make sure the cones are positioned closely together in a triangle. This will add a competitive edge, as players will need to be more precise and cautious when placing their balls onto the cones.
coaching_notes: • Team Coordination – Players should communicate well to coordinate their movements and make sure each ball is placed on a cone quickly and accurately. The faster they work together, the sooner they’ll get to the "bowling" phase.• Accuracy and Control – When placing the ball onto the cones, players should focus on accuracy, as missing the cone means they’ll need to run back and retry. Encourage a calm approach to ensure proper placement without rushing.• Bowling Accuracy – The player designated to knock the balls off should focus on controlling their shot, aiming to hit all three balls. A smooth, controlled throw will increase their chances of knocking them all off in one go.• Encourage Friendly Competition – Make sure to maintain the competitive aspect by timing the practice or offering points for how quickly the team can knock off all three balls. This will add excitement and engagement for the players.
progression_one: Add Time PressureIntroduce a countdown clock and challenge teams to place their balls and knock them off within a limited time. This will increase the urgency and competitiveness, encouraging faster execution.Focus: Improve teamwork and communication while under time pressure.
progression_two: Increase the DistanceIncrease the distance from which players must place their balls onto the cones. This will force them to adjust their throwing and placement techniques, adding a layer of challenge to the practice.Focus: Develop accuracy and control, even when the task becomes more difficult.

title: Donetsk Medium Sized Game
instructions_setup: This small to medium-sized game encourages central play with 4 neutral players located around the outside of the playing area. The 4 neutral players are limited to 1 touch and must be used to either retain possession, progress play during the build-up, or create an attacking advantage in wide areas.The team in possession can use the neutral players to maintain possession or transition the ball to key attacking areas. If a team scores after receiving a pass from one of the neutral players, they will be awarded with a bonus point. This rule encourages the central teams to actively engage with the 4 neutrals both during the build-up and attacking phases.
coaching_notes: • Utilizing Neutrals – Encourage players to frequently look for the neutral players as outlets to maintain possession and progress the attack. The neutrals should always be an option, providing extra support in both offensive and defensive transitions.• Quick Passing and Movement – Players in the central areas should focus on quick, decisive passing and off-the-ball movement to create space. The neutral players can help by providing easy passing lanes and opening up opportunities to attack.• Wide Play – Players should aim to use the neutrals to switch play and create wide attacks. Focus on getting the ball quickly to the flanks, where players can stretch the defense and create crossing or cut-back opportunities.• Bonus Point Motivation – Remind players of the importance of using the neutral players to create attacking opportunities. This bonus point rule will encourage more awareness of how to integrate neutrals into the build-up and finishing phases of the game.
progression_one: Neutral Player RestrictionsLimit the neutral players to only being able to play passes to the central areas or restrict them to a specific side of the field. This will force the central players to make quicker decisions and adapt to changing spaces.Focus: Improve decision-making and adaptability in build-up play.
progression_two: Remove the Bonus PointTake away the bonus point for scoring via the neutral players, and instead introduce a new point system based on key passes or assists involving the neutrals. This will add another layer of tactical thinking and encourage better utilization of the neutral players.Focus: Encourage tactical awareness and a more strategic use of the neutral players.

title: Dortmund 1v2 Pressure Evasion
instructions_setup: This 1v2 attacking drill focuses on evading defenders and scoring under pressure. Play begins with a pass across the grid to the attacker, who must then face two defenders. The attacker’s objective is to score into either of the two mini-goals positioned to the left and right of their initial receiving position. The attacker has the freedom to switch between the two sides of the grid, attempting to outmaneuver the defenders and finish on goal.This practice helps attackers work on their decision-making and creativity when faced with multiple defenders. It also encourages quick dribbling and the ability to read defensive pressure to exploit space effectively.
coaching_notes: • Evading Pressure: Encourage the attacker to use quick changes of direction, feints, and explosive bursts of speed to beat the defenders.• Head-Up Awareness: The attacker should constantly scan the field to identify which mini-goal offers the best opportunity and make quick decisions based on defender positioning.• Use of Space: Stress the importance of the attacker using the entire grid, switching sides as needed to create space and confuse the defenders.• Defensive Positioning: The defenders should focus on cutting off passing lanes and pressuring the attacker without committing too early, maintaining balance and positioning to prevent a shot.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for the attacker to score in one of the mini-goals, increasing the intensity of the drill and encouraging quicker decision-making and faster execution.Focus: Increases urgency and tempo, encouraging the attacker to act quickly under pressure.

title: Dortmund 2 Zone Possession Transfer
instructions_setup: This possession transfer drill focuses on maintaining ball possession while under pressure and executing quick switches of play across zones. The practice area consists of a large square divided into 4 smaller grids, with one team working within a set of vertical grids. Each team has 6 players—3 players are locked onto designated lines, while the other 3 players are free to roam the grid, looking to receive and distribute the ball. The attacking team must complete a minimum of 5 passes before they are allowed to switch play to a different zone.The defending team consists of 3 players, and their objective is to win possession and disrupt the attacking team's flow. If the defenders regain possession and manage to switch play, they take over the attacking role and must maintain possession in the same structure. This drill encourages effective positioning, teamwork, and the ability to execute precise passes under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Switching Play: Encourage players to look for opportunities to switch play once they have completed the required 5 passes, using quick, accurate passes to move the ball across grids.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders should focus on cutting off passing lanes, pressuring the player in possession, and forcing errors without committing too early.• Positional Awareness: The 3 roaming players should constantly be aware of their positioning, always creating options for the player in possession and moving intelligently to support the ball carrier.• Quick Transitions: Emphasize the need for quick transitions, both offensively when switching play and defensively when regaining possession, to maintain tempo and control.
progression_one: Increase Defender Numbers:Increase the number of defenders from 3 to 4 or 5, making it more challenging for the attacking team to maintain possession and switch play.Focus: Improves the attacking team's ability to keep possession while under more intense pressure, emphasizing passing accuracy and movement.

title: Dortmund 4 Phase Overloaded
instructions_setup: This overload drill is played on 1/3 of the pitch and is structured into 4 distinct phases: two wide phases, one central phase, and one full phase. The drill follows a wave-style pattern, where each phase progressively builds up to create overload situations for the attacking team. The phases allow for different types of attacking setups, starting with the ball played from a deep server into whichever phase is ready to be executed.Each phase is designed to offer the attacking team an overload in terms of players, encouraging them to exploit space and create goal-scoring opportunities. As play progresses through each phase, players work on improving their decision-making, timing of runs, and overall attacking combinations. The drill focuses on developing fluid transitions between different areas of the pitch, with the attacking team always having the numerical advantage to break down the defense.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Overload: Ensure the attacking team maintains numerical superiority in each phase, allowing them to create space and make better decisions under pressure.• Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of transitioning quickly between phases, with the attacking team rapidly shifting their focus from one area of the pitch to another.• Timing of Runs: The attackers must time their runs well to ensure they are in the right position when the ball is played, particularly in the wide and central phases.• Exploiting Space: Players should always look to exploit the space created by the overload, making intelligent off-the-ball runs to stretch the defense and create opportunities.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Attackers:Limit the number of touches each attacker can take in each phase, forcing them to move the ball quickly and work on first-time passes.Focus: Enhances the speed of play and encourages the attacking team to think and execute quickly, simulating match-like conditions.

title: Dortmund Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery drill, every player starts with a ball within their respective grid. Players are tasked with dribbling around the grid unopposed, using a variety of skills, turns, and changes of direction to develop close ball control and agility. This drill helps improve dribbling under different conditions and encourages players to think creatively with the ball.The coach will blow the whistle at different intervals to add complexity to the drill. Upon a single whistle, players must quickly exchange their ball with another player within their own grid, fostering quick reactions and decision-making. When the coach blows the whistle twice, players must change their ball with someone from the opposite side of the grid, increasing the challenge by involving spatial awareness and coordination with other players.
coaching_notes: • Variety of Skills: Encourage players to use a mix of dribbling techniques, including feints, turns, and accelerations, to maintain close control and keep the ball moving.• Quick Reactions: Players must react quickly to the whistle, developing their ability to make fast decisions and adapt to changing situations.• Spatial Awareness: When changing balls with a player across the grid, players should be aware of their positioning and the location of others, making sure to execute the exchange efficiently.• Control Under Pressure: Reinforce the importance of maintaining control of the ball while moving at speed, especially when switching balls or making sudden changes in direction.
progression_one: Introduce Defensive Pressure:Add one defender into each grid who will attempt to pressure the ball carrier. The attacker must still change balls at the sound of the whistle while evading the defender.Focus: Helps players improve their ball control under pressure, simulating more realistic game situations.
progression_two: Limited Touches per Dribble:Limit players to only two touches of the ball before they must change direction or pass it to a teammate. This forces quicker thinking and decision-making.Focus: Encourages faster decision-making and improves players' ability to dribble efficiently under time constraints.

title: Dortmund Build Up via Zones
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to help teams progress the ball from the defensive third to the halfway line while adhering to specific build-up principles. The team in possession must advance the ball into any of the three mini-goals placed along the halfway line. To add complexity and focus, the team must play directly through a pre-selected zone, simulating a key area of the pitch where a defensive midfielder or central player would typically operate. This zone can be adjusted depending on which aspect of the build-up play you want to target for improvement.The purpose of this exercise is to encourage players to play out from the back effectively, utilizing quick passes, off-the-ball movement, and decision-making. The team must maintain possession while navigating through the zone under pressure, developing their ability to control the game from deeper areas and progress through critical zones on the pitch.
coaching_notes: • Controlled Build-Up Play: Encourage short, sharp passes and quick ball circulation as players move the ball through the designated zone and towards the mini-goals.• Zone Awareness: Players should be aware of their surroundings when entering the designated zone, making sure to utilize this space effectively while under pressure from defenders.• Player Movement and Support: Focus on players making smart supporting runs into space after passing, especially around the key zone, to help maintain possession and create goal-scoring opportunities.• Passing Under Pressure: Work on passing with accuracy and pace in tight spaces to progress through the zone and move the ball quickly toward the mini-goals.
progression_one: Defensive Pressure in the Zone:Add a defender inside the critical zone to apply pressure to the team in possession, forcing them to make quicker decisions and better use of space.Focus: Develops the ability to maintain possession and play through a zone under pressure, simulating match-like conditions.
progression_two: Increase Passing Complexity:Limit the team in possession to using a minimum number of passes before they can enter the zone. This increases the tempo and forces players to focus on efficient ball movement.Focus: Encourages faster decision-making and quicker ball circulation, replicating the need for fast build-up in a game scenario.

title: Dortmund Conditioning SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game begins with a short burst of conditioning work where players sprint from their designated grid to the sideline and back. This sprint acts as a warm-up and prepares players for the intensity of the game. Once the players return to their grid, the small-sided game begins immediately, allowing the players to transition into game situations with no break in play. The game lasts for 30 seconds or until a goal is scored, ensuring that players remain engaged and focused on maintaining a high level of intensity throughout the drill.After either 30 seconds of play or a goal being scored, the teams jog back to the sideline, complete another sprint, and restart the cycle. This continuous rotation helps to develop both fitness and game-related skills under fatigue, simulating match conditions where players must remain sharp even as they get tired.
coaching_notes: • Speed and Endurance: Emphasize the importance of sprinting with maximum effort during the conditioning phase to simulate match intensity and improve overall fitness.• Quick Transition: Players should transition quickly from the conditioning to the game phase, ensuring they remain focused and ready to compete immediately once play begins.• Game Focus Under Fatigue: Remind players to maintain concentration and execute technical skills properly during the 30-second game phase, despite fatigue from the sprints.• Team Communication: Encourage players to communicate effectively throughout the drill, especially during transitions, to maintain team structure and shape during the game.
progression_one: Increase Sprint Distance:Extend the sprint distance or reduce the rest time between sprints to increase the conditioning demand and further challenge players’ stamina.Focus: Increases the conditioning element and simulates match fatigue, testing players' ability to maintain high intensity and decision-making throughout the game.
