progression_two: Limit Touches in the Game Phase:Limit the number of touches players can take during the small-sided game (e.g., two touches only) to increase the speed of play and encourage quicker decision-making.Focus: Encourages players to think quickly and make fast decisions while under fatigue, promoting faster ball movement and sharper tactical awareness.

title: Dortmund Double 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill begins with the coach serving a ball to one of the two attacking players. The attacker will then play out a 1v1 scenario against the defender, attempting to score in one of the two goals on a small-sided pitch. The 1v1 continues until the ball goes dead, either by a goal being scored, a tackle made, or the ball going out of bounds. Once the first phase concludes, the coach immediately serves a second ball into the second attacker, who now plays a 1v1 in the opposite direction, ensuring both attackers get multiple opportunities to showcase their skills.This drill emphasizes individual attacking and defending skills, focusing on decision-making, dribbling, and creating space in 1v1 situations. The quick transitions between each phase of the drill simulate match-like conditions, allowing players to work on their reactions and ability to perform under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Movement: Encourage attackers to use quick, sharp movements to beat the defender, utilizing feints, cuts, and changes of pace to create space.• Defensive Positioning: Focus on defenders maintaining a solid stance, forcing attackers wide and limiting their options while staying compact to block shots.• Decision-Making: Attackers should be encouraged to assess the situation quickly—whether to take on the defender, pass, or shoot, based on the position of the defender.• Quick Transitions: Remind players to transition immediately after the ball goes dead, ensuring they are always ready to attack or defend at full intensity when the next phase begins.
progression_one: Introduce Limited Touches for Attackers:Limit attackers to only two or three touches on the ball during the 1v1 phase. This encourages faster play and decision-making, while also improving ball control and efficiency.Focus: Promotes quick decision-making and improves attackers' ability to execute under pressure with fewer touches.
progression_two: Add a Neutral:Introduce a neutral to the 1v1 phase, creating a 2v1 situation for the attacker. This progression increases the challenge for the attacker, forcing them to think more tactically and make quicker decisions.Focus: Improves the attacker’s ability to handle pressure from multiple defenders and encourages better passing and positioning to break down defensive setups.

title: Dortmund Finish the Attack Rondo
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 3v1 rondo, where the three attacking players maintain possession against a single defender. After completing a specified number of passes, the attacking team breaks out of the rondo and transitions into a 3v2 attack. The aim is to exploit the overload created during the breakout and attempt to score in one of the mini goals positioned on either side of the area. If the defending players manage to win possession during the rondo phase, they have the opportunity to counter-attack and score in the mini goals.This drill emphasizes quick decision-making, ball retention under pressure, and rapid transition from defensive to attacking play. It also provides valuable practice in both attacking and defensive phases, simulating match situations where players must capitalize on overloads and win possession in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: Encourage the attacking players to focus on quick, sharp passing to retain possession in the 3v1, avoiding any slow touches that may allow the defender to intercept.• Movement Off the Ball: Instruct the attacking players to move constantly to create passing lanes, making it easier for the ball carrier to find options and maintain possession.• Attacking Transition: Once the ball breaks out of the rondo, emphasize the need for fast transitions, with attacking players immediately looking to exploit the 3v2 overload and move the ball into dangerous areas.• Defensive Pressure: For the defending player in the rondo, highlight the importance of positioning and anticipation, ensuring they read the game and attempt to intercept or force mistakes without diving into tackles unnecessarily.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Breakout:Introduce a time limit for how long the breakout can take after leaving the rondo. This forces the attacking players to make quicker decisions during the transition and encourages urgency in moving the ball forward into the 3v2 scenario.Focus: Increases tempo, helping players practice quick counter-attacks and develop the ability to exploit overloads efficiently.

title: Dortmund Finishing & SAQ
instructions_setup: This finishing drill focuses on combining speed, agility, and quick decision-making with a final shot on goal. The drill begins with the attacking player playing a forward pass to a second player before immediately moving through a set of poles in a speed, agility, and quickness (SAQ) drill. As the first player moves through the poles, the second player passes the ball to a third player, who then sets the ball back to the original player just as they exit the poles. The original player, now positioned for a shot, finishes the drill with a strike on goal.This drill emphasizes the importance of movement off the ball, quick transitions, and sharp finishing under pressure. The SAQ element helps players improve their footwork and agility, ensuring they can be dynamic both with and without the ball, while the final shot allows for precision under game-like conditions.
coaching_notes: • Quick Forward Pass: The player making the initial pass should focus on a crisp, forward-thinking ball to set up the second player. The ball should be delivered with enough pace for the receiver to move it forward quickly.• SAQ Focus: When going through the poles, ensure the player uses controlled, sharp movements to stay agile and maintain balance, enabling a quick transition to the final shot.• Timing the Set: The third player’s pass back to the original player should be timed precisely so that the player exiting the poles can take the shot in stride, maximizing the shot’s power and accuracy.• Shot Technique: Instruct the player receiving the ball after the SAQ to focus on striking the ball cleanly with proper technique, aiming for placement over power, while keeping their composure after the dynamic movement.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender to apply light pressure on the player taking the shot. This progression encourages players to stay composed under pressure and practice finishing with a defender closing in.Focus: Builds confidence in finishing under pressure, simulating a real game scenario where defenders challenge the striker.
progression_two: Vary the Poles Layout:Adjust the layout and number of poles for the SAQ section, making it more complex or varied to challenge the player’s agility and coordination further, improving their ability to navigate through tight spaces.Focus: Enhances footwork and agility, ensuring players can transition smoothly from technical skill to game-speed execution.

title: Dortmund Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This is a competitive 1v1 + shooting reaction drill that sharpens players' speed, decision-making, and finishing ability.The practice begins when the coach calls out two cone colours. Two players must sprint to the first cone, then the second, before racing toward a centrally placed ball just ahead of the cones.The first player to reach the ball initiates a 1v1 with the goalkeeper, aiming to score quickly. Once the 1v1 concludes, the coach immediately serves a ball to the second player, who must attempt a longer-range shot from deeper, simulating a follow-up opportunity under fatigue or delayed arrival.This drill promotes sharp reactions, sprinting under pressure, and different types of finishing scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Acceleration Mechanics: Encourage explosive sprints with good body posture; technique matters in these high-intensity races.• 1v1 Decision-Making: The first player must make quick choices—whether to dribble, shoot early, or round the keeper—based on the keeper’s positioning.• Second Player Focus: Stress composure and technique on the follow-up shot, especially when tired or under mental pressure after just missing the race.
progression_one: Serve Second Ball as a Half-Volley or Aerial Delivery:Instead of a grounded pass, the coach serves the second ball as a lofted delivery that must be struck on the half-volley or first-time.Focus: Challenges the second player’s technique and timing, promoting more advanced striking skills under pressure.

title: Dortmund Pass & Movement
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up focuses on improving key skills such as 1-touch passing, receiving on the half-turn, and quick combination play. Players will work through a series of passing drills where they must receive the ball with the appropriate foot, adjust their body to receive on the half-turn, and use quick, accurate passes to maintain the flow of the game. The drill emphasizes small, effective movements off the ball to create space and provide passing options, with a particular focus on speed and precision in executing the passes.The goal of this warm-up is to improve players' technical ability and their awareness of space, ensuring they can move the ball quickly and efficiently in tight situations. It also helps to develop fluidity in combination play, promoting a quick-thinking mindset that can be applied in real match scenarios.
coaching_notes: • 1-Touch Passing: Encourage players to pass the ball with one touch whenever possible, keeping the tempo high and the ball moving quickly. Focus on accuracy and speed in delivering the passes.• Receiving on the Half-Turn: Instruct players to receive the ball on the half-turn to immediately face the direction they want to play, reducing time and increasing decision-making speed.• Small Movements to Receive: Players should focus on making subtle, quick movements to offer themselves as a passing option. Emphasize that players should always be on the move to stay in the game and find space.• Combination Play: Encourage quick 1-2 passing between players to break down defensive lines. Ensure that players remain aware of their surroundings, always looking to play the next pass with intent and precision.

title: Dortmund Rondo to Counter
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 5v3 rondo, where the team in possession must complete a minimum of 8 passes before having the opportunity to score in either of the 2 mini-goals positioned around the grid. The defending team is tasked with disrupting possession and attempting to win the ball back through tactical pressure and interception. Once possession is won, the defending team transitions into an immediate counter-attack, aiming to score in the main goal with a 4v2 advantage.The key focus of this practice is to develop quick ball movement, accurate passing, and decision-making under pressure for the team in possession. The defending team, on the other hand, should focus on anticipation, cutting off passing lanes, and being proactive in winning the ball back to launch a swift counter-attack. This drill combines possession play with a realistic transition into attack, simulating game situations that require both technical and tactical awareness.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Movement: Emphasize fast, accurate passing to help the possession team complete the required number of passes. Encourage players to switch the ball and look for gaps in the defense to exploit.• Effective Pressing: The defending team should focus on closing down passing lanes and applying pressure at the right moments to force turnovers. Reinforce the importance of positioning and communication to prevent the ball from being passed easily.• Transition to Attack: Once possession is won, the defending team must transition quickly and decisively into a 4v2 counter-attack. Players should focus on creating overloads and exploiting the numerical advantage in the attacking phase.• Mini-Goal Scoring: For the attacking team, emphasize calmness and precision when shooting at the mini-goals. Encourage players to be creative in their movement and to look for the best passing option to break the defense.
progression_one: Introduce a Time Limit:Limit the amount of time the possession team has to complete the 8 passes before being allowed to score. This will force quicker decision-making and faster transitions.Focus: Enhances the speed of passing and creates a more competitive, game-like environment where decisions must be made quickly.
progression_two: Add a Second Defender to the Counter-Attack:Increase the difficulty for the counter-attacking team by adding a second defender, making the 4v2 counter-attack a 4v3. This will encourage more strategic movement from the counter-attacking players.Focus: Helps the attacking team work on finding solutions to break down a more organized defense while maintaining the tempo of their attack.

title: Dortmund SAQ & Finishing
instructions_setup: This drill, frequently used by Jose Mourinho, is designed to develop a player’s ability to combine and finish after completing a set SAQ (Speed, Agility, and Quickness) routine. The practice begins with players running through a series of agility cones, focusing on rapid footwork and quick direction changes. Once through the SAQ section, players receive a pass and immediately transition into a finishing opportunity on goal. The drill emphasizes both physical conditioning and sharp finishing, ensuring players can execute under pressure and transition smoothly between different aspects of play.The integration of SAQ exercises with finishing adds a dynamic layer to the practice, pushing players to develop their technical and physical skills simultaneously. The high intensity of the drill helps improve reaction times, coordination, and mental sharpness while maintaining a focus on the technical execution of the finish. This combination of fitness and finishing is ideal for game situations that require players to react quickly and be clinical in front of goal.
coaching_notes: • Agility and Speed: Encourage players to maintain high intensity throughout the SAQ portion, focusing on fast, explosive movements and quick changes of direction to replicate match scenarios.• Quick Decision-Making: After completing the SAQ section, players should quickly assess their options for the finish. Encourage them to be calm and precise with their shot selection, whether that’s going for a power finish or placing the ball accurately.• Finishing Under Pressure: The player should aim to take their shot immediately after the SAQ section, simulating the pressure of a real match where they need to finish quickly after making a run or receiving the ball.• Body Positioning: Remind players to maintain good body positioning throughout the drill, especially when receiving the ball after the SAQ section. Proper body alignment will help them execute cleaner, more controlled finishes.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce one or two passive defenders after the SAQ section to apply pressure on the attacking player, forcing them to make quicker decisions and increase the intensity of the finish.Focus: This progression simulates more game-like conditions where players need to finish under pressure while also making sure their movement through the cones remains sharp.
progression_two: Multiple Finishing Options:Allow players to choose different types of finishes after completing the SAQ routine (e.g., volley, chip, driven shot). This progression tests their ability to adapt to various scenarios in front of goal.Focus: Encourages versatility in finishing techniques and helps players improve their ability to make the best decision based on the situation.

title: Dortmund Throw In Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed throw-in routine drill is designed to help players rehearse structured patterns and movements to effectively retain possession or create attacking opportunities from throw-ins. The team will work on a variety of short, medium, and long throw-in routines, with an emphasis on timing, angles, and decision making.Players will position themselves based on the chosen routine — whether it’s a quick short option, a set play into feet or chest, or a long throw into the box. The thrower will look to deliver the ball into the designated area, while teammates execute coordinated movements to receive, lay off, or create space. The drill is unopposed, allowing the team to focus on technical precision, role clarity, and the fluid execution of pre-rehearsed routines.
coaching_notes: • Movement to Receive:Players must time their movements to arrive at the receiving zone just before the throw arrives. Movements should be sharp and purposeful, offering clear options to the thrower and forcing defenders to make difficult choices.• Support Angles & Lay-Offs:Ensure players are providing effective support angles, both in front and behind the ball. Encourage quick lay-offs, wall passes, or second-ball reactions to maintain tempo and exploit space.• Throwing Technique & Decision Making:The thrower should vary their delivery depending on the situation — flat and quick for short throws, loopy for longer distances, or driven throws for aggressive third-man plays. Decision making must be quick to take advantage of disorganized defenders.• Spacing & Role Clarity:Players should understand their role in the routine — including decoy movements, screening, or receiving under pressure. Effective spacing is critical to avoid congestion and give the thrower multiple viable options.• Communication & Triggers:Use visual or verbal cues to coordinate movement and ensure everyone is aligned with the chosen routine. Clear communication between the thrower and teammates helps maintain flow and reduce hesitation.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to provide light marking and simulate real match conditions. The defenders should track runners and apply mild pressure without fully contesting the throw-in.Focus: Helps the attacking team practice their routines under slightly pressured conditions, ensuring movement and execution can hold up in more realistic settings.

title: Dortmund Wide Overloads SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game (SSG) involves three teams of four players, where two teams compete in a 4v4 format while the third team serves as bounce players positioned along the outside of the grid. The bounce players are limited to one touch and play a key role in helping the teams maintain possession and progress the ball quickly. The main goal of the game is to score in one central goal, and teams rotate in and out, ensuring a dynamic and fast-paced environment with constant engagement.The game encourages quick transitions and fluid attacking play, as teams must rely on their bounce players to keep the ball moving quickly. With only one goal to score in, teams need to focus on fast, direct play to break down the opposition while using the bounce players effectively to maintain pressure and keep possession. This setup promotes a high-intensity, continuous flow of play and helps improve players’ decision-making, positioning, and communication.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of quick ball movement when switching possession, as players need to use the bounce players effectively to maintain a fast pace and build attacks.• Effective Use of Bounce Players: Encourage the team in possession to involve the bounce players by making smart passes and utilizing the one-touch rule to keep the game fluid. Players should be aware of space and timing when passing to the bounce players.• High Press and Intensity: The limited 1-touch rule for bounce players should encourage both attacking teams to press high and keep the tempo high. This intensity will help the players focus on creating opportunities quickly.• Space Awareness: Players must constantly be aware of the positioning of the bounce players and their teammates to maintain possession and exploit the wide areas. This requires quick decision-making and anticipation.
progression_one: Limit Possession Time for Attacking Teams:Implement a rule where each team can only maintain possession for a set amount of time (e.g., 15 seconds) before having to make a shot on goal or pass to a bounce player.Focus: This progression increases the urgency of ball movement and decision-making, encouraging quicker attacks and better use of space.
progression_two: Add a Second Goal:Introduce a second mini-goal for teams to score into, increasing the attacking options and forcing players to spread the game across the whole area.Focus: This progression enhances attacking variety, challenging teams to think about different ways to break down the opposition and create scoring opportunities.

title: England Attack & Counter
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on maintaining controlled possession on one side of the pitch while working on combination play to break down the opposition. The team in possession should focus on maintaining accurate, sharp passes to move the ball effectively and create scoring opportunities. After a goal is scored, or if the ball goes off-target, the player positioned on the central line can immediately counter-attack under pressure from a recovering defender.This transition encourages both attacking and defending teams to react quickly, ensuring the game stays dynamic and continuous. The defenders’ objective is not only to recover the ball but also to press the counter-attacking player, forcing them to make quick decisions while under pressure. If the defending team wins possession, they can pass the ball forward to the counter-attacker to keep the pace high and maintain attacking flow.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Passing and Movement: Encourage players to make quick, sharp passes to maintain possession and move the ball through the area. This requires good communication and awareness of teammates' positions.• Quick Transitions: As soon as possession is lost, the team must react quickly. The counter-attacking player should be ready to break forward, and the defenders should focus on recovering quickly to prevent the counter.• Pressure on the Counter: Defenders need to close down the counter-attacking player aggressively, forcing them to make a decision under pressure. The attacker should focus on making quick, accurate decisions to exploit space.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should stay compact and communicate effectively to close down passing lanes and prevent an easy forward pass to the counter-attacker.
progression_one: Introduce a Time Limit for Possession:Set a maximum amount of time (e.g., 15 seconds) that the team in possession can maintain the ball before they must either attempt to score or pass to the counter-attacking player.Focus: This progression increases the tempo and encourages faster decision-making from the attacking team, forcing them to maintain an attacking mindset while managing the possession time.
progression_two: Increase Pressure on the Counter-Attacker:Introduce a second defender who joins the counter-attack scenario, adding pressure and forcing the counter-attacker to make faster, more accurate decisions.Focus: This progression challenges the counter-attacker to deal with increased pressure and improve their decision-making when under duress, simulating more realistic game situations.

title: England Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to help players master various skills and techniques that are crucial in 1v1 scenarios. The focus is on improving close ball control, quick decision-making, and the ability to beat an opponent using a skill move. Players will dribble towards a central mannequin, where they will execute a pre-set skill to perform a take-on and then pass the ball forward into the next player, continuing the flow of the drill.By repeating this skill work, players can build confidence in executing take-ons in game situations. The emphasis is on using a variety of moves such as step-overs, feints, or body swerves to bypass the mannequin, simulating real game pressure and providing players with tools to break down defensive players effectively.
coaching_notes: • Skill Variety: Encourage players to use a range of moves, such as step-overs, drag-backs, and body feints, to help them become more unpredictable and versatile in 1v1 situations.• Close Control: Stress the importance of tight ball control when approaching the mannequin, ensuring that the player is able to execute the skill quickly and accurately without losing possession.• Explosive Movement: Players should focus on making quick, explosive movements after performing the skill to get past the defender or mannequin and create space for the next pass.• Head Up and Decision Making: Encourage players to keep their heads up as they approach the mannequin so they can read the situation and decide which skill or move will be most effective in that moment.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender who must attempt to stop the player from completing the skill move. The attacker must now beat the defender to progress, increasing the game realism.Focus: This progression will help players practice the skills under more realistic pressure, simulating actual game scenarios where they must execute moves while being defended against.
progression_two: Multiple Skills in One Take-On:Require players to perform two or three consecutive skills in one take-on to bypass the mannequin, creating a more challenging and unpredictable scenario.Focus: This progression encourages players to build a more sophisticated approach to 1v1 situations, improving their creativity and adaptability when taking on opponents.

title: England Breaking Lines
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on breaking lines and progressing the ball through compact defensive structures using numerical superiority.The setup consists of multiple vertical zones (typically 3 or 4), with 3 attacking players vs 2 defenders in each active zone. The aim is for the possession team to combine quickly and accurately to find forward passes that break into the next zone.Once a pass is made into the next zone, two players from the current zone can travel with the ball to maintain the 3v2 overload in the next section. This simulates real-game scenarios where players must support progression and create superiority through movement and timing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Speed: Encourage sharp passing and tempo. The quicker the ball moves, the more likely gaps open in a compact 2-man block.• Breaking Lines Criteria: Set clear expectations—passes must break two defenders, not just go sideways. Reward risk-taking and brave passes.• Body Positioning: Players must constantly scan, receive side-on, and play on the half-turn to progress play efficiently.Progression 1 : Add Recovery Defender on Transition:Once the ball is played into the next zone, one defender from the previous zone recovers and joins to add some pressure to the ball.Focus: Simulates defensive recovery runs and increases pressure on progression play.

title: England Build Up v Press
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on building possession under pressure and transitioning quickly to maintain attacking momentum. Play starts with two defenders sprinting into the grid to attempt to win possession. The attacking team must complete five passes on one side of the grid before transferring the ball to the other side. Once the ball is transferred, two new defenders sprint in to replace the original defenders, and the drill continues. If the defenders win possession, they transition into a counter-attack and attempt to score in one of the main goals.The key to success in this drill is for the attacking team to maintain composure under pressure and work together to complete passes. The defenders must be alert and aggressive in trying to win the ball and transition quickly into attack once possession is regained.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: Encourage players to move the ball quickly and decisively to complete the five-pass requirement efficiently, minimizing the chance of defensive interceptions.• Movement and Support: Players should focus on providing passing options for the ball carrier, using intelligent off-the-ball movement to create angles and maintain possession under pressure.• Transition Speed: Once the ball is transferred, the attacking team must be ready to switch focus and exploit space on the other side of the grid, while the defenders quickly recover to disrupt the new attack.• Defensive Aggression: Defenders should be proactive in closing down passing lanes and applying pressure, trying to force mistakes or intercept passes to quickly transition to an attacking scenario.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce an additional defender or reduce the number of passes needed before transitioning to increase the pressure on the attacking team and create a more challenging environment for maintaining possession.Focus: This progression simulates higher levels of defensive pressure, encouraging quicker decision-making and better positioning from the attacking players.

title: England Combinations SSG
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 2v2 in the first zone, where the team in possession aims to progress the ball into the next zone. If successful, one player from the attacking team can cross the line to create a 3v2 in the second zone. The objective is for the attacking team to work together, progress the ball, and create overloads to increase their chances of scoring.The players in the second zone must cross a dotted line in order to score, encouraging them to drive forward and make decisive runs once the ball has been played into the next zone. The defenders are tasked with limiting space and denying the attacking team from getting a shot at the goal.
coaching_notes: • Progressive Play: Emphasize the importance of quick passing and movement to progress the ball from one zone to the next, ensuring the team doesn't waste time or possession in the first zone.• Creating Overloads: Once the attacking team is able to progress the ball, the additional player joining to create a 3v2 should focus on exploiting the numerical advantage and creating space for goal-scoring opportunities.• Communication: Encourage players to communicate and make sure everyone is on the same page when transitioning from zone to zone, ensuring the attacking team keeps fluid movement and maintains possession.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders must stay compact and organized in the first zone, while transitioning quickly to limit the attacking team’s space once the overload is created in the second zone.
progression_one: Add More Defenders in the Second Zone:Increase the number of defenders in the second zone to make the transition from 2v2 to 3v2 more difficult, forcing the attacking team to work harder for space and possession.Focus: This progression develops attacking players' decision-making skills, as they must now choose when to create overloads and when to be patient with possession.
progression_two: Score in Multiple Zones:Allow the attacking team to score in any zone once they cross the dotted line, not just in the second zone. This forces the attackers to be more dynamic in their movement and adjust to different spaces for potential scoring chances.Focus: This progression encourages adaptability and creativity from the attacking players, as they need to be aware of multiple options for scoring across the different zones.

title: England Double Gate 1v1
instructions_setup: This 1v1 drill focuses on encouraging players to use their body effectively to escape opposition and drive through one of the two gates located on the outer sides of the grid in each zone. The objective is to develop close control, quick decision-making, and the ability to protect the ball while under pressure. Players must use their body to shield the ball and find a route to break free, either by using pace or skill.Once they successfully escape through one of the gates and transition into the next zone, they will pass the ball to the next attacking player and immediately switch roles to defend. The new defender must try to stop the oncoming attacker from escaping through the gates, ensuring a continuous flow of attacking and defensive transitions.
coaching_notes: • Body Positioning: Emphasize the importance of using the body to shield the ball when under pressure. Players should focus on keeping the ball close and using their body to protect it while driving toward the gates.• Quick Decision-Making: Encourage players to make quick decisions when approaching the gates, either using skill or pace to break free from the defender.• Transitioning Quickly: After escaping through the gate, players must quickly transition to a defensive role, staying alert to stop the next attacker from breaking through the gates.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should focus on closing down the attacker’s space, positioning themselves to block potential escape routes and prevent the attacker from passing through the gates.

title: England Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This drill begins with two defenders sprinting towards the halfway line, where they will compete for and win a header against an attacker or in the air. The focus is on aerial duels and the ability to clear the ball effectively from dangerous areas.After completing the header, the defenders must quickly recover by sprinting back towards their own penalty box, where they will deal with a cross from a wide area. The drill helps to simulate match scenarios where defenders need to win aerial challenges and then rapidly recover to deal with subsequent threats, ensuring they stay alert to the game’s demands.
coaching_notes: • Aerial Challenge Focus: Emphasize the importance of timing and positioning when going for headers. Defenders should aim to meet the ball at its highest point while ensuring they are in a good position to clear it effectively.• Quick Recovery After Header: Once the header is won, defenders must immediately focus on recovery, sprinting back quickly to defend the box and prepare for any crosses coming into the area.• Crossing Awareness: Defenders should always be aware of the ball's trajectory and the positioning of attackers to prevent easy headers or shots from the cross. Encourage defenders to stay goal-side of their marker.• Communication: Encourage defenders to communicate with each other, especially when recovering from a header, ensuring they cover the correct areas and are aware of potential threats.
progression_one: Add Attacking Players to Challenge Headers:Introduce one or two attackers to challenge for the header alongside the defenders. This will increase the pressure on defenders to win the aerial duel.Focus: This progression builds on defenders’ ability to compete in the air under pressure and refine their decision-making when facing a contested header.
progression_two: Cross Delivered with Varying Heights and Angles:Have the wide player deliver crosses at varying heights and angles to make it more difficult for defenders to judge the ball. This will challenge defenders’ positioning and timing.Focus: This progression helps defenders to adapt to different types of crosses, improving their ability to deal with a variety of aerial and ground deliveries in game situations.

title: England Front 2 Link Up
instructions_setup: This finishing drill is designed to develop the relationship between the front two strikers. The focus is on creating quick, effective link-up play between the forwards through a variety of passes and movements, ultimately leading to an unopposed finish.The drill helps improve communication, timing, and understanding between two attacking players, enhancing their ability to combine in match situations.
coaching_notes: • Pass from Midfielder: The drill begins with a pass played from a midfielder into one of the forwards. The receiving forward should be aware of their positioning and make sure they receive the ball in a way that allows them to quickly combine with the second striker.• Link-Up Play Between Strikers: After receiving the ball, the forward will play a pass to the second striker, either through a quick 1-2 combination, a lay-off, or a direct pass depending on the situation. Emphasize the importance of precise passing and the quick movement off the ball. The two forwards should be looking to communicate with each other, either verbally or with body language, to ensure fluid link-up play.• Movement: Both forwards should focus on intelligent, dynamic movement to create space for each other. One striker should always look to make a movement that pulls the defender out of position, allowing the other striker to receive the ball in a dangerous area.• Finishing: Once the second striker receives the ball, they should finish with composure, either with a placed shot or a powerful strike depending on the situation. The key is to finish quickly and efficiently, capitalizing on the work done by both forwards in the link-up play.• Timing and Decision-Making: The forwards must time their movements to ensure they are available for the pass and can take advantage of any gaps in the defense. They must also make quick decisions on whether to play a one-touch pass, take a touch to control the ball, or take a shot on goal.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure:Introduce one or two defenders to apply light pressure to the forwards as they combine. This will force the strikers to complete the link-up play under pressure, simulating a more realistic game scenario.Focus: Enhances the ability to link up and finish under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Offside Rule:Introduce the offside rule, meaning the forwards must time their runs carefully and avoid being caught offside when making their movements. This will improve their timing and understanding of attacking runs.Focus: Improves the awareness of offside traps and timing of forward runs.

title: England One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 drill focuses on developing sharp receiving skills, quick decision-making, and passing accuracy under pressure. The player receives a pass from the coach and, based on the coach’s call, must quickly scan, react, and pass the ball into one of four colour-coded mini goals. This simulates scanning and playing under changing visual cues in a game-like scenario.
coaching_notes: • Take a Controlled First Touch to Prepare the Pass – Guide the ball into your stride with intent to set up a clean, accurate pass.• Keep Your Head Up to React Quickly – As the coach calls a colour, scan instantly and adjust your body shape to face the correct goal.• Be Precise With Weight and Direction of Pass – Strike through the ball with purpose, aiming cleanly for the centre of the mini goal with correct pace.• Stay Balanced When Adjusting to Late Colour Cues – Keep your knees bent and stay light on your feet so you can quickly change angles and deliver clean technique.
progression_one: Vary Timing of the Coach’s Colour CallSometimes call the colour before the ball is passed, and other times as the ball is arriving to increase unpredictability and challenge reaction timing.Focus:Improves reaction speed, passing under pressure, and visual scanning before and during ball reception in unpredictable moments.

title: England Passing Between Lines
instructions_setup: This passing practice is designed to help build up play from the back, focusing on central defenders playing forward passes to players receiving between the lines. The use of mannequins replicates a defensive block, helping players understand the spatial dynamics and timing required to break down defensive lines.The practice focuses on improving decision-making, accuracy in passing, and understanding movement off the ball in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Starting Play with the Central Defenders: The drill begins with the central defenders playing a forward pass to a midfielder or attacker positioned between the lines of the defensive block. The defenders should be encouraged to vary the types of passes, using both direct and indirect methods to break the lines of defense.• Receiving Between the Lines: The player receiving the ball between the lines should focus on creating space to receive and should have their body position open to allow for a quick, controlled first touch. Emphasize the importance of awareness—players need to see both their immediate surroundings and the space behind the defensive line to make the correct decision.• Role of the Mannequins: The mannequins are positioned to simulate a defensive block, with 8 mannequins representing defenders in various positions on the field. The player receiving the ball between the lines should focus on how to maneuver around the defenders, either by playing quick passes, using feints, or by finding pockets of space to exploit.• Movement off the Ball: The players should focus on making intelligent runs to create space between the defensive lines, ensuring the player receiving the ball has options for the next pass. Good off-the-ball movement is key to creating passing lanes and breaking through defensive lines.• Progression to Passing and Moving: After receiving the ball, the player should look to quickly pass to the next player or forward into the attacking third. The player who passed the ball initially should follow their pass to support the next phase of play, continuing the build-up by moving into a new position or creating an option for the next pass.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure:Introduce one or two defenders to actively pressure the receiving player after the forward pass. This will force the player to be more decisive with their first touch and pass while under pressure.Focus: Enhances decision-making under pressure and reinforces build-up play under defensive duress.

title: England Sliding Rondo
instructions_setup: This double 4v2 rondo focuses on developing possession play while incorporating quick transitions and teamwork. The practice requires players to maintain possession on both sides of the grid, while also working on their movement and awareness as they switch from one side to the other.The emphasis is on keeping the ball moving quickly, maintaining team shape, and transitioning smoothly between offensive and defensive roles.
coaching_notes: • Possession Play on Both Sides: The practice starts with 4 players on each side of the grid, working as a possession team against 2 defenders in the middle. The players on the sides should focus on quick, short passes, maintaining good ball movement, and supporting each other with constant off-the-ball movement.• Quick Transitions: Once the ball is transferred across the grid, the players on the side where the ball is played must immediately sprint to the opposite side, forming a new team of 4. This transition simulates the fast changes in possession and requires players to be constantly on their toes, ready to shift from offense to defense.• Defenders’ Role: The 2 defenders in the middle should work on positioning, closing passing lanes, and attempting to intercept the ball. Encourage them to apply pressure without diving in, focusing on forcing the attackers into less favorable positions.• Player Movement: As the ball moves across the grid, players should focus on making supporting runs to create passing lanes. Off-the-ball movement is critical in maintaining possession, so players should always be looking for opportunities to offer options for the passer.• Transition Speed: The speed at which the side players transition into the opposite grid is crucial. This helps the players develop the ability to move quickly in a game scenario, reacting to turnovers and regaining possession in a new part of the field.
progression_one: Add a Third Defender:Introduce a third defender to increase the pressure on the possession team. This will challenge the attacking players to work even harder to maintain possession and execute quick passes to evade the extra defender.Focus: Enhances decision-making under pressure and the ability to maintain possession against a numerical disadvantage.
progression_two: Reduce Time Per Touch:To increase the intensity, impose a time limit on each player’s touch (e.g., 2 or 3 seconds). This forces players to make quicker decisions and play at a faster tempo, improving their speed of thought and reaction.Focus: Improves quick decision-making and ball movement in high-pressure situations.

title: England Warm Up
instructions_setup: This fun and dynamic warm-up drill focuses on improving ball control, agility, and defensive awareness. The drill encourages attackers to keep possession of the ball while also developing the ability to quickly react and transition into defense.
coaching_notes: • Ball Control: Players will start with the ball at their feet or in one hand, depending on the variation used. Attackers should focus on maintaining tight ball control, using quick footwork or hand movements to evade the "catcher."• Catcher’s Role: The "catcher" is tasked with trying to win possession of the ball. This can be done by using body positioning, quick feet, or arms (if the ball is in hand) to disrupt the attacker’s control and knock the ball out of the grid.• Switching Roles: If the catcher successfully wins possession, the player who lost the ball must immediately switch roles and become the new defender. This transition should be quick, keeping the energy high and the drill competitive.• Encourage Movement: Attackers should focus on using quick changes of direction, fakes, and agility to keep the ball away from the catcher. Off-the-ball movement is important in creating space and maintaining possession.• Winning the Game: The game continues until only one player remains with the ball. The last player standing can choose the next "catcher," making it a fun and competitive activity that keeps players engaged.

title: England Wide Overload & Finish
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 2v1 scenario in a wide channel, where the two attackers work together using quick combinations and movement to break down the lone defender and score into a mini goal. The drill is designed to focus on quick decision-making, effective off-the-ball movement, and clinical finishing.The initial phase has the two attackers combining to manipulate the defender’s position and create space for a goal-scoring opportunity. The first attacker should focus on making sharp runs into space and offering passing options, while the second attacker must be prepared to either receive the ball and shoot or provide support by making a well-timed run to assist in the attack. The combination should be quick, with minimal touches, to disorient the defender and create a clear path to goal.
coaching_notes: • Combination Play: Emphasize sharp, one-touch passing to move the ball quickly and break down the defender. Encourage attacking players to vary their passing angles and make intelligent, overlapping runs to confuse the defender and open up space.• Off-the-Ball Movement: The attackers must continuously move to offer passing options. As one attacker plays a pass, they should move into space to either receive the ball back or support the other player’s attack. Quick and intelligent movement off the ball is critical in breaking down the defense.• Timing and Precision: The attackers must time their passes and runs well to ensure the ball reaches the correct player at the right moment. Precision is key—misplaced passes or poorly timed runs will allow the defender to regain control.• Finishing Under Pressure: After completing the initial 2v1 phase, one of the attackers exits the grid and receives an unopposed pass from the coach. This phase allows the player to focus on taking a composed shot on goal. Encourage players to focus on their technique, keeping their shot controlled and aimed for placement rather than just power.• Defender’s Role: The defender must actively try to disrupt the attacking combination by closing down space and forcing the attackers to make quick decisions. The defender’s positioning should encourage attackers to use skill and vision to break through.• Transition to Unopposed Finish: After the 2v1 phase, the player who exits the grid will be in a position to receive the ball from the coach and complete an unopposed finish. This phase simulates the transition from attack to finish, requiring the player to adjust quickly from a passing sequence to a final shot on goal.

title: Everton 1v1 into 2v2
instructions_setup: This practice starts with two 1v1 situations and transitions into a 2v2. Two players will dribble around a pole directly ahead of them before playing a pass back into a teammate who will then attack 1v1. The initial ball carrier must transition to defend immediately after their pass into a teammate. Once both 1v1’s are complete, the coach will serve a second ball into the practice, and a 2v2 situation will unfold. This drill emphasizes both attacking and defending transitions, as well as teamwork in the 2v2 phase.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition from Attacker to Defender – After completing the 1v1 attack, players should focus on quickly transitioning into a defensive role. They need to be alert and ready to press or contain the opposing attacker, maintaining defensive shape.• 1v1 Attack Focus – Players should work on using quick feet, dribbling moves, and changes of direction to beat their defender in the 1v1 phase. The key is to be decisive and take on the defender with confidence while looking for an opportunity to take a shot on goal.• Support in 2v2 – In the 2v2 phase, players should focus on creating space for each other. The attacking duo should communicate to combine and break down the defense, using quick passes and off-the-ball movement to create goal-scoring chances.• Defensive Awareness in 2v2 – In the 2v2 phase, defenders should work together to cover each other’s positions. Communication is critical to ensure they don’t leave gaps, and they should look to press the attackers while maintaining balance to avoid being easily bypassed.
progression_one: Add a Third AttackerIntroduce a third attacker on one side of the 2v2 phase to create a momentary overload for the attacking team. This adds complexity and challenges defenders to adapt to numerical superiority in the attack.Focus: Encourages attackers to use their numbers effectively and defenders to adapt to overload situations.
progression_two: Time the 2v2 PhaseSet a time limit for the 2v2 phase, encouraging players to make quick decisions and play with urgency. This will increase the intensity and focus players on executing the right decisions under pressure.Focus: Simulates game-like conditions where players must act quickly, especially in transition moments.

title: Everton 1v1 Plus Neutrals
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on 1v1 attacking skills while utilizing two neutrals to create a 3v1 overload in favor of the player in possession. The attacking player must beat the defender using quick dribbling, feints, and creativity, aiming to score in one of the two mini goals on the defender’s side of the field. The neutrals, positioned outside the grid, can be used to support the attacker by providing additional passing options but are restricted to one touch per pass.The attacker can pass to a neutral to pull the defender out of position and create space for an attack. The goal for the player in possession is to combine dribbling and passing to bypass the defender and take a clear shot on goal.
coaching_notes: • Attacker's Dribbling Focus: Encourage attackers to use quick changes of direction and feints to deceive the defender. They should focus on keeping the ball close and recognizing when to take on the defender or pass to a neutral.• Neutrals' Role: Neutrals should help overload the defender by offering passing options. Encourage attackers to use them effectively to draw defenders out of position and create space to attack.• Timing and Decision-Making: Stress the importance of timing when to dribble or pass to a neutral. Attackers should read the defender’s movements to decide the best moment to make their move or pass.• Defender's Patience and Positioning: Defenders should focus on staying in front of the attacker and forcing them into less dangerous areas without committing too early. Positioning is key to maintaining pressure.• Creating Space for the Shot: Once the attacker beats the defender, encourage them to take advantage of the space and aim for a clean shot on goal, maintaining awareness of their shooting angle.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce a second defender to create a 3v2 situation. This encourages the attacker to be more strategic in using the neutrals and making quick decisions.Focus: Enhances decision-making under pressure and forces attackers to read defensive shapes.

title: Everton 3 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This 3-phase finishing drill works on multiple types of finishes. In the first phase, the player drives inside from the wide area before taking a shot on goal. In the second phase, the player receives the ball on the outside and shoots across goal. In the third phase, the player works on finishing from sharp movements across the defender’s path, simulating a real-game scenario where attackers must adjust quickly to the ball and take advantage of space in the box.
coaching_notes: • Driving Inside (Phase 1) – Encourage the player to commit to driving inside with pace, using their body to shield the ball from the defender. Once inside the box, the player should be focused on keeping the shot low and accurate, aiming for the far corner or the near post.• Shooting Across Goal (Phase 2) – When receiving the ball on the outside, players should focus on staying composed and shooting across the goal, either with the inside of the foot for accuracy or the laces for power. The emphasis should be on aiming for the far post to beat the goalkeeper.• Finishing After Quick Movements (Phase 3) – Players should focus on making sharp movements across the defender’s path, positioning themselves to receive the ball in space. This requires quick footwork and a quick decision to finish with either a first-time shot or a quick controlled touch before shooting.• Variation of Finishing Techniques – Players should be encouraged to vary their finishing techniques depending on the angle and situation. Whether it's a driven shot, a chip, or a side-footed finish, the player must adapt to the ball’s delivery and the defensive pressure.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a defender who can apply light pressure to the player during each finishing phase, simulating real defensive challenges.Focus: Forces players to make quicker decisions and improve their ability to finish under pressure.
progression_two: Limit the Time for Each FinishSet a time limit for each finishing phase, encouraging the attacker to complete each phase quickly and with composure.Focus: Increases the intensity and helps players develop the ability to finish in game-like scenarios where time and space are limited.

title: Everton 3v3 Small Sided Game
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is played as a 3v3 with momentary 3v2 overloads. After every goal scored, the player who scored must exit the grid and sprint around one of the two outer poles before re-entering the grid. This creates a brief period of overload for the team that has just conceded a goal, simulating a transition phase where the defending team is at a numerical disadvantage. The practice encourages teams to recover quickly and efficiently, and the greater the effort the goal scorer puts into recovering around the poles, the less chance the opposing team will have of conceding immediately after scoring.
coaching_notes: • Quick Recovery and Transitions – Players should focus on recovering quickly after scoring by sprinting around the poles. The faster they recover, the better positioned they’ll be to defend against a quick counterattack.• Exploiting Overloads – Teams with a numerical advantage (3v2) should look to exploit the overload by creating space and focusing on quick passing to break down the opposition’s defense.• Defensive Awareness in Transition – Defenders must stay alert and organized, especially when the opposing team is working with an overload. Anticipating passes and staying compact is key to handling these brief moments of vulnerability.• Maximizing Effort – Encourage players to put in maximum effort, both in terms of recovering quickly and maintaining intensity throughout the game. The effort to recover will directly impact the team’s ability to score and defend effectively.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for RecoverySet a time limit within which the goal scorer must complete their recovery around the poles before re-entering the grid.Focus: Increases the intensity of the recovery phase, encouraging faster transitions and higher work rate from players.
progression_two: Increase the Number of OverloadsIntroduce a second player who also exits the grid after a goal is scored, increasing the number of overloads.Focus: Adds further pressure on the defending team to transition and recover quickly, simulating more chaotic moments in a match.

title: Everton Attacking 2v2 with Wingers
instructions_setup: This small-sided game starts with a 2v2 attack, where the attacking team must attempt to score into either of the 2 mini goals located ahead of them. While in possession, teams can use the 2 neutral players on the outside (wingers). These wingers are limited to 1 touch and cannot score themselves. The practice continues until the defending team regains possession, at which point they can counter-attack and attempt to score into either of the 2 mini goals. The practice works on both attacking and defensive transitions, with a focus on using wingers for support.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Combinations – The attacking team should focus on quick, fluid combinations between the 2v2 players, using the wingers to stretch the defense and create space. The wingers should focus on providing wide support and offering quick passes to maintain offensive pressure.• Winger Movement – The wingers should be active and provide constant support by making well-timed runs and offering passing options. Since they are limited to 1 touch, they must be precise and make quick decisions to maintain the flow of the attack.• Defensive Shape and Pressure – The defending team should work on maintaining a compact defensive shape to prevent through balls or crosses from the wingers. They must also press quickly when the ball is played to the wingers to limit their ability to make an impact.• Transition and Recovery – When possession is regained, the defending team should immediately transition into attack. Players should be ready to exploit the open space and make quick decisions to launch a counter-attack towards the mini goals.
progression_one: Wingers Can ScoreAllow the wingers to score from crosses or passes delivered into the box. This will encourage more dynamic attacking play and give the wingers a more active role in the attack.Focus: Enhances the role of the wingers in creating and finishing scoring opportunities.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit for AttackingIntroduce a time limit for the attacking team to score once they have possession, forcing quicker decision-making and more urgent play.Focus: Increases the speed of play and emphasizes quick transitions and finishing under pressure.

title: Everton Finishing & 3v3
instructions_setup: Play starts with 3 players combining in the wide areas, focusing on quick passes and movement to create space. They deliver a cross into the box, aiming for one or two of the wide players to finish unopposed. The emphasis is on accurate crossing and attacking runs to get into goal-scoring positions.After the unopposed finish, the coach serves the ball back to the 3 players, who now attack in a 3v3 situation against 3 defenders. The defenders start from behind the goalkeeper, and the game continues until the ball goes dead. Both teams are encouraged to score during the 3v3 phase, with the focus on quick transitions and decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Crossing Quality: Players should focus on delivering accurate, well-paced crosses into the box. Emphasize the importance of varying the cross, including driven balls and lofted crosses, to catch the defenders off guard.• Timing of Runs: Attacking players must time their runs into the box effectively, attacking the space and the cross. Encourage attackers to read the delivery and adjust their runs to meet the ball.• Attacker’s First Touch: After the cross is delivered, players should focus on using their first touch to control the ball and set up an unopposed finish. Remind players to stay calm and composed in front of goal.• Transition to 3v3: Once the unopposed finish is completed, players immediately transition into the 3v3 scenario. Encourage quick thinking and movement as the attacking team works to break down the defenders.• Defender’s Positioning: Defenders should focus on staying goal-side, blocking passing lanes, and staying tight to their mark. They must also anticipate crosses and be ready to clear the ball or disrupt attacking moves.
progression_one: Increase Pressure in 3v3:Introduce a rule where defenders can press more aggressively earlier in the 3v3 phase. This increases the intensity and forces attackers to make quicker decisions.Focus: Enhances attackers’ ability to create space and make quick decisions under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Counter-Attack Option:Allow the defending team to play a long pass into the attacking area after a defensive clearance. This forces both teams to transition quickly from offense to defense and vice versa.Focus: Builds players' ability to shift between attacking and defending quickly while maintaining composure in high-pressure situations.

title: Everton Midfield SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game allows midfield players to work on their progressive passing ability. Both teams will have a goalkeeper or neutral player positioned on the end lines who are limited to 1 touch and can be used for playing forward combinations. If selected as goalkeepers, the end line players can also protect the 2 mini goals positioned on their line, making the goalscoring element of the practice more challenging.
coaching_notes: • Progressive PassingEncourage midfielders to focus on breaking lines and playing forward passes that transition quickly from defense to attack. Look for opportunities to switch the ball to the end line players to create space in the central areas.• Linking with End Line PlayersMidfielders should maintain awareness of the end line players and use them as outlets for combinations, particularly when the central options are blocked. This keeps possession fluid and allows for better ball progression.• Defensive Shape and PressureDefenders should focus on cutting off the passing lanes to the end line players and limit the midfielders’ ability to turn and progress forward. Good pressure on the ball is key to forcing mistakes and regaining possession.• Timing of Runs and PassingThe timing of runs and passes is critical. Midfielders should time their forward passes to coincide with runs made by the end line players, ensuring the ball is played into space or to feet for an immediate combination.
progression_one: Restrict Passes to End Line PlayersLimit the number of passes a team can make before they must use the end line players for a forward combination. This encourages quicker transitions and encourages players to use the end line players effectively as a support outlet.Focus: This progression enhances quick thinking and tactical movement.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to ScoreIntroduce a time limit for each team to score after they reach the end line. This forces teams to increase the pace of play, improving their decision-making under pressure.Focus: This progression emphasizes urgency and faster decision-making in the final third.

title: Everton One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 technical practice is designed for centre-backs to work on two key defensive and distribution actions. In the first phase, the centre-back must deal with a long aerial ball by positioning themselves early and clearing effectively. In the second phase, they receive a ground pass under light pressure and must take a positive touch before playing a diagonal, line-breaking pass into one of two mini goals placed beyond an imaginary midfield line.
coaching_notes: • Judge the Flight Early – Read the height and direction of the aerial ball quickly to position yourself in the best zone to win it cleanly under pressure.• High-Point the Header – Attack the ball at its highest point, using your arms for balance and leverage to dominate aerially and clear with distance and control.• Clean First Touch After Recovery – After regaining position, take a composed first touch to set yourself up for a forward pass and shift body weight into the strike.• Pass with Purpose and Weight – Play a sharp, diagonal line-breaking pass into the mini goal, focusing on body shape, timing, and weight to replicate in-game realism.

title: Everton Technical Warm Up
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up allows players to develop their ability to play 1-2 and 3rd man combinations. Players are arranged in a grid with a set number of passes required before progressing the ball to a teammate. The focus is on quick, short passes and understanding the movement of the third player involved in the combination play. The drill can be adjusted to increase the intensity and complexity by incorporating different passing patterns, such as switching the direction of play or introducing defenders.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing – Encourage players to focus on quick, accurate passes. The success of 1-2 and 3rd man combinations depends on fast decision-making and fast ball movement. Players should avoid taking extra touches to ensure the pace stays high.• Third-Man Movement – The third player should always be ready to move into space, looking for areas where they can receive a pass or provide a passing option. They should aim to be ahead of the ball, anticipating the next pass.• Timing of Runs – For combinations to work effectively, the timing of the player’s runs must be precise. The player receiving the ball after the initial pass should time their run to meet the ball at the right moment, creating space and increasing the chance of success.• Spacing and Angles – Players should maintain proper spacing and positioning, ensuring they create passing lanes for each other. This helps to keep the ball moving quickly and efficiently, which is key in these types of combination plays.
progression_one: Introduce DefendersIntroduce 1 or 2 defenders to increase pressure on the attacking team. This will encourage faster decision-making and improve the attacking team's ability to execute combinations under pressure.Focus: Enhances the ability to play under defensive pressure while maintaining quick, fluid combinations.
progression_two: Increase the Number of PlayersIncrease the number of players involved in the passing combinations to build a higher level of complexity. This forces players to think ahead and incorporate more players into the build-up play.Focus: Develops teamwork and improves understanding of how to create space for others.

title: Everton Wide Rondo to Finish the Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 4v1 rondo in a wide area, where the possession-based team aims to complete a set number of successful passes before breaking out of the grid. Once the required passes are made, the possession team transitions into a 4v4 attacking phase, where they must look to progress the ball into a scoring position.The attacking phase can remain as a standard 4v4 or be adjusted by overloading or underloading the attacking team, depending on the intended tactical outcomes. The focus during the breakout should be on quick transitions and maintaining possession under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: Players in the rondo must focus on maintaining quick, accurate passes and movement off the ball to break down the defender and ensure smooth transition to the attacking phase.• Transition Focus: As the team breaks out of the grid, emphasize the importance of quick decision-making and exploiting the space created during the transition. The players should aim to quickly reorganize into an attacking shape.• Attacking Shape: If the team is overloaded or underloaded, ensure they adjust their positioning and use the numerical advantage or compensate for the disadvantage by maintaining compactness and applying pressure in key areas.• Finishing Focus: Once the attacking phase begins, encourage players to be direct and decisive in their actions, looking to create shooting opportunities quickly or work the ball into dangerous areas.
progression_one: Increase Pressure on Possession Team:Introduce more defenders in the rondo (e.g., 4v2 or 4v3) to increase the intensity and pressure on the possession team. This will make the breakout phase more challenging and require quicker passing and decision-making.Focus: Enhances players’ ability to keep possession under pressure and transitions into attack with speed.
progression_two: Vary the Breakout Format:Adjust the attacking phase by either overloading or underloading the attacking team. If overloading, provide more attacking players to emphasize quick build-up play and space creation. If underloading, focus on creating more individual creativity and quick combinations.Focus: Develops adaptability in transition and encourages players to adapt to different attacking situations.

title: Fiorentina 1v1 & Recovery
instructions_setup: This fun warm-up practice allows players to compete head-to-head in an unopposed manner. The attacking players must sprint around the grid to the ball, while the defender sprints around the grid to the mini goals. The attacker must attempt to pass into either of the 2 mini goals with 1 touch, while the defender attempts to protect the 2 mini goals and block any forward pass.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions – The attacking player should focus on quickly reaching the ball and making an immediate decision on which mini goal to target. Quick reactions and decision-making will be key in this fast-paced practice.• Defensive Awareness – The defender must focus on positioning themselves between the attacker and the mini goals, anticipating the pass and blocking it if possible. Quick lateral movement and reading the attacker's intentions are important.• Passing Accuracy – The attacker should aim for a precise, 1-touch pass into the mini goals, ensuring the ball is played with accuracy and power to beat the defender.• Recovery Speed – Both the attacker and defender should be encouraged to recover quickly. The attacker needs to focus on being first to the ball, while the defender should concentrate on quickly getting into position to block the pass.
progression_one: Introduce CompetitionTo make the practice more competitive, introduce scoring. For every successful pass into a mini goal, the attacker scores a point. The defender scores a point by blocking the pass or intercepting the ball.Focus: Increased competitiveness and urgency to execute under pressure.
progression_two: Add Time LimitSet a time limit for each round. The attacker has a set amount of time to score, while the defender works to prevent it. This creates a sense of urgency and pushes players to react faster.Focus: Time management and rapid decision-making.

title: Fiorentina 3 Zone Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill focuses on quick 1-2 combinations from three different angles, encouraging players to improve their passing accuracy, timing, and movement. After each combination, players will pass the ball into the mini goal to complete the phase. The drill is designed to be high-paced, with players constantly rotating positions, ensuring high intensity throughout.The emphasis is on sharp passing, quick decision-making, and fluid movement, creating a dynamic and effective technical warm-up for the team.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: Encourage players to execute the 1-2 passes with speed and accuracy. The player receiving the ball should be prepared to move and make the return pass quickly, creating an efficient flow.• Angle and Timing: Stress the importance of the angles of the passes and the timing of the runs. Players should aim to pass into space, allowing for better control and smooth transitions between combinations.• Movement and Rotation: Ensure players are constantly moving into the next position after completing their combination. This movement is key to keeping the tempo high and ensuring that all players remain engaged in the drill.• Finishing Focus: After completing the combination, players should focus on accuracy when passing into the mini goal. The pass should be weighted properly, ensuring the ball reaches the target with precision.
progression_one: Add Pressure:Introduce passive pressure from defenders who can attempt to intercept the passes or challenge the players in the 1-2 combinations. This adds an element of defensive awareness and encourages players to make quicker decisions under pressure.Focus: Improves decision-making and passing accuracy under pressure.
progression_two: Vary Passing Distances:Adjust the distances between players during the 1-2 combinations, either increasing or decreasing the space between passes. This will challenge players to adjust their passing technique and improve control at different ranges.Focus: Develops passing accuracy and technique over varied distances.

title: Fiorentina 3v1 to 3v2 Attack
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on building attacking combinations and transitioning from a 3v1 overload to a 3v2 situation, promoting quick decision-making and fluid attacking play. Play begins with a 3v1 attack in the first zone, where the attacking team must attempt to cross the ball into the second zone. Once the attacking team successfully enters the second zone, they will face a 3v2 attack, where their objective is to score into one of two mini goals.If the defending team wins possession, they must pass the ball across the grid and attempt to score into either of the two mini goals. Upon scoring, the defending team swaps roles with the attackers, maintaining a dynamic flow and ensuring both teams are equally engaged in attacking and defending.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Overload: Encourage the attacking team to use their numerical advantage in the first zone, focusing on quick, accurate passing and movement to break down the defender.• Transition Speed: Once the ball is crossed into the second zone, the attacking team must quickly transition into a 3v2 attack. Encourage fast ball movement and intelligent positioning to exploit the overload.• Defensive Pressure: When defending, encourage players to work together to apply pressure on the attacking team. Defenders should communicate and cover passing lanes to force errors or win possession.• Quick Transition to Attack: If the defending team wins the ball, they should immediately look to switch the play and attack with speed. The focus should be on passing quickly across the grid and taking advantage of the space available.
progression_one: Add Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for the attacking team to score in the second zone (e.g., 15 seconds). This will add urgency and encourage quicker decision-making and attacking combinations.Focus: Increases the tempo and decision-making speed under time pressure.
progression_two: Increase Defensive Pressure:Introduce a third defender in the second zone, creating a 3v3 situation for the attackers. This progression encourages the attacking team to work even harder to create space and find shooting opportunities.Focus: Challenges attacking players to make quicker decisions and improve their ability to break down a more compact defensive setup.

title: Fiorentina 4-2-4 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 4-2-4 formation down into 2 specific zones where the possession team will play 6v3. The possession team can switch the ball back and forth freely, and one of the pressing players must transfer across zones once the possession team switches the ball, creating a pressing 3 at all times. The practice transitions into a 5v2 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Ball Switching – Encourage the possession team to move the ball quickly from one zone to the other, focusing on accurate and fast switches. The aim is to force the pressing team to work harder to cover the space and transition between zones.• Pressing & Transition – The pressing team must be disciplined in transitioning across the zones. As soon as the ball is switched, one defender should quickly move to the new zone to maintain pressure. This requires good communication and movement off the ball.• Positioning in Zones – The possession team should look to create space within their zones by stretching the defense and maintaining a high tempo in their passing. Players should be constantly scanning for gaps and be ready to receive the ball.• Defender Awareness – The pressing team should always be aware of the ball's position and anticipate where the ball will be switched next. They must stay compact and work as a unit to maintain pressure, preventing the attacking team from progressing easily.
progression_one: Limit TouchesIntroduce a restriction on the number of touches (e.g., 1 or 2 touches per player). This will force players to move the ball faster and make quicker decisions, increasing the intensity of the rondo.Focus: Enhancing quick passing and faster decision-making in tight spaces.
progression_two: Add an Extra AttackerAdd an extra player to the possession team (making it 7v3), which forces the pressing team to adapt and work harder to maintain pressure. The possession team will now have to be more patient and precise with their ball movement to break down the defenders.Focus: Developing patience in possession and maintaining structure when outnumbered.

title: Fiorentina Rondo & Wide Finishing
instructions_setup: This semi-opposed practice starts with a central 4v2 rondo. The idea of the practice is for the wider midfielders to make penetrative forward passes into wider players who make runs from out to in. After 5 passes, the 2 wider players in the rondo are allowed to play an unopposed pass into the wider player.As a progression, allow for the opposite wide player or the deepest player in the rondo to join the attack to allow for a simpler finish, encouraging them to make quick forward runs into the box.
coaching_notes: • Penetrative Passing – The wide midfielders should focus on making penetrative, forward passes into the wider players. The quality of these passes should be such that the receiving player is already on the move and can play forward immediately.• Movement from Wide Players – The wide players must make out-to-in runs to receive the ball.
