Timing is crucial here, as they need to be in the right position to receive and attack quickly once the pass is made.• Quick Transitions – After the pass is played into the wide player, they should transition quickly into a position to finish. This requires excellent awareness and the ability to quickly assess the best spot to finish the attack.• Support Runs – The central players must also make sure to offer support by being ready for any second-phase play. Encouraging players to constantly look for the next movement helps maintain the flow of the practice.
progression_one: Add Joining PlayerAllow the opposite wide player or the deepest player in the rondo to join the attack, adding an additional option for the final pass and encouraging quick forward runs into the box.Focus: Improving decision-making in attack and encouraging quick, well-timed runs into the box.
progression_two: Full Opposed PlayMake the rondo fully opposed, with defenders actively pressing the ball. The wide players must now make more decisive movements and quick passes, adding pressure to the finish as the practice becomes more competitive.Focus: Enhancing attacking play under pressure, improving timing, and precision in both the pass and finish.

title: Fiorentina SAQ into 1v1
instructions_setup: This high-intensity drill focuses on improving speed, agility, and quick decision-making under pressure. The drill begins with two players racing from one pole to the next, focusing on their speed and agility (SAQ) as they work to beat each other to the final pole. Once both players reach the final pole, the coach plays a pass down the middle, and the players must race to get onto the ball first before attempting to finish.The drill simulates a real game situation where speed and quick reactions are crucial. Players must be prepared to transition quickly from their race to the ball into a controlled finish under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Speed and Agility: Emphasize the importance of fast, explosive movements during the race between the poles. Players should focus on short, quick strides to maintain speed and avoid decelerating.• Quick Reaction to Pass: As soon as the coach plays the pass, players must react quickly and anticipate the ball’s trajectory. Encourage them to focus on getting to the ball first, making sure they don’t hesitate.• Finishing Under Pressure: Once the ball is controlled, players should focus on taking a quick and composed shot on goal. Emphasize the importance of accuracy over power, especially when under pressure from their opponent.• Competitive Mentality: Create a competitive environment between the two players to increase the intensity. Encourage them to push each other to work harder and improve their speed, reaction time, and finishing.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender who can challenge the player who reaches the ball first. This adds an element of defensive pressure to the finishing, simulating a more realistic attacking scenario.Focus: Enhances players' ability to finish under pressure and make quick decisions while being challenged by an opponent.

title: Fiorentina Switch of Play Rondo
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to enhance players' ability to maintain possession under pressure while incorporating quick transitions and switching of play. The practice begins with a 3v3 setup on one side of the grid, where the attacking team can use two neutrals positioned on the end line and central line to create a numerical advantage. The objective for the possession team is to complete a minimum of three passes on one side of the grid before switching the ball to the opposite side.Each successful switch of play earns the attacking team a point, encouraging quick ball movement and strategic positioning. The defending team must work hard to regain possession and transition into the attacking phase, challenging their defensive organization and pressing intensity.
coaching_notes: • Possession Play: Players must focus on maintaining possession under pressure, using short, quick passes to retain control of the ball. Encourage players to move into space, creating passing lanes and options for the ball carrier.• Switching Play: When the team successfully makes 3 passes, emphasize the importance of quick and accurate switches to the opposite side. Players should aim to move the ball quickly while maintaining their shape and width on the field.• Defensive Pressure: The defending team should focus on pressing intelligently, closing down passing lanes, and forcing mistakes. Encourage defenders to work together to regain possession and immediately transition into attack.• Movement off the Ball: Players should always look for space and angles to receive passes. Encourage off-the-ball movement to support the ball carrier and create more passing options.
progression_one: Limit Touches:Limit the number of touches per player (e.g., two-touch play) to increase the speed of play and force players to make quicker decisions.Focus: Improves decision-making and encourages quicker ball movement under pressure.

title: Fiorentina Wide Movements & Finish
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing practice, the focus is on attacking combinations in wide areas, followed by a well-timed attack into the box. Play starts with the attacking team combining in wide areas to break down the defensive structure. After completing the combination, three players— the center forward, the opposite winger, and a midfield runner— make timed runs into the box for a finishing opportunity. The drill is designed to simulate a fast and fluid attacking phase, allowing players to practice their runs and finishing technique.Once the combination is completed in the wide area, the focus shifts to players attacking the box for a shot on goal. This practice emphasizes timing, teamwork, and movement off the ball, providing a high-intensity, unopposed opportunity to develop finishing in game-like situations.
coaching_notes: • Combination Play: Players should focus on quick, precise passes and movement in wide areas to break down the defense. Encourage fluidity in their combinations and awareness of supporting players.• Attacking Runs: The center forward, winger, and midfield runner must time their runs into the box effectively, making sure to attack different areas to create space and opportunities for a finish.• Finishing Technique: Players attacking the box must be prepared to finish with composure and precision, focusing on keeping their shots on target and placing the ball in the corners.• Timing of the Cross: The player delivering the cross should focus on accuracy, aiming to deliver a ball that allows attackers to time their runs and finish effectively.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce one or two defenders to apply light pressure, encouraging attackers to make their runs quicker and more decisive while dealing with defensive pressure.Focus: Increases the intensity of the drill and replicates game-like conditions for attackers.
progression_two: Vary the Cross:Change the type of cross being delivered, such as a low cross, high ball, or driven cross, to challenge attackers in different ways and improve their finishing from various types of deliveries.Focus: Improves adaptability in finishing from different types of crosses.

title: Fortaleza 2 Way Finishing
instructions_setup: This two-way finishing drill is designed to develop short combination play and finishing under pressure on a small-sided pitch. Two teams of four players operate simultaneously on opposite sides. One team works on the left side, combining through quick passes and movement before finishing in the top goal, while the other team works on the right side, combining before finishing in the bottom goal.Each team must complete at least two to three passes between the four players before attempting a finish. After each shot, the ball is played back into the combination to maintain continuous flow and engagement. The drill encourages creativity, awareness of space, and timing in tight attacking areas.
coaching_notes: • Combination Play: Emphasise sharp, one- or two-touch passing and coordinated movement to break defensive lines and create clear shooting opportunities.• Finishing Technique: Reinforce varied finishing techniques, encouraging composure and accuracy under pressure.• Timing and Support: Coach players to move into space at the right moment to receive the ball, ensuring support angles and passing options remain open.• Awareness: Encourage players to scan the pitch, anticipate teammates’ movements, and adjust positioning dynamically.
progression_one: One-Touch Finishing: Require the final combination pass or shot to be taken first time to increase tempo and technical challenge.Focus: Improves speed of execution, decision-making, and finishing under realistic match conditions.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender: Introduce a passive defender to apply light pressure during the combination or finishing phase.Focus: Develops movement under pressure, spatial awareness, and composure when faced with defensive opposition.

title: Fortaleza 3 Way 1v1s
instructions_setup: This 1v1 triangular finishing drill is designed to develop attacking decision-making, finishing under pressure, and defensive transitions. Three mini goals are set up in a triangle, with a player stationed behind each goal.Team A starts as the attacker with Team B acting as the defender. The attacker can choose to score in either of the two goals that are not their own. Once the attacker shoots or loses the ball, the roles rotate: the team whose goal was attacked becomes the next attacker, the original attacker becomes the defender.The continuous rotation ensures high engagement, encourages quick thinking, and develops the ability to attack and defend effectively in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Decision-Making: Encourage attackers to quickly assess which goal offers the highest probability of scoring and react to the defender’s position.• Finishing Technique: Emphasise composure, accurate placement, and varied finishing angles in 1v1 situations.• Defensive Awareness: Coach defenders to anticipate attacking moves, close angles, and delay attackers without over-committing.• Transition Speed: Maintain quick rotations to simulate game-like pressure and develop rapid role switching between attacking and defending.
progression_one: Add a Starting Delay: Defender starts 1–2 steps behind the attacker, then accelerates once the attacker moves.Focus: Enhances timing, acceleration, and realistic 1v1 defensive engagement while still challenging the attacker.

title: Fortaleza Build & Counter Overloaded
instructions_setup: This “Playing Out From the Back” practice is designed to develop build-up play under pressure, passing accuracy, and defensive transitions in counter-attacking scenarios.The goalkeeper and five build-up players start from the back and attempt to progress the ball against three pressing players. Around 1/3 up the pitch, three additional players are positioned in a line: left, right, and centre. The build-up team’s objective is to successfully pass to any of these three players, maintaining possession under pressure.Once the ball is played into one of these three players, they immediately counter-attack, joining the three pressing players. The original build-up team, including the goalkeeper, transitions to defend against the counter-attack, now facing six opponents. The drill continues with a rotation of roles to ensure all players experience building from the back and defending counter-attacks.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy: Encourage precise, well-weighted passes to the receiving players under pressure.• Decision-Making: Coach build-up players to read the press, identify passing lanes, and choose the safest or most advantageous option.• Support Angles: Emphasise movement off the ball to create passing options and support the player in possession.• Defensive Transition: Ensure players quickly switch mindset when possession is lost, organising to defend against numerical disadvantages during counter-attacks.• Goalkeeper Involvement: Reinforce the goalkeeper’s role in distribution, communication, and defending in counter-attacking situations.
progression_one: Two-Touch Build-Up: Limit the build-up players to two touches before passing to one of the three line players.Focus: Develops quicker ball control, sharper decision-making, and faster reactions under pressure.

title: Fortaleza Double Movements Technical
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice is designed to develop ball control, passing accuracy, communication, and attacking movement. Five players work with a single ball in a squad-based rotation around a grid or marked area. Each corner of the area features a “gate” where a player can receive the ball.Before receiving, the player at each gate performs one of two specific attacking movements: a “show to go” or a “go to show,” which are signalled to teammates through movement or call. The passing sequence continues around the squad, emphasising timing, awareness, and clean execution.This practice encourages players to combine technical skills with tactical understanding, reinforcing movement off the ball and the connection between body positioning, visual cues, and passing options.
coaching_notes: • Passing Technique: Focus on accurate, well-weighted passes to the receiving player, using both feet when appropriate.• Attacking Movement: Ensure players perform the “show to go” and “go to show” movements sharply and clearly before receiving the ball.• Communication: Encourage verbal and non-verbal cues to signal intentions, ensuring smooth transitions and awareness among teammates.• Receiving and Control: Emphasise first touch orientation, body positioning, and readiness to continue the sequence with speed and precision.
progression_one: Progression OneAdd a Passive Defender: Introduce a passive defender who lightly pressures the receiver after the movements are completed.Focus: Develops composure under pressure, quick thinking, and adaptability when receiving in realistic scenarios.

title: Fortaleza Technical Into 1v1
instructions_setup: This technical dribbling and finishing practice is designed to develop ball control, dribbling under pressure, finishing accuracy, and transition into 1v1 attacking situations. Two players start each with a ball at opposite ends of a grid. Each player dribbles into the grid, navigating around a designated pole, before shooting at a mini goal—one on the left side and one on the right.The player whose ball hits the net first immediately receives a second ball from the coach. Both players then engage in a 1v1, attempting to score against their respective goalkeepers. The drill continues with rotations, allowing all players to practice dribbling, finishing, and 1v1 attacking and defending.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Technique: Emphasise close control, quick changes of direction, and body positioning when navigating around the pole.• Finishing: Encourage composure, accurate placement, and varied shooting techniques to challenge the goalkeeper.• Reaction and Decision-Making: Coach players to react quickly after the first shot, transitioning immediately into the 1v1 scenario.• 1v1 Awareness: Emphasise timing of runs, feints, and changes of pace to create space against the opponent.• Goalkeeper Involvement: Reinforce positioning, shot-stopping, and anticipation during both the initial shot and subsequent 1v1.
progression_one: Weaker Foot Dribble and Finish: Require players to dribble and shoot using their weaker foot.Focus: Develops ambidexterity, technical confidence, and balance under pressure.

title: France 1v1 with Transitions
instructions_setup: In this drill, play starts with a player attacking an unopposed mini goal. After successfully passing the ball into the mini goal, the player immediately transitions to the opposite side of the grid, where they must defend a 1v1 situation against an attacker. The defender’s objective is to prevent the attacker from scoring, while the attacker works to break down the defense and finish into the mini goal. This continuous flow of attacking and defending transitions is designed to improve both offensive and defensive decision-making under pressure.The drill focuses on rapid transitions, encouraging players to shift quickly between attacking and defending roles. This helps to develop the ability to recover and adapt to changing situations, enhancing the player’s overall defensive awareness and offensive timing.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Focus: Players should focus on being decisive and accurate when attacking the mini goal. The goal is to quickly take advantage of the space and score without hesitation.• Defensive Transition: Once the player has passed the ball into the mini goal, they must immediately transition into a defensive mindset. Encourage quick reactions and alertness to defend the 1v1 situation.• 1v1 Defending: The defender should focus on positioning, staying goal-side, and using their body to block the attacker’s path. Quick footwork and decision-making are key to closing down the attacker effectively.• Constant Movement: Players should maintain high intensity throughout the drill, ensuring a constant flow of transitions. Encourage both attacking and defending players to stay active and alert to the changing situations.
progression_one: Increase Pressure on Attacker:Allow the defender to press the attacker earlier, reducing the space and time they have to make decisions. This will force the attacker to act quicker and test their ability to finish under pressure.Focus: Improves attackers' ability to finish under pressure while developing the defender’s ability to deal with a faster-paced game.

title: France Evading Pressure
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a pass into a central player, who is immediately pressured by two opposition players. The player receiving the ball must use their body positioning, scanning skills, and effective receiving techniques to evade the pressure. Once they’ve successfully evaded the defenders, the player’s objective is to finish by scoring into any of the four mini goals positioned around the grid. This drill focuses on developing a player’s ability to make quick decisions, use feints and body movements to escape pressure, and maintain composure to finish effectively.The drill simulates game-like situations where players must maintain control under pressure, making it an excellent way to improve individual attacking skills in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Under Pressure: Encourage the central player to focus on their first touch and positioning. They should scan the field before receiving to identify potential passing lanes or gaps to exploit.• Evading Defenders: The player must use their body effectively to shield the ball and make quick changes of direction. Feints and quick turns should be emphasized to create space from defenders.• Decision-Making: After evading pressure, the player must make a quick decision on which mini goal to attack. Encourage the use of the space and the ability to choose the right goal depending on the defender’s positioning.• Finishing Composure: Once space is created, players should focus on finishing with composure, aiming for accuracy over power. Emphasize quick, clean shots into the mini goals.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce an additional defender, making it a 3v1 scenario. This increases the difficulty and encourages the player to focus on quick thinking and better evasion techniques.Focus: Enhances the player’s ability to deal with multiple defenders and make quicker decisions under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Touches:Limit the player to a maximum of two touches to receive and finish the ball. This forces them to make faster decisions and reduces the time they have to evade pressure.Focus: Improves quick decision-making and sharpens ball control under pressure.

title: France Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: In this dynamic drill, each of the four grids starts with five players and a ball. On the coach’s whistle, one player from each grid must sprint either clockwise or anti-clockwise to create a 4v1 overload scenario in their respective grid. The defender’s goal is to win possession, after which they must sprint back to their original grid. The drill is designed to emphasize quick transitions, pressure on the ball, and the ability to win possession and counter quickly. The grid size and distance between the grids can be adjusted to suit the players’ age, ability, and specific training objectives.This drill encourages players to work on their defensive and offensive transitions, promoting agility, communication, and teamwork.
coaching_notes: • Sprint and Transition: Emphasize the importance of quick decision-making when sprinting into the grid. Players must anticipate where the ball will be played and move quickly to close down the attacker.• Defensive Pressure: The lone defender must focus on staying goal-side and applying constant pressure. Encourage defenders to use their body to direct the ball away from dangerous areas and work as a unit to win possession.• Teamwork and Communication: Encourage communication between attackers and defenders to ensure the attacking players work together to maintain possession and the defender applies effective pressure.• Winning Possession: Once the defender wins possession, they should transition quickly and efficiently back to their grid to reset the drill. Encourage them to sprint hard and focus on maintaining possession.

title: France Man for Man SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game focuses on individual 1v1 matchups within a team framework. Whether it’s 4v4 or 8v8, players are locked into man-to-man marking and are only allowed to tackle their direct opponent. The emphasis is on individual defending skills, such as positioning, timing of tackles, and defensive awareness. While players are restricted to defending their assigned opponent, they are still allowed to block shots from other players on the field. However, they cannot tackle or regain possession from players they are not directly matched up against.This game encourages players to develop their personal defending skills while also maintaining team structure and awareness in a dynamic, competitive environment.
coaching_notes: • Man-to-Man Responsibility: Ensure players understand their role in marking their assigned opponent. They must focus on staying goal-side and using body positioning to block their opponent’s movements without being distracted by other players.• Tackling Technique: Encourage players to use proper tackling techniques when engaging with their assigned opponent, timing their tackles well and ensuring they do not dive in recklessly.• Blocking Shots: Defenders must be aware of when to step off their assigned player to block shots or prevent attempts on goal from other players, without overcommitting or leaving their mark open.• Awareness and Communication: Encourage communication between teammates to ensure they are aware of each other’s positions and movements. This will help in preventing overloads or gaps in the defensive shape.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Players:Increase the number of players on each team (e.g., 5v5 or 9v9), maintaining the man-to-man marking rule. This will test defenders’ ability to manage more attacking threats while sticking to their 1v1 matchups.Focus: Enhances the ability to defend multiple threats while still focusing on individual marking and tackling.

title: France One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This drill is designed for strikers to develop their finishing ability while also improving fitness. The player will run continuously from one end of the pitch to the other, finishing unopposed into two separate goals. This repetitive movement focuses on maintaining sharpness and accuracy under fatigue.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Controlled First Touch to Set Up Each Finish – Use a precise first touch to prepare for an effective and balanced shot on goal.• Vary Finishing Techniques Between Both Feet and Different Angles – Practice using both feet and adjust body positioning to score from various approaches.• Maintain High Intensity and Sprint Recovery Throughout the Drill – Push physical limits while ensuring quality is not sacrificed during finishes.• Concentrate on Quick Transitions Between Finishes and Sprints – Efficiently recover and prepare mentally for the next scoring opportunity.
progression_one: Increase Pace of Repetitions and Reduce Rest IntervalsShorten recovery time to simulate match fatigue and develop endurance alongside finishing quality.Focus:Improves physical stamina, finishing precision, and mental resilience under sustained pressure.
progression_two: Add a Passive Goalkeeper or DefenderIntroduce a passive goalkeeper or defender to increase challenge and sharpen decision-making during finishes.Focus:Enhances composure, shot selection, and accuracy when facing defensive pressure.

title: France Pass & Press
instructions_setup: This passing warm-up drill focuses on improving combination play under pressure. Players are encouraged to move the ball quickly and efficiently while dealing with semi-opposed pressure from a pressing defender. The practice is set up in a central grid, with players constantly moving to follow their passes. As each player receives the ball, they are immediately faced with pressure from a defender, requiring them to make quick decisions, use good passing technique, and maintain possession under pressure. The drill helps players develop their ability to pass and receive in tight spaces while under pressure, improving their composure and decision-making.The warm-up also encourages players to support each other, ensuring that options are available for the passer to make effective combinations and progress the ball through the grid.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: Emphasize the importance of quick, accurate passes. Players should focus on passing the ball one-touch or two-touch to keep the tempo high and avoid being closed down by the defender.• Body Positioning: Encourage players to receive the ball with their body open to the field. This allows them to quickly assess their options and make better decisions under pressure.• Movement After Passing: Players must immediately follow their pass, providing additional support and options for the player in possession. Constant movement helps create space and maintain attacking momentum.• Pressure Awareness: Players receiving the ball should constantly be aware of the defender's position. Encourage them to use body fakes, quick turns, and feints to evade the defender and maintain possession.
progression_one: Increase the Pressure:Introduce a second defender to apply more intense pressure on the player receiving the ball. This will encourage players to be even quicker in their decision-making and passing.Focus: Improves players’ ability to deal with more intense defensive pressure and work under greater stress.

title: France Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical passing pattern takes place within the central third of the pitch. The focus is on developing players' ability to execute line-breaking passes and switch play effectively under minimal pressure. Players work continuously through the pattern, concentrating on body shape, timing of movement, and quality of pass to facilitate quick, efficient changes of direction across the field.
coaching_notes: • Receiving at an Angle – Players should open up their body to receive passes on the back foot, allowing them to play forward or across the pitch seamlessly.• Speed of Play – Encourage players to move the ball quickly, with minimal touches, to replicate the tempo needed in game situations.• Passing Quality – Emphasize the importance of firm, accurate passes to maintain the rhythm of the switch and avoid breaking momentum.• Awareness Before Receiving – Players should scan the pitch before receiving to prepare their next action and ensure smooth transitions between passes.
progression_one: One-Touch PassingPlayers must complete the pattern using only one touch where possible, forcing quicker decision-making and sharper technical execution.Focus: Increasing the tempo of play and encouraging players to think ahead.
progression_two: Directional PlayIntroduce a directional element, where players must switch play twice before completing a set sequence, simulating breaking out of compact areas.Focus: Developing structured movement patterns and improving the timing of switches

title: France Possession Into Counter
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on building possession and creating opportunities to counterattack. The 7 possession-based players are tasked with completing a set number of passes (e.g., 5-10 passes) to earn a point. The defenders are positioned to pressure the possession-based team, and if they win possession, they must transition quickly to counterattack. The counterattack is in a 2v1 scenario. The attacking players are encouraged to exploit this 2v1 situation, while the defenders who lost possession must quickly recover and attempt to regain the ball.This drill helps improve ball retention, quick transitions, and creating goal-scoring opportunities during a counterattack.
coaching_notes: • Ball Retention: Emphasize the importance of quick, sharp passing to maintain possession. The players in possession should look to move the ball quickly, using width and depth to create space and make it difficult for defenders to win possession.• Counterattacking Focus: Once possession is won, defenders must immediately look to transition to attack. The countering team should exploit the 2v1 situation, focusing on quick, direct passes to break into the attacking area.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders must be patient and look to anticipate passes. When they win the ball, they should quickly look for opportunities to launch a counterattack before the attacking team can recover their shape.• Transition Speed: Both teams should focus on the speed of transition—whether it's maintaining possession or countering. Encourage the attacking defenders to exploit the space quickly and efficiently.
progression_one: Increase Pressure on Possession Team:Add more defenders to pressure the possession team, making it more difficult to complete passes and increasing the intensity of the drill.Focus: Forces the possession team to play quicker and more intelligently, while improving defensive transition.
progression_two: Limit Passes:Reduce the number of passes required to earn a point. For example, instead of 5 passes, require 3-4 passes to encourage faster decision-making and quicker ball circulation.Focus: Increases the speed of play and forces the possession team to be more decisive with their passing.

title: France Possession Transfer
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on possession and penetrating through a central line to switch play. It is set up with three teams of four players: two teams in possession positioned in separate zones, and one defensive team located centrally. The attacking teams work together to move the ball and attempt to penetrate the central line, creating an opportunity to switch play to the opposite zone. The defensive team is tasked with screening the central line with two players while the other two players actively press the teams in possession. The aim is to maintain possession and look for opportunities to break the central line and create switches.The drill encourages quick passing, good positioning, and intelligent movement, while also simulating game situations where teams need to break through defensive blocks and shift the ball efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Passing and Movement: Encourage quick, precise passes and off-the-ball movement to break the defensive shape. Players should look for the best passing lanes and be ready to receive passes in space.• Central Penetration Awareness: Emphasize the importance of recognizing when to penetrate the central line. The ball carrier should be aware of the defensive pressure and decide when to play the ball through the central area to switch the play.• Defensive Pressing: Defenders should work together to apply pressure on the ball, closing down the passing lanes, and anticipating passes. The two players screening the central line need to prevent easy penetration and force the attacking team to play wide.• Switching Play: Once the central line is broken, the attacking team should quickly switch play to the other zone, looking to exploit the space on the opposite side.
progression_one: Increase Defensive Pressure:Allow the defensive team to apply more aggressive pressure as soon as the ball enters their half. This forces the attacking teams to move the ball faster and make quicker decisions under pressure.Focus: Enhances decision-making and passing under pressure, improving the speed of play.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for the attacking teams to break the central line and switch play. If they don't achieve this within the allotted time, they must reset and try again.Focus: Adds urgency to the drill and encourages faster ball movement and more decisive attacking play.

title: Frankfurt 3-2-5 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 3-2-5 formation down into 3 specific zones where the possession team will play either 5v2 or 4v2. Players can play through the zones freely, and 4 of the players (the central players) are tasked with playing in 2 different zones. The practice transitions into a 6v4 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Zone Awareness – Players must be aware of their positioning in relation to the zones and focus on playing the ball quickly through the areas. Encourage players to be aware of which zone they are operating in and use the space effectively.• Central Player Movement – The central players must be constantly moving between the two zones to create passing options. They should focus on offering support and being available for quick passes, while also maintaining strong communication to organize play.• Quick Passing & Combinations – Emphasize quick, sharp passing and combinations to break through the defensive shape. Encourage the possession team to move the ball with purpose and avoid being static in their positioning.• Defensive Pressure – The pressing team should focus on staying compact, applying pressure to the ball carrier, and working together to close down passing lanes. Communication and coordinated pressing will be crucial in preventing the possession team from progressing through the zones.
progression_one: Add Restriction on PassingLimit the number of touches each player can take in the rondo (e.g., 1 or 2 touches per player). This forces players to focus on quick decision-making and movement off the ball.Focus: Improving the speed of play and decision-making in tight spaces.
progression_two: Add More DefendersIncrease the number of defenders (e.g., add an additional defender in each zone), making it harder for the possession team to break through the defensive shape. The possession team must work harder to create passing lanes and maintain possession.Focus: Developing the ability to break down a more compact and organized defense.

title: Frankfurt Countering Underloaded
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on counter-attacking during transitional moments with an emphasis on exploiting overloads and recovering under pressure. The drill begins with a forward pass to a player positioned at the edge of the attacking area. Upon receiving the pass, the player has a brief opportunity to attack with a 2v1 overload, as two defenders are positioned outside the area and can recover to challenge. The attacking players must capitalize on the temporary overload, using quick passes, movement, and decision-making to break the defense. If the overload is not utilized effectively, the attackers are likely to face a 2v3 situation and must finish under greater defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Exploiting the Overload – Encourage the attacking players to act quickly, making sharp runs and quick passes to take full advantage of the 2v1 overload. The player with the ball should look for the best option: dribbling, passing, or shooting based on the defense's positioning.• Attacker’s First Touch – The player receiving the pass should take a controlled first touch that sets up their next move. It should be quick and direct to push the attack forward while maintaining the element of surprise.• Decision-Making in Overload – The key in this drill is to exploit the numerical advantage. If the 2v1 is not used effectively, the attackers should be prepared to make quick decisions as the defense recovers. Emphasize recognizing when to shoot, pass, or dribble based on the defensive setup.• Recovering Defenders – The defenders, upon seeing the pass to the edge of the area, must quickly recover into position. This adds pressure to the attackers and encourages defensive discipline in transition.• Finishing Under Pressure – If the overload is wasted and the defenders recover, the attackers must finish the attack in a 2v3 situation. Encourage composure and quick decision-making in these more challenging circumstances.
progression_one: Limit Time for OverloadSet a time limit (e.g., 5–7 seconds) for the attackers to use the 2v1 overload before defenders recover. This adds urgency and pushes attackers to make quicker decisions under pressure.Focus:Encourages quicker attacks and sharp decision-making when faced with temporary overloads, while also working on finishing under pressure when the overload opportunity is lost.
progression_two: Add More Defenders to the AttackAfter the first overload phase, allow the defending team to add an extra defender (e.g., 2v2 into 3v3). This increases the defensive challenge and forces attackers to be even more creative in breaking down the defense.Focus:Helps attackers refine their decision-making and movement when the situation becomes more crowded, simulating real-world counter-attacks where defenders recover quickly.

title: Frankfurt Finishing the Attack (4 Phase)
instructions_setup: This practice allows players to attack in multiple different scenarios: 1v0, 1v1, and 2v1. The drill runs through four phases, starting with a 1v0 where the attacker works alone to finish. The attacker then transitions to defend in a 1v1 against an incoming attacker. Following that, the scenario progresses to a 2v1, where the attacker has an advantage and finally transitions into a second 2v1 with a different attacking setup. This high-intensity drill enables players to experience a variety of attacking combinations from multiple areas of the pitch.
coaching_notes: • Finishing in 1v0 – The initial phase allows the player to work on finishing without pressure. Encourage attackers to focus on composure, taking a touch if necessary, and finishing either low and hard or with precision depending on their distance from goal.• Defending in 1v1 – When the player transitions to defending, they should focus on positioning and timing their challenge. They should be patient, preventing the attacker from turning and forcing them into wide or less dangerous areas.• Exploiting the 2v1 Overload – In the 2v1 phase, the attacker should look to combine quickly with their teammate, using their numerical advantage to break down the defender. Quick passing and movement off the ball will be key to making the most of the overload.• Adaptability in Different Scenarios – Players need to adjust to each phase quickly, from being the attacker in the 1v0 phase to defending in the 1v1 and then transitioning into a 2v1 attack. The ability to switch mindsets and roles under pressure is key for this practice.
progression_one: Add a Defender to 1v0In the first phase, after a set number of repetitions, introduce a defender who starts at a distance, making it a 1v1 instead of 1v0. This forces the attacker to be more decisive with their shot and adds realism to the finishing phase.Focus: Encourages players to deal with pressure while finishing and improves their ability to make quick decisions.
progression_two: Time the PhasesIntroduce a time limit for each phase, requiring players to complete each stage within a set time frame. This increases the intensity of the drill and forces players to think and act quickly.Focus: Simulates high-pressure game situations where decisions and execution must be fast and efficient.

title: Frankfurt Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This warm-up drill focuses on sharp passing combinations and the execution of overlapping runs, with the ball moving from end to end. The two central players are fixed in their positions and serve as the key players in each phase of the drill. The practice requires players to play quick, accurate passes while utilizing overlapping runs to break down defensive lines and create space. The ball must always go through the central players, ensuring they remain integral to the flow of the practice. The combination of sharp passing and movement off the ball ensures a dynamic and effective warm-up, preparing players for match scenarios that require both technical passing and intelligent movement.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Passing: Players must focus on playing quick, precise passes to maintain fluidity in the drill. The pace of the pass is essential to ensure the ball moves through the central players without delay, allowing for smoother transitions.• Overlapping Runs: Emphasize the importance of timing and the angle of overlapping runs. Players should look to make well-timed runs outside or inside of the ball carrier, aiming to stretch the defense and provide additional options.• Central Players' Role: The central players need to be aware of their positioning, always offering a passing option while maintaining their fixed positions. They should be comfortable receiving passes under pressure and distributing the ball efficiently.• Movement Off the Ball: Players should focus on their movement off the ball, always looking for ways to create passing lanes. They must be aware of the space they are running into and adjust their runs based on the ball’s position and the defender’s movements.

title: Frankfurt Rondo to Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: This semi-opposed drill begins with a 3v1 rondo in a wide area, encouraging ball retention and quick combination play. The aim is to complete five consecutive passes before playing forward into a waiting winger. Once received, the winger delivers an unopposed cross into the box for a centre forward to finish. If the defending player in the rondo wins possession, they can break quickly and attempt to score into one of two mini goals placed centrally to simulate vertical transitions.
coaching_notes: • Ball Circulation – The team in possession should focus on quick, purposeful passes to shift the defender and open up the forward passing lane.• Timing of Pass – The final pass into the winger should be well-timed, allowing them to take a positive first touch into space and prepare the cross.• Finishing Movement – The centre forward must time their movement into the box to meet the cross with purpose, adjusting to the type and pace of delivery.• Defensive Pressing – The lone defender should press with high intensity, anticipating passes and looking for cues to intercept and transition quickly.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender on the CrossIntroduce a passive defender to apply light pressure on the winger during the cross.Focus: Encourages more realistic delivery technique under mild pressure and improves crossing consistency.
progression_two: Add a Second Attacker in the BoxInclude a second forward arriving in the box to provide more crossing options.Focus: Develops decision-making for both the crosser and attackers regarding timing, positioning, and type of delivery.

title: Frankfurt Rondo to Switch of Play
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 3v3(+1) rondo on one side of a 10x10 yard grid. The possession-based team aims to make a set number of passes before attempting to switch play to the opposite side. Once the ball is switched, the attacking team must quickly transition into an attacking phase, looking to exploit the space created. As the ball moves across, the opposition player positioned at the other pole is allowed to make a recovery run, attempting to pressure the attacking team as they advance. This encourages quick passing, intelligent movement, and rapid transitions between possession and attack, helping players improve their decision-making and tactical awareness in high-pressure situations.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: The team in possession should focus on making quick, accurate passes to maintain fluidity. Players must use the extra neutral player effectively to create numerical superiority and move the ball efficiently across the grid.• Switching Play: Once the required number of passes is achieved, the team should look to switch play quickly to the other side, using the open space to advance the ball. Timing and accuracy of the switch are key.• Recovery Runs: The opposition player positioned at the other pole must sprint to apply pressure to the attacking team. This teaches attackers to handle pressure and make quicker decisions when the defending team recovers.• Movement Off the Ball: Off-the-ball movement is critical in this drill. Players should constantly be scanning for passing lanes and making runs to receive the ball in space. Communication is vital to ensure players are always offering options.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce additional defenders on the opposite pole to increase pressure on the attacking team during the switch, forcing quicker play and more dynamic decision-making.Focus: Enhances attacking players’ ability to perform under pressure and make faster transitions from defense to attack.
progression_two: Limit Touches:Limit the number of touches each player can have (e.g., 2-3 touches). This forces players to focus on quick passing and decision-making, encouraging fast and effective play.Focus: Improves the tempo of the game, encouraging quicker transitions and reducing unnecessary ball retention.

title: Germany 1v0 to 4v4
instructions_setup: This attacking drill progresses through multiple phases, gradually increasing in complexity and intensity. The drill starts with a simple 1v0 situation and builds up to a fully balanced 4v4 scenario. The goal of this practice is to help players work on attacking combinations, decision-making, and exploiting numerical advantages. The progression from 1v0 to 4v4 helps players develop their skills in different attacking situations, from finishing in isolation to working with teammates in more congested areas. The drill emphasizes quick transitions, intelligent movement off the ball, and effective use of overloads to break down defenders.
coaching_notes: • Phase 1 (1v0): Focus on individual finishing techniques. Players should work on timing their runs, accuracy, and composure when attacking the goal without opposition.• Phase 2 (2v1): Introduce the concept of overloads, encouraging the attacking players to use quick passes and creative runs to exploit the defender. Emphasize timing of the pass and the movement of the second attacker to create space.• Phase 3 (2v2): Now that both teams have equal numbers, players must focus on combination play and positional awareness. Encourage attackers to use wide play, overloads, and quick transitions to beat the defenders.• Phase 4 (3v2): Attackers have a numerical advantage. Focus on how to exploit the overload, encouraging attackers to move the ball quickly and make intelligent runs to break down the defense.• Phase 5 (3v3): Balanced play. Focus on maintaining width and depth in attack, as well as communicating with teammates to ensure the attack remains fluid. The attackers must make smart choices to create space and opportunities.• Phase 6 (4v3): The attacking team now has a larger numerical advantage. Encourage overlapping runs, crosses, and quick changes of direction to exploit the extra attacker effectively.• Phase 7 (4v4): Full, balanced attack. Focus on improving decision-making in high-pressure situations, with all players contributing to both the build-up and the final attack.

title: Germany 3rd Man Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill focuses on developing third-man passing combinations, a key tactic for breaking down opposition defenses. The drill involves two balls being used simultaneously: the first ball moves through a vertical third-man combination, and the second ball works through a horizontal third-man combination. Players must be quick to adjust between vertical and horizontal passes, ensuring fluid movement and sharp decision-making. The drill helps players develop awareness of space, timing, and positioning, as they learn to create passing lanes and use third-man runs to advance the ball efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Third Man Concept: Emphasize the importance of the third player in the combination. After playing the ball to the second player, the first player must make an intelligent off-the-ball run, either providing support for the next pass or creating space for the ball to be played into.• Timing and Movement: Encourage players to time their runs effectively, ensuring they are always in position to receive the pass and move the ball forward. Off-the-ball movement is key to creating angles for the third-man pass.• Quick Decision-Making: With two balls in play, players must react quickly to each pass, deciding when to play vertically or horizontally. The transition between these two types of passes should be seamless, maintaining the flow of the exercise.• Ball Movement: Stress the need for crisp, accurate passes. Players should focus on ensuring the ball is passed with the correct weight and pace to maintain the flow of the drill and avoid disrupting the rhythm.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender into the drill to increase the pressure on the attacking players. This forces them to be quicker and more precise with their third-man passes, while also encouraging them to use better movement to escape defensive pressure.Focus: Improves passing under pressure and enhances attacking players' ability to use third-man combinations to break down defensive lines.

title: Germany Building into Midfield
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 3v1 rondo where the team in possession aims to complete a set number of passes before transitioning to attack. Once the team has completed the required number of passes, they must attempt to play forward into one of the three mini goals. The two outer mini goals are positioned to replicate midfielders receiving on angles, challenging the attacking team to find creative ways to break down the defense.The defending team consists of two players positioned outside the rondo grid. Their primary responsibility is to screen and protect the three mini goals, increasing the pressure on the attacking team as they try to build up and make a successful pass into one of the goals.
coaching_notes: • Rondo Focus: Encourage quick passing and sharp movement to create space for the team in possession. Players should focus on quick ball circulation and positioning to break the pressure of the 1 defender in the rondo.• Pressure on Mini Goals: Defenders positioned outside the rondo should always be aware of the ball and anticipate passes toward the mini goals. They must track the attackers' movements and close off any potential scoring opportunities.• Attacking Progression: Once the set number of passes is completed, players should aim to attack quickly, looking for opportunities to exploit the angles and space in the mini goals. Midfielders should work on timing their runs and positioning to receive the ball in good attacking areas.• Defensive Awareness: The defending players must stay compact and focused on protecting the mini goals. They should aim to read the play and intercept passes into the goal areas, while also being prepared to press the player in possession to disrupt the build-up.
progression_one: Increase Defensive Pressure:Add a second defender inside the rondo to increase the pressure on the attacking team. The additional defender should challenge the possession side to make quicker decisions.Focus: Improves decision-making and encourages quicker ball movement under pressure.
progression_two: Add More Mini Goals:Introduce additional mini goals to increase attacking options. Players can score in any of the mini goals, and defenders must cover multiple potential targets.Focus: Expands attacking creativity and challenges defenders to cover more space.

title: Germany Distance Shooting SSG
instructions_setup: In this small-sided game, teams play 4v4 centrally, with a specific focus on shooting from distance. To score, players must shoot from behind the dotted line, which creates a challenge to strike from outside the box. This setup encourages players to practice taking shots from range and finding opportunities to score from deeper positions.The depth of the dotted line can be adjusted depending on the players' age or ability, providing flexibility in terms of the shooting difficulty. This allows for better development of shooting techniques and decision-making under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Shooting Technique: Encourage players to focus on their shooting technique, specifically when shooting from distance. Players should be mindful of their foot placement and strike the ball cleanly with accuracy, not just power.• Positioning for Shots: Players should be aware of their positioning in relation to the dotted line, ensuring they have the opportunity to receive the ball in a good shooting position. They should also be aware of defenders trying to close down shooting lanes.• Shot Selection: Encourage players to assess the situation before shooting, considering factors like the goalkeeper's position, defensive pressure, and the angle of the shot. Players should not rush but rather choose their shots wisely.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders should focus on closing down players attempting shots from distance. This requires good positioning and timing to block or deflect shots, forcing attackers to take less favorable attempts.
progression_one: Vary Shooting Distance:Adjust the position of the dotted line to make the shooting distance shorter or longer, depending on the skill level of the players.Focus: Helps players develop the ability to shoot from varying distances and under different levels of pressure.

title: Germany Double 1v1
instructions_setup: n this drill, the attacking player will receive two balls from the coach in quick succession. The player starts by receiving the first ball and engages in a 1v1 with a defender. Once the first 1v1 goes dead, the coach serves the second ball immediately into the attacker, who then plays another 1v1 scenario, either against the same defender or a new one. This drill is designed to enhance the player's ability to quickly recover and transition between offensive situations while maintaining focus.The drill encourages quick thinking and sharp decision-making, as the attacker must immediately react to the second ball without much time to rest or reset. It mimics real-game scenarios where a player may need to quickly recover from one challenge and immediately face another.
coaching_notes: • 1v1 Technique: The attacker should focus on using quick changes of direction, body feints, and pace to beat the defender in the first 1v1. After the first challenge, they must reset quickly to face the second 1v1 with similar intensity.• Quick Transition: Encourage the attacker to transition smoothly between the two 1v1s. There should be no hesitation between engaging the first defender and facing the second. The ability to recover quickly is key.• Defender's Positioning: Defenders should focus on closing down space quickly and forcing the attacker into less favorable positions. Defenders should try to force the attacker into predictable movements, making it easier to defend.• Stay Calm Under Pressure: Encourage the attacker to stay calm and composed, especially after the first 1v1. Rapid transitions can be mentally and physically taxing, so staying focused on the task is important.
progression_one: Vary the Distance:Adjust the starting distance between the attacker and the defender to make the initial 1v1 challenge easier or harder.Focus: Helps the attacker practice different techniques, whether it’s beating a defender from a close distance or creating more space for a longer attack.

title: Germany Finish on the Move
instructions_setup: This finishing drill focuses on combining different types of passes and runs to improve attacking timing and decision-making. Players will work on three key movements: straight runs with diagonal passes, diagonal runs with straight passes, and diagonal runs with diagonal passes. Four poles are set up in a diamond shape to guide the players in visualizing and executing these passes and runs accurately.The drill requires players to adapt to different attacking scenarios by recognizing which run and pass combination will best break down the defense. Each combination helps players refine their ability to receive and finish in dynamic, real-game situations
coaching_notes: • Run Timing: Players should focus on timing their runs to meet the ball in stride. The run must be quick, purposeful, and well-coordinated with the pass. For straight runs with diagonal passes, the attacker should time the run to arrive at the right angle for the pass.• Pass Accuracy: The passer must focus on delivering accurate and well-weighted passes, particularly when executing diagonal passes. The ball must be played with the correct pace to reach the attacker’s feet or to set up a finish.• Body Position: Players must ensure they are in the correct body position to receive the ball and finish. When running diagonally, players should adjust their body to receive the pass in a way that makes it easy to finish towards goal.• Finishing Technique: Emphasize a variety of finishing techniques based on the type of pass received. Whether it’s a driven shot, a chip, or a placed finish, players should adjust to the ball’s trajectory and use the appropriate technique.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce defenders who can apply light pressure to force the attacking player to make quicker decisions on their runs and finishes.Focus: Helps players pr
progression_two: Increase Speed of Play:Increase the pace of the drill, requiring the players to execute the combinations faster while maintaining accuracy and composure in their runs and finishes.Focus: Builds the ability to perform under increased intensity, simulating match-like conditions where quick thinking and fast execution are crucial.

title: Germany Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness and conditioning drill combines technical passing with aerobic conditioning. Players will focus on making quick 1-touch passes before sprinting around the poles and reaching the opposite side in time to receive and play another 1-touch pass. The drill emphasizes speed, endurance, and technical precision under fatigue, making it ideal for improving overall fitness while maintaining passing accuracy.The circuit-style setup encourages players to maintain intensity and focus on both their fitness and technical execution. This drill can be adapted to suit various fitness levels and can be intensified by increasing the distance between poles or the number of passes required.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: Players must focus on making crisp, accurate 1-touch passes. The key is to keep the ball moving quickly while ensuring it reaches the target with precision.• Efficient Sprinting: Encourage players to sprint as fast as possible around the poles, focusing on maintaining proper running form and not losing speed between passes.• Timing and Speed: Players must time their sprints so they arrive in time to play the next pass. This builds awareness of space and timing, crucial for both fitness and technical success.• Recovery Between Sprints: Emphasize brief moments of recovery between sprints. Players should pace themselves during the sprints to avoid burnout while still maintaining a high level of intensity.
progression_one: Increase Distance Between Poles:Increase the distance between the poles, requiring longer sprints and more effort to maintain the same level of intensity.Focus: Increases cardiovascular endurance and challenges players’ ability to recover and maintain speed over longer distances.
progression_two: Add Multiple Touches:Introduce a variation where players need to make 2 or 3 touches before passing. This will emphasize control and passing accuracy under pressure.Focus: Enhances technical control and passing under a higher level of pressure while still maintaining the focus on sprinting and fitness.

title: Germany Half Pitch Countering
instructions_setup: This counter-attacking drill focuses on developing quick transitions from deep positions, utilizing the space behind the defensive line. The drill simulates a real match scenario where the attacking team must exploit the space after winning possession. A player will pass into the space behind the defensive line, triggering a 4v2 counter-attack. The attackers must transition rapidly and try to create a scoring opportunity within a 10-second time limit.The drill promotes quick thinking, pace, and decision-making, all while emphasizing the importance of exploiting spaces behind defenders during counter-attacks. The time limit creates a sense of urgency, pushing the attackers to move quickly and make decisive choices.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Emphasize the need for players to transition quickly from defense to attack. As soon as possession is gained, they must look to move the ball forward swiftly into the space behind the defensive line.• Exploiting Space: The attackers should focus on running into the available space behind the defense, timing their runs to stay onside and creating depth for better passing options.• Accuracy of Pass: The player passing into the space should aim for accuracy, ensuring the ball is played into an area that gives the attacking team a clear advantage. The ball should allow attackers to run onto it at speed.• Defenders’ Positioning: Defenders must quickly recover and adjust their positioning to block the space. They should look to force attackers wide or slow down the counter by closing down the space.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure:Introduce an additional defender who starts from behind the counter-attacking team, forcing the attackers to think even more quickly and find space in tighter areas.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and enhances the attackers' ability to finish or create chances under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Time Limit:Increase the time limit from 10 seconds to 15 seconds, allowing attackers a bit more time to make decisions and increase their options in the final third.Focus: Provides attackers more time to evaluate options and make better decisions while still maintaining the urgency of the drill.

title: Germany Receive & Play
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to focus on the technical skills of receiving and passing forward, which is essential for maintaining possession and progressing the ball up the field. The drill involves four teams working within a grid that is split into 16 different zones. Each team will be assigned to a vertical line, with one player positioned in each horizontal zone. Players will pass the ball forward into the next player, aiming to progress the ball vertically through the grid. This encourages a fast and direct style of passing, helping players develop the ability to make forward passes under pressure.The setup allows players to work on their passing accuracy, receiving under pressure, and making quick decisions to progress the ball forward. The grid structure also creates a controlled environment to reinforce the concept of moving the ball quickly from one zone to the next, maintaining fluidity in possession.
coaching_notes: • Passing Forward: Players should focus on making accurate forward passes, aiming to progress the ball through the grid as quickly as possible. Encourage players to play passes with pace to allow the receiver to continue the movement.• Receiving Under Pressure: Emphasize the importance of receiving the ball in a way that prepares the player to immediately play forward. Encourage players to open their body and scan for options before receiving the pass.• Movement off the Ball: Encourage off-the-ball movement to create passing lanes for the player with the ball. Players should make runs into open space, ensuring they are available for a forward pass.• Decision-Making: Players must make quick decisions on whether to pass forward or hold the ball. Encourage the habit of always looking for the most progressive pass available.
progression_one: Increase Speed of Play:Reduce the amount of time players have to make a pass after receiving the ball. This can be done by introducing a time limit or increasing the pressure from defenders.Focus: Enhances players' ability to make quick decisions and pass under pressure, improving speed of play.
progression_two: Add Defenders:Introduce a defender to each vertical line, forcing players to think more about the timing and placement of their passes, ensuring they are playing into space and not directly into the defender's area.Focus: Encourages players to use their vision and creativity to pass into space and avoid pressure.

title: Germany Rotational Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo drill is designed to develop players' understanding of positional rotations and how to maintain possession while dynamically moving within the grid. A 4v2 is played out on each side of the grid, where the central player is not fixed and can rotate in or out of the grid based on the set rotational pattern. The objective is to keep possession while constantly moving and adjusting positions, ensuring that players are always available for a pass and aware of the space around them. The central player’s role is to add flexibility to the rondo, forcing players to adjust their positioning and movement in response to the ball.By incorporating rotation into this drill, players will improve their ability to recognize space, change positions on the field, and maintain fluidity in possession. This encourages adaptability and helps players understand how to create overloads and maintain control during dynamic game situations.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness: Players must always be aware of their position in relation to the ball and their teammates. Emphasize the importance of maintaining balance in the grid, with players spread out to create space for passing.• Rotational Movement: The central player should rotate in and out of the grid based on the established pattern. Players on the outside should adjust their positions accordingly to maintain possession and create passing options.• Pass and Move: Encourage players to play one-touch or two-touch passes and immediately move into new positions. This keeps the drill moving at a high tempo and ensures that players are always active and engaged.• Pressing and Covering: Defenders must work together to apply pressure while also covering the passing lanes. The attacking team should focus on quick ball movement and constant rotation to break the defensive pressure.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Possession:Introduce a time limit, such as 30 seconds, for the team in possession to maintain control. This will encourage quicker decision-making and more fluid rotations.Focus: Improves decision-making under time pressure and reinforces the importance of quick ball movement.
progression_two: Introduce More Defenders:Add an additional defender to the grid, making it a 4v3 or 4v4. This forces the attacking team to be more creative with their rotations and passing to break down the increased defensive pressure.Focus: Develops the ability to maintain possession and execute rotations under increased pressure.

title: Germany Warm Up & SAQ
instructions_setup: This warm-up drill is designed to combine speed, agility, and quickness (SAQ) with running, providing players with an effective way to prepare physically for the demands of a game. It is used regularly by FC Bayern of Germany to enhance players' explosiveness, balance, and footwork. The drill incorporates various running patterns, cone work, and directional changes to ensure players are constantly engaged and mentally focused. The movements performed in this drill simulate the dynamic changes in direction, acceleration, and deceleration that players encounter during matches, ensuring a well-rounded preparation for the game ahead.The combination of SAQ exercises and running drills ensures that players are prepared both physically and mentally, improving their reaction times, coordination, and overall fitness. This warm-up also prepares players to perform under pressure, as they must constantly adjust their movements to respond to changing directions and positions.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Movements: Encourage players to focus on explosive movements, such as quick starts and stops, as they go through the SAQ and running sections of the warm-up. This will help improve their acceleration and deceleration.• Proper Footwork: Emphasize the importance of proper footwork and body positioning, particularly when making sharp cuts or quick directional changes. Encourage players to stay low and balanced to avoid unnecessary injury.• Mental Focus: Players should remain mentally focused on their movements and transitions, as the drill requires quick thinking and reaction. Stress the importance of maintaining concentration throughout the warm-up.• Recovery Between Efforts: Ensure that players have short rest intervals between the running phases to allow for recovery, maintaining the high intensity of the drill without causing fatigue.
progression_one: Add Ball Work:Introduce a ball into the drill, making it more game-specific. Players can dribble or pass the ball while performing the SAQ and running movements, simulating the demands of match situations.Focus: Improves ball control, decision-making, and movement under pressure during high-intensity situations.
progression_two: Increase Intensity:Increase the speed and frequency of the movements or reduce rest time between phases to elevate the intensity. This challenges players’ endurance and improves their ability to maintain high levels of performance throughout the match.Focus: Enhances cardiovascular fitness and ensures players can maintain high-intensity movements over longer periods.

title: Getafe 1v1 Finishing
instructions_setup: This 1v1 finishing drill takes place inside the penalty box with two full-sized goals, one placed on the edge of the area to create a mini pitch. The drill involves 4 players positioned outside the grid, each with a ball. The attacker must use quick movements, sharp cuts, and good communication to create separation from the defender, allowing them to receive a pass and take a shot on goal. The defender’s task is to stay alert and prevent the attacker from getting a shot off, while the attacker has the added challenge of having two goals to aim for, making the decision-making process more dynamic.The players outside the grid feed the balls into the attacker, forcing them to time their movements and decisions carefully. The defender needs to stay focused and position themselves well to block potential shots on both goals. This drill helps develop finishing under pressure, quick decision-making, and the ability to work in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Quick Movement and Separation: Emphasize the importance of the attacker using quick, deceptive movements to create separation from the defender. Encourage attackers to change direction rapidly and use their body to shield the ball.• Effective Communication: Encourage constant verbal communication between the attacker and the players outside the grid who are serving the balls. This helps with timing and positioning, allowing the attacker to anticipate and prepare for the pass.• Defender Awareness: The defender must stay alert and anticipate the attacker’s moves. They should focus on positioning themselves to cut off shooting angles and force the attacker into less dangerous areas of the box.• Shooting Decision: The attacker must make quick decisions about which goal to aim for, depending on the defender's positioning. Encourage attackers to focus on accuracy over power when finishing.
progression_one: Change of Angle:Adjust the positioning of the players outside the grid so they serve balls from different angles. This forces the attacker to adjust their positioning and make decisions based on varying types of service.Focus: Improves the attacker’s ability to finish from different angles and under varying pressures from the defender.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 10 seconds) within which the attacker must receive a pass and take a shot. This increases the intensity and challenges the attacker to make decisions more quickly.Focus: Develops the ability to make quick decisions and finish under time pressure.

title: Getafe 2 Phase Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: This cross and finishing drill is designed to improve your team's ability to finish from close range. The drill is split into two phases. In Phase 1, the attacking players make their run into the box, with a cross coming from one side. The attackers aim to finish from close range into the goal. After completing the first phase, the attackers quickly turn around and switch direction to attack the opposite goal. In Phase 2, a cross comes from the opposite side, and the attackers again look to finish from close range.The key to this drill is the quick transition between the two phases, ensuring attackers are ready to adjust and finish from both sides of the box. This helps players develop the ability to react quickly to crosses, improving their finishing skills and awareness of space around the goal.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Run: Encourage attackers to time their runs well to meet the cross at the optimal moment. Players should be encouraged to attack the ball with pace and be ready to strike as soon as the cross comes in.• Finishing Under Pressure: Emphasize the importance of finishing under pressure from defenders. Attackers should focus on keeping their shots on target, aiming for placement over power, especially when finishing from close range.• Quick Transition: After completing a finish, attackers should quickly turn and get ready to attack the opposite goal. This helps improve their ability to quickly recover and stay alert during the transition between phases.• Crossing Quality: Encourage the players providing the crosses to deliver accurate and varied balls, ensuring the attackers are presented with different types of crosses (high, low, driven, or floated).
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender in each phase to apply pressure on the attacking player. This forces the attacker to be more aware of their positioning and decision-making when receiving the ball.Focus: Enhances finishing under pressure and improves decision-making when facing defenders in the box.
progression_two: First-Time Finishing:Encourage players to attempt first-time finishes whenever possible. This adds a layer of difficulty and simulates real-match scenarios where the ball may come quickly and require a first-time strike.Focus: Develops the ability to finish quickly and efficiently, reducing the time spent adjusting for the shot.

title: Getafe 2 Touch Game
instructions_setup: This ball mastery game serves as a technical warm-up, focusing on touch control and passing accuracy. Players are allowed a maximum of two touches and must ensure the ball remains below knee height. Each team of two players is positioned inside their own square grid, with the grids set 10 meters apart. The objective is to deliver a powerful pass to the opposing team and challenge their first touch. A point is awarded for every time the opposition takes a touch that causes the ball to fall outside of their grid.This drill emphasizes passing power, precision, and the ability to control the ball under pressure. Players must focus on keeping the ball within the designated area while managing to pass it accurately and effectively.
coaching_notes: • Control Under Pressure: Encourage players to focus on their first touch, ensuring they can control the ball even when it is passed with power. Players should aim to keep the ball close to their body to maintain possession within the grid.• Pass Precision: Passes should be firm but not too heavy, allowing the receiving player to control the ball effectively. The goal is to challenge the opponent’s first touch while maintaining control of the ball.• Body Positioning: Players should use their body to position themselves well for the pass, ensuring they are able to receive and pass accurately within the given space.• Quick Decision Making: Players must react quickly to each pass and anticipate the trajectory of the ball to adjust their first touch accordingly. The focus should be on minimizing mistakes while maintaining speed and accuracy.

title: Getafe 3 Coloured Possession
instructions_setup: In this drill, three teams of three players each engage in a 6v3 possession-based exercise. Two of the teams always maintain possession in a 6v3, working the ball around to retain control and create opportunities. The defending team, consisting of three players, must focus on regaining possession and preventing the teams in possession from switching the play.Once the defending team successfully wins possession, they transition to join the team in possession. The team that lost possession will then transition into defense and attempt to regain the ball. This drill emphasizes continuous transition, quick thinking, and effective ball retention.
coaching_notes: • Possession Awareness: Encourage the teams in possession to focus on quick, accurate passing and movement to maintain control. Players should scan the field constantly to identify passing lanes and support options.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders must apply pressure quickly and efficiently, staying compact to force the attacking team to make mistakes. They should look to intercept passes and close down passing lanes.• Transition Speed: Once possession is won, defenders should immediately transition to attack, keeping the tempo high. Quick decision-making is essential as the team must shift from defense to offense within seconds.• Communication: Players must communicate constantly, both when in possession and when defending. Clear communication ensures that everyone is on the same page and helps maintain team shape, especially when transitioning.

title: Getafe Build into Counter Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 2+GK v1 build-up where the team in possession aims to progress the ball through to any of the 3 forward players positioned further up the pitch.
