The build-up team must focus on quick, controlled passing and creating angles to break the defensive lines, while the goalkeeper supports the build-up play.Once the ball reaches one of the 3 forward players, the next phase begins: a 3v2 attacking scenario. The attackers must then work to break down the two defenders and create a scoring opportunity. Throughout this drill, there are various moments of transition that simulate realistic counter-attacking situations.If the single defender in the build-up phase wins possession, they immediately initiate a counter-attack. During the 3v2 phase, if the two defenders regain possession, they have the opportunity to counter by passing the ball forward to the three attackers on the opposite side and continuing with a 3v2 attack.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Quality: The attacking team must focus on sharp, accurate passing and maintaining good spacing to progress the ball effectively through the lines. The goalkeeper plays a key role in supporting this build-up.• Movement off the Ball: Forward players should make dynamic runs to create space and angles for the ball carrier, enabling better passing options. Timing and communication are essential in breaking the defensive lines.• Defensive Pressure: Defenders must stay compact and work together to delay the attacking team. In the 3v2 phase, defenders should focus on narrowing down options for the attackers and force them into less dangerous positions.• Counter Attack Awareness: Once possession is won, all players should immediately transition to a counter-attacking mindset. The team regaining possession must look to exploit space quickly, while the attackers must support the counter with well-timed runs.
progression_one: Add Extra Attacker:Introduce a fourth attacker to the initial 3v2 phase, turning it into a 4v2 attack. This progression provides more attacking options and helps develop team play in numerical superiority situations.Focus: Enhances decision-making and teamwork in high-pressure situations, increasing the challenge for defenders and providing attackers with more opportunities to finish.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Set a time limit of 10-15 seconds for each phase of play (build-up, attack, and counter). This forces the attacking team to move quickly and make decisions under pressure while encouraging the defending team to respond swiftly when they win possession.Focus: Increases the tempo of the drill, helping players improve their speed of thought and execution in both attacking and defensive transitions.

title: Getafe Counter Press Rondo
instructions_setup: This 7v4 rondo focuses on improving possession retention and the ability to counter-press immediately after losing the ball. The attacking team of seven players must work together to maintain possession, looking for opportunities to break through the defensive lines of the four defenders. If the defending team wins possession, they must quickly transition and attempt to move the ball into one of the end zones to score.Each end zone is approximately 10 meters long and has two mini goals placed at the end. The attacking team can counter-press to prevent a goal by quickly recovering possession. The defenders must work to transition quickly and accurately, while the possession team must stay alert and organized to ensure they can regain control before the ball crosses into the scoring zone.
coaching_notes: • Possession Control: The team in possession should focus on maintaining control with quick, short passes and effective movement off the ball. They must be patient but also look for opportunities to penetrate through the defending players.• Counter Pressing: As soon as possession is lost, the players in possession should immediately counter-press, applying pressure to the ball carrier to prevent an easy transition into the end zone. This requires excellent fitness, awareness, and communication.• Defender Transitions: Defenders should look to exploit space in the end zones quickly but must stay aware of the counter-press, as the original possession team will be looking to regain the ball.• End Zone Focus: The defending team should work on quick transitions into the end zones, aiming to score within a set time frame. The key to success here is decision-making – whether to take on a shot quickly or to pass to a better-placed teammate.
progression_one: Restrict Time in End Zones:Limit the time the defending team can spend in the end zone to 5-7 seconds. This forces the attackers to counter-press quickly and regain possession before the defenders have a chance to fully set up a goal-scoring opportunity.Focus: Encourages urgency in both counter-pressing and attacking, improving decision-making under pressure.

title: Getafe Creating Triangles
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical passing drill is designed to develop quick passing and movement, with an emphasis on 1-touch combinations. The grid has two players fixed on each end line, while two other players are positioned on the vertical lines. The players on the vertical lines will travel up and down the grid, focusing on passing the ball to the players on the end lines before receiving it back and progressing up and down the field.The practice encourages fluid movement, quick decision-making, and precise passing as players move the ball through the grid. The fixed players on the end lines serve as targets for combination play, which helps players improve their passing accuracy, awareness, and first-touch control. The key here is to work efficiently, keeping the ball moving quickly and making well-timed runs.
coaching_notes: • 1-Touch Passing: Players should focus on delivering accurate 1-touch passes, ensuring the ball is played into the path of the teammate for easy control. This practice sharpens quick thinking and improves passing accuracy.• Movement Off the Ball: The players on the vertical lines should focus on constant movement, looking to make themselves available for passes by changing their positioning based on the ball's movement. Good timing and awareness are essential for this.• Fluid Transitions: After each pass, players must quickly transition to a new position, ensuring a continuous flow of play. The player receiving the ball should always be ready to control it and play it forward or back to maintain the rhythm of the practice.• Passing Range: Vary the distance and angle of passes between players on the end lines to simulate different game situations. Players should aim to develop both short-range and longer-range passing accuracy.
progression_one: Add a Dribble Component:Introduce a dribbling phase where the players on the vertical lines must dribble the ball a set distance before playing their 1-touch combination. This adds an extra layer of skill development and simulates real-game situations where players must control the ball under pressure.Focus: Enhances dribbling under control and the ability to quickly transition from dribbling to passing.

title: Getafe Finish the Attack Overloaded
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 4v4 in the center of the grid, with four additional bounce players positioned around the grid. These bounce players are restricted to 1-touch play, providing quick support for the attacking team. The team in possession can use the bounce players to create an 8v4 advantage when attacking, encouraging quick, fluid combinations and decision-making in tight spaces.The aim is to develop fast attacking combinations and awareness of players around the ball. By using the bounce players, the team in possession can unlock space, create overloads, and quickly progress the ball forward. The defending team must focus on pressuring the ball and preventing easy access to the bounce players.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: Players must focus on playing quick, sharp passes to keep the tempo high. The bounce players should be used effectively to create additional space, helping to stretch the opposition defense and open passing lanes.• Awareness of Bounce Players: Players in possession need to constantly scan for the bounce players to exploit the overload when attacking. Bounce players should be ready to receive the ball and make an immediate impact with 1-touch play.• Pressure on the Ball: Defenders need to focus on applying constant pressure to the player with the ball, forcing them into difficult decisions and limiting their options. The defensive team should also be aware of the bounce players and position themselves accordingly to deny easy passes.• Switching Play Quickly: When the team loses possession, they must transition quickly to defense and prevent the attacking team from exploiting the bounce players. The defending team must be quick to organize and counter the overload.
progression_one: Restrict the Bounce Player's Movement:Limit the bounce players' movement to certain zones on the pitch (e.g., they can only stay in the middle third). This forces the team in possession to be more creative with how they use the bounce players and ensures that attacking play is more deliberate and focused.Focus: Develops creativity and tactical awareness, requiring the team to work together and find space in more specific areas of the field.

title: Getafe One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This three-phase finishing drill focuses on timing and quality of runs between mannequins and finishing from different angles. The player will make successive runs: first between mannequins for a finish in the gap, then in behind the mannequins for a low finish, and finally across the shoulder of the mannequins to finish at a more acute angle.
coaching_notes: • Time Runs Precisely to Stay Onside and Create Space – Perfecting the timing of each run is crucial to get clear shooting opportunities.• Use Explosive Acceleration to Beat Defenders (mannequins) – Quick bursts between mannequins simulate game scenarios where sharp changes of pace create chances.• Keep Body Balanced and Eyes on Goal for Quality Finishes – Maintain composure and focus to execute accurate finishes from varying angles.• Adjust Finishing Technique According to Run Type and Angle – Use different finishes (placed, driven, or chipped) depending on the position and shot angle.

title: Glasgow 1v1 Attacking & Defending
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a lateral pass played across the grid to trigger the 1v1. As soon as the pass is made, both the attacker and defender sprint around their designated outside cones before entering the playing area to engage in the duel. This creates a dynamic, game-realistic start that forces sharp reactions and immediate acceleration.Once the players enter the grid, the attacker aims to drive forward at pace and create a shooting opportunity, while the defender attempts to delay, block forward progress, and win back possession. If the defender regains the ball, they are encouraged to counter and score to maintain realism and competitiveness. Use 4–6 players per grid and set up multiple areas to ensure high repetition and intensity throughout the session.
coaching_notes: • Positive First Touch: Encourage the attacker to take their first touch forward and attack space quickly to put immediate pressure on the defender.• Use of Body and Feints: Highlight how attackers can disguise intentions by using shoulder drops, changes of angle, and body positioning to unbalance the defender.• Speed Variation: Coach players to accelerate explosively after the initial move but also to decelerate and re-accelerate when needed to create separation.• End Product: Reinforce the importance of finishing actions—once the attacker creates space, they should get their shot off early with control and composure.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Score:Introduce a 4–5 second time limit for the attacker to get a shot away after entering the grid. This forces quicker decision-making and reduces unnecessary slowing of the duel.Focus: Encourages decisive attacking actions and improves the speed of execution.
progression_two: Defender Counter Line:Add a counter line or mini target that the defender can break into or score in if they win the ball. This increases realism and encourages both players to transition immediately upon possession change.Focus: Enhances transition behaviours and motivates defenders to win the ball with purpose.

title: Glasgow 3v1 Possession Transfers
instructions_setup: This practice is organised across four small possession grids, each containing one locked-in defender. The attacking team has eight players who are free to move between grids, enabling them to create a 3v1 numerical advantage in any zone. Play begins with the attacking team circulating the ball, looking to combine quickly and transfer possession from one grid to another while maintaining control.The aim for the attackers is to recognise where overloads can be created, move efficiently to support the ball, and use fast combinations to break out of pressure. If a defender wins possession, they immediately transition to attack and can score in any of the four mini goals positioned around the outside. This keeps all players alert to defensive pressing triggers and attacking transitions.
coaching_notes: • Create Overloads: Encourage attackers to move early and form 3v1 situations, giving the ball-carrier clear angles and passing options.• Switching Play: Reinforce quick recognition of where the space is—players should scan across all grids and transfer the ball away from pressure when possible.• One- and Two-Touch Rhythm: Highlight the need for fast circulation, crisp passing, and purposeful movement to maintain tempo and shift defenders.• Support Positions: Coach players to adopt clever supporting angles around the ball to keep possession secure while maintaining forward transfer options.
progression_one: Set Pass Targets Before Transferring:Require the attackers to complete a designated number of passes (for example, 3–5) within a grid before they are allowed to transfer the ball into another area. This increases discipline, scanning, and patience during the build-up phase.Focus: Improves controlled possession, teamwork, and decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Allow Two Defenders Per Grid:Permit defenders to leave their original zones and join another grid, turning moments into potential 3v2 situations. This raises the intensity and forces attackers to move the ball even quicker while recognising pressure cues.Focus: Develops speed of circulation, spatial awareness, and the ability to retain overloads under increased defensive pressure.

title: Glasgow Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: This attacking practice is played across two consecutive zones, creating a double 3v2 scenario. The attacking team consists of two attackers supported by one neutral player, giving them a consistent overload of three. The task begins in the first area, the build zone, where the attackers must combine to beat two defenders using movement, sharp passing, or dribbling to progress into the second zone.Once they successfully enter the attacking zone, the attackers immediately face another pair of defenders in a second 3v2 situation. Here they must find a way to create space, isolate a defender, and finish the attack with quality. The structure encourages fluid combinations, clever support play, and the ability to break defensive lines across multiple phases of play.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Combinations: Encourage the attackers to use quick give-and-go movements, third-man runs, and set passes to break the defensive line in both zones.• Off-Ball Movement: Highlight supporting runs that pull defenders away, create passing lanes, and open space for the next action.• Dribbling to Commit Defenders: Coach the ball-carrier to drive at defenders with purpose, drawing pressure to create clear 2v1 moments for teammates.• Timing of Forward Play: Emphasise patience when needed but explosive forward movement once space is created to maintain the numerical advantage.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Finish the Attack:Introduce a 6–8 second limit for the attackers to progress through both zones and attempt a finish. This encourages quicker ball circulation, faster movements off the ball, and more game-realistic tempo.Focus: Speeds up decision-making and improves attacking urgency.
progression_two: Defenders Can Recover Between Zones:Allow one defender from the build zone to recover into the attacking zone once the ball transitions forward. This creates moments of temporary equality or overloaded defence, forcing attackers to read pressure and adapt.Focus: Develops realism in transitions and improves the attackers' ability to create advantages even when defensive numbers change.

title: Glasgow Front 2 Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice is designed for two centre forwards working through four consecutive finishing phases. The first two phases begin centrally, with each attacker running onto a pass, taking one controlled touch between the mannequins to guide the ball into the box, and then finishing on goal. This focuses heavily on the quality, direction and weight of the first touch while reinforcing composure when entering the penalty area.The next two phases come from wide areas, with crosses delivered from both the left and right sides. The attackers must time their movements effectively, adjust their body shape, and attack the cross with intent. All four finishing actions flow continuously, creating a high volume of repetitions and helping players refine their timing, coordination and end product.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Emphasise coordinated movement so attackers arrive onto the pass or cross at the right moment rather than being static or arriving too early.• First Touch Quality: Reinforce taking the touch into space and between mannequins to set up the finish cleanly and keep the action fluid.• Body Shape and Composure: Coach forwards to open their body, stay balanced, and choose the correct finish when entering the penalty area.• Attacking the Cross: Encourage aggressive movement, attacking the correct zones, and adjusting steps to meet the ball cleanly.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender on the Crosses:Introduce one passive defender inside the box during the crossing phases. Their role is to add light pressure, occupy space, and force the attackers to make smarter movements to find finishing angles.Focus: Improves movement timing, scanning, and finishing under mild defensive interference.
progression_two: Add a Finishing Time Constraint:Set a 3–4 second limit from the moment the attacker receives the ball or the cross is delivered to finish the action. This replicates match tempo and increases the demand on first-touch quality and quick decision-making.Focus: Enhances speed of execution, sharpness in front of goal, and realistic finishing behaviours.

title: Glasgow Overloaded & Transition
instructions_setup: This practice combines an overloaded attacking phase with an immediate defensive transition. Play begins with a 2+1v2 scenario, where two attackers supported by a neutral player create a 3v2 advantage. Their objective is to combine quickly and finish into one of the mini goals, focusing on sharp movement, fast circulation and decisive end product.Once the attacking phase ends—either through a goal, save, or turnover—the two attackers must instantly transition to the opposite side of the grid. There, they become defenders and face a fresh 2+1v2 overload against two attackers and one neutral player. This shift demands fast recovery, awareness and the ability to reset defensively under pressure. The practice creates continuous repetitions of attack, transition and defend.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Movement and Rotation: Encourage attackers to create width, depth and angles, using the neutral player for quick combinations and third-man runs.• Speed of Attack: Highlight the importance of moving the ball quickly to exploit the overload before defenders can delay or recover.• Transition Mindset: Coach players to react instantly once the first phase ends—sprint into defensive positions and organise quickly.• Defensive Engagement: Emphasise delaying the attack, cutting central options and working together to force predictable actions.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Score:Introduce a 5–6 second limit for the overloaded team to finish their attack. This raises the intensity and encourages faster combinations, sharper movement and more decisive actions.Focus: Improves attacking urgency and clinical decision-making.

title: Hamburg Between Lines & Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed attacking practice focuses on breaking lines and creating finishing opportunities from wide areas. Play starts with a controlled pass in midfield before a forward, line-breaking pass is played into a player positioned between the lines. On receiving, the attacker turns quickly and plays a threaded pass into the path of an onrushing full back, who delivers a cross for the finish.In the second variation, the between-the-lines player combines with the wide full back using a 1–2. The full back sets the ball back into the half space, allowing the original attacker to receive on the move and deliver a cross into the box for a finish. Both variations encourage clean progression through central areas before exploiting wide spaces.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Line-Breaking Passes: Encourage firm, accurate passes that break defensive lines and allow the receiver to play forward on the first touch.• Body Shape Between the Lines: Coach the receiving player to open up on the half turn to see both the wide runner and the box.• Timing of Full-Back Runs: Emphasize delayed, explosive runs from wide areas to arrive at speed for the cross.• End Product: Reinforce accurate crossing and composed finishing based on the type of delivery.
progression_one: Add Passive Defenders:Introduce one or two passive defenders in central areas to apply light pressure on the between-the-lines player, forcing sharper scanning and quicker decisions.Focus: Improves awareness, tempo and realism in build-up play.
progression_two: Limit Touches on Key Actions:Restrict the between-the-lines player to two touches and the crosser to one or two touches before delivery.Focus: Encourages fast combinations, cleaner execution and match-realistic tempo.

title: Hamburg Build Up Technical
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice is designed to reinforce key build-up principles such as back-foot receiving, forward body shape and quick ball circulation. The practice operates with two balls simultaneously, ensuring a high tempo and constant engagement for all players.Both balls are played into two central players, who must scan, receive on the back foot and play forward where possible. After receiving centrally, players are required to move the ball out to supporting teammates positioned around the outside before resetting their position for the next repetition. The continuous flow of passes encourages rhythm, timing and technical consistency while replicating common build-up patterns seen in match play.
coaching_notes: • Back-Foot Receiving: Emphasise opening the body and receiving on the furthest foot to allow players to play forward with their next action.• Body Shape Before the Pass: Encourage players to scan early and adopt an open stance to see both sides of the pitch.• Pass Detail and Weight: Reinforce firm, accurate passes played into the correct foot to support clean ball progression.• Tempo and Concentration: With two balls in play, stress constant focus, communication and movement to maintain flow.
progression_one: Two-Touch Requirement for Central Players:Central players must receive on the back foot with their first touch and play forward with their second.Focus: Improves first-touch quality, awareness and speed of ball circulation.

title: Hamburg Create & Finish
instructions_setup: This practice is designed to link possession, progression and end product. Play begins in the first zone with a 4v2 possession scenario. The attacking team must retain the ball under pressure while looking for the right moment to progress play through a central player positioned between the zones.Once the ball is played forward into the attacking zone, the practice becomes live against two defenders and a goalkeeper, where the attackers must combine quickly and attempt to finish the attack. The transition between zones encourages players to recognise when to secure possession and when to play forward with purpose.To increase challenge and control tempo, the possession team in the first zone can be required to complete a set number of passes before progressing the ball into the attacking phase.
coaching_notes: • Central Player Awareness: Encourage the central player to constantly scan, adjust their body shape and receive on the half-turn.• Timing of Progression: Reinforce patience in possession followed by decisive forward play when the opportunity presents itself.• Speed of Attack: Once the ball enters the attacking zone, emphasise quick combinations and direct movement to exploit the defence.• Finishing Detail: Coach composure in front of goal, selecting the correct finish based on defensive pressure and goalkeeper positioning.
progression_one: Minimum Pass Requirement in Zone One:Set a target number of passes (e.g. 5–8) before the ball can be played into the attacking zone.Focus: Encourages ball retention, movement off the ball and controlled build-up.
progression_two: Add a Recovering Defender:Allow one defender from the first zone to recover into the attacking zone after the ball is progressed.Focus: Increases realism, challenges attacking decision-making and encourages faster execution.

title: Hamburg Half Space Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice focuses on combination play from the half space and timing of forward runs. Play starts with an attacker positioned in the half-space, who plays a pass out wide to a supporting wide player. Immediately after releasing the ball, the attacker makes a straight, aggressive run towards goal.The wide player then delivers a first-time return pass back into the half space, allowing the attacker to run onto the ball and finish with minimal disruption. The practice is mirrored on both sides of the pitch, enabling players to work on both right- and left-foot finishes while developing rhythm, movement and finishing technique.
coaching_notes: • Pass Detail into Wide Areas: Encourage accurate passes into the wide player’s path to allow a clean first-time return.• Timing of the Forward Run: Reinforce explosive movement after the initial pass, ensuring the attacker arrives onto the ball at speed.• Body Shape for Finishing: Coach players to open up their body when receiving in the half space to finish cleanly across goal.• Composure in Front of Goal: Emphasise calm decision-making and correct finish selection based on distance and angle.
progression_one: Two-Touch Finish Only:Require attackers to take one touch out of their feet and finish with the second touch.Focus: Improves first-touch quality, balance and controlled finishing.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender:Introduce a passive defender who applies light pressure as the attacker receives the return pass in the half space.Focus: Increases realism and encourages quicker execution under pressure.

title: Hamburg Technical Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice is designed to develop rhythm, coordination and consistency in possession. Two balls are in play at the same time, ensuring a high tempo and constant involvement for all players. The practice encourages players to move the ball quickly, receive under light pressure and maintain focus while executing repeated passing actions.Players are required to circulate possession with accuracy and intent, constantly adjusting their positioning to support the next pass. The simultaneous use of two balls challenges concentration, communication and technical quality, making this an effective warm-up or technical activation within a session.
coaching_notes: • Pass Quality: Emphasise firm, accurate passes played to the correct foot to support the next action.• First Touch Detail: Encourage players to prepare their body and first touch to play smoothly into the next pass.• Scanning and Awareness: Reinforce regular scanning before receiving to maintain awareness of ball movement and teammates.• Tempo and Focus: With two balls in play, stress concentration and
progression_one: Two-Touch Maximum:Limit players to two touches to increase tempo and sharpen technical execution.Focus: Improves first-touch quality and speed of play.

title: Helsinki 1v1 Back to Goal to 2v1
instructions_setup: This drill develops an attacker’s ability to receive under tight pressure, combine quickly, and then create separation for a 1v1 scoring opportunity. Play starts with the attacker receiving a pass while a defender applies close pressure from behind. The attacker plays a quick 1-2 with an unopposed teammate before making a decisive movement or run to break free from the defender. This initiates a 1v1 duel where the attacker aims to beat the defender and score into the main goal.The drill sharpens first touch, combination play, spatial awareness, and dribbling skills under pressure. Defenders improve their tracking, positioning, and one-on-one defending in realistic attacking scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Stress tight, controlled first touches to help attackers maintain possession under intense pressure – Clean control is vital for executing the quick 1-2 successfully and keeping attacking flow.• Encourage quick, sharp 1-2 passing to disrupt defender’s positioning and create attacking space – Fast combinations make it harder for defenders to anticipate and close down.• Remind attackers to use feints and sharp changes of direction to create separation from defenders – Effective body movement deceives defenders and opens clear paths to goal.• Emphasize composure and precision when finishing 1v1 against the goalkeeper – Players should focus on placement and timing to maximize scoring chances under pressure.
progression_one: Limit 1-2 TouchesRestrict the attacker and teammate to one or two touches during the 1-2 combination to increase challenge.Focus: Enhance attackers’ quick thinking, sharp passing, and movement efficiency in tight spaces.

title: Helsinki 2v1 Overlap to Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing attacking players' ability to combine through natural overlapping runs against a single defender. Two attackers start with the ball and work together to create passing angles and overlaps to penetrate the defense. The defender must stay alert, communicate, and position themselves effectively to block passing lanes, delay the attackers, and prevent them from scoring into the main goal.The attackers practice timing their overlapping runs and quick combination play to outsmart the defender. Meanwhile, the defender improves one-on-one defending, decision-making, and anticipation under pressure. This drill promotes teamwork, spatial awareness, and sharp attacking movements in a realistic 2v1 scenario.
coaching_notes: • Encourage attackers to time overlapping runs precisely to create clear passing options – This coordination helps disrupt defensive positioning and open scoring chances.• Stress quick, accurate passing between attackers to maintain attacking momentum and pressure – Sharp ball movement forces the defender into difficult decision-making.• Remind the defender to stay goal-side and anticipate overlaps early – Positioning and reading the attackers’ intentions are crucial to cutting off passes and delaying attacks.• Emphasize communication between both attackers to exploit space and create scoring opportunities – Vocal teamwork maximizes effectiveness and prevents defensive recovery.
progression_one: Defender Starts CloserHave the defender start closer to the attackers to increase defensive pressure and force quicker attacking decisions.Focus: Improve attackers’ speed of combination and defender’s reaction time in tighter spaces.
progression_two: Add Time LimitSet a time limit for attackers to score to encourage faster attacking play and composure under pressure.Focus: Develop attackers’ quick decision-making and finishing ability in high-pressure situations.

title: Helsinki 3rd Man Technical
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving players’ understanding and execution of 3rd man passing combinations to create attacking opportunities. Players work in groups of three, positioned in a triangular shape, where the ball is passed between two players before being played into the third player who makes a timed run into space. The drill encourages sharp timing, awareness of teammates’ movement, and quick, accurate passing to break defensive lines effectively.Players rotate roles regularly, practicing playing both the initial passes and the decisive 3rd man pass. This activation emphasizes communication, anticipation, and precise ball control, helping players develop fluid attacking patterns in game situations.
coaching_notes: • Encourage players to communicate clearly and call for the ball early – This improves timing and ensures smooth, coordinated passing sequences throughout the drill.• Focus on sharp, accurate passes with the correct weight and pace – Proper passing technique allows the third player to receive and move forward efficiently without breaking stride.• Emphasize the importance of timing runs into space for the 3rd man – Well-timed movement creates space and options, breaking down defensive lines effectively during attacks.• Reinforce quick decision-making under moderate pressure – Developing mental sharpness helps players adapt quickly to changing scenarios and maintain flow.
progression_one: Increase Pace and ComplexitySpeed up the passing tempo and add an additional player to the combination, creating more complex passing angles and movement requirements.Focus: Develop faster decision-making, sharper technical execution, and better spatial awareness under increased complexity.

title: Helsinki Breaking Lines Semi Opposed
instructions_setup: In this drill, a central midfielder receives a pass and must control it with a precise first touch. Their second touch is a pass into one of three mini goals positioned ahead. While the player is unopposed in receiving and controlling the ball, there are two defenders positioned to protect and block the three mini goals, creating an obstacle to find and break the defensive lines with accurate passing. This setup encourages sharp decision-making and improves the ability to identify and exploit passing lanes under simulated pressure.The midfielder must focus on quick ball control and accurate distribution to successfully penetrate the defended zones. The defenders’ positioning challenges the passer to read the game and select the best passing option, emphasizing spatial awareness and timing.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize a clean, controlled first touch to set up an accurate second pass – This allows the player to quickly prepare for the pass and exploit the gaps between defenders more effectively.• Encourage scanning of the mini goal options before receiving the ball – Early awareness helps in quicker decision-making and reduces hesitation when under pressure.• Stress precise, well-weighted passes into the mini goals to beat the defenders – Accuracy here is crucial to successfully breaking the defensive lines and maintaining possession.• Promote calmness and composure when executing passes near the defended goals – Helps players remain confident and make smart choices under simulated defensive pressure.
progression_one: Passive Defensive PressureIntroduce light but consistent pressure from the defenders during the midfielder’s first touch to simulate more realistic game pressure and force quicker decisions.Focus: Develop ball control and passing precision while coping with increased defensive challenge and limited space.

title: Helsinki Central Penetration & Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on quick combination play and precise finishing involving an attacking midfielder and a striker. The attacking midfielder receives a pass from the wide area and must play a first-time pass through mannequins positioned centrally. The onrushing striker times their run to meet the pass and take a controlled shot to score. The practice is mirrored with two teams working simultaneously, one attacking up the grid and the other down, allowing repetition and flow without interruption, which helps players build confidence and sharpen attacking instincts under consistent practice conditions.The drill develops timing, vision, passing accuracy, and clinical finishing, preparing players for sharp attacking movements in game situations. Players learn to improve coordination and awareness, enhancing their ability to perform under pressure in competitive matches.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp, accurate first-time passing through tight gaps between mannequins – This encourages quick ball movement and vision in congested attacking areas.• Encourage precise timing of the striker’s run to connect effectively with the pass – Well-timed runs increase scoring chances and reduce offside risks.• Stress controlled shooting with composure immediately after receiving the pass – Players should focus on accuracy and calm execution in front of goal.• Highlight the importance of communication and eye contact betw
progression_one: Active Defensive PressureAdd active defenders who press both the attacking midfielder and striker. The midfielder must find quicker, smarter passing lanes, and the striker must adjust runs to lose markers and create shooting chances under pressure.Focus: Develop technical skill under pressure, enhance movement off the ball, and improve composure when finishing against defenders actively disrupting play.

title: Helsinki Dummy, Set & Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill focuses on movement, combination play, and crossing. The pattern begins with a central dummy receiver who checks short, lets the ball run past, then spins to receive a set pass from the next supporting player. After controlling the set pass, they immediately play it wide to a winger who has timed their run. The winger drives forward and delivers a cross into the box for two onrushing attackers to finish.The sequence flows continuously with players rotating roles, encouraging fluid movement and rhythm. This drill enhances timing, finishing technique, and coordination between central and wide players in attacking scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Focus on the dummy receiver's movement and timing – Sharp changes of direction create realistic match-day separation from defenders and disrupt defensive lines.• Emphasize accuracy and weight of the set pass – The pass must allow the receiver to play forward quickly, staying composed under pressure when executing.• Encourage wingers to deliver early, driven crosses – Low or whipped deliveries increase finishing opportunities and simulate realistic match tempo and final-third urgency.• Urge attackers to time their runs across defenders – Arriving in sync with the cross helps with clean contact and goal-scoring chances in crowded penalty areas.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender in the BoxIntroduce a passive defender to increase awareness and movement from attackers during the finishing phase.Focus: Improve attackers' timing, positioning, and adjustment to defensive presence while still maintaining finishing quality under tighter pressure.
progression_two: Vary the Cross Type and Delivery AreaWingers must deliver different types of crosses (cutbacks, early inswingers, or deep far-post balls), challenging attackers to adapt.Focus: Develop versatility in attacking runs and finishing techniques based on the type and angle of delivery received from different zones.

title: Helsinki One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 finishing drill is designed to sharpen a player’s movement, finishing variety, and composure in and around the penalty area. The player completes four finishes by collecting a ball from four different positions along the edge of the box. After each finish, they must sprint toward the centre circle, where the coach plays a pass for a first-time finish into a mini goal—replicating a realistic set-pass scenario under fatigue and movement.
coaching_notes: • Time the Approach and Finish With Precision – Adjust stride and body shape when approaching each ball to strike with balance and clean contact.• Stay Mentally Sharp Between Phases of the Drill – Quickly refocus after each action to execute the next with clarity and purpose.• Adjust Foot Position When Finishing From Different Angles – Use varied finishing techniques to match the position of the ball and your body.• Attack the Ball Early for Set-Pass Finishes – Anticipate the coach’s pass and meet the ball in stride for a clean first-time strike.
progression_one: Add Pressure With Time ConstraintsIntroduce a countdown or stopwatch to complete all four finishes within a set time frame to increase urgency and decision speed.Focus:Improves efficiency, movement quality, and composure under game-like time pressure.
progression_two: Vary the Type of Set Pass From CoachMix driven, lofted, and bouncing passes for the mini goal finishes to challenge first-time technique and reaction timing.Focus:Develops adaptability, first-touch decision-making, and quick foot preparation under pressure.

title: Helsinki SAQ & Reactions
instructions_setup: This dynamic SAQ and reactions drill is designed to enhance explosive movement, quick directional changes, and sharp reaction timing. Players begin standing opposite a coach or server. On a visual or verbal signal, they must react instantly by working quickly over a set of mini hurdles placed in front of them, focusing on light, rapid footwork.After clearing the hurdles, players immediately burst into a short sprint zone, where two cones force them to make two sharp changes of direction. The drill finishes with a final 5–10m sprint to complete the movement pattern before jogging back to reset. This is repeated at high intensity in short bursts.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp reactions to the initial signal – Players must stay focused and alert, reacting instantly to replicate unpredictable match scenarios.• Promote light, fast feet over the hurdles – Keep knees low and posture upright to maximize foot speed, control, and coordination across all steps.• Focus on posture and body shape through turns – Players should stay low with tight foot placement to support clean, explosive changes of direction efficiently.• Encourage a powerful final sprint phase – Sprinting technique should stay strong after fatigue, with arms driving and head forward through the finish.
progression_one: Add a Ball Carry After Final SprintAfter the final change of direction, players collect a ball and dribble quickly into a designated target zone to finish.Focus: Improve transitional speed while introducing control under fatigue and pressure, simulating quick attacking transitions in match situations.
progression_two: Add a Reactive Directional Cue at First ConeThe coach points left or right after the hurdles, dictating the player's first change of direction off the sprint.Focus: Sharpen cognitive processing, reaction speed, and agility by forcing spontaneous movement decisions after initial footwork activation.

title: Helsinki Y Passing & SAQ
instructions_setup: This drill develops quick, accurate passing combined with explosive speed and agility. Players start at the base of the Y and execute passes along the arms of the Y shape to activate sharp passing skills and quick decision-making. After the final pass at the top of the Y, players immediately perform a short SAQ (Speed, Agility, Quickness) ladder drill to boost footwork and acceleration. Upon completing the ladder work, players quickly return to the starting position to repeat the sequence. This blend of technical passing and dynamic movement enhances coordination and physical responsiveness in game-like scenarios.Players are trained to maintain precision and composure during passing while developing rapid foot speed and body control, both essential for high-tempo match situations. The drill also emphasizes timing and spatial awareness throughout the passing pattern and physical activation.
coaching_notes: • Focus on crisp, accurate passes with proper weight and timing – This ensures the ball reaches teammates quickly and under control, maintaining the flow and tempo of the drill.• Encourage quick, controlled first touches to set up the next pass efficiently – Players should prepare their body position early to maintain fluidity and minimize delays.• Stress sharp SAQ ladder footwork emphasizing high knees and quick ground contact – Enhances explosive acceleration and improves neuromuscular coordination essential for dynamic play.• Promote constant communication and eye contact between players – Improves anticipation and awareness, helping players adjust their timing and positioning proactively.
progression_one: Increased Passing SpeedPlayers increase the pace of passes along the Y pattern while maintaining accuracy and composure under faster tempo.Focus: Enhance decision-making speed and passing precision under quicker, more demanding conditions.

title: Inter 3v2 with Transitions
instructions_setup: The drill begins with a 3v2 attacking phase, where the attacking team of three players aims to break down the defensive team of two and attempt to score. Once the 3v2 attacking phase concludes, the attacking players must quickly transition to defense. They must sprint back to the halfway line to defend against a fixed player who will immediately attack them as soon as the attacking phase finishes.The goal is to develop both attacking and defensive transitions, emphasizing speed, decision-making, and the ability to quickly shift focus between attacking and defending roles.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Phase Focus: The 3 attackers should focus on quick ball movement, creating angles, and combining efficiently to break down the 2 defenders. The aim is to finish quickly and decisively once an opportunity arises.• Transition to Defense: After the attacking phase, the 3 players must transition immediately to defense. Speed is key in recovering ground and ensuring that the defending 1v1 is contested effectively.• Defending 1v1: Once the transition happens, the defenders must be quick to close down the ball, keep their body shape between the attacker and goal, and force the attacking player wide to limit shooting options.• Communication: Players need to communicate effectively when transitioning. The defenders must call for help if they are overloaded or need to track a player back into position.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit to the attacking phase (e.g., 10-15 seconds). This encourages urgency in the attacking team to create and finish chances quickly while also training the defenders to react faster during the transition phase.Focus: Creates a sense of urgency, simulating game situations where quick transitions are critical.

title: Inter Build Up Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed practice focuses on playing out from the back in a structured, fluid manner. 11 players are positioned on the pitch, with the goalkeeper remaining fixed in their position. The practice starts with the goalkeeper playing the ball to the defenders, who then work through a variety of build-up patterns, progressing the ball up the field towards the forwards. Once the ball reaches the forwards, the team circulates the ball back down the other side, returning to the goalkeeper.Players are encouraged to follow every pass, constantly moving and shifting the formation to support the ball. This helps develop a full-team understanding of building possession from the back to the attacking third, emphasizing movement, spacing, and fluidity.
coaching_notes: • Ball Movement: Players should focus on quick, accurate passing with minimal touches. The aim is to keep the ball flowing up the field, using short and long passes effectively to create space.• Player Movement: After each pass, players must move to support the ball, providing options to maintain possession and facilitate the next pass. Constant movement is key for breaking defensive lines.• Building from the Back: Defenders and midfielders should work on playing through tight spaces and finding angles to progress the ball forward. This includes making quick passes to feet and anticipating where the ball will go next.• Role of the Goalkeeper: The goalkeeper plays a key role in the build-up, distributing the ball with precision to set up attacks. The goalkeeper must communicate with the team to ensure smooth transitions from defense to attack.
progression_one: Add Pressure:Introduce light, semi-opposed pressure from a few defenders at key stages (e.g., after the ball is played to the midfielders). This will challenge players to deal with the pressure and test their ability to maintain possession while progressing up the field.Focus: Encourages players to improve decision-making and ball control under pressure, making the drill more game-realistic.

title: Inter Build Up SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is designed to encourage building up through the central zone and exploiting the half spaces on either side of the field. The pitch is divided into three zones: a large central zone and two narrow channels on either side, replicating the half spaces. Teams are set up to play a 5v5 game, with the objective of progressing the ball centrally into the two mini goals located on their side of the grid, which are positioned in the half-space channels. Each side has two mini goals, creating multiple attacking options.The focus of the game is to use the central area for ball progression and then exploit the half spaces to create scoring opportunities. This practice helps improve attacking play in tight spaces, encouraging creativity and awareness of positioning in the final third.
coaching_notes: • Building Up Play: Players should focus on playing out from the back, using the central zone to maintain possession and create passing lanes. Encouraging good movement off the ball is key to progress the ball through the midfield and into the attacking zones.• Exploiting the Half Spaces: The half-space channels should be used effectively to create overloads and open up passing lanes for the forwards. Players need to be aware of these spaces and look to receive and play passes into them to advance the attack.• Decision-Making: Encourage players to make quick decisions in the final third, either playing a through ball or crossing into the mini goals in the half-space channels. Quick and accurate passing is essential to break down the defense.• Defensive Shape: Defenders should focus on cutting off passing lanes into the half-space channels and be aware of the attackers' positioning. They should force the opposition to play wide or make difficult passes through the central zone.
progression_one: Restrict Passes:Limit the number of passes a team can make in the central zone before they must play into one of the half-space channels. This encourages quicker play and the need to transition the ball into the final third more efficiently.Focus: This progression emphasizes faster transitions and maintaining attacking pressure.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player in one of the half-space channels who always plays for the attacking team. This player can help maintain possession and create an overload in the attacking half, encouraging better use of the space.Focus: This progression allows teams to focus on using the half-space more effectively and creating overloads to break through the defense.

title: Inter Conditioning & Finish
instructions_setup: In this drill, two teams of two work on attacking and finishing, while incorporating fitness through sprints. Play starts with the first team attacking one of the goals, receiving a cross and attempting to score. Once the shot is taken, the players must immediately sprint 30 yards to the opposite side of the field. Upon arrival, they will then attempt to score in the opposite goal after receiving another cross. This cycle is repeated, creating a continuous loop of fitness and finishing work.The drill is designed to help players improve their finishing ability while also focusing on their endurance, speed, and ability to recover quickly. The intensity of the drill increases as players continue to alternate between attacking and sprinting.
coaching_notes: • Timing the Runs: Players must time their runs correctly to meet the crosses in dangerous positions. Encourage good communication between the player delivering the cross and the one attacking the goal.• Finishing Under Pressure: Players should focus on finishing quickly and accurately, especially after sprinting long distances. Quick reactions are important to score before the defenders can recover.• Sprinting Recovery: The sprint back after finishing should be done at maximum effort, ensuring players recover and maintain a high level of intensity throughout the drill.• Cross Accuracy: Players delivering the crosses should focus on providing accurate balls into the box, with variation in height and timing to challenge the attackers.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce a defender in the box to pressure the attackers during the finishing phase. This adds a layer of challenge, forcing players to finish under pressure while maintaining the intensity of the drill.Focus: This progression enhances both fitness and decision-making under pressure, simulating match-like conditions.
progression_two: Increase Sprint Distance:Increase the sprint distance to 40 or 50 yards, depending on the fitness level of the players. This longer sprint will further challenge the players’ stamina and speed, requiring them to recover more efficiently between attacks.Focus: This progression helps improve fitness levels while maintaining finishing accuracy under fatigue.

title: Inter Finish into Counter
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing quick attacking combinations and transition play. The drill begins with two attackers performing a 1-2 combination to create an unopposed finishing opportunity. Once the finish is completed, the two players positioned at the top of the grid immediately transition into a counter-attacking phase, taking advantage of the unbalanced defenders who must quickly transition after the finish.The emphasis is on the speed and accuracy of the combination play, along with the attackers’ ability to exploit the space and capitalize on the defenders’ lack of balance after the finish.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combination Play: The two attacking players should aim to move quickly, playing sharp passes to execute the 1-2 combination. Timing is crucial to create the best angle for a clean finish.• Finishing with Composure: After the 1-2, the finishing player should focus on maintaining composure and accuracy, finishing efficiently into the open goal. Encouraging quick, calm finishing after a fast move is key.• Transition to Defense: Once the finish is made, the defenders must quickly transition into counter-attacking mode. Encourage quick, decisive movements from the defenders to prevent any easy goals during the counter phase.• Attacking Decision-Making: The two players initiating the counter must decide whether to use their numbers advantage effectively, looking for a quick shot or a pass into space for the most dangerous attacking position.
progression_one: Limit Counter Attack Time:Set a time limit (e.g., 10 seconds) for the counter-attack after the finish. This forces defenders to transition quickly, creating more urgency in the drill. Attackers must also work efficiently to exploit the unbalanced defense before they recover.Focus: This progression enhances speed of play and quick thinking during both the attacking and defending phases.

title: Inter Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness drill combines attacking play with recovery runs, designed to improve both offensive and defensive transition speed. The drill begins with a pass into the attacker, and immediately, two defenders must react and make recovery runs to stop a 1v1 situation. The attacker is only allowed to finish once they have reached the box, which ensures that the defenders have time to recover and challenge the attack.The main focus is on improving the defenders’ ability to recover quickly and the attackers’ ability to capitalize on the 1v1 opportunity.
coaching_notes: • Recovery Runs: The defenders must quickly react and sprint back to cover the attacker. Focus on explosive movement and sprinting efficiency to close the space quickly and put pressure on the attacker before they reach the box.• Attacker's Composure: The attacker should stay composed while approaching the goal. Once inside the box, they should aim for a well-placed shot, taking into account the time spent closing the distance and the defending pressure.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Both attackers and defenders must make quick decisions under pressure. Attackers should assess the situation and determine whether to shoot early or dribble, while defenders must decide how to close down the space effectively.• Communication: Encourage the defenders to communicate with each other during the recovery runs to avoid confusion, while the attacker should focus on making quick, smart decisions.
progression_one: Add Extra Attacker:Introduce a second attacker to the situation. The defenders now face a 2v1 situation in the box, which increases the attacking pressure and requires the defenders to focus on tactical positioning and communication in recovery.Focus: This progression enhances defenders' ability to recover while

title: Inter Free Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed free kick routine drill is designed to help players rehearse and refine various attacking free kick patterns from wide or central areas. The team will focus on the key components of a successful set-piece routine including delivery, movement, and timing. Players will position themselves according to the selected routine (e.g., near post runs, edge of the box setups, far post overloads) and execute planned movements without opposition.The free kick taker will deliver the ball into a designated area, aiming for the appropriate target zone based on the play design. Meanwhile, attacking players will make synchronized runs to either meet the delivery or create decoy movements to free up teammates. This unopposed format allows the team to work on precise timing and technical execution without the distraction of defenders.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing & Synchronization:Attackers must time their runs perfectly in relation to the free kick taker’s delivery. Runs should be coordinated so that the ball is met at the optimal point, with staggered timing to create different attacking options.• Varied Movements:Players should rehearse a variety of runs including curved runs, late arrivals at the far post, and quick darts into central zones. Decoy runs and quick direction changes are essential to unsettle defenders in real match scenarios.• Delivery Execution:The free kick taker should focus on consistent and accurate delivery, using different techniques such as whipped, floated, or driven balls based on the routine. The quality of the ball into the target area is crucial to the success of the routine.• Role Clarity:Ensure every player knows their specific job in the routine — whether it’s to attack the ball, screen a defender, make a decoy run, or be in position for a second ball. Clarity in roles improves execution and reduces hesitation.• Communication:Strong verbal and non-verbal communication is essential between the free kick taker and the runners. Agreed cues or signals should trigger the movement so that everyone is synced to the delivery.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to lightly mark the runners and challenge aerially. Their role is to track movements and apply mild resistance without aggressively disrupting play.Focus: This adds realism and forces the attacking team to fine-tune timing and positioning under game-like conditions while still maintaining the structure of the routine.

title: Inter Individual Mastery
instructions_setup: This individual mastery drill focuses on improving dribbling, change of direction speed, and forward passing. The player begins with the ball and the coach (or a second player) will call out a color. The player with the ball must then travel vertically up the grid, weaving around every cone of the selected color. The drill is designed to enhance dribbling skills and the ability to make quick directional changes while maintaining control of the ball.As the player approaches the final cone, they will be required to pass the ball forward to a target or to a designated player, promoting the connection between individual dribbling and game-related passing.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Technique: Emphasize using the correct foot for dribbling, with close ball control. Players should use both feet and keep the ball under control while weaving around the cones, ensuring that they are not rushing but maintaining effective dribbling speed.• Change of Direction: Focus on quick, sharp changes of direction when approaching each cone. Encourage players to make quick cuts and accelerate immediately after each turn to improve their speed and agility.• Forward Passing: After completing the dribbling portion, the player should transition smoothly into a forward pass, maintaining good passing technique. Players should focus on the timing of their pass and the accuracy of the delivery, ideally aiming for a target or player in motion.• Awareness and Focus: As players move through the drill, they should stay alert and focused on the coach's calls, responding quickly and efficiently to changes in direction.
progression_one: Introduce a Defender:Introduce a defender to challenge the player’s dribbling. The defender's task is to prevent the player from reaching the final cone. The player must still complete the drill, now having to beat the defender with changes of direction or quick acceleration.Focus: This progression helps improve players' ability to maintain control while under pressure, and to make decisions quickly when facing a defender.
progression_two: Vary the Passing Target:Change the passing target after the dribbling portion. Instead of a single target, have multiple passing options available. This forces the player to scan the field and make a more tactical decision about where to pass after completing the dribble.Focus: This progression develops decision-making and situational awareness when transitioning from dribbling to passing.

title: Inter Into the Path Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing drill focuses on movement off the ball and finishing under minimal pressure. The drill setup involves 4 poles, with 3 of them occupied and 2 goals positioned at opposite ends of the grid. The drill begins when a player moves from an occupied pole to the vacant one. Upon reaching the vacant pole, the player receives a pass and takes an unopposed shot on goal. Once the finish is completed, the pattern continues, with the next vacant pole being filled and the process repeating.This drill encourages players to make intelligent runs off the ball, timing their movements to receive the pass in an ideal position for a clean shot on goal.
coaching_notes: • Movement Off the Ball: Encourage players to make dynamic, purposeful runs towards the vacant pole. Timing and positioning are key for receiving the ball in a goal-scoring area. Players should work on their anticipation to ensure they arrive at the pole in sync with the pass.• Finishing Technique: Focus on quick, composed finishing with both feet. Players should aim to hit the target regardless of the angle, ensuring they keep the shot low and focused on placement over power. Encourage players to finish with calmness, aiming for the corners of the goal.• Passing and Timing: Emphasize the importance of accurate and timed passes. The player delivering the ball should focus on precision and speed to ensure that the receiving player is in a good position to shoot. The player receiving the pass should focus on controlling it and getting the shot off quickly.• Decision Making: Players should practice different types of finishes, whether it's a driven shot, a finesse shot, or a first-time strike, depending on the scenario. Encourage players to recognize when to shoot early and when to take a touch to set up a better angle.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender into the drill who starts a few yards away from the shooter. The defender's role is to apply light pressure, forcing the attacking player to be quicker with their decision-making and finishing.Focus: This progression simulates real-game pressure, encouraging players to get the shot off quickly while adjusting to defensive pressure.

title: Inter Passing & Dribbling
instructions_setup: This passing and dribbling mastery practice focuses on developing close control, dribbling techniques, and passing accuracy. The setup involves 8 stations placed on the outside of a grid, with 4 cones in the center. Players will alternate between dribbling through the center cones and passing around the outside stations. The combination of these tasks enhances players' ability to maintain possession, execute quick passes, and change direction effectively while keeping control of the ball.The focus is on improving both technical and decision-making skills by integrating dribbling and passing in a dynamic environment. Players should work on their ability to execute quick turns, changes of direction, and accurate passes under minimal pressure.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Control: Players should focus on maintaining close control of the ball while navigating through the central cones. Encourage players to use both feet and perform various turns, such as the inside/outside cuts and pullbacks, to enhance their dribbling skills. Emphasize the importance of staying low to the ground and using small touches to keep the ball close.• Passing Accuracy: When passing around the outside stations, players should focus on delivering crisp, accurate passes to their teammates. The emphasis should be on using both feet to make quick passes, ensuring that the ball reaches its target accurately and without unnecessary force. Players should also work on passing with proper timing and weight to facilitate smooth transitions.• Awareness and Timing: Encourage players to keep their heads up, scanning the area around them for both passing options and space to dribble. Players should make quick decisions about when to dribble and when to pass, incorporating fluid transitions between the two.• Body Positioning: While dribbling, players should maintain proper body positioning to shield the ball from imaginary defenders. Encourage them to use their body to protect the ball while setting up for the next move, whether it's a pass or a change of direction.
progression_one: Two-Ball Combination:Introduce a second ball into the practice, where players must dribble through the center cones with one ball while simultaneously passing the other ball around the outside stations. This will require players to manage both tasks simultaneously, improving multitasking and awareness.Focus: This progression challenges players to multitask and improve their focus, ensuring that they can execute both dribbling and passing skills at the same time.

title: Inter Penetrate & Counter Press
instructions_setup: This possession-based drill encourages players to recognize and execute penetrative passes under pressure. The setup involves 6 attacking players aiming to retain possession while being pressed by 3 defenders. A central triangle is marked out within the grid, and the team in possession is rewarded with a point every time they successfully play a pass through the triangle.The defenders are incentivized to win possession and are rewarded with 3 points if they can score into any of the 4 mini goals located at the corners of the grid. This dual scoring system motivates both the attackers to break lines and the defenders to transition quickly.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Split Passes: Players should actively look for opportunities to split defenders with passes through the central triangle. Emphasize body positioning and passing angles to break lines effectively.• Support Behind the Ball: Ensure supporting players are positioned intelligently to recycle possession if forward options are closed off. Movement off the ball is key to creating new passing lanes.• High Tempo Play: Encourage quick, sharp ball movement to create disorganization in the defending team. One- and two-touch play can help maintain rhythm and speed of play.• Defensive Transitions: Defenders must react quickly upon winning possession. They should immediately look to exploit disorganization and score into the mini goals within a few seconds.
progression_one: Limit Touches:Reduce the number of touches allowed for the team in possession (e.g., max 2-touch). This increases the tempo of play and forces quicker decision-making under pressure.Focus: Enhances speed of play and forces players to think one step ahead when receiving the ball.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player inside or outside the triangle who always plays with the team in possession. This adds an extra outlet and encourages better use of overloads and switching play.Focus: Helps players recognize when and how to use numerical advantages to penetrate the defensive block.

title: Inter SAQ & Warm Up
instructions_setup: This warm-up and SAQ (Speed, Agility, Quickness) drill is designed to sharpen reaction time and improve decision-making. Two players are involved per rep—one positioned at the top and the other at the bottom. The top player is always the decision-maker, initiating the movement, while the bottom player must react to their actions.Various variations can be used to challenge players both physically and cognitively. Movements include mirroring in the same or opposite direction, circling a central pole, and sprinting through designated gates, all of which demand focus, fast feet, and sharp reactions.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Sharp Movement: Encourage players to stay light on their feet and explode into movement as soon as the cue is given.• Body Shape Matters: Reinforce staying in an athletic stance to allow quicker transitions and faster reactions to directional cues.• Cognitive Engagement: Push the decision-maker to be unpredictable and switch up their movement pattern to truly challenge the reacting player.• Consistency & Recovery: Ensure high intensity for each rep, with adequate rest between sets to maintain quality output and avoid fatigue.
progression_one: Use Visual or Verbal Cues:Instead of physical movement from the decision-maker, introduce external cues such as colored cones, hand signals, or verbal commands to initiate the reaction.Focus: Enhances reaction time and focus under less predictable conditions.
progression_two: Add Ball Movement:Include a football in the decision-making process. The top player can dribble in one direction or perform a skill move before sprinting, and the reacting player must mirror or chase.Focus: Combines technical ability with agility and awareness.

title: Inter Switch of Play Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo is designed to develop quick and intelligent switches of play in possession. The game begins with a 3v1 in one area of the grid while two additional defenders are positioned to screen the central zone. Possession players must complete a set number of passes (e.g., 5) before attempting to switch play to the opposite side.Switches can be made in two ways—via the wide unopposed players for 1 point, or through the central zone for more points due to the difficulty and risk involved. This setup encourages decision-making, timing, and awareness of space and pressure.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Patience & Tempo: Players should maintain good tempo while waiting for the right moment to switch play.• Scan for Options Constantly: Players must be scanning both wide and central options, weighing up risk versus reward on each pass.• Reward the Risk: Reinforce the value of switching through the center by highlighting how it can break defensive structures when timed well.• Quick Transitions Post-Switch: Encourage immediate speed and movement after a successful switch to take advantage of unbalanced defenders.
progression_one: Limit Touches:Restrict all players to 2 touches to increase difficulty and encourage quicker decision-making.Focus: Improves technical sharpness and forces rapid scanning and passing decisions.

title: Istanbul Breaking Lines Into 2v1
instructions_setup: This 2v1 attacking drill begins with an attacker playing a forward, line-breaking diagonal pass into a teammate positioned higher up the pitch. After making the pass, the first attacker makes a supporting forward run to join the receiver, instantly creating a 2v1 scenario. The pair then look to combine quickly and attack the goal at speed.The objective is to exploit the temporary overload and finish the attack by using intelligent movement, quick decision-making, and sharp execution. The defender starts deeper and must react quickly to recover and delay the attack, adding a game-realistic transition element to the exercise.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise Quality and Weight of Diagonal Pass – The first pass must break a line and arrive with enough pace and direction to set up the attacking movement properly and give the receiver time.• Encourage Early Recognition of Overload Options – Players must quickly read the situation to decide between passing, dribbling, or combining to maximize the advantage and create a high-quality chance.• Stress Timing and Angle of Supporting Run – The initial passer must time their run perfectly and choose a clever supporting angle to maintain the 2v1 advantage and keep the defender guessing.• Promote Speed and Purpose in Final Third Attacks – The combination and finish should be carried out with tempo, accuracy, and minimal touches to replicate game-like transitional moments and fast attacking play.
progression_one: Defender Starts Closer to ReceiverAdjust the starting position of the defender so they are positioned closer to the second attacker, increasing pressure on the pass and forcing quicker decisions from the attacking pair.Focus: Develops decision-making speed, sharpness in movement, and ability to play under tighter conditions that mirror match-day pressure more accurately.
progression_two: Add a Recovering Defender from BehindIntroduce a trailing defender who begins behind the attacker who plays the diagonal pass and recovers after the pass is played, creating a 2v2 under pressure as the attack develops.Focus: Trains attacking players to execute fast combinations while under pressure and helps improve awareness of recovering defenders in dynamic attacking transitions.

title: Istanbul Build Up to Emergency Defending
instructions_setup: This practice starts with the goalkeeper initiating play by passing to one of two defenders. The defender then plays a forward pass intended to reach two attackers who enter a 2v2 attacking phase. The forward pass simulates a risky or misplaced ball that results in a potential loss of possession, requiring the defenders to immediately transition from building out to urgent defending.The defenders must react quickly to the turnover, shifting mindset instantly from offense to defense with intensity and focus. This drill trains players to recognize when possession is lost and react under pressure to contain and regain the ball in a high-tempo defensive situation.
coaching_notes: • Stress the Importance of Accurate Passing from the Goalkeeper to Defenders – Good initial distribution is key to building play but also sets up the scenario for quick transitions if possession is lost.• Encourage Sharp, Decisive Forward Passing by Defenders – The forward pass should be purposeful, but players must understand the risk and be prepared to defend immediately if possession is lost.• Reinforce Urgency and Communication in Defensive Transition – Defenders need to quickly organize, press, and cover space with strong communication to limit the attackers’ options.• Promote Mental Readiness for Sudden Turnovers – Players must anticipate the switch from build-up to defending, keeping alert and maintaining intensity throughout the drill.
progression_one: Add an Additional Attacker in the 2v2 PhaseIncrease the attacking numbers to 3v2 after the forward pass, forcing defenders to work harder in recovery and defensive positioning.Focus: Develops defenders’ ability to stay compact and communicate effectively under increased pressure and numerical disadvantage.

title: Istanbul Defending Crosses 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving individual defensive skills for full backs in wide defensive areas, particularly when defending crosses. The full back will face a winger in a 1v1 situation positioned at the edge side of the penalty box. The winger’s objective is to use skill, speed, and movement to create separation from the defender and deliver an effective cross into the box. Inside the box, two mini goals are positioned where attackers would typically arrive, giving the winger a clear target to aim for.The full back must work on positioning, timing, and decision-making to prevent the winger from getting a quality cross. This drill encourages defenders to maintain close marking and anticipate the winger’s actions, while also building confidence in dealing with crossing situations under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Proper Defensive Body Positioning and Angling – The defender must stay balanced and use body shape to force the winger away from dangerous crossing positions.• Encourage Close Marking and Timing of Tackles – The full back should maintain tight marking without diving in too early, focusing on winning the ball cleanly or forcing a poor cross.• Promote Anticipation of the Winger’s Movement and Cross Timing – Reading the winger’s intentions allows the defender to be proactive in blocking or intercepting crosses.• Stress Recovery Speed and Aggression in 1v1 Defensive Duels – If beaten, the defender needs to recover quickly and apply pressure to disrupt the winger’s crossing rhythm.
progression_one: Increase the Winger’s Options by Adding an Additional Attacker in the BoxAdd a second attacker making runs into the box alongside the winger’s cross to increase complexity and challenge the defender’s decision-making and positioning.Focus: Enhances defender’s ability to track multiple attacking threats and adapt to more dynamic crossing situations.

title: Istanbul Fast Paced 3v2s
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to develop quick combination play and decision-making in tight attacking situations. Inside a 20x25 yard grid, three attackers will drive forward and use precise, coordinated passing and movement to bypass two defenders positioned centrally.
