Once successful, the attackers must deliver a direct pass to the end line ahead, connecting with the next trio of attackers who will immediately work their way back down the grid, maintaining constant attacking pressure.The drill is continuous and fast-paced, with rapid transitions between attack and defense. The two defenders also switch quickly, utilizing designated zones on the left and right sides of the grid to ensure smooth and efficient defender changeovers, encouraging sharp communication and awareness from all players.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Sharp, Timely Combination Play by Attackers – Players must use quick, accurate passing and intelligent movement to outmaneuver defenders in tight spaces.• Stress Effective Communication and Awareness Among Defenders – Defenders should coordinate closely to maintain their defensive shape and execute smooth, rapid changeovers during transitions.• Promote Quick Decision-Making During Transitions – Attackers need to maintain focus to quickly link up with the next group and keep the momentum going without hesitation.• Focus on Maintaining High Intensity and Tempo – The continuous nature of the drill requires players to sustain energy and concentration throughout, simulating real-game pressing and counter-pressing demands.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Bypass DefendersSet a maximum time for attackers to get past the two defenders, encouraging faster combinations and urgency in execution.Focus: Improves speed of play and ability to operate efficiently under time pressure in attacking scenarios.

title: Istanbul Half Space Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on finishing from crosses delivered into the box originating from the half-space. The winger initiates the move by driving aggressively down the line, drawing defenders and creating space. After reaching the byline, the winger cuts the ball back with a controlled pass to a deeper player—typically the full back—who is positioned to quickly deliver a first-time cross into the penalty area. Two attackers make coordinated runs into the box, aiming to finish unopposed with clinical precision.The drill emphasizes timing, accurate crossing, and sharp movement inside the box, allowing attackers to practice finishing with minimal pressure but realistic attacking patterns. It also develops understanding between wide players and full backs in creating goal-scoring opportunities from wide and half-space areas.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Controlled, Penetrative Runs by the Winger – The winger should drive with pace but maintain close ball control to effectively draw defenders and create crossing opportunities.• Stress Crisp, First-Time Crossing by the Full Back – The full back must deliver accurate, well-weighted crosses early to catch defenders off guard and provide quality service for attackers.• Promote Coordinated and Timed Runs from Attackers – Attackers need to time their movement perfectly to meet the cross in dangerous areas with confident, composed finishes.• Focus on Composure and Variety in Finishing Techniques – Even unopposed, attackers should practice different finishing methods—volleys, headers, and first-time shots—to build adaptability in game scenarios.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender in the BoxIntroduce a defender shadowing the attackers to simulate pressure but without active contesting, encouraging attackers to improve decision-making and composure under mild pressure.Focus: Enhances attackers’ ability to find space and adjust finishing techniques with light defensive presence.
progression_two: Limit Time for Cross and FinishSet a time limit between the winger’s cutback and the attackers’ finish, encouraging quicker decision-making and execution.Focus: Develops players’ speed of play and sharpness in attacking phases, simulating fast-paced match conditions.

title: Istanbul Positional Rondo to Finishing
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 4+3v4 possession rondo split across two adjacent grids. Each grid becomes a 4v2 scenario, with one of the three neutral players operating along the centre line and supporting possession in both zones. The focus in the rondo phase is on quick combinations, movement off the ball, and switching play through the neutral line player.Once the team in possession completes a set number of passes (e.g. 6–8), they are allowed to play a forward pass out of the rondo grid, penetrating beyond mannequins that represent a defensive line. An attacker makes a forward run to receive and finish unopposed on goal. If the four defenders win the ball during the rondo phase, they immediately switch roles with the other team of four players.
coaching_notes: • Reinforce Quick, Sharp Passing in Tight Spaces – Players must move the ball with speed and precision to maintain possession and manipulate the defenders’ shape to create openings.• Encourage Supportive Positioning from Neutral Players – The +3 players should constantly adjust their angles to offer passing options and help the ball travel across zones efficiently.• Emphasise the Timing of Penetration Beyond the Grid – The final pass and run must be well-timed to exploit space behind the mannequins and create a realistic chance on goal.• Promote Smooth Transition from Rondo to Attack – Once the target number of passes is completed, players should be alert and proactive in shifting mindset from possession to penetration and finishing.
progression_one: Add Passive Pressure on the FinisherIntroduce a passive defender in the finishing zone who tracks the attacker to simulate light pressure and force quicker decision-making during the finish.Focus: Enhances composure and shot selection under moderate pressure while maintaining the unopposed finishing structure of the drill.
progression_two: Restrict Time Between Pass Completion and Final BallOnce the required number of passes is hit, players have a 3-second window to play the penetrating pass and make the attacking run.Focus: Builds urgency and reaction speed following a successful rondo phase, mimicking moments where time and space to exploit the final third are limited.

title: Istanbul Possession & Penetrate SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is played as a 5v5 within a central grid, where players aim to dominate possession and work to break the defensive structure of the opposing team. On each end of the grid are four mannequins positioned across a line, creating narrow gates into a final zone. Beyond each line of mannequins is a goalkeeper and a full-sized goal.The aim is for teams to play through or around their opponents, using clever movement and sharp passing to penetrate past the mannequins. Once a successful pass is played through the mannequins, one attacker can run through unopposed into the final zone and finish past the goalkeeper.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Patience in Possession with Forward Intent – Players must circulate the ball intelligently while always looking for a moment to exploit space behind the mannequins and break lines effectively.• Emphasise Timing and Weight of Penetrative Passes – The through ball must be perfectly timed and well-weighted to meet the runner in stride and avoid interception or a loss of momentum.• Promote Constant Scanning and Off-Ball Movement – Encourage players to check shoulders, adjust body shape, and make blindside runs to create passing lanes that allow penetration.• Reinforce Sharp, Composed Finishing Under Minimal Pressure – Once in the finishing zone, the attacker should remain composed and focus on clean technique to beat the goalkeeper confidently.
progression_one: Add a Recovering Defender in the Final ZoneAfter a successful penetrating pass, allow one defender to recover and enter the final zone to apply late pressure to the attacker during the unopposed finish phase.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and calm finishing under pressure while rewarding well-timed passes and movement in the build-up phase.
progression_two: Limit Time on the Ball After PenetrationOnce an attacker enters the finishing zone, they have a 3-second time limit to shoot, encouraging rapid execution once behind the defensive line.Focus: Develops instinctive finishing, improves efficiency in front of goal, and mimics game-like moments where time and space are limited after penetrating passes.

title: Istanbul Technical Passing & Finishing
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill is designed to improve combination play, timing of movement, and accuracy in the final action. Players rotate through passing roles while working through various combination patterns that involve short passes, quick lay-offs, and movement off the ball. The drill ends with a pass into a mini goal, encouraging focus on end product.Throughout the practice, players should use different passing variations such as third-man runs, one-twos, and receiving on the back foot. After each pass, players follow their pass to the next position, maintaining the rhythm and rotation of the drill while staying alert to the next combination.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Timing and Sharpness of Movement – Players must time their runs precisely and stay connected to each action in the pattern to ensure fluidity and realism in the combination.• Encourage Clean, Accurate Forward Passes – Passes must be played with good weight and direction to allow the next player to play forward smoothly without breaking the tempo or flow.• Promote Use of Multiple Passing Variations – Include one-twos, third-man movements, disguise, and bounce passes to help players think ahead and apply variety under minimal pressure.• Stress Composure on Final Pass into Goal – Even in an unopposed setting, players should remain composed, focus on body shape, and play with precision to develop consistent end-product quality.
progression_one: Final Pass Must Be One-TouchThe final ball into the mini goal must be delivered first-time after the final combination, forcing players to set up the move earlier and communicate clearly.Focus: Enhances scanning, awareness, and early preparation of body shape to execute a clean one-touch final pass under time constraints.

title: Italy 1v1 & 2v2
instructions_setup: This dynamic transition drill begins with an unopposed finish from a wide area, giving the attacker a clean opportunity to score. Immediately after the shot, the same player must recover and defend a live 1v1 against a new attacker.Once that 1v1 is complete, the original attacker (who defended) transitions once more into a 2v2 attacking phase, joining forces with another player to attack and finish a second time. This drill develops finishing, recovery runs, 1v1 defending, and quick mental transitions between phases.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Recovery Runs: Stress the importance of turning quickly and sprinting back to defend with urgency after finishing.• Stay Mentally Switched On: Each phase requires a different mindset—players must adjust instantly between attacking and defending.• Use Body Position Effectively: In the 1v1, encourage defenders to stay side-on and guide attackers into less dangerous areas.• Combination Play in 2v2: Support attackers in creating angles and combining to beat defenders in the final phase.
progression_one: Add Passive Defender to Finishing Phase:Include a shadowing defender in the unopposed finish to simulate light pressure and increase the demand on the attacker.Focus: Enhances composure and decision-making under slight defensive pressure.
progression_two: Introduce Time Limits:Add a time limit to the 2v2 phase (e.g., 8 seconds) to encourage fast and purposeful play.Focus: Trains players to be direct and decisive in attacking transitions.

title: Italy 2 Player Mastery
instructions_setup: In this technical ball mastery drill, players work in pairs with one ball between them. The objective is to pass through as many coloured gates as possible while moving around the grid together. Each pair must remain mobile, constantly adjusting their position and spacing to find and play accurate passes through the various gates without repetition.This drill helps develop passing accuracy, communication, awareness, and movement off the ball, all while maintaining technical focus in a fun, competitive format.
coaching_notes: • Pass with precision and timing: Encourage players to focus on accurate passing with proper weight and timing to successfully play through each gate.• Keep moving as a pair: Players should constantly move and adjust their body positions to support each other and open up new passing angles.• Scan the field constantly: Emphasize head-up play and scanning to quickly identify which gates are free and how to position accordingly.• Use both feet and surfaces: Encourage players to use both feet and different surfaces (inside, outside) for improved technical variety and development.
progression_one: Add Defender in Central Area:Introduce a passive or active defender who can intercept passes if players get too close to the middle zone.Focus: Encourages better movement, positioning, and decision-making under pressure.

title: Italy Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: Play begins with two attacking players combining before initiating a 2v1 attacking phase on the top side of the grid. The focus here is on creating and exploiting the numerical advantage to generate a quality goal-scoring opportunity.Once this initial 2v1 is complete, the same two attackers quickly transition back to the original side of the grid, where a cross is delivered from a wide area. The attackers must time their runs and finish the chance, creating a second 2v1 attacking scenario—this time from a wide delivery.
coaching_notes: • Play combinations with speed and intent: Encourage quick one-touch or two-touch play to manipulate the defender and create space for a clean finish.• Exploit the overload quickly: Players should take initiative when in the 2v1, attacking decisively and choosing the right moment to pass or shoot.• Time movements for the cross: Both attackers must communicate and time their runs based on the crosser's body shape and delivery angle.• React and transition quickly: Reinforce the importance of high-intensity transitions between phases to mimic game speed and maintain attacking momentum.
progression_one: Passive to Active Defender on Cross:Start with a passive defender during the crossing phase, then gradually increase pressure with a fully active defender.Focus: Improves timing, awareness, and finishing under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Touches in Build-Up:Limit the attackers to a maximum of two touches in the combination phase before the 2v1.Focus: Develops quick decision-making and precise technical execution.

title: Italy Counter & Recovery
instructions_setup: This counter-attacking drill is designed to simulate a disorganised defensive setup, where the defenders are forced to recover after a misplaced pass. The drill begins with a forward pass from one of the defenders to an attacker, intentionally replicating a poor or misplaced pass. As soon as the ball is played, play becomes live, and the attacking players immediately transition to exploit the unbalanced defensive unit, focusing on creating a numerical advantage on the counter-attack.The aim is to develop fast, direct play and decision-making under pressure, making use of any gaps left by defenders who are out of position. The attacking team must take advantage of these moments to generate scoring opportunities.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Once the ball is played, encourage attackers to transition quickly from defence to attack. The emphasis should be on speed and urgency to exploit the disorganisation of the defensive team. Players should look to attack with purpose and use the space before defenders can recover.• Exploiting Gaps: Focus on attacking the spaces left by defenders who are caught out of position. Players should constantly scan the field for opportunities to exploit wide areas or gaps in the central defense, ensuring they make runs that stretch the opposition and create numerical superiority.• Decision Making: Attackers should practice making quick decisions about when to pass, dribble, or shoot. Players should understand when to play simple passes to progress the attack and when to take a riskier option to break down the defense.• Defensive Recovery: Defenders must be aware of the counter-attacking threat and work on recovering quickly. Encourage defenders to track runners, communicate effectively, and aim to reorganize their shape as quickly as possible to prevent goals on the counter.
progression_one: 2v1 Counter-Attack:Introduce a second defender into the drill, making it a 2v1 counter-attack. The attackers now have to make quicker decisions and work together to outplay the two defenders, creating an even more realistic scenario for quick decision-making in a counter-attack.Focus: This progression encourages attackers to work as a pair, developing combinations and timing their movements to break down the two defenders. It also improves defensive decision-making on how to handle an attacking overload.

title: Italy Crossing & Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed crossing and finishing drill takes place in a central area, encouraging players to combine centrally before finishing and then quickly transitioning to attack a wide cross. Two attackers work with two neutral players to create a central combination, leading to a first shot on goal. Immediately after the finish, the two attackers must react, turn, and attack a cross delivered from the opposite side, aiming for a second finish into the other goal.
coaching_notes: • Combination Detail – Focus on crisp, accurate passing and well-timed movement during the central combination to create space for the first finish.• Finishing Quality – Players should concentrate on clean, decisive finishes off the combination to simulate real goalscoring chances.• Reaction Speed – After the initial shot, encourage quick reactions to transition and attack the cross at pace.• Timing of Runs – Players must time their runs into the box when attacking the cross to arrive at the right moment for an effective finish.
progression_one: One-Touch Central CombinationPlayers are limited to one touch during the central combination, increasing the speed and sharpness of the build-up.Focus: Improving technical execution and tempo in tight spaces.
progression_two: Delayed CrossesThe wide player delays the cross by 1–2 seconds, forcing the attackers to adjust their movement and timing before attacking the delivery.Focus: Developing patience, reading the cross, and adjusting movement inside the box.

title: Italy High Press SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is designed to develop high pressing tactics. The pitch is divided with two lines on either side, creating a pressing zone. Teams must press aggressively in this area to regain possession.When a team wins possession inside the pressing zone and scores, they are awarded double goals. This drill challenges players to assess the risk-reward of pressing high and teaches them when it is most effective, balancing risk with timing.
coaching_notes: • Pressing Zone Awareness: Encourage players to recognize when to engage in high pressing within the designated zone. They should apply pressure quickly to force turnovers, but also understand when it’s best to hold back and avoid unnecessary risks.• Communication: Clear communication is vital for coordinating the press. Players should constantly call out for support, making sure the press is synchronized and organized to close down space efficiently.• Defensive Transition: When possession is regained, emphasize quick transitions from defense to attack. Players should look to exploit the open spaces created by the press, aiming to capitalize on counter-attacking opportunities.• Timing the Press: Teach players to judge the correct timing for engaging in high pressing. They should aim to trap opponents in the pressing zone and force mistakes, but be cautious not to press too early and leave gaps in defense.
progression_one: Add a Counter-Attack Option:Allow the defending team to play out to a designated counter-attacking area, where they can score a goal. This creates a balance between pressing high and being aware of counter-attacks.Focus: This progression encourages players to focus on the risk-reward factor, as they need to press high while considering the possibility of a counter-attack when they lose possession.
progression_two: Introduce a Goalkeeper in the Pressing Zone:Introduce a goalkeeper to the pressing zone. When possession is won in the pressing zone, the team must now finish with a shot on target, facing the goalkeeper.Focus: This progression sharpens finishing under pressure, combining the high pressing strategy with the added challenge of finishing against a goalkeeper under fast transition conditions.

title: Italy One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 technical drill is designed for central midfielders to work on receiving, scanning, ball manipulation, and decision-making. A square is marked out with four different coloured cones in each corner. As the coach passes into the square, they simultaneously call a colour. The midfielder must scan, receive the ball, dribble around the designated cone, and then play a pass back to the coach. Occasionally, the coach can shout “goal” instead of a colour, prompting the player to pass into one of two mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Constant Scanning Before and After Receiving – Maintain head movement to locate colour cues, space, and position of cones before the ball arrives.• Positive First Touch into Direction of Travel – Take the first touch toward the called colour to prepare for a clean dribble around the cone.• Controlled Dribbling with Head Up – Keep the ball close while moving at speed, staying aware of the coach’s voice for further instructions.• Pass Accuracy Off Both Feet – Deliver precise, well-weighted passes back to the coach or into the mini goal using either foot confidently.

title: Italy Overloaded Possession
instructions_setup: This possession practice encourages players to maintain and move possession while being overloaded. The setup involves 5 players in possession, with 5 bounce players positioned strategically – 4 in the corners and 1 at the center of the grid. The drill focuses on building quick, effective ball movement with support from extra players.The bounce players act as extra options, allowing the possession team to create a 10v5 when in possession. To increase the intensity and speed up play, the bounce players can be limited to a set number of touches, forcing the team to make quicker decisions and keep the tempo high.
coaching_notes: • Movement and Support: Players in possession should constantly look for options from the bounce players. Encourage them to move dynamically to create passing lanes, supporting each other for effective ball movement.• Quick Passing: Emphasize the importance of quick, accurate passes to maintain tempo. The bounce players must deliver fast, one-touch passes to maintain possession while avoiding defensive pressure.• Decision Making: Players must make quick decisions based on the pressure and positioning of defenders. Encourage players to scan the field before receiving the ball, allowing them to make quicker decisions when in possession.• Communication: Communication is key in a possession-based practice. Encourage players to talk and signal to each other, especially when coordinating with the bounce players for effective support.
progression_one: Touch Limit on Bounce Players:Introduce a touch limit for the bounce players (e.g., 1-2 touches per player). This forces the possession team to play quicker and create space to receive the ball.Focus: This progression encourages quicker ball circulation and decision-making under pressure, improving the pace of play.

title: Italy Switch of Play Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo is designed to develop quick switches of play, encouraging fast decision-making and ball circulation. Play starts as a 4v2 rondo on one side of the pitch, and after a set number of passes, the possession team can switch play through the central player positioned between the rondo grids. The focus is on maintaining possession while working the ball into an advantageous position for a switch.Players must transition quickly to the opposite grid to ensure there’s always a 4v2, as the opposite zone initially starts with just a 2v1. This means that after the switch, two attackers and one defender must move across to balance the numbers in the new grid.
coaching_notes: • Fast Ball Circulation: Encourage players to move the ball quickly to stretch the defenders and create passing lanes. The possession team should focus on making fast, accurate passes to maintain control and set up for the switch.• Timing the Switch: The switch of play should be well-timed to catch the defenders off guard. Players must look for the right moment to switch once they’ve achieved sufficient control on the initial side. The central player should make an early pass to start the transition.• Transitioning Quickly: Once the switch is made, players must quickly move across to ensure a numerical advantage. The attackers should be alert and sprint to the new grid, while the defenders should track their movement.• Communication: Effective communication is vital to coordinate the switch and ensure everyone is in position to maintain possession. Players should use verbal and non-verbal cues to indicate when to switch.
progression_one: Add a Third Defender:Introduce a third defender into the rondo. The additional defender increases the pressure on the possession team and forces them to make faster decisions and work harder to maintain possession and complete the switch.Focus: This progression challenges the possession team to deal with more defensive pressure while maintaining quick ball movement and effective switches.

title: Lazio 1v1 with SAQ & Finish
instructions_setup: In this 1v1 drill, players will start by racing around two poles, which helps to develop agility and speed. The player starting on the left side of the grid races around the poles before receiving a pass from the byline, with the objective of finishing on goal.As soon as the shot is taken, the player must quickly turn and transition to defend. The player starting on the right side of the grid will then sprint to receive a pass from outside the area, initiating a 1v1 scenario in which they will attempt to score against the transitioning defender.
coaching_notes: • Speed and Agility: Encourage players to focus on quick, explosive movement as they race around the poles. They should aim to generate speed with each turn, preparing themselves to receive the pass and take the shot on goal immediately.• Finishing Under Pressure: Players should focus on making quick, composed finishes under pressure. Whether it’s a driven shot or a controlled placement, the aim is to be efficient with the first touch and finish decisively.• Quick Transition: Emphasize the importance of transitioning quickly from attack to defense. After taking the shot, players need to react fast and adjust their positioning to prepare for the 1v1 defending situation.• Defending 1v1: Defenders should focus on closing down the attacker’s space while staying on their toes. Encourage defenders to remain balanced and control the distance between them and the attacker to force them into a less advantageous position.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender into the 1v1 scenario. This will force the attacker to make quicker decisions, either by passing or moving the ball to a better position, and challenge the defenders to work together to contain the attacking player.Focus: This progression will develop teamwork in defense while also improving the attacker’s decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Touches for Attackers:Limit the attacking player to a set number of touches (e.g., 1 or 2 touches). This will help speed up the play, forcing the attacker to make quicker decisions on their dribbling and shooting.Focus: This progression enhances the ability to make fast decisions and improves technical skills under time constraints, encouraging players to be more effective in tight situations.

title: Lazio 3rd Man Run & Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice focuses on developing 3rd man attacking combinations, allowing players to practice quick and effective link-up play in the final third. Play begins with a 3rd man combination, where one player plays a pass into a teammate who then makes a return pass to the original player. This player then delivers a wide pass into the box, where another player finishes off the play with a shot.The practice runs from bottom to top and then vice versa, utilizing the same two central players for the 3rd man combinations. These two players should ideally be your central midfielders, as they are often responsible for initiating and linking attacks in game situations. The setup includes two goals placed 40 yards apart to replicate match conditions and encourage high-intensity movements.
coaching_notes: • 3rd Man Movement: Emphasize the importance of intelligent runs off the ball. The player receiving the first pass should look to play a quick combination and immediately look for space to receive the return pass. This movement should be timed to perfection to ensure that the player receiving the ball is in a good position to cross or finish.• Wide Delivery: The player making the wide pass must focus on accuracy and timing. Encourage them to deliver the ball into a dangerous area, targeting the run of the attacking players in the box. The cross should be driven or floated depending on the position of the attackers.• Finishing Under Pressure: The two players in the box should focus on their finishing technique, aiming for composure under pressure. Encourage a variety of finishes, including volleys, headers, or first-time shots, to replicate real game scenarios.• Timing and Fluidity: This drill requires excellent timing from the central players to maintain fluidity in the attacking moves. Encourage players to focus on maintaining a good rhythm and working together to create overlapping runs and passing options.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a passive defender into the box, allowing them to apply light pressure on the players attempting to finish. This will simulate game pressure and encourage the attacking players to make quicker decisions when finishing.Focus: This progression adds a layer of realism to the drill, allowing players to work on finishing under pressure and adjusting to defensive situations.

title: Lazio Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on evading pressure and making precise passes under defensive pressure. Play begins with the coach passing the ball into the attacker, who must then evade pressure from the defender and attempt to pass the ball into one of the cones, knocking it off the base.For each cone knocked off, the attacker is rewarded with a point. If the defender wins possession or the attacker fails to knock a ball off the cone, the roles are reversed, and the defender becomes the attacker. This drill helps improve the attacker’s ability to make accurate passes under pressure while challenging the defender to apply pressure effectively.
coaching_notes: • Evasion and Ball Control: The attacker should focus on using quick changes of direction, body feints, and close ball control to evade the defender. Encouraging the attacker to maintain balance while keeping the ball close is crucial to staying in control during the evasion.• Passing Accuracy: Emphasize the importance of delivering precise passes to knock the cones off. The attacker should aim to pass with accuracy and consistency, adjusting the pace of the ball to ensure it hits the cone without being intercepted by the defender.• Defensive Pressure: The defender should focus on closing down space quickly and applying pressure without overcommitting. They should work on their positioning to anticipate the attacker’s movements, aiming to intercept the pass or force the attacker into a mistake.• Decision Making: Encourage the attacker to make quick decisions on which cone to target. They should be aware of the defender’s positioning and adjust their strategy accordingly to make the most effective pass under pressure.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for each attacking phase, requiring the attacker to knock as many cones off as possible within a set time frame. This will increase the intensity of the drill and encourage quicker decision-making from the attacker.Focus: This progression encourages speed and efficiency, pushing the attacker to make decisions faster while maintaining control and accuracy in passing.
progression_two: Add More Cones:Increase the number of cones in the grid, allowing the attacker to choose from more targets. This variation will test the attacker’s ability to quickly assess the best target and make multiple passes in a short amount of time.Focus: This progression encourages better spatial awareness and tactical thinking, as the attacker needs to quickly analyze their surroundings and choose the best cone to aim for.

title: Lazio Layered Countering
instructions_setup: This counter-attacking drill begins with a 2v1 overload and progresses to a 3v2. The play starts with a pass into the attacking players, who must then attack quickly and decisively while being overloaded. The goal is to score in the central mini goal, encouraging attackers to exploit the space and attack with pace.The drill simulates a transition from defense to attack, emphasizing quick decision-making and exploiting numerical advantages to break down a defense. Players must learn to recognize when to exploit the overload and make the most of the situation by focusing on attacking central spaces.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Players should focus on transitioning from defense to attack with speed. Encourage the attackers to move quickly after receiving the pass, and avoid hesitating. A fast break increases the likelihood of exploiting the defensive overload before the opposition can recover.• Exploiting the Overload: Attackers must recognize the numerical advantage and look to penetrate the central spaces. Encourage the attackers to make runs that pull defenders out of position and create opportunities to break through.• Passing and Timing: Emphasize the importance of accurate passing and timing. The player on the ball should aim for quick, well-timed passes to the attacking teammate to ensure they maintain the pace of the counter-attack. The receiving player should look to get the ball under control and shoot or pass quickly.• Composure in Front of Goal: Encourage attackers to stay calm in front of the mini goal and finish with precision. It’s important that they remain composed, taking the best shot based on the situation and goalkeeper positioning.
progression_one: Increase the Defenders:Add an additional defender to the drill, making the transition from 2v1 to 3v2. This progression increases the difficulty for the attackers, forcing them to work harder to break through the defense.Focus: This progression simulates more realistic counter-attacking situations, where attackers must deal with a higher level of defensive pressure while maintaining the pace and composure required to score.
progression_two: Add a Goalkeeper:Introduce a goalkeeper to the central mini goal. This adds the challenge of finishing under pressure, with the attacking team needing to adjust their shots and decision-making in front of goal.Focus: This progression emphasizes finishing under real-game conditions, encouraging attackers to stay composed while facing a goalkeeper and aiming for accuracy rather than power.

title: Lazio Making Forward Runs
instructions_setup: This practice is split into three separate zones: one on the left, one on the right, and a central void zone. Each team has 3 players, with one team in the left zone and the other in the right zone. The objective is for both teams to work through unopposed combination play within their designated zones. On the coach’s whistle, the teams must transition and travel from one end to the other using longer combination passes to cover the central void zone.This drill emphasizes fluid passing and quick transitions, with an emphasis on using both short and longer passes to progress the ball through the zones efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Fluid Passing Combinations: Encourage players to move the ball quickly and accurately within their zone. They should focus on maintaining a good rhythm with short, sharp passes while staying aware of the players around them. Timing and accuracy in passing are key for maintaining possession and building up the attack.• Quick Transitions: Players should react quickly when the coach whistles and transition smoothly from short combinations to longer passes. Timing the movement into the central void zone is crucial, as the players should take advantage of the open space to progress the ball effectively.• Movement Off the Ball: Players need to make intelligent runs to offer passing options and create space for their teammates. Encourage them to focus on making runs that pull defenders out of position, creating space for receiving the ball and continuing the flow of play.• Communication: Communication is essential during both the short and longer passing phases. Players should talk to each other to ensure they’re on the same page regarding the next pass and movement, reducing the chance of mistakes and improving overall coordination.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce one defender into the central zone who can challenge the team once they transition through the central area. The defender should look to apply pressure and try to win possession.Focus: This progression adds pressure and challenges the attacking team’s ability to execute precise passes and make quick decisions under pressure as they transition through the central zone.
progression_two: Increase the Number of Defenders:Introduce two defenders into the central zone to increase difficulty. This forces the attacking team to work even harder to find passing lanes and make more creative combinations.Focus: This progression simulates a more difficult scenario, where attackers need to work together, adjust their positioning, and move the ball more rapidly to break down a higher level of defensive pressure.

title: Lazio Overloaded Build Up
instructions_setup: This build-up drill encourages two midfield players to find space or quickly combine in order to progress play forward into either of the two mini goals located within their grid. The drill starts with two deeper players positioned on the baseline, who are completely unopposed but may be limited to a specific amount of time in possession to maintain tempo and urgency in the build-up phase.The main objective is for the midfielders to link up and move the ball efficiently, while the defending players try to disrupt the play and win possession. If the attacking team fails to score or the defending team wins possession, play switches to the opposite side of the grid, with the new team in possession attempting to build up into the mini goals on their side.
coaching_notes: • Finding Space and Quick Combinations: Encourage the midfield players to actively move off the ball, creating options for the player in possession. They should focus on using short, quick passes to break the lines and move the ball forward, while maintaining an awareness of the space around them to exploit openings.• Time and Decision Making: The deeper players need to make decisions quickly, especially with a limited time in possession. They should focus on keeping the ball moving and making decisive passes into the midfielders, who can either dribble or pass forward toward the mini goals.• Progressing Play: Players should work on progressing the ball quickly, focusing on building attacks and recognizing the best moments to pass forward into space or take on defenders. Timing and awareness of the defensive positioning is essential for a successful build-up.• Defensive Pressure: The defending players should focus on pressuring the attacking team without over-committing, ensuring they can intercept passes or force errors. They should work on closing down passing lanes and forcing the attacking team into making rushed decisions.
progression_one: Limit Time for Possession:Limit the amount of time the two baseline players have in possession (e.g., 5 seconds) to increase the intensity of the build-up. This forces the players to move the ball quicker, creating a more dynamic and fast-paced environment.Focus: This progression encourages faster decision-making, sharper passing, and more dynamic movements to ensure the ball is advanced before the time limit expires.

title: Lazio Overloaded Possession
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice encourages players to create overloads in specific areas of the pitch. The setup involves dividing the field into six grids, where the defending team can have a maximum of one player per grid, while the attacking team can have up to three players in each grid. The attacking team must focus on utilizing their numerical advantage to create space and move the ball effectively across the grid system.The attacking team’s objective is to move the ball into at least five of the six grids before attempting to score in any of the mini-goals. If the defending team wins possession, they can immediately counter-attack and score into any of the mini-goals. This encourages quick transitions and rewards the defending team for regaining possession.
coaching_notes: • Creating Overloads: The attacking team should focus on positioning to create numerical advantages in each grid. Players should move intelligently to fill space and overload areas to break down the defensive structure, making it easier to progress the ball forward.• Quick Transitions: Emphasize the need for quick and decisive transitions between the grids. Players must move the ball rapidly to exploit the overloads and avoid allowing the defending team to reorganize. The attacking team should look for quick passes and movements to retain possession.• Defensive Awareness: The defending team should focus on compact positioning and closing down passing lanes. Despite being outnumbered in each grid, defenders must remain disciplined, work as a unit, and anticipate passes to disrupt the attacking flow.• Spacing and Timing: Encourage attacking players to be aware of their positioning relative to their teammates. Timing the runs and passes is crucial for breaking the defensive lines and finding space in the grids. Players should avoid overcrowding any one grid and spread out to increase the attacking options.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 1 minute) for the attacking team to move the ball into five grids before attempting to score. This forces the attacking players to move the ball quickly and makes the exercise more game-like in terms of pace and urgency.Focus: This progression increases the intensity of the drill, challenging the attacking team to work under pressure, make quicker decisions, and accelerate the pace of play.

title: Lazio Penetrate Behind SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game encourages attacking players to make runs in behind central defenders to create goal-scoring opportunities. The game is structured with two central defenders who are locked onto the line, meaning they cannot leave their designated area. The defending team’s role is to intercept any forward passes played into the space behind the central defenders.Attacking players are tasked with making runs into the space behind the defenders. If they successfully receive a pass into the space, they are presented with a clear chance to finish on goal unopposed. This practice helps improve timing of runs, passing accuracy, and finishing under minimal pressure.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Encourage attackers to time their runs well, ensuring they stay onside and break through at the right moment. The key is to make the run as soon as the pass is played, taking advantage of the space behind the central defenders.• Passing Accuracy: The player delivering the pass should focus on accuracy and weight, ensuring it reaches the attacker in stride without being intercepted by the defenders. Passing into space with precision will increase the chances of a successful finish.• Attacking Awareness: Attackers should stay aware of the space behind the defenders, constantly looking for opportunities to make runs that create goal-scoring chances. Communication between attackers and passers is key to ensuring that the correct timing is maintained.• Defensive Discipline: The central defenders must stay disciplined, ensuring they cover the space and anticipate forward passes. They should be quick to react, using positioning to block off potential runs and prevent attackers from getting a clear shot at goal.
progression_one: Limit Number of Touches:Limit each player to a maximum number of touches (e.g., 2 or 3 touches). This forces attackers to play quickly, making sharp runs and quick passes to exploit the space behind the defenders.Focus: This progression encourages quick ball movement and enhances the speed of play, simulating game situations where attacking players need to act quickly in front of goal.

title: Lazio Rondo to Finish
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a 4v2 rondo positioned on one side of the 18-yard box. The aim is for the possession team to complete a designated number of passes (e.g., 5-6) under pressure. Once this target is reached, they must play a penetrative pass into the two central attackers positioned just outside or inside the penalty area.As the ball is played into the attackers, the two defending players from the rondo must immediately recover into the central area and attempt to block the shot or delay the play.To increase the difficulty and realism, both attackers must combine before shooting—meaning the first attacker to receive the ball must play a set pass or lay-off to their teammate, who then attempts to finish.
coaching_notes: • Rondo Focus: Encourage quick decision-making, one-touch passing, and off-ball movement to maintain possession under pressure.• Timing of Central Pass: The final pass into the attackers should be crisp and well-timed—players must scan the central area and recognize the moment to break lines.• Attacker Combination: Emphasize communication and awareness of defensive pressure before combining for a finish.• Defensive Recovery: Encourage the defenders to react instantly once the ball is played into the central area to close space.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender in the Central Zone.:Introduce a passive defender near the attackers during the combination phase.This player doesn’t tackle but applies light pressure to force quicker decisions.Focus: Increases difficulty of the attacking combination and forces attackers to scan and react faster.
progression_two: Limit Time to Finish After Receiving.:Add a 4-second time limit for the two attackers to get a shot off after receiving the ball.This encourages sharp, instinctive play and simulates real match tempo.Focus: Improves attacking urgency, quick combinations, and execution under time pressure.

title: Leicester 1v1 Att & Def
instructions_setup: This drill starts with two players completing a set number of passes to each other. Once the set number of passes has been completed, the attacker will turn through one of two gates and attempt to go through on goal. The defender's role is to immediately react by sprinting through the opposite gate and recovering to prevent the attacker from scoring.The focus of this practice is to simulate quick transitions from attack to defense, improving both attacking timing and defensive recovery. Players must work on decision-making, quick reactions, and maintaining pressure throughout the play.
coaching_notes: • Pass and Move: Emphasize the importance of accurate passing and moving after the pass. Attackers should focus on creating space and timing their turn through the gate. The player passing the ball should ensure it’s in a position that allows for a smooth transition to goal.• Defensive Reaction: The defender must react quickly, sprinting through the opposite gate immediately after the attacker turns. They should focus on closing the space effectively while maintaining a strong defensive stance to prevent the shot.• Attacking Timing: The attacker must make a quick decision about which gate to go through, using their body positioning to protect the ball and accelerate towards goal. Timing is key to ensuring they get through the gate before the defender can recover.• Defensive Awareness: The defender must read the attacker’s movements, staying alert to their change of direction. Recovery speed and positioning are essential for preventing the attacker from getting a clean shot at goal.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender who starts in a position further away from the play. Once the attacker makes their move, the second defender can join the action, increasing the defensive pressure.Focus: This progression encourages attackers to make quicker decisions while adding complexity to the defensive recovery, testing both their attacking and defensive skills under increased pressure.
progression_two: Limit the Attacker’s Touches:Limit the attacker to a maximum of 2 touches before attempting to go through the gate and shoot. This forces the attacker to be quicker in their decision-making and transition.Focus: This progression enhances the speed of play, encouraging faster reactions from both the attacker and defender while maintaining intensity throughout the drill.

title: Leicester 3v2 to Double 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 3v2 in the central area, simulating an attacking overload in and around the penalty box. Once the initial 3v2 phase is completed, 2 of the defending players transition into the wider zones to defend a 1v1 against the attacking player with a mini goal positioned for them to defend. The remaining attacking player can now engage in an underloaded 1v2 in the central area, providing an additional challenge.The focus is on both attacking and defensive transitions, with players needing to quickly adjust to the changing dynamics of the game. This practice is great for improving defensive recovery and attacking decision-making in dynamic situations.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Decision Making: Encourage attackers to make quick, decisive choices, utilizing overloads and exploiting gaps in the defense. Players should focus on creative combinations to break down the defense and make the most of their numerical advantage.• Defensive Transition: Defenders must react quickly once the 3v2 phase ends and transition to the wide areas to defend a 1v1. The focus is on recovery speed, closing down the attacker, and making sure they maintain defensive shape and positioning.• 1v2 in Central Areas: The remaining attacking player in the central area must make quick decisions, deciding when to take on the defender or make a pass to create an opportunity for a shot on goal. Encourage creativity and awareness of the space.• Wide Zone Defending: The defenders transitioning into the wide areas must focus on staying compact and maintaining defensive discipline when under 1v1 pressure. They should aim to force the attacker wide and prevent them from taking a direct shot on goal.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player in the wide zone who can assist the attacking team. This gives the attackers more options to exploit and puts more pressure on the defenders to manage their transitions.Focus: This progression encourages the attackers to think quickly and adjust to the additional support in the wide areas while testing the defenders' ability to handle a numerical disadvantage.

title: Leicester Build & Counter Press
instructions_setup: This practice is a 5v3 possession and counter attack drill designed to develop patient build-up play and reactive counter pressing. The team in possession must aim to complete ‘x’ number of passes to score 1 point, while the 3 defending players try to regain possession and break quickly into any of the 4 mini goals located around the grid.To replicate realistic transitions, the 2 end line players (from the team in possession) are allowed to enter the central zone immediately after a turnover. This simulates a quick counter press — turning what begins as a 3v1 counter attack into a 3v3, forcing players to react quickly in both offensive and defensive moments.
coaching_notes: • Controlled Build-Up: Encourage patience in possession, using support from the end line players to recycle play. Players should constantly move and scan for passing lanes, aiming to keep the ball circulating with minimal touches.• Counter Pressing Reaction: Upon losing possession, players must react immediately to close down the ball and block passing lanes. Emphasize urgency, teamwork, and communication to restore balance and delay the counter.• Transition Speed: Focus on how quickly the defending team can counter once possession is won. Players should attack with pace and directness, aiming to reach the mini goals before the press recovers.• Use of Support Players: The end line players must stay alert and read the game. Their movement and positioning after a turnover are vital to restoring shape or supporting the press.
progression_one: Add Touch Limit for End Players:Limit the end line players to one or two touches to increase speed of play and decision-making. This encourages quick movement off the ball and sharper passing.Focus: Improves tempo of possession and sharpens reactions during build-up and transitions.
progression_two: Bonus Goal on First-Time Finish:If the counter-attacking team scores from a first-time finish, award an extra point. This encourages quick execution and decision-making in front of goal.Focus: Adds realism to counter attacks by encouraging fast, instinctive play in final third moments.

title: Leicester Counter Attack SSG
instructions_setup: This small sided game is designed to promote explosive counter attacking moments by manipulating space and team shape. A unique rule requires all players to be inside the opposition half before a team is allowed to score, encouraging advanced positioning and forward movement.This condition leaves space in behind, creating natural counter attacking chances for the out-of-possession team. If they regain the ball, they can immediately exploit the open half with pace. Goals scored on the counter do not require all players to be in the opposition half.
coaching_notes: • Space Exploitation: Encourage attackers to recognise and exploit large gaps left in behind by a fully committed team. Look for quick, early passes into space or long carries.• Commitment to Press: Teams trying to score must press with intensity and keep shape high up the pitch — but must be wary of overcommitting and being exposed.• Decision Making in Transition: Players must quickly assess whether to drive, pass, or shoot on the counter. Encourage intelligent runs and support play to increase options.• Game Awareness: This setup helps players think about game management — when to press, when to drop, and how to control tempo depending on score or time left.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Score:Once all players are in the attacking half, teams must score within 10 seconds. This pushes urgency and forces quick decision-making in the final third.Focus: Encourages fast interplay and movement once possession is established high up the pitch.
progression_two: Counter Bonus for 3-Pass Goals:Award a bonus point if a counter attack results in a goal after just 3 or fewer passes. This adds value to quick, vertical transitions.Focus: Emphasises direct play and clinical execution under pressure during counters.

title: Leicester Evading Pressure
instructions_setup: This reaction-based practice begins with two players inside a circle — one in possession and one as the chaser. The possession player must dribble around the circle in any direction, evading the pressing defender for as long as possible using changes of pace and direction.On the coach’s whistle, the possession player can attempt to break free and play forward into either of the two mini goals outside the circle. This drill promotes close control, awareness under pressure, and decision-making in transition moments.
coaching_notes: • Change of Direction: Encourage sharp turns, stop-start movements, and the use of both feet to keep the defender off balance and unpredictable.• Awareness: Players must constantly scan the defender’s body position and anticipate the best moment to break free toward the mini goals.• Whistle Reaction: The whistle signals a moment of transition — challenge players to react instantly and find the right pass under pressure.• Body Position: Help players understand how to shield the ball effectively, using their body to create space while dribbling or when preparing to pass.

title: Leicester Finishing Races
instructions_setup: This warm-up drill sees two teams compete in a head-to-head finishing challenge that blends passing combinations with one-touch execution. Each team must complete a series of forward passes, culminating in a chipped pass over a mini goal to a teammate positioned behind it, who must finish with a single touch.Players rotate roles after each attempt, and variations can be introduced — such as right foot only, left foot only, or heading finishes — to increase difficulty and engagement.
coaching_notes: • Chipped Delivery: Encourage lofted passes with the correct weight and height to clear the mini goal while setting up an ideal one-touch finish.• Body Shape for Finish: The receiving player should adjust their body early to ensure they are balanced and prepared to finish in one touch.• Timing of Movement: Players must time their runs well to meet the chipped ball in stride and avoid arriving too early or late.• Variation Focus: Use the finishing restrictions to target specific technical skills and challenge players to improve weaker foot or heading ability.
progression_one: Competition with Time Limit:Set a timer for each round and challenge teams to score as many goals as possible within a time frame using one-touch finishes.Focus: Increases intensity, promotes quicker decision-making, and builds match-like tempo.

title: Leicester Half Pitch Build Up
instructions_setup: In this build-up drill, the pitch is divided vertically into two halves, with two simultaneous 6v4 games taking place — one on each side. The objective for the team in possession is to build play through their half, encouraging structured build-up patterns and intelligent movement under pressure.Because possession is restricted to one half, the defending team can focus on setting effective pressing traps and anticipating passes. Both goalkeepers operate in the same full-size goal but are stationed only within their designated half, further reinforcing the split-pitch dynamic.
coaching_notes: • Half-Pitch Awareness: Players must stay composed and make intelligent decisions in tight spaces, using quick movement and passing to create gaps in the press.• Structured Pressing: The pressing team should be coached on when and how to step in, recognizing cues to trigger pressing traps and force errors.• Goalkeeper Distribution: Encourage the goalkeepers to remain involved by initiating play and supporting the build-up with accurate passes and clear communication.• Rotational Movement: Build-up players should rotate positions frequently to disorganize the press and maintain fresh passing options in the limited space.
progression_one: Add a Floating Player:Introduce a neutral floating player who can operate across both halves, always supporting the team in possession to provide overloads.Focus: Encourages quicker ball circulation and forces defenders to constantly adjust to shifting overloads.
progression_two: Switch Play After X Passes:Allow the possession team to switch to the opposite half only after completing ‘x’ number of passes, creating a more advanced build-up challenge.Focus: Promotes patience in possession while also developing awareness of space and switching under pressure.

title: Leicester One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This individual practice is designed for a centre forward to work on set play combinations, sharp movement, and finishing from various angles. The drill begins with the forward dropping short to receive a pass to feet. They then play a one-touch set pass into one of two mini goals positioned nearby. Immediately after, they spin sharply and collect one of three stationary balls placed in left, centre, and right channels before finishing into a full-sized goal.
coaching_notes: • Check Shoulder Before Dropping – Be aware of space and surroundings before receiving, with constant scanning and body orientation to stay sharp.• Crisp Set Pass with Realism – Focus on a firm, accurate set pass into the mini goal with proper weight and technique, simulating a real in-game layoff.• Explosive Movement After Release – Accelerate into space immediately after the set, using a sharp directional change to separate from a defender.• Decisive First Touch and Finish – Approach each ball with a clean first touch and adjust body shape quickly for a composed, clinical finish.

title: Leicester Penetrating Patterns
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill focuses on developing penetration and timing when playing through a midfield block. Four mannequins are set up to represent a compact midfield line. The practice begins with a square pass played across the face of the block, followed by a well-timed penetrative pass through the mannequins to a wide receiver on the opposite side.Once received, the ball is circulated back through the opposite side using the same pattern — square pass across, followed by a penetrating pass through the midfield block to the other flank. This continuous rotation encourages rhythm and precision in breaking lines.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Pass: Ensure players wait for the right moment to play through the block — when the receiver is moving and the lane is open.• Body Positioning: Receivers should be on the half-turn and open to receive the ball in stride, encouraging a fluid transition into the next action.• Weight & Angle: Focus on the accuracy and weight of both square and penetrating passes, ensuring the ball travels cleanly through tight channels.• Communication & Scanning: Players must constantly scan the block and communicate with teammates to time their runs and support movements.
progression_one: Add One-Touch Limit on Penetrative Pass:Players must play the penetrating pass first-time once the square pass is received.Focus: Improves anticipation, scanning, and speed of execution when breaking lines.
progression_two: Add Passive Pressure Behind the Block:Introduce passive defenders or moving mannequins behind the block to simulate real opposition pressing.Focus: Trains players to be aware of pressure after breaking the line and make quick decisions upon receiving.

title: Leicester Positional Rondo
instructions_setup: This positional rondo allows teams to develop key aspects of modern play — possession retention, penetration through central areas, and pressing upon transition. Five players look to keep possession against three active pressing defenders, while two additional defenders are locked in position to screen the central line and block any through balls.Once the team in possession completes ‘x’ number of passes, they are permitted to transfer the ball across the central line. If the pressing team wins possession, their immediate objective is to counter and score into one of the mini goals while the original possession team applies an aggressive counter press.
coaching_notes: • Create Angles & Passing Lanes: Players must constantly adjust their positions to support the ball carrier. Movement should help break lines and open up passing options quickly under pressure.• Play with Purpose: Encourage players to scan before receiving and take minimal touches. The goal is purposeful possession — playing forward or across with intent, not just keeping the ball.• Screen the Line Effectively: Defenders on the central line should remain active and alert. Emphasize good positioning to cut off split passes and read play before it develops.• React to Transitions Quickly: If possession is lost, the team must immediately press with urgency and communication. Winning the ball back within seconds should be the goal in transition moments.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player Inside the Grid:Introduce one neutral player in the central zone to help create overloads and increase the tempo of play. This encourages quick combinations and creative play to split defenders.Focus: Promotes finding the free man in tight spaces and improves penetration under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Possession Time to Transfer:Once the possession team completes ‘x’ passes, they must transfer within a 5-second window. This adds urgency and forces quicker decision-making when switching play.Focus: Sharpens execution and encourages rapid play when changing the point of attack.

title: Leicester Reaction to Transitions
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 4v1 rondo in an extremely tight 3x3 yard space, focusing on close control and fast decision-making under pressure. Once the single defender wins the ball and knocks it out of the rondo area, the practice immediately transitions into a 7v4 possession game across a larger space, involving the original 5 rondo players plus 2 goalkeepers as neutral support.The 4 defenders, now acting as a pressing unit, aim to regain possession and counter quickly into either of the mini goals. This drill combines technical precision with transitional reactions and quick thinking.
coaching_notes: • Quick Play in Tight Spaces: In the rondo, players must use one or two touches and keep their body open to play quickly under extreme pressure.• Sharp Transition Awareness: Players must instantly recognize the shift from rondo to possession phase. Movement off the ball and shape adjustment are critical to retain control.• Defensive Unit Communication: The 4 defenders must coordinate their press, close down passing angles, and hunt the ball together during the possession phase.• Fast Counter Execution: Upon winning the ball, defenders should look forward immediately and counter with purpose, aiming to exploit the moment of imbalance.
progression_one: Restrict Goalkeepers to 1-Touch Play:Allow goalkeepers only one touch to increase tempo and encourage better movement and quicker decision-making by possession players around them.Focus: Promotes sharper thinking and movement to support quicker circulation from deeper areas.

title: Leicester Switch to Penetrate
instructions_setup: In this drill, teams focus on quickly switching play across the grid to create scoring opportunities. The objective is to score by either finishing into one of the two mini goals or dribbling through one of the two gates on the opposite side of the grid.One player from each team must always be positioned within each half of the grid, ensuring that at any given time, you have a maximum of 4v4 on one side and a 1v1 situation on the other side. This setup encourages both quick ball circulation and exploitation of space across the field.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Movement: Encourage players to switch play rapidly and look for the best option to either score or progress the ball quickly to the opposite side. Fast transitions between zones are key.• Maintain Positional Discipline: Ensure that players keep their positions, particularly in the 1v1 areas, to create a more dynamic and challenging attacking/defending environment.• Use of Space: The team in possession must exploit the space created by the 1v1 situation, encouraging players to make runs that force defenders to react and commit.• Immediate Decision-Making: Players should make quick decisions about whether to cross, dribble, or shoot, without overthinking the options.
progression_one: Bonus Points for Crosses or Overlaps:Award a bonus point for any successful cross or overlapping run that results in a goal. This encourages wide play and team coordination to create more goal-scoring chances.Focus: Promotes teamwork, wing play, and the ability to deliver accurate crosses under pressure.

title: Leipzig 1v1 into 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 1v1 scenario where an attacker begins from a wide position, attempting to score against a central defender. After the first phase is complete, the drill progresses to a 2v1, with a second attacker joining the play. However, the defending team will have a recovering defender who can turn it into a 2v2 situation.The second defender starts 3 yards behind the second attacker, which gives the defending team an opportunity to react and recover, testing their defensive resilience and ability to delay or prevent a goal-scoring chance.
coaching_notes: • Initial 1v1 Focus: Encourage attackers to be direct and create angles to beat the defender. Defenders should focus on maintaining good positioning, closing down space, and preventing an easy shot.• Quick Transition to 2v1: When the second attacker joins, attackers should look to combine quickly, using the overload to break down the defense. Defenders must react quickly to prevent being outnumbered and keep their shape.• Defender Recovery: The recovering defender must track back with intensity and aim to disrupt the attacking flow. They should look for opportunities to press or force the attackers into less dangerous positions.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Attackers must make quick decisions, whether to pass, shoot, or create space for a better opportunity. Encourage fast thinking and fluid movement in both attacking and defensive situations.
progression_one: Add More Recovering Defenders:Add an additional defender starting further from the play (e.g., 5-7 yards behind). This forces the attacking team to be even more creative in how they use the 2v1 advantage, while defenders must work harder to track the attackers.Focus: Increases the difficulty for attackers and defenders, refining their positioning and communication during defensive recoveries.

title: Leipzig 2 Zone Overloaded
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 4v3 attacking scenario in the first zone, where the attacking team aims to progress the ball into the opposition's penalty box. If successful, the attack moves into a 2v1 situation, with only two of the four attackers moving into the penalty area to finish the play.If the defending team wins possession, they transition quickly and attempt to score in either of the two mini-goals, focusing on a fast counterattack. This drill encourages quick transitions, decision-making under pressure, and precise finishing.
coaching_notes: • 4v3 Build-Up: The attacking team should focus on maintaining possession and creating overloads to break down the defense. They should move the ball quickly and look for openings to progress into the final third.• 2v1 Finishing: In the final phase, the attackers should aim to exploit the 2v1 advantage, using quick passes and intelligent movement to break through the defenders and finish with accuracy. The defenders must focus on closing down options and preventing a clean shot.• Defensive Recovery: The defending team must transition quickly after losing possession, immediately focusing on blocking shooting lanes and applying pressure to the attackers. They should communicate effectively to cover the mini-goals and restore balance in defense.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Attackers need to decide whether to pass or shoot in the 2v1 scenario, while defenders must decide whether to press or cover. Encourage players to read the situation and act quickly.
progression_one: Add Time Limit to Attack:Set a time limit for the attacking team to progress the ball and complete the 2v1 finishing phase. This forces attackers to move quickly and make decisions under time pressure, while also encouraging defenders to press more aggressively.
progression_two: Add Extra Defenders to Final Phase:Introduce an additional defender in the penalty area for the 2v1 scenario, making it a 2v2 for the finish. This forces the attackers to be more creative and precise with their movements, while defenders must communicate and work together to stop the shot.Focus: Increases the difficulty for attackers and enhances defensive organization in the final third.

title: Leipzig 3rd Man Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing practice uses a Y-shaped setup with four stations. The drill begins with the initial player playing an up-back-and-through combination to one of the two tips of the Y. The second station player will then spin around and finish off a set pass from one of the higher players. After each finish, players rotate through the stations to maintain a high intensity and maximize repetitions.This practice focuses on improving quick decision-making, movement off the ball, and finishing under pressure in dynamic situations.
coaching_notes: • Up-Back-and-Through Combination: Players should focus on precise passing and timing during the up-back-and-through sequence. Encourage the player receiving the ball to make a quick and accurate first touch to set up the next phase of the play.• Quick Movement and Spin: The second station player must react quickly, spinning around to receive the ball and finishing efficiently. Focus on proper body positioning to receive the ball in stride and execute a clean finish.• Finishing Technique: Players should focus on composure in front of goal, aiming to finish with accuracy and control. Encourage different types of finishes, such as placing the ball in the corners or using the inside of the foot to ensure precision.• Rotation and Intensity: Players should rotate quickly between stations, maintaining a high tempo to simulate match-like conditions. Stress the importance of constant movement and staying engaged throughout the practice.
progression_one: Add Defenders for Pressure:Introduce a passive defender in the final phase to add pressure to the shooter. This will force the player finishing to make quicker decisions and adjust their shot based on the defensive pressure.Focus: Increases decision-making speed and finishing under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Touches for Finishing:Limit the number of touches each player can take when finishing. For example, each player may only be allowed two touches: one to control the ball and the second to finish. This encourages quicker reactions and sharper finishing techniques.Focus: Encourages quicker, more decisive finishes and improves ball control under time constraints.

title: Leipzig Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This ball mastery drill encourages players to attack free space and break out of tight areas while maintaining ball control. Play begins with a pass into the attacker, who must attempt to break out of the grid while keeping possession of the ball. The 3 defenders work together to close down the attacker, aiming to block any path out of the grid. The attacker has 7 seconds to break free from the defenders and exit the grid.The drill focuses on improving individual ball control, decision-making under pressure, and quick movement to exploit space.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: The attacker should focus on quickly scanning for open space and making fast decisions to escape the defenders. Encourage the use of feints, changes of direction, and sharp acceleration to beat defenders.• Ball Control and Touches: Emphasize keeping the ball close to the feet to maintain control while navigating through tight spaces. The attacker should use light touches to maneuver the ball efficiently and avoid getting crowded by the defenders.• Defensive Coordination: The defenders should move in sync, ensuring they cover all possible exits and force the attacker toward specific areas. They should stay compact and avoid leaving gaps for the attacker to exploit.• Timing and Speed: The 7-second limit forces the attacker to act quickly and the defenders to react efficiently. Encourage both groups to focus on timing their movements to maximize the pressure or breakout opportunity.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Defenders:Increase the number of defenders to 4 or 5, making it harder for the attacker to break out. This will challenge the attacker to think creatively and use a wider range of skills to escape the pressure.Focus: Promotes creative problem-solving and quick reactions when facing a greater number of defenders.

title: Leipzig Breaking Lines
instructions_setup: This penetration drill is designed to develop quick ball circulation and effective line-breaking passes. Four players will be positioned in the middle zone and their objective is to block or intercept forward passes. The two teams of 4, positioned in either end zone, will work together to play and receive passes, using movement and positioning to manipulate the opposition block. The goal is to create and exploit a line-breaking opportunity through precise passing and movement.The practice helps improve passing accuracy, spatial awareness, and the ability to break through defensive lines under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Circulation: Encourage players to circulate the ball quickly within the team, using short, sharp passes to move the opposition block and create gaps for forward passes. The tempo should remain high to stretch the defense and create openings.• Recognizing Passing Lanes: Players should constantly scan the field to identify potential passing lanes. Encourage players to look for spaces between the defenders or to break through defensive lines with incisive passes when possible.• Movement off the Ball: Players in the end zones should move dynamically to offer passing options. Their positioning should be fluid, always looking to stretch or shift the opposition’s defensive structure and create new passing opportunities.• Defensive Awareness: Players in the middle zone should be proactive in blocking or intercepting passes. They must communicate and position themselves to close down passing lanes quickly and force the attacking team to recycle the ball.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Progression:Introduce a time limit for completing a line-breaking pass (e.g., 30 seconds). This encourages faster decision-making and helps players understand the urgency of breaking defensive lines.Focus: Improves tempo and decision-making under time pressure, pushing players to recognize and exploit opportunities more quickly.
progression_two: Limit Passes to One or Two Touches:Limit players to one or two touches to increase the pace of circulation and challenge them to make quicker, more accurate decisions.Focus: Enhances passing accuracy and quick decision-making, forcing players to execute under pressure and with limited touches.

title: Leipzig Build Up via Full Backs
instructions_setup: The session starts with a 4v3 possession game in the central zone, where the build-up team also has 2 full-backs positioned in wide channels, each locked into their zone.
