Only the full-backs from the build-up team are permitted in these wide areas, encouraging the use of width and intelligent switching of play.The build-up team has two ways to score points:1) By successfully playing into a full-back who then scores in a mini goal located in their channel.2) By dribbling the ball over a central line, simulating progressive build-up through the thirds.The pressing team (the three defenders) must disrupt play, win the ball, and then counter-attack quickly, simulating a transition moment.
coaching_notes: • Build-up Focus: Encourage players to create angles and use the full-backs as wide outlets to stretch the opposition and switch play.• Full-back Play: Full-backs must be alert, well-positioned, and ready to receive under pressure with a positive first touch toward goal.• Central Penetration: Teach players to recognize when to break the line through dribbling, exploiting central gaps when wide options are denied.• Defensive Transition: Highlight urgency and compactness in the pressing team, emphasizing quick transitions to attack after winning possession.
progression_one: Full-Backs Can Recover Centrally on Transition:If the build-up team loses possession, the wide full-backs are now allowed to leave their channels and recover into the central zone to help defend the counter-attack.This adds a layer of defensive responsibility and realism, mimicking the demands placed on full-backs in real match scenarios when possession is lost high or during build-up.Focus: Encourages awareness, fitness, and transition speed from wide areas. Also tests communication and compactness in defensive recovery.

title: Leipzig Continuous Countering
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on quick transitions and counter-attacking in tight situations. Play starts with an attacker dribbling towards two defenders, triggering a 3v2 counter attack. The attacking players must work quickly and efficiently to attempt to score within a 7-second time period, emphasizing speed, decision-making, and accuracy.If the defenders win possession, they must immediately pass the ball across the grid to the other two defenders. These defenders will then combine and attempt to score in the opposite direction. The practice alternates starting positions, so the two defenders will rotate and take turns defending on both sides of the grid, ensuring a varied defensive challenge.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Emphasize the importance of speed when transitioning from defense to attack. Players should move quickly to exploit space and attack the goal within the 7-second window. Timing is crucial for maintaining an advantage during counter-attacks.• Efficient Passing and Movement: Encourage attacking players to move off the ball and offer quick, accurate passes to break down the defense. Players should look for opportunities to switch the ball across the grid or find space to shoot quickly.• Defensive Positioning: Defenders must work together to block passing lanes, pressuring the attacking players to force mistakes. They should always stay compact and anticipate the attackers’ movements, ensuring they don’t allow a quick goal.• Communication: Constant verbal and non-verbal communication is key, especially for defenders. Encourage players to talk and give direction to each other, ensuring they stay organized and respond quickly to any changes in the attack.
progression_one: Add a Touch Limit for Attackers:Limit the attacking players to two or three touches each to speed up the attack and force quicker decision-making. This progression promotes faster movement and execution under pressure.Focus: Increases the tempo of the counter-attack, helping players make quicker decisions and execute plays with urgency.

title: Leipzig One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 drill is designed to develop a striker’s ability to attack and finish headers from close range. The player will continuously run into the box to meet throws from behind the goal, attacking the ball with power and accuracy. After each header, they sprint back to a marker outside the penalty area before returning to the box for the next repetition, building both technical skill and fitness.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Timing the Run Perfectly to Meet the Ball at Its Highest Point – Good timing maximizes power and accuracy in the header.• Use Proper Body Positioning to Generate Power and Direct the Ball Effectively – Lean into the ball and direct headers with intention towards goal areas.• Keep Eyes on the Ball Throughout to Maintain Concentration and Precision – Tracking the ball ensures clean contact and better finishing.• Maintain High Intensity and Quick Recovery Between Repetitions – Build stamina and sharpness to sustain quality headers during fatigue.
progression_one: Increase Speed Between Runs and HeadersPush the pace of sprints and headers to simulate game intensity and improve endurance.Focus:Enhances explosive power, timing, and cardiovascular fitness under continuous effort.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender in the BoxIntroduce a passive defender to apply light pressure, forcing sharper decision-making and better body control.Focus:Develops composure, aerial duel skills, and precision when challenged by opposition.

title: Leipzig Overloaded SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game focuses on improving central defenders' ability to make forward passes under pressure. Play begins with a 3v2 in the defensive zone, where the 2 defending players must work under pressure to find an attacking player with a forward pass. The defenders must scan for options and make quick decisions while facing pressure from the attackers.If the defenders manage to find a forward pass, a 4v2 attack will unfold in the attacking zone, giving the attacking team a numerical advantage to create goal-scoring opportunities. The defenders' success in building from the back will be measured by their ability to progress the ball effectively and make the correct decisions under pressure.If the 2 pressing players win possession from the defenders, they will quickly counter-attack with the aim of scoring. The goalkeeper is restricted from playing a direct pass to the attackers; instead, the ball must be played out by one of the 2 defenders, ensuring the defenders have to be involved in the build-up.
coaching_notes: • Pressure Management: Defenders must remain calm under pressure and prioritize making accurate, forward passes. Encourage them to scan for attacking options before receiving the ball and to communicate with teammates to create passing lanes.• Forward Pass Decisions: Central defenders should focus on playing penetrating passes to the attackers when possible. They should not hesitate to break the first line of defense and play directly into the attacking players to progress the play.• Building Under Pressure: The defenders should aim to move the ball quickly and efficiently to avoid being closed down by the pressing players. Encouraging movement off the ball and creating space for the pass will help facilitate a successful build-up.• Counter-Attack Awareness: When possession is lost, the defenders need to be alert and transition quickly to stop the counter-attack. The pressers should use their speed and positioning to exploit the defensive transition and capitalize on the turnover.
progression_one: Include More Pressing Players:Introduce a third pressing player, making it a 3v2 situation for the defenders. This adds a layer of difficulty and forces the defenders to be more precise with their passing and movement under pressure.Focus: Develops the defenders' ability to deal with increased pressure and improves their composure when faced with more pressing opponents.

title: Leipzig Positional Rondo
instructions_setup: This positional rondo involves 3 teams of 4 players, with 2 teams working together in possession while the third team acts as the defending group. The aim of the practice is for the possession team to maintain control of the ball by utilizing 2 pivot players, who will act as key links to facilitate quick, accurate passes. These pivots will help the possession teams shift the ball across the grid while looking for opportunities to penetrate the defensive block.The defending team, on the other hand, must focus on preventing any penetrative passes into the attacking team’s final third. Their objective is to intercept or block any forward passes and win possession as quickly as possible. This practice simulates game-like scenarios where players need to think about both maintaining possession and working under pressure from the defenders.
coaching_notes: • Use of Pivot Players: Encourage the possession players to maintain a high level of support for the pivot players. These pivots should be constantly moving, offering themselves for the ball and maintaining balance in possession.• Awareness of Defenders: The attacking players should be aware of the defending team’s positioning and the pressure they are applying. They need to work quickly to open passing lanes and avoid getting trapped by the defenders.• Defensive Shape: The defending team must maintain good compactness and focus on blocking passing lanes into the central areas. The defenders should press as a unit, not allowing the pivot players to turn or play penetrative passes.• Quick Transitions: If the defenders win possession, they should look to quickly transition into attack. Players should be ready to exploit any space left by the possession team as they recover to stop the ball.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession Team:Limit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches). This will increase the tempo of the practice and force the possession players to make quicker decisions under pressure.Focus: Develops quick decision-making and sharp passing to maintain possession under limited touch restrictions.

title: Leipzig Triangle Passing Pattern
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice is designed to develop 3rd man combinations for progressing the ball through tight spaces. The setup involves two stations opposite each other with a square grid in between, creating a dynamic passing environment. Players will travel in and out of the grid, performing a series of 3rd man combinations to advance the ball forward.The practice focuses on quick, precise passing, encouraging players to look for opportunities to combine with teammates in a way that opens up space and bypasses defenders. The movement off the ball is crucial as players need to make runs to receive the ball and facilitate fluid combinations. The aim is to maintain possession while progressing through the grid and ultimately creating a goal-scoring opportunity.
coaching_notes: • 3rd Man Runs: Encourage players to make dynamic third-man runs, timing their movements to ensure they are available for a pass once their teammate plays the ball. The player receiving the ball should always look to play it forward into space, facilitating continuous movement.• Passing Tempo: The practice should be quick-paced, with emphasis on fast and accurate passes. Players must be comfortable with the ball under pressure and play with intent to move the ball forward efficiently.• Anticipation: Players need to anticipate the ball and the next pass. Constant scanning and reading the game will allow them to make the right decision on when to receive the ball and when to pass it on to the third player.• Fluid Movement: Emphasize fluid movement between players. There should be no hesitation when transitioning between passes, as the ball moves quickly through the grid to break down any defensive lines.
progression_one: Add a Goal or Target Area:Set up a target area or mini-goal at the end of the grid. Players must complete the third-man combination and successfully pass the ball into the target area to score. This encourages players to complete the combination with a purpose and create a scoring opportunity.Focus: Reinforces the importance of completing combinations with the end goal in mind, helping players develop attacking instincts while executing third-man passes.

title: Leverkusen 1v1 Attack & Defend
instructions_setup: This attacking practice encourages quick 1v1 attacks from multiple angles around the box, with the aim to beat defenders and create goal-scoring opportunities. Play starts with a ball into the central forward, who must attempt to beat the defender and score within a short time frame.Once each attacking phase is complete, the attacker must travel to an outside station and play a short combination with a teammate to bring a new attacker into play. If the defender wins possession and scores into any of the mini-goals, they are rewarded with a rest period and switch with another defender. This rotation helps maintain intensity while promoting competition and quick decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: Encourage attackers to make fast decisions when in possession. They should be prepared to either take on the defender directly or create space for a quick shot or pass, based on the defender's position.• Change of Direction: Attacking players must use quick changes of direction to beat the defender. Explosive movements and sharp turns will help them create separation and take advantage of any space in the box.• Defender's Focus: Defenders should be taught to stay patient and focus on positioning rather than committing too early. They must aim to delay the attack, forcing the attacker into less favorable positions to limit scoring chances.• Combination Play: When moving to the outside station, players should focus on quick, short combinations to break down the defensive lines. The combination should be fluid, with players making timed runs and passes to maintain momentum.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender to increase the pressure on the attacker. The attacker must now beat both defenders or look to combine with teammates to outmaneuver the defense.Focus: Develops the ability to attack with support and helps players refine their 1v1 skills under increased defensive pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for each phase of the attack. This encourages attackers to make quicker decisions, reducing the time they have to beat defenders or set up a scoring opportunity.Focus: Encourages attackers to execute their moves under time pressure, simulating real-game scenarios where decisions need to be made rapidly.

title: Leverkusen 3 Phase 2v2
instructions_setup: In this 3-phase practice, the area is set up using two penalty areas positioned back-to-back (vertically), with one goalkeeper in the main goal. There are 3 neutral players stationed outside the grid, each with a ball, who will serve the ball into the attacking players. The attacking team will then work through 3 consecutive 2v2 attacks. The neutral players can assist the attacking players with one-touch passes in the deeper zone but cannot enter the attacking zone.Each phase of the practice emphasizes different aspects of the 2v2 attack, such as positioning, movement, and decision-making, while working with the neutral players to create overload situations in the attacking zones.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: The attacking players should look to combine quickly, using one-touch passes to break down the defending team. Emphasize the importance of quick decision-making in tight spaces.• Use of Neutral Players: The neutral players can assist by providing extra support with one-touch passes from the deeper zone. Ensure that the attacking players use these passes effectively to progress the play quickly and create goal-scoring opportunities.• Attacking Movement: Players should focus on their movement off the ball to create space and make themselves available for passes. The attackers must work together to create overloads and open up spaces in the opposition's defense.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should focus on their positioning to prevent the attacking team from exploiting spaces. Encourage communication between the defenders to effectively deal with the overload situations created by the neutral players.
progression_one: Add More Neutral Players:Increase the number of neutral players on the outside of the grid to create even more overload situations in favor of the attacking team. This will challenge the defenders to communicate and work harder to close down spaces.Focus: Enhances the ability of attackers to exploit overloads, improve combination play, and make quicker decisions when under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Neutral Player Touches:Reduce the number of touches the neutral players are allowed to make to force the attacking players to work faster and more efficiently. This also helps the attackers focus on their timing and runs to receive passes.Focus: Improves attacking speed and the ability to execute quick, decisive plays with fewer options, simulating a more realistic game scenario.

title: Leverkusen Double 1v1 & 2v2
instructions_setup: Play starts with two separate 1v1 battles taking place on the edges of the grid in a narrow space. The attackers in these 1v1 duels aim to beat their defenders and create an opportunity to progress the ball. Once both 1v1's are complete, a 2v2 battle will take place in the middle zone, with the coach serving a ball into the opposite team to initiate the next phase.All 1v1's and 2v2's are played to a finish, with both teams having the ability to score in either of the 2 mini goals. This structure encourages dynamic transitions and quick decision-making as players move from individual duels to a more cooperative team situation.
coaching_notes: • 1v1 Focus: Players must use quick footwork, agility, and ball control to beat their defender in tight spaces. Encourage attackers to create separation through explosive changes in direction, while defenders should focus on positioning to block angles and delay the attack.• 2v2 Transition: Once the 1v1 battles are complete, players must quickly transition into the 2v2 situation. Encourage attacking players to use the width of the field and overload the defenders, while defenders should communicate to cover the space and prevent an easy goal.• Creative Finishing: Both the attackers and defenders should be ready to react to changing ball positions. Attackers should be encouraged to shoot quickly when possible, while defenders should work together to close down shooting angles and force the attacker into difficult situations.• Fluidity in Possession:

title: Leverkusen Front 2 Link & Finish
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing practice, two centre forwards operate inside an 8x8 yard grid positioned just outside the penalty area. Two central midfielders serve continuous passes into the grid, where the forwards must combine quickly before finishing on goal.The key rule is that both centre forwards are restricted to only one touch each. This constraint encourages sharp movement, precise positioning, and intelligent combination play to create one-touch finishing opportunities inside the box.
coaching_notes: • Body Shape When Receiving – Forwards must constantly adjust their body to receive at the correct angle, allowing them to redirect or lay off the ball effectively.• Movement Off the Ball – Players should rotate, check away, and time their runs to ensure they're never static and are always offering an option for a first-time combination.• One-Touch Combinations – Focus on disguised flicks, lay-offs, and wall passes with the correct weight and direction to create space for the partner.• Finishing Variety – Encourage different types of one-touch finishes: near-post, far-post, lifted finishes, and firm drives—always with quality and quick decision-making.
progression_one: Add Rotating Defender in GridIntroduce a passive or semi-active defender inside the grid to apply light pressure and test the forwards' ability to combine under more realistic pressure.Focus:Sharpens awareness, off-the-ball movement, and the ability to find space and deliver quality with limited touches under defensive presence.
progression_two: Increase Grid Size and Add Third MidfielderExpand the grid to 10x10 yards and allow a third midfielder to enter, supporting from deep for central overloads and late supporting combinations before finishing.Focus:Improves spatial awareness, timing of support runs, and adds an extra layer of combination options for more dynamic one-touch attacking patterns.

title: Leverkusen Passing Activation
instructions_setup: This passing/mastery warm-up involves 4 outer stations and 1 central pole. Players at opposite stations will play a 1-2 combination centrally before changing direction and playing a pass out to one of the side stations. After playing the pass, the player will follow the ball to the side station. The same sequence occurs at the opposite side, where the player plays a two-touch combination and then passes out to the sides, following their pass to the next station.This warm-up helps players work on their passing accuracy, quick combinations, and movement off the ball to different areas of the grid. It enhances both technical ability and spatial awareness in a dynamic, high-tempo setting.
coaching_notes: • 1-2 Combinations: Emphasize crisp, quick passes when performing the 1-2 combinations, encouraging players to focus on timing and accuracy. The first pass should be firm and directed towards the player’s receiving foot to make the return pass easier.• Directional Movement: After the combination, players should change direction immediately and move with purpose to the side stations. This helps them develop awareness of space and improve their ability to move after playing a pass.• Passing Quality: The passes to the side stations should be weighted properly to ensure they are easy for the next player to control. Encourage players to play with both feet to improve their versatility in different game situations.
progression_one: Increase the Passing Distance:Expand the grid and increase the distance between stations. This will force players to focus on longer passing accuracy and control, while maintaining the flow of the combination play.Focus: Enhances players' ability to make longer, more accurate passes while maintaining a high tempo and effective movement.

title: Lima 4+2 Build & Finish
instructions_setup: In this build and finish practice, play starts with a 2v2 in the first zone, where the attackers look to retain possession and find one of two central players to progress play forward. Once a central player receives, they move into the second zone and combine with two additional attackers to create a 3v2 attacking scenario, attempting to score into two mini goals. The practice focuses on effective build-up play, forward progression and decision-making in attacking overloads.
coaching_notes: • Passing Quality & Weight:Emphasise accurate, well-weighted forward passes that allow teammates to play on the move and maintain attacking rhythm.• Receiving Under Pressure:Encourage players to receive on the back foot, protect the ball and play forward whenever possible.• Movement to Create Passing Lines:Coach constant off-the-ball movement to create angles, support the ball and disrupt defensive structure.• Speed of Decision Making:Promote quick recognition of space, overloads and finishing opportunities in the attacking zone.
progression_one: Minimum Passes in Build-Up Zone:Require the attacking pair to complete a set number of passes before finding a central player to progress.Focus:Encourages patience in possession, improved circulation and better timing of forward passes.
progression_two: Add Defensive Recovery Runner:Allow one defender from the first zone to recover into the second zone after progression.Focus:Increases realism, challenges attackers to play quicker and improves decision-making under pressure.

title: Lima Attacking Fullbacks
instructions_setup: In this unopposed attacking practice, players work through a series of passing actions focused on progressing the ball from central areas into wide positions. Once the winger receives, they are tasked with finding either an overlapping or underlapping full back, who then delivers a cross into the box. Two attackers time their movements to attack the cross and finish, with all actions performed unopposed to maximise technical quality, timing and attacking detail.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Central Passing:Emphasise accurate, well-weighted forward passes that allow the winger to receive facing forward with minimal adjustment.• Timing of Overlaps and Underlaps:Coach full backs to recognise cues, accelerating at the correct moment to arrive on the ball with momentum.• Crossing Technique & Decision Making:Encourage varied crossing techniques, adjusting delivery based on movement, body shape and finishing zones.• Attacking Movement in the Box:Reinforce coordinated runs, different attacking lines and correct spacing to attack front and back zones.
progression_one: Two-Touch Maximum in Build-Up:Limit players to two touches during the passing sequence before the cross is delivered.Focus:Improves first-touch quality, sharper passing tempo and quicker recognition of attacking opportunities.
progression_two: Finishing Zones or Touch Restrictions:Assign finishing zones or require first-time finishes from crosses inside the penalty area.Focus:Enhances composure, finishing accuracy and realistic attacking habits under time-based pressure.

title: Lima Build & Press Breakout
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 5v3 rondo inside a central grid, with the possession team tasked with retaining the ball under pressure. Once the 3 defenders win possession or force the ball outside the grid, four outside players immediately become live and join the defenders, who now transition into a team of 7 in possession against 5 pressing players. The objective for the 7 is to retain possession for a minimum of 10 passes, while the 5 pressing players attempt to win the ball and score into either goal. Two of the outside players are goalkeepers positioned in goals, adding realism to the transition and decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Transition:Emphasise immediate reaction on regain or loss, switching mindset quickly between pressing and possession roles.• Support Angles in Overload:Coach players to create constant passing lanes, offering depth, width and clear body shapes to receive.• Ball Circulation Under Pressure:Encourage quick circulation, minimal touches and intelligent ball speed to unbalance the pressing unit.• Pressing Organisation & Triggers:Reinforce coordinated pressing, clear triggers and compact distances when attempting to win possession.
progression_one: Two-Touch Limit for the 7v5:Restrict the possession team to two touches once the practice transitions into the overload phase.Focus:Improves first-touch quality, faster decision-making and sharper ball speed under realistic pressure.
progression_two: Directional Scoring on Regains:Require the pressing team to score within a time limit after regaining possession.Focus:Encourages explosive counter-pressing reactions and quick attacking decisions after winning the ball.

title: Lima Technical Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice focuses on developing core passing fundamentals at a high tempo. Players work on receiving, passing and moving continuously, following their pass each time to rotate through different positions and angles. The emphasis is on first-touch quality, body shape, awareness and pass execution, ensuring players are consistently preparing themselves to play forward and maintain rhythm throughout the practice.
coaching_notes: • First Touch Quality:Encourage players to take a positive first touch into space, setting up the next action efficiently and smoothly.• Open Body Shape:Reinforce receiving side-on where possible to see multiple options and play forward with minimal adjustment.• Weight and Accuracy of Pass:Focus on well-weighted passes played with purpose, ensuring the receiver can maintain tempo without breaking stride.• Movement After the Pass:Coach players to follow their pass with intent, moving quickly to support, rotate positions and maintain flow.
progression_one: Weaker Foot Emphasis:Encourage or require passes to be played using the weaker foot where possible during the practice.Focus:Develops technical balance, confidence on both feet and improved adaptability in match-realistic situations.

title: Lima Wide Rotation Pattern
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice focuses on developing passing detail, timing and rotation between wide and central players, with two balls circulating simultaneously to maintain high tempo and concentration. Players continuously receive, pass and rotate, following their pass to reinforce realistic movement patterns, awareness of teammates and rhythm within positional relationships. The practice emphasises clean ball circulation, body orientation and coordination between roles.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Passes:Emphasise playing passes at the correct moment to support fluid rotations and avoid breaking rhythm or tempo.• Receiving on the Back Foot:Encourage players to receive across their body to play forward naturally and connect actions smoothly.• Quality of Rotation:Coach players to move decisively after passing, understanding where to rotate and how to support the next action.• Communication and Scanning:Reinforce early scanning and clear verbal or visual cues to coordinate movements and maintain flow.

title: Lisbon 1v1 Into Unopposed Finish
instructions_setup: This dynamic 1v1 drill challenges players to take on a defender just outside the penalty area, working on close control, dribbling under pressure, and decision-making in tight spaces. The attacker aims to score in one of two mini goals while facing direct defensive pressure. Upon scoring, the player immediately transitions to receive an unopposed finish inside the penalty area from a coach positioned behind the main goal.If the attacker fails to score in the initial 1v1 phase, roles switch, and they become the defender in the next repetition, keeping intensity and focus high throughout continuous rotations.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Close Ball Control While Dribbling – Maintain tight control to navigate past the defender effectively and create shooting opportunities.• Encourage Quick Decision-Making Under Pressure – Players must read the defender’s movements and decide when to dribble or shoot swiftly.• Focus on Accurate Finishing in Both Phases – Prioritize clean strikes on goal whether under pressure or unopposed to maximize scoring chances.• Stress Smooth and Fast Transitions Between Roles – Switching quickly between attacker and defender roles keeps players engaged and simulates match intensity.
progression_one: Reduce Time Allowed for the 1v1 PhaseShorten the window to beat the defender to increase pressure and enhance quick thinking under tighter constraints.Focus:Develops faster reaction times, sharper dribbling skills, and improved composure during quick offensive transitions.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender in the Unopposed Finishing PhaseIntroduce a passive defender to slightly challenge the finish without full defensive pressure, encouraging improved spatial awareness and technique.Focus:Enhances finishing accuracy while adapting to minimal defensive pressure and encourages maintaining technique under slight contest.

title: Lisbon 4 Player Technical Passing
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing close control, quick passing, and effective overlapping runs between four players. The sequence involves one player passing to a teammate and then immediately making an overlapping run around them to receive a return pass. The players continuously rotate through the roles, maintaining sharp timing and accurate passing throughout the drill.By emphasizing movement off the ball and dynamic combinations, this drill improves coordination, spatial awareness, and technical precision in tight areas.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Sharp, Accurate Passing – Ensure all passes are well-weighted and directed to facilitate smooth overlaps without breaking rhythm.• Emphasize Timing of Overlapping Runs – Players should time their runs perfectly to receive the ball in stride and maintain attacking momentum.• Focus on Body Positioning for Quick Receives – Proper body orientation enables clean first touches and quicker passing decisions.• Promote Communication and Awareness – Players should constantly communicate to coordinate movements and avoid collisions or hesitation.
progression_one: Increase pace of passing and runningSpeed up the tempo to simulate game-like conditions, encouraging quicker decision-making and sharper technical execution.Focus:Develops players’ ability to perform overlapping combinations accurately at higher speeds under realistic pressure.

title: Lisbon Diagonal Set & Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing attacking combinations and smooth finishing. A player starts by playing a diagonal pass to a teammate, who then executes a quick 1-2 with the passer. After the return pass, the receiving player makes a timed run around a mannequin into the box to receive the ball and finish unopposed on goal.The continuous flow of the combination encourages timing, movement off the ball, and composure in front of goal without defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Crisp and Accurate Diagonal Passing – Ensure the initial pass sets up the 1-2 and run effectively with good weight and timing.• Focus on Timing the Run Around the Mannequin – The attacker’s movement should be perfectly timed to receive the ball in a strong scoring position.• Stress Quick, Clean First Touches During the 1-2 – Good control is key to maintaining speed, rhythm, and momentum in the attacking combination.• Promote Composure and Accuracy in the Finish – Even without pressure, focus on clean, confident, and technically sound striking of the ball.
progression_one: Add a passive defender on the run to lightly contest the attackerIntroduce a passive defender positioned near the mannequin to challenge timing and decision-making without applying full defensive pressure, promoting sharper awareness.Focus:Enhances movement timing, adaptability under mild pressure, and reinforces accurate finishing with a slight defensive challenge.

title: Lisbon Double Finish Inside The Box
instructions_setup: This drill develops attacking combinations and finishing by splitting the action into two key phases. First, the player works with a teammate outside the box to complete a combination play, receiving a through ball and finishing with a controlled shot. After scoring, the player quickly recovers by running back outside the box, performing a sharp turn around a mannequin, and then sprinting back into the penalty area for a second unopposed finish.The continuous flow of movement, combination play, and finishing sharpens both technical skills and fitness in an attacking context.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Precise Combination Play Outside the Box – The initial pass and movement should be crisp to create clear scoring chances.• Stress Timing and Accuracy of the Through Ball – Ensure the through ball splits the defense effectively for a clean first-time finish.• Focus on Quick Recovery and Sharp Movement Around the Mannequin – The turn and sprint must be explosive to maintain intensity and readiness for the second finish.• Promote Composure and Clinical Finishing in Both Phases – Even without pressure, focus on confident, well-placed shots to maximize scoring efficiency.
progression_one: Increase speed of combination and recovery runsPush players to perform the passing sequence and recovery runs at a higher tempo to simulate game pace and improve endurance.Focus:Enhances sharpness, reaction time, and ability to sustain high-intensity finishing during match scenarios.
progression_two: Add a passive defender on the initial combination phaseIntroduce light defensive pressure during the combination outside the box to challenge decision-making and precision under mild pressure.Focus:Develops composure, quick thinking, and technical accuracy when faced with defensive disruption during build-up play.

title: Lisbon Mastery Into 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a pass played across the grid to start the sequence. The receiving player dribbles the ball up to the top of the grid and makes a controlled run around a mannequin. After this, they immediately transition into a 1v1 situation against a defender who starts positioned on the bottom line of the grid. The attacker’s objective is to beat the defender and score into either of the two mini goals located on the bottom line.This drill focuses on technical mastery in tight spaces, close ball control, and quick transitions from dribbling to attacking. The 1v1 phase challenges the attacker to use skill, timing, and decision-making to create scoring opportunities under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Controlled Dribbling Around the Mannequin – Smooth, close control sets up a strong foundation for the 1v1 attack and allows better preparation for the next phase.• Encourage Sharp and Confident 1v1 Attacking Moves – The attacker must use quick feints and changes of direction to beat the defender effectively.• Stress Defensive Readiness and Positioning – The defender should maintain balanced positioning and anticipate the attacker’s moves to minimize space efficiently.• Promote Accuracy and Composure in Finishing – Scoring into one of the two mini goals requires clean, decisive strikes under pressure to increase success rate.
progression_one: Introduce a timed element for the 1v1Add a time limit for the attacker to score, increasing intensity and encouraging faster decision-making and execution in the 1v1 phase.Focus:Improves urgency, quick thinking, and composure under time pressure in attacking scenarios.

title: Lisbon Progression Rondo & Counter
instructions_setup: This dynamic drill begins with a 3v2 rondo positioned just outside the penalty area. The team of three players aims to complete six consecutive passes, maintaining possession and control before progressing the ball forward to score into one of two mini goals. If the two defenders succeed in winning possession, the drill swiftly transitions into an attacking phase.Upon gaining the ball, the two defenders leave the rondo grid to join an attacker stationed near the penalty spot, creating a 3v2 attacking situation. Meanwhile, one of the original three rondo players shifts to defend alongside the remaining defender, forming a 2v3 defensive group. This creates a fast-paced counter-attacking phase focused on quick decision-making and teamwork.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Quick, Accurate Passing in the Rondo – Maintain sharp ball circulation to build confidence and patience in possession.• Stress Awareness and Communication During Transition – Players must quickly identify roles and adapt during the switch from rondo to counter-attack.• Promote Explosive Movement in the Counter Attack – Attackers and defenders should use speed and positioning to exploit numerical advantages effectively.• Emphasize Composure and Clinical Finishing in Attack – Players must stay calm and focused to convert chances efficiently in the counter phase.
progression_one: Reduce allowed passes in rondo to 4 before progressionLower the number of passes needed to increase pressure on the rondo team and force quicker decisions.Focus:Improves rapid ball circulation, mental sharpness, and transition speed under tighter constraints.

title: Lisbon Technical Diamond Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill involves players positioned in a diamond shape, working on smooth and precise passing combinations around the shape. Players focus on quick, one-touch or two-touch passes, moving the ball efficiently around the diamond. The final player in the sequence is responsible for playing a penetrative pass into one of two mini goals positioned on either side, based on whether the passing pattern has progressed clockwise or anticlockwise.The drill develops vision, timing, and accuracy, encouraging players to read the game and choose the correct passing option under controlled pressure. It also helps improve communication and off-the-ball movement to create passing angles and support.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Crisp and Accurate Passing – Ensure each pass is well-weighted to maintain the drill’s tempo and rhythm.• Focus on Player Movement Off the Ball – Support and positioning are key to creating clear passing lanes and maintaining flow.• Stress Awareness of Passing Direction – Players must recognize whether the pattern is clockwise or anticlockwise to select the correct mini goal for the final pass.• Promote Vision and Timing of Penetrative Pass – The last pass should be well-timed and precise to effectively break the defensive line represented by the mini goals.
progression_one: Add a passive defender near the mini goalsIntroduce a defender applying light pressure to encourage sharper, more precise final passes and better decision-making in tight spaces.Focus:Develops composure, passing accuracy, and the ability to execute under mild defensive pressure with limited time.

title: Lisbon Third Man Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice begins with three players positioned outside the penalty area, working together to complete a 3rd man attacking combination. The movement should be sharp and purposeful, encouraging quick passing and dynamic support play. The third player in the combination receives the final pass facing forward and drives towards goal.Before finishing, the attacker engages in a 1v1 action against a mannequin positioned on the edge of the box. This mannequin represents a defender and should be used to simulate a change of direction or skill move before striking at goal unopposed. The focus is on smooth attacking combinations followed by clean execution in front of goal.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Quality 3rd Man Movement and Support – Ensure players time their runs and passes to break lines and create space for the final receiver.• Emphasize Tempo and Rhythm in the Combination – Quick, clean passes with minimal touches keep the move realistic and match-relevant.• Focus on Sharp Change of Direction at the Mannequin – Use a decisive skill move to simulate beating a defender before striking the ball.• Promote Composure and Clean Technique When Finishing – Players should stay balanced and focus on placement and power during the shot.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender Behind the MannequinPlace a passive defender near the mannequin to create light pressure, encouraging the attacker to be more precise with their move and finish.Focus:Improves execution of skill under pressure and enhances timing in attacking decisions, especially in tight spaces.
progression_two: Use Weak Foot for the Final ShotInstruct the attacker to finish using their weaker foot after the 1v1 movement around the mannequin.Focus:Develops confidence and technical control when finishing with the weaker foot under realistic match-like conditions.

title: Liverpool 2 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: In this drill, two teams of two work on attacking and finishing, while incorporating fitness through sprints. Play starts with the first team attacking one of the goals, receiving a cross and attempting to score. Once the shot is taken, the players must immediately sprint 30 yards to the opposite side of the field. Upon arrival, they will then attempt to score in the opposite goal after receiving another cross. This cycle is repeated, creating a continuous loop of fitness and finishing work.The drill is designed to help players improve their finishing ability while also focusing on their endurance, speed, and ability to recover quickly. The intensity of the drill increases as players continue to alternate between attacking and sprinting.
coaching_notes: • Timing the Runs: Players must time their runs correctly to meet the crosses in dangerous positions. Encourage good communication between the player delivering the cross and the one attacking the goal.• Finishing Under Pressure: Players should focus on finishing quickly and accurately, especially after sprinting long distances. Quick reactions are important to score before the defenders can recover.• Sprinting Recovery: The sprint back after finishing should be done at maximum effort, ensuring players recover and maintain a high level of intensity throughout the drill.• Cross Accuracy: Players delivering the crosses should focus on providing accurate balls into the box, with variation in height and timing to challenge the attackers.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce a defender in the box to pressure the attackers during the finishing phase. This adds a layer of challenge, forcing players to finish under pressure while maintaining the intensity of the drill.Focus: This progression enhances both fitness and decision-making under pressure, simulating match-like conditions.
progression_two: Increase Sprint Distance:Increase the sprint distance to 40 or 50 yards, depending on the fitness level of the players. This longer sprint will further challenge the players’ stamina and speed, requiring them to recover more efficiently between attacks.Focus: This progression helps improve fitness levels while maintaining finishing accuracy under fatigue.

title: Liverpool Build Up & Finish
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 3v1 build-up phase in one half of the grid. After completing 'x' number of passes, the team in possession must play forward and transition into a 3v2 attacking phase. The attacking team will attempt to break down the defense and score in the opposite goal.If the defending team wins possession during the 3v1 phase, they are immediately allowed to counterattack without needing to complete any further passes. This encourages quick transitions and improves reaction times both offensively and defensively.
coaching_notes: • Patient Build-Up: The team in possession should focus on maintaining control and completing 'x' number of passes in tight spaces, using short, quick touches to move the ball around the grid. The key is to maintain composure and look for the right moment to progress forward.• Quick Transition: If the defending team wins possession, they should look to counterattack as quickly as possible. Encourage immediate, decisive forward passes, aiming to exploit the numerical advantage before the defenders can reorganize.• Spacing and Timing: When transitioning into the 3v2 phase, the attacking team should focus on maintaining good width and depth, pulling defenders out of position to create space. Timing runs and passes is crucial to ensure a successful attack.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should work together to press and close down the ball quickly. If the defending team wins possession, they need to immediately switch focus to counterattacking, aiming for a fast-paced, direct approach.
progression_one: Introduce a Time Limit:Add a time limit for each phase. The attacking team must complete the 3v2 attack within a set number of seconds after transitioning, which will increase the urgency and intensity of the exercise.Focus: Promotes quicker decision-making, faster transitions, and sharper passing under time pressure.
progression_two: Rotate Defensive Roles:After each phase, rotate the defensive players so that different individuals get the opportunity to experience both attacking and defending roles. This ensures that all players improve their ability to transition in both directions.Focus: Develops both attacking and defensive skills, enhancing players' adaptability and overall game understanding.

title: Liverpool Counter & Recovery
instructions_setup: This practice simulates a situation where the attacking team makes a misplaced pass, creating an opportunity for the defending team to counterattack. The practice begins with a pass into the attacker, which is deliberately mishandled, allowing the defender to recover and challenge the counterattack.After the misplaced pass, the defender must quickly recover around a central pole and then attempt to stop a 2v1 counterattack. The attacking team must move quickly and exploit the momentary overload, aiming to score into the middle goal while the defense is disorganized.
coaching_notes: • React Quickly to Mistakes: After the misplaced pass, the defender must react rapidly to recover and engage the counterattack. Emphasize the need for defenders to be proactive, getting back into position as soon as possible.• Counterattack with Speed: The attacking team should focus on transitioning quickly, using the overload to their advantage. Encourage quick, direct passing and decisive runs to exploit the defensive gap before it can be closed.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Players involved in the counterattack should be encouraged to make quick decisions, deciding when to pass and when to shoot. Focus on creating opportunities with fewer touches and faster execution.• Defensive Awareness: The defender who is recovering around the pole must focus on positioning and timing their challenge. Encourage the defender to be aware of the attacking players’ movements and be prepared to disrupt the attack at the right moment.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce a second defender into the recovery phase to create a 3v2 scenario. This will allow the defenders to have a better chance of stopping the counterattack, but the attackers will still be outnumbered, encouraging them to be quicker and more efficient.Focus: Challenges attackers to move faster and make better decisions when faced with an increased defensive presence.

title: Liverpool Create through Attacking MDF
instructions_setup: In this drill, players are tasked with creating attacks through the space occupied by the attacking midfielder. The practice starts with a 3v3 setup centrally, with two bounce players stationed along either end line. These bounce players must be utilized to progress the ball and facilitate movement forward into attacking positions.To score a point, teams must successfully dribble through one of the two sets of poles positioned directly ahead of them. The bounce players provide support and help move the ball into advanced areas, ensuring teams use width and creativity to break through the defense.
coaching_notes: • Utilizing the Bounce Players: The bounce players should always be available as an outlet, helping to switch play and create new angles for attack. Encourage players to look for them when the central area is congested, using quick passes to reset and break the defensive shape.• Movement Off the Ball: Players in possession should make dynamic off-the-ball runs to create space for their teammates. Focus on encouraging the attacking midfielders to recognize when to move into pockets of space and when to stretch the defense.• Decision-Making in the Final Third: When approaching the goal or pole sets, players should decide whether to shoot, pass, or dribble based on the defensive pressure. Encourage attackers to be composed and clinical with their choices in front of goal.• Defensive Shape and Pressing: The defending players must remain compact and organized in the central area while tracking runners from the attacking side. Emphasize the importance of closing down space quickly and preventing the ball from reaching the bounce players.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for each attacking phase, where teams must attempt to score within a set period (e.g., 30 seconds). This progression forces teams to move quickly and execute faster decisions in both attack and defense.Focus: Increases the tempo of play, encouraging players to think and act faster while maintaining their composure.
progression_two: Increase Pressure with Extra Defenders:Add an extra defender to the central area to make the game 4v3 for the defending team. This will create more pressure on the attacking side and force them to find quicker, more effective ways to break through the midfield.Focus: Develops attacking players' ability to break down organized defenses and improves their technical execution under pressure.

title: Liverpool Double 1v1 into 2v2
instructions_setup: Play starts with 4 players engaging in two 1v1 matchups on half of the pitch. Each team must complete their respective 1v1 challenges, with the players involved in those matchups then transitioning to form teams for a 2v2 on the full pitch.To decide which team begins with possession, the coach can serve the ball to the team that completed their 1v1s the quickest. This encourages urgency and decision-making, as players must transition rapidly from individual duels to a collective team effort.
coaching_notes: • Winning the 1v1: Players should focus on using a variety of techniques to beat their defender, whether through quick dribbles, fakes, or changes in pace. Emphasize the importance of finishing or creating space to progress into the 2v2.• Quick Transition to 2v2: After completing the 1v1, players must quickly adjust their mindset from individual play to team collaboration. Encourage communication, positioning, and off-the-ball movement in the 2v2 to ensure they create chances and defend effectively.• Creating Space in the 2v2: Attackers should focus on stretching the field and working together to exploit gaps in the defense. Encourage the use of passes and movement off the ball to create opportunities for 1v1 situations in the final third.• Defensive Shape in the 2v2: Defenders should stay compact and work together to cover space, making it harder for the attackers to break through. Emphasize the importance of communication and tracking the attacking players' movements.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for 1v1sIntroduce a time limit for each 1v1 battle (e.g., 10 seconds) to increase the intensity of the drill. This forces players to be more decisive in their individual battles, promoting quicker decisions and faster transitions to the 2v2 phase.Focus: Sharpening players' urgency in 1v1 situations, encouraging rapid attacking moves and quicker defensive reactions under time pressure.

title: Liverpool Free Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed free kick routine drill is designed to help players rehearse and refine various attacking free kick patterns from wide or central areas. The team will focus on the key components of a successful set-piece routine including delivery, movement, and timing. Players will position themselves according to the selected routine (e.g., near post runs, edge of the box setups, far post overloads) and execute planned movements without opposition.The free kick taker will deliver the ball into a designated area, aiming for the appropriate target zone based on the play design. Meanwhile, attacking players will make synchronized runs to either meet the delivery or create decoy movements to free up teammates. This unopposed format allows the team to work on precise timing and technical execution without the distraction of defenders.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing & Synchronization:Attackers must time their runs perfectly in relation to the free kick taker’s delivery. Runs should be coordinated so that the ball is met at the optimal point, with staggered timing to create different attacking options.• Varied Movements:Players should rehearse a variety of runs including curved runs, late arrivals at the far post, and quick darts into central zones. Decoy runs and quick direction changes are essential to unsettle defenders in real match scenarios.• Delivery Execution:The free kick taker should focus on consistent and accurate delivery, using different techniques such as whipped, floated, or driven balls based on the routine. The quality of the ball into the target area is crucial to the success of the routine.• Role Clarity:Ensure every player knows their specific job in the routine — whether it’s to attack the ball, screen a defender, make a decoy run, or be in position for a second ball. Clarity in roles improves execution and reduces hesitation.• Communication:Strong verbal and non-verbal communication is essential between the free kick taker and the runners. Agreed cues or signals should trigger the movement so that everyone is synced to the delivery.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to lightly mark the runners and challenge aerially. Their role is to track movements and apply mild resistance without aggressively disrupting play.Focus: This adds realism and forces the attacking team to fine-tune timing and positioning under game-like conditions while still maintaining the structure of the routine.

title: Liverpool One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 drill is designed to develop a player's ability to receive under control, dribble with intent, and finish the move with an accurate pass. The player works through a series of technical tasks that require quick feet, sharp ball control, and decisive execution. Each repetition ends with a pass into a mini goal to simulate playing a decisive final ball.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Taking a Positive First Touch Into Space – Guide the ball into your path to set up the next action cleanly and keep momentum going forward.• Maintain Close Control While Dribbling at Speed – Keep the ball within playing distance when accelerating, turning, and navigating tight areas with sharp touches.• Scan Before Receiving to Make Early Decisions – Check surroundings for space, pressure, and next action before the ball arrives to stay one step ahead.• Use Different Surfaces When Passing Under Pressure – Vary between inside, laces, and outside foot for better control, disguised passes, and improved weight.
progression_one: Increase the Speed of RepetitionsReduce rest time and increase tempo to challenge decision-making and technique under fatigue.Focus:Improves technical execution, body control, and passing clarity while under physical and mental pressure.

title: Liverpool Passing Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this passing warm-up, two players positioned horizontally to each other will run 30 yards, passing the ball side to side through a series of vertically positioned mannequins. The players should focus on precise, short passes as they work around the mannequins. Once they reach the top of the grid, they'll jog back down and repeat the drill.
coaching_notes: • Accurate Passing: Emphasize the importance of crisp, accurate passes between the players. The ball should be passed with enough weight to ensure it reaches the intended player, but not too much that it becomes difficult to control.• Body Position: Players should maintain good body position when receiving the ball, staying on their toes and ready to receive and quickly pass. This will help improve the flow of the exercise and encourage fluid movement.• Head Up and Scanning: Encourage players to keep their heads up and scan for the next pass. This helps with better decision-making and awareness of teammates' movements.• Communication: Encourage vocal communication between players to help them stay organized and ensure smooth transitions throughout the drill.
progression_one: Add 1-Touch Passing:Introduce a one-touch passing restriction once players reach the top. This increases the tempo of the drill, helping players develop quick decision-making and ball control under pressure.Focus: Enhances the ability to pass quickly and accurately, encouraging quicker reactions and improving the flow of passing sequences.
progression_two: Add Movement After Passing:Players must make a forward run or move laterally after completing a pass. This progression focuses on encouraging dynamic movement off the ball and helps replicate the need for players to move into space in real-game scenarios.Focus: Promotes off-the-ball movement, improving players' ability to create space and offer passing options.

title: Liverpool Receiving Between Lines
instructions_setup: This ball mastery drill focuses on developing a player’s ability to receive the ball between the lines and quickly turn into space to play a forward pass. Players will travel through the grid, receive a pass from the coach, and then use various techniques to turn into space and deliver a quality forward pass into the mini goal.
coaching_notes: • First Touch and Control: Emphasize the importance of a clean first touch when receiving the ball. The player should control the ball with the inside or sole of the foot, directing it into space to set up the next move efficiently.• Turning Technique: Encourage players to use different turning techniques, such as the Cruyff turn or a quick pivot, depending on the situation. This will help them maintain possession while changing direction to face forward.• Passing Accuracy: When playing the forward pass, players should aim for precision and weight, ensuring the pass is played with the correct amount of force to reach the mini goal. Focus on both short and long-range passing.• Awareness and Vision: Encourage players to constantly scan the field for space before receiving the ball. This allows them to make better decisions on the type of turn and pass needed to progress play.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure:Introduce a passive defender who applies pressure on the player after receiving the ball. The defender’s role is to force the player into making quicker decisions while maintaining control of the ball and executing a forward pass.Focus: Develops the ability to perform under pressure and encourages quick thinking, improving players' decision-making when receiving in tight spaces.
progression_two: Increase the Distance of the Pass:Increase the distance between the player and the mini goal, requiring a longer, more accurate pass. This will challenge the player’s passing ability, helping them improve their vision and weight of pass over greater distances.Focus: Improves long-range passing accuracy, helping players develop the ability to pass effectively over a larger area.

title: Liverpool Rondo to Finishing
instructions_setup: Play begins with 6 players in possession against 2 defenders in a tight grid. The team in possession must complete 'x' number of passes before they can attempt to score. This encourages quick ball circulation, communication, and movement off the ball to break down the defensive pressure. The attacking team must focus on maintaining possession while looking for opportunities to progress and take a shot on goal.If the defending team wins possession, they can immediately attempt to score in either of the goals, adding an element of pressure and creating a transition phase for both sides. This promotes the importance of defensive work and counter-attacking from the defenders, while the attacking team must react quickly to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Ball Circulation: Encourage quick, sharp passes between players while maintaining a good spread across the grid. Players should focus on moving into space to create passing options and ensure fluidity in the attack.• Quick Decision Making: Players need to make decisions quickly and play at tempo to avoid being caught out by the defenders. Encourage players to think ahead and anticipate the next pass or movement.• Defensive Transition: Once possession is lost, players should immediately react to pressure the ball, forcing errors or creating turnovers. Emphasize the importance of high work rate in regaining possession.• Maintain Shape: In possession, players should keep good width and depth to stretch the defensive block and create passing lanes. Avoid congesting the space and allow for better movement and options.
progression_one: Increase Passes Required:Increase the number of passes required before the attacking team can attempt to score. This will force the attacking team to keep possession for longer periods and improve their patience in build-up play.Focus: Develops patience in possession and improves ball retention under pressure.
progression_two: Defenders Play Out of Possession:Allow the defending team to attempt to play out from the back once they win possession, rather than immediately going for a goal. This can encourage them to build confidence and composure in transition.Focus: Enhances defensive skills in possession and promotes a more structured transition from defense to attack.

title: Liverpool Up & Down SSG
instructions_setup: In this dynamic small-sided game, three separate pitches are used simultaneously, with each team playing 2v2 (or 3v3), and each game is limited to 1 minute of play. This format creates a fast-paced environment where players must think and act quickly. The focus is on compact and efficient play, with each team trying to outplay their opponents in a short, intense period.At the end of each minute, the winning team moves up a pitch (unless they're already playing on the top pitch), while the losing team drops to the next pitch (unless they are on the bottom). If the game ends in a draw, the team that scored first is declared the winner. In the case of a 0-0 draw, the highest-ranked team will be considered the loser, adding a unique twist and keeping the pressure on even the top teams.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision Making: Players need to make fast decisions as the game is played at high speed. Encourage players to focus on creating opportunities and exploiting the spaces available in a short amount of time.• High Intensity: Emphasize constant movement, both with and without the ball, to keep the game quick. Players should always be in motion, creating space and angles for their teammates.• Mental Focus: The fast-paced nature of the game means players must remain focused and alert, even if the tempo slows down. Quick restarts are crucial to maintaining momentum.• Teamwork and Communication: Since each game is only 1 minute long, effective communication and team cohesion are essential. Players should constantly be in sync, offering options and support for one another.
progression_one: Increase Game Length:Extend the time on each game to 2 minutes to allow players to build more offensive and defensive combinations while maintaining the same level of intensity.Focus: Develops stamina and consistency in high-pressure situations.
progression_two: Introduce a 'Power Play' Period:Designate a 20-second 'power play' where one team has an additional player for the duration of the period, adding an extra tactical challenge for both teams.Focus: Promotes quick decision making and adaptability under different tactical conditions.

title: Liverpool Wide Overloads
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 2v1 overload in the wide areas, where a full-back and winger combine to progress the ball. The focus is on building quick, dynamic combinations on the flanks to break down defensive pressure and create attacking opportunities. Players need to work together to shift the opposition and make the most of the overload in the wide space.Once the wide progression is successful, two attacking players make runs into the box, where they will face off against two defending players in a 2v2 scenario. The attacking players aim to finish from a cross delivered into the penalty area. Timing of runs, communication, and accurate delivery are crucial to completing the attack.
coaching_notes: • Wide Combinations: Focus on the quick interplay between the full-back and winger. They should aim to move the ball quickly, utilizing the overload to create space for forward progression.• Crossing Timing: Encourage the winger to deliver early crosses when possible, but also to wait for the attacking players to get into position. Timing of the delivery should align with the attacking runs into the box.• Attacking Runs: Players making runs into the box should focus on timing their movements to attack the space created by the cross. They must aim for varied runs to create confusion for the defenders.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders must track attackers and communicate to prevent easy goals. They should focus on staying compact while defending in a 2v2 scenario.
progression_one: Add a Third Defender:Introduce a third defender to the 2v2 scenario, making it a 3v2 for the defending team. This increases the challenge for the attacking players and allows defenders to practice managing overloads.Focus: Enhances defensive positioning and communication under pressure.
progression_two: Finish with Different Techniques:Limit finishing to one specific technique, such as heading, volleys, or finishing with the weaker foot, to encourage technical development in various aspects of attacking play.Focus: Develops different finishing techniques and improves players' adaptability in the final third.

title: Lorient 1 & 2 Touch Technical
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up allows players to work in a small space and develop their 1- and 2-touch passing in a high-intensity practice. Variation 1 shows players using 1 touch only before moving out to the side for the next player, while variation 2 shows the players using 2 touches before moving out for the next player. In the 2-touch variation, players must work on close control and slowing the ball, allowing them to make a clean forward pass with their second touch.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing Decisions – In the 1-touch variation, players should focus on making quick, decisive passes. They need to scan the field before receiving the ball to ensure they can pass immediately. This will improve their ability to read the game and make fast decisions under pressure.• Close Control in 2-Touch – In the 2-touch variation, players should use their first touch to control the ball, setting up their second touch for a clean pass. Emphasis should be placed on close control, ensuring the ball stays within a manageable range for the second touch.• Movement off the Ball – Players should always be moving to create passing angles. Whether in the 1-touch or 2-touch variation, players need to position themselves to receive the ball effectively and pass it to the next player without delay.• Passing Accuracy – Players should focus on the accuracy of their passes. The second touch should be precise and clean, allowing the next player to receive the ball in the best possible position for their next move.
progression_one: Increase SpeedAs players become more comfortable with the 1- and 2-touch variations, increase the intensity and speed of the practice. Players should focus on executing each pass quicker while maintaining accuracy.Focus: Speed and precision under pressure.
progression_two: Add Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to apply light pressure on the players. This encourages players to be more efficient with their touches and passing decisions, simulating a more game-like scenario.Focus: Handling pressure while maintaining accuracy and quick decision-making.

title: Lorient 3 Phase Crossing
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing drill focuses on developing players’ ability to cross the ball after making positive forward runs in wider areas. The practice involves three phases:The first phase sees players making a run into the wide areas to receive a pass and cross the ball (low, driven, or floated).The second phase involves the same crossers but from a different angle or a deeper position.The third phase requires the crossers to repeat the process under stress or fatigue, encouraging them to maintain high-quality crosses in a dynamic situation. Players should complete all three phases in one repetition to simulate real match conditions.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing and Movement – Players must focus on making positive, timed runs into the wide areas. These runs should be made with enough speed and intent to meet the ball in stride, enabling an effective cross.• Crossing Techniques – Encourage variety in crossing techniques. Low, driven crosses should be used for players arriving at the near post, while floated crosses are ideal for players attacking the far post or for crosses into the back of the box.• Decision-Making – Players should make quick decisions on the type of cross to play, depending on the movement and positioning of the attacking players in the box. Knowing when to use a driven or floated ball can make a huge difference.• Fatigue Management – Since the drill progresses through three phases, remind players to maintain focus and energy management throughout. Quality crosses should remain the priority, even as fatigue sets in.
progression_one: Mini Goals as TargetsPlace several mini goals as targets instead of one big goal. This adds a layer of decision-making for the crossers, who must target specific areas rather than aiming for a single large goal.Focus: Develops accuracy and decision-making while adding variety to the crossing technique based on the runners’ positions.
progression_two: Multiple Runners into the BoxIntroduce multiple runners into the box, forcing the crossers to read the situation and adapt their crosses accordingly.Focus: Increases the challenge for crossers by replicating game scenarios where multiple attacking players are competing for the ball in the box.

title: Lorient 343 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 343 formation down into specific zones, where the possession team will play 4v2 or 3v2. The #6 can be allowed to slide vertically to create 4v2's in the top 2 zones, while the #9 is required to slide horizontally to work across 2 zones. The practice transitions into a 6v3 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness – The #6 should focus on their movement between zones, ensuring they create overloads in the top two zones. Encourage the player to be aware of when to slide vertically and when to remain in position to help control the build-up.• Pressing Principles – The pressing team should work on closing down passing lanes and forcing the possession team into less favorable areas. Pressing players need to anticipate the ball and use their positioning to limit the number of passing options for the attackers.• Horizontal Movement – The #9 should focus on working across two zones to support the build-up play and provide passing options. They must adjust their position to maximize space and facilitate quick transitions.• Quick Transitions – If the pressing team regains possession, they need to transition quickly into a 6v3 central overload. Players must be aware of the available space and exploit it to create attacking opportunities.
progression_one: Smaller GridReduce the size of the grid to increase pressure on the possession team. This will force quicker decision-making and improve passing accuracy under pressure.Focus: Improving decision-making and passing speed under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Counter-Attack PhaseAllow the pressing team to counter-attack quickly if they regain possession, transitioning from a 6v3 central overload into a fast-paced counter. The defending team must react and reorganize quickly to prevent the counter.

title: Lorient 3v2 Counter Attacking
instructions_setup: This is a continuous 3v2 counter-attacking drill that emphasizes quick transitions and decision-making in overload situations. Each phase begins with a 3v2 attack toward goal. Once the attack concludes, one attacker (the last player to touch the ball) drops out, while an additional attacker joins the two defenders to form the new attacking trio for the next wave. The ball is always served by the coach to the fresh attacker, maintaining tempo and encouraging fast, realistic transitions between attack and defense.
coaching_notes: • Transition Speed – Emphasize rapid transition from defense to attack and vice versa. Players should react immediately to the change of phase, simulating a real match environment.• Communication – Encourage defenders and attackers to communicate clearly during overlaps, recovery runs, and tracking runners to manage the overload.• Decision-Making in Overload – The 3 attackers must quickly identify when to exploit numerical superiority through passes, dribbles, or shots.• Defensive Shape – The 2 defenders should focus on delaying the attack, staying compact, and forcing play into less dangerous areas to buy time for recovery.
progression_one: Limited Touches for AttackersRestrict the attacking trio to two-touch play to increase speed of thought and ball movement.Focus: Enhances quick decision-making and forces players to be efficient with limited touches in the final third.
progression_two: Time Limit to ScoreIntroduce a five-second time limit for the 3v2 attack to result in a shot on goal.Focus: Increases urgency in the attack and simulates the fast-paced nature of counter-attacking opportunities in matches.

title: Lorient 442 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 442 formation down into specific zones, where the possession team will play 3v2. The team out of possession must have 1 player in all 4 zones at all times, meaning they can press with any 2 players inside the ball zone. The practice transitions into a 5v3 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Movement in Possession – The possession team should focus on maintaining a fluid and dynamic structure, with the 3 players in the ball zone working together to create passing lanes and overload the defenders. The key is to use short, sharp passes to break the defensive lines and progress the ball.• Pressing with 2 Players – The defending team should use two players inside the ball zone to press aggressively. One player should always be ready to intercept or block passes, while the second player helps close down space and force the attacking team to play backwards or make a mistake.• Spatial Awareness – Both the attacking and defending teams must have excellent spatial awareness. The attacking team should constantly adjust their positions to open up passing lanes, while the defending team must keep their shape intact and work as a unit to prevent easy passes.• Transition to 5v3 – Once the defending team wins possession, they should look to transition quickly into a 5v3 overload centrally. This allows them to create a numerical advantage and exploit the space in the central areas before the defending team can reorganize.
progression_one: Reduced Grid SizeTo increase the tempo and pressure, reduce the size of the grid. This forces quicker decision-making and requires players to be more precise with their passes and movements. The defending team will need to be even more coordinated in their pressing efforts.Focus: Improving speed of play and pressure awareness.
progression_two: Additional Attacking SupportAdd a neutral player or two who can be used by the possession team to help break through the press. These neutral players should be positioned outside the ball zone and able to receive passes, giving the attacking team more options and space to work with.Focus: Enhancing attacking movement, creating overloads, and building effective passing sequences.

title: Lorient Attacking 2v2
instructions_setup: This practice starts with a pass into a centre forward who is under pressure from a defender behind. As soon as the pass is played, all players become live and engage in a 2v2 situation until the ball is dead. Teams can alternate roles after every repetition or complete a set number of reps before switching.
