Players should rotate through both attacking and defending roles, ensuring they experience starting positions both with their back to goal and facing forward.
coaching_notes: • Back-to-Goal Play – When the centre forward receives the ball under pressure, they must focus on holding possession, using their body to shield the ball and creating space for a quick pass or turn.• Forward-Facing Play – Players in the attacking phase should aim to break free of their defender quickly, using smart movement and timing to receive the ball in a forward-facing position to exploit attacking opportunities.• Defensive Awareness – Defenders should pressure the attacker efficiently, focusing on positioning themselves to block passes or anticipate turns, ensuring they are tight but not over-committed.• Transition and Switching Roles – Encourage quick transitions between attacking and defending roles. Players should react swiftly, either by closing down the ball after losing possession or making the most of counter-attacks when regaining the ball.
progression_one: Limit Touches for AttackersRestrict the attackers to a set number of touches (e.g., two or three).Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and increases the intensity of the 2v2 situations, simulating match conditions.
progression_two: Add a Support PlayerIntroduce a neutral player or additional attacker to support the 2v2 scenario.Focus: Adds complexity to the attacking phase, challenging defenders to deal with more threats and allowing the attackers to combine in a more dynamic manner.

title: Lorient Close Combinations & Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on quick, fluid combinations in and around the penalty area. In Variation #1, the centre forward drops deep to receive the ball and plays a first-time pass around the corner for a forward runner to attack the space. In Variation #2, the centre forward again drops deep but this time plays a 1-2 combination, receiving the return pass in the vacated space beyond the defenders to finish on goal. Both variations aim to enhance the timing and execution of quick attacking combinations in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – The forward runners must time their movements to meet the ball in stride, ensuring they’re in the right position to receive the pass and finish with minimal delay.• Combination Play – Emphasize quick, sharp passing between attackers. The centre forward should focus on playing the pass with the right weight, while the runner should focus on their positioning to break the defensive line.• Body Positioning for Finishing – Attackers should be aware of their body positioning when receiving the ball, preparing themselves to finish quickly and accurately under pressure.• Awareness of Space – Players should always be scanning for available space, whether it’s the deep run after a 1-2 or the space around the corner for a quick pass. The centre forward should identify and exploit gaps in the defence.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce one defender to apply passive pressure on the attacker as they receive the ball.Focus: Simulates more realistic game pressure, improving attackers’ ability to perform quick combinations while under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Vary the Cross or DeliveryInstead of always playing through the centre, vary the delivery to either side, allowing the forward runners to make different attacking runs.Focus: Increases variety in attacking combinations and encourages players to adjust their runs based on different delivery types.

title: Los Angeles 1v1 Transitional Dribbling
instructions_setup: This is a continuous 1v1 dribbling practice where players must constantly transition between attacking and defending roles. Players score points by beating their opponent in a 1v1 and dribbling through either of the 2 gates.The starting zones are positioned 5 yards behind the main zone, allowing players enough time to transition back into the zone after their attacking phase. This setup ensures that players are always moving and can practice quick recoveries after an attack.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Quick Transitions – Encourage players to quickly shift from attack to defense. After every attacking phase, they need to transition back quickly to defend the next 1v1.• Change of Pace – Players should focus on varying their pace during the dribble, using sudden bursts of speed to beat their opponent. This will keep the defender guessing and improve their attacking skills.• Defensive Awareness – In the defensive phase, players should focus on positioning themselves well to prevent the attacker from getting past them. They must balance aggression with control to avoid being easily beaten.• Exploit the Space – Once the ball is won, the attacker should look for the quickest path to the gates. Encourage players to use their dribbling skills to exploit the space and get through the gates as efficiently as possible.
progression_one: Add More GatesIncrease the number of gates in the area, giving players more options for scoring. This will force attackers to be more creative with their dribbling and decision-making, while defenders will need to work harder to cover more angles.Focus: Decision-making and exploiting multiple scoring opportunities.
progression_two: Introduce Time Limit for TransitionsAdd a time limit for how quickly players must transition between attacking and defending phases. This will increase the intensity and focus on speed of recovery and attack.Focus: Speed of recovery and maintaining focus under pressure.

title: Los Angeles Attacking Full Backs
instructions_setup: In this practice, players develop the ability to dribble at speed with the ball while under pressure from behind. The two attacking players must dribble and combine before scoring into the mini goal, once the ball has crossed the dotted line. The two defending players must make recovery runs and attempt to stop the attacking duo from scoring by putting them under pressure, forcing a mistake, or regaining possession.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling with Speed and Control – Emphasize the importance of dribbling at full speed while maintaining control of the ball. The attacking players should focus on quick changes of direction to keep the defenders off balance. Encourage them to use their body to shield the ball from the defenders, especially when under pressure.• Effective Combination Play – The attacking players should work together to create space and create an overload. This could involve quick passes, one-twos, or overlapping runs to break down the defensive structure. Stress the importance of timing and movement off the ball to support each other in tight spaces.• Defensive Recovery and Pressure – The defenders must focus on making quick recovery runs after losing initial position. They should work on closing down the attacking players quickly, forcing them to make decisions under pressure. Encourage defenders to be proactive in their attempts to regain possession or block shooting lanes.• Finishing Under Pressure – The attacking players need to be clinical in their finishing once they have created an opening. The emphasis should be on shooting with composure and precision when presented with a chance to score into the mini goal. Encourage them to be aware of the defender’s positioning and adjust their shots accordingly.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Attacking PlayerIntroduce a neutral attacking player who plays in the space between the defenders and the goal. This player can help with combination play, creating a 3v2 overload in favor of the attackers.Focus: This progression allows the attacking team to work with an extra player to open up space and practice fluid combinations under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Defenders to One Recovery RunLimit the defenders to only one recovery run, after which they must stay in position or act as a passive defender. This will increase the attacking team’s opportunities to break the defensive line and score.Focus: This progression forces the defending players to be more strategic in their recovery and positioning, while the attackers get more chances to break through and practice finishing.

title: Los Angeles Back 3 Build Up Patterns
instructions_setup: This passing activation allows players to work on developing build-up patterns and relationships while playing in a back 3 shape. The build-up is heavily focused on a 3-2 build-up shape with central combinations. The aim is to create a fluid transition from the back, ensuring the ball is circulated efficiently before being played into the attacking areas.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness – Ensure that the players in the back 3 maintain good width to stretch the opposition. The wing-backs should push high to provide width, while the central defenders maintain strong positioning to retain possession.• Central Combinations – Emphasize the importance of central passing patterns between the center-backs and midfielders. Encourage players to recognize when to play short, quick combinations and when to switch play.• Building Through the Midfield – In this shape, it's vital for the two central midfielders to offer support to the ball carrier, constantly looking for angles to receive and progress the play. Ensure that they rotate positions, creating space for each other.• Switching the Play – Teach the defenders to use diagonal switches effectively to break the opposition’s lines. This requires the center-backs to look for space and pick out long, accurate passes to the wing-backs or midfielders.
progression_one: Add Pressing OppositionIntroduce opposition players who will press the central areas. The defenders must adapt their build-up play, ensuring they play with composure and look to bypass the press with quick passing or well-timed switches.Focus: Improving decision-making under pressure when building from the back.
progression_two: Wing-Back MovementHave the wing-backs make timed overlapping or underlapping runs once the ball has moved into midfield. This will allow them to receive the ball further up the pitch, increasing the attacking options for the team.Focus: Using wing-backs effectively as attacking outlets and ensuring the build-up from the back is dynamic and progressive.

title: Los Angeles Create in Wide Areas
instructions_setup: This attacking practice focuses on creating and finishing opportunities in wide areas. Play starts with the goalkeeper making a long pass to a central player. The central player then passes the ball into one of the two wide grids on the field. From this point, the attacking team must work to progress the play down the wide area. To increase the attacking options, the deeper central player or one of the central attackers can join the wide grid to create a 4v3 or 5v3 overload. Once the ball is successfully progressed in the wide area, the team must attempt to finish the attack with 2 or 3 players attacking the space in the box.
coaching_notes: • Wide Area Progression – The initial pass into the wide grid should be precise and well-weighted. The player receiving the ball in the wide area must quickly decide whether to drive toward the byline, cut inside, or deliver a cross.• Overloading the Wide Area – Encourage the deeper central player or central attackers to join the wide grid in order to create an overload, which forces the defending team to adjust and open up space for attacking opportunities. This will help develop attacking width and supporting runs.• Movement in the Final Third – Once the ball is in the wide area, attackers should look to make runs into the box. One attacker should aim for the near post, another for the far post, and one should be ready to make a late run for a cutback. Emphasize timing of runs and spacing to create goal-scoring opportunities.• Quick Decision-Making – The player with the ball in the wide area should make a quick decision on whether to cross, dribble, or pass based on the position of the attacking runners and the defenders.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure in Wide AreasIntroduce a defender into the wide grid to create a 3v2 or 4v3 overload. This will challenge the attacking team to be more precise with their decision-making and movement in tight spaces.Focus:Improves decision-making in tight areas and encourages attacking players to recognize when to commit defenders and when to pass.
progression_two: Targeted FinishingSet up mini-goals or cones inside the box to serve as specific target areas. Players should focus on delivering accurate crosses into these areas for specific attacking players to finish, replicating the need for precision in crossing.Focus:Develops accuracy in crossing and finishing under pressure, ensuring that attackers can finish crosses in specific target zones (e.g., near-post, far-post, or central).

title: Los Angeles Double 1v1 in Wide Areas
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on developing 1v1 ability in wide areas before cutting inside to create shooting opportunities. The drill runs with two live balls, and play always starts with the goalkeepers who serve passes into the attackers. The attackers must then play 1v1 in a narrow wide channel, aiming to beat the defender and find space for a shot on goal. Once they have created the opportunity, they should finish with composure.
coaching_notes: • 1v1 Skill Development – Attackers should focus on using a variety of dribbling moves (e.g., feints, step-overs, or quick changes of direction) to beat the defender. The key is to get the defender off balance and commit them, allowing the attacker to break into space.• Cutting Inside – After beating the defender in the wide area, the attacker should focus on cutting inside with speed, making sure to shield the ball from the defender. This will open up the angle for a shot while keeping the defender out of the equation.• Creating Shooting Space – Attackers should focus on using their body position and quick footwork to create space for themselves when cutting inside. They must also be aware of the goalkeeper's positioning to ensure they can get a clean shot off.• Composure in Front of Goal – Once in shooting range, attackers must focus on finishing with composure. Whether it's a low shot to the far post or a powerful strike, the emphasis should be on accuracy and technique.
progression_one: Add Defenders in the BoxIntroduce additional defenders inside the box to challenge the attacker once they cut inside. This increases the pressure and encourages attackers to be more precise with their dribbling and finishing.Focus: Increases difficulty, simulating more realistic game scenarios where attackers face multiple defensive challenges.
progression_two: Vary the Passing DeliveryChange the type of pass the goalkeeper plays into the attacker (e.g., high ball, driven pass, or chipped pass). This will encourage attackers to adjust their first touch and make decisions quickly.Focus: Helps attackers adapt to different types of service and refine their ability to control and attack from various angles.

title: Los Angeles Finishing From Cutbacks
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on attacking movements and finishing from cutbacks. The sequence starts with a short passing combination between central players, leading to a threaded through ball into a wide runner. The wide player drives toward the byline and delivers a cutback into the box, where a single attacker times their run for an unopposed finish. Emphasis is placed on timing, movement, and clean execution in front of goal.
coaching_notes: • Wide Player Delivery – Encourage consistent cutbacks pulled into the edge of the 6-yard box or penalty spot. Vary the angle and speed depending on the runner’s position.• Attacker’s Run Timing – The attacker must time their run so they arrive at the right moment, avoiding being too early or late. Emphasize scanning and reading the wide player’s body shape.• First-Time Finishing – Encourage players to finish with one touch when possible. Focus on balance, body shape, and hitting the corners.• Quality of Combination Play – Ensure initial passes and through balls are played with sharpness and accuracy to replicate game tempo.
progression_one: Passive Defender in the BoxAdd a passive defender near the cutback zone to create mild interference and force the attacker to adjust their movement and finishing angle.Focus:Helps the attacker refine movement in tight areas and develop composure when finishing under slight pressure.
progression_two: Two Attackers Timing Separate RunsIntroduce a second attacker into the box, with one making a near-post run and the other arriving centrally or far post.Focus:Promotes varied attacking options and decision-making for both the crosser and the finishers. Encourages awareness and communication in front of goal.

title: Los Angeles Finishing From Long Diagonals
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on forward passing, forward running, and finishing. The drill begins with a horizontal pass, after which the passer immediately makes a hard forward run to attack space inside the box. The player who received the initial pass then plays a long diagonal ball into the space where the attacking player is running. Players should be encouraged to vary their finishing techniques, using either first-time finishes or taking a touch to control the ball before finishing, depending on their distance from goal and the timing of the pass.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – The player making the forward run must time their movement to arrive in the box just as the ball is played into the space. They should look to anticipate the pass and attack the space quickly and decisively.• Passing Accuracy – The player delivering the diagonal ball should focus on accuracy and weight, ensuring the ball is played into the correct area for the attacker to run onto, allowing for an easy first-time finish or a controlled touch.• Finishing Technique – Encourage players to adjust their finishing technique based on the situation. For close-range balls, a first-time finish may be ideal, while a controlled touch followed by a finish is better for balls played further away.• Awareness of Space – The player receiving the ball must be aware of the space they are attacking and adjust their run accordingly. The key is to ensure the ball is played into a position where the attacker can control and finish without pressure from defenders.
progression_one: Add Defenders for PressureIntroduce a defender into the box to apply light pressure on the attacker after receiving the ball, forcing them to finish under pressure.Focus: Simulates real-game conditions, where attackers must finish while dealing with defensive pressure.
progression_two: Vary the Type of CrossVary the type of diagonal pass (e.g., low driven crosses, lofted crosses) to challenge the attacker to adjust their finishing technique.Focus: Enhances the attacker’s ability to finish from different types of deliveries and improve adaptability in the box.

title: Los Angeles Mastery Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this warm-up drill, one player is located centrally within a grid, surrounded by 3 outside players. Directly ahead of the outside players are 3 gates, each a different color. The central player is positioned inside the gates, requiring quick adjustment based on the passes and commands from the outside players.The outside players will pass the ball into the central player and shout a color corresponding to one of the gates. The central player must quickly adjust, dribble or pass the ball out of the grid through the colored gate called out. The drill is continuous, with the central player working for 45 seconds before switching to another player.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: The central player needs to be alert and ready to react quickly. They should focus on quickly processing the color shout and adjusting their movement or pass to execute the correct response.• Body Positioning: As the central player, always try to be in a balanced and open body position, which will allow for quicker adjustments when a specific gate color is called out. This encourages a fluid transition in movement.• Pass Accuracy and Timing: When passing out of the gates, the central player must ensure the pass is accurate and timed well. This is key to maintaining the flow of the drill and keeping the outside players ready for their next actions.• Communication from Outside Players: The outside players should shout the gate color clearly and use visual cues when necessary. It’s important that their calls are quick and direct, which will help the central player anticipate and act efficiently.
progression_one: Increase the Complexity of Gate Movements:Introduce additional variations such as requiring the central player to dribble through the gate, or to make a quick change of direction before passing the ball out. This progression would add complexity to the central player’s movements.Focus: Develops agility, reaction time, and the ability to make decisions quickly under pressure while also improving technical passing accuracy.

title: Los Angeles Thirds & Finishing
instructions_setup: In this 3rd’s practice, the players will progress through three zones. The first two zones are single-defended, where players must work to progress the ball while overcoming one defender. After these initial phases, they will enter the final zone, where a 3v2 attack occurs. The attacking players must make use of their forward momentum, utilizing quick attacking combinations and dynamic movements to finish the attack at speed. The goal is to exploit the overload in the final zone and create a goal-scoring opportunity through well-timed runs and precise passing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations – Players should focus on using quick passing combinations (such as one-twos or wall passes) to break through the defended zones. This will help maintain attacking momentum and force the defenders to react under pressure.• Decision Making – Encourage attackers to make quick decisions about when to pass and when to attack the space themselves. Players should recognize when the 3v2 overload occurs and make sure they take advantage of this numerical superiority to create a high-quality scoring chance.• Speed and Timing – Timing of runs and passes is crucial. Players should aim to move the ball quickly through the zones while also timing their forward runs to receive the ball in stride. The emphasis should be on executing the final pass or shot at speed to avoid giving defenders a chance to recover.• Movement off the Ball – The attackers should focus on making constant runs off the ball to create passing lanes and stretch the defenders. Players should look for opportunities to drag defenders out of position, opening up spaces for teammates to exploit.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure in Early PhasesIntroduce a second defender into the first two zones to increase the difficulty and pressure. This progression will challenge the attackers to work even faster and more efficiently in breaking down the defense.Focus:Improves ability to make quick decisions and perform under pressure.
progression_two: Transition Phase After Final AttackOnce the attack in the 3v2 zone is completed, transition the remaining attackers to defend in a counter-attacking scenario. This will encourage the attackers to move quickly into defense, simulating the transition from offense to defense after an attack.Focus:Develops understanding of both attacking and defending transitions in fast-paced game situations.

title: Lyon 4 Phase Fitness Rondo
instructions_setup: The practice consists of four 5x5 grids, each with one ball, and five teams. The attackers aim to maintain possession, while the defenders focus on winning the ball back.Each grid will operate as a 4v1 rondo, with the attacking team working to keep possession. Once a defender wins the ball in a grid, they shout a signal to indicate the rotation. Upon hearing the signal, the four defenders rotate simultaneously, moving to the next grid in a predetermined order. The rotation continues until each defender has had the chance to defend in all four grids.
coaching_notes: • Defensive Intensity: Defenders should focus on closing down space quickly and anticipating the attackers' passes. The goal is to win the ball as quickly as possible while applying pressure without leaving gaps.• Attacking Movement: The attacking players should focus on quick, sharp movement off the ball to create passing lanes and options for the player in possession. The key is maintaining possession and playing simple passes to retain the ball.• Communication: Both defenders and attackers must communicate continuously. Defenders should call out their movements, and attackers should give clear passing cues to each other. Communication helps maintain fluidity in the rondo.• Staying Active: Encourage the defenders to stay active and engaged, especially during the transitions between grids. The drill’s intensity relies on quick rotations and high work rates. Attackers should also focus on quick ball movement to challenge the defenders.
progression_one: Add Time PressureIntroduce a time limit for how long attackers must maintain possession (e.g., 30 seconds). If the attackers maintain possession for the set time, they earn a point. This encourages faster ball movement and decision-making under pressure.Focus: Increases the pace of play, forcing attackers to be more decisive and defensive players to be more aggressive in their pressing.

title: Lyon 7 Angle Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing drill focuses on developing the ability to finish from various angles around the penalty area. A center player is positioned at the top of the box and is surrounded by seven servers positioned at different angles. The servers pass the ball in from different directions, simulating varied game situations where an attacker might receive passes from different areas on the field. The center player must react quickly to each pass, maintaining focus and sharpness in their finishing.As the coach calls out a number, the attacker must react to the pass and finish with a maximum of two touches. This encourages quick decision-making, touch control, and precise finishing under pressure. The exercise mimics real match scenarios where strikers must adjust to different types of service and take advantage of goal-scoring opportunities with minimal time to execute.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions: Encourage the attacker to focus on reacting quickly to the coach's call. Speed of movement and decision-making are key to ensuring they can complete the finish in just two touches.• First Touch: The first touch should be under control and set up the attacker for a quick, accurate finish. The focus should be on soft touches that allow for a clean shot at goal.• Finishing Accuracy: Remind the player to aim for specific areas of the goal. They should be encouraged to finish with precision rather than power, targeting corners or the space the goalkeeper has left open.• Adaptability: The attacker should be adaptable, adjusting their body position based on the angle of the ball and their distance from goal, ensuring a variety of finishing techniques are used.
progression_one: Increase Touch Limitation:Reduce the number of touches allowed to one per pass. This forces quicker decisions and more clinical finishes in tight spaces.Focus: Develops quicker reactions and sharper finishing techniques in high-pressure situations.

title: Lyon Cross & Finish Game
instructions_setup: This practice is designed to simulate a fast-paced, continuous attacking and defensive scenario. Three attacking players will work together to deliver a cross into the box, while three defenders attempt to deny them any goal-scoring opportunities. The defenders must stay alert and position themselves effectively to prevent a shot on target, using communication and teamwork to disrupt the attacking play.Once the defensive team completes their task, they must quickly transition to the opposite side of the grid, where they will now become the attacking team. This transition is seamless, allowing for continuous play with new attacking players constantly entering the grid. This drill is especially useful in pre-season training, as it combines attacking play with the necessity for quick transitions, while also helping players work on disguised runs and attacking timing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of quick transitions between attack and defense. Players should be ready to move quickly and be alert when the switch happens, maintaining intensity throughout.• Disguised Runs: Encourage attackers to use disguised runs, making it harder for defenders to anticipate their movements. These runs should be timed well, ensuring they arrive at the right moment to receive the cross.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should focus on staying compact, blocking passing lanes, and communicating with teammates to prevent attackers from getting a clean shot on goal.• Crossing Accuracy: Instruct the attacking players delivering the crosses to focus on accuracy and timing. The ball should be delivered to areas that give attackers a better chance to score, such as the near post or back post areas.

title: Lyon Finish & Follow In
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on sharp, close-range finishing under minimal pressure to develop striker confidence and precision. The first attacker receives a pass and shoots quickly from close range, aiming to beat the goalkeeper cleanly. Immediately after the initial shot, a second attacker makes a sharp follow-up run into the penalty area to capitalize on any rebounds, spills, or saves from the goalkeeper. This repetition helps improve reaction speed, awareness, and opportunistic finishing in front of goal.By isolating the finishing phase without defensive pressure, players build technical shooting skills and develop instincts for reacting to second balls. The drill encourages timing runs, maintaining focus, and sharp decision-making in realistic goal-scoring scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize quick, composed shooting from the first attacker – Players must focus on accuracy and power to beat the keeper efficiently.• Encourage the second attacker to anticipate rebounds aggressively – The follow-up runner should read the goalkeeper’s actions and react quickly for second-chance opportunities.• Reinforce proper body positioning and balance in finishing – Both attackers should stay balanced to shoot or control rebounds effectively under pressure.• Promote communication and spatial awareness in the penalty area – Players must stay aware of each other’s positions to avoid collisions and maximize scoring chances.
progression_one: Add a Passive DefenderIntroduce a passive defender applying light pressure on the initial shooter to increase shooting difficulty while maintaining the follow-up focus.Focus: Improve composure under mild pressure, accuracy, and quick decision-making in finishing situations.
progression_two: Reduce Recovery TimeDecrease the time allowed between shots to simulate match intensity, encouraging faster shooting and quicker follow-up reactions.Focus: Enhance stamina, concentration, and speed of execution during high-tempo goal-scoring opportunities.

title: Lyon Positional Possession & Counter
instructions_setup: In this practice, a team of 4 players in possession aims to use 3 neutral players to create a numerical advantage of 7v4 against the defending team. The possession team focuses on maintaining control by effectively combining with the neutrals to progress play and break defensive lines. When the defending team wins the ball, they immediately transition to attack by attempting to score in either of the two mini goals positioned at each end of the grid. Upon scoring, the defending team switches roles with the previous possession players, while the 3 neutrals always remain neutral throughout the drill.This drill develops high-level possession skills under pressure, encouraging players to exploit numerical superiority with quick passing and smart movement. It also sharpens defensive reaction and transition awareness as players must quickly switch from defending to attacking phases while adapting to dynamic situations.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, accurate passing involving neutral players – Players should use sharp, well-weighted passes to fully utilize the numerical advantage consistently.• Demand constant movement and spatial awareness off the ball – Players must find pockets of space and offer effective support to maintain possession under pressure.• Reinforce quick transitions between defense and attack – Players need to react rapidly after turnovers and adapt positioning to counterattack with intent.• Stress communication and teamwork throughout all phases – Players should clearly communicate roles, ball movement, and defensive adjustments to optimize team shape.
progression_one: Limit Neutral Player TouchesRestrict neutral players to a maximum of two touches to increase the challenge and speed of play in possession phases.Focus: Develop quicker decision-making, sharper passing, and improved off-the-ball movement under increased pressure and limited touches.

title: Lyon Rondo with Counter
instructions_setup: In this drill, three teams of two take part in a 4v2 rondo, where the possession team must complete a minimum of six passes to earn a point. The defending duo's objective is to regain possession and immediately transition into a counter-attack. Once they win the ball, they should aim to score into the mini-goal that the possession team lost the ball from, creating a dynamic shift between attacking and defending.The game encourages quick transitions, tactical awareness, and ball retention. The defending players are incentivized to press effectively, while the possession players are challenged to maintain control and create space for passing options. After successfully regaining possession and scoring in the counter-attack, the defending team swaps places with the players who were previously on the outside, keeping the drill fluid and continuously engaging.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of quick transitions after regaining possession. Defenders should immediately look to attack once the ball is won, creating a 2v1 overload against the possession team.• Ball Retention: Possession players should focus on making simple, quick passes and finding spaces for one-touch or two-touch play to meet the six-pass target.• Pressing: The defending players must stay compact and look to force errors by closing down passing lanes, being patient in their attempts to win the ball back.• Awareness and Communication: Players need to be aware of their surroundings at all times, with possession players needing to communicate to maintain the passing flow, while defenders coordinate to press effectively as a unit.
progression_one: Limit Touches:Limit the number of touches for the possession players (e.g., one or two touches max). This forces them to be more efficient in their passing and movement.Focus: Enhances quick thinking, better touch control, and sharpness in passing decisions.

title: Lyon Sprints & 2v2s
instructions_setup: This drill combines explosive sprint work with quick transition to a competitive 2v2 phase. Each team has four players split into two pairs. One player from each pair sprints up the field and tags their partner, who then sprints back down. Once both sprints are complete, the remaining two players from each team immediately engage in a 2v2 attacking and defending phase. After the phase ends, players rotate roles, ensuring everyone completes both sprinting and 2v2 work. This drill develops speed, endurance, and sharp decision-making in transition scenarios.By linking intense sprinting with quick game play, players improve their physical conditioning and ability to maintain technical focus under fatigue. The drill simulates real-game demands where rapid recovery and immediate tactical engagement are essential.
coaching_notes: • Stress explosive acceleration and deceleration during sprints – Players must sprint with maximum effort and control their speed when tagging teammates, ensuring smooth transitions.• Encourage sharp, focused play during the 2v2 phase – Players should maintain quick passing, movement, and defensive positioning despite significant physical fatigue.• Reinforce smooth and efficient tagging transitions – Timing and communication are key to seamless role changes between sprint and game phases for fluidity.• Promote awareness of spacing and angles in small-sided play – Players must use available space effectively to create and deny scoring opportunities consistently.
progression_one: Increase Sprint Distance and 3v3 PhaseExtend sprint distances for greater endurance demands and change the small-sided game to a 3v3 for enhanced tactical complexity.Focus: Build greater stamina and develop teamwork under increased player numbers and physical stress challenges.

title: Lyon Switching Play to Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill begins with three players combining on one side of the pitch through quick, precise passing to build rhythm and open space. After the combination, a long diagonal switch is played to a wide winger. The winger must take a positive first touch forward, controlling the ball efficiently to create crossing opportunities. From this wide position, the winger delivers a cross into the penalty area where two attackers time their runs to finish effectively and score.The focus is on developing clean combination play, accurate long passing, and quality first touches to set up attacking chances. The attacking players practice timing their runs and finishing unopposed, allowing them to concentrate fully on technique and positioning without pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp, accurate passing during the initial 3-player combination – Players should focus on crisp passes with the right weight and timing to break defensive lines.• Encourage a decisive, forward first touch from the winger – This touch should open space and allow the winger to quickly deliver an effective cross.• Reinforce timing and angle of attacker runs into the box – Attackers must synchronize their movements to arrive at the optimal moment for a high-quality finish.• Focus on quality of crosses into the penalty area – Crosses should be well-weighted and targeted, allowing attackers to finish comfortably with either foot or head.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender to the WingerIntroduce a passive defender who lightly pressures the winger, forcing a quicker decision and more precise first touch under mild pressure.Focus: Improve winger’s composure, ball control, and crossing accuracy when faced with defensive pressure.
progression_two: Include Defensive Pressure on AttackersAdd two defenders in the box to challenge the attackers, requiring sharper timing and more precise finishing under realistic defensive pressure.Focus: Enhance attackers’ ability to time runs and finish cleanly in tight, contested situations.

title: Madrid 1v1 SSG
instructions_setup: In this continuous 1v1 drill, players will attack 1v1 against a defender and, once their phase is complete, will immediately transition to defend against the next player who enters the square grid. Players begin with one attacker and one defender on opposite sides of the grid.The play follows a clockwise pattern, meaning the next player to attack will always be the next available player clockwise to the previous player, ensuring a seamless transition between attacking and defending.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick transitions: Players must immediately shift focus from attack to defense and vice versa, maintaining high intensity. Attackers should sprint into space after their phase, while defenders must recover quickly to challenge the next attacker.• Attackers should focus on creating space: Encourage attackers to use feints, sharp turns, and quick directional changes to break past defenders. Their first touch should be purposeful to create separation, allowing more options in tight spaces.• Defenders must stay compact and use positioning: Emphasize the importance of positioning to force attackers into less dangerous areas. Defenders should use lateral movements, staying low to the ground, and guiding attackers away from goal.• Players should attack with speed: Encourage attackers to be explosive and confident, taking defenders on as quickly as possible. The faster they attack, the more difficult it is for defenders to set up and react.
progression_one: Increased Time for Attacks:Increase the time attackers have to create a shot or pass before transitioning. This allows defenders more time to recover and adds difficulty to the attack.Focus: Attacker decision making under time pressure while defenders focus on quick recovery.

title: Madrid 2 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This 2-phase finishing drill helps players focus on both combination play and quick finishing under pressure. The first phase involves a center forward combining with a central midfielder, turning, and finishing on goal. In the second phase, after the finish, the forward quickly transitions to receive a pass from behind the goal and completes a 1-touch finish.The drill challenges the player to maintain focus during rapid transitions and make quick decisions in both combination play and finishing situations.
coaching_notes: • Combination Play: Encourage the center forward to make quick, sharp movements when receiving the ball from the midfielder to create space for the shot. Timing and communication are key.• Quick Turn and Finish: Once the ball is played, the forward should focus on quickly turning and taking a clean shot. Encourage using both feet and finishing with composure under pressure.• Transition to Second Phase: After the first finish, the player should transition quickly to the second phase, anticipating the ball from behind the goal. Focus on movement off the ball to create a clear shot at goal.• 1-Touch Finish: The 1-touch finish should be sharp and clinical. Players must focus on striking the ball cleanly, ensuring the shot is on target, and using proper technique.
progression_one: Increase Speed of the Combination:Reduce the time between the pass and the shot in the first phase. The center forward should complete the combination and finish in under 5 seconds.Focus: This progression increases the tempo of the drill, making it more game-realistic and challenging for the forward to act quickly.
progression_two: Add a Defender in the Second Phase:Introduce a passive defender in the second phase to pressure the forward once they receive the ball from behind the goal. The defender should not challenge until the ball is received.Focus: This progression adds a decision-making element in the second phase, forcing the forward to choose their finish quickly while under slight pressure.

title: Madrid 3 Zone Overloaded
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on attacking from different zones on the pitch, simulating a real-game scenario where attackers progress through the central and wide areas before finishing in the penalty box. The drill involves three zones: a central zone, the left side of the penalty area, and the right side of the penalty area. The first zone starts with an attack played from the defender, followed by attacking in the other two zones to finish.The drill encourages players to adapt to different positions and angles while attacking, promoting versatility and decision-making in varied attacking situations.
coaching_notes: • Zone Awareness: Players should focus on adapting their movements to each zone. In the central zone, attackers should aim to create space for a direct shot, while in the wide zones, they must adjust their angles for crossing and finishing opportunities.• Combination Play: Encourage attackers to link up with teammates in each zone. Timing the runs and passes is crucial to breaking down the defense effectively and generating shooting opportunities.• Quick Transitions: Players must be prepared to quickly shift from zone to zone. This helps simulate game-like transitions where attackers constantly change positions to exploit gaps in the defense.• Finishing with Composure: In all zones, focus on finishing with composure, whether it's a first-time shot, a controlled finish, or shooting under pressure. Make sure players remain calm when they approach goal.
progression_one: Vary the Starting Point for the Attack:Randomly switch the starting point for the attacking play. One time, the attack may start in the central zone, and the next time it could start in a wide zone. This variation forces attackers to adapt and be versatile in their approach to goal.Focus: This progression builds players' adaptability to different attacking situations, whether they’re starting wide or centrally. It challenges their spatial awareness and decision-making in dynamic contexts.

title: Madrid Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This drill combines ball mastery with fitness to help players develop their technical ability while enhancing their endurance. Players are required to travel long distances from the central zone before playing a combination with the outside players. This drill is ideal for pre-season as it challenges both technical skills and physical conditioning.The drill includes overlapping runs and precise passing to ensure the players maintain sharp technical execution while also building fitness through constant movement and high-intensity work.
coaching_notes: • Efficient Movement: Encourage players to use their body positioning to make the overlapping runs as efficient as possible. Players should avoid slowing down and should always be aware of their next move, whether that’s playing a pass or making the next run.• Timing of the Overlap: Emphasise the importance of timing when making the overlapping run. Players should look to time their runs so they receive the ball back inside the grid at the right moment, allowing them to continue play without losing momentum.• Fitness and Endurance: While focusing on technique, also ensure that players keep their intensity up. Remind them to push themselves when travelling long distances across the grid to build stamina while maintaining control of the ball.• Technical Precision: When receiving the ball, players should focus on controlling it quickly and efficiently to play the next pass without slowing down the flow of the exercise. Quality ball control is key to maintaining the rhythm of the drill.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a passive defender to apply light pressure to the player receiving the ball. This will force the attacking player to make quicker decisions and execute passes with more precision under mild pressure.Focus: This progression helps players develop their ability to handle pressure while maintaining high levels of technical quality and fitness.
progression_two: Increase the Distance:Increase the length players must travel from the central zone before passing to the outside player. This progression challenges their stamina and forces them to maintain technical quality over longer distances.Focus: This will help improve players' endurance while ensuring they remain composed and technically sound during longer periods of activity.

title: Madrid Build v Mid Block
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on helping teams develop their ability to penetrate central spaces against a mid-block defensive setup. The attacking team must work quickly to break down the defensive line and create goal-scoring opportunities, while the defending team looks to shut down the central passing lanes and win the ball back.The drill emphasizes quick, dynamic movement and intelligent decision-making when playing through tight spaces. The defenders are locked into the central grid, creating a challenging situation for the attacking team to break through.
coaching_notes: • Quick Ball Movement: Encourage the attacking players to move the ball rapidly and with purpose to create gaps in the defense. The quicker the ball is moved, the more likely it is to drag defenders out of position and create space to penetrate.• Creating Angles for Passing: Players should always be looking to create angles to receive the ball, making it easier for the passer to penetrate the defensive block. Encourage attacking players to move off the ball to pull defenders out of position.• Decision Making: Players must make quick decisions on whether to play a forward pass, shoot, or pass to a teammate. Encourage them to keep their heads up and assess the options available as the ball moves through central areas.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders should stay compact and look to deny central passing lanes, forcing the attackers into wide areas or less dangerous zones. The defensive team must stay alert to quickly transition into attack once they win possession.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Attackers:Limit the number of touches the attacking players can have (e.g., 2-3 touches). This forces them to make quicker decisions and execute passes faster, simulating real game situations where speed is crucial to breaking down defenses.Focus: This progression improves the speed and sharpness of the attacking play, teaching players to play at a faster tempo when facing defensive blocks.

title: Madrid Finishing & 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a simple 2-player combination that leads into an unopposed finish, allowing players to focus on technique and precision. After completing the finish, the two attacking players transition quickly to defend horizontally across the width of the box, where they must protect the two mini goals positioned on either side of the box.Once the first finishing phase is completed and the players transition into their defensive roles, a 2v2 phase begins. The team who attacked in the first phase must now defend the opposite mini goals while the other team looks to create goal-scoring opportunities in the second 2v2 phase.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitioning: Stress the importance of players quickly switching from attacking to defending. Players must be alert and transition with intensity, as the speed of the switch can be the difference between conceding and recovering the ball.• Defensive Shape: The defending players must stay compact and ensure they cover the mini goals effectively. Encourage them to communicate, track runners, and work together to limit the attacking team’s space and options.• Finishing Accuracy: During the initial 2-player combination, players should focus on placing the ball with precision, aiming for corners and testing the goalkeeper. Encourage composure in front of goal to develop their finishing skills.• Attacking Support: In the second 2v2 phase, attackers should look for quick passing combinations and intelligent off-the-ball movement to break down the defense. Timing and positioning are key to creating high-quality chances.
progression_one: Add a Defender in the 2v2:Introduce an additional defender to the 2v2 phase, making it a 3v2 for the attacking team. This progression increases the difficulty and challenges the attackers to work harder to create space and finish under pressure.Focus: This progression improves the attackers' ability to create goal-scoring opportunities against a numerical disadvantage, teaching them to move the ball quickly and decisively.
progression_two: Time Limit for Finishing Phase:Add a time limit to the first finishing phase, requiring the attacking players to complete their 2-player combination and finish within a specific time frame (e.g., 10 seconds). This progression simulates the need to execute under pressure and forces attackers to be more efficient.Focus: This progression emphasizes quick decision-making and execution, simulating real-game situations where attackers must take advantage of limited opportunities.

title: Madrid One Touch Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing drill focuses on developing players’ ability to execute 1-touch set passes and 1-touch passes. The grid is set up as a square, with two stations placed in each corner: one above and one to the side. As the ball is played forward (vertically, for example), the player receiving the pass must play a cushioned set pass, enabling the next player to play a first-time horizontal pass across the square.This drill encourages quick thinking and sharp technical execution, helping players refine their passing skills while also improving their ability to support play and maintain rhythm in possession.
coaching_notes: • Set Pass Technique: Focus on the technique of the cushioned set pass. Players should ensure they are using the inside of their foot to direct the ball gently into the path of the next player, allowing them to easily receive and play a first-time pass.• Passing Accuracy: Emphasize the importance of precise passes, especially the first-time horizontal pass, which should be firm, accurate, and delivered to the correct foot of the receiving player. This ensures fluidity and consistency throughout the drill.• Quick Decision-Making: Encourage players to play at a high tempo with minimal touches. Speed in decision-making is key for maintaining the flow of the game and ensuring that passes are played quickly and accurately.• Movement Off the Ball: Players should constantly move to create passing angles and offer support. Make sure players are aware of their positioning, looking for open spaces to receive the ball and pass it effectively.
progression_one: Increase the Speed of Play:Reduce the time players have to complete the passing sequences. Set a time limit (e.g., 10 seconds) for completing the full rotation around the grid. This progression challenges players to execute the passing pattern faster, increasing the intensity and simulating match conditions where quick passing is crucial.Focus: This progression improves the players' ability to maintain accuracy while increasing the tempo, reinforcing the importance of speed and precision in both passing and receiving.

title: Madrid Plus 2 Possession
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice involves 4 outside players combining with 2 inside players to create a 6v4 possession scenario. The team of 6 must attempt to keep possession and complete 'X' number of passes for a point, encouraging quick and accurate passing to maintain control of the ball.The defending team of 4 players must attempt to regain possession and then score into any of the 4 mini goals scattered around the area. If the defending team successfully regains possession and scores, they swap positions with the 4 outside players, creating a dynamic flow to the drill.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy and Movement: Emphasize the importance of sharp, accurate passing to maintain possession. Players should also focus on creating passing lanes and supporting each other, constantly moving to offer options and space for the ball carrier.• Defensive Shape: The defending team must remain compact and work together to block passing lanes. Encourage them to press in unison to put pressure on the ball and force mistakes, with a strong focus on communication.• Transition to Attack: As soon as possession is regained, players must transition quickly from defense to attack. This can be achieved by encouraging fast, direct passes to exploit gaps and immediately threaten the mini goals.• Awareness and Patience: The team in possession should be patient, waiting for an opportunity to break down the defense. Encourage players to be aware of their surroundings, look for weak spots, and wait for the right moment to progress the ball forward.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Passes for a Point:Increase the number of passes the attacking team must complete to earn a point (e.g., from 'X' to 'Y'). This forces the team to maintain possession for longer periods and develop better passing combinations.Focus: This progression enhances the attacking team's ability to keep the ball under pressure and work together to break down the defense, while also improving their patience and decision-making in possession.

title: Manchester 1-Touch Finish Race
instructions_setup: This warm-up drill sees two teams compete in a head-to-head finishing challenge that blends passing combinations with one-touch execution. Each team must complete a series of forward passes, culminating in a chipped pass over a mini goal to a teammate positioned behind it, who must finish with a single touch.Players rotate roles after each attempt, and variations can be introduced - such as right foot only, left foot only, or heading finishes - to increase difficulty and engagement.
coaching_notes: • Chipped Delivery: Encourage lofted passes with the correct weight and height to clear the mini goal while setting up an ideal one-touch finish.• Body Shape for Finish: The receiving player should adjust their body early to ensure they are balanced and prepared to finish in one touch.• Timing of Movement: Players must time their runs well to meet the chipped ball in stride and avoid arriving too early or late.• Variation Focus: Use the finishing restrictions to target specific technical skills and challenge players to improve weaker foot or heading ability.
progression_one: Competition with Time Limit:Set a timer for each round and challenge teams to score as many goals as possible within a time frame using one-touch finishes.Focus: Increases intensity, promotes quicker decision-making, and builds match-like tempo.

title: Manchester 1v1 up to 4v4
instructions_setup: This drill starts with the coach calling out a number between 1 and 4. For example, if the coach shouts "3," then 3 players from each team must enter the playing area, creating a 3v3 scenario. This allows for a variety of matchups such as 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, or even 4v4, depending on the numbers the coach calls out.To simplify the process, the coach can number players 1 to 4 and call out specific numbers (e.g., "2 and 3"), which means only players 2 and 3 from each team will enter the playing area for a 2v2. This variation keeps the game unpredictable and forces players to adapt to different situations.
coaching_notes: • Adaptability: Players must remain adaptable to different matchups as the coach calls different numbers. Encourage players to be flexible in their positioning and decision-making, depending on the number of players involved.• Quick Transitions: The quick changes in numbers mean that players need to transition rapidly between attacking and defending. Emphasize the need for quick reactions, such as pressing or supporting teammates, when the numbers change.• Awareness and Communication: Encourage players to communicate with each other regarding the number of players they need to work with. They should be aware of which players are involved and how that affects their positioning and movement on the field.• Spacing and Support: With different numbers on the field, maintaining proper spacing is essential. Encourage players to spread out when they have more numbers and compact when they are outnumbered, while always looking for quick passes and movement off the ball.
progression_one: Limit the Time for Each Scenario:Add a time limit (e.g., 30 seconds) for each scenario (1v1, 2v2, etc.). After each time limit is up, the coach will call out a new number, and the game continues in a new configuration.Focus: This progression challenges players to think quickly and execute their moves under pressure, enhancing their decision-making and speed of play.
progression_two: Goal Scoring in All Configurations:Allow teams to score in any configuration (1v1, 2v2, etc.) by shooting into mini goals or large goals. This encourages players to apply their skills in different attacking and defensive situations.Focus: This progression helps players practice their finishing and defending techniques in varying numerical situations, simulating real game scenarios where numbers may fluctuate quickly.

title: Manchester 1v1 with Transitions
instructions_setup: Play begins with a player attacking the mini goal unopposed. After receiving the ball, they will pass it into the mini goal and immediately transition to defend a 1v1 situation on the opposite side of the zone. This forces the player to quickly shift from an attacking role to a defensive one, testing their ability to adapt to different game scenarios.The transitions are continuous, creating a constant flow of 1v1 situations. This drill can be used to improve both attacking and defending skills in rapid succession, helping players to develop stamina and mental focus.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Emphasize the importance of a quick transition from attack to defense. Players should immediately switch gears and focus on defending once the ball is passed into the mini goal.• Defensive Stance: Players should maintain a low and balanced stance when defending, keeping their body weight on the balls of their feet, ready to react quickly to the attacker’s moves.• Attacker Awareness: Attackers need to be aware of the defender’s position and look for quick ways to exploit space to beat the defender. Encourage smart movement and precise timing for the finish.• Continuous Flow: The continuous nature of the drill means players must stay focused and energized throughout. Encourage players to maintain high intensity and not lose concentration, as they will be constantly switching between attacking and defending.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Attacking:Limit the amount of time players have to complete their attack on the mini goal (e.g., 10 seconds). This encourages faster decision-making and enhances their ability to perform under time pressure.Focus: This progression encourages speed and urgency when attacking, ensuring players don't become too slow in their decision-making.

title: Manchester 2v1 to 3v2+1
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a 2v1 attacking situation where two attackers combine quickly to beat a single defender and finish on goal. As soon as the 2v1 phase ends (regardless of outcome), the two attackers must quickly transition to defend against a new wave of three attackers, creating a 3v2 counter-attack in the opposite direction.During the 3v2 phase, a recovering defender from the original team can sprint back into play to create a 3v3 scenario, encouraging realistic game-like transitions, recovery runs, and defensive resilience under pressure.
coaching_notes: • In the initial 2v1, encourage sharp combination play, early decision-making, and clinical finishing to exploit the advantage.• Focus on the attackers' reaction time after the first phase, demanding immediate recovery and defensive positioning without delay.• Highlight the need for defensive communication and compactness when facing the 3v2 situation, forcing attackers wide or delaying play.• Stress the importance of the recovering defender's work rate, timing their run to have a real impact on the 3v3 transition.• Reinforce positive transition habits by rewarding quick reactions, both offensively and defensively, during the changeover between phases.
progression_one: Time Limit to Score in 3v2 PhaseImpose a 6–8 second limit for the attacking team during the 3v2 phase to attempt a shot, forcing quicker decision-making and a game-realistic tempo.Focus: Improving speed of thought in attacking overloads and adding urgency to transitional moments.
progression_two: Delayed Entry for Recovering DefenderSlightly delay the recovering defender’s release (e.g., after 2 seconds) to initially challenge the 3v2 before balancing into a 3v3 scenario.Focus: Sharpening attackers' ability to exploit brief overloads and defenders' ability to recover positioning dynamically.

title: Manchester Back 3 Build Up
instructions_setup: Play begins with a 3v2 setup, where the defending team (3 players) must work together to progress the ball into a lone midfielder positioned centrally. The midfielder's goal is to evade pressure and then play the ball forward into either of the two mini goals.Once possession is regained by the defenders in one of the two zones, they transition into a counter attack. The defending team can either have a 2v3 or 3v4 situation, depending on where the possession is won, and they must attempt to score quickly by exploiting the numerical advantage.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Play: Encourage the back 3 to focus on patient, intelligent passing to work the ball into the lone midfielder. The midfielder should remain calm under pressure and use good decision-making to find an option.• Pressure on the Midfielder: Defenders should be encouraged to close down the lone midfielder quickly, making it difficult for them to play forward. Defensive pressure is crucial to limit the midfielder's options.• Counter Attack Awareness: Once possession is won by the defenders, they must immediately shift into attack. Encourage players to make quick decisions, moving the ball rapidly and exploiting the numerical advantage in the counter attack.• Timing of Runs: Players should make their runs at the right time to support the ball carrier during the counter attack. Well-timed, intelligent runs can create overloads and open up goal-scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Limit Time to Progress:Add a time constraint (e.g., 15-20 seconds) for the team of 3 defenders to successfully progress the ball into the midfielder. This encourages quicker decision-making and a faster pace of play.Focus: This progression increases the urgency for the defending team to move the ball quickly and efficiently into the midfielder, speeding up the overall play.
progression_two: Restrict Passing Options for the Attacking Team:Limit the number of passes the attacking team can make before shooting. For example, the team may only be allowed to make three passes before they must attempt to score into one of the mini goals.Focus: This progression adds a layer of pressure to the attacking team, encouraging them to make quicker, more direct attacking decisions.

title: Manchester Breakout into Overload
instructions_setup: Play begins with a 2v2 setup, where the two attacking players aim to find a forward pass into the player positioned between the lines. This player will then turn or combine with another teammate to progress into the attacking zone.If the attacking team successfully finds the forward pass, they can now complete the attack in a 3v2 overload, giving them an advantage to finish. If the defending team wins possession, they must attempt to score into either of the two mini goals or dribble the ball over the central line to transition into their own attack.
coaching_notes: • Forward Pass Awareness: Attackers should focus on creating angles to receive a forward pass and quickly transition into attack. The player between the lines should be aware of the space and timing to receive the ball and play it forward.• Combination Play: Encourage players to use quick combinations to break the defensive line. When the ball is played to the player between the lines, they should look to either turn or combine quickly with the attackers to move forward into the attacking zone.• Defensive Transition: When the defending team wins possession, they should look to act immediately, either by attempting to score in the mini goals or by making a fast dribble over the central line. This reinforces the importance of quick transitions and not allowing the attack to set up.• Numerical Overload: When attackers successfully create a 3v2 overload, they should look to use their advantage by moving the ball quickly, making intelligent runs, and finishing the attack efficiently.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Touches:Limit the attacking players to only two touches per player. This will encourage quicker decision-making and ball movement.Focus: This progression will increase the tempo of the attacking play, promoting faster transitions and better decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Counter Attack Option:Once the defending team wins possession, allow them to have a 2v2 or 3v3 counter attack with no restrictions on the number of touches.Focus: This progression encourages the defending team to counter quickly and use their numbers effectively in the transition phase.

title: Manchester Build Up into 2v2
instructions_setup: This semi-opposed build-up drill allows teams to work on specific patterns of play while progressing from the middle third into the attacking third. The play ends with a 2v2 attack in a small grid positioned just inside the wide areas of the halfway line, where there are two mini goals that teams can score into.The attacking team must work the ball through the build-up phase, focusing on moving the ball quickly and efficiently, before entering the 2v2 zone. In the progression, a center forward positioned on the halfway line can drop into either grid, creating a 3v2 overload and offering more attacking options.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Play: Encourage the team to focus on maintaining possession in the middle third and using quick, short passes to transition the ball towards the wide areas. Players should look to switch the ball when necessary and identify space for attacking runs.• Movement Off the Ball: Off-the-ball movement is key for creating space in the wide grids. The attacking players should look to make diagonal runs into space and support the ball carrier, ensuring they have multiple options for progression.• Quick Transition into Attack: When the ball reaches the 2v2 grid, attackers should look to use their numerical advantage and play quickly to exploit any spaces left by the defenders. Make sure they focus on timing their runs to receive the ball in good positions to finish.• Center Forward Drop-In: In the progression, the center forward should look to drop into the grid intelligently, creating overloads for the attacking team. The attacking players must look to use this advantage, with the center forward offering a focal point for combination play.
progression_one: 3v2 Overload in Wide Grid:Introduce a center forward who starts on the halfway line and can drop into either of the grids, creating a 3v2 overload in the wide area. The extra player in the grid should help increase passing options and support the attack.Focus: This progression encourages attacking teams to make use of overloads and give them more attacking options to break down defensive setups.
progression_two: Introduce a Defender in the Build-Up:Add a defender into the build-up phase who will look to disrupt the attacking team’s passing. The offensive team must still focus on completing the build-up play and create an effective transition into the 2v2 finishing area.Focus: This will improve the attacking team’s ability to work under pressure, while also developing their ability to create space and make decisions in tight situations.

title: Manchester Conditional Rondo
instructions_setup: This transfer rondo involves three teams of six players, with two teams in possession and one team defending. The possession teams must work together to keep the ball, while the defending team works to regain possession by applying pressure on the ball.In this drill, three defenders press into the ball-sided grid, while the other three defenders screen the central line to prevent any easy passes across. After completing 'x' number of passes, the possession players are allowed to transfer the ball to the opposite side of the grid, where the defending team will then shift their pressure to the new ball carrier.
coaching_notes: • Ball Retention: The possession teams must focus on quick, accurate passing to retain the ball and move it across the grid. Encourage players to make short, sharp passes and always be aware of the next pass.• Defensive Positioning: Defenders must work together to create pressure on the ball while screening potential passing lanes. The three players pressuring the ball should work to limit the space the ball carrier has, while the others need to anticipate and block any central passes.• Transfer Timing: The possession teams should focus on timing their transfers effectively. After completing the required number of passes, they should look for opportunities to switch the ball to the opposite side, ensuring the ball is moved quickly to exploit spaces created by the defenders' positioning.• Anticipation and Awareness: Defenders must stay alert, constantly adjusting their positioning to either press or screen based on the ball’s location. The attacking players must also read the movement of the defenders to make the right decisions when transferring the ball.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Passes:Increase the number of passes required before the ball can be transferred to the opposite side of the grid. This will encourage the possession teams to be more patient with their ball movement and increase their ability to retain possession under pressure.Focus: This progression encourages better ball control and decision-making under pressure while improving players' passing accuracy.
progression_two: Defender Overload:Add an extra defender into the drill, so there are four defenders pressing the ball-sided grid. This will increase the intensity of the drill and make it harder for the possession teams to maintain control, encouraging them to move the ball quicker and more intelligently.Focus: This progression will help players develop the ability to deal with defensive overloads and improve their decision-making when faced with a greater number of defenders.

title: Manchester Conditioning 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 2v2 on one side of the grid, while a third team completes shuttle runs on the opposite side. The objective is for the 2v2 teams to score, at which point they must quickly transition to the other side, collect a ball from the center, and initiate a new 2v2 phase.The team not involved in the current 2v2 phase is continuously running shuttle drills, maintaining fitness while being aware of when they must quickly transition into the live play. This keeps all players engaged and improves their agility, fitness, and ability to transition between attacking and defending situations.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Encourage the teams to transition quickly after scoring. As soon as the ball is in the back of the net, the team must immediately run to the opposite side, collect the ball from the center, and begin a new 2v2. This promotes speed and awareness of the need to shift between attack and defense.• Endurance and Awareness: The team completing shuttle runs must stay alert to the game’s progression. They need to be prepared to immediately transition into the live 2v2 phase and perform efficiently. The shuttle runs should be done with high intensity to enhance overall fitness.• Communication and Support: The 2v2 teams should communicate and work together to create goal-scoring opportunities. Ensure that the attacking players support each other with good positioning and quick decision-making. The defenders should focus on positioning to cover passing lanes and anticipate the attacking moves.• Focus on Fitness: Make sure the players not involved in the live 2v2 are pushing their fitness levels. These players should focus on maintaining high intensity during shuttle runs, building their endurance for transitions between phases.

title: Manchester Counter & Recoveries
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a pass into the central forward, who must combine quickly and exploit a temporary 3v1 counter-attack. The attacking team looks to make the most of this overload to create a goal-scoring opportunity before the defenders can fully recover. The central defender must attempt to delay the attacking team, while two other recovering defenders get back into position to restore balance, turning the situation into a 3v3.This drill helps players focus on quick attacking play when they have numerical superiority, while defenders practice delaying tactics and quick recovery runs to regain defensive shape.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combination Play: The central forward should combine rapidly with teammates to take advantage of the temporary overload. Encourage quick, accurate passes to exploit the defensive imbalance before the defenders can recover.• Delay Tactics: The central defender must delay the attackers as long as possible, forcing them to play slower and make more difficult decisions. This buys time for the two recovering defenders to get back into position.• Defensive Recovery: The two recovering defenders must sprint back with intensity, looking to restore balance in the defensive shape. They should focus on communication, making sure to track runners and cover potential passing lanes to disrupt the counter-attack.• Decision-Making in the Attack: The attackers should look to take quick, decisive actions. They need to assess whether to shoot, pass, or continue building the attack as soon as the overload presents itself. Encourage attacking players to take risks when possible, but also to be aware of their options.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Set a time limit for the attackers to exploit the 3v1 advantage, such as 5–10 seconds, to encourage urgency in decision-making. This forces the attackers to be quicker in their actions and keeps the tempo high.Focus: This progression increases the pressure on the attacking team to make fast decisions and capitalize on the overload, improving their ability to transition quickly from defense to attack.
progression_two: Restore the 4v3 with a Second Central Defender:Introduce a second central defender, giving the defending team a 4v3 advantage after the initial 3v1 phase. This requires the attackers to be more precise in their play to break down the extra defender and create space in the final third.Focus: This progression challenges the attacking team to adapt to a more balanced defensive setup and develop a greater understanding of when to release the ball or take on defenders. It also simulates a realistic scenario where a counter-attack leads to a more balanced defensive situation.

title: Manchester Double Finish into 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill starts with two unopposed finishes in and around the area, allowing the attacker to focus on finishing technique. After the second finish is complete, the attacker who completed the first of the two finishes will receive a second ball and immediately transition into a 1v1 scenario, where they must attempt to beat the defender and score.Once the 1v1 phase is complete, the two attackers switch roles, and the practice restarts, ensuring both players get a chance to work on both finishing and attacking under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Finishing Technique: Encourage the attacker to focus on precise finishing with both feet, aiming for the corners of the goal. The focus should be on calmness and accuracy in the first unopposed finishes before transitioning into the more dynamic 1v1 phase.• 1v1 Decision-Making: The attacker must quickly assess the 1v1 situation and decide whether to dribble past the defender, shoot immediately, or use a change of direction to create space. Emphasize quick thinking and effective use of body feints and dribbling techniques.• Timing of the Transition: As soon as the second finish is complete, the attacker should quickly shift into the 1v1 mindset, remaining focused on their positioning and readiness to receive the second ball for a quick attack.
