The transition should be smooth and seamless to maintain intensity.• Defender Pressure: The defender in the 1v1 should focus on cutting down angles and forcing the attacker into less advantageous positions. Encourage defenders to stay patient, not diving in too early, and forcing the attacker into making a mistake or rushing their shot.
progression_one: Defender Switches after Finishes:After the attacker completes the 1v1, switch the roles so that the defender who was previously defending transitions into the attacker, and vice versa. This encourages both players to work on both their attacking and defending skills in a dynamic situation.Focus: This progression ensures that players get balanced development in both attacking and defending, maintaining high intensity and engagement throughout the drill.

title: Manchester Dribbling & Score SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game encourages players to dribble forward into space and utilize quick thinking in tight situations. Play starts 4v4 centrally, with 4 bounce players positioned around the outside, each limited to 1 touch. The central players are tasked with creating opportunities to dribble through the defense and into the end zone, where they must be in control of possession to score.Once a team successfully dribbles into the end zone with possession, they win the round. The losing team quickly switches with the outside players, and play restarts. This setup promotes fast-paced play and enhances players' dribbling and decision-making skills.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Technique: Encourage players to use a variety of dribbling techniques, such as quick touches, changes of direction, and feints, to beat defenders and break into space. Players should focus on keeping the ball close while maintaining control in tight spaces.• Awareness of Space: Players must constantly scan the field to identify available space and exploit gaps in the defense. Encourage players to make runs into open areas, drawing defenders out and creating lanes for teammates.• Decision-Making in Possession: Players need to decide whether to dribble, pass, or take on a defender based on the space and pressure they face. Encourage players to recognize when to hold possession, when to accelerate into space, and when to release the ball to bounce players.• Quick Transition: When possession is lost, the transition to defense should be quick and organized. Encourage defending players to close down space quickly and force the attacking team into making rushed decisions.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Implement a time limit for each round, such as 2 minutes per possession. This creates urgency for teams to move the ball quickly and make decisive actions to score. Teams must balance speed with maintaining possession in order to achieve the goal.Focus: The time limit adds pressure and encourages quicker decision-making in both attacking and defending situations.
progression_two: Limited Dribbles per Player:Limit each player to a specific number of dribbles, such as 3 dribbles per player per possession. This encourages players to be more efficient with the ball, combining dribbles and passes to move the ball forward while still keeping possession.Focus: This progression encourages faster ball movement and forces players to make quicker decisions under pressure.

title: Manchester Finding Space 1v1
instructions_setup: In this 1v1 drill, players in possession focus on creating space through quick changes of direction and deception skills. Their goal is to pass or cross the ball into one of the two mini goals positioned in the attacking area. The defenders, on the other hand, are tasked with blocking or intercepting any crossing or passing attempts to deny the attacking player from scoring.Each phase is limited to 10 seconds to increase the intensity and simulate game-like pressure. This encourages both attacking players to make fast, decisive decisions, and defenders to react quickly under time constraints.
coaching_notes: • Deception and Change of Direction: Attackers should use various moves, such as feints and quick direction changes, to create space between themselves and the defender. Encourage attackers to use their body to deceive and unbalance the defender.• Quick Decision-Making: Attackers need to make quick decisions on whether to cross or pass, depending on the situation. Emphasize the importance of assessing the defender’s positioning and choosing the most effective option.• Defending under Pressure: Defenders should stay compact and read the attacker’s movements carefully. Encourage them to close down the ball quickly and try to block the cross or intercept the pass while maintaining balance.• Time Management: The 10-second limit should push players to act fast and increase the intensity. Stress the need for rapid decision-making and swift execution on both the attacking and defending sides.
progression_one: Defender Pressure:After each successful pass or cross into the mini goal, the defending player must transition quickly to defend the opposite side of the grid, making it a continuous 1v1 with a faster turnaround. This simulates more realistic game pressure.Focus: This progression increases the intensity by requiring defenders to transition quickly between defending and attacking, encouraging players to maintain high energy throughout the drill.

title: Manchester Free Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed free kick routine drill is designed to help players rehearse and refine various attacking free kick patterns from wide or central areas. The team will focus on the key components of a successful set-piece routine including delivery, movement, and timing. Players will position themselves according to the selected routine (e.g., near post runs, edge of the box setups, far post overloads) and execute planned movements without opposition.The free kick taker will deliver the ball into a designated area, aiming for the appropriate target zone based on the play design. Meanwhile, attacking players will make synchronized runs to either meet the delivery or create decoy movements to free up teammates. This unopposed format allows the team to work on precise timing and technical execution without the distraction of defenders.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing & Synchronization:Attackers must time their runs perfectly in relation to the free kick taker’s delivery. Runs should be coordinated so that the ball is met at the optimal point, with staggered timing to create different attacking options.• Varied Movements:Players should rehearse a variety of runs including curved runs, late arrivals at the far post, and quick darts into central zones. Decoy runs and quick direction changes are essential to unsettle defenders in real match scenarios.• Delivery Execution:The free kick taker should focus on consistent and accurate delivery, using different techniques such as whipped, floated, or driven balls based on the routine. The quality of the ball into the target area is crucial to the success of the routine.• Role Clarity:Ensure every player knows their specific job in the routine — whether it’s to attack the ball, screen a defender, make a decoy run, or be in position for a second ball. Clarity in roles improves execution and reduces hesitation.• Communication:Strong verbal and non-verbal communication is essential between the free kick taker and the runners. Agreed cues or signals should trigger the movement so that everyone is synced to the delivery.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to lightly mark the runners and challenge aerially. Their role is to track movements and apply mild resistance without aggressively disrupting play.Focus: This adds realism and forces the attacking team to fine-tune timing and positioning under game-like conditions while still maintaining the structure of the routine.

title: Manchester Number 9 Finishing
instructions_setup: This 4-phase finishing practice focuses on developing various types of runs and movements for center forwards, including runs in behind the defense, across the face of goal, and third-man runs. The drill encourages attackers to make different types of movements to receive the ball and finish, simulating realistic match situations where a center forward must adapt to the ever-changing dynamics of the game.The practice involves different types of service from the players or coach, with each phase targeting a different type of attacking run. This is designed to improve the player’s timing, movement off the ball, and ability to finish in different scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Attackers should time their runs to perfection. Emphasize the importance of reacting quickly to the pass and making runs at the right moment to exploit space behind the defense or across the face of goal.• Variety of Movements: Encourage attackers to vary their runs by making diagonal runs, direct runs into the space behind the defense, or cutting across the center-back to receive passes. They should understand when to make each type of run depending on the situation.• Supporting Play: The attackers should use good communication and timing to support each other’s runs. Encourage third-man runs where a player offers an option for the ball after one or two players have already made runs.• Finishing Under Pressure: Attackers should work on finishing with both feet and from different angles. Encourage composure in front of goal, especially when the ball is played into tight areas or when under pressure from defenders.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce one or two defenders to challenge the attacking players as they make their runs. Defenders should attempt to block or intercept passes, increasing the intensity of the drill.Focus: This progression simulates match conditions, where attackers must deal with pressure and timing, while defenders focus on preventing goals.
progression_two: Increase the Speed:Increase the speed at which the ball is played into the attackers, forcing them to make quicker decisions and movements. Reduce the time between each phase to maintain a high tempo throughout the drill.Focus: This progression enhances decision-making under pressure and the ability to execute quick runs and finishes at a higher pace.

title: Manchester Pass & Receive
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical passing practice focuses on improving players' ability to receive the ball between the lines and progress play through quick combination play. Players will work on their passing accuracy, timing, and movement off the ball to create passing lanes and break defensive lines.By practicing in an unopposed scenario, players can focus on the technical aspects of receiving the ball under control, positioning themselves between the lines, and combining with teammates to maintain possession and advance the play.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Under Pressure: Emphasize the importance of receiving the ball with good posture and awareness of surroundings. Players should be encouraged to open up their body and receive with a touch that allows them to play forward or play to the next player in the sequence.• Quick Combination Play: Encourage fast, one-touch or two-touch passing to maintain the tempo of the drill. Players should work on timing their runs and passes to create space between the defensive lines and keep possession flowing.• Movement Off the Ball: Players should always be aware of their positioning to create passing lanes for the player on the ball. Encourage off-the-ball runs to provide options for quick passes and to pull defenders out of position.• Progressing Play Forward: Focus on the ability to break the lines with passing. Players should look to play through balls, chip passes, or threaded passes to penetrate into the next phase of play, whether that’s into a forward or between defenders.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a passive defender to apply light pressure on the player receiving the ball. The defender's role is to create some challenge in terms of positioning but not actively intercept passes.Focus: This progression increases the difficulty of receiving between the lines while maintaining a focus on maintaining possession and using combination play to advance the ball.
progression_two: Add More Defenders:Introduce more defenders into the practice, allowing for 1v1 or 2v2 situations where players must work harder to maintain possession and find the right angles for passing and receiving.Focus: This progression improves players' decision-making under pressure, as they will need to use more creative combinations and quicker movement to break defensive lines.

title: Manchester Possession to Finish
instructions_setup: In this possession-based small-sided game, teams of 8 play against 4 defenders with the goal of completing 10 successful passes before having the opportunity to score. Upon reaching 10 passes, the attacking team can score either into the main goal or any of the two mini goals within their grid.If the defending team manages to win possession, they must transition quickly under pressure to move the ball into their side of the grid and begin their 8v4 phase of possession, aiming to complete 10 passes and score.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy and Tempo: Emphasize the importance of maintaining a high tempo while ensuring accurate passes. Players should focus on quick ball circulation and movement off the ball to create passing lanes and options for the player in possession.• Defensive Shape: Defenders should work on maintaining compactness and positioning to deny passing lanes. Encourage the defending team to press aggressively and work together to win possession, but also be mindful of leaving space for the attackers to exploit.• Transition Play: Upon regaining possession, defenders must quickly transition to the attack. Encourage quick, decisive passes to move the ball out of pressure and into their side of the grid. The team transitioning should look for the first available option to keep the momentum going.• Spatial Awareness: Players in possession must use the space effectively to stretch the defending team. Encourage the attackers to move the ball into the wider areas or between the lines to create more space and better opportunities to progress the attack.
progression_one: Add Time Pressure:Implement a time limit (e.g., 30 seconds) for the attacking team to complete 10 passes and score. This progression will push the attacking team to increase their speed of play and decision-making under time pressure.Focus: Encourages quick passing and movement under pressure, improving players' ability to make decisions in tight situations.
progression_two: Limit the Touches:Reduce the number of touches per player to one or two touches. This forces the team in possession to focus on sharp, quick passes and increases the intensity of the game.Focus: This progression encourages faster ball movement, improves first-touch accuracy, and enhances overall decision-making in tight spaces.

title: Manchester Progress Overload Rondo
instructions_setup: This 3-grid rondo focuses on encouraging players to switch play effectively by utilizing the free player. In either of the end grids, the possession team will have a 3v1 advantage, while in the narrow central grid, they will play with a 2v1 overload. The aim is to create quick, dynamic play by using the space and the free player to maintain possession and shift the ball efficiently between the grids.
coaching_notes: • Switching Play: Encourage the team in possession to recognize when to switch the ball from one grid to the other. Players should focus on using the free player to maintain possession and quickly shift the play to open up new attacking opportunities.• Movement and Positioning: Off-the-ball movement is crucial. Encourage players to constantly adjust their positions to create passing lanes, ensure they’re in a good receiving position, and make themselves available to receive passes from the free player.• Defensive Pressure: The defending team must stay compact, close down passing lanes, and apply pressure to the ball carrier. They should focus on working together to prevent the attacking team from easily switching the play and finding the free player.• Decision Making: Players should focus on making quick decisions to either pass, dribble, or switch play, depending on the positioning of the defenders and teammates. Encouraging smart, sharp passes will keep the tempo high and force the defending team to react.
progression_one: Limit Passes:Limit the number of passes per player (e.g., 2 touches per player). This progression encourages players to make quicker decisions and forces faster ball movement.Focus: Improves decision-making speed, ball control, and passing accuracy under pressure, promoting quicker transitions and dynamic play.

title: Manchester SAQ & Reactions
instructions_setup: This warm-up and SAQ (Speed, Agility, Quickness) drill focuses on improving a player's reaction time and ability to change direction quickly. Two players will play a sequence of 1-touch passes back and forth, and at any point during the drill, the top player will sprint either left or right. The bottom player must react quickly and attempt to win the sprint race to the designated spot.This drill helps players develop their explosive speed, footwork, and agility under pressure. By reacting to sudden directional changes, players will improve their mental sharpness, anticipation, and ability to transition quickly from one movement to another.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reaction: Emphasize the importance of quick reactions when the top player changes direction. The bottom player must stay alert, anticipating the sprint direction and responding instantly to the call.• Explosive Speed: Encourage the bottom player to use their explosive speed to get off the mark quickly. Focus on short, sharp steps to reach maximum speed in the shortest time possible.• Footwork: Work on the footwork of both players, ensuring that their steps are quick and their body positioning remains low for agility. The top player must use a proper push-off to maximize speed, while the bottom player should stay on their toes for fast reactions.• Anticipation: In addition to reacting, encourage the bottom player to anticipate the sprint direction. This helps build mental sharpness and allows players to prepare mentally before reacting physically.
progression_one: Add Directional Changes:Allow the top player to change direction multiple times within the sequence, forcing the bottom player to react and change direction as well.Focus: Increases the complexity of the drill and challenges the players' ability to change direction quickly, improving agility and decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Speed of Passing:Reduce the time taken to complete each 1-touch pass, forcing both players to make quicker decisions and react faster.Focus: Enhances quick thinking and reaction time under pressure, promoting faster decision-making and sharper movements.

title: Manchester Switching Play to Create
instructions_setup: In this switching play drill, teams will play 5v5 in the middle third of the pitch, with the objective of scoring into one of the three mini goals. Each mini goal represents a progressive pass into the attacking third, allowing the players to create attacking opportunities through quick, dynamic movements. The goal is to break down the defensive team by switching play rapidly across the field.The focus is on creating overloads and isolating defenders by utilizing quick passes and movement. Players must recognize when to switch the ball and exploit the space created by the opposition's positioning. This drill helps improve tactical awareness, ball circulation, and the ability to quickly transition from one side of the pitch to the other.
coaching_notes: • Quick Switching: Players should focus on making quick passes and switching the play rapidly. Emphasize the importance of keeping the ball moving to catch the opposition off balance and create space for attacking opportunities.• Overloading the Flanks: Encourage players to use the switches to overload one side of the field. Once an overload is created, players should look to isolate defenders and take advantage of the space available.• Positioning for the Switch: Players not directly involved in the switch should focus on positioning themselves to receive the ball or support the play once it has been switched across the field.• Recognizing the Right Moment: Teach players to recognize when the switch is on and when it is most effective. Encourage them to wait for the perfect timing to move the ball, creating gaps in the defensive lines for attackers to exploit.
progression_one: Restrict the Number of Passes:Limit the number of passes a team can make before switching play. This forces players to move the ball more quickly and think ahead, increasing the tempo of the game.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and ball movement, forcing players to think strategically and execute their passes efficiently.

title: Marsaille 1v1 With Transition
instructions_setup: This 1v1 recovery defending drill begins with a defender dribbling out from the byline, just outside the penalty area. The defender then plays a forward pass into an attacker positioned just beyond the edge of the semi-circle. Immediately after the pass, the defender must sprint around one of two cones placed wide on either side of the penalty area to simulate a delayed recovery.This delay allows the attacker to advance unopposed for a few seconds before engaging in a live 1v1 duel. The purpose of the setup is to create a realistic scenario where the attacker has a head start and the defender must recover quickly, make up ground, and attempt to stop the attacker from scoring.
coaching_notes: • Defender Transition Speed – Emphasize explosive acceleration after the pass to simulate realistic recovery runs under match conditions.• Attacker Tempo – Encourage attackers to drive forward immediately, using their head start to challenge the recovering defender with speed and direction changes.• Defensive Recovery Angles – Defenders should take smart recovery angles, aiming to delay or force the attacker wide rather than diving in too early.• Body Positioning – On recovery, defenders must stay low with side-on body shape to react and adjust more effectively in 1v1 moments.
progression_one: Attacker Chooses Cone After PassAllow the attacker to choose which cone to run around after making the pass, adding a reaction element and forcing the attacker to scan and adapt.Focus:Improves decision-making, scanning, and sharpens the attacker’s awareness of pressure and space.

title: Marsaille Mastery Into 1v1
instructions_setup: The practice begins with each player running through an unopposed ball mastery phase. In this phase, they drive towards a mannequin and perform a specific skill (e.g., a step-over, feint, or drag-back) to maneuver around the mannequin. After completing the skill move, they drive the ball into a grid where the 1v1 phase begins.Once in the grid, the player immediately engages in a 1v1 situation with an opposing defender. The objective for the attacking player is to beat the defender and score into either of the two mini goals located within the grid. The defender’s goal is to prevent the attacker from scoring by using defensive positioning, timing, and tackling.
coaching_notes: • Mastery and Control: Encourage players to execute the ball mastery phase with close control, focusing on precise, quick movements to beat the mannequin. This phase helps develop touch and confidence in tight spaces.• Skill Execution: Players should aim to be creative when performing the skill move on the mannequin, selecting the most appropriate skill for the situation. The move should be sharp, using the ball to quickly shift direction and commit the defender.• Attacker Mindset: During the 1v1, the attacker should focus on quick decision-making, assessing the defender’s positioning and choosing the best direction to attack. Exploiting space and using changes of pace are key to beating the defender.• Defensive Principles: Defenders should focus on positioning, staying balanced, and not diving in too early. They must force the attacker to one side and use proper timing to tackle without committing fouls.
progression_one: Add a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit for the 1v1 phase (e.g., 10 seconds). If the attacker doesn't score within the time limit, the defender wins the point. This encourages both attackers and defenders to play with more urgency and decision-making.Focus: Increases the intensity of both attacking and defending, requiring quicker actions and more decisive play.
progression_two: Add a Second DefenderIntroduce a second defender in the grid after the first defender has been beaten or the time limit expires. This creates a 2v1 situation, and the attacker must now work to break down two defenders to score into the mini goals.Focus: Challenges attackers to adapt to increased pressure, requiring improved dribbling and quick decision-making under more difficult circumstances.

title: Marsaille Possession to Countering
instructions_setup: Play begins with a 6v3 possession game in the top half of the grid. The attacking team aims to complete 10 consecutive passes under pressure. Once achieved, they can attempt to score in one of two mini goals positioned just above the possession area, reinforcing patience, movement, and ball control under overload conditions.If the defending team of 3 wins possession, they must quickly transition by playing a pass into the bottom half of the grid, triggering a 2v2 counter-attacking scenario. The two attackers then drive toward the main goal to finish against a goalkeeper, emphasizing quick transition play, support movement, and clinical finishing.
coaching_notes: • Possession Patience – Encourage players to stay composed during the 6v3, using support angles and quick movement to maintain control and work toward the 10-pass goal.• Body Position in Possession – Receiving players should open their body and scan before each touch to play quickly and effectively under pressure.• Transition Speed – On turnover, defenders must switch mentality instantly and find the forward pass to trigger the 2v2, simulating real counter-attacking moments.• Clinical 2v2 Execution – In the final third, attackers must decide quickly between combination play or individual actions to beat defenders and finish under pressure.
progression_one: Limit Touches in the 6v3 PossessionIntroduce a 2-touch or 3-touch maximum rule for the 6v3 possession to increase ball speed and player awareness during buildup.Focus:Improves tempo, scanning, and decision-making under tighter technical constraints while maintaining structure in possession.
progression_two: Add a Recovery Defender Into the 2v2After the pass is made into the 2v2 area, allow one of the original 3 defenders to recover and support, making it a 2v3 and increasing pressure on the attackers.Focus:Challenges attackers to combine quickly and finish before the overload is lost, enhancing their urgency, movement timing, and decision-making under numbers-down pressure.

title: Marsaille Reactions Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this drill, 3 players will move clockwise and anticlockwise around 3 poles positioned in a triangle shape. Around the players, roughly 10 meters away, will be 4 mini-goals, one located on each line of the square grid. Each mini-goal will be identified by a color, which can be marked using cones.The coach will direct the players to rotate clockwise or anticlockwise. At any moment, the coach will shout out a color corresponding to one of the mini-goals. The 3 players must react quickly and attempt to pass the ball into the mini-goal that matches the color called out. A point is awarded to the player who successfully passes the ball into the correct mini-goal.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Reaction: Players must react quickly to the coach’s color call, transitioning immediately from their rotation around the poles to focus on the correct mini-goal.• Passing Accuracy: Emphasize the importance of a precise and well-weighted pass into the mini-goal. Players should aim for accuracy, not just speed, to ensure the ball reaches the target.• Body Position and Awareness: Players should maintain awareness of their surroundings, ensuring they position themselves correctly to make a clean pass toward the mini-goals when the color is called. Proper body orientation will improve reaction time and pass quality.
progression_one: Increase Rotation Speed:Increase the speed of the rotations around the poles to add a higher intensity. The coach can also randomly change the direction of the rotations, requiring players to adjust even quicker when the color is called.Focus: Enhances players’ agility, fitness, and reaction speed while maintaining the accuracy and control needed to pass into the correct mini-goal.

title: Marseille Beating the Opposition 1v1
instructions_setup: This 1v1 drill focuses on developing the player's ability to receive the ball under pressure and quickly turn to progress the play. The attacker must work on controlling the ball while under pressure from the defender, using techniques such as shielding and body positioning to protect the ball and evade pressure.The coach plays the ball into the grid, prompting both the attacker and defender to react immediately. The attacker’s goal is to control the ball, turn quickly to face the goal, and then finish by scoring into one of the two mini goals. The defender’s objective is to prevent the attacker from turning and playing forward by pressuring the ball and trying to win possession.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Under Pressure: Encourage players to receive with their back foot and open their body to allow for a quicker turn. Remind them to stay calm and composed when under pressure from behind.• Using the Body to Protect the Ball: Players should use their body to shield the ball and make it difficult for the defender to win possession. Teach them to pivot and protect the ball with the body, keeping their body between the ball and the defender.• Quick Turning: After receiving, players should focus on turning quickly to face the goal. Whether they use a drag back, feint, or a simple pivot, the key is to create space for themselves in a swift motion.• Finishing Under Pressure: Once the player turns, they should be encouraged to take a quick shot or pass into the mini goal. Stress the importance of decision-making when under pressure and finishing with composure.
progression_one: Defender Gains a Head Start:The defender gets a slight head start by being allowed to move before the ball is played in. This creates additional pressure for the attacker to receive and turn under more intense conditions.Focus: Increases the urgency and speed of the drill, helping attackers develop the ability to perform under more pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Set a time limit for the attacker to receive, turn, and finish. This forces the attacker to be quick and decisive in their actions while under pressure.Focus: Enhances decision-making and execution under pressure, developing the ability to play efficiently in tight situations.

title: Marseille Breaking Lines
instructions_setup: In this drill, players work on breaking defensive lines through quick ball movement and intelligent positioning. The aim is to find and pass to two teammates who are positioned beyond the opposition's defensive line, replicating scenarios that occur in real match situations.The setup includes 3 players in possession versus 3 defenders in a locked central grid. The 3 attackers must circulate the ball quickly, using clever movement and combination play to disrupt the defensive structure. The team shape resembles a 2-3-3-2, with 3 defenders trying to block access while 2 target players wait beyond the line to receive a penetrating pass.
coaching_notes: • Create Passing Angles: Encourage players to constantly shift and rotate to create angles for forward passes, using the width and depth of the grid.• Disorganise the Defence: Attackers must use movement, decoy runs, and quick combinations to pull defenders out of position and open up passing lanes.• Weight and Timing of Passes: Passes into the final line must be played with the right weight and at the right moment to give receivers the best chance to control and play forward.• Scanning and Awareness: Players should scan before receiving to know where teammates, opponents, and space are located, helping them make quicker decisions.
progression_one: One Defender Allowed to Press Into Next Zone:Allow one defender from the middle grid to step into the attacking zone once the ball is played forward, creating added pressure for the receiving players.Focus: Forces attackers to make more precise and well-timed passes under increased pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to Score:Give the attacking team 10 seconds to find a line-breaking pass and reach the forward players. If unsuccessful, possession switches.Focus: Encourages quicker tempo, faster decision-making, and game-realistic urgency in build-up play.

title: Marseille Finishing In Behind
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill starts with a pass from the central player to a wide player. After receiving the ball back from the wide player, the central player will then thread a precise pass through the mannequins to a teammate positioned on the opposite side of the grid. The receiving player is then expected to make a run in behind the mannequins and finish on goal.The focus of this drill is on accurate passing, timing of the runs, and finishing under no pressure. By removing opposition, players can work on their technical execution and focus on the details of the pass and finish.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy: Stress the importance of precise and accurate passing, especially when threading the ball through the mannequins. The pass must be weighted correctly to allow the receiving player to run onto it smoothly.• Timing of Runs: The receiving player must time their run to arrive in the space behind the mannequins. Encourage them to start their run just as the central player is about to play the ball, ensuring they are onside and in a good position to finish.• Finishing Focus: The player receiving the pass should focus on finishing the ball with composure. Remind them to keep their shots low and aimed towards the corners of the goal to increase their chances of scoring.• First Touch: Encourage players to focus on their first touch as they receive the ball. A good first touch will set them up for a clean finish and give them more time to compose themselves before shooting.
progression_one: Add Movement or Dummy Runs:Introduce movement from the mannequins or have other players make dummy runs to simulate opposition defenders, making the drill slightly more game-realistic.Focus: This progression adds a layer of complexity to the drill, encouraging players to read the situation and adapt their finishing based on the positioning of defenders.
progression_two: Add a Defender for Pressure:Add a defender to apply light pressure to the receiving player just before they finish, forcing them to make quicker decisions and finish under pressure.Focus: This progression simulates a more realistic match scenario, helping players to deal with pressure and finish effectively while being closed down.

title: Marseille Finishing Overloaded
instructions_setup: Play begins with an attacker dribbling into the first of three zones where they are immediately met by a defender. The attacker must use skill, decision-making, and movement to progress through each of the zones while maintaining control of the ball and fending off defensive pressure.In each of the three zones, a bounce player is positioned on the side of the grid. The attacker can combine with this bounce player to create a temporary 2v1 advantage. Once the attacker progresses through all zones, they will enter the final area to attempt a shot on goal.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Positive First Touches: Attackers should use their first touch to drive forward and engage the defender early.• Use the Bounce Player Effectively: Look for quick give-and-go combinations with the bounce player to bypass defenders and maintain momentum.• Protect the Ball Under Pressure: Attackers must use their body intelligently to shield the ball and stay balanced while dribbling through tight spaces.• Timing of Movement: Players should time their approach into each zone to avoid rushing and maximize use of the bounce support.
progression_one: Limit Bounce Player to One Touch:Restrict the bounce player to only one touch to increase the speed and difficulty of combinations.Focus: Develops quicker decision-making and sharper execution in tight spaces.
progression_two: Add a Recovery Defender in Final Zone:Once the attacker enters the final zone, a recovering defender can enter to add pressure before the shot.Focus: Introduces realistic pressure before goal, encouraging composure and quick execution in finishing.

title: Marseille Warm Up & SAQ
instructions_setup: In this warm-up and SAQ drill, players will play a one-touch pass with a partner before turning out quickly to complete a designated SAQ sequence. This sequence may include agility ladders, cones, or hurdles, designed to replicate explosive football-specific movements. The drill blends technical sharpness with physical preparation, activating both cognitive and muscular systems.The focus is on developing quick reactions, coordination, and readiness for the session ahead. It allows players to warm up dynamically while integrating ball work and reactive speed. The rhythm and timing of each action are key to maintaining high-quality execution throughout the drill.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reaction to Stimulus: Players must respond instantly to their partner’s pass and initiate the SAQ movement without hesitation. Encourage focus and urgency in every repetition.• Sharp Passing: Emphasize clean, accurate one-touch passes using the correct technique to maintain fluency and rhythm in the warm-up.• Explosive Turns: After each pass, players should turn sharply and explode into the SAQ phase, reinforcing match-like acceleration and deceleration.• Consistent Movement Quality: Focus on keeping footwork clean and body positioning balanced throughout the SAQ sequence. Precision and effort matter more than speed alone.
progression_one: Add Directional Cue from Coach:After the pass, the coach calls out “left” or “right,” forcing players to react and turn in that direction before starting the SAQ. This adds unpredictability and simulates match-like reaction demands.Focus: Sharpens decision-making and improves response time under external cues, simulating in-game reaction scenarios.
progression_two: Include a Second Touch Rebound Pass:After completing the SAQ run, players receive a second ball from their partner and must play a controlled return pass before resetting.Focus: Reinforces technical quality under fatigue and promotes continuity in movement and ball control.

title: Milan 1v1 Recovery
instructions_setup: Play begins with a pass into the attacker, who must attempt to score in a 1v1 scenario while being chased and pressured by a recovering defender. The attacker must use clever movement, speed, and sharp decision-making to get a shot off before the defender can recover and challenge.Once the initial phase is complete, the coach immediately serves a second ball to the defender. The defender now becomes the attacker and must quickly transition to score into one of the two mini goals, while the original attacker must react and transition into a defensive role to stop the counter.
coaching_notes: • Attack Under Pressure: Encourage attackers to stay composed when under pressure and to use body positioning and quick decision-making to get a shot away effectively.• Recovery Speed: Defenders must sprint back with intent, aiming to close the distance and apply pressure as quickly as possible to delay or block the shot.• Transition Mentality: Both players must show intensity and awareness in transitioning roles—attacker to defender and defender to attacker—reacting immediately to the coach’s second ball.• Controlled Finishing: In both phases, emphasize quality finishing. Players should stay composed and look to pick out corners, even under fatigue or pressure.
progression_one: Add Time Limit for Each Phase:Set a 5-second limit for the attacker to score and a 5-second window for the counter-attack. This increases intensity and simulates game-like pressure.Focus: Promotes urgency, decision-making under pressure, and effective execution in time-sensitive situations.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Bounce Player:Introduce a neutral bounce player near the middle who can be used in the second phase to link play before finishing.Focus: Encourages combination play and awareness of supporting options during attacking transitions.

title: Milan Build Up from Throw-Ins
instructions_setup: This playing out from the back drill allows players to develop specific build-up patterns when restarting from a defensive throw-in. The focus is on structured movements, support angles, and quick combinations to escape pressure and transition from defense into attack effectively.Play begins with a throw-in taken in the defensive third. Once the ball is in play, the team in possession must work to build out and progress play, with the objective of scoring into one of the three mini goals. The pressing team looks to disrupt the build-up, win possession, and immediately counter-attack toward goal.
coaching_notes: • Movement Around the Throw-In: Encourage intelligent movement and rotation to provide the thrower with multiple options. Players should look to create space and be aware of pressing triggers.• First Touch Quality: Emphasize the importance of a clean first touch under pressure, especially in tight areas near the touchline and in the defensive third.• Building Through Pressure: Focus on supporting angles and communication. The receiving player must recognize pressure cues and combine quickly to bypass the press.• Defensive Transition: When possession is lost, players must react immediately to counter-press or recover into defensive positions to deny the counter-attack.
progression_one: Limit Number of Passes Before Scoring:Allow only a set number of passes before the attacking team must attempt to score in a mini goal.Focus: Encourages quicker progression, sharper passing, and increased urgency to break lines and exploit space.

title: Milan Combinations & Finish
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill on the edge of the area, players work on sharp, short passing combinations in tight spaces before finishing on goal. The focus is on technical execution, timing, and composure when striking the ball after quick build-up play.Players rotate through roles, executing various passing patterns such as wall passes, lay-offs, and third-man runs. The final player in the sequence will break into space and take a first-time or composed finish from the edge of the box.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Combinations: Encourage quick, precise passing with minimal touches. Players should stay focused on the rhythm and timing of each movement within the sequence.• Quality Finishing: Emphasize clean and composed finishes. Players should aim for accuracy over power, using different surfaces of the foot when appropriate.• Body Positioning: Players must open up their body appropriately to receive and finish in stride. This will improve balance and fluidity in their movement.• Movement Off the Ball: Highlight the importance of supporting runs, third-man movements, and timing to ensure the passing sequence flows smoothly.
progression_one: Add Passive Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to add slight pressure and force quicker decision-making without full contact.Focus: Improves speed of play and decision-making in tight areas, simulating more game-like conditions.
progression_two: Alternate Finishing Types:After each round, specify the type of finish (e.g., first-time shot, outside of the foot, weak foot).Focus: Develops players’ finishing versatility and comfort using both feet under varying scenarios.

title: Milan Continuous Countering
instructions_setup: Play starts with two recovering defenders positioned at the top and bottom of the grid, with one of them in possession of the ball. The defender with the ball initiates play by passing into one of the three attacking players positioned centrally.Upon receiving the ball, the attacking team must break forward quickly and take advantage of the initial 3v1 overload. As the counter develops, the two recovering defenders sprint back to support, aiming to restore balance and turn the situation into a 3v3 before the attackers can score.
coaching_notes: • Fast Counter Attacks: Encourage the attacking players to break forward at speed and make early decisions to exploit the overload before the defenders recover.• Delaying Defenders: The initial lone defender should focus on delaying the attack to give teammates time to recover, using smart positioning and body shape.• Timing of Recovery Runs: Defenders must react quickly and recover at full speed to close down space and restore defensive balance.• Decision Making in Overload: Attacking players should recognize when to pass, dribble, or shoot, making the most of their numerical advantage before it becomes a 3v3.
progression_one: Time Limit to Score:Set a time constraint of 6–8 seconds for the attacking team to score after receiving the ball to increase pressure and decision speed.Focus: Promotes high-tempo transitions and rapid decision-making under time pressure, replicating match intensity.
progression_two: Alternate Numbers:Introduce variations like 2v1, 3v2, or 4v2 to challenge players with different overload dynamics and recovery demands in transition.Focus: Develops adaptability and sharpens both attacking efficiency and defensive organization across multiple game scenarios.

title: Milan Corner Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed corner routine drill is designed to help players learn various corner delivery techniques and movements to create goal-scoring opportunities. The team will practice their set-piece routine with a focus on timing, spacing, and coordination. Players will position themselves according to the chosen routine (e.g., near post, far post, edge of the box, etc.) and work to execute the set play under minimal pressure.The corner taker will deliver the ball into the designated area, while the other players make runs to attack the ball or create space. The focus is on smooth, well-timed movements and effective ball delivery. The drill is unopposed, allowing the attacking team to concentrate on executing their routine to perfection.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Ensure that attacking players time their runs to the ball correctly. Whether it’s attacking the near post, far post, or edge of the box, the players should be well-timed in their movements to meet the delivery.• Movement to Create Space: Players should work on off-the-ball movement to pull defenders out of position, making it easier for teammates to get a clear shot at goal. Movement should be quick and dynamic, with players changing direction to create space in key areas.• Delivery Quality: Emphasize the importance of delivering the ball with the correct weight, pace, and accuracy. The corner taker must consistently place the ball into the designated area, whether it’s a driven cross, floated ball, or short corner.• Target Areas: Players should understand where to attack based on the type of delivery (e.g., near post, far post, or central). Each player should be aware of their role in relation to the ball's flight path and their teammates’ movements.• Communication: Encourage clear communication between the corner taker and attacking players. This ensures everyone knows when to make their run and where the ball will be delivered.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from Defenders:Introduce passive defenders to lightly pressurize the attackers during the delivery and movement. The defenders should focus on tracking runs and challenging for the ball but not actively blocking or winning it.Focus: Develops the ability to execute corner routines while under light pressure, simulating more realistic game situations and forcing players to adjust their timing and runs.

title: Milan Double Rondo
instructions_setup: In this rondo drill, players work on maintaining possession and executing quick switches to progress the ball to the opposite side of the grid. The attacking team starts in a 4v2 situation on one side, with two players waiting on the other side to receive the ball once it has been transferred. This helps to develop the ability to switch play quickly and accurately, maintaining possession under pressure.The setup encourages continuous movement, with players having to constantly rotate and adapt to changing situations. The ball is transferred to the opposite side after a set number of passes, and the players on the central line must switch with the outer players to keep the flow of the drill going.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: Emphasize the need for fast, accurate passes and constant movement to create passing lanes. Players must anticipate the ball and be ready to move into space immediately.• Timing of the Switch: The switch must happen at the right moment, ensuring that players on the receiving end of the pass are ready to control and maintain possession under pressure.• Spatial Awareness: Players should always be scanning the area to identify the best passing options and anticipate where the ball will be played next.• Communication: Constant communication is essential to ensure players are aware of their positioning and when to execute the switch, especially with the outer players involved in the rotation.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Passes Before Switching:Extend the number of passes the possession team must complete before switching the ball. This forces players to hold possession longer, improving their ability to maintain control under pressure.Focus: Encourages players to develop patience and composure when under pressure, and promotes improved passing accuracy over longer sequences.

title: Milan Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness and conditioning drill combines high-intensity sprinting with low-intensity jogging to improve both speed and endurance. The drill focuses on alternating between sprinting and jogging across a divided pitch, with the intensity increasing as the exercise progresses. The goal is to push players to their physical limits while ensuring a manageable recovery period during each rep.The pitch is split into six sections, and each repetition increases the sprinting intensity while decreasing the jogging phase. Players gradually progress from sprinting 1 part and jogging 5 parts, to sprinting 6 parts and jogging none, maximizing their cardiovascular conditioning and stamina.
coaching_notes: • Proper Sprinting Form: Encourage players to maintain proper sprinting technique, focusing on drive, posture, and foot strike to maximize speed and efficiency during the sprints.• Recovery Focus: Ensure players understand the importance of the jogging phase as a recovery period. The jog should be light and controlled to prepare them for the next sprint.• Pacing and Intensity: Players should aim to maintain a consistent pace throughout the drill, with increasing sprint intensity. Proper pacing will help them maintain peak performance for the entire drill duration.• Mental Toughness: Emphasize the need for mental resilience, encouraging players to push through the fatigue and maintain focus, particularly as the sprinting phases increase.

title: Milan Overload Underload
instructions_setup: In this drill, players work on transitioning between attacking and defending phases, with a focus on exploiting overloads and countering when the opposition is unbalanced. The first phase starts as a 2v1 attack, where the two attacking players look to break through the defender and score into a mini goal (or main goal if you have 2 goalkeepers). The defender is tasked with trying to win possession and prevent a goal.Once the 2v1 phase ends, the drill quickly transitions into a 1v2 phase. The single attacking player must immediately transition to attack, taking advantage of the temporary overload as the two defenders are momentarily unbalanced.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Players should focus on quickly switching between attack and defense. Encourage attackers to make the most of the overload by moving the ball quickly and looking for the best option to score.• Exploit the Overload: In the 1v2 phase, the attacker must focus on using their speed and positioning to exploit the numerical advantage. Timing their attack and using deceptive moves can create space for a shot on goal.• Defenders' Recovery: Defenders must work on quickly regaining their balance after the 2v1 phase. They should focus on closing down the space quickly and communicating to ensure the 1v2 phase is dealt with effectively.• Decision Making: Attackers must make rapid decisions during both phases. In the 2v1, they should work on combining effectively with their teammate, while in the 1v2, they must make quick, intelligent choices about whether to dribble, pass, or shoot.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Scoring:Impose a time limit for the attacking player to score in the 1v2 phase (e.g., 10 seconds). This progression encourages faster decision-making and emphasizes the need for quick, decisive actions in attack.Focus: Increases the tempo of the drill, pushing players to think and act quickly in high-pressure situations.

title: Milan Passing Activation
instructions_setup: In this drill, players focus on improving their technical passing ability by executing short, quick combinations and penetrating passes. The objective is to develop fluid movement, sharp passing, and the ability to break through defensive lines with incisive passes. The drill encourages quick ball circulation and decision-making to create attacking opportunities.The setup involves players working in tight spaces, passing the ball quickly between themselves while looking to break the defensive line with a penetrative pass. The key focus is on maintaining control of possession while searching for opportunities to progress the ball forward through short combinations.
coaching_notes: • Quick and Accurate Passing: Players should prioritize fast, accurate passing while ensuring they don’t hold onto the ball for too long. The faster the ball moves, the more difficult it is for defenders to press and intercept.• Use of First Touch: Encourage players to use their first touch to set up the next pass or move the ball into space. A good first touch can open up options for the next player.• Penetrative Passing: Players should always look for opportunities to break the lines with penetrative passes, aiming to move the ball forward quickly into advanced positions.• Awareness and Scanning: Players need to scan the field before receiving the ball to understand their options and make quicker decisions. Awareness of space, teammates, and opposition positions is key to maintaining fluid combinations.
progression_one: Add a Defender to Pressure the Pass:Introduce a passive defender to increase pressure on the passer. The defender should close down the passing lanes and challenge the players to make quick decisions.Focus: Forces players to make quicker, more precise passes and encourages them to work under pressure while maintaining possession.
progression_two: Limit the Number of Touches:Restrict the number of touches a player can take to increase the intensity and improve the speed of play. For example, limit each player to 1 or 2 touches maximum.Focus: Encourages players to play faster, with sharper passes and quicker decision-making, helping to replicate match conditions where time and space are limited.

title: Milan Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: In this drill, players work on their passing technique and footwork while engaging in quick ball movement. The drill involves two interjoined diamond shapes with a cone in the center, where players pass the ball, follow their pass, and focus on maintaining fluid movement in different directions. The goal is to develop a sense of timing, accuracy, and speed while working with two balls simultaneously.The setup consists of two diamond patterns placed side by side, with one cone in the middle where both diamonds converge. Players pass the ball around the diamonds, following their passes and working through the different directions. The drill emphasizes quick footwork, precise passing, and seamless transitions as players work in both clockwise and counter-clockwise directions with two balls.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy: Emphasize the importance of making accurate passes to the next player. Players should focus on delivering passes with the right weight and precision, ensuring the ball travels smoothly to the receiving player.• Quick Follow and Movement: Players must quickly follow their pass and be ready to receive or make the next pass. Speed and fluidity are key as players transition between the different sides of the diamond.• Focus on Body Shape: Encourage players to position their bodies correctly when receiving and passing. They should always be facing the next pass to ensure fluid transitions and avoid unnecessary delays.• Awareness of Space: Players should always be aware of their teammates’ movements and anticipate the next pass. This awareness will help improve the timing of the drill and make the transitions more seamless.
progression_one: Add a Directional Change After Each Pass:After each pass, players must change direction (e.g., clockwise to counter-clockwise or vice versa) to increase the intensity and challenge players to adjust their positioning and movement.Focus: Encourages quick decision-making, improves players' ability to adjust their body shape on the move, and develops greater control when changing directions.
progression_two: Introduce a Third Ball:Add a third ball into the drill, increasing the tempo and encouraging players to work even faster. Players should maintain their passing rhythm while being mindful of the additional ball and avoid unnecessary delays.Focus: Increases the intensity of the drill, forcing players to think quicker and work on their ability to maintain precise passing under pressure, improving their decision-making speed.

title: Milan Penetration SSG
instructions_setup: In this penetration-focused small-sided game, teams work to break through the central line to create 2v2 attacking opportunities. The game is played in three zones: the first and third zones feature 2v2 play, with the central zone containing one neutral player who is always part of the defending team. The central player's role is to disrupt play by screening the central line and making interceptions, preventing smooth progression through the middle of the pitch.Teams must focus on quick ball movement and smart positioning to break through the opposition’s defensive structure. The aim is to penetrate the central line and create a numerical advantage by transitioning into a 2v2 situation in the final zone. If the central defender intercepts the ball, they join the attacking team in a 3v2 counter-attack, adding an extra dynamic to the game.
coaching_notes: • Quick Penetration: Encourage players to make quick, decisive passes to penetrate the central line and create 2v2 opportunities. Timing and positioning are key to breaking through the opposition's defense.• Central Player’s Role: The central defender must be alert and proactive in reading the game, attempting to intercept passes and disrupt the attacking team’s flow. Teach them to always be aware of the ball’s position and anticipate passes into the attacking zones.• Fluid Transitions: When the central defender wins possession, emphasize the importance of quickly transitioning to attack. The newly-formed 3v2 situation should be exploited by moving the ball rapidly to create clear chances on goal.• Communication and Support: Players should constantly communicate with teammates, especially in the central zone, to ensure they are always aware of the central defender’s movements and can adjust their positioning accordingly.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Passes:Set a limit on the number of passes the attacking team can make before attempting to break through the central line. This forces quicker decision-making and faster ball movement, encouraging dynamic attacks.Focus: Improves the speed of decision-making, forcing players to think and act faster in high-pressure situations.

title: Milan Possession to 1v1
instructions_setup: In this drill, teams play 4v3 possession in two separate grids, with each player numbered from 1 to 7. The objective is for the teams to maintain possession while the coach randomly calls out a number between 1 and 7. Once the number is called, the two players corresponding to that number must immediately engage in a 1v1 battle, while the rest of their team continues to focus on possession.The drill encourages players to be sharp and quick in their transitions from team play to individual duels. It helps develop both tactical awareness during possession and individual decision-making in high-pressure 1v1 situations. The possession period provides a chance for players to work on their passing, movement, and communication, while the 1v1 element challenges them to react quickly and apply pressure effectively.
coaching_notes: • React Quickly: Players must be prepared for the coach to call out their number at any time. Encourage them to stay focused and ready to engage in the 1v1 whenever their number is called.• Use of Space in Possession: While maintaining possession, players should work to find space, make accurate passes, and keep the ball moving. Ensure they are aware of their teammates' positions and the numbers of potential 1v1 opponents.• 1v1 Focus: In the 1v1 duel, players should focus on controlling the ball, using quick touches to evade pressure, and defending with intensity. Both attacking and defending players should focus on using body positioning and speed to win the duel.• Communication and Teamwork: Emphasize the importance of verbal and non-verbal communication in the possession phase. Players must support their teammates while being ready to transition into 1v1 situations.
progression_one: Introduce a Time Limit for 1v1 Duels:Limit the time for each 1v1 duel. If one player wins the ball or a clear advantage is created, the duel ends and possession resumes in the grid.Focus: Increases the intensity of the 1v1 situations and encourages players to be more decisive and aggressive in duels.
progression_two: Add a Scoring Opportunity After 1v1:Once the 1v1 is resolved, the player who wins possession can attempt to score into a mini goal or pass back to their team. If they lose possession, the attacking team can attempt to score immediately.Focus: Adds a competitive element, motivating players to win their 1v1s in order to gain a scoring opportunity for their team.

title: Milan Receiving Angles
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery drill, two players face each other, each positioned inside a 4-colored square. One player begins with the ball and, before passing it to the opposite player, calls out a color. The player receiving the pass must receive the ball and position themselves around the cone of the called-out color, simulating a quick decision-making process while maintaining ball control.This drill emphasizes both technical ball control and spatial awareness, as players must quickly adjust their position to receive the ball while following instructions. It challenges players to improve their first touch, reaction time, and ability to perform under pressure while developing their understanding of spatial movement.
coaching_notes: • Focus on First Touch: Encourage players to take a controlled first touch that allows them to quickly position themselves around the correct colored cone. The touch should be deliberate and aimed at setting up the next movement.• Quick Decision-Making: Players should practice responding immediately to the color call, quickly adjusting their body positioning and executing a clean pass or reception to the right area.• Body Positioning: Remind players to maintain proper body positioning when receiving the ball. They should always be ready to move and open up space to receive passes from any direction.• Communication and Anticipation: Players should communicate with each other and anticipate the color call, staying focused and alert to ensure they can react promptly when the color is announced.

title: Milan Transitional Rondo
instructions_setup: In this 4v4+2 rondo drill, one team is positioned on the outside of the grid, while the other team defends in the center. The team in possession can utilize the two central players to create a 6v4 overload, allowing them to maintain possession and create better passing options. The team on the outside earns 1 point for every ‘x’ number of passes completed, encouraging quick and efficient ball circulation.If the defending team wins possession, they must complete a set number of passes (e.g., ‘x’ passes) in a 4v2 scenario before transitioning to the attacking role. This gives the defending team a chance to regain control and practice transitioning from defense to attack.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: Encourage players on the outside to make quick, sharp passes to exploit the numerical advantage. They should also focus on constant movement to create passing lanes and maintain possession.• Using the Central Players: The two central players should be utilized as key outlets to create overloads, helping the attacking team maintain possession and progress the ball quickly through the center.• Pressure and Recovery: The defending team should be taught to apply pressure intelligently and try to intercept or block passes. Once possession is regained, they must quickly shift to a more attacking mindset and complete their ‘x’ passes.• Transitioning Quickly: Emphasize the importance of rapid transitions. Once the defending team wins the ball, they need to execute fast, accurate passes to make the most of their 4v2 advantage and switch roles quickly.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Touches:Introduce a restriction on the number of touches each player can take (e.g., maximum of two touches). This encourages faster ball movement and prevents the possession team from holding the ball too long.Focus: Promotes quick thinking, faster ball circulation, and decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to Complete ‘X’ Passes:Introduce a time limit for the defending team to complete their ‘x’ passes once they regain possession. This will force them to focus on speed and accuracy when transitioning into an attacking phase.Focus: Enhances the ability to move the ball quickly under time pressure, simulating game scenarios where fast transitions are critical.

title: Milan Warm Up Game
instructions_setup: This warm-up drill sees two teams compete in a head-to-head finishing challenge that blends passing combinations with one-touch execution. Each team must complete a series of forward passes, culminating in a chipped pass over a mini goal to a teammate positioned behind it, who must finish with a single touch.Players rotate roles after each attempt, and variations can be introduced — such as right foot only, left foot only, or heading finishes — to increase difficulty and engagement.
coaching_notes: • Chipped Delivery: Encourage lofted passes with the correct weight and height to clear the mini goal while setting up an ideal one-touch finish.• Body Shape for Finish: The receiving player should adjust their body early to ensure they are balanced and prepared to finish in one touch.• Timing of Movement: Players must time their runs well to meet the chipped ball in stride and avoid arriving too early or late.• Variation Focus: Use the finishing restrictions to target specific technical skills and challenge players to improve weaker foot or heading ability.
progression_one: Competition with Time Limit:Set a timer for each round and challenge teams to score as many goals as possible within a time frame using one-touch finishes.Focus: Increases intensity, promotes quicker decision-making, and builds match-like tempo.

title: Millwall 3rd Man Attacking SSG
instructions_setup: In this drill, play starts with a pass to the goalkeeper, who is responsible for initiating the build-up. The players are organized in a 5v5 setup, with all players locked into one side of the pitch. The opposite side of the field remains completely unoccupied, but the goalkeeper provides the numerical advantage, creating a 6v5 overload in possession. The attacking team’s objective is to play through the lines and create space on the open side of the pitch.The team in possession must pass to the central player on the central line and then execute a 3rd man combination to break through. After completing the combination, the attacking team aims to exploit the space on the unoccupied side of the field and finish the attack with a goal.
coaching_notes: In this drill, play starts with a pass to the goalkeeper, who is responsible for initiating the build-up. The players are organized in a 5v5 setup, with all players locked into one side of the pitch. The opposite side of the field remains completely unoccupied, but the goalkeeper provides the numerical advantage, creating a 6v5 overload in possession. The attacking team’s objective is to play through the lines and create space on the open side of the pitch.The team in possession must pass to the central player on the central line and then execute a 3rd man combination to break through. After completing the combination, the attacking team aims to exploit the space on the unoccupied side of the field and finish the attack with a goal.
progression_one: Restrict the Number of Touches:Limit the number of touches for each player (e.g., a maximum of two touches per player). This forces quicker decision-making and ensures a faster tempo in the build-up.Focus: Promotes quick ball circulation and decision-making, creating a more dynamic build-up.

title: Millwall Contact & React
instructions_setup: In this warm-up drill, players work on developing awareness of contact and reacting quickly to different physical situations. The drill starts with players engaging in shoulder-to-shoulder contact, where they push lightly against each other. On the coach’s whistle, players must quickly react and sprint away from the contact position.The coach can also vary the starting procedure by switching from shoulder-to-shoulder to back-to-back contact, requiring players to adjust their reactions accordingly. This variation helps build agility, awareness, and quick reactions, while also enhancing the players’ ability to handle contact situations.
coaching_notes: • Reacting to Contact: Encourage players to maintain balance and posture while engaging in shoulder-to-shoulder or back-to-back contact. Reacting quickly and maintaining control is key to the drill’s success.• Quick Sprinting: Upon the coach’s whistle, players should focus on accelerating quickly and maintaining a high sprinting posture. The faster the reaction, the more effective the drill.• Balance and Posture: Players should use their body to absorb contact and stay on their feet. Emphasize keeping a low center of gravity to ensure stability during the contact phase.• Variety in Starting Positions: By changing the starting positions (shoulder-to-shoulder or back-to-back), players develop adaptability and improve their reactions to different physical challenges on the pitch.
progression_one: Add a Directional Change:After the coach’s whistle, add a directional change requirement (e.g., sprint in one direction, then quickly change direction). This challenges players to react to different types of movement.Focus: Helps players work on their agility and adaptability, enhancing their ability to react and change direction rapidly.
progression_two: Increase the Distance:Increase the distance the players must sprint after the whistle. This requires players to accelerate and maintain top speed over a longer distance, further improving their sprinting capabilities.Focus: Promotes endurance and the ability to sustain high-speed efforts after contact.

title: Millwall Technical Passing
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing pattern mixes short combinations in the initial phase with longer passes to switch the play. Two square grids, positioned roughly 20 meters apart, are set up. Players complete quick one- or two-touch passes inside one grid, then switch the play with a longer diagonal pass to the opposite grid. Once the ball arrives, the same combination and switch sequence continues.
coaching_notes: • Short Passing Quality: Emphasize sharp, accurate passing during the combination phase. Players should focus on keeping the ball on the ground and playing with proper weight and direction.• Scanning and Timing: Players should scan before receiving and play their pass at the right time to maintain rhythm and avoid rushed decisions.• Body Shape: Encourage open body positions to receive on the back foot and play forward quickly, especially when preparing for the switch.• Weight and Accuracy of Long Passes: Switches of play must be well-timed and struck with precision to allow a smooth transition between grids.• Movement After Pass: Players must move purposefully after playing a pass to maintain angles and keep the tempo high.
progression_one: Add Passive Pressure:Place one passive defender in each grid to force players to adjust their position and stay alert during the short combination phase.Focus: Helps players improve decision-making and positioning under slight pressure while maintaining technical execution.

title: Milwall 3 Team Possession & Penetration
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice focuses on penetration, breaking lines, and transitioning between attack and defence. Two teams of six players each will work together in a 12v6 scenario, with the aim of retaining possession and breaking defensive lines, specifically through the two central players. When possession is regained, the teams must quickly switch between attacking and defending, maintaining a fluid 12v6 structure throughout the drill. To allow for smoother transitions, the two central players can combine immediately after regaining possession, giving teams a moment to readjust their positional structure before play resumes.
coaching_notes: • Breaking the Lines – Encourage players to look for opportunities to pass through the central areas, either by penetrating with the ball or through precise, forward-thinking passes to the central players.• Transition Speed – On regaining possession, teams should shift their mindset immediately from defence to attack (or vice versa), focusing on quick passes and decision-making to exploit the transitional phase.• Support and Movement – Off-the-ball movement is key. Players should make runs that create passing lanes and angles for teammates, ensuring support is always available to maintain possession and progress the ball.• Central Players' Role – The two central players should act as focal points for possession, looking to link play and create penetration opportunities into more advanced positions.
progression_one: Add Pressing Triggers for DefendersIntroduce a pressing trigger for the defending team to increase pressure when possession is regained (e.g., after a certain number of passes).Focus: Tests the attacking team’s ability to react quickly under pressure while maintaining fluidity in transitions.
progression_two: Limit the Number of Passes Before PenetrationSet a rule where teams must complete a certain number of passes (e.g., 5) before attempting to break the lines and penetrate forward.Focus: Encourages quick ball circulation and precise decision-making to open up the defence.

title: Milwall 4231 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 4231 formation down into specific zones, where the possession team will play 4v2. The #10 is required to slide vertically to work in both the top and bottom zones, while the #9 is required to slide horizontally to create the 4v2 in the top zones. The practice transitions into a 6v3 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Movement of #10 – The #10 should focus on sliding vertically between the top and bottom zones. Their movement should create space for passing and help connect the midfield with the attack. Encourage them to always look for opportunities to link up play and be available for a quick ball into feet.• Movement of #9 – The #9 must slide horizontally to work across the top zones. This movement is key to creating a 4v2 overload and providing a target for quick passes. Their positioning should stretch the defensive shape, creating space for teammates to play through.• Defending Team's Pressing – The defending team should work together to close down the passing lanes and force the possession team into mistakes. The key to success in pressing is maintaining good communication and awareness of the space in the grid.• Transition to 6v3 – When the defending team wins possession, the practice transitions into a 6v3 overload centrally. The pressing team should look to exploit the central space and move the ball quickly to capitalize on the numerical advantage.
progression_one: Reduced Grid SizeReduce the grid size to increase the intensity of the rondo. This will force quicker decision-making and improve players' ability to play under pressure. The defenders will have less time to press, and the attacking team must be sharp in their passing.Focus: Improving speed of play, awareness, and decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Additional Attacking PlayersAdd a neutral player or two on the outside to help the possession team progress the ball more effectively. These neutrals should be able to receive passes and help break down the pressing team by providing additional options.Focus: Enhancing positional play, passing angles, and creating overloads through neutral players.

title: Milwall Build & Switch Centrally
instructions_setup: This 2v1 build-up drill focuses on central progression and switching play under pressure. The practice begins with the goalkeeper playing into a centre back, initiating a 2v1 scenario versus a single presser. The objective for the defenders is to combine centrally and play into one of two mini goals positioned either deeper or higher up the pitch, simulating vertical progression or quick central switches. If the presser wins the ball cleanly, they can immediately counter toward a main goal with a time-limited opportunity.
