coaching_notes: • Support Angles – The supporting defender must offer clear angles for progression, either to break pressure directly or to switch play into the opposite mini goal.• Movement to Receive – Encourage the initial receiver to take positive touches and move the ball with purpose, forcing the presser to commit before releasing the pass.• Timing of Release – The pass into the mini goals should be well-timed and accurate, capitalizing on the moment the presser is bypassed.• Defensive Pressure – The presser must press with intensity and intelligence, attempting to intercept without fouling, while being ready to transition quickly if possession is won.
progression_one: Add a Second PresserIntroduce a second pressing player who enters after the first pass is made to increase pressure on the build-up.Focus: Improves decision-making speed and ball security under more realistic central pressing conditions.
progression_two: Limit Pass Count Before ScoringRestrict the defenders to a maximum of three passes before they must play into a mini goal.Focus: Encourages quick ball circulation and precise execution under time and space constraints.

title: Milwall Build Up Rondo & Countering
instructions_setup: Play starts with a central rondo, where the build-up team is looking to make 5 consecutive passes before playing into either of the 2 mini goals. If the defending players win possession, they should look to quickly transition and play into either of the 2 wide attackers. These attackers can then cross the ball into the box unopposed, replicating a fast counter-attack. This drill encourages both build-up play and rapid transitions into attacking situations.
coaching_notes: • Pass Precision and Timing – The build-up team should focus on the quality and timing of their passes during the rondo phase. Precision in passing and movement off the ball is essential to maintaining possession and progressing the ball forward.• Pressing and Transition – When defending, players should focus on pressing the ball aggressively to win possession. Once the ball is won, they should transition quickly to a counter-attack, looking to exploit the wide areas for a quick cross into the box.• Wide Play and Crossing – The wide attackers should focus on making quick, accurate crosses into the box. The crosses should vary in height and delivery, depending on the position of the players in the box, to maximize scoring opportunities.• Decision-Making and Awareness – Players need to make quick decisions during both the build-up and counter-attacking phases. Knowing when to play simple passes in the rondo or when to release the ball into the wide areas quickly is crucial for creating scoring chances.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Wide AreasIntroduce a defender to the wide areas to pressure the crossing players. This will replicate the defensive pressure often seen in a real game situation and force the attackers to work under pressure when delivering crosses.Focus: Improves decision-making under pressure and the accuracy of crossing.
progression_two: Limit the Time for the Counter-AttackAdd a time limit for the counter-attack phase. The team that transitions to attack must deliver a cross or attempt a shot within a set period after winning possession.Focus: Increases urgency in the transition phase and sharpens the ability to move the ball quickly into dangerous areas.

title: Milwall Finding the CF
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 3v3+1 in the central zone. The team in possession must complete a minimum of five successful passes, utilizing a one-man overload. After completing the five passes, the team in possession must attempt to play a forward pass into either of the two centre forwards located on the end lines. The centre forwards must finish the ball into one of the two mini goals with a single touch. This practice is transitional, meaning that as soon as the defending team wins possession, they become the 4v3 side and must attempt to make five successful passes before trying to play the ball into the centre forwards.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness – The players in the central zone must be aware of space and positioning to maintain the overload and create passing lanes. Encourage them to rotate positions to ensure the overload remains effective.• Quick Passing & Movement – Emphasize the importance of quick, accurate passing to break down the defense. Players should focus on moving off the ball to provide support and make themselves available for the next pass.• Centre Forward Movement – The centre forwards should focus on timing their runs and positioning to receive the ball. They need to be proactive in their movements to create space and be ready to finish the ball on their first touch.• Transition Speed – When possession is regained, the transition to attack should be quick. The defending team must immediately shift focus to maintaining possession and breaking lines to reach the centre forwards.
progression_one: Increase the Passing RequirementIncrease the number of passes required to be made before a forward pass into the centre forward is allowed. For example, increase to 7 or 8 successful passes before the forward pass.Focus: Forces the team in possession to build up play with more patience, requiring better movement and more control.
progression_two: Limit the Time to Find the CFImplement a time limit for how long the team can take to play the ball into the centre forwards after completing the required passes.Focus: Increases urgency in finding the centre forward quickly, simulating pressure to deliver the ball efficiently under game conditions.

title: Naples 1v1 with Back to Goal
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving a player's ability to receive the ball with their back to goal while under pressure. The practice begins with the attacker entering the box and preparing to receive the ball while being closely marked by a defender. Once the ball is played, the attacker must use their body to shield the defender, turn, and evade the pressure to finish at the goal directly behind them. This drill is great for developing the ability to play under pressure, maintain possession, and quickly transition into a shooting opportunity.
coaching_notes: • Receiving with Back to Goal – Emphasize the importance of body positioning when receiving the ball with the back to goal. The player should use their first touch to shield the defender and position themselves for the next move, ensuring they remain balanced and ready to turn.• Shielding and Protection – Encourage attackers to use their body to shield the ball, protecting it from the defender. Strong, confident body positioning is crucial to maintaining possession and avoiding losing the ball to a tackle.• Quick Turn and Transition – Focus on the attacker’s ability to quickly turn and change direction once the ball is received. Encourage sharp, decisive movements to escape the defender and quickly transition into a shooting position.• Composure and Finishing – Stress the importance of maintaining composure when finishing. The attacker should aim for accuracy over power when shooting at the goal, ensuring they place the ball effectively to beat the goalkeeper.
progression_one: Defender Pressure IncreaseIncrease the intensity of the defender's pressure, requiring the attacker to use more skill and creativity to evade the defender. This will test the attacker's ability to deal with stronger defensive pressure and improve their decision-making.Focus: Improve composure, quick decision-making, and ball protection under greater pressure.
progression_two: Limit TouchesLimit the number of touches the attacker is allowed to take after receiving the ball. This forces quicker decisions and helps develop the attacker’s ability to control and turn the ball swiftly, preparing them for more intense game situations.Focus: Enhance speed of play and the ability to control and turn quickly in tight spaces.

title: Naples 3+3 vs 3+3 SSG
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving counter-attacking skills, team coordination, and creating numerical advantages. The practice begins with 4 attackers and 4 defenders positioned directly ahead of each other. The coach serves a ball into one of the attackers, initiating a 4v3 situation. As the ball is played, the defender in line with the receiver must immediately make a recovery run around a cone placed ahead of them. The attacking team’s objective is to exploit the 4v3 advantage and score, while the defending team’s goal is to delay the attack until the recovering defender can rebalance the numbers and create a 4v4 scenario.
coaching_notes: • Creating Numerical Advantage – Emphasize the importance of exploiting the 4v3 overload by making quick, precise passes and intelligent runs. The attackers should work together to create space and break down the defense, using the advantage to create high-quality scoring chances.• Quick Transition and Decision Making – Focus on the attackers’ ability to transition quickly from defense to attack. Once the ball is played, attackers must make quick decisions to take advantage of the numerical superiority and look for the most effective passing or shooting options.• Defensive Delay and Recovery – Instruct defenders to delay the attacking play by positioning themselves to block passing lanes and force the attacking team into less dangerous areas. The recovering defender should focus on regaining position quickly and supporting their teammates in rebalancing the defense.• Timing of Runs – Encourage attackers to time their runs effectively, moving into space to receive the ball and maintain the numerical advantage. They should be ready to attack quickly and decisively as soon as the ball is played.
progression_one: Add a Second Recovery DefenderIntroduce a second defender who can assist in the recovery process, providing the defensive team with more time to reorganize and create a more difficult situation for the attacking team. This adds a layer of complexity and helps to improve the attackers' ability to deal with tighter defensive situations.Focus: Develop the ability to adapt to changing situations and finish under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Time PressureSet a time limit for the attacking team to score, increasing the urgency of the play. This encourages quicker transitions, faster decision-making, and more efficient use of the overload situation, improving counter-attacking under time constraints.Focus: Improve decision-making under pressure and develop the ability to finish quickly during counter-attacks.

title: Naples 4v2 Rondo to 2v2 Attack
instructions_setup: This drill starts with a 4v2 rondo in which two players from each team sprint across the grids to compete for possession. The team that wins possession inside the grid can then transition into a 2v2 attacking phase, with the team gaining possession first receiving a time advantage. If both teams win possession, they will compete in a 2v2 scenario. If only one team wins possession inside the rondo grid, they will attack in a 2v0 situation. The focus is on improving transition play, possession under pressure, and quick decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Possession Under Pressure – Encourage players to maintain composure and quality when under pressure in the rondo. The team in possession should focus on quick, precise passes, creating triangles and using effective movement off the ball to maintain possession. Players must quickly adjust to defensive pressure and look for the best passing option.• Transition to Attack – Once possession is won, the team should immediately transition into attack, either into a 2v2 or 2v0 scenario. The attacking team must move quickly and decisively, utilizing quick passing and smart movement to exploit any space in the defensive setup. Emphasize the importance of making quick, direct runs after winning possession.• Team Shape and Communication – In both the rondo and 2v2 scenarios, emphasize maintaining a solid team shape. Encourage players to communicate with their teammates to ensure proper spacing, defensive coverage, and effective support.• Defensive Awareness – Defenders should focus on positioning, cutting off passing lanes, and applying pressure to force errors from the attackers. The defending team should be prepared to transition quickly if possession is regained, and should aim to delay the attack until the recovering players can join the defensive phase.
progression_one: Add Time PressureIntroduce a time constraint for how long a team can maintain possession in the rondo before they must transition into attack. This adds urgency and pushes players to make quicker decisions and execute faster transitions.Focus: Improve speed of transition and decision-making under time pressure.
progression_two: Increase Defenders in 2v2Add an additional defender to the 2v2 phase, increasing the difficulty and forcing the attacking team to find creative ways to break down a stronger defensive line. This will improve both individual and team attacking decision-making under pressure.Focus: Develop attacking creativity and quick decision-making against a numerical disadvantage in the 2v2.

title: Naples 4v3+1 Counter Attacking
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving counter-attacking skills, team coordination, and creating numerical advantages. The practice begins with 4 attackers and 4 defenders positioned directly ahead of each other. The coach serves a ball into one of the attackers, initiating a 4v3 situation. As the ball is played, the defender in line with the receiver must immediately make a recovery run around a cone placed ahead of them. The attacking team’s objective is to exploit the 4v3 advantage and score, while the defending team’s goal is to delay the attack until the recovering defender can rebalance the numbers and create a 4v4 scenario.
coaching_notes: • Creating Numerical Advantage – Emphasize the importance of exploiting the 4v3 overload by making quick, precise passes and intelligent runs. The attackers should work together to create space and break down the defense, using the advantage to create high-quality scoring chances.• Quick Transition and Decision Making – Focus on the attackers’ ability to transition quickly from defense to attack. Once the ball is played, attackers must make quick decisions to take advantage of the numerical superiority and look for the most effective passing or shooting options.• Defensive Delay and Recovery – Instruct defenders to delay the attacking play by positioning themselves to block passing lanes and force the attacking team into less dangerous areas. The recovering defender should focus on regaining position quickly and supporting their teammates in rebalancing the defense.• Timing of Runs – Encourage attackers to time their runs effectively, moving into space to receive the ball and maintain the numerical advantage. They should be ready to attack quickly and decisively as soon as the ball is played.
progression_one: Add a Second Recovery DefenderIntroduce a second defender who can assist in the recovery process, providing the defensive team with more time to reorganize and create a more difficult situation for the attacking team. This adds a layer of complexity and helps to improve the attackers' ability to deal with tighter defensive situations.Focus: Develop the ability to adapt to changing situations and finish under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Time PressureSet a time limit for the attacking team to score, increasing the urgency of the play. This encourages quicker transitions, faster decision-making, and more efficient use of the overload situation, improving counter-attacking under time constraints.Focus: Improve decision-making under pressure and develop the ability to finish quickly during counter-attacks.

title: Naples Attacking 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving players' 1v1 attacking skills, specifically receiving under pressure and creating separation from the defender. Players will start by receiving the ball with pressure from behind. The attacker’s goal is to either turn or use quick footwork to break free from the defender and score by either shooting into the central mini goal or dribbling through a coned gate. If the defender wins possession, they must immediately transition to attack by dribbling through the coned gate ahead of them to continue the drill.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Under Pressure – Focus on the attacker’s ability to control the ball and maintain composure when receiving under pressure. Encourage the use of quick touches and scanning the surroundings to prepare for the defender’s challenge. Players should try to receive the ball in a way that allows them to either turn or create separation with their first touch.• Creating Separation – Emphasize the importance of using body feints, quick direction changes, and pace to create space between the attacker and defender. The attacker should focus on using their body to shield the ball, using the defender’s momentum against them to break free.• Decision Making in 1v1 Situations – Encourage players to assess whether they should turn and attack the goal directly, or dribble to the coned gate, depending on the positioning of the defender and available space. Timing and a clear understanding of the defender’s movements are key to making the correct decision.• Defensive Pressure and Transition – Instruct defenders to apply pressure effectively, using positioning to force the attacker into less favorable situations. If the defender wins the ball, they must transition immediately into attack, focusing on dribbling through the coned gate. This sharpens both the defender’s ability to recover the ball and the attacker’s ability to react to the pressure.
progression_one: Add a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit for each attack, encouraging the attacker to make quicker decisions and increase the intensity of the play. This will help players develop the ability to finish under pressure and transition faster.Focus: Increase speed and decision-making in attacking situations under time pressure.
progression_two: Multiple DefendersAdd a second defender to increase the difficulty of the drill. This forces the attacker to use quicker, more creative movements to beat two defenders and score or dribble through the gate. The attackers must adapt to multiple defenders and use better decision-making to create goal-scoring opportunities.Focus: Develop skills to break down multiple defenders in 1v1 situations and improve decision-making under pressure.

title: Naples Multi-Directional 1v1
instructions_setup: In this drill, players work on their 1v1 attacking and defending skills with the added challenge of multiple goals to target. The play begins with a pass from the defender to the attacker, who then has the task of attacking 1v1 and attempting to dribble through one of the two black gates positioned on opposite sides of the square.The defender’s main objective is to stop the attacker from scoring while also having the option to switch to the offensive role by attempting to dribble through the other two gates if they regain possession cleanly. This drill promotes both attacking creativity and defensive resilience, while encouraging players to think quickly and transition between roles.
coaching_notes: • Attacker's Approach: Encourage the attacker to use a variety of dribbling techniques to beat the defender, such as feints, changes of pace, and quick directional changes. The focus is on driving forward and exploiting gaps in the defense.• Defender's Positioning: Defenders should focus on staying goal-side of the attacker and forcing them toward one side of the grid. Encourage defenders to remain patient and not dive into tackles prematurely, allowing the attacker to make the first move.• Gate Awareness: Both players should keep the gates in mind, with attackers aiming to use the gates as quick exit points and defenders working to anticipate the attacker’s movement toward them.• Transitioning Quickly: If the defender wins the ball, they should immediately transition into the attacking role, looking for the quickest route to score by dribbling through one of the two gates. This transition is key to improving their ability to shift between attacking and defending.
progression_one: Increase the Number of Defenders:Add a second defender into the drill, creating a 2v1 scenario for the attacker. The attacker must now navigate through more defensive pressure while still trying to use the gates to score.Focus: Increases the challenge for the attacker, requiring better ball control, decision-making, and the ability to handle multiple defenders.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 30 seconds) for each phase of the drill. The attacker must attempt to score within this time, while the defender must defend within the time frame as well.Focus: Promotes faster decision-making and increased urgency in both attacking and defending situations, simulating more game-like pressure.

title: Naples Technical Breaking Lines
instructions_setup: This technical practice focuses on improving players' ability to play forward and break defensive lines using two different variations. Players will practice passing and movement to break through defensive setups, encouraging them to find and exploit spaces in the opposition's defensive structure.
coaching_notes: • Breaking Defensive Lines – Emphasize the importance of players using quick, well-weighted passes to break through the opposition’s defensive lines. Players should focus on reading the game and identifying opportunities to play forward, aiming for the most effective passing lane.• Movement off the Ball – Encourage players to make dynamic, intelligent runs to create options for their teammates. Off-the-ball movement is key to offering passing lanes and creating space for the ball carrier to break lines.• Precision in Passing – Ensure players focus on the quality of their passes when attempting to break lines. The passes should be firm, accurate, and played into space to allow for efficient transitions and attacking opportunities.• Decision-Making under Pressure – Challenge players to make decisions quickly when attempting to break lines, especially when under pressure. Developing this skill will help them identify the right moments to pass forward and disrupt the opposition's defensive shape.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce passive or active defenders to apply pressure on the player attempting to break the lines. The defenders should focus on limiting passing options and forcing the player to make quicker, more accurate decisions when breaking through the defensive structure.Focus: Develop the ability to break lines under pressure and make quick decisions when options are limited.
progression_two: Increase the Number of PlayersAllow additional players to participate, increasing the complexity of the exercise. This forces players to make decisions faster and manage multiple options, encouraging them to maintain fluid passing combinations to break through an expanded defensive setup.Focus: Improve the ability to break lines in more complex situations with additional defenders and passing options.

title: Naples Throw In Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed throw-in routine drill is designed to help players rehearse structured patterns and movements to effectively retain possession or create attacking opportunities from throw-ins. The team will work on a variety of short, medium, and long throw-in routines, with an emphasis on timing, angles, and decision making.Players will position themselves based on the chosen routine — whether it’s a quick short option, a set play into feet or chest, or a long throw into the box. The thrower will look to deliver the ball into the designated area, while teammates execute coordinated movements to receive, lay off, or create space. The drill is unopposed, allowing the team to focus on technical precision, role clarity, and the fluid execution of pre-rehearsed routines.
coaching_notes: • Movement to Receive:Players must time their movements to arrive at the receiving zone just before the throw arrives. Movements should be sharp and purposeful, offering clear options to the thrower and forcing defenders to make difficult choices.• Support Angles & Lay-Offs:Ensure players are providing effective support angles, both in front and behind the ball. Encourage quick lay-offs, wall passes, or second-ball reactions to maintain tempo and exploit space.• Throwing Technique & Decision Making:The thrower should vary their delivery depending on the situation — flat and quick for short throws, loopy for longer distances, or driven throws for aggressive third-man plays. Decision making must be quick to take advantage of disorganized defenders.• Spacing & Role Clarity:Players should understand their role in the routine — including decoy movements, screening, or receiving under pressure. Effective spacing is critical to avoid congestion and give the thrower multiple viable options.• Communication & Triggers:Use visual or verbal cues to coordinate movement and ensure everyone is aligned with the chosen routine. Clear communication between the thrower and teammates helps maintain flow and reduce hesitation.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to provide light marking and simulate real match conditions. The defenders should track runners and apply mild pressure without fully contesting the throw-in.Focus: Helps the attacking team practice their routines under slightly pressured conditions, ensuring movement and execution can hold up in more realistic settings.

title: Netherlands 1v1 Attacking & Mastery
instructions_setup: This 1v1 drill is unopposed, with the attacking player using their physical and technical skills to deceive the defender and create space to score into any of the 3 mini goals. Once the attacker crosses the central line, they must remain locked into that side of the grid, making the practice effectively unopposed. Focus on improving decision-making, ball control, and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Deception & Creativity – Encourage the attacking player to use feints, body fakes, and changes of pace to create separation from the defender. Players should work on being unpredictable and constantly shifting their body to confuse the defender.• Body Positioning – Teach the attacker to maintain a low center of gravity and stay balanced while making quick, agile movements. Body positioning should allow for quick changes of direction and quick acceleration.• Finishing Technique – Players should focus on finishing with composure, whether with a controlled shot, quick placement, or using both feet. Encourage finishing into the corners of the mini goals for greater accuracy.• Decision-Making – Attacking players must decide quickly whether to take on the defender, use a change of direction, or shoot. Speed and confidence are key when making these decisions.
progression_one: Add a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit (e.g., 10-15 seconds) for the attacking player to beat the defender and score. This will create a sense of urgency and simulate real-game pressure.Focus: Improve decision-making under time constraints and speed up the attacking process.
progression_two: Add Passive DefenderIntroduce a passive defender who applies light pressure but does not actively challenge the attacker. This allows the attacking player to work on their skills under a slightly more game-like situation, with the focus still on deception and finishing.Focus: Enhance the attacking player's ability to create space and finish under light defensive pressure.

title: Netherlands 1v1 Boxes
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into a central player. The central player must take a first touch through either one of the boxes located to the side of them. After the initial pass is made, the passer must make a recovery run and attempt to stop the attacker from breaking in and out of the box before scoring into the mini goals. This drill focuses on the attacker’s ability to quickly create space and finish, while the defender works on recovery speed and defensive positioning.
coaching_notes: • Quick First Touch – The central player should focus on taking a quick first touch into one of the boxes, allowing them to make a strong move in the direction of the mini goal. A controlled touch sets up the attacker for success in breaking the defender’s line.• Attacker’s Movement – Encourage the attacker to work on quick, agile movements to get into the box and around the defender. They should be aware of their positioning and try to stay unpredictable in their movements.• Defensive Recovery – The defender must focus on recovering quickly after the initial pass. They should anticipate the attacker’s movements and attempt to get into position to prevent the attacker from entering the box and scoring.• Finishing Under Pressure – The attacker should be encouraged to finish quickly, with composure, as the defender will be closing down their space. A quick, decisive shot is necessary to avoid being pressured by the recovering defender.
progression_one: Add a Second DefenderIntroduce a second defender to challenge the attacker after they break out of the box. This will force the attacker to be more creative and focus on making quicker decisions.Focus: Improve the attacker’s ability to break down multiple defenders and make quicker, more effective decisions.
progression_two: Time the AttackerSet a time limit (e.g., 10 seconds) for the attacker to enter the box and finish. This will encourage quick, decisive play, helping the attacker improve under time pressure.Focus: Increase the attacker’s decision-making speed and ability to finish under pressure.

title: Netherlands 2v1 with Transitions
instructions_setup: Play begins with a pass into a deeper teammate, creating a 2v1 scenario in the attacking phase. Each phase is timed for 7 seconds, promoting fast and fluid attacking play. Once the attacking team has finished their attack, the initial receiver transitions to defend against the opposition’s 2v1. As a progression, you can allow the next 2v1 phase to begin immediately, forcing players to transition more quickly and with greater focus.
coaching_notes: • Fast Transitions – Stress the importance of quick transitions from attack to defense. Players should immediately switch from attacking to defending without hesitation, focusing on positioning and communication.• Timing of Runs – In the attacking phase, encourage players to time their runs and passes quickly, aiming for a decisive and swift attack within the 7-second time limit. The player in possession should look to exploit the space and make the most of their numerical advantage.• Defending the 2v1 – When transitioning to defense, emphasize proper defensive positioning. The defender should focus on cutting off passing lanes and forcing the attacking player to make decisions under pressure. Quick decision-making is crucial when defending a 2v1.• Decision-Making Under Pressure – Encourage players to make quick, confident decisions, whether attacking or defending, especially as the drill moves at a fast pace. Players should focus on sharp decision-making within the short 7-second window.
progression_one: Start Immediately After TransitionAllow the next 2v1 phase to begin immediately after the transition, promoting quicker decision-making and faster transitions.Focus: Improve reaction speed and adaptability during transitions between attack and defense.
progression_two: Introduce Extra DefendersAdd another defender to make the 2v1 into a 2v2. This will encourage the attacking team to make quicker, more effective passes to break down the defense.Focus: Improve offensive decision-making under increased defensive pressure and help players better handle defensive transitions.

title: Netherlands 2v2 Attacking
instructions_setup: The drill starts with the attacker dribbling towards the grid. The attacker can pass to either one of their teammates, who are positioned between two gates. Once one of the attackers between the gates receives the ball, a 2v2 scenario is created. The attacking team will aim to score in the main goal, while the defending team attempts to stop the attack and dribble through the vacant gate on regaining possession.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making – Encourage the attacking players to make quick decisions when receiving the ball, looking for the best option between passing or dribbling into space. Awareness of the teammate's position between the gates is key for effective play.• Movement Off the Ball – The attacking players should focus on intelligent off-the-ball movement to create space for a pass or better shooting opportunities. Timing runs and creating angles to support the player with the ball is crucial.• Defensive Pressing – The defending players must focus on applying pressure without overcommitting. They should aim to block passing lanes and force the attacker into less dangerous areas, preventing easy shots on goal.• Transitioning Quickly – When possession is regained by the defending team, they must transition into attack quickly, aiming to dribble through the vacant gate to score. Emphasize the importance of immediate counter-attacks to catch the attacking team off guard.
progression_one: Introduce a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit for the attacking team to score. If they do not score within a set period (e.g., 10-15 seconds), the play stops, and the drill restarts with a new set of attackers and defenders.Focus: Increase the pace of play and improve decision-making under time pressure.
progression_two: Add More DefendersIncrease the number of defenders to make it a 3v2 situation. This will force the attacking team to be more creative with their passing and movement to break down a more compact defense.Focus: Improve attacking team’s ability to break down a stronger defensive setup and adapt to numerical disadvantages.

title: Netherlands 3v1+2 Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into the central attacker. This attacker then decides which side the attacking team will play on with their first touch. Once the attacker takes their first touch, the play becomes live in a 3v1 attack. Two defenders will be recovering from the sides, attempting to rebalance the numbers and turn the scenario into a 3v3, aiming to stop the attack.
coaching_notes: • First Touch Direction – The central attacker must use their first touch to either commit a defender or create space for themselves and their teammates. The touch should be purposeful and aimed at initiating an attack toward the most advantageous side.• Speed of Play – The attacking team should focus on moving the ball quickly to exploit the numerical advantage, maintaining fluidity and pace in their passing and movement to break down the defense.• Recovery Defenders – The two recovering defenders should work in unison to quickly close down space and re-establish numerical equality. They need to be aware of where the ball is at all times, communicating with each other to effectively stop the attack.• Decision-Making in Attack – The attackers should look to make decisions on the fly, choosing to pass, dribble, or shoot based on the positions of the defenders and their teammates. The attack should focus on using quick combinations to break through defensive lines.
progression_one: Introduce a Time LimitSet a time limit (e.g., 15-20 seconds) for the attacking team to score. If they fail to score within the time frame, the defenders win the point and the play restarts.Focus: Speed up decision-making and increase the urgency of the attacking play.
progression_two: Add Another DefenderAdd a third defender to the scenario, making it a 3v2 for the attacking team. This progression forces the attackers to work harder to break down the defense and improve their ability to create space under pressure.Focus: Improve attacking team’s ability to break down a more compact defense and work effectively in overloaded situations.

title: Netherlands 3v2 & Countering
instructions_setup: The practice begins with an unopposed forward pass into the central player. Once the central player takes their first touch, it becomes a live 3v2 attacking scenario, where the attacking team of 3 attempts to score. If the attacking team scores, the play restarts and the opposite team begins their attacking phase. However, if the defending team wins possession, they immediately transition into a counter-attack. Counter-attacking goals are rewarded with double points, as they require both a possession regain and a completed 3v2 scenario.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition & Decision Making – Encourage quick thinking and fast decision-making for both the attacking and defending teams. Attackers should look to exploit the overload quickly, while defenders should aim to regain possession and launch an immediate counter.• Movement & Support in Attack – The attacking team should focus on off-the-ball movement to create space for each other. Players must be aware of the best options to exploit the 3v2 overload and pass quickly to maintain fluidity.• Defensive Positioning & Compactness – Defenders need to stay compact and work together to delay the attacking team. They should always be aware of the attackers' positioning, trying to funnel them into less dangerous areas, while preparing to quickly counter when they win possession.• Counter-Attack Speed – The defending team, once they win possession, must transition quickly to take advantage of the numerical advantage in the counter-attack. This requires fast ball circulation and accurate passing to complete the attack.
progression_one: Add a Third DefenderIntroduce a third defender for the defending team, making it a 3v3 situation for the counter-attacking phase. This will challenge the attacking team to maintain fluidity while adding more pressure to the counter-attack.Focus: Improve attacking and defensive awareness while making quick decisions under pressure.
progression_two: Set Time Limit for Counter-AttackIntroduce a time limit for the counter-attacking phase (e.g., 10 seconds to score after regaining possession). This encourages the defending team to act quickly and the attacking team to handle the pressure of a fast transition.Focus: Enhance the speed and efficiency of counter-attacks while maintaining composure in high-pressure situations.

title: Netherlands Build-Up Centrally
instructions_setup: This build-up practice focuses on central build-up play. The team working on the build-up has 3 players locked into each side of the grid, while the defending team can also have a maximum of 3 players on one side of the grid. The attacking team should aim to draw pressure on one side before breaking lines or switching play to the opposite side in order to progress the ball. If the defending team wins possession, they must counter-attack in a 3v2 scenario and score into any of the 3 mini goals within 7 seconds.
coaching_notes: • Patient Build-Up Play – Encourage the attacking team to be patient and controlled when building up play. They should look to draw defenders out of position and break lines with quick, precise passes to create space and progress the ball.• Switching the Play – Stress the importance of switching the ball quickly and efficiently from one side of the grid to the other. The team must look for opportunities to change the angle of attack and exploit spaces left by the defending team.• Defensive Pressure & Awareness – Defenders need to remain compact and press effectively, ensuring they don’t allow the attacking team to easily break lines. When the defending team wins possession, they must transition immediately and capitalize on the 3v2 overload.• Quick Counter-Attack – The defending team must look to counter quickly, focusing on moving the ball forward fast to exploit the numerical advantage in the 3v2 scenario. Scoring within 7 seconds puts pressure on both teams to be sharp and efficient in their actions.
progression_one: Limit Number of TouchesLimit the number of touches each player can have (e.g., 2 touches per player) to encourage quicker decision-making and faster ball movement, increasing the pressure on the attacking team.Focus: Improve speed of play and decision-making during build-up and counter-attacks.
progression_two: Add a Goalkeeper to the Counter-AttackIntroduce a goalkeeper for the defending team, adding a further challenge to the counter-attacking phase. This will require the defending team to be even more precise in their passing and finishing.Focus: Enhance finishing under pressure and improve the defending team’s ability to transition effectively with a goalkeeper involved.

title: Netherlands Rondo & Finishing
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into one of the rondo grids, and two defenders must follow to create a 4v2 scenario. The team of four players must attempt to make five passes in the rondo grid. Once they complete five passes, they can shoot and score for a point. If the defending two players win possession, they aim to pass the ball back to either of the other two defenders located on the poles for a point. If the defenders win possession but the ball goes out of the grid, it's still considered a successful action, but no point is awarded.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy & Quick Decision-Making – Emphasize the importance of accurate, quick passes in the rondo. Players should be constantly scanning for passing options and move the ball quickly to avoid being trapped by defenders.• Defensive Pressing – Defenders should work together to apply pressure, cutting off passing lanes and forcing mistakes. They need to stay compact and anticipate the direction of play.• Movement off the Ball – Players should focus on their off-the-ball movement in the rondo. Encourage them to make sharp, deliberate movements to create space for themselves and their teammates.• Transition to Attack – Once the 5 passes are completed, the team must quickly transition to a finishing phase. Encourage players to remain calm and composed when they receive the ball for the shot, focusing on precision and technique.
progression_one: Increase the Number of PassesIncrease the number of passes required before shooting to make the rondo more challenging. Players must be even more precise and quick in their passing under pressure.Focus: Encourage players to maintain composure and patience, even when the pressure increases, while maintaining quick passing tempo.
progression_two: Add More DefendersAdd another defender to the grid, increasing the difficulty of maintaining possession. The attacking team must now adjust their positioning and passing speed to maintain control of the ball.Focus: Improve passing accuracy under pressure and focus on creating space in tight situations.

title: New York 1v1 Arrival Activity
instructions_setup: This fun warm-up practice splits players into attackers and defenders. On the whistle, the defending players must sprint to a position beneath the ball to protect the goal, while the attacking players sprint to the ball and attempt to score. Each repetition is limited to 10 seconds, meaning attacking players must act with urgency and speed to get a shot off quickly.
coaching_notes: • Defender Positioning & AwarenessDefenders must focus on quickly getting into position to defend the goal. They should use their sprint to gain the correct position, always keeping an eye on the ball and the attacker. Emphasize defensive stance and body shape to prevent the attacker from getting a clear shot.• Attacker’s Speed and First TouchThe attacking players need to sprint to the ball as quickly as possible, ensuring their first touch is controlled and sets them up for a fast finish. Encourage them to keep the ball close to their body for better control and quicker decision-making under pressure.• Urgency & Decision MakingBoth attackers and defenders should focus on quick reactions and high intensity during the 10-second time frame. Attackers must decide whether to take the shot or try a quick move to get past the defender. For defenders, the challenge is to read the attacker’s movement and close down the space rapidly.• Game-Like ScenariosMake sure that both attacking and defending players stay mentally switched on, as this drill mimics fast-paced, real-game scenarios where players often have limited time to react. Encourage the attackers to aim for different areas of the goal (low corners, far post) to increase the variety of finishing skills.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for the DefenderDefenders must touch the goal post before they can defend. This limits the defender's time to set up and increases the urgency for them to get into position faster.Focus: This progression challenges defenders to improve their ability to quickly react and position themselves under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Number of DefendersAdd a second defender to challenge the attacking player even more. This could create a 2v1 situation, where attackers need to make quick decisions and potentially beat both defenders.Focus: This progression helps attackers improve their ability to handle multiple defenders and enhance their creativity in attack.

title: New York 4-D-2 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 4D2 formation down into specific zones where the possession team will play 4v2 or 5v2. The team in possession must move the ball from grid to grid, with the attacking grid having an extra player who can roam freely inside to create a 5v2. This roaming player replicates a creative number 10 role, adding flexibility and creativity to the possession.
coaching_notes: • Fluidity and Movement – The key for the team in possession is constant movement. Encourage the possession players to rotate positions, with the roaming player (number 10) creating space and offering passing options in the attacking grid. This movement will help stretch the defensive team and break their shape.• Quick Passing and Switching Play – Emphasize quick, sharp passing with one or two touches to keep the tempo high and prevent the defenders from closing down the space. Encourage the possession team to switch play quickly from one grid to the next, making use of the extra player in the attacking grid to stretch the defense.• Defensive Pressure and Positioning – The defending team should focus on maintaining compactness and good positioning. The 4 defenders should work together to apply pressure to the ball while covering the passing lanes, trying to force mistakes or recover possession by intercepting passes.• Role of the Roaming Player – The roaming player in the attacking grid should be encouraged to look for pockets of space and be unpredictable in their movement, similar to the role of a creative attacking midfielder or number 10. This player should always be an option for the ball, but also be able to support the other attacking players with runs into deeper or wider positions.
progression_one: Limit Number of Touches for DefendersLimit the defenders to only 1 or 2 touches to increase the intensity of the drill and force the attacking team to move the ball quickly.Focus: This progression encourages faster decision-making and sharp passing from the possession team while testing the defenders' ability to react quickly and close down space.
progression_two: Add a 3rd Defending PlayerIntroduce a third defending player in the grid to create a more challenging 5v3 situation. This forces the possession team to be even more creative with their movement and passing.Focus: This progression adds complexity to the drill, increasing the pressure on the possession team and improving their ability to break down more compact defensive setups.

title: New York Attacking Overloaded & Finish
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 2v2 centrally and 2 neutral players positioned on the outside. The attacking team must combine with the help of the neutral players to progress the ball into the area. Once the attacking players arrive in the area, the practice becomes unopposed, allowing the attackers to freely finish on goal. If the defending players win possession, they should attempt to score into either of the 2 mini goals located outside the grid, and they can also use the neutral players to help with progression. The neutral players are limited to one touch only.
coaching_notes: • Utilizing Neutral Players – The attacking team should focus on quick, efficient combinations with the neutral players to progress the ball quickly into the final third. The use of neutral players should aim to stretch the defense and create passing lanes.• Movement in the Final Third – Once inside the area, attackers should focus on dynamic and fluid movement to create space for themselves and their teammates. Good off-the-ball movement will open up better shooting angles or passing opportunities.• Defensive Transition – When defending, players must quickly shift focus from defending the initial 2v2 to the potential counterattack. They should aim to block passing lanes and force the attackers into difficult angles.• Composure in Finishing – In the unopposed finishing phase, attackers should maintain composure and work on a variety of finishes. Depending on the position and angle, they should look to finish first time, use a touch to control, or place the ball into the corners.
progression_one: Add Time Limit for FinishingIntroduce a time limit for the unopposed finishing phase. The attackers must complete their shot within a set amount of time after arriving in the area.Focus: Encourages quick decision-making and maintaining composure under pressure.
progression_two: Limit the Number of PassesLimit the number of passes the attacking team can make before entering the final third. This forces the team to work more efficiently with the neutral players and push the ball forward quickly.Focus: Increases tempo and sharpens the attacking team’s ability to transition quickly from build-up to finishing.

title: New York Creating Centrally
instructions_setup: This is a 2-phase practice. Play starts with a 2v1 attack in the first zone, where the two attacking players are simply looking to progress through the zone via passing combinations or dribbles. Once through the first zone, the attacking players must complete a 2+1v2 phase, where they are attempting to score in any of the two mini goals.The attacking two are encouraged to make use of the neutral end line player once they arrive in the second zone, to create a 3v2 advantage.
coaching_notes: • Progressing Through the First Zone – In the initial 2v1 phase, the attacking team should focus on making quick, sharp passes or taking on defenders to progress through the zone. Encourage the attacking player in possession to either use a 1-2 pass or dribble with pace to break the defensive line.• Utilizing the Neutral Player in the Second Zone – Upon entering the second zone, the attacking players should make use of the neutral end line player. This player should be used to create a 3v2 overload, allowing the attacking team to work with an extra player to break down the defense. The neutral player must stay onside and be available to receive the ball to facilitate quick combinations.• Timing and Movement – The attackers should coordinate their runs and passes, ensuring they work together to exploit the overload. The player with the ball should be aware of the runners and time passes effectively. The off-the-ball player must make sure their runs are timed well to provide an option for the ball carrier.• Defensive Awareness – The defending team needs to be disciplined in tracking runs and maintaining good positioning. They must work together to minimize the impact of the extra player in the second phase and limit goal-scoring opportunities. Encourage defenders to be proactive in closing down the passing lanes and reacting quickly to transitions.
progression_one: Add a Second Neutral PlayerIntroduce a second neutral player in the attacking zone who can join the attack at any point. This gives the attacking team a greater numerical advantage (4v2) and forces the defending team to adjust their defensive shape.Focus: This progression provides more space for the attackers to create and finish, helping them practice exploiting overloads more efficiently.
progression_two: Limit the Attackers’ TouchesLimit the number of touches the attacking players can have in the first zone (e.g., two touches max per player). This increases the speed of play and forces the attackers to make quicker decisions and move the ball faster.Focus: This progression encourages the attackers to focus on quick combinations and dynamic play to progress the ball through the first zone more efficiently.

title: New York Cross & Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing drill allows players to develop their finishing from close range, specifically from low driven balls played from the cut-back zones. Play begins with a forward pass into one of the 2 deeper players. The deeper player will then set the ball back for the crosser, who will deliver a first-time low, driven ball across the face of goal. The 2 forwards will attack the cross at speed, aiming to finish the ball into the goal. The focus is on quick reactions, precise finishes, and timing runs into the box.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs – The forwards should focus on attacking the ball at the right moment. They must time their runs to meet the cross at pace, ensuring they are in position to finish quickly and decisively. Explosive runs into the box are essential for this type of cross.• Finishing Technique – Players should be encouraged to finish with power and accuracy, focusing on getting a clean strike on the ball while keeping it low and on target. Emphasize the importance of keeping their shots low, especially when receiving crosses from wide areas.• Crossing Accuracy – The crosser should focus on delivering low, driven balls across the face of goal. Precision is key, as the cross must be placed in an area where the attackers can make a quick finish. The ball should be played into the path of the forwards, avoiding heavy touches or high crosses.• First-Time Deliveries – Encourage the crosser to hit the ball first-time to maintain the speed of the play and create more dynamic, fluid attacking situations. First-time crosses allow for less time for defenders to react and increase the attacking team's chances of scoring.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce 1 or 2 defenders in the box to apply pressure to the forwards during the attacking phase. This will add a layer of realism and increase the difficulty of finishing under pressure.Focus: Develops the ability to finish in tight, contested spaces while under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Vary the CrossesHave the crosser vary the type of ball delivered (low driven, floated, or chipped) depending on the run of the forward. This will force the forwards to adjust and improve their finishing technique in different situations.Focus: Enhances adaptability and finishing skills for various types of crosses.

title: New York Receiving Under Pressure
instructions_setup: This mastery-level practice challenges a single attacker to receive under pressure and make decisions in a high-intensity environment. The attacking player begins by receiving a pass and has 7 seconds to either beat the press and drive into space or play a pass into one of four mini goals positioned ahead. Three defenders are tasked with pressuring the ball carrier while also protecting the mini goals. The attacker must read the pressure, manage their touch and body position, and find a way to exploit space or gaps between defenders.
coaching_notes: • Receiving Body Shape – The attacker must open up and receive on the back foot whenever possible, allowing them to face forward and quickly assess their options.• First Touch Direction – Encourage players to take their first touch away from pressure and into space, giving themselves more time to pick out a target.• Decision-Making Under Pressure – Players must scan constantly and decide quickly whether to dribble into space or play into a mini goal, depending on defender positioning.• Defensive Compactness – Challenge defenders to stay compact while pressing. They must communicate and shift together to deny easy goal-scoring or passing lanes.
progression_one: Add a Supporting AttackerIntroduce a second attacker to create a 2v3 situation. The ball carrier can now combine with a teammate, increasing the decision-making complexity.Focus:Improves communication, movement off the ball, and the attacker’s ability to draw pressure and release to a teammate in better space.
progression_two: Reduce Time LimitLower the time limit from 7 seconds to 5 seconds once players demonstrate comfort with the initial challenge.Focus:Encourages sharper first touches, quicker decisions, and a higher tempo, simulating real match pressure and urgency.

title: New York SSG & Finishing
instructions_setup: This practice begins as a 3v3 small-sided game (SSG). Each time a goal is scored, two players, one from each team, must run out of the grid to an area designated for unopposed finishing. The players will complete the unopposed finish before swapping with the player who passed them the ball. This rule allows both teams to earn an additional goal after each score in the SSG, promoting both attacking play and finishing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition After ScoringEncourage players to transition quickly from the SSG to the finishing area after scoring a goal. The key to taking advantage of this rule is speed and awareness. Players should be ready to sprint to the finishing area without hesitation in order to maximize the opportunity for an additional goal.• Finishing Under PressureEven though the finishing part is unopposed, remind players to simulate match pressure by focusing on composure and precision. Encourage them to aim for different parts of the goal (corners, lower or upper sections) to develop a variety of finishing techniques. Players should always approach the finish as if it were in a real game.• Focus on Passing and MovementThe passing player should deliver the ball with good weight and accuracy, ensuring it is in a position that allows the finisher to complete the shot efficiently. Off the ball, players should be aware of positioning and movement, ensuring they stay in sync to create these scoring opportunities after every goal.• Defensive Transition AwarenessWhile the focus is on attacking, remind the defending players to maintain awareness of the transition rules. If the defending team loses possession in the SSG, they must quickly recover and track back to prevent the attacking team from gaining an extra goal through the unopposed finish.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a passive defender in the finishing zone to increase difficulty. The defender can put mild pressure on the player finishing, simulating a real match situation where attackers need to be more clinical under pressure.Focus: This progression encourages the attacker to finish with more composure while managing pressure from an opponent.
progression_two: Limit Number of Finishing OpportunitiesLimit the number of goals a team can score from the finishing zone (e.g., only one extra goal per team per cycle). This adds a tactical element where teams must balance playing for the additional finish with maintaining defensive discipline in the SSG.Focus: This progression helps develop a balanced approach, ensuring teams don’t neglect their defensive responsibilities while chasing extra goals.

title: New York Technical Overlapping Warm Up
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up focuses on developing players' ability to make well-timed overlapping runs. Players will start in pairs, with one acting as the ball carrier and the other as the support player. The ball carrier will pass to the support player and then make an overlapping run to receive the ball back into space. To add intensity and keep the players engaged, two balls will be running simultaneously, encouraging quick decisions and more touches per player.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Overlap – Emphasize the importance of timing when making the overlapping run. The supporting player must wait until the ball carrier is ready to pass before committing to the overlap to avoid running into offside positions or unnecessary congestion.• Receiving in Space – Ensure the player making the overlapping run focuses on receiving the ball into space with their first touch. This helps the player maintain the pace of the attack and move the ball forward efficiently.• Quick Transitions – Since two balls are being used, players should focus on quick decision-making. After completing one set of overlaps, players should transition quickly to the other ball, increasing the overall intensity and engagement.• Support and Communication – Encourage players to communicate, especially with the ball carrier, by using their body language and verbal cues. This ensures that the timing of the runs and passes is synchronized.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender into the drill. This defender can apply pressure but should not challenge the pass. This progression encourages attackers to make decisions under pressure and refine their passing and receiving skills.Focus: Helps players get used to overlapping runs while under the pressure of a defender, improving their ability to execute in match-like conditions.
progression_two: Full-Pitch OverlapExtend the practice to a larger space, where players will overlap across the entire width of the pitch. This allows them to practice the overlap in a more realistic game scenario, incorporating longer passes and different angles of attack.Focus: Reinforces the concept of overlapping runs in various situations, encouraging players to use the entire width of the field for dynamic attacking play.

title: Newcastle 1v1 With Recovery
instructions_setup: In this drill, both the attacker and defender begin side by side before sprinting off at angled directions to create separation and space. As the attacker moves forward, they receive a pass from the coach to initiate the 1v1 duel. The attacker must use speed, skill, and decision-making to beat the defender and finish by scoring in the main goal. This setup replicates real-game situations where players need to create space quickly before engaging in a duel under pressure.The drill focuses on explosive first movements, quick transitions from sprinting to ball control, and sharp finishing under defensive pressure. It also challenges defenders to track and close down attackers effectively while maintaining balance and positioning.
coaching_notes: • Encourage explosive, angled sprints to create immediate separation – Players must use strong acceleration and sharp angles to gain an advantage before receiving the ball.• Demand attackers maintain composure and control after the sprint – Effective first touch and ball control are vital to set up the 1v1 attack smoothly.• Reinforce defenders’ focus on quick recovery and positioning – Defenders should anticipate the attacker’s moves and adjust body shape to force less dangerous angles.• Emphasize precise and composed finishing under pressure – Attackers must focus on accuracy and timing when shooting to maximize scoring chances.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to FinishIntroduce a strict time limit for attackers to complete the 1v1 and shoot, increasing urgency and decision-making speed.Focus: Improve speed of execution and quick thinking under pressure.

title: Newcastle 2v1 Counter to 3v2 Build Up
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 2v1 attacking scenario where two attackers combine to score in the main goal against a single defender. The attackers focus on quick passing, movement, and creating clear scoring chances in their numerical advantage. Once this phase finishes, two defenders positioned behind the goal immediately join the play as the coach serves a ball to start the next phase.Now, the two attackers must quickly transition to defend against three defenders plus a goalkeeper who attack two mini goals. This 3v2 + GK phase challenges the attackers to recover rapidly, maintain strong defensive positioning, and communicate effectively to protect the goals. The defenders use their numerical advantage to create scoring opportunities, while the attackers focus on cohesive defending under pressure.This drill improves players’ ability to switch between attacking and defending roles quickly, sharpens fitness and focus, and develops defensive organization during transitional moments.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, creative passing and movement during the initial 2v1 attack – Players should use sharp combinations to break down the defender efficiently and create clear chances.• Demand immediate and focused defensive transition after the first phase – Attackers must react quickly, adjust positioning, and communicate to organize defensive shape.• Stress strong defensive teamwork and communication in the 3v2 + GK phase – Attackers must support each other, cover space, and stay compact to limit scoring opportunities.• Promote high intensity, mental alertness, and physical effort throughout the drill – Rapid role changes require concentration and stamina to maintain effectiveness in both phases.
progression_one: Set a Time Limit for the 2v1 AttackIntroduce a short time constraint (e.g., 8–10 seconds) to increase urgency and quicken attacking decisions.Focus: Speed up play and encourage rapid, precise combinations under pressure.
progression_two: Limit Touches in Defensive PhaseRestrict attackers and defenders to a maximum of two touches in the 3v2 + GK phase to increase pace and technical demand.Focus: Improve quick control, passing accuracy, and decision-making in tight, high-pressure situations.

title: Newcastle 3 Phase Counter Attacking
instructions_setup: This dynamic drill develops quick transitions and decision-making through three consecutive attacking phases. It begins with 2 attackers centrally engaging in a 2v1 situation, aiming to create scoring opportunities under pressure. Once this phase finishes, the drill immediately shifts into a 3v2 scenario where a wide attacker dribbles into the play, joined closely by a recovering defender positioned just behind, intensifying the challenge for the attackers. The final phase switches to the opposite side, expanding to a 4v3 situation with the same flow, demanding rapid adjustment and teamwork.This continuous progression trains players to react swiftly to changing numbers, improves their ability to exploit numerical advantages, and encourages sharp attacking patterns under realistic counter-press conditions. The drill enhances stamina, communication, and tactical awareness across multiple game-like situations.
coaching_notes: • Stress quick decision-making in each phase to exploit numerical advantages – Players must identify and act on spaces rapidly to maintain attacking momentum and break defensive lines effectively.• Encourage precise, fast ball movement combined with supportive off-ball runs – Effective passing and timely movement create overloads, confusion, and scoring chances for attackers.• Reinforce defensive recovery speed and positioning in transitional phases – Defenders need to close down attackers quickly to prevent dangerous breaks and limit scoring opportunities.• Promote clear communication and awareness of shifting game contexts – Players must stay alert to transitions, adjusting roles seamlessly and supporting teammates consistently.
progression_one: Implement Time Limits per PhaseSet strict time restrictions on each attacking phase to encourage faster play and decision-making.Focus: Enhance tempo, mental sharpness, and efficient use of space under pressure.

title: Newcastle 4 Ball Technical Combinations
instructions_setup: This drill challenges players to simultaneously cycle four balls around a designated area, focusing on sharp technical skills and constant movement. Players use a combination of normal passes and 1-2 combinations to keep all four balls moving smoothly and continuously. The exercise demands high levels of concentration, precise ball control, and quick decision-making to maintain rhythm without losing possession.The key objective is to develop players’ ability to handle multiple passing sequences under pressure, improving their first touch, passing accuracy, and off-the-ball movement. This practice also enhances communication and spatial awareness as players coordinate to keep the flow consistent and fluid.
coaching_notes: • Encourage crisp, accurate passes on all balls – Players must focus on correct weight, timing, and direction to keep the drill flowing smoothly without interruptions.• Promote constant off-the-ball movement and positioning – Players should anticipate the next pass, moving to create angles and support for teammates actively.• Reinforce sharp 1-2 combinations to accelerate ball circulation – These quick exchanges help break defensive lines and improve team coordination and timing.• Demand high communication and awareness throughout the drill – Players need to talk and scan constantly, ensuring all balls are accounted for and passing lanes remain open.
progression_one: Increase Passing SpeedEncourage players to speed up their passing and movement, pushing their technical and mental sharpness under increased tempo.Focus: Enhance reaction times, precision, and decision-making under faster-paced conditions.

title: Newcastle Around the Corner Technical
instructions_setup: This technical drill focuses on improving players’ ability to receive and play first-time passes around a corner or angled area. Players practice controlling or directly passing the ball immediately after receiving it, emphasizing speed, accuracy, and sharp decision-making in tight spaces. The drill replicates game scenarios where quick one-touch play around corners helps break defensive lines and maintain attacking momentum.Players work on body positioning to open up passing lanes, controlling the ball under pressure, and executing precise first-time passes to teammates in the correct timing and direction. This helps develop fluidity and sharpness in transitional play, enabling quicker attacks and better ball circulation.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize clean first touches to set up accurate, immediate passes – Players should control or strike the ball decisively with the right weight and direction for smooth flow.• Encourage open body positioning to scan and identify passing options quickly – Proper body shape allows quicker decision-making and better passing angles around corners.• Reinforce timing and anticipation to play passes at the optimal moment – Players must be alert and synchronized to maintain tempo and break defensive pressure effectively.• Promote communication and eye contact between players – Clear signals and calls ensure coordinated movements and successful first-time exchanges.
progression_one: Add Passive Defensive PressureIntroduce light defensive pressure near the corner to simulate game intensity, forcing quicker decisions and cleaner execution.Focus: Develop composure, accuracy, and speed of play under mild defensive challenges while maintaining effective ball circulation.
progression_two: Increase Passing SpeedChallenge players to accelerate the tempo of first-time passes, demanding quicker reactions and sharper technique.Focus: Boost technical sharpness, mental alertness, and fluidity under higher pace conditions.

title: Newcastle Beat the Full Back
instructions_setup: This drill begins with the full back passing the ball out wide to the winger, simulating a turnover or loss of possession. The winger then immediately attacks in a tight 1v1 scenario within a confined zone, aiming to beat the full back by using quick, skillful dribbling to create space. The attacker’s objective is to score by passing or dribbling into one of two mini goals positioned in the zone. This setup encourages the winger to use sharp 1v1 moves, feints, and changes of pace to exploit defensive gaps and openings effectively.The drill develops close control, quick decision-making, and individual attacking skills under pressure. It also helps the defender improve their positioning, anticipation, and tackling in a realistic defensive duel that replicates common match situations on the flank.
coaching_notes: • Encourage attackers to use varied 1v1 moves and changes of pace – Players should focus on unpredictable dribbling to create space and beat their defender effectively.• Demand defenders maintain a low, balanced stance and read body language – Full backs must stay alert, use quick footwork, and anticipate the attacker’s intentions to block passing lanes.• Reinforce quick decision-making and timing of attacking runs – Wingers need to assess when to accelerate, cut inside, or pass to exploit openings decisively.• Emphasize controlled finishing into mini goals under pressure – Attackers should focus on accuracy and composure when selecting the correct mini goal to score.
progression_one: Narrow the Attack ZoneReduce the width of the attacking zone to increase pressure on the winger, forcing quicker decisions and sharper dribbling skills.Focus: Enhance close control, spatial awareness, and rapid execution under tight defensive pressure.

title: Newcastle Double Ended Countering
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing quick, effective counter attacks in a 3v2 attacking scenario. Play begins with three attackers moving quickly against two defenders in one direction, aiming to create scoring opportunities through fast combination play and decisive finishing. Once this phase concludes, the same two defenders immediately transition to defend against another 3v2 counter attack moving in the opposite direction. This back-to-back sequence challenges defenders to maintain concentration and positioning under sustained pressure, while attackers work on rapid decision-making and exploiting numerical advantages.The continuous nature of the drill enhances players' stamina, communication, and transition speed between attacking and defending. It simulates real match situations where teams must quickly react to turnovers and launch immediate counter attacks or recover defensively with high intensity.
coaching_notes: • Encourage attackers to exploit numerical advantage quickly – Players should focus on fast ball movement and smart positioning to create scoring chances early.• Demand high defensive concentration and communication – Defenders must stay organized, anticipate attackers’ runs, and communicate clearly throughout both phases.• Reinforce rapid transition between attacking and defending roles – Players must adjust quickly, maintaining sharpness and intensity in both phases without losing shape.• Emphasize effective finishing under pressure – Attackers should focus on calm, accurate shots while defenders apply close pressure to disrupt scoring attempts.
progression_one: Reduce Recovery Time for DefendersShorten rest periods between defensive phases to increase physical and mental fatigue, simulating high-intensity match conditions.Focus: Enhance stamina, resilience, and concentration under continuous pressure.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Support PlayerIntroduce a neutral player who supports the attacking team, increasing passing options and complexity during counter attacks.Focus: Improve decision-making and movement in overload situations.

title: Newcastle Receiving & Playing Forwards
instructions_setup: This technical drill focuses on developing precise 1-2 passing combinations to create forward momentum and scoring opportunities. Players work in pairs to practice quick, sharp passes where the first player passes to a teammate, immediately makes a forward run to receive the return pass, and then plays a forward pass into a mini goal. The emphasis is on timing, accuracy, and communication to ensure smooth interplay and effective penetration through the defensive line.Players must maintain proper body positioning to receive the ball on their front foot, enabling a clean first touch and controlled forward pass. The drill enhances quick decision-making, ball control under pressure, and passing accuracy, essential for building fluid attacking sequences in match situations.
coaching_notes: • Encourage crisp, well-weighted passes throughout the 1-2 combination – Players must execute passes with the correct pace and accuracy to maintain rhythm.• Emphasize sharp, timed runs immediately after the initial pass – Off-the-ball movement is crucial for receiving the return pass in optimal positions.• Reinforce quality first touches towards the direction of play – Players should control the ball quickly and prepare to play forward passes effectively.• Focus on accurate, penetrating passes into the mini goal – Final passes must be decisive, with good weight and direction to simulate realistic scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Increase Passing SpeedChallenge players to perform the 1-2 combination at a faster tempo to simulate match intensity and improve reaction times.Focus: Develop quick passing and sharper decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Passive DefenderIntroduce a passive defender to increase pressure on the players, encouraging better awareness and movement off the ball.Focus: Enhance spatial awareness, timing, and passing accuracy under defensive pressure.

title: Nottingham 2 Way Finishing
instructions_setup: In this 2-way finishing practice, 2 attackers will dribble balls vertically on the grid before making a forward pass. After making the forward pass, they must turn and circle back around the mannequin on the same side of the grid in which they started, to receive the opposite ball for an unopposed finish.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling with Purpose – The attackers should focus on maintaining control of the ball while dribbling towards the pass zone. Encourage them to use quick, sharp touches to accelerate and approach the forward pass area with purpose.• Pass Timing – The forward pass should be timed to meet the other player’s run. Both players must communicate to ensure that their passes are accurate and well-timed for the receiving player to have an easy opportunity to finish.• Turning Quickly – After making the pass, attackers should quickly pivot and circle around the mannequin to get back into position to receive the ball for the next shot. Encourage efficient and fast movements to ensure they can get back in time for the finish.• Finishing Technique – The attackers should focus on finishing with composure and accuracy when they receive the pass for the shot. They must keep their heads up, focus on the target, and avoid rushing the finish.
progression_one: Add DefendersIntroduce a defender or two to add pressure as the attackers go to receive the ball for the finish. This will simulate real-game conditions where attackers must finish under pressure.Focus: Finishing under pressure and improving composure when there are defenders present.
progression_two: Limited TouchesLimit the attackers to only 1 or 2 touches when receiving the ball to encourage quick, decisive finishing and quick transitions.Focus: Improving speed of play and reducing hesitation when finishing.

title: Nottingham 2v1 Boxes
instructions_setup: The objective of this practice is for two players to either retain or progress possession.
