Each box is set up as a 2v1, with a secondary defender positioned in the central zones.While playing the 2v1, the two players in possession can combine and retain possession together or progress the ball to the opposite grid. Players should be encouraged to progress play when possible but must also retain possession through passes and dribbles.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing & Movement – Emphasize quick, sharp passing between the two players in possession. Encourage movement off the ball to create space and better passing angles.• Decisions on Progression – Players should be aware of when to progress the play and when to keep possession. Encourage players to read the game and make quick decisions based on the pressure they face.• Shielding & Protecting the Ball – The player on the ball should focus on shielding and using their body to protect the ball when under pressure, keeping possession until a safe passing option becomes available.• Central Defender Awareness – The secondary defender in the central zone must remain alert and anticipate the direction of play. Encourage them to apply pressure without committing too early, forcing the attacking team to make decisions under pressure.
progression_one: Add a Third DefenderIntroduce a third defender to create a 2v2 in the boxes. This will increase the challenge for the attacking players, encouraging them to combine even more effectively to create space and progress the play.Focus: Improving ball retention under pressure and quick decision-making in tighter spaces.
progression_two: Limit Touches for the Possession PlayersLimit the number of touches allowed for the players in possession to increase the pace of play. This forces quicker decisions and encourages faster ball movement and combination play.Focus: Speed of play and maintaining possession while under pressure.

title: Nottingham Finishing From Close Range
instructions_setup: This finishing practice begins with a short 1-2 passing combination in a wide area to simulate dynamic wing play. After combining, the wide player delivers a cross into the box for the centre forward to finish from close range. Immediately following the initial finish, the centre forward continues their movement by running around and through two mannequins positioned just outside the penalty area, where they receive a second ball thrown in the air by a coach for a first- or second-time finish.This drill focuses on sharp attacking movements, varied types of finishes, and maintaining quality under repeated physical and technical demands.
coaching_notes: • Wide Combination Timing – Ensure players execute the 1-2 at high speed with sharp touches to maintain the flow and replicate in-game tempo.• Body Shape for Finishing – Centre forwards should adjust their body early to attack the cross effectively, setting up for a clean and decisive strike.• Movement Between Finishes – Encourage high-intensity movement after the first finish to simulate game-like recovery and positional readjustment.• Second Finish Technique – The second ball is aerial, so players must focus on reading the flight and selecting an appropriate technique (volley, half-volley, header).
progression_one: Add Passive Defender in the BoxInclude a passive central defender who follows the striker’s run into the box to simulate pressure during the first finish from the cross.Focus:Enhances movement timing, positioning between defenders, and concentration during delivery under light pressure.
progression_two: Varied Second Ball DeliveryHave the coach mix in bouncing balls, headers, and clipped lobs for the second finish, requiring the striker to adapt and use multiple finishing techniques.Focus:Develops versatility in execution, body control, and composure when reacting to unpredictable second-phase service.

title: Nottingham FUN Passing Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This is a fun, competitive warm-up game with two teams, each working unopposed inside their own grid, aiming to score into their own mini goal. The grid is divided into four zones, spaced every 5 yards moving away from the mini goal.Players start from different zones and try to score in their own goal. The further back the ball is played or carried from, the more points the team earns when they score. For example, a goal scored from the closest zone to the mini goal earns 1 point, while a goal scored from the furthest zone earns 4 points, with intermediate zones earning 2 or 3 points accordingly.The game encourages players to balance risk and reward, deciding whether to take safer, closer scoring chances or attempt more challenging plays from further away for higher points.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Creativity – Players should explore dribbling, passing, and combination plays to progress through zones and maximize points.• Risk vs Reward Awareness – Help players understand when to attempt long-range plays and when to prioritize possession with easier chances.• Movement and Support – Emphasize off-ball movement to create passing options and maintain fluid attacking play inside each grid.• Finishing Focus – Promote sharp, accurate finishing under different conditions and from varying distances.
progression_one: Time-Limited Scoring AttemptsSet a time limit for each scoring attempt (e.g., 10 seconds) to increase urgency and decision speed.Focus:Improves quick attacking transitions and encourages sharp execution under time pressure.
progression_two: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a passive defender inside each grid to apply light pressure during scoring attempts, increasing challenge and realism.Focus:Develops composure, creativity, and decision-making when under defensive pressure.

title: Nottingham Wingers Attacking 1v1
instructions_setup: In this attacking drill, a winger receives the ball wide and must take on a defender in a 1v1 situation. The objective is for the winger to use skill, speed, and decision-making to beat the defender and score into a mini goal positioned near the end line. The defender applies pressure to challenge the attacker and prevent the goal.
coaching_notes: • Decision Making – Encourage the winger to quickly assess when to dribble past or use feints to creatively create space and open shooting angles.• Body Position and Balance – Emphasize staying low and balanced to maintain control during rapid changes of direction and shield the ball effectively.• Use of Pace – Teach the winger to vary speed effectively to unbalance the defender and exploit any hesitation or mistakes.• Finishing Under Pressure – Focus on composure and accuracy when shooting in tight 1v1 scenarios to maximize scoring chances.
progression_one: Timed Defender PressureAdd a defender who starts 2-3 yards behind and begins chasing the winger after a short delay, increasing urgency and encouraging quicker attacking decisions.Focus:Improves reaction speed, decision-making under pressure, and ability to protect the ball while attacking.

title: Orlando 2 Phase Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, play takes place on a vertically-aligned small-sided pitch roughly the size of two 18-yard boxes stacked together (36 yards long). Each team consists of two attackers, with one team active while the other rests.The active pair begins behind the top goal, sprinting forward into the top box to finish from a wide cross. Immediately after the first finish, they transition down into the bottom box to complete a second finish from another wide cross—simulating quick attacking movements and repeated final-third actions.After both finishes, the active team rotates out to rest while the next pair completes their two finishes, maintaining intensity and recovery balance throughout the drill.
coaching_notes: • First Movement Sharpness – Emphasize a game-like sprint to attack the top-box cross at speed, replicating in-game urgency and positioning.• Adjusting Runs to Cross – Attackers should vary runs (front post, back post, late arrival) based on the cross type and deliverer’s position.• Quick Transition Between Boxes – Players must switch mental and physical gears instantly to prepare for the second cross after the initial finish.• Composure on Final Ball – Despite repeated efforts, attackers should stay calm in front of goal and focus on clean, accurate finishing techniques.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender in Second BoxIntroduce a passive defender into the bottom box to create mild resistance, forcing attackers to adjust their timing and movement for the second finish.Focus:Improves scanning, timing, and adaptability under light pressure while still prioritizing technique.
progression_two: Introduce a Timed Finish RequirementSet a 5-second limit from entering the bottom box to completing the second finish, encouraging urgency and efficiency in transitioning between finishes.Focus:Increases game-realistic tempo, decision-making speed, and encourages quick recovery into optimal finishing positions.

title: Orlando 2v2 Press & Cover
instructions_setup: In this drill, players focus on the press and cover principle, which is crucial for effective defending. One defender is tasked with pressing the ball carrier, while a second defender covers the central space, ensuring that the defensive team stays compact and organized.As the ball is passed backward, the pressing defenders must adjust their positioning and squeeze the play, continuing to work together to maintain defensive pressure. The focus is on communication, maintaining balance, and ensuring that the defenders are always in the right position to support each other.
coaching_notes: • Pressing the Ball Carrier: The player pressing the ball should stay close to the ball carrier, applying pressure without diving into tackles. The goal is to force the attacker into making a rushed decision while staying balanced.• Covering the Central Space: The second defender must ensure they are covering the central passing lanes and be ready to intercept any passes played into dangerous areas. This defender should stay in a position to quickly support the press or shift to cover other threats.• Adjusting to the Ball: As the ball is passed backward, the pressing defenders must adjust their positioning quickly. This requires awareness and good communication to maintain pressure on the ball carrier while controlling the central space.• Compactness and Squeezing Play: The defenders should work together to reduce the space available to the attacking team, keeping the team compact and forcing the ball into less dangerous areas. Squeezing the play is key to preventing the opposition from building up attacks.

title: Orlando Attacking 1v2
instructions_setup: Play begins with a pass from the defender to the attacker. As soon as the attacker takes their first touch, a second defender joins the practice to create a 1v2 situation. The attacker’s goal is to maintain speed and exploit any space available in order to keep the situation favorable and avoid it becoming a complete 1v2 scenario. The attacker must attack quickly to create opportunities and maintain an advantage over the defenders.
coaching_notes: • Quick First TouchEncourage the attacker to take a quick and positive first touch, pushing the ball into space and setting up a potential attack. The quicker the first touch, the more space the attacker will have before the second defender arrives, making it easier to keep the situation as a 1v1 for longer.• Exploiting the SpaceThe key to success in a 1v2 situation is to exploit the space and keep the defenders off balance. Encourage the attacker to use their pace, agility, and creativity to get past the defenders. Changing direction quickly, using feints, and creating separation from the defenders are all essential strategies for success.• Composure in Tight SituationsOnce the second defender joins, remind the attacker to stay composed and make calculated decisions. Rushing or losing control of the ball will allow the defenders to regain the advantage. Focus on the attacker’s ability to read the situation, control the ball under pressure, and make an intelligent decision to either shoot or pass.• Creating Angles and TimingThe attacker should aim to manipulate the defenders by creating angles and timing their movements effectively. This could include cutting inside to draw the defenders and create space, or using quick changes of pace to force one defender out of position. Encourage attackers to be unpredictable in their approach, making it difficult for the defenders to anticipate their next move.
progression_one: Add More DefendersIntroduce a third defender who can act as a "support defender" that enters after the 1v2. This progression simulates a more complex situation where attackers must deal with additional defensive pressure.Focus: This increases the difficulty, requiring the attacker to make quicker decisions and create more space to retain the upper hand.
progression_two: Limit Time to AttackReduce the time the attacker has to take a shot or make a pass once the second defender enters. This increases the urgency of the decision-making process and ensures that attackers keep up the pace.Focus: This progression trains players to make fast, effective decisions under pressure, simulating real game scenarios.

title: Orlando Build & Break Lines
instructions_setup: In this unopposed build-up practice, play starts with a pass between two centre backs (CBs). One CB then plays a forward pass to the central defensive midfielder (CDM), who quickly passes the ball back to the opposite CB that has moved slightly higher up the pitch. That CB then plays a vertical pass into a mini goal, simulating a short and controlled build-up pattern between the CBs and CDM.
coaching_notes: • Body Position and Awareness – Encourage players to always receive with an open body shape to improve vision and passing options.• Timing and Movement – The CB moving higher must time their movement perfectly to receive under minimal pressure and create passing angles.• Passing Precision – Focus on accurate, weighted passes to maintain possession and enable smooth progression through the lines.• Patience and Composure – Players should stay calm during the sequence to replicate realistic short build-up play under pressure.
progression_one: Passive Defensive PressureIntroduce a passive defender applying light pressure on the CDM or CBs, forcing quicker decision-making and sharper passing accuracy.Focus:Develops composure under mild pressure and improves quick ball circulation through midfield.

title: Orlando Build Up Patterns
instructions_setup: This passing activation allows a team to develop their build-up patterns using a midfield 3. There are three different variations that the players can play through to work on different types of build-up and movement.
coaching_notes: • Variation 1 – Short Passing & Quick InterchangesEncourage the midfield 3 to play short, quick passes with an emphasis on fast combinations. The players should focus on maintaining possession while looking to break lines with short passes or by using overlapping movements. Timing and angles of support are key to maintaining fluidity in the build-up.• Variation 2 – Switch of Play & Wide PlayIn this variation, the team should look to switch the ball quickly from one side to the other, using the width of the field to stretch the defensive lines. The midfielders need to be aware of the space and play the ball quickly to the wide areas, where the wingers or full-backs can receive and attack further up the field.• Variation 3 – Deep Laying Pivot & Forward ProgressionThe deep-lying midfielder should focus on playing progressive passes to the two more advanced midfielders, who in turn can play forward passes into the attack. This progression helps develop vertical passing, enabling the team to break the opposition’s defensive lines and penetrate the final third effectively.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a small defensive unit to press the build-up from the midfield. This simulates game situations where the attacking team must retain possession and work through pressure.Focus: This progression helps players improve their decision-making when facing pressure and reinforces the need for quick ball movement and spatial awareness.
progression_two: Limit the Number of TouchesTo increase intensity and focus on quick passing, limit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., maximum 2 touches).Focus: This progression enhances the speed of play and forces the midfielders to make faster decisions while maintaining accuracy in their passes.

title: Orlando Build Up v Counter
instructions_setup: In this build-up vs counter drill, the team in possession is supported by two goalkeepers, creating a 7v4 scenario where the attacking team must retain possession against the four pressing defenders. The objective is to focus on building up play from the back while under pressure, encouraging intelligent ball circulation and positioning to outplay the pressing defenders.If the defending team wins possession, they transition into a counter-attack with the aim of scoring in either of the two goals located at the opposite end. The team in possession must be vigilant and maintain quick, precise passing to break through the press. The players along the sides of the grid can enter the central area to help disrupt the counter-attack, providing an additional layer of defensive support if the ball is lost.
coaching_notes: • Maintaining Possession Under Pressure: The team in possession must focus on moving the ball quickly and accurately, making use of their numerical advantage with the goalkeepers. Players should move to create passing angles and maintain a calm, composed mindset to avoid losing the ball under pressure.• Transitioning to Defense: The defending team must be alert to any opportunity to win possession, closing down passing lanes and forcing mistakes. Upon winning the ball, they should aim to transition into a quick counter-attack, exploiting any gaps left by the attacking team.• Supporting the Counter-Attack: The four players on the side of the grid can support the defending team’s counter-attack by quickly getting into position, either by cutting off passing options or joining the counter to increase numbers in the attack. Timing and awareness are key here.• Quick Decision-Making: Both the attacking and defending teams must be quick in their decision-making. The attackers should look to break down the defense by moving the ball efficiently, while the defenders need to react rapidly to regain possession and capitalize on a counter-attacking opportunity.
progression_one: Add a 2nd Phase of the Counter-Attack:Once the defending team wins possession, they are allowed to play an additional pass before attacking the goal, simulating a more realistic counter-attack scenario where players may need to look for a better option.Focus: Enhances the attacking team’s ability to quickly build up under pressure, while challenging the defenders to make fast, accurate decisions and execute a more structured counter-attack.

title: Orlando Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: In this finishing drill, the striker begins by making a movement to either the left or right pole, as determined by the coach or server. As the striker makes this movement, a defender, who starts behind the server, begins to recover and apply pressure on the attacker. Once the attacker receives the pass, they must quickly turn and attack the goal to finish, while being closely pressured by the recovering defender.This drill works on both the striker's movement off the ball, their ability to finish under pressure, and their decision-making when closing down the goal.
coaching_notes: • Off-the-Ball Movement: Encourage the striker to make a sharp and purposeful movement towards the poles to create space for themselves. This movement should be explosive, allowing them to receive the ball in a favorable position to attack the goal.• Receiving Under Pressure: The striker must focus on controlling the ball efficiently despite pressure from the defender. Remind them to receive with their body open and prepare to shoot quickly, minimizing time on the ball.• Finishing Under Pressure: The striker should maintain composure when shooting under pressure. Encourage them to focus on placement over power and aim for the far corners of the goal to increase the likelihood of scoring.• Defender's Pressure: The recovering defender should apply pressure, forcing the striker to make a decision quickly. The attacker should be prepared to adjust their finish based on the defender's positioning.
progression_one: Increase Defender Pressure:Start the defender closer to the attacker, reducing the time and space for the striker to finish. This progression encourages the striker to be even more decisive in their movement and finishing.Focus: This will increase the challenge of finishing under pressure, simulating real match conditions where defenders are constantly closing down the attacker.
progression_two: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender who arrives shortly after the first. The attackers will now need to make quicker decisions and may need to look for a different finishing option.Focus: This progression replicates a more intense match situation where attackers are under more pressure from multiple defenders, improving their ability to handle stress and execute a quality finish.

title: Orlando One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This 1-to-1 technical passing drill is focused on sharp combination play, quick movement, and accurate decision-making. The player begins each rep by completing a short 1-2 pass before sprinting forward to receive a second pass from the coach. After receiving, they must play a well-weighted pass into one of two mini goals, encouraging scanning, timing, and execution.
coaching_notes: • Accelerate Immediately After Playing the Initial Pass – Time your run sharply to arrive in rhythm for the next ball and maintain attacking momentum.• Receive on the Back Foot to Open the Body – Angle your touch to face the mini goals instantly and create more passing options.• Scan Both Mini Goals Before the Final Pass – Make a quick decision on which goal is best based on timing, space, and angle.• Use a Quality Final Pass With Correct Weight – Deliver the ball with enough pace and precision to simulate a purposeful attacking pass.
progression_one: Alternate the Side of the Final PassEncourage the player to vary which mini goal they pass into each rep to develop two-sided vision and decision-making.Focus:Improves passing accuracy, two-footed distribution, and awareness of available targets under time pressure.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender During the Second PhasePlace a passive defender between the player and the mini goals to apply light pressure and disrupt the passing lane.Focus:Enhances composure, timing of the final ball, and ability to adjust passing lines under defensive presence.

title: Orlando Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical passing drill focuses on improving the accuracy and timing of vertical passes while maintaining fluid ball movement. Players will work on passing the ball forward to break through lines, while simultaneously ensuring the ball is controlled and passed between cones to maintain rhythm and precision.The setup involves four vertical cones placed in a line. Players will pass the ball forward, then play a pass between the cones, and continue this pattern all the way to the top of the grid. The movement should be continuous, with each pass building up towards the goal. This drill allows players to work on both passing accuracy and decision-making in a controlled, low-pressure environment.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy: Emphasize the importance of making accurate forward passes, ensuring the ball travels smoothly and directly to the next player or target cone.• Use of Cones for Spatial Awareness: Players must be aware of the cones' positioning and ensure that their passes are played accurately between them, maintaining good technique and precision throughout.• Fluid Movement: The drill should be done with fluid, continuous movement, ensuring the player plays forward and back with minimal delay. Focus on transitioning quickly between forward passes and cone passes.• Body Position and Technique: Ensure players position themselves correctly when receiving and passing the ball. They should receive the ball with an open body to be able to pass smoothly in the intended direction.
progression_one: Add a One-Touch Pass Between Cones:Players now must play a one-touch pass when passing through the cones. This will encourage faster play and better ball control, focusing on quick, efficient decision-making and passing.Focus: Enhances first-touch passing skills and encourages quicker decision-making, improving the pace and fluidity of the play.
progression_two: Vary the Passing Length:Change the length of the vertical passes (shorter or longer), forcing players to adjust the weight of their passes while maintaining accuracy and timing. This progression challenges the players to control and pass over different distances.Focus: Improves the players' ability to judge the appropriate weight for different passes, ensuring they can maintain precision regardless of the distance between them and the target.

title: Orlando Reactions Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this fun reactions warm-up, a coach will shout 'left', 'right', or 'GO'. Upon hearing the call, the players must react accordingly by either shuffling to the left, shuffling to the right, or sprinting forward to reach the ball placed directly ahead of them. The goal is to react quickly and get to the ball before the opposing player does.To increase the challenge, a coloured pole can be placed behind the players. The coach will then call out a specific colour, prompting players to run to that pole before proceeding with the main reaction (shuffling left, right, or sprinting forward). This introduces an extra layer of complexity to the practice, adding a fourth action to the exercise.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions – Players must focus on reacting instantly to the coach’s call. The quicker they react, the better they’ll perform in high-pressure game situations. Encourage them to anticipate the next move as much as possible to stay one step ahead.• Agility and Movement – Players should keep their center of gravity low when shuffling and explode forward when sprinting. This will help improve their agility and speed, which are essential for both offensive and defensive play.• Focus on Directional Changes – Emphasize the importance of rapid directional changes. Players should avoid hesitating when changing direction, which is key in both defensive and attacking scenarios.• Mental Sharpness and Awareness – Players should stay mentally focused and aware of both the coach’s commands and the positioning of their opponents. The practice develops the ability to remain alert and make quick decisions on the fly.
progression_one: Add More ActionsIntroduce more commands like 'turn' or 'jump' to increase the variety of actions players have to perform. This will enhance their overall reaction time and movement skills.Focus:Develops adaptability to various game situations and increases overall reaction speed.
progression_two: Head-to-Head ChallengeSet up a competitive element where players go head-to-head, and the first one to reach the ball or pole wins a point. This adds a competitive edge and increases motivation.Focus:Encourages a competitive mindset and enhances game-day intensity.

title: Orlando Technical Activation
instructions_setup: This mastery activation is a fantastic arrival activity, designed to allow players to get a high number of touches on the ball in a short space of time. The focus is on developing multiple skills in an unopposed environment, including passing, dribbling, and ball control.Set up a grid (e.g., 10x10 meters) with cones or markers scattered throughout to create space for various drills. Players will engage in individual activities, alternating between passing sequences, dribbling, and technical touches.Encourage players to incorporate different types of touches and skills, such as inside/outside touches, step-overs, feints, and quick turns during the dribbling phase.
coaching_notes: • Variety of Skills – Encourage players to use a variety of touches and dribbling techniques during their activation, such as using the inside, outside, and sole of the foot. They should also work on feints, quick turns, and changes of direction to develop their agility and ball control.• Focus on Speed and Fluidity – Emphasize the importance of fluid movement when dribbling and passing. The key is to encourage players to maintain speed without sacrificing control. This will improve their ability to play at a higher tempo during matches.• Passing Accuracy – Players should focus on accurate short passes and one-touch passing during the activation. Encourage them to focus on keeping passes crisp and precise while engaging with the ball efficiently.• Engage Both Feet – Encourage players to use both feet during the dribbling and passing phases. This will ensure they develop their ability to be two-footed, improving their versatility and overall technical ability.• Work on Touch and Control – As players work through the technical activation, encourage them to focus on their first touch and ball control. A good first touch sets up the next action, whether it’s a pass or dribble.
progression_one: Incorporate a Time LimitAdd a time limit to complete a series of skills or passes (e.g., 30 seconds or 1 minute) for each player. This forces them to accelerate the pace of their work while maintaining accuracy and technical ability.Focus:Improves speed of play and helps players develop the ability to think and act quickly under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Light PressureIntroduce a light defender to create a mild pressure scenario where the attacking player must dribble or pass while being lightly pressured. This will simulate real match situations where players need to maintain technical ability while under defensive pressure.Focus:Encourages players to focus on decision-making while still maintaining the technical aspects of their game, especially in tight spaces.

title: Orlando Technical Into 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with a technical passing combination, which ends in a pass into one of the mini-goals. Once the technical aspect has been completed, the practice transitions into a 1v1 attack, where the attacking player will attempt to beat the defender and score into either of the two mini-goals.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Passing Accuracy – Emphasize the importance of accurate passing during the technical combination. Players should focus on crisp, well-weighted passes to set up the 1v1 situation effectively.• Speed of Play – Encourage players to move quickly through the technical part of the drill and transition smoothly into the 1v1 scenario. The quicker they complete the passing sequence, the more pressure they’ll place on the defender in the 1v1 phase.• 1v1 Techniques – In the 1v1 scenario, the attacking player should focus on their dribbling techniques, including fakes, changes of pace, and direction to beat the defender. Encourage the attacker to be direct and creative while maintaining control.• Defender Positioning – Defenders should work on proper positioning, staying compact, and timing their tackles. They should aim to delay the attacker and force them into less dangerous areas while being careful not to overcommit.
progression_one: Add Time PressureTo increase the challenge, set a time limit for the technical passing section, with players needing to complete the passing combination and transition into the 1v1 within a set time.Focus: This progression will increase the intensity, pushing players to move and think quickly, sharpening both their passing and decision-making.
progression_two: Defensive RestrictionsLimit the defender's ability to move or make tackles in the 1v1 phase, allowing the attacker more freedom to try different dribbling moves.Focus: This progression focuses on developing the attacker’s confidence in 1v1 situations and allows them to experiment with different techniques without the pressure of defending tactics.

title: Orlando Transitioning Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo drill focuses on recovery runs and transition play, helping players work on quick reactions, fitness, and maintaining possession under pressure. The drill is designed to simulate game-like scenarios where players must recover quickly after losing possession and transition into a defensive role.The setup includes 3 grids, with 2 grids being live at any given time. Each live grid consists of a 4v2 rondo, where the team in possession is tasked with maintaining control of the ball, while the defenders attempt to win possession. Once the 2 defenders win possession in one grid, the player who lost possession and the player to their right must sprint into the open grid and become the 2 defenders, immediately transitioning into a defensive role.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition: Emphasize the importance of rapid recovery runs and quick transitions from attack to defense. Players must react instantly when possession is lost and move into the next grid without hesitation.• Pressure and Support: Encourage players to provide quick support to the ball carrier while maintaining proper spacing to make it easier for the team in possession to keep the ball. The defenders must press aggressively to force turnovers.• Communication: Players should be vocal and communicate their movements, especially when transitioning into new grids. Clear calls will help teammates adjust their positions accordingly.• Fitness and Stamina: Ensure players understand the importance of maintaining a high intensity throughout the drill, pushing themselves to recover quickly and continue working at pace.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Transition:Implement a time limit for each transition phase (e.g., 5 seconds to enter the new grid and start defending). This progression challenges the players to recover quickly and shift focus to defense under time pressure.Focus: Enhances the players’ urgency and ability to recover and transition defensively within a limited time, simulating game-like conditions.

title: Oslo Attacking Overloaded
instructions_setup: This attacking overload practice begins with a player dribbling forward to commit defenders before releasing a pass into one of two wide attackers positioned on the left and right. Once the wide player receives, the practice becomes live with a 3v2 attacking scenario, involving the initial dribbler, the wide attacker and a central number 9 attacking against two defenders.The attacking unit is encouraged to combine quickly, create overloads and attack the goal with purpose. The practice can be progressed by allowing the opposite winger—who does not initially receive the pass—to join the phase, creating a 4v2 and increasing the attacking options and decision-making demands.
coaching_notes: • Positive Dribbling: Encourage the initial attacker to drive forward with intent to attract defenders before releasing the pass.• Wide Player Decision-Making: Reinforce quick choices upon receiving—dribble, combine or deliver based on defender positioning.• Movement of the Number 9: Coach the striker to vary movements, offering support, stretching the defence or creating space for runners.• Speed of Attack: Emphasise fast combinations and forward momentum to exploit the numerical advantage.
progression_one: Allow the Opposite Winger to Join:The winger on the far side is released once the first pass is played wide, creating a 4v2 attacking overload.Focus: Increases attacking options, off-ball movement and recognition of overloads.
progression_two: Touch Limit on Attackers:Restrict attackers to two touches where possible to increase tempo and force quicker decisions.Focus: Develops speed of play, combination quality and composure in the final third.

title: Oslo Finishing From In-Swingers
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice focuses on creating goalscoring opportunities from inswinging deliveries. Play begins with a square pass in midfield, after which the midfielder plays the ball out wide to a winger. Upon receiving, the winger takes a touch back inside—either cutting infield or slightly withdrawing the ball—to create the angle for an inswinging cross into the penalty area.Two attackers make coordinated runs into the box to attack the delivery and finish unopposed. The practice replicates common match scenarios where wide players cut inside or cut back before whipping the ball towards the back-post or central finishing zones.
coaching_notes: • Wide Player’s First Touch: Encourage a controlled touch inside to set up the correct body shape for an inswinging delivery.• Crossing Detail: Reinforce the importance of pace, trajectory and accuracy, targeting back-post and central areas.• Timing of Attacking Runs: Coach the two attackers to vary movements, attacking different zones to maximise finishing options.• End Product: Emphasise composed finishing based on the type and height of the cross.
progression_one: One-Touch Finish for Attackers:Require the attackers to finish first time from the cross.Focus: Improves timing, anticipation and finishing technique.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender:Introduce a passive defender in the box to apply light pressure and force more realistic movement and finishing decisions.Focus: Increases realism and challenges composure in the penalty area.

title: Oslo Progressive Attacking
instructions_setup: This progressive attacking practice is designed to build finishing actions through increasing levels of pressure and numerical complexity. Three attackers start with a ball each, positioned outside the main playing area.Phase 1: The central attacker begins with a 1v0 finish against the goalkeeper, focusing on clean technique and composure. After completing the finish, they quickly recover their position to receive a second ball played in from one of the supporting attackers.Phase 2: As the second ball is introduced, one defender becomes active, creating a 2v1 scenario. The two attackers must combine quickly to create another finishing opportunity.Phase 3: Immediately after the second phase, the two attackers receive a pass from the third attacker, who joins the practice alongside a second defender. This creates a 3v2 attacking scenario, requiring fast combination play, movement and decision-making before finishing.The practice flows continuously, challenging attackers to adapt as the numbers change while maintaining attacking intent.
coaching_notes: • Composure in Phase One: Encourage clean technique and calm finishing in the unopposed phase.• Speed of Combination: Reinforce quick passes and movement as defenders are introduced.• Decision-Making Under Pressure: Coach attackers to recognise when to shoot, pass or carry as the overload evolves.• Attacking Movement: Emphasise supporting angles, depth and timing of runs to exploit numerical advantages.
progression_one: Time Limit for Each Phase:Introduce a strict time window for each attacking phase to maintain tempo and intensity.Focus: Improves attacking urgency and speed of execution.
progression_two: Add Recovery Runs:Allow defenders to recover from different angles or distances to increase unpredictability.Focus: Enhances realism and forces sharper attacking decisions.

title: Oslo React & 1v1
instructions_setup: This reactive finishing practice develops decision-making, agility, and 1v1 attacking and defending. An attacker and a defender start by passing the ball back and forth. At any moment, the attacker can spin left or right and run through a designated gate to collect a ball and enter a 1v1 against the goalkeeper.Simultaneously, the defender must sprint through the opposite gate and attempt to recover in time to challenge the 1v1. This drill encourages quick thinking, explosive movement, and realistic attacking and defensive transitions under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Attacker Decision-Making: Encourage scanning and quick choice of which direction to spin and attack.• First Touch and Control: Emphasise clean ball control when receiving through the gate to set up the 1v1 effectively.• Defensive Recovery: Reinforce explosive sprinting, anticipation and correct body positioning to challenge the attacker.• Finishing Execution: Coach composure and accuracy when finishing under pressure from the recovering defender.
progression_one: Time Limit to Score:Introduce a 4–5 second limit for the attacker to finish after collecting the ball.Focus: Increases tempo and forces faster decision-making.

title: Oslo React & Finish 1v1
instructions_setup: This reactive finishing practice combines coordination, reaction speed and 1v1 decision-making. Two teams start opposite each other, with one player from each team working simultaneously through their own agility ladder using quick footwork.After completing the ladder, both players meet in the central area. At this moment, the bottom player reacts to a trigger and breaks either left or right to collect a ball and attack the goal in a 1v1 against the goalkeeper. The top player immediately transitions into a defensive role, reacting to the attacker’s movement and attempting to recover and stop the goal-scoring opportunity.The practice encourages fast reactions, sharp transitions and realistic 1v1 finishing scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Footwork Quality: Emphasise light, quick steps through the ladder while maintaining balance and control.• Reaction Speed: Coach attackers to explode immediately on the trigger and commit to their chosen direction.• Attacking Intent: Encourage positive, direct play in the 1v1—attack space, commit the defender and finish decisively.• Defensive Recovery: Reinforce quick reactions, recovery angles and controlled defending to delay or block the shot.
progression_one: Delayed Trigger for the Defender:Give the attacker a split-second head start before the defender can react.Focus: Encourages aggressive attacking play and confident finishing.

title: Paris Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: In this ball mastery drill, players work on their dribbling skills and their ability to execute quick 2-player combinations. The drill emphasizes ball control, speed, and precision in tight spaces, providing an opportunity for players to practice both individual and team-oriented skills.The drill begins with players dribbling through a set of vertical cones, focusing on maintaining close control while navigating the obstacles. Once at the top of the grid, the player performs a 2-player combination with a teammate, before rotating positions. The player who was at the top of the grid dribbles quickly back down to the starting point (without going through the cones), while the original dribbler takes their position at the top, ready to repeat the process.
coaching_notes: • Close Ball Control: Encourage players to keep the ball close to their feet while dribbling through the cones, using small, quick touches to maintain control, especially when working in tight spaces.• Quick Combinations: Focus on timing and communication during the 2-player combination at the top of the grid. The players should make quick passes, anticipating the movement of their teammate and being prepared for a return pass.• Movement Off the Ball: Stress the importance of good movement off the ball. The player at the top of the grid should position themselves in an area that allows for a clean combination, while the dribbler should look to create space for the pass.• Speed and Agility: Players should work on their speed and agility, moving quickly through the cones and executing the combination play at a high tempo. Quick changes of direction are key to the success of this drill.
progression_one: Increase Speed and Complexity of Combinations:Incorporate more complex combination plays, such as give-and-go or wall passes, to increase the difficulty and challenge players to make decisions faster.Focus: This progression develops players’ technical ability and sharpens their decision-making skills in executing more advanced combinations at higher speeds.

title: Paris Build Up & Transitions
instructions_setup: In this build-up drill, the team in possession is tasked with progressing play into one of the two wide players, who are locked into small 5x5-yard grids located in opposite corners of the halfway line. This drill focuses on building play from the back and transitioning quickly to exploit spaces in wide areas.Play begins with the team in possession looking to progress the ball through the middle of the field and out to the wide player in one of the grids. Once the ball reaches the wide zone, a counter attack is triggered from the opposite side, where the other wide player must join the attack and counter against an unbalanced defense in a 7v7 scenario. The attacking team must transition quickly to exploit the overload on the opposite side.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition Play: Players should focus on quickly moving the ball from defense to attack, making use of quick passes and transitions to move the ball into the wide areas.• Wide Play Utilization: The wide players must make themselves available to receive passes, creating width to stretch the opposition and provide options for the ball carrier.• Timing and Movement: The timing of the pass to the wide player is crucial. Players need to recognize when to make runs, either into the wide space or central areas, to support the attack and pull the opposition out of position.• Exploiting Imbalances: Upon reaching the wide zone, players must quickly identify the 7v7 situation and exploit the unbalanced defense. Movement off the ball and quick decisions will create openings for the counter attack.

title: Paris Channel 1v1's
instructions_setup: In this drill, players are encouraged to beat a defender in a 1v1 scenario before scoring into one of the mini goals. The focus is on individual attacking skills and the ability to maintain possession under pressure, while also encouraging defenders to work on positioning and anticipation.Play begins with the attacker attempting to beat the defender and score in the mini goal. If the attacker successfully scores, the defender remains as a defender and prepares to face a new attacker.If the defender wins possession and manages to dribble over the end line, they switch roles and become the attacker, while the player who lost possession becomes the defender. This drill emphasizes continuous movement and the quick transition between attack and defense.With three narrow channels available, a total of three individual practices can run simultaneously, reducing waiting times for players and increasing repetitions.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Creativity: Encourage attackers to use a variety of dribbling techniques, such as feints, quick changes of direction, and close control to beat the defender.• Defensive Positioning: Defenders must focus on maintaining a strong defensive stance, staying close enough to pressure the attacker but also being ready to recover if the attacker changes direction.• Quick Transitioning: The drill requires both players to transition quickly between attack and defense, so focus on the ability to switch mindsets and adapt rapidly to the changing situation.• Decision-Making: Both the attacker and defender must make split-second decisions. Attackers must decide when to take on the defender, and defenders must assess whether to commit to a tackle or contain the attacker.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for attackers to score once they have beaten the defender, such as 10 seconds. This encourages quicker decision-making and faster attacks.Focus: This progression aims to increase the tempo of the drill, forcing attackers to act decisively and defenders to react quickly to pressure.

title: Paris Finishing In Behind
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, players work on the key movement of getting in behind the defensive line to receive a pass and finish on goal. The focus is on timing the run, positioning, and finishing technique as players look to exploit space behind the defense.The drill begins with the player starting at the edge of the box or a designated starting point. A coach or player will play a pass into the space behind the defense (or cones in this case), and the player must time their run to get in behind and finish past the goalkeeper into the goal.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Run: Encourage players to focus on their timing, making their run just as the ball is played, ensuring they are onside and in the best position to receive the pass.• Anticipating the Pass: Players should anticipate where the ball will be played, making sure they make the run into the space at the right moment to stay ahead of any defenders.• Finishing Under Pressure: Players should focus on staying composed when finishing, taking quick touches to set up the shot and finishing with accuracy either with their dominant foot or a first-time strike.• Using the Space: Remind players to recognize the space they are attacking and use it wisely, focusing on staying wide or cutting in depending on the situation to create a better angle for finishing.
progression_one: Varying Pass Types:The coach or another player will vary the type of pass played—through balls, chipped passes, or driven balls—so players must adjust their runs and finishing technique accordingly.Focus: This progression develops the player's ability to read different types of passes and adjust their movement and finishing technique under different circumstances.
progression_two: Add a Defender:Introduce a passive defender who starts behind the player receiving the ball. The defender can apply light pressure to challenge the player but is not actively defending, allowing the player to work on getting in behind while under light pressure.Focus: This progression introduces a level of pressure to replicate match situations, helping the player work on their movement and finishing while being aware of defenders closing in.

title: Paris Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: In this high-intensity possession drill, players work on speed, communication, and decision-making. The objective is to win possession inside a small grid and then sprint back to the poles to reset, all while maintaining clear communication with teammates.The drill involves four teams of three players. Three teams are located inside separate 8x8-yard grids, while the fourth team is stationed on poles above each grid. At the coach's whistle, all three players in each grid must sprint to win possession of the ball. As soon as a team wins possession, all three players sprint back to their poles and the process repeats. This cycle continues for three rounds.
coaching_notes: • Communication and Teamwork: Encourage players to communicate clearly with each other, especially the player who wins possession. They should quickly relay the message for the other two teammates to sprint back to the poles, maintaining efficiency.• Winning Possession: Players must work together to win possession through pressure and positioning, ensuring that the entire team is actively involved in the challenge.• Speed and Reaction: Focus on the players’ ability to sprint back to their poles efficiently, improving their ability to react quickly and transition between offense and defense.• Decision-Making: Players should be encouraged to make quick decisions when winning possession, choosing whether to pass immediately or maintain control of the ball, depending on the situation.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit:Implement a time limit for each round, where teams must win possession and return to their poles within a set time (e.g., 20 seconds). If they fail, they restart the round.Focus: This progression increases urgency and speed, challenging players to work more efficiently in both possession and transition phases.

title: Paris One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This unopposed 1-to-1 winger drill focuses on decision-making, dribbling, and execution in wide areas. The winger receives a pass out wide and drives toward a mannequin positioned just outside the box. As they approach, the coach shouts either “1” or “2.” If “1” is called, the winger takes the ball down the line and delivers a cross into a mini goal near the six-yard box. If “2” is called, the winger cuts inside and finishes on goal.
coaching_notes: • Scan Early to Prepare Before Receiving – Check surroundings before the ball arrives to plan your first touch and route.• Drive at Defender with Controlled Aggression – Approach the mannequin at pace with tight touches to force a decision point.• Disguise and Commit on Final Move – Use body feints or changes of pace to sell the action and commit the mannequin.• Deliver with Purpose Based on Decision – Cross or shoot with precision depending on coach's call, maintaining technical control.

title: Paris Passing Pattern
instructions_setup: This unopposed technical passing drill focuses on improving players' ability to execute short, quick passes followed by longer, more penetrating passes. The drill helps players develop their passing range and the ability to switch between different types of passes in fluid situations.In this drill, there are two balls working simultaneously, with players mirroring each other’s movements. After each pass, the player follows their pass around the cones to the next position to receive and pass again.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: Encourage players to make quick, accurate decisions when deciding whether to play a short or long pass, ensuring the timing of their passes is well-executed.• Passing Technique: Focus on the quality of both the short and long passes. For the short passes, players should use the inside of the foot for accuracy, while long passes should be driven with the laces to cover more distance.• Movement and Follow-up: Players should follow their pass to the next position, ensuring continuous movement and fluidity throughout the drill, simulating a game-like scenario where movement after the pass is crucial.• Body Position: Players should be encouraged to receive the ball with their body open to the field, ensuring they are in a position to play the next pass quickly and efficiently.
progression_one: Change the Length of Long Passes:Adjust the length of the long passes in the drill, varying between a medium-range pass (30-40 yards) and a long-range pass (50+ yards). This variation helps players adapt to different passing distances.Focus: This progression helps players build confidence and accuracy when varying the length of long passes, improving their versatility in different match situations.

title: Paris Switch & Overload
instructions_setup: This drill begins with an unopposed switch of play, focusing on improving passing accuracy and timing in transition. The objective is to encourage quick decision-making and effective attacking play once the defenders enter the scenario.The play starts with an unopposed switch of play from one winger to a central player, and then the ball is passed to the opposite winger. As soon as the ball reaches the opposite winger, the attack transitions into an opposed phase. The attackers must now play out a 3v2 scenario, with a 7-second limit to complete the attack.
coaching_notes: • Accurate Switching of Play: Encourage players to focus on making a crisp, accurate switch of play from one winger to the other, ensuring the ball is delivered quickly and precisely to allow for fast transitions.• Quick Reaction to Opposed Phase: As soon as the ball reaches the opposite winger, the attackers must quickly transition to playing in a 3v2 scenario. Players should be aware of the need to exploit the numerical advantage within the time limit.• Movement off the Ball: Encourage attackers to move into space and make supporting runs to provide options for the ball carrier. Players should vary their movements, using decoy runs and diagonal runs to create confusion for the defenders.• Decision-Making Under Time Pressure: With the 7-second limit, attackers must make quick decisions to either create a shooting opportunity or pass to a teammate in a better position.
progression_one: Increase Attackers to 4v3 or 5v4:In this progression, the attacking team now has either a 4v3 or 5v4 advantage in the opposed phase. The setup allows for more players to be involved in the attack, creating additional passing options and space to exploit.Focus: The larger numerical advantage gives the attacking team more freedom to move the ball quickly, make more varied runs, and force the defenders into tougher decision-making. The goal is to encourage better movement off the ball, quick decision-making, and effective use of the numerical superiority to create goal-scoring opportunities.

title: Paris Wide Attacks SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is a standard 6v6 or 7v7 setup, with the added challenge of rewarding teams with an extra point or goal if the ball is delivered from any of the four wide areas. These wide zones are marked with squared cones on the flanks of the field.The objective is to encourage players to focus on attacking through the wider channels and commit more players to the offensive play in these areas. The game promotes the use of width, providing more space for creativity and forcing teams to work on wide plays and crosses, while also allowing defenders to practice closing down wide spaces effectively.
coaching_notes: • Utilize Width: Encourage players to spread the play, using the width of the field to stretch the opposition’s defense and create space for the ball to be delivered into dangerous areas.• Quick Transitions: Stress the importance of quick transitions from defense to attack, especially when the ball is switched to the wide areas. Players must move quickly to exploit the space and take advantage of the extra point opportunity.• Crossing and Finishing: Focus on quality delivery from the wide players. Encourage attackers to time their runs well and make themselves available in the box for a well-placed cross.• Support the Wide Play: Players in central positions should provide support to the wide players, either by offering options for short passes or by preparing for a second phase of attack.
progression_one: Add Restriction on Central Play:Limit central players to completing a certain number of passes before the ball must go wide to earn the extra point. This forces the team to work through the width of the field and focus on ball movement to the flanks.Focus: Encourages teams to focus on attacking through wide areas and emphasizes ball circulation before utilizing the wide zones.

title: Prague 4 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This is a continuous 4-phase unopposed finishing drill involving three players working together through a series of attacking patterns. Each phase represents a different style of movement, combination, or delivery that leads to a shot on goal, encouraging repetition, rhythm, and variety in finishing scenarios.The practice focuses on developing timing of runs, clean technical execution, and finishing under minimal pressure. Once a shot is taken in one phase, players immediately transition into the next, cycling through all four phases before restarting the sequence.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize clean execution of passing and movement between phases – Players should maintain high technical quality and flow through each attacking pattern• Encourage communication and timing of runs into key areas – Players must coordinate movements to ensure arrivals into shooting zones are well-timed and not rushed• Focus on body shape and finishing variety during shooting moments – Players should practice using different surfaces and shot types based on the delivery• Reinforce tempo and sharpness throughout all four phases – Even though unopposed, players should treat each sequence with game-like intensity and purpose
progression_one: Reverse the Sequence DirectionHave players complete the four phases in reverse order to challenge their adaptability and sharpen their awareness in new sequences.Focus: Promotes flexibility in pattern recognition and reinforces movement in different directions across the attacking third.

title: Prague Beat the Defender 1v1
instructions_setup: In this drill, the attacker receives a pass back to goal while being tightly marked by a defender. The initial pass comes from a teammate and is played into the attacker’s feet, requiring the attacker to control the ball under pressure and prepare for a 1v1 confrontation. The attacker’s objective is to use skill moves and quick turns to create space and beat the defender.Once the attacker has separated from the defender, they must spin around and score into the mini goal located behind them. This drill focuses on improving close control, deception, and finishing under pressure in tight areas, replicating scenarios attackers face in games when receiving back-to-goal.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Sharp, Controlled First Touches to Shield the Ball Effectively – A good first touch helps the attacker maintain possession and sets up their ability to spin or dribble away from pressure.• Promote Use of Deception and Quick Changes of Direction – Skill moves like spins, step-overs, or feints should be used to create separation and confuse the defender.• Focus on Timing the Spin and Accelerating Away from the Defender – The attacker must choose the right moment to turn quickly and exploit any gaps before the defender can recover.• Stress Accuracy and Composure When Finishing Into the Mini Goal – After beating the defender, clean and confident shooting technique is critical to convert the opportunity successfully.
progression_one: Limit the Attacker’s Touches Before ScoringRestrict the attacker to a maximum of three touches after receiving the ball, encouraging sharper control, quicker decision-making, and more efficient execution.Focus: Develops sharper technical skills and faster thinking to increase effectiveness in tight, high-pressure 1v1 scenarios.

title: Prague Dribble to Commit
instructions_setup: This attacking practice is split into two connected grids to simulate progressive attacking phases. In the first zone, two attackers face one defender in a tight 2v1 scenario. The attackers must use combination play and dribbling skills to successfully beat the defender and carry the ball across the line into the second zone.Once the attacker successfully dribbles past the defender and over the boundary into the second zone, they join two teammates to face two defenders in the penalty area. This creates a 3v2 overload, emphasizing quick decision-making, combination play, and clinical finishing under pressure in a realistic attacking environment.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Close Control and Effective Use of Feints in the 2v1 to Beat the Defender – Sharp dribbling and clever body movement are key to creating space and progressing the attack.• Promote Quick Communication and Combination Play Between Attacking Players – Passing and movement off the ball should be fluid to maintain possession and create scoring opportunities in the 3v2.• Focus on Maintaining Width and Depth in the Second Zone to Stretch the Defense – Creating space between defenders opens passing lanes and shooting opportunities in tight penalty area scenarios.• Stress Composure and Accuracy When Finishing Under Pressure – Players must remain calm and choose the best shooting option quickly to capitalize on the overload advantage.
progression_one: Make the First Defender More AggressiveIncrease the pressure in the first zone by allowing the defender to engage more aggressively and attempt interceptions, raising the difficulty of dribbling into the second zone.Focus: Enhances attackers’ dribbling under pressure and ability to maintain possession while progressing play into the penalty area.
progression_two: Add a Neutral Player to Support the AttackersIntroduce a neutral attacker who supports the team in both zones, increasing passing options and encouraging more dynamic combination play.Focus: Improves attacker creativity and movement off the ball, increasing complexity and decision-making in attacking phases.

title: Prague Finishing Into 2v1
instructions_setup: This two-phase practice begins with an unopposed attacking combination outside the box, where players work together to execute quick, precise passes leading to a controlled finishing opportunity. The initial phase focuses on fluid attacking patterns and accurate shooting to build confidence and technique without pressure.In the second phase, a defender initiates play by passing to a deeper attacker, who immediately links up with the initial shooter to create a 2v1 attacking scenario. The defender who played the pass now transitions quickly to defend the 2v1, simulating game-like defensive urgency and encouraging attackers to exploit overloads efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Crisp, Accurate Passing and Movement in the Unopposed Combination Phase – Sharp interplay and quick decision-making are crucial to create high-quality finishing chances.• Encourage the Shooter to Transition Quickly into Support Play for the 2v1 Phase – This promotes fluid attacking dynamics and teaches players to stay involved beyond their initial action.• Stress Defensive Awareness and Immediate Recovery for the Defender After the Pass – The defender must rapidly shift mindset from passing to active defending, simulating realistic game transitions.• Focus on Exploiting Numerical Advantages in the 2v1 Phase with Quick, Decisive Attacking Moves – Attackers should utilize speed, angles, and passing options to outsmart the defender under pressure.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure During Phase 1Introduce a passive defender during the unopposed attacking combination to increase difficulty and encourage quicker decision-making under light pressure.Focus: Develops attackers' composure and ability to maintain precision passing while sensing defensive pressure early.
progression_two: Allow the Defender to Play Aggressively in the 2v1Increase the intensity of the defending phase by permitting the defender to press aggressively and attempt to intercept passes or force errors.Focus: Enhances attackers’ creativity, movement, and execution under more realistic, high-pressure defensive conditions.

title: Prague Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: This is a high-tempo finishing drill designed to simulate match-realistic pressure from behind. An attacker will make a forward run and receive a through ball from a teammate or coach, entering the box with a recovery defender chasing immediately behind them. Although the finish itself may be unopposed, the pressure is intense and forces quick, clean execution.The key technical focus is on the attacker’s first touch, body shape, and ability to remain composed with a recovering defender closing them down. This helps improve finishing under duress and replicates moments where attackers have half a yard of space before being caught.
coaching_notes: • Focus on the weight and angle of the first touch – The initial touch must take the attacker away from the recovering defender while positioning the ball perfectly to shoot quickly.• Encourage composure in the final action under pressure – Players must resist panicking and focus on striking cleanly, using minimal touches when necessary.• Highlight the importance of scanning before receiving the through ball – Attackers should be aware of space, the goalkeeper’s position, and the trailing defender before the ball arrives.• Reinforce clean body shape and shooting technique at speed – Even with pressure, players should maintain balance and stay over the ball when finishing.
progression_one: Recovery Defender Starts Closer to the AttackerReduce the initial distance between the attacker and defender so the pressure arrives almost instantly as the ball is received.Focus: Increases the demand on quick reactions, clean touches, and rapid execution of the finish under tight pressure.

title: Prague Receiving to Attack
instructions_setup: This practice begins with three players working the ball in a central zone, aiming to break through a defensive line of two defenders who are actively screening and blocking forward passes. The focus is on speed of play, disguise, and timing of the pass to penetrate the defensive screen effectively.Once the attacking trio successfully plays through the line, the receiving attackers engage in a 3v2 attacking phase against two recovering defenders in the final third. The transition from build-up to final action replicates real match scenarios where breaking a line creates numerical overloads in dangerous areas.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick passing combinations to disorganize the defensive screen. – Use short, sharp passes with minimal touches to move defenders out of shape and open space between them.• Reinforce the importance of scanning and playing with head up. – Players should check shoulders constantly to assess options and time their forward passes effectively under pressure.• Promote disguised passes and body feints to manipulate space. – Attackers should use clever deception with body shape to shift defenders and exploit gaps in the screen.• Challenge players to support forward immediately after penetrating. – Once the line is broken, initial passers must quickly join the attack to maintain overloads and finish moves with tempo.
progression_one: Add a Recovering Defender From the Initial ZoneIf the ball breaks the line, one of the original screening defenders recovers into the 3v2 to make it a 3v3.Focus: Encourages urgency in transition, attacking decisiveness, and quicker play before the recovering defender disrupts the overload advantage.
progression_two: Allow Defenders to Step Out and PressRather than holding position, defenders in the screen can step out to press, forcing attackers to react and adjust angles and timing.Focus: Trains adaptability in build-up play, player awareness, and the importance of timing and disguise in forward passing under pressure.

title: Prague Short Passing Mastery
instructions_setup: This technical drill focuses on players developing a clean first touch and close control by receiving the ball and shifting it around an oncoming passive defender. Players will begin by standing opposite a server or teammate who passes the ball in, and their task is to take a sharp first touch to either side of the approaching player and then dribble into space.The emphasis is on reacting quickly, choosing the correct direction, and mastering close ball control with both feet. The passive defender serves as a moving obstacle to help simulate real in-game pressure and challenge the player’s awareness, body positioning, and first-touch decisions.
coaching_notes: • Focus on receiving with the correct foot depending on defender’s approach – Players should scan before the ball arrives to decide the best direction to take their first touch• Encourage sharp, purposeful first touches that move the ball out of pressure – Touch should take the ball into space with intent to accelerate away• Promote light, quick footwork when shifting around the oncoming player – Players must stay on their toes and use short steps for fast adjustments• Reinforce scanning before and after receiving to improve decision-making – Awareness of pressure and space is key for mastering first touch under pressure
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender With More PressureInstead of jogging, the passive defender moves with more intent, forcing the attacker to adjust touch and direction under semi-realistic pressure.Focus: Develops composure and ball security when taking a first touch with limited time and space.
progression_two: Vary the Delivery (Aerial or Driven)Alternate between different types of passes — some firm, some lofted — to improve control under various first-touch scenarios.Focus: Builds all-around technical control and prepares players for diverse in-game receiving situations.

title: River Plate 1v1 with Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: In this 1v1 drill, play starts with both players dribbling around the grid. Once both players complete a full circuit and return to their starting positions, they must attempt to score into the opposite mini goal.The objective is for each player to be the first to get their shot off, gaining the advantage for the second phase of the drill. The player who successfully shoots first will start the second phase, where a coach or a third player will pass a second ball to them. This initiates an opposed 1v1 scenario, forcing the player to quickly transition from shooting to defending and re-engaging in the drill.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Start: Focus on quick reactions and acceleration when returning to the starting position, ensuring players can burst into space and get a shot off before their opponent.• Composure in Shooting: Encourage players to stay calm and focus on accurate, controlled shots when finishing on goal, ensuring that they are not rushed by the pressure of the opponent.• Transition Speed: Emphasize the importance of transitioning quickly from the shooting phase to the defending 1v1. The player must be able to quickly switch mentality from attacker to defender.• Defensive Positioning: In the opposed 1v1 phase, remind players to use proper defensive posture, forcing the attacker into a position where they are limited in their options.
progression_one: Add Time Limit:Introduce a time limit for the first phase of dribbling and shooting. Players must complete the circuit and shoot within a specific time frame to encourage urgency and increase intensity.Focus: Increases the need for speed and decision-making under pressure, making both the dribbling and shooting phases more challenging.
progression_two: Introduce Multiple Defenders:In the second phase, allow the player who wins the first 1v1 to now face two defenders in a 2v1 situation. This creates a higher level of difficulty, requiring the player to think faster and make better decisions under pressure.Focus: Develops the ability to maintain possession and attack while under defensive pressure, enhancing decision-making in high-intensity scenarios.

title: Riverplate 2 Phase Finishing the Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into two attacking players positioned on the edge of the box. As soon as the pass is played, a defender puts pressure on them, and they will play out a 2v1 attack. After completing the first phase, the two attackers must retreat to the restart line. The second defender then becomes live, and a cross from one of the two wide positions will come into the box. The play transitions into a 2v2 attack, simulating a final effort to finish after the initial attacking phase.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making – In the 2v1 phase, the attackers need to make quick decisions about whether to shoot or pass. Encourage them to read the defender’s positioning and decide whether to go for goal or create an angle for a teammate.• Attacking Space – The attacking players must recognize the space available to them. When receiving the ball, they should focus on either turning and facing the goal or driving towards the defender to create a shooting opportunity.• Crossing and Timing – In the 2v2 phase, the players should focus on delivering precise crosses with timing that fits the attacking players’ runs. The attackers need to time their movements to arrive in the right area, whether it’s near post, far post, or central to the box.• Defensive Pressure – Defenders should focus on staying compact and preventing attackers from making easy runs into dangerous areas. In the 2v2, they need to communicate and decide when to apply pressure on the ball and when to cover the space.
progression_one: Add Extra DefendersAdd an additional defender in the 2v2 phase to increase defensive pressure and force the attackers to make quicker decisions under more realistic game conditions.Focus: Encourages attackers to move quickly and be creative in a more congested area, improving finishing under pressure.
progression_two: Alter Cross DeliveryChange the method of cross delivery, such as requiring the cross to be lofted or driven, or having the cross come from a different angle (e.g., from a deeper position).Focus: Develops attackers’ ability to finish from a variety of crosses and different types of deliveries.

title: Riverplate 2v2 to 2v1
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a 2v2 duel in a central zone, where both teams compete for possession and aim to combine quickly. The objective is to play into a designated end zone once a clean pass or dribble breaks the line. Positioned inside each end zone is a supporting attacker, creating a 2v1 situation once the ball transitions out of the middle.Once in the end zone, the two attackers must work together to outplay the lone defender and score into one of two mini goals. The central players are not allowed to recover, ensuring a fast-paced transition and a numerical advantage for the attacking side.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: Central players should look to create short, sharp passing sequences with limited touches to break lines and exploit space.• Movement to Receive: Encourage attackers to constantly shift positions within the central zone, creating passing lanes and confusing defenders.• Composure in Overload: In the 2v1 scenario, attackers must stay calm, draw the defender, and use unselfish play to create clear scoring chances.• Defensive Decision-Making: The lone defender in the end zone should delay and angle their positioning to force low-quality shots or passes.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for ScoringOnce the ball enters the end zone, attackers have 6 seconds to get a shot off.Focus: Increases urgency, encourages faster combinations, and mimics real game tempo under pressure.
progression_two: Alternate Entry RulesTeams can only enter the end zone through a set condition — e.g., three passes or a one-touch wall pass — before progressing.Focus: Forces greater awareness and intentional build-up, developing structured play over chaotic transitions.

title: Riverplate 4 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: In this 4-phase finishing practice, the attacker focuses on making dynamic runs across the defender to receive the ball in space. The key objective is for the attacker to move both inside and outside the defender to create separation and receive a pass for a quality finish.The practice is split into 4 phases, with the attacker making runs in different directions to challenge the defender. After completing all 4 finishes, the attackers will switch roles, allowing them to work on their offensive runs and also recover during their rest periods. This high-intensity drill combines technical finishing with the fitness aspect of constant movement.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing – Encourage attackers to time their runs across the defender effectively. The run should be made when the ball is played, allowing the attacker to meet it in stride and finish with minimal delay.• Inside and Outside Runs – Attackers should vary their runs, using both inside and outside movements to break the defender’s line of sight and create space.
