Inside runs can be used to cut across defenders and finish centrally, while outside runs can be used to stretch the defense and create crossing angles or finish from wider positions.• Finishing Under Pressure – Once the attacker has made the run and received the ball, they should focus on finishing quickly and accurately under pressure. Stress the importance of maintaining composure and making clinical decisions when finishing the attack.• Work/Rest Balance – The practice should be high-intensity, with attackers moving quickly and covering a lot of ground. Ensure there are adequate rest periods between the phases, so attackers can recover and repeat the high-intensity efforts.
progression_one: Add a Defender ChallengeIntroduce a defender who will try to close down the space and prevent the attacker from receiving the ball in the desired position. This will challenge the attacker’s ability to make smart runs and find space behind the defender. The defender should not actively engage the attacker until the ball is passed, simulating match conditions.Focus:Improves attacker movement and the ability to find space while being pressured by a defender.
progression_two: Add a Quick Transition After FinishAfter each finish, the attacker must quickly transition to defend against the next attacking phase. This adds a fitness component to the drill and keeps the practice fast-paced. Attackers will finish, recover, and then switch roles, ensuring they stay engaged throughout the practice.Focus:Increases fitness levels and helps attackers work on quick transitions between attacking and defending.

title: Riverplate Breaking Lines Transfer
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice focuses on developing the ability to play line-breaking passes during the build-up phase. The drill begins with a 4v2 rondo where two defenders press into a grid. The team in possession must complete 5 passes within the grid before attempting to break the defensive lines and progress the ball into the opposite zone. The ball is passed through 2 central players who replicate a midfield pair to simulate progression through a midfield. If the team successfully breaks the lines and progresses, the two screening defenders now press in the opposite grid, while the two players who originally pressed drop into screening roles.
coaching_notes: • Passing and Movement – Emphasize the importance of quick, accurate passing and intelligent movement off the ball. Players must create angles for the passer to break the defensive lines.• Line-Breaking Passes – Encourage players to look for vertical passes into space, through defenders, or splitting the lines. These passes should be played with the right weight and timing to ensure the ball bypasses the defenders.• Midfielders’ Role – The two central players who replicate midfielders should be active in supporting the ball carrier, offering clear passing lanes while also positioning themselves to receive the ball in space to help transition play.• Pressure and Transition – Once the ball is successfully progressed, the pressure shifts. The original defenders who pressed now drop into screening roles, while the previous screeners must transition to apply pressure. This shift allows players to practice both defending and attacking transitions.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Breaking the LinesSet a time limit (e.g., 20–30 seconds) for the team in possession to break the lines after 5 passes. This increases the intensity and urgency in decision-making.Focus:Improves the speed of decision-making and encourages quicker thinking when breaking the lines and progressing the play.
progression_two: Restrict Number of Touches for AttackersLimit the number of touches each attacking player can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches max), forcing quicker and more efficient passing and movement.Focus:Helps improve players' ability to think and move quickly under pressure, replicating game-like conditions where time and space are limited.

title: Riverplate Finishing From Through Balls
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on creating and finishing goal-scoring opportunities from 3rd-man through balls. The drill begins with a passing combination between two players, one of whom will lay off a ball for a third player making a late run into space. The third player receives a well-weighted through ball and finishes on goal. The practice allows attackers to work on timing, movement off the ball, and finishing after receiving a pass that exploits the defense’s gaps.
coaching_notes: • 3rd-Man Run Timing – The key focus is on the timing of the third player’s run. They must not anticipate too early or too late, timing their run to receive the ball in stride and with space to attack.• Combination Play – Encourage quick, fluid combinations between players. The second player in the combination should aim to deliver the through ball to the third player with accuracy and weight to avoid the defense recovering.• Finishing with Composure – Players must focus on composure and accuracy when finishing, ideally using one touch or quickly setting themselves up for a first-time finish. Encourage shooting to the corners or keeping the ball low.• Positive Attacking Mindset – Encourage attackers to always look for forward options, making positive runs and constantly scanning for potential through balls.
progression_one: Add a Defender Pressuring the 3rd-ManIntroduce a passive defender who pressures the 3rd player just before receiving the through ball, forcing quicker decisions and tighter finishes.Focus:Encourages the player receiving the through ball to adjust their timing, positioning, and finishing technique under pressure.
progression_two: Multiple Runners into the BoxAdd additional runners into the box, with the third player now needing to assess and choose the best option for a pass or finish (e.g., lay off to a player arriving at the far post, or finish directly).Focus:Develops decision-making in fast-paced attacking scenarios and improves the attacker’s ability to read space and choose the best option in the final third.

title: Riverplate Half Space Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing practice, play begins with a deep pass into a wide player positioned in the wide channel. Upon receiving the ball, the wide player plays a forward pass into the half space or cutback zone, targeting a supporting runner. That runner then delivers a cross into the box for an attacker to finish. The drill is focused on rehearsing timing and movement into key areas without opposition.
coaching_notes: • Wide Player Body Shape – Encourage players to receive on the back foot and play forward early into the half space with open body positioning for better vision.• Timing of Half Space Runs – Supporting runners must time their movement to arrive just as the ball is released into the zone, ensuring they aren’t too early or late.• Delivery Type – Focus on accurate cutbacks or low driven crosses that match the attacking run and position, replicating realistic in-game deliveries.• Finishing Decisions – Attackers should adjust their positioning based on the delivery and aim for one-touch, clinical finishes under realistic pressure scenarios.
progression_one: Passive Defender in Half SpaceIntroduce a passive defender to apply light pressure on the half space runner before the cross, forcing better ball control and awareness.Focus: Timing under slight pressure and adapting movement to deliver accurately while maintaining composure in tight areas.
progression_two: Double Runs into the BoxAdd a second attacker making a delayed run to create options for near-post and far-post finishes, increasing variation in the final third.Focus: Movement coordination and decision-making when attacking the cross with multiple finishers creating different threats.

title: Riverplate Hexagonal Passing
instructions_setup: This hexagonal passing practice is designed to replicate various build-up patterns used in a back-3 formation. Players form a hexagon, with one player in the center and others positioned around the outside. The players on the outside pass the ball to the center player, who must control and distribute the ball back out to another player. This drill can be adjusted for different age groups and skill levels by altering the distances between players and the types of patterns used.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Positional AwarenessPlayers should be aware of their positioning relative to each other, especially in tight spaces. Encourage players to move dynamically in order to create passing lanes. The player in the center should be scanning and anticipating passes before they arrive, ensuring smooth and quick transitions.• Pass and Move with PurposePlayers must move immediately after passing the ball to maintain the fluidity of the drill. Encourage purposeful movement to ensure the ball is constantly circulating, and players are always ready to receive a pass or create a new passing option.• Precision in PassingAccuracy in passing is key for maintaining tempo in this drill. Players should aim to deliver crisp, precise passes to the player in the center, ensuring they’re not forced to make awkward touches. The center player should use a good first touch to control the ball and distribute it quickly.• Adapt for Different Skill LevelsFor beginners or lower skill levels, reduce the distance between players and allow more time for each pass. As the players improve, increase the distance, add pressure (e.g., with defenders or timed passing), and introduce more complex patterns to simulate different tactical situations.
progression_one: Add Defenders to Increase PressureIntroduce 1 or 2 defenders to the central area to apply pressure on the center player. This will encourage quicker passing and decision-making under pressure.Focus: This progression simulates real-game pressure and forces the attacking team to make quicker, more accurate decisions.
progression_two: Vary Passing PatternsIntroduce different passing patterns, such as 1-2s or diagonal switches, to challenge the players' creativity and ability to build attacks in different formations.Focus: This progression helps improve a team's ability to break lines and switch play, which is crucial in a back-3 setup.

title: Riverplate Semi Opposed Finishing
instructions_setup: In this semi-opposed finishing practice, the attacking team sets up in a diamond shape just outside the penalty area. The deepest player in the diamond, positioned closest to the goal, will drop deeper to receive a pass from the highest player in the diamond. From here, they will play a quick 1-2 combination with either of the side players.During the initial phase, a defender applies pressure to the central forward, but once the 1-2 is played, the defender drops off, allowing the striker to receive the ball unopposed and finish towards goal.This drill focuses on combination play, timing of runs, and finishing with composure under semi-opposed conditions.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Pass: Encourage the deepest player to time their drop effectively to receive the ball in a good position. The pass from the highest player should be firm and accurate, allowing for quick combination play.• 1-2 Combination: Players must focus on quick and sharp passing during the 1-2. Emphasize the importance of making precise passes and intelligent movement, especially from the player receiving the ball, who must make a forward run towards goal.• Pressure and Transition: The defender should put pressure on the forward during the initial phase but drop off quickly once the 1-2 is executed. Remind the striker to stay focused and be ready to finish quickly once they receive the ball unopposed.• Finishing with Composure: Once the defender drops off, the striker should take advantage of the unopposed opportunity to finish with composure. Encourage them to keep their shots low and aim for the far corners of the goal.
progression_one: Add a Deflection:Introduce a deflection element where a defender can make an attempt to block or deflect the 1-2 pass. This will force the striker to adapt their finishing technique and become more flexible in their approach.Focus: This progression helps improve decision-making when the attack is not perfectly executed and simulates real match situations where defenders can still disrupt play.
progression_two: One-Touch Finishing:To increase the difficulty, require the striker to take a one-touch finish after receiving the ball back from the 1-2 combination. This progression will force the striker to focus on clean ball control and quicker decision-making in tight situations.Focus: This will simulate real match conditions where attackers must finish quickly under pressure with minimal time on the ball.

title: Roma 1v1 Evading Pressure
instructions_setup: In this drill, the player in possession must use their body to evade an oncoming defender. The drill begins with a pass from the defender to the attacker, who must then use their body to shield the ball and create space away from the defender.Once the attacker has controlled the ball, they are tasked with dribbling toward either of the two mini goals located at the bottom and right side of the grid. To score, the attacker must first cross a marked line that encourages them to dribble and beat the defender before taking a shot. The defender's goal is to press and challenge the attacker without conceding space for a clean shot.
coaching_notes: • Body Positioning: Emphasize the importance of using the body to protect the ball and shield it from the defender. The player should focus on creating space by using their arms and body to block the defender’s path.• Change of Pace: Encourage attackers to vary their pace after using their body to shield the ball. A sudden burst of speed after the feint will give them an advantage in escaping the defender.• Proper Footwork: Focus on quick and precise footwork to maneuver around the defender, using sharp turns and body shifts to maintain control of the ball.• Dribbling Before Shooting: Reinforce the need to dribble past the marked lines before taking the shot. This ensures that players engage in the dribbling phase first, allowing them to set themselves up for a better angle and clearer shot.
progression_one: Add a Defender's Tackle:Introduce a tackling phase where the defender is allowed to challenge the ball once the attacker has passed the marked line but before the shot is taken. The defender can tackle from behind or side to side, forcing the attacker to be quicker in their decision-making.Focus: Encourages the attacker to be more aware of the defender’s position, improving dribbling under pressure and the ability to protect the ball until the moment is right for shooting.

title: Roma Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This mastery drill is designed to encourage quick dribbling and 1v1 take-on skills. Players will dribble down the long sides of the grid towards a mannequin and perform a take-on using various dribbling techniques. On the shorter sides, players must dribble through a set of cones to improve their agility and close ball control.The goal is for players to use quick feet and body movements to evade defenders and keep possession of the ball. They should aim to execute different dribbling skills such as step-overs, feints, or sudden changes of direction when approaching the mannequin. On the shorter sides, players work on tight control and rapid acceleration through the cones.
coaching_notes: • Dribbling Techniques: Focus on teaching players different dribbling moves (e.g., step-overs, feints, and quick shifts in direction) to beat the mannequin and defenders.• Close Control: Emphasize maintaining close control of the ball while dribbling, especially when approaching the cones or tight spaces.• Acceleration: Encourage players to use bursts of speed after each take-on, quickly accelerating to get past the defender or into a shooting position.• Body Feints: Use body feints and sudden changes in direction to throw off defenders and create space for the player to move forward.

title: Roma Finishing from Close
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, two attackers will make runs past two mannequins positioned on the penalty spot and finish from close range. The ball will be crossed from the wide area into the space near the goal line, just outside the penalty box, where the attackers will arrive to meet the ball and take a shot on goal.The attackers must time their runs effectively to avoid running into the mannequins and create space to receive the ball for a close-range finish. The focus is on making quick, decisive movements and finishing the cross from a tight angle or close range to mimic real match situations.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Run: Emphasize the importance of timing the run to meet the cross in the correct position, ensuring the attackers are in the right spot to finish as soon as the ball arrives.• Body Positioning: Players should focus on being balanced and in a strong position to strike the ball, making sure their body is over the ball to ensure accuracy and power.• Quick Decision-Making: Encourage attackers to make a quick decision on whether to take a first-time shot or control the ball based on the speed and accuracy of the cross.• Finishing Technique: Stress the importance of using the inside of the foot or the laces to strike the ball, aiming for placement and power into the corners of the goal.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender who will press the attackers as they make their run to receive the ball. The attacker now has to finish under pressure, either by taking the shot early or using a feint to evade the defender.Focus: This progression adds a layer of pressure, encouraging the attacker to finish quickly and accurately while being aware of the defender's position.

title: Roma Overload to Isolate
instructions_setup: In this overloaded practice, one team operates in a 5v4 scenario within one half of the grid. Their objective is to complete five passes under pressure before attempting to switch play across the grid to a teammate in space, finishing the move by scoring into a mini goal.The defending team works to win back possession during the 5v4 phase. If they win the ball, their task is to quickly transfer possession to one of their two teammates positioned on the opposite side of the grid, initiating a counter-attack.
coaching_notes: • Patience in Possession: Encourage players to remain composed and patient while completing the five passes, using the overload advantage effectively.• Switching Awareness: Players should scan regularly to recognize when the switch is on and execute it with precision and speed.• Weight and Direction of Pass: Focus on ensuring passes are played with the correct weight and to the correct foot to maintain rhythm and speed of play.• Defensive Urgency: The defending team must press with intensity and communicate to cut off passing lanes, aiming to disrupt the sequence before the switch can happen.
progression_one: Add a Floating Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral player who always plays with the team in possession, increasing the overload and encouraging quicker passing combinations before the switch.Focus: This adds an extra outlet for passing and teaches players to exploit numerical advantages with quick, intelligent play.
progression_two: Increase Pressure After the Switch:Once the ball is switched to the opposite side, allow one defender to recover and apply pressure immediately, forcing quicker decision-making in the final action.Focus: Helps develop speed of play after a switch and forces attackers to capitalize on transitional moments with urgency.

title: Roma Turn Into 1v1
instructions_setup: Play starts with two passes played into central players who are positioned next to a central mannequin. These central players must quickly receive, turn sharply, and drive toward goal with the objective of scoring into a mini goal from close range.Immediately after making the initial pass, the two outside players must sprint onto the pitch and apply pressure, turning the drill into a live 1v1 scenario. This transition creates a dynamic moment where attackers must be decisive, and defenders must recover and engage quickly.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Turns on the Move: Emphasize quick and controlled turns upon receiving the ball, using the body and first touch to escape the mannequin and face forward with immediate intent.• Acceleration After Turn: Attackers should explode into space immediately after the turn to gain separation before the defender can recover and block the shooting lane.• Defensive Recovery Speed: Focus on fast reactions from the defenders. They should sprint onto the pitch and apply pressure while remaining balanced and not diving in too early.• Finishing Under Pressure: Attackers must stay composed when shooting, timing their shot while under pressure from the recovering defender closing the angle.
progression_one: Add a Second Mini Goal:Place an additional mini goal on the opposite side. After turning, the attacker must decide which goal to attack based on the defender’s position.Focus: Encourages decision-making and scanning, as the attacker must read the defender's recovery run and choose the better shooting option.

title: Roma Unopposed Countering
instructions_setup: This unopposed countering drill allows players to develop specific movements and passing sequences that are directly relevant to fast counter-attacking scenarios. Three players enter the grid and execute structured attacking patterns, simulating real match tempo.Three mannequins are positioned centrally to act as obstacles, helping replicate defenders and encouraging players to adjust angles and timing of runs. These movements should be sharp, dynamic, and repeatable to help develop instinctive play during quick transitions.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Passes: Ensure each pass is made at the right moment to maintain attacking momentum and disrupt defensive shape.• Angle of Support: Players off the ball must position themselves effectively to offer clear, progressive options at speed.• Body Shape to Receive: Receiving players should open up with their first touch to play forward quickly and efficiently.• Movement Off the Ball: Emphasize sharp, purposeful runs that mimic real game counter-attack scenarios.• Communication Between Players: Encourage early and clear calls to ensure fluid movement and decision-making.
progression_one: Add Finishing Phase:Introduce a final pass that sets up a shot on goal after the third movement. Players must time their final run behind the mannequins to simulate breaking a defensive line.Focus: Adds purpose to movement by finishing the attack, reinforcing sharp passing and movement toward goal.
progression_two: Introduce Shadow Defenders:Add passive or semi-active defenders to follow runners or block passing lanes. Attackers must now react to pressure and adapt their counter patterns accordingly.Focus: Builds game realism by forcing players to adapt their decisions and angles in tighter spaces.

title: Rotterdam 1v2 & 2v2s With Recovery
instructions_setup: In the 1v2 phase, play starts with a dribble up the field and a pass into the attacker. The attacker then attempts to attack at speed in a 1v1 scenario before the recovering defender gets back into position, turning it into a 1v2. In the 2v2 phase, the setup is the same, but the attacker will initially have a momentary 2v1 advantage. The attacker must then exploit this overload, attacking at speed and trying to take advantage of the attacking overload before the defender recovers.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Speed – Attackers should focus on moving at speed as soon as they receive the ball, making it difficult for defenders to recover. They should take on defenders directly, using quick touches to break past them.• Decision-Making in 1v2 – In the 1v2 phase, attackers need to make quick decisions about whether to dribble or pass. They should assess the positioning of both defenders and choose the best option to beat the 1v2 scenario.• Exploiting the Overload in 2v2 – In the 2v2 phase, attackers should recognize the overload and use it to their advantage. They should look to create space through quick passes, off-the-ball movement, or by isolating one defender to beat with pace.• Defender Recovery – Defenders should focus on recovering quickly into the play. In both phases, defenders should use their positioning to force the attacker into less dangerous areas and be aware of the overload situation to minimize gaps.
progression_one: Add a Third Defender in 2v2Introduce a third defender after a set number of repetitions, increasing the difficulty of the 2v2 phase and forcing attackers to think more creatively.Focus: Forces attackers to make quicker decisions and adapt to an increasing level of pressure.
progression_two: Limit the Time for the AttackersSet a time limit within which the attackers must score, adding pressure to finish quickly.Focus: Enhances the speed of play and encourages quick decision-making and finishing under pressure.

title: Rotterdam Attacking 2v1s
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on fast-paced 2v1 situations and is perfect for use as a warm-up or arrival activity. Play starts with a pass into a deeper player, who then dribbles up the pitch and combines with a teammate to score into one of the mini goals. If the defending player wins possession, they can counter-attack to the opposite mini goals. Teams will take turns attacking, and the practice is timed and scored, with the team scoring the most goals being crowned the winner.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combination Play – The player in possession should focus on making quick, accurate passes to the teammate to create an opportunity in the 2v1. Timing the pass and movement will help break down the defender and create a goal-scoring chance.• Movement off the Ball – The supporting player must anticipate the ball and position themselves in space to receive it. Good movement off the ball will stretch the defender, creating more space for a shot or further combination.• Defending 2v1 – The defender should aim to delay the attackers' progress and force them into less dangerous areas. They should also focus on reading the play, anticipating the pass, and positioning themselves to cut off the most likely attacking options.• Composure in Front of Goal – The attacking duo should focus on finishing with composure, whether that’s through quick one-touch finishes or taking an extra touch to get closer to goal. It’s important to stay calm and pick the best option in front of goal.
progression_one: Add a Third DefenderIntroduce a third defender after a set number of reps, making it a 2v2 for a short period before returning to the 2v1. This progression adds an element of unpredictability and forces attackers to make quick decisions.Focus: Encourages attackers to adapt to changing situations and work together under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to ScoringPlace a time limit on each attacking phase. The attackers must score within the time limit or they lose possession, and the defenders gain a point for successfully stopping the attack.Focus: Increases urgency and encourages quick thinking and fast play in both attacking and defending.

title: Rotterdam Combinations & Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill is set up like two 18-yard boxes facing each other, creating two small-sided game areas on either side of a central line. Two neutral players are stationed in the middle zone to facilitate the combination play.One player from a team starts by initiating a double 1-2 pass sequence with both neutral players before driving forward and finishing into the goal. After their shot, a player from the opposite team mirrors the action in the other direction. Teams alternate turns, focusing on sharp combinations and clean finishes.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Combination Play: Encourage fast, sharp 1-2s to replicate real match tempo and keep the movement fluid and purposeful.• Timing of Final Run: Focus on perfectly timed runs into space after the second 1-2 to create an ideal angle for finishing under no pressure.• Body Shape When Receiving: Players should receive the ball with an open stance to play quickly and keep their options visible at all times.• Controlled Finishing Technique: Reinforce calm, composed finishing inside the box, ensuring accuracy and correct body mechanics when striking.
progression_one: Add Time Pressure:Introduce a time limit (e.g., 5 seconds) from the start of the combination to the finish to replicate pressure and urgency in front of goal.Focus: Encourages quick decision-making, sharper movements, and more decisive finishing in limited time.
progression_two: Introduce Passive Defender:Add a passive defender to apply light pressure during the second 1-2 or just before the shot, forcing players to adjust their body position and timing.Focus: Develops awareness under pressure, timing, and technical execution in more realistic situations.

title: Rotterdam Create & Finish the Attack
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 5v4 possession format in the first zone. The attacking team must attempt to progress play beyond the engagement line by playing around or through the defensive 4 players. If they successfully progress the ball into the attacking zone, they will attempt to finish the attack in a 3v2 format. If the defending team wins possession in either of the 2 zones, they must immediately look to progress the ball forward into any of the 3 mini goals located on the halfway line. This drill encourages attacking progression, quick transitions, and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Possession and Progression – The attacking team should focus on maintaining possession and using quick, creative combinations to break through the defensive 4 players. They should aim to create space and angles to progress the ball into the attacking zone while keeping the tempo high.• Decision-Making in the Final Third – Once the ball is in the attacking zone, the attacking team should focus on quick decision-making in the 3v2 scenario. They must assess whether to play the ball to the open player or take on the defender, all while working to finish the attack quickly.• Defensive Shape and Pressing – The defending team in the first zone should focus on staying compact and communicating to prevent the attacking team from progressing too easily. In the second zone, defenders must quickly assess the 3v2 situation and look to close down the attacking options while maintaining a strong defensive shape.• Quick Transitions – When the defending team wins possession, they must immediately switch to attack and focus on progressing the ball quickly into the mini goals. This fast transition helps replicate real-game counter-attacking situations, requiring quick thinking and decision-making.
progression_one: Add a Time LimitIntroduce a time limit for the attacking team to progress the ball into the attacking zone. This forces quicker ball movement and decision-making under pressure.Focus: Increases tempo and urgency, encouraging faster progression and decision-making.
progression_two: Limit the Number of TouchesLimit the number of touches for players in the attacking team, forcing quicker passes and decisions. For example, only 2 touches per player.Focus: Encourages fast ball movement, improving passing speed and limiting defensive time to recover.

title: Rotterdam Pressing & Counter Pressing
instructions_setup: This practice allows players to develop their build-up play and work on pressing and counter-pressing. The drill runs as a 7v4, with 4 players located on the outer lines and 3 neutral players (2 of which are goalkeepers) working centrally. The team in possession must maintain the ball and aim to complete a set number of passes, while the defending team works to regain possession. If the defending team wins the ball, they should attempt to counter-attack and score into either of the 2 goals. The 4 outer players can counter-press to prevent the attacking team from scoring. Once the defending team regains possession and scores, they will switch roles with the 4 outer players, becoming the possession team.
coaching_notes: • Building from the Back – The team in possession must focus on maintaining patience and composure while working the ball around the field. The goal is to complete multiple short passes to draw the defending team out and open space for a forward progression.• Pressing Strategy – The defending team should work on applying coordinated, intense pressure to regain possession. They must focus on positioning, cutting off passing lanes, and closing down space quickly to force mistakes. Pressing high and trapping the ball near the touchline can be effective.• Counter-Pressing – After losing possession, the outer players must immediately work to counter-press, attempting to win the ball back as quickly as possible. This requires quick transitions and an aggressive mindset to stop the opposing team from exploiting the counter-attack.• Counter-Attacking – Upon regaining possession, the defending team should look to attack quickly, utilizing the neutral players (goalkeepers) to help progress the ball forward. Speed and decision-making are crucial in counter-attacks to exploit the gaps left by the opposing team.
progression_one: Increase Defensive PressureAdd additional defenders or reduce the number of neutral players in the middle to increase the pressure on the attacking team. This will challenge the attackers to maintain possession and work through tighter spaces.Focus: Develops the ability to play under pressure while maintaining possession.
progression_two: Limit Passes for AttackersReduce the number of passes the attacking team is allowed to complete before attempting to score. This will encourage quicker decision-making and a faster build-up.Focus: Enhances the attacking team's ability to transition from build-up to goal-scoring opportunities efficiently.

title: Rotterdam Rondo into Cutbacks
instructions_setup: Play starts with a 4v2 rondo in the central area. The team of 4 in possession must complete a minimum of five passes before playing a pass into either of the two wide players positioned on the outside. Upon successfully passing the ball into the wide players, they will initiate a 3v2 attack, with the two wide players and the centre forward attacking against two defenders. If the defending team in the rondo manages to win possession while being outnumbered 2v4, they can counterattack and attempt to score in the main goal.
coaching_notes: • Rondo Principles – Ensure the team in possession focuses on quick, accurate passing to maintain control and create opportunities for forward passes into the wide players. Encourage players to move to open spaces and provide passing options.• Wide Player Awareness – The wide players must focus on their positioning and timing when receiving the ball. They should be aware of the defenders and be ready to cut inside or make a quick cross for the centre forward.• Attacking Combinations – The two wide players and the centre forward should focus on combining quickly once the ball is passed into the wide areas. Quick passes and intelligent movements are essential to break down the defenders in a 3v2 situation.• Defensive Pressure – The defenders in the rondo need to apply constant pressure to win the ball, while also being aware of the counterattack opportunities once possession is regained. Focus on recovery speed and communication.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for the RondoIntroduce a time limit (e.g., 30 seconds) for the team in possession to make the five passes. If they fail, the defending team switches roles.Focus: Adds pressure to the attacking team, simulating game scenarios where quick ball circulation is essential.
progression_two: Add a 3rd Defender to the AttackAllow the attacking team to add a third player into the wide area, creating a 3v3 situation. This encourages the attacking team to break down the defenders with more options in the wide areas.Focus: Forces the defending team to be more disciplined in their defensive organization and requires attackers to make quicker decisions in tight situations.

title: Rotterdam Technical Passing Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This technical passing warm-up encourages players to focus on 1-touch combinations, specifically set passes and line-breaking forward passes. The practice involves two balls working simultaneously, with players required to follow their pass to maintain the flow of the drill. Players should work on quick, precise passing and movement to ensure the ball is always progressing forward. The aim is to improve both passing accuracy and the ability to play quickly in tight spaces, setting up the team for more dynamic possession play.
coaching_notes: • 1-Touch Passing – Players should focus on making clean, accurate 1-touch passes to ensure the ball moves efficiently and quickly. Stress the importance of soft touches to maintain ball control.• Breaking Lines with Passes – Emphasize the importance of playing forward passes that break defensive lines, whether through the midfield or direct into attacking areas. This helps the team progress the ball quickly.• Movement After the Pass – After each pass, players must follow their ball, providing support and positioning themselves for the next pass. This maintains fluidity and sharpens players' ability to move into new spaces.• Awareness and Speed – Encourage players to scan the field before receiving the ball, enabling them to make quicker decisions and execute passes under time pressure, improving overall game tempo.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce passive defensive pressure, with defenders applying light pressure on the players receiving the ball.Focus: This progression simulates game-like conditions, where players need to make quick decisions while under pressure.
progression_two: Increase Passing DistanceIncrease the distance between players to encourage longer passes while maintaining 1-touch combinations.Focus: This challenges players to maintain passing accuracy and pace over greater distances, helping them improve long-range passing and timing.

title: Rotterdam Transitional Possession Grids
instructions_setup: This practice is a possession-based drill where each team has 2 players on the end lines and 3-5 players working centrally. When in possession, teams should attempt to make 10 consecutive passes for a point. If the defending team wins possession, they must quickly transfer the ball across to the opposite side of the grid. If successful, the defending team will begin their possession phase with all central players moving over to the opposite grid. This practice focuses on maintaining possession and transitioning quickly after regaining the ball.
coaching_notes: • Maintaining Possession – The attacking team should focus on quick, short passes to maintain possession and progress the ball through the grid. Players must be aware of their positioning and movement off the ball to create passing lanes and avoid being trapped by the defenders.• Pressure and Intensity – Defenders should work on applying pressure and staying compact to limit passing options. They must stay alert to prevent easy passes and look for opportunities to win the ball back through tactical positioning.• Quick Transition – When the defending team regains possession, they need to make a quick decision to transfer the ball across the grid and move into the opposite grid. This transition phase should be fast to simulate real-game counter-attacking situations.• End-Line Play – The two players on the end lines must be ready to receive passes and support their team in possession. They should be able to switch positions as needed, moving across the grid to help maintain offensive pressure and provide passing outlets.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for PassingIntroduce a time limit for the attacking team to complete their 10 passes. This will increase the tempo of play and add pressure to retain possession while making quick decisions.Focus: Encourages faster ball movement and more dynamic play under time constraints.
progression_two: Increase Defensive PressureAdd an additional defender to the central grid, making the defending team work harder to win possession. This will force the attacking team to adapt and focus on creating better passing angles.Focus: Increases intensity and forces attacking players to work on quick decision-making and maintaining possession under pressure.

title: Salzburg 2v1 to 4v2 Recovery
instructions_setup: This practice begins with the goalkeeper serving a ball into two attackers, initiating a 2v1 attacking phase. The attackers aim to combine quickly, commit the defender and finish on goal with quality. The defender’s task is to delay, force predictable actions and attempt to prevent the shot.Once the 2v1 phase is complete—whether through a goal, save or turnover—the two attackers must immediately transition into defenders. At the same time, three additional players join the original defender to form a team of four. This creates a 4v2 attacking phase in the opposite direction, with the new attacking team aiming to score into the main goal. The transition demands rapid recovery, organisation and decision-making under pressure while giving attackers repeated opportunities to attack at speed.
coaching_notes: • 2v1 Exploitation: Encourage attackers to commit the defender, recognise the moment to release the ball and finish early once the advantage is created.• Transition to Defend: Coach the two attackers to switch mindset instantly—recover with urgency, take up defensive positions and protect central space.• Delay and Engage: Reinforce the importance of delaying actions in the 4v2 phase, buying time and forcing the attackers into wider or slower decisions.• Attacking Tempo: Highlight sharp, purposeful play in both phases, with quick combinations and controlled finishes.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for the 2v1 Attack:Give the attackers 4–5 seconds to create their shooting opportunity in the opening phase. This increases intensity and forces sharper decision-making.Focus: Improves attacking urgency and clarity in overload moments.
progression_two: Allow Recovering Defenders to Win Extra Points:Award bonus points if the two recovering defenders prevent a goal in the 4v2 phase. This motivates high-energy recovery runs and encourages better defensive organisation under pressure.Focus: Enhances recovery habits, defensive resilience and transitional awareness.

title: Salzburg Emergency Defending
instructions_setup: This emergency defending practice begins with one of the defenders playing a pass into the two forwards. Immediately after releasing the ball, that defender must step out and engage the attackers, creating a brief 1v2 situation. During this window, the attackers are encouraged to attack quickly and exploit the overload before defensive support arrives.As the first defender engages, a second defender sprints around a designated pole or cone before recovering back into the practice. Their goal is to restore balance and create a 2v2 as quickly as possible. The attackers attempt to finish the attack with speed, while the defenders work on emergency recovery, delaying actions, and compactness under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Exploit the Overload: Encourage attackers to attack early—drive forward, combine quickly or isolate the lone defender before the second defender arrives.• Defensive Delaying: Coach the first defender to delay and slow the attackers down, buying time for the recovering defender to enter the phase.• Recovery Sprint Quality: The recovering defender should sprint around the outside marker with urgency, then enter with control to re-establish defensive shape.• Attacking Tempo: Highlight the need for fast, purposeful movements from the forwards to take full advantage of the momentary 2v1.
progression_one: Introduce a Time Constraint for Attackers:Add a 3–4 second limit for the attackers to create a shooting opportunity before the recovering defender arrives. This sharpens their intent and forces quicker decision-making.Focus: Speeds up attacking actions and encourages decisive exploitation of overloads.

title: Salzburg Tag & Touch Rondo
instructions_setup: This practice is played across two small possession grids with three teams of three players. Two teams operate as possession groups, one in each grid, while the third team acts as the defending/pressing group. Play begins with both possession teams circulating the ball freely.One defender must sprint into either grid and attempt to win possession. As soon as they win the ball or force it out of play, they must exit the grid and physically tag a teammate. The tagged player must then sprint into the opposite grid and repeat the process. This continues continuously for a set work period before rotating roles between teams. The practice promotes repeated high-intensity actions, quick reactions and constant awareness.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Possession Play: Encourage the possession teams to play quickly with one- and two-touch combinations to avoid pressure and maintain control.• Scanning and Awareness: Coach players to check both grids frequently, recognising where the defender is coming from and adjusting their support positions.• Defensive Intensity: Reinforce that pressers must enter the grid at full speed, win possession decisively and transition quickly to tag the next defender.• Transitions Between Grids: Highlight the importance of sprinting out of the grid immediately after regaining or forcing possession, maintaining tempo and realism.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession Teams:Apply a two-touch limit for players in both grids. This increases the speed of circulation and forces players to adopt sharper angles and quicker support movements.Focus: Improves quick combinations, ball circulation and off-ball timing.
progression_two: Add Directional Targets for Defenders:When a defender wins the ball, they must play into a designated mini target or bounce pass to a coach before sprinting out to tag a teammate. This adds purpose to the press and rewards clean regains.Focus: Encourages controlled defensive actions and purposeful transitions after winning possession.

title: Salzburg Tag & Touch Rondo #2
instructions_setup: This variation keeps the same structure as the Salzburg Touch & Tag Rondo #1 but is played as a 4v2 in each grid. Set up two possession boxes side by side with three teams. Two teams start as the possession sides (one in each grid), and the third team works as defenders/pressers.On the coach’s signal, two defenders sprint together into one of the grids, creating a 4v2 situation. Their aim is to press aggressively and win possession or force the ball out of play. Once this happens, The defenders immediately sprints out of the grid to tag waiting teammates, who then sprint into the next grid and again attempt to win possession. This continues for a set time period before rotating roles between teams. The practice promotes high-intensity pressing, quick reactions and sharp possession under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Play Away from Pressure: Encourage the possession team to recognise where the two defenders are pressing from and move the ball quickly into safer areas.• Support and Shape: Coach players to maintain good spacing and angles to keep at least two passing options available to the ball-carrier at all times.• Defensive Coordination: Emphasise communication between the two pressers so one applies direct pressure while the other covers passing lanes and anticipates interceptions.• Intensity and Recovery: Highlight the need for defenders to enter at full speed, work intensely for short periods, then recover while teammates press the opposite grid.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession Teams:Apply a two-touch limit for players in both grids. This increases the speed of circulation and forces players to adopt sharper angles and quicker support movements.Focus: Improves quick combinations, ball circulation and off-ball timing.
progression_two: Add Directional Targets for Defenders:When a defender wins the ball, they must play into a designated mini target or bounce pass to a coach before sprinting out to tag a teammate. This adds purpose to the press and rewards clean regains.Focus: Encourages controlled defensive actions and purposeful transitions after winning possession.

title: Sao Paulo 1v1 Transitions
instructions_setup: This 1v1 transitions practice is designed to develop attacking and defensive behaviours in rapid succession. Two goalkeepers are positioned in opposite goals on a small-sided pitch, which is divided vertically into two equal channels.Play begins with a 1v1 attack in the right-hand channel, where the attacker attempts to beat their opponent and score. Immediately after the phase ends, the same player must transition quickly across into the left-hand channel to defend a new 1v1 against an opponent attacking in the opposite direction. The practice creates continuous moments of attacking followed by defending, encouraging high intensity, focus and quick role adaptation.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Intent: Encourage positive, direct play in the first 1v1-commit the defender, attack space aggressively and finish with confidence and control.• Transition Speed: Reinforce immediate reaction after the first phase, sprinting across quickly to recover and defend without any hesitation.• Defensive Body Shape: Coach defenders to delay, stay balanced, angle the attacker away from goal and avoid diving in.• Physical Intensity: Emphasise repeat sprint efforts, mental focus and maintaining high concentration across multiple consecutive transitions.
progression_one: Time Limit to Score:Set a 5-second window for each attacking phase to increase urgency, tempo and decision-making under pressure.Focus: Improves speed of execution, attacking efficiency and realistic game intensity.
progression_two: Add a Recovery Defender:Introduce a second recovering defender who can join after a short delay, creating a 2v1 defensive scenario.Focus: Enhances realism, defensive coordination and challenges attackers to make quicker, sharper decisions.

title: Sao Paulo 2 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing practice is built around two consecutive attacking phases, encouraging combination play, movement and composure in front of goal. Play begins with two attackers working together to create penetrating combinations, aiming to break through and produce a finish into the first goal.Immediately after the first attempt, a third attacker joins with a second ball. The two original players must quickly adjust their positioning and combine again with the new player, creating a second attacking phase that leads to another finishing opportunity in the opposite goal. The practice flows continuously and challenges players to maintain technical quality, timing and decision-making across multiple actions.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Combinations: Encourage sharp, purposeful passing with clear intent to penetrate defensive lines and eliminate pressure quickly.• Movement After the First Finish: Reinforce quick recovery and intelligent repositioning to support the second phase without standing still.• Communication Between Attackers: Emphasise verbal and non-verbal cues to coordinate movements, timing and supporting angles effectively.• Composure in Front of Goal: Coach calm execution and correct finish selection despite repeated actions and rising physical fatigue.
progression_one: Touch Limit on Attackers:Restrict players to two touches per action to increase tempo and force quicker combinations and decision-making.Focus: Improves speed of play, technical sharpness and execution under increased pressure.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender:Introduce a passive defender who applies light pressure during both phases to increase realism and scanning demands.Focus: Develops awareness, movement under pressure and finishing composure in more game-like scenarios.

title: Sao Paulo Crossing & Finishing
instructions_setup: This crossing and finishing practice is designed to develop wide-area combinations, quality of delivery and attacking movement inside the box. Two attackers start in central positions, with one of them playing a pass out into a wide area. On the flank, two wide players combine using quick passes, overlaps or underlaps to create space for a cross.Once the wide combination is completed, the ball is delivered into the penalty area for the two central attackers to attack and finish. The practice is set up on both sides of the pitch, allowing the attacking group to alternate between right and left, encouraging variety in movement, crossing angles and finishing techniques.
coaching_notes: • Wide Combination Quality: Encourage sharp, well-timed combinations that create separation from defenders and clear crossing angles consistently.• Crossing Detail: Reinforce accurate delivery with the correct weight, height and trajectory based on attackers’ movements.• Timing of Runs: Coach attackers to delay, then explode into finishing zones to avoid arriving too early or late.• Attacking Movement: Emphasise varied runs across the near post, central and back-post areas to disrupt defensive positioning.
progression_one: One-Touch Cross:Require the wide player to deliver the cross first time after the combination to increase tempo and technical demand.Focus: Improves speed of execution, crossing technique and realism under time pressure.
progression_two: Add a Passive Defender:Introduce a passive defender in the box to apply light pressure on attackers during the finishing phase.Focus: Develops movement under pressure, awareness of space and composed finishing in realistic scenarios.

title: Sao Paulo Finishing & Transitional 1v1
instructions_setup: This finishing and 1v1 practice is designed to develop composed finishing followed by immediate defensive transition. Two players start with a ball each—one positioned at the top of the penalty area and the other starting behind the goal.The first attacker dribbles forward towards a mannequin, beats it with a positive move and finishes unopposed against the goalkeeper. As soon as the shot is taken, that same player must immediately transition into a defensive role.At the same time, the second player dribbles from behind the goal, moving up and around a second mannequin before entering the pitch. Once they emerge, the practice becomes live in a 1v1 scenario, with the second attacker trying to beat the first player (now recovering as a defender) and score. The drill links technical finishing with recovery runs and realistic 1v1 defending.
coaching_notes: • Positive Dribbling to Finish: Encourage the first attacker to drive at the mannequin with speed, intent and a decisive final action.• Transition Reaction: Reinforce instant mindset change after shooting, reacting quickly and sprinting to recover into a strong defensive position.• 1v1 Attacking Intent: Coach the second attacker to be aggressive, commit the defender and attack space with confidence.• Defensive Body Shape: Emphasise delaying, staying balanced and showing the attacker away from central finishing zones.
progression_one: Time Limit to Score in 1v1:Give the second attacker 4–5 seconds to finish once they enter the pitch.Focus: Increases tempo, attacking urgency and realism in transitional 1v1 situations, forcing quicker decisions under game-like pressure.
progression_two: Add a Touch Limit for the Finisher:Limit the first attacker to two touches before shooting in the unopposed phase.Focus: Improves first-touch quality, finishing efficiency and faster defensive transitions under realistic physical and cognitive demands.

title: Sao Paulo Passing & Penetration
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice focuses on ball circulation, receiving and movement under continuous tempo. Two balls are used simultaneously, with players cycling around different positions or passing patterns—one team moving clockwise and the other counterclockwise. The practice emphasizes awareness, scanning, body positioning and accurate passing. Each sequence ends with a pass into a mini goal, encouraging players to execute passes with the correct weight and timing while maintaining control and composure.
coaching_notes: • Passing Accuracy: Emphasise crisp, well-weighted passes with correct timing, body shape and follow-through to maintain tempo.• First Touch Quality: Encourage players to control the ball efficiently on the first touch to prepare for the next pass.• Scanning and Awareness: Reinforce constant scanning of teammates, opponents and space to make informed passing decisions.• Movement Off the Ball: Coach players to anticipate the next pass, create angles and maintain rhythm while cycling through positions.
progression_one: Two-Touch Passing Only:Require players to control and pass each ball within two touches, increasing tempo, technical demand and cognitive focus.Focus: Improves first-touch quality, accuracy and decision-making under pressure while keeping the practice realistic and fast-paced.
progression_two: Add Mini-Goal Scoring Points:Assign points for successfully completing a pass into the mini goal or hitting a target after each cycle.Focus: Encourages precision under pressure, reinforces attention to detail and motivates players to maintain consistent tempo and control.

title: Schalke 2 Way Finishing 2.0
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice starts with an up-back-and-through combination before a cross into the box for a 2-player finish. To add an element of chaos to the practice, 2 groups will play at the same time, attacking different ends of the field. This addition requires players to be more aware of the positioning of others in the area before making passes and runs, turning the practice into a semi-opposed-like scenario.
coaching_notes: • Combination Play – Encourage quick, fluid combination play (up-back-and-through) before the cross. Players should focus on timing their movements and passing to break through defensive lines effectively, allowing the cross to come in at the right moment.• Awareness of Surroundings – As two groups are attacking at the same time, players must keep a constant awareness of their positioning relative to others in the area. Encourage communication between players to avoid collisions and confusion during the practice.• Movement into the Box – Players should time their runs into the box to meet the cross at the right moment, ensuring they are ready to finish. Attackers must focus on getting into space and making their movements unpredictable to beat defenders.• Finishing Accuracy – When the cross comes in, attackers should concentrate on accuracy and composure to finish effectively. Emphasize getting low and striking with precision, focusing on the far post or placing the ball in the corners.
progression_one: Introduce DefendersAdd a single defender to each group to increase the level of pressure on the attackers. This will simulate game situations where defenders are present during crosses and finishes.Focus: Improving finishing under pressure and defending awareness when attacking.
progression_two: Limit PassesLimit the attackers to only 2 passes (up-back-through) before the cross to encourage quicker decision-making and faster attacks into the box.Focus: Improving speed of play and reducing hesitation in decision-making and finishing.

title: Schalke 2v2 to Transitional 1v1
instructions_setup: This is a 2-phase practice aimed at helping attackers develop their ability to transition quickly and effectively. Play starts with a 2v2 attack (Phase 1). Once a goal is scored or the ball goes dead, both attackers must transition to opposite sides of the grid, where they will defend in a 1v1 scenario (Phase 2).
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition from Attack to DefenseEncourage attackers to transition quickly after the 2v2 phase, focusing on switching their mindset from offensive to defensive play. The faster they get into position for the 1v1 phase, the better their chances to successfully defend or regain possession.• Defensive Positioning & TimingOnce attackers switch to defense, remind them to focus on proper body positioning and timing of tackles. They should aim to force the attacker wide or into less dangerous areas, avoiding getting caught out by a quick move or feint.• Speed of Play in the 2v2In the 2v2 phase, attackers should aim to create overloads and quick passing combinations to break down the defense. Speed of thought and decision-making is key in this phase, so they should always look for quick passes and movement off the ball.• 1v1 Decision Making & ComposureIn the 1v1 phase, defenders must be composed and not dive in too quickly. Attackers should look to be direct, using their body to protect the ball and either create a shot on goal or a passing opportunity. Encourage attackers to make confident decisions, whether it’s trying to beat the defender or pass to a teammate.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for TransitionAdd a time limit between phases (e.g., 5 seconds after the ball goes dead) to challenge players to transition more quickly. This will increase the intensity and test players' decision-making under pressure.Focus: This progression improves the speed of transitions and encourages faster recovery after losing possession.
progression_two: Add a Neutral AttackerAfter the 2v2 phase, add a neutral attacker who can join the team with possession. This creates a temporary 3v2 situation during the transition to 1v1.Focus: This progression simulates real game pressure, where attackers must adjust their defending and attacking responsibilities as the numbers change.

title: Schalke Back to Back Penetrative Passes
instructions_setup: In this technical passing warm-up, 3 mannequins will be positioned along the center of the grid. There will be 2 balls working simultaneously, with each team having a player starting on the central mannequin. The objective is for the teams to play a variety of penetrative passing combinations, working the balls from end to end while maintaining quick and accurate passing.The players must use a variety of techniques to break the defensive lines, playing one-touch or two-touch passes depending on the situation. The drill encourages teamwork, passing accuracy, and movement off the ball to maintain fluidity and pace.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing Combinations: Encourage quick, precise passing to ensure the ball moves from one end to the other with minimal delay. The faster the ball is played, the more effective the drill will be.• Penetrative Passing: Focus on using the mannequins to help break defensive lines and progress the ball forward. Players should aim to make penetrative passes to create space and allow the ball to advance.• Movement Off the Ball: Players should continuously move to receive the ball and create passing angles. This helps maintain the flow of the drill and ensures the attacking team is constantly in motion.• Switching Play: Encourage players to switch the ball from one side to the other to stretch the opposition and create opportunities for forward penetration. The passing team should look for quick transitions and changes in direction.
progression_one: Limit Touches:Restrict players to a maximum of one or two touches to increase the speed of play and improve decision-making under time pressure. This encourages quicker passing and faster decision-making.Focus: Enhances the ability to execute fast, accurate passes in tight spaces, promoting effective use of the ball in real-game situations.

title: Schalke Breaking Lines Into Transitional 2v2
instructions_setup: Play starts with two defenders dribbling out of the penalty area before making unopposed passes into either of the mini goals ahead. After making the passes, both defenders must immediately transition to defend against two attacking players. The attackers are tasked with exploiting the unbalanced defensive players and creating a quick scoring opportunity in a 2v2 situation.
coaching_notes: • Initial Pass Accuracy – The defenders should focus on playing precise passes into the mini goals, aiming to break lines and shift the focus towards the attacking phase. This will force the defending players to quickly transition from an offensive to a defensive mindset.• Quick Transition to Defence – As soon as the pass is made, defenders must immediately turn and transition into defensive mode. Encourage the defenders to react quickly to the loss of possession, positioning themselves efficiently to prevent the attackers from capitalizing on the overload.• Attacking Timing and Movement – The attacking players should look to use the transitional phase to their advantage, making quick, sharp movements and looking to exploit the momentary defensive imbalance. They should work in tandem to create space and find passing lanes.• Defensive Awareness – Defenders must focus on closing down space quickly while maintaining proper defensive positioning. They need to recognize when to press and when to drop off, especially if the attackers are using quick, fluid combinations.
progression_one: Add a Third AttackerIntroduce a third attacker into the practice, creating a 3v2 overload in favor of the attacking side. This will increase the pressure on the defending team to react even faster and organize themselves in real-time.Focus: This progression challenges defenders to cope with a more dynamic and unbalanced defensive scenario.
progression_two: Pressure From the Attacking MidfielderAllow one of the attacking players to start higher up the field, so that they can apply immediate pressure on the defenders once they transition. This will force defenders to deal with a quicker offensive setup, adding intensity to the practice.Focus: Encourages defenders to think quickly and make decisions under pressure, while also developing attackers’ ability to capitalize on fast breaks.

title: Schalke Build Up & Counter
instructions_setup: In this build-up practice, 2 players will cross over and defend in a 5v2 phase. The team in possession must attempt to make ‘X’ number of passes before scoring into the mini goals for a point. One team will build up into the wide areas, while the other team will build up into central areas. Teams will switch sides periodically. After each goal is scored or possession is won, players will transition to the opposite side of the grid to start the next phase of 5v2.
coaching_notes: • Transition Quickly Between RolesEncourage players to transition quickly between attacking and defending roles. Once possession is won, defenders must instantly switch to attacking positions, and vice versa. Quick transitions will keep the tempo high and make the practice more game-realistic.• Focus on Width and CentralityWhen building up, one team should focus on creating width to spread the defense, while the other focuses on central combinations. Players must recognize when to use the wide areas and when to play through the center, depending on where the most space is available.• Passing Accuracy and TempoIn the build-up phase, emphasize passing accuracy and tempo. Players should aim to complete the required passes with speed but also with precision. Encourage quick one-touches and sharp movement off the ball to maintain fluidity in the attack.• Defensive Pressure and CompactnessFor the defending team, maintaining defensive compactness is key. Defenders should work together to close down passing lanes and limit space in the areas where the opposition wants to build up. The 5v2 phase requires defenders to be proactive in intercepting passes or forcing the attacking team into less dangerous areas.
progression_one: Add a Third DefenderIntroduce a third defender to increase the difficulty for the attacking team. The defenders will need to work harder to stay compact and stop the buildup.Focus: This progression helps improve the defenders' ability to work together and manage overload situations.
progression_two: Limit Touches for AttackersLimit the attackers to a certain number of touches to increase the speed of play and force them to make quicker decisions.Focus: This progression helps develop quicker thinking and faster ball circulation under pressure.

title: Schalke In & Out Rondo
instructions_setup: This possession-based rondo is designed to challenge players to play both around and through pressure. Four players are positioned on the outside edges of a square grid, with a fifth teammate located in a smaller central square. Three defenders are placed inside the larger grid, aiming to win back possession during the rondo.The team of five plays keep-ball (5v3) using short combinations and the central player as a pivot to retain possession under pressure. If the defending trio wins the ball, they immediately transition and attempt to score in any of the four mini goals positioned on the outer sides of the grid. The team that lost possession must instantly counter-press to prevent the shot.
coaching_notes: • Support Angles: Wide players must constantly adjust their body shape and positioning to provide clear angles for the central player and switch the point of attack.• Central Pivot Use: Encourage quick passes in and out of the central square, using the inside player to break pressure and maintain rhythm.• Counter Pressing Intensity: If possession is lost, players must react instantly and press with speed and cohesion to close down space and delay or prevent the shot.• Defensive Transition Awareness: Defenders should anticipate loose touches or predictable passes and break quickly once possession is won, choosing the nearest mini goal to exploit.
progression_one: Limit Outside TouchesAllow only one or two touches for outside players to increase tempo and decision-making speed.Focus: Promotes sharper passing, quicker support play, and improves scanning under time pressure.
progression_two: Add a Neutral FloaterIntroduce a neutral player who always plays with the team in possession and moves freely within the grid.Focus: Increases numerical superiority, encouraging more through-ball opportunities and dynamic movement patterns.

title: Schalke In Behind & Across the Front
instructions_setup: This 2-phase finishing drill works on two specific types of attacking movements that are crucial for forwards in game situations. The first phase focuses on completing an unopposed finish after making a run in behind a defensive line, while the second phase works on running across the face of a defensive line before finishing.The drill is designed to improve both finishing under no pressure and the timing of movements to break down defensive lines.
coaching_notes: • Phase 1 – Movement in Behind: The attacker must time their run well to receive the ball in behind the defensive line. Encourage players to start their run from an onside position and to stay alert for the right moment to make the attacking run. They should focus on staying calm and composed when receiving the ball to finish effectively.• Phase 2 – Movement Across the Face: In the second phase, the forward needs to make a run across the defensive line to receive the ball. Emphasize the importance of quick, sharp changes of direction to deceive defenders and make themselves available for a cross or through ball. The movement should be purposeful, with the aim to get in front of the defender to receive a pass in a dangerous area.• Finishing Technique: For both phases, players should focus on finishing with composure, using the inside of the foot for placement or the laces for power, depending on the situation. Encourage them to keep their heads over the ball and strike with accuracy rather than power.• Timing of Runs: Timing is key in both phases. In Phase 1, players should focus on making their run when the ball is being played through, ensuring they stay onside and time their finish correctly. In Phase 2, the forward must time their cross the defensive line to be in the right position for the pass.
progression_one: Add Defensive Pressure:Introduce one defender to apply light pressure to the attacker after they make their movement in behind. This will force the forward to finish under pressure, improving their composure in game situations.Focus: Enhances the ability to finish under pressure and improve timing when running behind a defensive line.
progression_two: Crosses and Variations:Add a wide player who will serve in crosses for the attacker to run across the face of the defense. Players will now need to focus on their movement across the defensive line to meet the cross, making sure they time their movement to be in front of the defender.Focus: Improves attacking runs across the defensive line and finishing from crosses.

title: Schalke Possession & Press
instructions_setup: This practice works on a team's ability to retain possession under pressure. Play begins with a pass into either grid, and the defending team sends 3 players to press the 6 players in possession. If the 6 players can complete 10 successful passes, they can score into the main goal. The drill lasts for 4 minutes, and at the end of each 4-minute cycle, the team that conceded the least number of goals while defending and pressing is considered the winner.
coaching_notes: • Pass and Move with PurposeEncourage the 6 players in possession to focus on quick, purposeful passes and effective off-the-ball movement. This keeps the defenders on the move, making it difficult for them to maintain pressure and win the ball. Always ensure players are creating passing options for the ball carrier.• Pressing Triggers for DefendersThe 3 defenders should work as a unit, pressing based on specific triggers, such as the ball being passed into a player’s feet or when a player takes too many touches. Emphasize the importance of timing and communication when initiating the press to limit the options of the player in possession.• Compactness and Support in PossessionThe 6 players in possession need to stay compact and close together. Encourage them to pass and move quickly, and support the ball carrier at all times. The spacing should be optimal to avoid unnecessary turnovers. Focus on players offering themselves for a quick one-touch or two-touch pass to advance the play.• Defender Recovery and TransitionWhen the 3 defenders lose possession, they need to transition quickly to counter-press. They should immediately try to win the ball back or force the opposition into a poor decision. Teach defenders to focus on their positioning and not overcommit when pressing to avoid being caught out of shape.
progression_one: Increase Passes RequiredIncrease the number of passes required for the 6 players to score (e.g., from 10 to 12 or 15) to add more pressure and challenge the attacking players to retain possession for longer. This progression will test their ability to hold onto the ball while dealing with more intense pressing.Focus: This progression focuses on improving the attacking team's composure and precision under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Fourth DefenderAdd a fourth defender to create a more difficult situation for the attacking players, forcing them to make quicker decisions under increased pressure. The extra defender can provide more angles and make it harder for the 6 players to complete the required passes.Focus: This progression increases the intensity for the team in possession, sharpening their decision-making and ball control.

title: Schalke Technical 1 to 12 Warm-Up
instructions_setup: Each player is given a number between 1 and 12 by the coach. The players must pass the ball from player 1 all the way through to player 12, with player 12 then making a return pass to player 1. The drill requires high levels of communication, quick passing, and awareness to maintain fluidity throughout the exercise.
coaching_notes: • Effective Communication – Encourage players to constantly communicate with each other, especially regarding the timing of passes and positioning. They should give verbal or visual cues to help keep the flow of the practice smooth.• Passing Accuracy and Timing – Players should focus on making accurate, well-weighted passes to ensure the ball reaches the next player efficiently. Passing too hard or soft will disrupt the flow of the practice.• Movement After the Pass – Players should always move to support their teammate after making a pass. The next player should be ready to receive the ball and continue the chain, maintaining quick and purposeful movement throughout the drill.• Awareness of Positioning – Each player should maintain awareness of where they are in relation to the other players and the ball. They should always be ready to adjust their positioning to maintain the flow of the exercise.
progression_one: Add Extra BallsTo increase the challenge, add extra balls into the practice. This will require players to make quick decisions and keep their heads up to avoid confusion while maintaining their passing accuracy.Focus: This progression will improve players' decision-making and ability to manage multiple passes in a high-paced environment.
progression_two: Time PressureIntroduce a time limit for completing the circuit of passes. For example, the team must complete the pass sequence within a set time frame, with the return pass to player 1 marking the completion of the drill.Focus: This progression will challenge players to maintain speed and accuracy under pressure, promoting fast, sharp decision-making.

title: Shanghai Progress Play Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo drill is designed to develop a team's ability to switch play quickly and effectively through central areas. The setup includes three zones: two end zones with a 4v2 overload and a central zone with a 2v2 battle.Play begins with a 4v2 in one of the end zones, where the attacking team aims to maintain possession. The goal is to eventually progress the ball through the 2v2 central zone and transfer it cleanly into the opposite 4v2 zone, encouraging quick switching and intelligent positioning.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Ball Movement: Emphasize sharp, accurate passing to quickly shift defenders and open up passing lanes for the switch to be played.• Body Shape to Receive: Players should open up their body before receiving to allow quick, forward-facing play into the central area with limited touches.• Central Awareness and Timing: The central players must time their movement and positioning to receive under pressure and play forward effectively and early.• Communication and Cues: Constant verbal and visual communication is vital to prepare central players and trigger support options during the switch.
progression_one: Limit Central Touches:Restrict central players to a maximum of two touches when receiving the ball before playing forward or switching zones.Focus: Encourages scanning, quick decision-making, and precise execution under time pressure and spatial constraints.
progression_two: Increase Central Pressure:Add a third defender in the central zone to increase pressure and make progression more difficult for the attacking side.Focus: Develops composure under pressure, sharper off-the-ball movement, and accurate passing in crowded central areas.

title: Slovakia 3rd Man Finishing
