instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on developing the ability to play fluid third-man combinations in central areas. The drill begins with a forward pass from one player to another. The original passer then makes a forward run into the space, receiving a third-man pass (a pass from a player other than the initial recipient). The player who receives the third-man pass then finishes the attack unopposed.
coaching_notes: • Third-Man Runs – Encourage players to recognize when to make the third-man run into space. The timing of the run is crucial, as it needs to be timed perfectly to receive the pass and finish effectively.• Passing Precision – The passers should focus on playing accurate and well-weighted passes to ensure the third-man runner can receive the ball in stride and set up a clean finish.• Quick Decision-Making – Players should develop the ability to make quick decisions regarding when to play the ball, when to make the run, and when to finish. This involves good spatial awareness and anticipation of the movements of teammates.• Finishing Under Control – When the third-man pass is received, players should focus on finishing with composure, using their second touch to place the ball accurately into the goal.
progression_one: Add a Defender to Pressure the FinishIntroduce a passive defender to provide light pressure as the third-man runner receives the pass and prepares to finish. This will challenge the attacker to stay composed under pressure and make quicker decisions.Focus:Helps players practice finishing under pressure and improve the timing and accuracy of their third-man runs.
progression_two: Increase the Number of CombinationsExpand the practice to involve multiple third-man combinations in sequence. For example, after the first third-man finish, the ball is quickly recycled to a new combination and a new third-man run, keeping the drill fluid and fast-paced.Focus:Improves players’ ability to link multiple third-man runs together and maintain a high tempo in attacking situations.

title: Slovakia 3rd man switching rondo
instructions_setup: This practice is set up with two adjacent grids, each containing a 4v2 rondo. Only one ball is in play between both grids. The objective for the team in possession is to retain the ball under pressure in their grid and look for opportunities to switch the ball to the opposite grid using a third man combination.The third man concept allows players to disguise and break lines of pressure by involving a supporting player who doesn’t initially receive the first pass but becomes the key link to switch the ball across. Defenders remain in their respective grids and must adjust positioning based on the movement and potential switches.
coaching_notes: • Third Man Movement: Encourage players to recognize moments to act as the third man—supporting behind or to the side of the play to allow clean switches between grids.• Scanning and Awareness: Players must consistently scan both grids to assess where the next pass should go and how to exploit gaps in the defensive shape.• Body Shape for Switching: Receiving players should open up their body when possible to play forward or switch first time, keeping the tempo high.• Defensive Shifts: Defenders should anticipate the switch and adjust as a unit, aiming to cut out lanes or intercept through-passes between the grids.
progression_one: Add a Floating Neutral PlayerIntroduce one neutral player who operates between both grids to assist with switching play and maintaining possession.Focus: Promotes third man support, intelligent positioning, and offers an extra passing option to build play.
progression_two: Limit Touches to Two per PlayerRestrict players in both grids to a maximum of two touches.Focus: Increases the speed of play, demands better decision-making, and encourages sharper movement off the ball.

title: Slovakia Attacking 1v1 to Finish
instructions_setup: This 1v1 practice is set up on half a pitch, using the width of the 18-yard box. A central zone is marked out with two small gates positioned around 10–15 yards outside the box, one on each side. The coach starts each repetition by playing a pass into a single attacker, who is immediately pressed by a defender as they enter the central zone.The attacker’s objective is to beat the defender and drive through either of the two gates. If successful, the practice becomes unopposed, and the attacker continues forward to take a free shot on goal. Defenders aim to delay or dispossess without fouling.
coaching_notes: • Positive First Touch: Attackers should focus on receiving the ball in a way that allows them to immediately face forward and assess the defender’s positioning.• 1v1 Execution: Encourage attackers to use feints, changes of pace, and sharp direction shifts to create space and beat the defender cleanly.• Defensive Body Shape: Defenders must stay low and balanced, guiding attackers away from goal and toward less dangerous areas.• Composed Finishing: Once through the gate, attackers should settle and execute controlled, accurate finishes when unopposed.
progression_one: Add Time Limit for Gate EntryIntroduce a time constraint (e.g., 6–8 seconds) for the attacker to break through a gate, increasing urgency and intensity of the duel.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making, more explosive attacking play, and sharper defensive reactions.
progression_two: Make One Gate InactiveBefore each rep, the coach calls out one gate that is closed. The attacker must now beat the defender and score through the active gate only.Focus: Forces players to scan and adapt, improving awareness, tactical flexibility, and directional control under pressure.

title: Slovakia Build Up & Transition
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on developing build-up play and transitioning quickly between attacking and defending phases. The drill starts with a 4v2 build-up phase. The goalkeeper and three outfield players work together to build possession, with the objective of progressing the ball through one of two gates placed in the attacking half. Once the ball is passed through a gate, the team in possession immediately transitions to defend against a counter-attack. The counter phase lasts for 10 seconds to replicate the intensity of a real game, and players must react quickly. If the two defending players win the ball before the attack is completed, the counter phase starts immediately.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Focus – Encourage patience and composure in the build-up phase. The ball carrier should focus on finding the best passing options, using wide players, and opening passing lanes. Emphasize creating angles for support and maintaining possession under pressure.• Quick Transitions – The moment the ball is passed through a gate, players must transition into defensive roles quickly. The defending team must close down space and pressure the ball carrier immediately, while the attacking team should reorganize into defensive shape.• Decision-Making Under Pressure – Players must make quick decisions in the build-up and counter phases. Attackers should look for opportunities to exploit space, while defenders should recognize when to press and when to delay.• Intensity of Counter Attack – The 10-second time limit for the counter phase encourages attackers to work quickly and defenders to recover efficiently. This adds realism and forces players to think and act rapidly during transitions.
progression_one: Add More Defenders to the Build-Up PhaseIncrease the defensive pressure in the build-up phase by adding one more defender (making it 3v2). This will force the attacking team to be more precise and creative in their play.Focus:Improves decision-making in tight spaces and encourages the build-up team to maintain possession under increased pressure.
progression_two: Multiple Gates and Varying TimingIntroduce multiple gates in different areas of the field to progress the ball through, creating different options for the attacking team. Additionally, vary the timing of the counter-attack (e.g., let the defenders win possession but delay the counter for a few seconds) to increase unpredictability.Focus:Develops spatial awareness and adaptability, encouraging attackers to use various passing options and defenders to stay alert and adaptable during transitions.

title: Slovakia Buildup to 1v1 Attack
instructions_setup: This practice begins with an unopposed build-up sequence on a half-pitch setup. A centre back starts the play by passing to a full back, who then connects inside to a central midfielder. This phase is designed to simulate structured buildup from the back, with all players receiving and playing under no pressure to begin with.Once the central midfielder receives the ball, they play a disguised or timed through ball back toward the starting direction of the practice. At that moment, a 1v1 duel begins between an attacker running onto the through ball and a defender who recovers to challenge. The attacker’s aim is to beat the defender and finish on goal.
coaching_notes: • Structured Build-Up: Emphasise clean passing, proper body shape, and correct receiving angles in the unopposed build-up phase to replicate real-game rhythm.• Timing of the Pass: Central midfielders should time their through balls precisely, matching the forward’s run and ensuring the ball arrives in stride.• Attacking the Space: Attackers should accelerate quickly onto the through ball, using body feints or touches to unbalance the recovering defender.• Defensive Recovery: Defenders must transition rapidly from passive to active, tracking the attacker’s run while positioning to delay or tackle cleanly.
progression_one: Add Passive Pressure in Build-Up PhaseIntroduce passive defenders to apply light pressure during the initial build-up sequence to increase scanning and urgency without disrupting rhythm.Focus: Enhances composure, decision-making, and spatial awareness during the early stages of possession.
progression_two: Add a Second Recovering DefenderA second recovering defender starts deeper and joins the 1v1 late, potentially turning it into a 2v1 defensive scenario if they arrive in time.Focus: Encourages the attacker to make quicker decisions and adds realism to the counter-attacking transition.

title: Slovakia Finishing From Cutbacks
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing practice, players focus on creating attacking moments that lead to a cutback delivery. The pattern begins with a short passing combination between central players, followed by a through ball into a wide runner. The wide player then drives toward the byline before cutting the ball back into the box. Multiple attackers time their runs to arrive in the box for a finish. The emphasis is on movement, timing, and quality of the final action.
coaching_notes: • Cutback Delivery – Encourage wide players to vary the angle and weight of their cutbacks. Deliveries should be pulled back into space behind defenders, allowing attackers to run onto the ball rather than waiting flat-footed.• Timing of Runs – Attackers must stagger their runs — one near post, one central, one deeper — to attack different zones. Late runs are often the most effective for finishing cutbacks.• Quality of Finish – Emphasize composure and technique when finishing from cutbacks. Players should stay over the ball, aim for corners, and finish with minimal touches when possible.• Speed of Combination – The initial combination and through ball should be played with pace and precision to simulate real-game tempo and pressure.
progression_one: Passive Defender Inside the BoxAdd one or two passive defenders inside the box to introduce mild pressure. They can block cutback lanes but do not actively tackle.Focus:Encourages attackers to find better angles and timing to evade marking and increases the realism of decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Live Defender Closing Wide PlayerIntroduce a live defender who starts centrally and must recover to close the wide player delivering the cutback. Forces quicker execution of the cross and increased urgency from attackers in the box.Focus:Enhances decision-making for the crosser under pressure and demands sharper runs and finishes from the attacking players.

title: Slovakia Passing Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this passing activation warm-up, players will work on various passing combinations, including overlaps, underlaps, and 3rd man runs. Players will move through a series of short, sharp passing drills that emphasize timing, movement, and accuracy. This warm-up can be adjusted for different skill levels by varying the distance between players or adding pressure from defenders as needed.
coaching_notes: • Timing of RunsPlayers should focus on the timing of their runs, especially during overlaps, underlaps, and 3rd man combinations. The player making the overlapping or underlapping run should do so at the right moment to create space and provide a passing option for the player with the ball.• Quick Passing and MovementEncourage players to pass the ball quickly and to move into space after passing. The focus should be on moving the ball efficiently and not letting it "stick" at any point. Movement off the ball should be as important as the passing itself to ensure smooth transitions and fluid play.• Focus on CommunicationPlayers should communicate with each other during the warm-up. Whether calling for the ball, directing traffic, or signaling a run, effective communication helps synchronize the movement and passing. This is crucial for making quick, decisive plays during real-game situations.• Accuracy and Weight of PassesEnsure that players focus on the accuracy and weight of their passes. Over- or under-hit passes can disrupt the flow and timing of the drill. Encourage players to deliver crisp, controlled passes, ensuring they are the correct weight for the receiver to continue their movement smoothly.
progression_one: Add Defenders for PressureIntroduce passive defenders who apply light pressure to the ball carrier. This will force players to make quicker decisions and execute their passes under more realistic conditions.Focus: This progression helps improve decision-making under pressure and simulates game-like situations where players need to react to defenders.
progression_two: Vary Passing CombinationsSwitch up the passing patterns by introducing variations such as 1-2s, wall passes, or diagonal switches. This keeps the warm-up dynamic and challenges players to adapt to different attacking styles.Focus: This progression helps players develop versatility in their passing combinations, improving their ability to create chances from different positions.

title: Slovakia Tag Warm Up
instructions_setup: Set up two cones along the top line and two cones directly opposite on the bottom line, creating two vertical lanes. One player begins on the top line and the other on the bottom. The top player moves laterally between their two cones using quick, deceptive footwork and must suddenly tap one of the cones.As soon as the cone is tapped, the bottom player reacts by tapping the cone on their line that corresponds vertically, then immediately attempts to tag the top player before they can sprint across the bottom line. The drill focuses on reaction time, movement disguise, and acceleration under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Deception in Movement: The top player should use body feints, sharp changes of pace, and unpredictable timing to disguise which cone they intend to tap.• Sharp Reactions: The bottom player must stay light on their feet, maintain a low stance, and react instantly to the attacker’s movement cues.• Explosive First Steps: Both players should focus on generating powerful first steps from a standing position to either escape or close the distance quickly.• Game Awareness: Encourage players to scan for subtle body language cues and anticipate movements with composure and alertness.
progression_one: Add a Fake Tap RuleAllow the top player to perform one fake tap (hand feint without touching the cone) before committing to a real tap.Focus: Improves deception and forces the defender to remain balanced and not overcommit to false movements or feints.
progression_two: Introduce a Time ConstraintThe defender must attempt to tag the attacker within 3 seconds of tapping the cone.Focus: Adds urgency to the drill, helping both players sharpen their decision-making speed and increase reaction time under pressure.

title: Sociedad 3v2 Cross & Finish
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into an unopposed winger positioned on one side of the grid. The winger’s task is to deliver crosses into the box for the attacking players. Upon receiving the ball, the three attackers must sprint across the grid and enter the box, creating a 3v2 attacking scenario.Once the play concludes, the roles reset, and a new 3v2 attack begins from the opposite side of the grid. The winger can either turn and cross directly or play a quick combination with one of the three attackers before delivering the cross into the box.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Attackers should time their runs well to arrive in the box at the right moment, ensuring they are prepared to receive the cross while defenders are still tracking them.• Crossing Techniques: Encourage the winger to vary their crossing technique—driven balls, lofted crosses, and cutbacks—to make the deliveries harder to defend.• Quick Combinations: When the winger plays a quick combination, attackers must be ready to support the winger with fast, intelligent movement to create space for the final delivery.• Finishing in the Box: Attackers should focus on creating a variety of finishing options in the box, such as first-time shots, headers, or controlled finishes, depending on the delivery.
progression_one: Limit Time for the Cross:Introduce a time limit of 5 seconds for the winger to deliver the cross once they receive the ball, adding urgency and forcing quicker decision-making.Focus: Encourages faster thinking and better anticipation from both the winger and the attackers, improving overall attacking tempo and fluidity.

title: Sociedad 433 Rondo
instructions_setup: This positional rondo simulates the movement principles of a 4-3-3 formation, using a large rectangle divided into four connected grids. Within these grids, the possession team engages in a 4v2 rondo in whichever grid the ball is currently located.To maintain shape and encourage intelligent movement, certain players are required to shift horizontally or vertically so that each active grid always has four possession players. This models how players must support the ball across different zones in a real match while staying connected to team structure.As the ball transitions from one grid to another, players must slide accordingly to maintain numerical superiority in the live area. Defenders (2 per rondo) apply pressure in the active grid.
coaching_notes: • Shape Awareness: Emphasize maintaining the team’s shape while adjusting positioning based on the ball’s location.• Communication: Players must constantly scan and talk to each other to coordinate which players shift and who holds in neighboring zones.• Speed of Play: Focus on quick, accurate passes and smart movement to unbalance the defenders and keep the rondo flowing.• Positional Discipline: Reinforce roles and responsibilities within the 4-3-3 structure, ensuring players understand when to shift and when to hold their zone.
progression_one: Limit Touches in the Active Grid:Impose a 2-touch maximum for the possession players in the active rondo grid.Focus: Increases tempo, encourages sharp passing, and quick decision-making under pressure.

title: Sociedad Attack Overloaded
instructions_setup: This attacking overload drill begins with a 1-2 combination between the central attacker and the defender. Once the attacker receives the ball back, they must play one-touch passes to either of the two wide attackers positioned on the flanks.Upon the pass to either wide attacker, play becomes opposed, and a 2v1 attacking scenario unfolds. The wide attackers must hold up possession briefly, allowing the central attacker to cover ground and support the attack, creating a 2v1 opportunity.
coaching_notes: • 1-2 Combination Awareness: Encourage the central attacker to use sharp and quick movements when playing the 1-2 with the defender. This will create space for a more effective and accurate pass back.• Wide Attackers’ Timing: The wide attackers must time their runs into space, ensuring they receive the ball at the right moment and can immediately engage in the 2v1 attack with the central attacker.• Hold-Up Play: The wide attackers must be patient and hold up possession until the central attacker arrives, maintaining control of the ball and preventing unnecessary pressure from the defender.• Quick Transition to 2v1: Once the wide attackers have possession, they must transition quickly into the 2v1 scenario with the central attacker, utilizing their numerical advantage to break down the defense.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Wide Attackers:Introduce an additional defender to press the wide attackers, creating a 2v2 scenario for the wide attackers. This will force the central attacker to make quicker decisions and improve their ability to support under pressure.Focus: Develops the wide attackers' ability to handle pressure and use quick passes or dribbles to break through a defensive setup while maintaining support from the central attacker.

title: Sociedad Ball Mastery
instructions_setup: This mastery drill serves as a great pre-season fitness practice, combining technical skills with conditioning. Players will travel into one of the outside players and complete a pre-defined technical skill, such as a pass, dribble, or first touch, before running to a different corner and performing the same skill again.After a set period of time, the central players will switch with the outside players, ensuring everyone participates in both technical and conditioning aspects. The coach should vary the technical skills throughout the session to keep the drill challenging and engaging.
coaching_notes: • Focus on Technique: Emphasize the importance of completing each technical skill with precision, even under fatigue. The quality of the skill should not diminish as players progress through the drill.• Maintain Consistent Movement: Players should focus on maintaining a steady pace throughout the drill, ensuring they are constantly moving between corners and completing the skills without slowing down.• Effective Transitions: Encourage players to transition quickly between stations, using proper footwork and body positioning to ensure they are always ready to perform the next skill.• Conditioning with Intensity: As the drill progresses, players should aim to push themselves both technically and physically, simulating the demands of real-game situations where speed and skill are needed under pressure.
progression_one: Increase Skill Difficulty:Increase the difficulty of the technical skills required for each station, such as introducing more complex passing combinations or advanced dribbling techniques. This will force players to think quickly while performing at a high level.Focus: Enhances players’ ability to execute more complex technical movements while maintaining speed and fluidity, improving both skill level and fitness.
progression_two: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender into the mix to apply pressure as players execute the technical skills. The defender should aim to force the player into making quicker decisions, enhancing both fitness and technical sharpness under pressure.Focus: Increases the intensity of the drill by introducing defensive pressure, improving players' decision-making and execution in game-like scenarios.

title: Sociedad Breaking Lines & Overload
instructions_setup: Play begins with an unopposed forward line-breaking pass from the center-back (CB) into one of the three forward players. Once the ball is played into the attacking players, the drill becomes live, and the three attackers must work together to combine and create a goal-scoring opportunity in an overloaded 3v2 scenario.The attacking players are encouraged to use quick, intelligent passes and movement to break down the defending team and score in the  goal.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Pass: The center-back should focus on timing the forward pass accurately, ensuring it is played into the path of the attackers and allows them to exploit the space before the defenders can react.• Combination Play: Attackers should focus on quick combinations to break down the defensive unit. Short, sharp passes and good movement off the ball will allow the attackers to keep the defenders off-balance and create goal-scoring chances.• Creating Overloads: The attackers should aim to utilize the overload, ensuring they are constantly making runs and options to maximize the advantage of having three players against two defenders. Spacing and communication are key.• Finishing Under Pressure: Once the overload is created, attackers should focus on finishing with composure, making the most of the goal-scoring opportunities by being quick and accurate in front of goal.
progression_one: Add a Defender to Apply Pressure:Introduce a defender who applies pressure to the forward players as they attempt to combine and finish. This encourages attackers to make quicker decisions and execute under more realistic match conditions.Focus: Enhances decision-making and finishing under pressure, simulating real-game situations where attackers must execute quickly with limited time.
progression_two: Limit Touches:Limit the number of touches that each attacker can take before they must pass or shoot. This encourages quicker decision-making and helps to improve the speed of the attacking play.Focus: Increases the speed of attack and forces players to think and execute faster, promoting quicker combinations and sharper decision-making.

title: Sociedad Build Up with Transitions
instructions_setup: In this build-up drill, the team in possession is tasked with progressing the ball through controlled passes into any of the three mini goals positioned along the halfway line. The attacking team must maintain possession and work together to break down the defensive shape, aiming to score in one of the mini goals.If the defending team wins possession, the two wide players positioned on the sidelines immediately become live, and a counter-attack begins. The defending team, now unbalanced and disorganised, must quickly adjust to defend the counter-attack, which adds a sense of urgency and unpredictability.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Play: Encourage the attacking team to maintain possession through quick, short passes and smart movement off the ball. The goal is to progress the ball patiently and create space, allowing the team to break through the opposition and attack the mini goals.• Wide Player Involvement: The wide players should always be looking for opportunities to receive the ball and stretch the defending team. Their role is crucial in creating space and pulling the opposition out of position for successful build-up play.• Quick Transition After Losing Possession: Defenders should be coached to react immediately when possession is lost. The key focus should be on transitioning quickly into a counter-attacking scenario and exploiting the disorganised defending team.• Counter-Attack Precision: In the event of a counter-attack, attackers should focus on quick decision-making, efficient passing, and directness to capitalize on the unbalanced defenders, aiming to score before the defensive team can regroup.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Passes Before Attacking:Set a limit on the number of passes the attacking team can make before attempting to score in the mini goals. This adds pressure to progress the ball quickly and encourages faster decision-making in the build-up play.Focus: Encourages the attacking team to move the ball quickly and make fast, intelligent passes to break through the defense before the defenders can recover.

title: Sociedad Countering from Deep
instructions_setup: Play starts with the team in possession controlling the ball in one half of the pitch, with the objective of breaking the opposition down and creating a scoring opportunity. The attacking team must maintain possession, create space, and work through the opposition’s defense to score.If the defending team wins possession, they are required to play a forward pass into the space on the unoccupied side of the grid. This triggers a 2v1 counter-attack, with two wingers joining the play against one recovering defender who is attempting to prevent the goal-scoring opportunity.
coaching_notes: • Controlled Possession: The attacking team should focus on patience, quick passing, and intelligent movement to create openings. Encourage players to work together, maintaining possession and looking for gaps in the opposition's defensive setup.• Defensive Transition: Upon losing possession, the defending team must quickly react and apply pressure to prevent an easy counter-attack. Focus on tracking runners and recovering defensive positions quickly.• Quick Forward Pass: When the defending team gains possession, they must look for a quick, accurate forward pass to initiate the counter-attack. This pass should exploit the unoccupied side of the grid, allowing the attacking wingers to get into advanced positions.• 2v1 Counter-Attack: The wingers should focus on using speed and good decision-making to exploit the 2v1 situation. The defender in the counter-attack must communicate effectively and try to slow down the attacking wingers until help arrives.
progression_one: Limit the Time in Possession:Impose a time limit for the attacking team to maintain possession (e.g., 20 seconds) before they must attempt a shot. This encourages faster decision-making and more dynamic movement when attacking, while also increasing the pressure on the defending team.Focus: Encourages the attacking team to make quicker decisions when progressing the ball forward, while also pressuring the defending team to be more proactive in winning possession.
progression_two: Add More Defenders in Transition:Introduce an additional defender into the counter-attack phase to create a 3v2 situation. The defending team must now react faster and work harder to counter the overload, while the attacking wingers need to maintain their composure and exploit the additional defender.Focus: Enhances the attacking team’s ability to deal with added defensive pressure, while improving the defending team’s ability to recover and deal with overload situations.

title: Sociedad Diamond Finishing
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, four players are positioned in a diamond shape on the edge of the penalty area. The drill focuses on quick passing combinations and movement to create shooting opportunities. Players work through various combinations, ensuring that all four players are involved in the build-up before a shot on goal.The ball is played between the players in different sequences, such as one-touch passes, wall passes, or quick give-and-go’s. After completing the combination, the player receiving the final ball takes a shot at goal. This drill emphasizes precise passing, movement off the ball, and clinical finishing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: Focus on quick, one-touch passes to maintain the speed of play and break down the defensive line. Encourage players to keep the ball moving at a fast tempo to create space for the final shot.• Movement Off the Ball: Emphasize the importance of players moving into space after making a pass. Players should be proactive, constantly looking for an opportunity to receive the ball or create a passing lane for their teammate.• Finishing: Encourage players to focus on composure and accuracy when taking the shot. Players should vary their finishing techniques, such as placing the ball in the corners or using quick reactions for volleys and first-time shots.• Timing of Runs: Timing is key in this drill. Players must time their runs into the box and receive the ball in stride, which will help them create better shooting angles and avoid being caught offside.
progression_one: Add Pressure from a Defender:Introduce a defender who starts at a distance and closes down the player receiving the ball for the final shot. This forces the attacker to take quicker decisions, improve their shooting under pressure, and execute a better finish.Focus: Improves the attacking team’s ability to deal with defensive pressure and take shots with precision under time constraints.
progression_two: Vary the Passing Combinations:Change the passing combinations so that players are forced to use different techniques and engage in more dynamic movements. For example, include diagonal passes, through balls, or flicks to increase the complexity of the drill.Focus: Develops versatility in attacking play, encouraging players to be creative and use different passing techniques to create goal-scoring opportunities.

title: Sociedad Dribble & 1v1
instructions_setup: In this unopposed drill, the attacking player dribbles up toward the goal area before turning back through a marked gate and attempting to score. The focus is on quick direction changes and sharp turns, simulating a real game scenario where the attacker must quickly react to the defender’s positioning.The defender starts from a marked position and sprints down the box, turning back through the same gate before attempting to close down the attacker and prevent the shot. The drill promotes sharp decision-making, quick reactions, and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Direction Changes: Emphasize the importance of quick and controlled changes in direction when turning through the gate. This will help the attacker deceive the defender and create a clearer path to goal.• Defensive Positioning: Teach the defender to close the space effectively and maintain balance while sprinting and turning. The defender should aim to make the attacker feel pressured while not overcommitting too early.• Finishing Under Pressure: Encourage the attacker to maintain composure when taking the shot. The goal is to finish accurately and efficiently, even when under pressure from the defender closing in.• Timing of the Turn: Timing the turn is essential for both the attacker and defender. The attacker must turn quickly enough to maintain control of the ball and still have a chance to finish, while the defender must make sure they turn at the right moment to challenge the shot.
progression_one: Add a Second Defender:Introduce a second defender who pressures the attacker as they attempt to dribble and shoot. This will increase the challenge for the attacker and force them to make quicker decisions on when and how to shoot.Focus: Increases decision-making speed, as the attacker must now navigate multiple defenders while maintaining composure and focus on their shot.
progression_two: Vary the Gate Size:Adjust the width of the gate to make it wider or narrower, which will force the attacker to adjust their dribbling and turning techniques. A narrower gate will require more precise dribbling and better control, while a wider gate may allow more freedom in movement.Focus: Develops the ability to execute tight turns and precise dribbling under varying conditions, enhancing the attacker’s overall agility and adaptability.

title: Sociedad First Touch & Pass
instructions_setup: In this drill, players are positioned in a diamond shape and pass the ball around the diamond in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction. However, there is a twist: when a pass is made, the passer must follow their pass and run towards the receiver. The receiver, instead of simply receiving the ball, uses the oncoming player as a barrier and performs a skill (such as a feint, body swerve, or quick turn) to move around the passer and retrieve the ball on the opposite side. This encourages creativity and sharp movement off the ball.The drill helps improve passing accuracy, off-the-ball movement, and the ability to use an incoming defender or teammate as a shield to execute quick skill moves.
coaching_notes: • Quick Movement After the Pass: Emphasize the importance of the passer moving quickly to support the receiver. The passer should stay dynamic and follow the ball with pace, creating a continuous flow of passing and movement.• Use of the Barrier: Encourage the receiver to recognize when the passer is closing in and to use the oncoming player as a barrier for a quick turn or feint. This allows the player to maintain possession and move efficiently to the other side of the defender.• Skill Execution: Focus on the variety and effectiveness of the skills performed by the receiver. The goal is to deceive the oncoming player using quick footwork or body movement, enabling the receiver to glide around and take control of the ball.• Timing of the Turn: Timing is key when using the passer as a barrier. The receiver should execute the skill at the right moment to ensure they can evade the defender and retrieve the ball without losing possession.
progression_one: Increase the Pace:Increase the tempo of the drill, requiring players to make quicker decisions and execute their skills under more pressure. Reducing the time to perform the skill will simulate game-like scenarios where quick thinking and swift movements are essential.Focus: Develops decision-making speed and the ability to execute skills under pressure while maintaining possession and composure.

title: Sociedad Long Ball SSG
instructions_setup: In this small-sided game, the focus is on a team's ability to handle long balls. Play starts with the goalkeeper, who distributes the ball to a center-back (CB) who is unopposed. The CB must then play a direct long ball into the opposition's box. From there, play becomes live, with both teams competing to score or defend until the ball goes out of play or a goal is scored. The drill simulates real-game scenarios where teams must deal with direct, long passes and quickly transition between defense and attack.This exercise improves the players' ability to handle aerial balls, win second balls, and transition quickly after receiving or playing long passes.
coaching_notes: • Winning Aerial Duels: Emphasize the importance of timing when dealing with long balls. Defenders and attackers should focus on winning headers or contesting the ball in the air with strong, well-timed jumps.• Quick Transition: Encourage players to transition quickly once the ball is played into the box. Both attackers and defenders should be aware of the potential for a fast counterattack after the long ball is played.• Communication and Positioning: Defenders must communicate with their goalkeeper and each other, organizing themselves to deal with the long pass effectively. Attackers should position themselves intelligently, anticipating where the ball will land and adjusting their runs accordingly.• Finishing Under Pressure: For attackers, it’s crucial to stay composed when receiving the ball in the box. Focus on making quick decisions and finishing efficiently under pressure, as they often won't have much time or space.
progression_one: Include a Second Phase After the Long Ball:Once the long ball is played, the defending team must try to clear the ball or counterattack by playing a quick ball out to the other side of the field, simulating a transition scenario.Focus: Enhances defensive organization and the ability to deal with long passes while also improving quick transitions and counterattacks.

title: Sociedad Making Forward Runs
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on encouraging players to make dynamic forward runs into the box, specifically targeting midfielders and opposite wingers. Play begins with a 4v2 setup in a deeper position, where the team in possession is tasked with progressing the ball and playing a forward pass into the central player, who is positioned between the lines.Once the central player receives the ball, they then play a pass to one of the wide players. This pass triggers the movement of the midfielder and the opposite winger, both of whom make forward runs into the box to create attacking options. The goal is to quickly overload the box and create goal-scoring opportunities.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Emphasize the importance of timing when making forward runs. Midfielders and wingers must time their movements well, ensuring they enter the box at the right moment to receive the ball and create space for themselves.• Quick Decision-Making: The central player must make quick decisions when receiving the ball, playing an accurate pass into the wide player, and quickly recognizing when to trigger the forward runs from the midfield and opposite winger.• Creating Overloads in the Box: The forward runs from the midfielder and winger should aim to create a numerical advantage in the box. This requires players to be aware of the defenders' positions and adjust their runs to maximize the attacking threat.• Off-the-Ball Movement: Encourage wide players to move quickly into space after receiving the ball, looking for opportunities to cross or combine with the arriving runners. Off-the-ball movement should be fluid and decisive, as timing is crucial to breaking down defensive lines.

title: Sociedad One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This individual technical practice focuses on refining core skills: first touch, passing accuracy, and close control dribbling. The player works back and forth with the coach in a flowing sequence that includes receiving a pass, controlling it cleanly, returning the ball with accuracy, and performing short, sharp dribbling movements before repeating. The continuous nature of the drill allows for repetition, rhythm, and refinement under increasing intensity.
coaching_notes: • Crisp, Accurate Passing – Focus on clean contact and proper weight when returning passes to maintain a consistent tempo throughout the drill.• Sharp First Touch – Encourage the player to take their first touch into space or prepare it for the next action efficiently, keeping it within immediate control.• Tight Dribbling Control – Use small, frequent touches with both feet during dribbling phases, keeping the ball close under pressure simulation.• Stay Light on Feet – Maintain an athletic, low stance throughout, allowing for quick adjustments between receiving, passing, and dribbling.

title: Spain 1v1 with Transitions
instructions_setup: In this drill, play starts with an attacker completing an unopposed finish into the goal. Once the finishing phase is completed, the attacker must immediately transition and sprint through the central gate located in the middle of the practice area (a hexagon). The transitioning player then attempts to prevent the new attacker coming from the opposite side from scoring.The practice area is set up as a hexagon with a gate at the center. The transitions are continuous, with players quickly shifting from offense to defense and back again, simulating a high-intensity, game-like scenario where players must be alert to both attacking and defensive responsibilities.
coaching_notes: • Transition Speed: Emphasize the importance of quick transitions between offense and defense. Players must immediately shift from their finishing phase to defensive duties, ensuring they cover the central gate and attempt to block the incoming attack.• Finishing Under Pressure: Focus on the attacker’s ability to finish with composure and accuracy despite the transition to the defensive phase. Encourage quick, sharp shots on goal to capitalize on limited time and space.• Defensive Awareness: Teach the defending player to quickly recognize the situation and sprint through the gate with urgency. Once through the gate, they must position themselves to block or intercept the new attacker's path to goal.• Continuous Intensity: The drill should maintain a high tempo, requiring players to stay engaged throughout the entire practice. Players need to be alert and stay mentally focused, as there’s little downtime between attacking and defending.

title: Spain 2 Phase Overloaded
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on a fast-paced 3v2 attacking phase, where the attacking team must quickly create a goal-scoring opportunity. Play starts with a pass from the coach into space, triggering the first 3v2 phase. The attacking team aims to move the ball quickly and efficiently, looking for an opportunity to score.As soon as the first 3v2 phase concludes (either through a goal or the ball going out of play), the coach plays a second ball into the field, initiating a second 3v2 phase in the opposite direction. The attacking team must quickly shift and adjust to the new phase of play, continuing to focus on speed and decision-making.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Emphasize the importance of fast transitions from offense to defense and vice versa. The attacking team must move the ball quickly to break down the defense, while the defenders need to react swiftly and organize themselves when the ball changes direction.• Attacking Speed: Encourage the attacking team to play at speed, focusing on quick passes and movement to overload the defenders. The attackers should look for opportunities to exploit space quickly before the defenders can react.• Decision Making in Numbers: Stress the importance of making quick decisions in the 3v2 scenario. The attacking team should focus on creating a numerical advantage, while the defenders need to stay organized and compact to limit the attacking options.• Anticipation and Communication: In the second 3v2 phase, attackers and defenders must communicate effectively and anticipate the ball’s movement. The attackers should constantly be on the move, and defenders should communicate to ensure they don’t get pulled out of position.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Box:Introduce a third defender in the final phase (the defending team will have 3 defenders instead of 2), requiring attackers to work together more effectively and create better overload situations.Focus: Increases the defensive pressure, forcing the attacking team to improve their combination play and decision-making under pressure.

title: Spain 3rd Man Finishing
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, four players are positioned in a diamond shape on the edge of the penalty area. The drill focuses on quick passing combinations and movement to create shooting opportunities. Players work through various combinations, ensuring that all four players are involved in the build-up before a shot on goal.The ball is played between the players in different sequences, such as one-touch passes, wall passes, or quick give-and-go’s. After completing the combination, the player receiving the final ball takes a shot at goal. This drill emphasizes precise passing, movement off the ball, and clinical finishing.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations: Focus on quick, one-touch passes to maintain the speed of play and break down the defensive line. Encourage players to keep the ball moving at a fast tempo to create space for the final shot.• Movement Off the Ball: Emphasize the importance of players moving into space after making a pass. Players should be proactive, constantly looking for an opportunity to receive the ball or create a passing lane for their teammate.• Finishing: Encourage players to focus on composure and accuracy when taking the shot. Players should vary their finishing techniques, such as placing the ball in the corners or using quick reactions for volleys and first-time shots.• Timing of Runs: Timing is key in this drill. Players must time their runs into the box and receive the ball in stride, which will help them create better shooting angles and avoid being caught offside.
progression_one: Add Pressure from a Defender:Introduce a defender who starts at a distance and closes down the player receiving the ball for the final shot. This forces the attacker to take quicker decisions, improve their shooting under pressure, and execute a better finish.Focus: Improves the attacking team’s ability to deal with defensive pressure and take shots with precision under time constraints.
progression_two: Vary the Passing Combinations:Change the passing combinations so that players are forced to use different techniques and engage in more dynamic movements. For example, include diagonal passes, through balls, or flicks to increase the complexity of the drill.Focus: Develops versatility in attacking play, encouraging players to be creative and use different passing techniques to create goal-scoring opportunities.

title: Spain Breaking Lines
instructions_setup: This possession transfer drill focuses on improving players’ ability to operate between lines and find pockets of space to receive the ball. The practice involves three teams of five players each. The team in possession must make a minimum of five passes before attempting to switch the play. The key rule is that possession must go through one of the three players located along the central line before switching, ensuring they pass behind the two defending players who are screening the central line. This encourages players to move intelligently between the lines to maintain possession and facilitate attacking play.
coaching_notes: • Movement Between Lines: Emphasize the importance of players moving between the lines to create passing options. Players should constantly be scanning the field and making runs into space to receive the ball, keeping the flow of possession smooth and consistent.• Quick Decision Making: Encourage quick, intelligent decisions when switching the play. Players should focus on receiving the ball in open space and looking to progress it with minimal touches, helping to maintain tempo and fluidity.• Central Line Usage: Highlight the importance of using the central line effectively. The central players must stay aware of the defensive pressure and offer themselves as an option to receive the ball behind the screening defenders, making sure they create passing lanes that help the team progress.• Defensive Screening Awareness: Train the defenders to remain disciplined in screening the central line, preventing easy passes into the central players. Defenders should communicate and adjust their positioning based on the movement of the attacking players and the ball.
progression_one: Increase the Passing Requirements:Increase the number of passes the team in possession must complete before switching the play (e.g., 7 or 10 passes). This forces players to be more patient, keeping possession for longer periods and requiring more movement and support to maintain fluidity in the attack.Focus: Helps develop patience in possession, encouraging players to work together and create additional space before attempting the switch.

title: Spain Build Up v Press
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing the team’s ability to play out from the back and progress the ball up the field, creating attacking opportunities. Play begins with the goalkeeper distributing the ball to the team in possession, who must work the ball forward and score in one of the three mini goals located on the halfway line. The attacking team is encouraged to pass through the defensive lines and use possession to break the opposition’s defensive structure.If the defending team wins possession, they must immediately transition into a counterattack. This drill simulates real match situations where possession is won or lost quickly and the team must adapt to both attacking and defending principles.
coaching_notes: • Building from the Back: Emphasize the importance of playing out from the back with composure. The defenders and goalkeeper must work together, using short, accurate passes to progress the ball and avoid being trapped by the opposition’s press.• Spatial Awareness: Players must constantly scan for space and support options when playing out from the back. The midfielders should position themselves between the lines to offer passing lanes and facilitate ball progression forward.• Quick Transition: Once the ball is won by the defending team, the transition to attack must be quick and direct. Defenders should look to exploit the opposition’s disorganization and attack with speed to catch the opponent off guard.• Defensive Shape: Defenders must be aware of their positioning when the ball is lost. They should quickly recover to prevent a counterattack and work together to block passing lanes while maintaining a compact shape.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for Scoring:Introduce a time limit for the attacking team to score once the ball is played out from the back. This forces the team to work efficiently and decisively in their build-up, ensuring they don't waste time when advancing up the field.Focus: Develops decision-making and urgency in the attacking phase, encouraging the players to combine quickly and look for scoring opportunities.

title: Spain Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This drill incorporates both technical skill development and fitness by combining a 2v2 small-sided game with shuttle runs. The drill starts with two players on each team playing a 2v2 match on one side of the grid, while the other side consists of 4 players completing shuttle runs. The aim is to work on both the game-related skills in the small-sided match and the physical conditioning through the shuttle runs.Once a goal is scored in the 2v2 match, the teams switch zones. The players who were playing in the 2v2 now move to the shuttle run area, while the players who were doing shuttle runs switch to the 2v2 game. This ensures that all players are involved in both attacking/defending and fitness aspects of the practice.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision Making: In the 2v2 match, players need to make quick decisions in tight spaces, using short, accurate passes to break down the defense. Encourage players to be creative and look for quick combinations with their teammate.• Movement Off the Ball: Players should focus on their off-the-ball movements, making runs into space to receive passes and create options for their teammate. This helps improve positioning and awareness.• Shuttle Run Intensity: During the shuttle runs, players should focus on maintaining a high level of intensity and speed. Remind them to recover quickly between each shuttle and transition efficiently from sprinting to the next task.• Managing Fatigue: The transition between the 2v2 and shuttle runs should be swift, allowing players to experience both high-intensity periods and skill-building moments. Encourage players to manage their fatigue, as this drill challenges their physical and mental endurance.
progression_one: Increase the Goal Scoring Requirement:Set a requirement that a team must score two goals before switching zones. This will add a competitive element to the 2v2 game and encourage players to focus on both the attacking and defensive aspects of the small-sided game.Focus: Encourages consistency in attack and defense, requiring players to maintain focus on their technical execution for a longer period.
progression_two: Add Defenders to the Shuttle Run Area:Introduce two defenders to the shuttle run area who will try to intercept or challenge the shuttle runners. The runners must still complete the shuttle runs but now have to navigate around defenders. This adds a challenge to the fitness aspect, simulating game-like pressure while improving conditioning.Focus: Develops physical conditioning under pressure, improving players' ability to perform fitness tasks while under defensive pressure.

title: Spain Overlap & Passing Activation
instructions_setup: This unopposed drill focuses on improving technical passing and movement off the ball, specifically through overlapping runs. Players work in pairs, passing the ball to each other while completing overlapping runs. The pattern is designed to help players develop their passing accuracy, timing, and decision-making, while also improving their fitness through continuous movement.The drill starts with two players at one end of the field, passing the ball back and forth. As the ball is passed, the player without the ball makes an overlapping run, receiving the ball back on the run to continue the sequence. Once the ball has traveled to the opposite end, the next pair of players will start the same pattern, working in the opposite direction. The practice continues with alternating pairs, ensuring players focus on both their passing technique and movement.
coaching_notes: • Pass with Precision: Encourage players to focus on passing with accuracy, especially when delivering the ball for the overlapping run. The ball should be played into space, allowing the player making the run to receive it comfortably.• Timing of Overlapping Runs: The player making the overlapping run must time their movement well to receive the ball at the right moment. This ensures the run is effective and the player can continue the flow of the drill without interruption.• Body Shape for Receiving: Players receiving the ball should open their body to make the pass easier and prepare for a quick touch into space. Emphasize the importance of being prepared to receive the ball on the move.• Constant Movement: Encourage players to stay active throughout the drill. Once the ball is passed, players should move quickly to support their partner and be ready for the next pass. This keeps the tempo high and mimics real game situations.
progression_one: Increase the Pace:Increase the tempo of the drill, requiring quicker passes and faster overlapping runs. This will improve the players' ability to execute the pattern at a higher speed, simulating match conditions.Focus: Improves passing speed, timing, and movement under pressure.
progression_two: Add a Dribble and Pass Element:Before the overlap, the player in possession of the ball must take one or two dribbles before passing. This progression forces the player to make quick decisions on when to pass and when to take on an opponent, improving dribbling under pressure and decision-making.Focus: Encourages dribbling skills and decision-making when progressing the ball.

title: Stockholm 2 Phase 2 Ended Finishing
instructions_setup: This dynamic finishing drill features two teams working simultaneously on opposite ends of the pitch, mirroring each other’s movements. Each player starts by dribbling up and around a pole, focusing on close ball control and sharp turns before shooting unopposed into the main goal. Immediately after their first shot, the player quickly turns and receives a pass to finish with a second shot into the opposite goal.Because both players operate at the same time on either end, both goalkeepers remain actively involved throughout the drill, ensuring constant shooting practice and goalkeeper engagement. This setup encourages quick transitions, consistent finishing practice, and sustained focus over two successive phases.
coaching_notes: • Encourage tight ball control and sharp dribbling around the pole – Players should focus on close touches, precise footwork, and maintaining speed and balance while under slight fatigue.• Stress the importance of quick, accurate finishing on both shots – Composure and proper technique are crucial to convert opportunities efficiently under time pressure and after intense effort.• Promote sharp awareness and body positioning when receiving the second pass – Effective first touches and good posture set up quality shooting opportunities immediately after turning sharply.• Emphasise continuous intensity and focus throughout both phases – Players need to maintain high concentration and mental resilience to execute back-to-back finishing effectively with minimal rest.
progression_one: Introduce a passive defender applying light pressure after the pole dribbleThis increases difficulty by encouraging better shielding, quicker decision-making, and improved composure under mild defensive pressure to simulate game-like scenarios.Focus: Develops ball control under pressure, improves quick thinking, and builds confidence in tight finishing scenarios with realistic contest.
progression_two: Add a time limit for completing both phases of the drillThis encourages players to increase tempo, improve cardiovascular fitness, and maintain accuracy under growing physical and mental fatigue during finishing practice.Focus: Enhances stamina, speed of execution, and technical precision during high-intensity finishing sequences requiring sharpness under fatigue.

title: Stockholm Chip It Races
instructions_setup: This fun and fast-paced warm-up game features two teams racing head-to-head on a small-sided pitch. Each team works together to complete a specific passing combination before attempting to chip the ball over one mini goal and into the opposing team’s mini goal. The challenge lies in balancing speed and precision, as teams must execute quick, accurate passes while moving rapidly to outpace their opponents.Teams earn one point for every successful chipped goal scored, encouraging competitive intensity and teamwork. The drill promotes sharp technical skills, quick decision-making, and effective communication under fun, game-like pressure, setting a lively tone for the session ahead.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise the balance between speed and precision during passing – Players should focus on accurate, well-weighted passes while maintaining high tempo and intelligent movement off the ball.• Encourage quick communication and teamwork – Clear verbal and non-verbal cues help coordinate timing, positioning, and anticipate teammates’ next moves effectively.• Stress proper technique and timing when chipping the ball – Players must use the correct weight, trajectory, and body positioning to successfully chip the ball over the mini goal.• Promote competitive spirit while maintaining fair play – Healthy competition increases intensity, focus, and motivation while ensuring respect and sportsmanship throughout.
progression_one: Reduce the time allowed to complete the passing combinationThis increases intensity and forces quicker decision-making, sharper execution, and mental focus under increased pressure.Focus: Develops speed of play, mental sharpness, spatial awareness, and technical accuracy in tight time frames.
progression_two: Require teams to complete an additional pass before chipping the ballThis adds complexity to the passing combination, requiring better teamwork, ball control, and patience during build-up play.Focus: Enhances passing precision, spatial awareness, decision-making, and patience in structured attacking sequences.

title: Stockholm Finishing Under Pressure 1.0
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass across the grid to an attacker who can take their first touch either up or down toward one of the two main goals. The defender who played the initial pass immediately sprints to apply pressure on the attacker, aiming to disrupt their rhythm and decision-making. This simulates realistic game pressure and challenges the attacker’s composure and ball control under defensive pressure.Inside both the top and bottom zones, a teammate of the attacker is positioned to receive a quick 1-2 combination pass. The attacker must execute this one-two link effectively before finishing by scoring in the respective main goal. This drill encourages sharp passing, quick movement, and precise finishing, while the defender works on closing down space rapidly and timing their pressure to force mistakes.
coaching_notes: • Encourage attackers to use their first touch to create space and control direction – This allows better execution of the 1-2 combination under intense pressure from defenders.• Stress defenders must sprint quickly to apply immediate pressure – Timely closing down reduces attacker’s options and forces hurried, less effective decisions.• Promote quick, accurate 1-2 passing between attacker and teammate – Sharp, well-timed combinations open critical scoring opportunities despite tight defensive attention.• Emphasise composure and precision when finishing – Attackers must stay calm and strike accurately despite aggressive pressure from the defender closing in.
progression_one: Limit attackers to two touches during the 1-2 combinationThis forces quicker decision-making and sharper execution in tight spaces.Focus: Develops technical precision, speed of play, and ability to perform under realistic pressure.
progression_two: Add a second defender to increase pressure during the finishing phaseThe additional defender creates a more challenging environment, encouraging attackers to improve their awareness, movement, and composure.Focus: Builds mental toughness, spatial awareness, and improves finishing skills under intense defensive pressure.

title: Stockholm Finishing Under Pressure 2.0
instructions_setup: In this finishing under pressure drill, play begins with a horizontal pass into a server or coach positioned centrally. The coach then plays a first-time pass through two mannequins to simulate a defensive line, with the attacker timing their run to break onto the ball and finish on goal.A defender starts five yards behind the attacker and can chase immediately once the pass is made, applying pressure from behind. This forces the attacker to finish under realistic pressure while maintaining control, composure, and technique in front of goal.
coaching_notes: • Focus on the attacker’s timing of the run – They must remain onside, explode through the mannequins, and meet the ball with good body shape and momentum.• Emphasise composed finishing under pressure – Attackers should stay calm, choose the right surface to strike with, and keep their head over the ball when shooting.• Defender must apply intelligent pressure from behind – Sprinting recovery, using body contact legally, and forcing the attacker onto their weaker side are key principles.• Highlight the quality of the coach’s pass – It must split the mannequins cleanly, replicate game-realistic tempo, and arrive at the correct angle and speed for the attacker.
progression_one: Add a second defender recovering from a different angleIntroduce another defender starting 8–10 yards wide, creating pressure from a diagonal line. This adds complexity and forces attackers to make quicker decisions under layered defensive stress.Focus: Encourages attackers to scan and adapt quickly, promoting sharper movement and varied finishing techniques under changing angles of pressure.
progression_two: Vary service to create unpredictabilityAllow the coach to vary the weight, angle, or timing of the through pass. Some passes should force the attacker to adjust body shape, take a touch, or strike first-time from awkward positions.Focus: Improves striker adaptability, reinforces body positioning, and demands cleaner finishing from different setups under high pressure.

title: Stockholm Inverted Winger Into 4v3
instructions_setup: In this overloaded attacking practice, play begins with an unopposed passing combination involving central players and a wide player. The ball is worked into the winger, who inverts their run inside from the flank to trigger a 4v3 attacking phase toward the main goal. This movement encourages fluid build-up play, intelligent positioning, and quick combination passing in the final third.The defending team must work cohesively to delay and disrupt the overload. If they win possession, they can immediately transition and break out toward two mini goals positioned on the opposite side of the grid. This provides an opportunity to develop quick counter-attacking instincts and decision-making under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise the timing and angles of the initial combination – Clean, well-timed passes help create rhythm and prepare the wide player to receive on the move and attack space centrally.• Encourage the winger to drive inward with purpose – Their first touch and body shape should allow for quick penetration, drawing defenders and creating space for teammates.• Promote intelligent movement from supporting attackers – Players must read the play and adjust positions to offer angles, receive under pressure, and exploit the overload.• Focus on compact, disciplined defending from the three defenders – Defensive shape, communication, and delaying tactics are key to dealing with the numerical disadvantage effectively.
progression_one: Add a recovering defender to create a delayed 4v4Introduce a recovering fourth defender who starts behind the play, arriving late into the phase to balance numbers after a short delay. This tests attackers’ urgency and ability to exploit overloads quickly.Focus: Improves attacking speed, recognition of momentary advantages, and forces defenders to recover intelligently under pressure.
progression_two: Add touch limits for attackers during overloadLimit attackers to a maximum of two or three touches each to encourage faster decision-making, cleaner technical execution, and sharper interplay under pressure.Focus: Enhances tempo of play, supports quicker ball circulation, and challenges players to combine efficiently in tight spaces.

title: Stockholm Line Breaking Finishing
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, players work on breaking defensive lines by passing between four mannequins set up to simulate a back four. A supporting striker makes a well-timed run beyond the mannequins to receive and finish in a 1v0 situation. The drill is designed to replicate attacking movements and decision-making when running in behind.The passer alternates between three available passing gaps between the mannequins to vary the direction and angle of the final ball. This variation encourages different types of movement from the striker, who must read the pass, adjust their run, and finish with speed and precision. The drill helps sharpen timing, off-the-ball movement, and clinical finishing under minimal pressure.
coaching_notes: • Focus on the weight and accuracy of the pass – It should split the mannequins cleanly, arrive with proper pace, and guide the striker into a shooting stride.• Encourage explosive movement from the striker – Sharp sprints, curved runs, and quick acceleration help break defensive lines and simulate match-relevant situations.• Emphasise body shape before finishing – Strikers must open up, prepare the touch early, and use minimal steps before executing the shot on goal.• Vary finishes based on angle – Depending on which gap is used, players should choose different techniques (inside foot, laces, across goal) to improve versatility and decision-making.
progression_one: Allow strikers to start from different zonesStrikers can begin runs from varying starting positions (wider or deeper) to attack different passing angles. This creates more game-relevant movement patterns and tests their ability to adapt to different through balls.Focus: Enhances timing, awareness of space, and ability to adjust body shape to shoot effectively from multiple positions.

title: Stockholm Protecting Possession Technical
instructions_setup: This technical practice focuses on protecting possession under pressure in a central zone. A pass is played into the middle of the grid, where a player must receive the ball while facing moderate pressure from behind. The player’s objective is to shield the ball effectively, maintain control, and then play a precise pass out to one of the four designated corner zones.This drill develops players’ ability to use their body to protect the ball, improve first touch awareness, and execute accurate outlet passes under realistic game pressure. The moderate defensive pressure challenges players to make smart decisions quickly while retaining possession and helping their team build play from tight areas.
coaching_notes: • Stress the importance of strong body positioning when receiving under pressure – Players should use their arms and hips effectively to shield the ball and create space from defenders.• Encourage a calm and controlled first touch to set up the outlet pass – A well-weighted touch helps maintain possession and enables smoother passing options.• Promote awareness of available passing lanes before receiving – Players must scan and anticipate teammates’ movements to quickly choose the best outlet.• Emphasise quick, accurate passing to the corners after protecting possession – Speed and precision in the pass reduce pressure and aid effective team progression.
progression_one: Increase defensive pressure intensityApply closer, more aggressive pressure on the receiver to improve shielding skills, quicker decision-making, and composure in tighter possession situations.Focus: Builds stronger ball protection, sharper awareness, and faster technical execution under high-pressure conditions.
progression_two: Add a touch limit on the receiverRestrict the receiver to two touches maximum before passing out to the corners to develop faster ball control, quicker passing decisions, and more efficient possession retention.Focus: Enhances technical precision, decision speed, and tactical awareness in pressured possession scenarios.

title: Stockholm Technical Penetration Warm Up
instructions_setup: This fast-paced technical activation works on sharp 1-2 passing combinations followed by quick finishing into mini goals. Play flows continuously from one end of the grid to the other using two balls sequentially, encouraging players to maintain high intensity, quick decision-making, and precise execution throughout.Players pair up to practice crisp one-two passes to break defensive lines before finishing by scoring into a designated mini goal. As soon as one sequence ends with a finish, the next ball is played from the opposite end to keep the rhythm and focus sharp.
coaching_notes: • Encourage players to use sharp, well-weighted passes in the 1-2 combinations – Precise passing enables smoother ball progression and better timing for receiving players.• Stress the importance of quick, intelligent movement off the ball – Effective runs create space and options for passing, increasing the chance to break through.• Promote accurate and composed finishing into the mini goals – Players should focus on technique and timing, maintaining composure even under fatigue.• Emphasise continuous communication between players – Clear signals help coordinate passes and runs, ensuring seamless flow in the end-to-end sequences.

title: Stoke 1v1 & 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on individual defending and attacking in 1v1 situations, followed by a transition to a 2v2 scenario. The players will develop their ability to handle direct duels with an opponent and transition seamlessly into a more complex attacking scenario. The drill promotes both individual defending skills and team play in overloaded situations.The drill begins with the first defender playing a diagonal pass to an attacker, initiating the first 1v1. After completing the 1v1, the second defender plays a similar diagonal pass to the second attacker, starting the second 1v1. Once both 1v1s are complete, the defending team will pass to the attackers, who now transition into a 2v2 situation in the same area, working together to try and score.
coaching_notes: • 1v1 Defending Focus: In the 1v1 scenarios, defenders should focus on maintaining good positioning and timing their challenges well. Emphasize keeping their body between the attacker and the goal, using good footwork to block the attacker's path.• Quick Decision Making: Attackers in the 1v1 phase should focus on using their skills to beat the defender with quick changes of direction or acceleration. Encourage creativity in the attacker's movement to open up space for a shot or pass.• Seamless Transition to 2v2: After completing the 1v1s, attackers must quickly transition into a 2v2 scenario. Encourage them to communicate with their teammate, focusing on movement off the ball to create space and options for the player in possession.• Compact Defending in 2v2: In the 2v2 phase, defenders must work together to stay compact and limit space for the attackers. Emphasize the importance of positioning, covering, and anticipating the attackers' movements to force them into less dangerous areas.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player:Introduce a neutral attacker to the 2v2 phase to create a 3v2 overload for the attacking team. This progression will challenge defenders to work on their communication and organization when facing an overload.Focus: Helps defenders improve their ability to cope with overloads and work as a unit.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit:Limit the amount of time attackers have to score in the 2v2 scenario. This encourages quick decision-making and promotes urgency in both attacking and defending phases.Focus: Improves reaction time, decision-making under pressure, and quick transitions.

Encourage players to keep the ball moving at a fast tempo to create space for the final shot.• Movement Off the Ball: Emphasize the importance of players moving into space after making a pass. Players should be proactive, constantly looking for an opportunity to receive the ball or create a passing lane for their teammate.• Finishing: Encourage players to focus on composure and accuracy when taking the shot. Players should vary their finishing techniques, such as placing the ball in the corners or using quick reactions for volleys and first-time shots.• Timing of Runs: Timing is key in this drill. For example, include diagonal passes, through balls, or flicks to increase the complexity of the drill.Focus: Develops versatility in attacking play, encouraging players to be creative and use different passing techniques to create goal-scoring opportunities.

title: Stoke Build Through the Thirds
instructions_setup: This drill emphasizes building play through the thirds of the pitch, working on creating overloads in each zone to progress the ball effectively. It focuses on decision-making, timing of passes, and creating space for the player on the ball. The drill allows players to develop their ability to transition from defense to attack while maintaining possession and breaking down opposition lines.Play starts in the first zone, where the team in possession has a 4v3 overload. Once the ball is successfully progressed into the central zone, one player from the first zone can join to form a 4v3 overload in the central area. Upon reaching the end zone, the team can once again overload with a 4v3. The ball must be moved from end to end, ensuring progression through each phase. If the defending team wins possession, they should look to counter and score into any of the four mini-goals placed in the end zones.
coaching_notes: • Maintaining Width: The attacking team should stretch the field and maintain width throughout the build-up phase, creating space for the ball carrier to pass or drive forward.• Quick Transitions: Emphasize the quick transition from one zone to the next. As soon as possession is won, play should move quickly to the next area with fast and direct passing.• Overloading to Create Space: Players should be aware of the overload opportunities in each zone and work on quick support to help maintain the advantage and keep the attacking flow going.• Compact Defending: The defending team should remain compact, limiting space and forcing the attacking team to play wide or back. Encourage good pressing as soon as possession is won.
