progression_one: Limit Time in Each Zone:To increase intensity, limit the amount of time the attacking team can spend in each zone. This forces quicker thinking, faster passes, and more dynamic movement.Focus: Encourages quicker decision-making and improved passing speed under pressure.

title: Stoke Passing & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This passing and mastery drill focuses on improving players’ passing and receiving techniques, while also incorporating conditioning. The players will work on various types of passes, such as short passes, long passes, and through balls, while moving between designated poles. This practice helps develop both technical and fitness levels simultaneously by focusing on receiving and distributing under pressure.The drill setup consists of 4 poles, with 3 players occupying a pole each, and 1 spare pole. The players positioned at the bottom poles work between their designated pole and the empty pole. These players will be required to receive passes from the two players positioned at the top poles, who will work the ball back and forth. The players at the bottom should focus on moving quickly and positioning themselves to receive the ball while maintaining intensity throughout the drill.
coaching_notes: • Fluid Movement: Players must constantly adjust their positioning between the poles, using quick directional changes to receive and pass accurately under pressure.• Passing Accuracy: Ensure players are focusing on proper passing technique. Passes should be weighted correctly, and players must communicate effectively with their teammates.• Conditioning Focus: Emphasize the importance of maintaining a high work rate and moving quickly between poles to develop fitness as well as technical skills.• Receiving Under Pressure: Players at the bottom must work on receiving the ball with a good first touch, making sure they can control and distribute quickly, even when fatigued.
progression_one: Increase the Distance Between Poles:Increase the distance between the poles to make the passing and receiving more challenging. This forces the players to adjust their passing and movement to maintain effective communication and ball control over longer distances.Focus: Develops longer passes and encourages players to improve their fitness by covering more ground during the drill.

title: Sunderland 2 Ways 2v2's
instructions_setup: In this 2v2 practice, players will continuously attack in a 2v2 format, with the direction of play switching after every phase. The practice is timed, with a short rest period between each rep. The practice should be scored, and the team with the most points at the end is the winner. This practice is a great arrival activity or a main part of the session, promoting quick transitions and attacking combinations.
coaching_notes: • Quick TransitionsEncourage players to quickly switch their mindset between attacking and defending. After a goal or a turnover, players should be ready to immediately transition into the new direction of play. The quicker the transition, the more successful they’ll be in exploiting the opponent’s moment of unpreparedness.• Attacking CombinationsIn the 2v2 format, players should focus on quick passing combinations and movement off the ball to create space. Encourage attackers to work together, using quick give-and-go plays, one-touch passes, and overlapping runs to break down the defense.• Defensive Awareness and CompactnessWhen defending in a 2v2, players must communicate and stay compact. Encourage defenders to apply pressure quickly on the ball carrier, forcing them to make a rushed decision. The defenders should also maintain awareness of the second attacker and try to force them into a poor position, limiting space and options for the attackers.• Finishing with ComposureWhen the attacking team gets into shooting positions, players should focus on composure and technique. Encourage attackers to choose the best option (e.g., finishing low and to the corners, or passing to an unmarked teammate) rather than rushing the shot. Good decision-making in the final third is crucial to maximizing scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Add Neutral PlayersIntroduce neutral players who can act as support for the attacking team, creating a temporary 3v2 in the attacking phase.Focus: This progression allows the attacking team to have more options and focus on creating overloads to break the defense.
progression_two: Limit Touches for AttackersLimit the attacking players to 2 or 3 touches maximum before they must shoot or pass.Focus: This progression speeds up the game, forcing players to make quicker decisions, improving their technical ability and attacking speed.

title: Sunderland Attacking 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on quick transitions, 1v1 attacking, and defending under pressure. Both the attacker and defender will start by sprinting around a pole before entering the field of play. Once they enter the field, the coach serves a ball into the attacker, who then plays out a 1v1 scenario against the defender. This drill emphasizes explosive movements, quick thinking, and finishing under pressure.Both players must react quickly and make immediate decisions upon entering the field, with the attacking player aiming to score and the defender working to stop them. The drill also includes a sprinting element, which keeps players engaged and sharp during transitions.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reactions: Both attacker and defender must focus on explosive movements, reacting to the coach’s ball serve quickly and efficiently.• 1v1 Decision Making: Attackers should focus on their first touch and dribbling skills, looking for a chance to break the defender’s line. Defenders need to maintain close pressure and force the attacker into less dangerous areas.• Finishing Under Pressure: Attackers must focus on their finishing skills in tight situations, while defenders should work on positioning and timing their challenges to prevent a goal.• Transition Speed: Whether attacking or defending, players need to be aware of the transition to the next phase (sprinting back to the pole) after a goal or possession win, keeping the intensity high throughout.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a second defender to create a 2v1 situation for the attacker. This will force the attacker to make faster decisions and improve their ability to finish under more defensive pressure.Focus: Enhances decision-making and quick ball movement under increased defensive pressure.
progression_two: Add Time Limit for Reactions:After a goal or possession win, introduce a time limit for how quickly players need to return to the pole and get ready for the next phase. This will emphasize conditioning and quick recovery after each play.Focus: Builds endurance and forces players to recover quickly, maintaining intensity throughout the drill.

title: Sunderland Breakout Rondo
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a double-gridded 5v2 rondo. The team out of possession is attempting to regain the ball or knock it into the outer grid. Once the ball is won or successfully passed into the outer grid, the defending team transitions into defensive players, and the practice expands into an 8v5 rondo. The team that was in possession now has more space to work with, and they aim to maintain possession and keep the ball moving efficiently.
coaching_notes: • Transition Speed & AwarenessThe key to this practice is how quickly players transition from defending to attacking. Once the ball is won or passed into the outer grid, defending players must immediately shift into offensive positions and support the new attackers. Encourage fast thinking and rapid transition to capitalize on the overload in the larger grid.• Focus on Movement & SupportIn the 8v5 phase, it’s essential for players to provide continuous support for the ball carrier. Emphasize intelligent off-the-ball movement to ensure passing lanes are always open, allowing the team to maintain fluidity and possession. The five defenders in the larger grid should look to press and close down passing options, creating a more challenging environment.• Ball Speed & Decision-MakingIn both the 5v2 and 8v5 phases, the team in possession should focus on quick, sharp passing and excellent decision-making. Encourage players to move the ball efficiently while scanning for the best option. This will help them progress the ball effectively while avoiding being trapped by the defenders.• Defensive Pressure & Pressing TriggersThe defending team needs to work together to regain possession. Remind them to focus on pressing as a unit, not allowing too much space for the attacking team to exploit. Use pressing triggers (e.g., poor first touch, excessive dribbling, or a poor pass) to initiate defensive pressure. If they successfully win the ball, they must transition quickly into the 8v5 to maintain defensive balance.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Attacking TeamTo increase difficulty, limit the number of touches each player can take in the 8v5 phase (e.g., two-touch). This forces the attacking team to play at a faster tempo and improves their passing and decision-making under pressure.Focus: This progression encourages quicker ball movement and sharper decision-making under increased pressure.
progression_two: Add More DefendersIncrease the number of defenders in the 8v5 phase to make it more challenging for the attacking team. For example, move to a 7v6 or even an 8v7 scenario.Focus: This progression enhances the defensive team’s ability to press effectively while pushing the attacking team to play even more quickly and cohesively.

title: Sunderland Build & Progress Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo starts with a 4v2 setup, with the goalkeeper involved for the team in possession. The team building possession aims to progress the ball through a narrower central channel and into the opposite side of the grid, where two out-of-possession players will follow to apply pressure. To facilitate this build-up, one player from the possession team can drop into the central grid to receive the ball and either help progress the play or drag the defending player out of position. This creates space for forward-breaking passes through the central channel.
coaching_notes: • Build-Up Play with the GoalkeeperEncourage the team in possession to use the goalkeeper effectively as a support player in their build-up phase. The goalkeeper should be comfortable with short passes and help to facilitate play, ensuring the ball is moved out of pressure while maintaining possession. This will allow the team to keep control and make intelligent forward passes.• Movement to Create Passing LanesThe player dropping into the central grid needs to have excellent timing and movement. Their role is to create space by pulling the defenders out of position and facilitating the progression of the ball through the central channel. Focus on making sure this player is always aware of the positioning of the defenders and creates options for their teammates through clever, well-timed runs.• Utilize the Central Channel EffectivelyThe key objective of this practice is to progress the ball through the central channel. Encourage quick, decisive passes and support play to break the defensive line. Players should aim to make forward-thinking passes through the central grid, exploiting the space left when defenders are drawn out.• Pressure After Ball LossOnce the ball is played into the opposite side of the grid and defenders press, remind the attacking team to maintain composure and look for quick, efficient solutions. Encourage the team to stay compact and continue passing and moving, especially under pressure, to either retain possession or transition quickly into the next phase of play.
progression_one: Add More DefendersIntroduce additional defenders into the central grid to increase pressure on the possession team. For example, change to a 4v3 or 5v3 setup in the build-up phase.Focus: This will force the possession team to play more quickly, make quicker decisions, and become more efficient in their build-up play.
progression_two: Limit Touches for Possession TeamLimit the number of touches for the team in possession (e.g., 2 or 3 touches maximum). This forces faster ball movement, encouraging quicker decision-making and increasing the intensity of the practice.Focus: This progression improves the team’s ability to play under pressure and develop sharper passing combinations in tight spaces.

title: Sunderland Build Up Centrally
instructions_setup: In this practice, the possession team aims to build and finish the attack against a 2-2 defensive formation, replicating the two central midfielders and two centre forwards from a 4-4-2 structure. The attacking team works to progress the ball centrally, using passing and movement to break down the defense. If the defending players win possession, they can counter-attack into the main goal, with two extra wide players joining the attack to facilitate fast breaks and transitions.
coaching_notes: • Use of Central SpaceEncourage the possession team to focus on building play through the central channels. Players should look to create passing lanes and overload the middle of the pitch with quick, dynamic passing. Players should make runs off the ball to support the player on the ball, helping to maintain possession and unlock the defensive structure.• Combination Play Between Midfielders and ForwardsThe attacking team should look to use quick combinations between the central midfielders and forwards to break down the 2-2 defensive structure. Focus on sharp, one- or two-touch passing to progress the ball quickly and into dangerous areas. Encourage the forwards to drop deep to receive passes and link up with the midfield.• Defensive Transition and Counter-AttackWhen the defending team wins possession, the focus is on transitioning quickly into attack. Encourage the defending team to counter-attack with speed, making use of the two wide players to stretch the opposition and create overloads in the attack. The wide players should be looking to receive early passes to exploit space on the flanks.• Recognizing Defensive GapsThe attacking team must be aware of gaps in the defensive structure created by the 2-2 setup. Look for spaces between the midfielders and forwards, and exploit these openings with incisive passes. The central midfielders should aim to deliver passes into the feet of the forwards, or even play through balls into the space behind the defensive line.
progression_one: Add Pressure to Possession TeamAdd a third defender in the central zone to increase defensive pressure. This will force the possession team to move the ball faster and be more precise in their decision-making.Focus: This progression helps to develop the attacking team’s ability to play quickly under pressure and recognize opportunities to break down a tighter defensive structure.
progression_two: Limit Possession Team's TouchesLimit the number of touches each player can take (e.g., 2 touches maximum) to increase tempo and intensity in the practice.Focus: This forces quicker, sharper passing and movement, helping the team develop a faster build-up and more dynamic attacking play.

title: Sunderland Build Up Overloaded
instructions_setup: This drill simulates a pressured build-up from the goalkeeper, focusing on quick decision-making, passing under pressure, and finding space to progress the ball forward. Play starts with the goalkeeper passing to the center-back (CB), who is immediately under pressure from the central forward (CF). The CB must make a quick decision, passing to either the central midfielder (CM) or the right-back (RB), depending on the positioning of the second pressing player.Once the ball reaches the RB or CM, they must work together to create space and combine effectively to break the defensive line, ultimately aiming to score in the mini goals. This drill encourages precise passing and off-the-ball movement in a pressured environment.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision Making: The center-back must make a fast decision under pressure, deciding between the CM or RB based on the positioning of the second pressing player.• Spatial Awareness: The CM and RB must be aware of their positioning and work together to create space, making sure to support each other with effective runs and positioning.• Pass Accuracy Under Pressure: Players must focus on executing precise passes, even when under pressure from the pressing forward. The CB and the wide players (CM, RB) need to keep composure.• Combination Play: The CM and RB must focus on quick, one-touch passing and effective off-the-ball movement to break down the defensive setup and progress the ball forward.
progression_one: Add More Defenders:Introduce a second forward pressing the ball to make it 2v1 against the center-back. This forces quicker decision-making and increases pressure on the build-up.Focus: Enhances the ability to play out from pressure, creating better passing lanes and improving tactical awareness.
progression_two: Limit Time for Decisions:Limit the time the center-back has to make the decision of whom to pass to, encouraging quicker thinking and faster reactions in a high-pressure environment.Focus: Develops composure under pressure and helps players make faster, more effective decisions in the build-up phase.

title: Sunderland Double 2v1s
instructions_setup: This attacking practice is designed around two consecutive 2v1 scenarios, promoting quick decision-making and exploiting numerical advantages. The pitch is split into two horizontal zones. In each zone, there is one defender and two attackers. The attacking team must beat the first defender in Zone 1 before immediately transitioning into Zone 2 to create a goalscoring opportunity against the second defender. The drill runs continuously for a set period (e.g., 3–4 minutes) with the same two defenders working through fatigue and repeated pressure situations.
coaching_notes: • Overload Exploitation – Emphasize creating width and depth in the 2v1. Attackers should avoid being too narrow and must understand how to manipulate the defender’s positioning to create a passing or dribbling lane.• Speed of Play – Encourage quick, purposeful play to take advantage of the overload before the defender can recover or delay. The faster the attackers transition from Zone 1 to Zone 2, the greater their chance of success.• Decision-Making – Players must decide when to dribble, pass, or shoot based on the defender’s positioning. Promote scanning and early decision-making to keep the attack fluid.• Defensive Resilience – For the defenders, this drill builds stamina, composure under fatigue, and 1v2 defending skills like delaying, blocking passing lanes, and timing tackles.
progression_one: Live Defender RecoveryAfter the attackers pass into Zone 2, the defender from Zone 1 is allowed to recover and join the play, creating a 2v2 situation in the second zone.Focus:Improves attacking players’ ability to recognize transitions and make quicker decisions under increased defensive pressure.
progression_two: Limited Touches in Zone 1Limit attackers to a maximum of two touches each in the first zone, forcing quicker combinations and sharper movement.Focus:Increases tempo and challenges players to think and act faster while still executing quality passes and movements.

title: Sunderland Isolating Wide 1v1
instructions_setup: This attacking practice focuses on isolating the wide player in a 1v1 situation. Play starts with a switch of play to a wide player, who receives the ball in space. The wide player must then attack the space at speed, with the options to either create a crossing opportunity for teammates or find space to shoot on goal themselves.As the wide player advances, 3 players (including the central midfielder (CM), center forward (CF), and wide attacker (WI)) must make runs into the box, providing options for the cross or finish.The defending team consists of 3 players who start in a set position and must quickly slide and shift to put pressure on the receiving winger, aiming to block both shots and crosses.
coaching_notes: • Wide Player's Role – The wide player should focus on attacking the space with speed, either to get by their defender or create a passing opportunity for a cross. Encourage the wide player to be decisive in their actions, reading the defender’s position and choosing whether to take them on, cross, or shoot.• Movement from Teammates – The central midfielder, center forward, and wide attacker should focus on timing their runs into the box, attacking different areas (near-post, far-post, or edge of the box) depending on the type of cross. Encourage the attackers to make dynamic runs and create space for themselves to receive a pass or finish a cross.• Defensive Pressure – The defending players need to focus on closing down the wide player quickly and ensuring they do not get a free shot or cross. They should be prepared to shift and slide as the wide player progresses towards goal, preventing both crosses into the box and potential shots on goal.• Decision-Making – The wide player should develop the ability to read the game and make quick decisions based on the positioning of the defenders and the attackers making runs into the box. Knowing when to cross and when to shoot is key to creating effective attacks.
progression_one: Add Defensive PressureIntroduce a second defender to create a 2v1 situation against the wide player. The wide attacker will now have to deal with increased defensive pressure, making it more challenging to create a cross or shot.Focus:Improves the wide player’s decision-making and ability to beat multiple defenders, enhancing their ability to create under pressure.
progression_two: Add a GoalkeeperIncorporate a goalkeeper into the practice so that the wide player can shoot at goal after either taking on the defender or delivering a cross. The attackers should aim to finish any crosses or convert shots on goal while dealing with defensive pressure.Focus:Simulates real match scenarios where wide players must make decisions while under pressure and aim for a goal.Would you like this drill adjusted to fit into a larger Week 65 attacking session or tailored to work on specific aspects of wide play?

title: Sunderland Possession & Counter Press
instructions_setup: In this practice, the team in possession plays 6v4 and should attempt to make ‘x’ amount of passes for a point. The objective is to develop counter pressing abilities. If the defending team (4 players) wins possession, the 6 players must immediately counter press to prevent the defenders from scoring into any of the 4 mini goals. The defending team can use 2 end line players for support if they win possession, which emphasizes the need for a quick and intense counter press from the attacking team to avoid conceding.
coaching_notes: • Counter Pressing ReactionAs soon as possession is lost, the 6 attackers must immediately transition into a counter press, putting immediate pressure on the defenders and preventing easy progression. Encourage rapid movement to close passing lanes and force mistakes.• Intensity & Work RatePlayers must show a high level of intensity in their reaction to losing possession. The team in possession should not slow down the pace but continue pressing with urgency, anticipating and closing down spaces quickly.• Defensive Communication & PositioningWhen the defenders regain possession, the 6 attackers should be vocal and position themselves effectively to prevent the counter. Ensure that the defenders maintain good shape and communication when using the end line players to create overloads.• Compactness & Supporting the PressEncourage the 6 attackers to stay compact and work together when pressing. Players should cover each other’s space and limit passing options to force the defending team to play into pressure, reducing the opportunity for counter-attacks.
progression_one: Limited Touches for DefendersLimit the number of touches defenders can have to increase the pressure on the defending team. This makes it more difficult for them to play out and forces them into quicker decisions, thus improving the counter pressing intensity.Focus: This progression enhances the speed and effectiveness of the counter press.
progression_two: Additional End Line Player for AttackersIntroduce an extra neutral player for the attacking team who can help them maintain possession when under pressure. This creates a 7v4 scenario and gives the team in possession more space to work with, while encouraging the defending team to react even quicker when they regain possession.Focus: This progression helps improve the defending team's reaction time and speed in regaining control.

title: Sunderland Winger & CF Combinations
instructions_setup: This finishing drill focuses on a specific winger and centre forward (CF) combination play. The winger will receive the ball from deep, take a positive first touch inside, and play a pass to the centre forward. After completing the pass, the winger will make a blindside run behind the full back to receive the ball in space. The winger then attempts to finish from an angle.
coaching_notes: • Positive First Touch – Emphasize that the winger's first touch inside must be positive and decisive, aiming to move the ball away from pressure and create space for the inside pass to the centre forward.• Inside Pass Timing – The winger must time the pass to the centre forward well, ensuring that the ball is played with the correct weight and at the right moment to allow the CF to make a quick turn or shot.• Blindside Run – Encourage the winger to make a blindside run behind the full back, stressing the importance of timing and deception to beat the defender. The run should be quick and timed so that the winger can receive the ball in space without being tracked.• Finishing from the Angle – When receiving the ball from the CF, the winger should focus on finishing with composure. Depending on the angle, encourage the use of either a first-time shot or a controlled touch before finishing, making sure to aim for the far post or create the best angle to score.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender to pressure the winger and centre forward. This adds an element of defensive pressure, forcing the attackers to make quicker decisions and refine their combination play under match-like conditions.Focus: Builds the ability to execute the combination under pressure, simulating real game scenarios.
progression_two: Change the FinishAllow the winger to either finish with a shot or cross the ball to another attacking player in the box. This progression creates a more dynamic situation where the winger has multiple finishing options, helping them improve their decision-making in the final third.Focus: Expands the attacking options for the winger and CF combination, allowing players to adapt to different situations and increase their versatility in attack.

title: Sydney 4 Phase Finishing
instructions_setup: This 4-phase finishing practice allows a forward to develop their ability to finish on both feet. Two of the finishes come from through balls, where the forward must receive and finish on the half turn. The other two finishes come from cut-back zones.The forward is limited to 2 touches for each phase to encourage good movement, a positive first touch, and finishing at match speed.
coaching_notes: • Positive First Touch – Encourage the forward to take a positive, forward-moving first touch when receiving the ball, setting them up for a quick and decisive finish.• Finishing with Both Feet – Focus on developing the ability to finish on both feet. The forward should practice finishing from various angles and positions, ensuring they're comfortable shooting with either foot.• Timing & Movement – Emphasize the importance of timing runs into the box, especially when receiving through balls or anticipating cutbacks. The forward should be aware of their positioning in relation to the defenders and the ball.• Match Speed – Push the forward to maintain match speed throughout the practice, simulating the pace and intensity of a real game. The quicker the forward can execute the finish, the more effective the training will be.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender who will apply light pressure on the forward as they receive the ball and attempt the finish. This will simulate match situations where the forward is under some pressure when receiving and finishing.Focus: Improving finishing under pressure and maintaining composure with defenders nearby.
progression_two: Vary the Ball DeliveryVary the type of delivery for the through balls and cutbacks. Use a mixture of driven balls, chipped passes, and crosses to challenge the forward’s ability to finish from different types of service.Focus: Adapting finishing technique based on different ball deliveries.

title: Sydney Breaking Lines & Overloaded
instructions_setup: Play starts with 1 goalkeeper and 2 defenders building play and attempting to break the lines of a defending 3 players. If they are successful in breaking a line and progressing the ball into their attacking 3 players, a 3v2 attacking scenario plays out. Players are locked into their specific grids and are completely unopposed in the build-up phase. The attacking overloaded phase changes the practice to a fully opposed scenario.If the defending 3 successfully intercept the build-up or regain possession, they can attack quickly against the unbalanced build-up team.
coaching_notes: • Breaking Lines in Build-Up – The defenders should focus on breaking the opposition’s defensive lines with quick, sharp passes or intelligent movement. Encourage the goalkeeper to be involved in starting play from the back, playing short or long passes to the defenders.• Composure Under Pressure – During the 3v2 attacking scenario, emphasize quick decision-making and composure in the final third. Players should be patient, selecting the right moment to shoot or pass based on the defenders' positioning.• Wide Play – The attacking players should look to stretch the defense by using width. This will open up space in the middle for players to receive passes and exploit gaps in the defense.• Recovery Defending – If the defending team regains possession, encourage quick transitions to attack. They should look to exploit the imbalance in the build-up team, countering swiftly before the defensive shape can reset.
progression_one: Increase Defensive PressureIntroduce additional defenders to the build-up phase, forcing the team in possession to break more complex lines. This progression will test the defenders’ ability to remain composed under pressure and make quicker, sharper decisions.Focus: Improving the ability to break multiple lines under defensive pressure.
progression_two: 1v1 Defending ChallengeOnce the attacking team reaches the 3v2 phase, the defenders must engage in 1v1 duels to stop the attacking progress. This allows players to work on their individual defending skills and timing of tackles in an overloaded attacking situation.Focus: Enhancing 1v1 defending abilities in transition scenarios.

title: Sydney Breaking Lines & Switching
instructions_setup: This unopposed build-up practice allows players to develop their ability to play line-breaking passes and switch play. Both forward passes in this practice are angled, completing a switch of play and encouraging the central player to receive at angles that facilitate this switch.
coaching_notes: • Angle of Passes – Players should focus on playing the forward passes at sharp angles to break defensive lines. The receiving player must be positioned to facilitate an easy switch of play and must read the angle of the pass carefully.• Receiving at Angles – The central player receiving the ball should always aim to receive with an open body position, ready to play the switch pass quickly. This creates momentum and allows for a smoother transition to the opposite side.• Timing of the Pass – The timing of the line-breaking passes is crucial. The ball should be played when the receiving player is in the correct position to receive, preventing the pass from being intercepted or forced backward.• Speed of Play – Encourage quick play to transition the ball through the lines. Players should focus on executing quick, clean passes to maintain tempo and catch the defending team off guard.
progression_one: Add OpponentsIntroduce one or two passive defenders who will try to intercept or pressure the receiving players. This forces the attacking team to make quicker decisions and adapt to a more competitive scenario.Focus: Improving the ability to play under pressure while maintaining accuracy in line-breaking passes.
progression_two: Increase the DistanceIncrease the distance between the central player and the wide players to create more space for the pass. This allows players to focus more on accurate and long-range passes to switch play effectively.Focus: Enhancing the ability to execute longer, more precise line-breaking and switching passes.

title: Sydney Continuous 2v1 & Transitions
instructions_setup: This is a fun starter activity that allows players to work on dribbling and passing, both unopposed and in opposed 2v1 combinations. The central player, who plays a pass into one of the outer grids, will momentarily act as a defender in a 2v1 situation. The attacking 2 players attempt to combine and break out of the grid, transitioning back into the unopposed central zone.
coaching_notes: • Passing & Dribbling Combinations – Focus on quick, accurate passing and good movement off the ball. Encourage the attacking duo to work together, using short, sharp passes to break down the defender in the 2v1.• Decision Making in 2v1 – The player with the ball in the 2v1 situation should read the defender's position and decide whether to dribble, pass, or shoot based on the defender's actions. Encourage creativity and quick thinking.• Transition Speed – Once the attacking duo breaks out of the grid, they should transition back quickly into the central zone. Stress the importance of maintaining the pace of the game to keep the flow and intensity high.• Defensive Awareness – The central defender should be aware of their positioning in the 2v1 situation. Encourage them to close down space quickly but also read the attackers' intentions to avoid being easily bypassed.
progression_one: Additional DefendersIntroduce an additional defender into the outer grid to create a more challenging 2v2 scenario. This progression will help players develop their ability to work in slightly more pressured conditions while maintaining control and composure.Focus: Improving decision-making and passing under pressure in 2v1 situations.
progression_two: Timed TransitionMake the transitions from the outer grid to the central zone time-based, adding a sense of urgency. Players will now need to complete the 2v1 and transition back into the central zone within a set time, encouraging faster decision-making and movement.Focus: Enhancing speed of play and quick transitions in small-sided scenarios.

title: Sydney Fast Break Countering
instructions_setup: Play starts with a pass into one of two attackers, who are positioned in a 2v1 scenario. Once either of the attackers takes their first touch, play is live. With 2 recovering defenders, the aim is to counter-attack quickly and efficiently to take advantage of the overload. The attacker who played the initial pass also becomes live, meaning the 2v1 has the potential to become a 2v3 or 3v3 depending on the situation.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making – Encourage attackers to make quick decisions once the ball is received, whether to shoot, pass, or continue dribbling. The goal is to exploit the overload before the defending team can recover fully.• Speed of Play – Focus on maintaining a fast pace in the transition phase. Encourage players to accelerate into the open spaces and make quick, accurate passes to capitalize on the numerical advantage.• Defender Positioning – The defenders should quickly work to organize themselves during the counter, but also be aggressive in closing down the attackers. Ensure they are not caught out of position while trying to regain possession.• Attacking Movement – The attacking players should be constantly moving to create passing options and to stretch the defensive shape. Effective off-the-ball movement will increase the chances of successfully completing the counter-attack.
progression_one: Increased DefendersIntroduce an additional defender to make the scenario more difficult, creating a 2v2 or 3v3. This progression will challenge the attackers to make quicker decisions and work together more effectively to break down the defenders.Focus: Improving quick decision-making and offensive combinations under pressure.
progression_two: Timed CounterImplement a time limit on the counter-attack phase, requiring attackers to complete the transition within a set period (e.g., 10 seconds). This forces the attackers to act quickly and take advantage of the overload before the defenders can reorganize.Focus: Enhancing speed and efficiency in counter-attacking situations.

title: Sydney Finishing & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This practice allows a centre forward to play through 4 finishes while also improving their conditioning. The forward must attack from end to end, with 4 wide servers crossing 1 ball into the box each time. A coach will call out which player is to cross as the forward is arriving in order to add a layer of difficulty to the practice.
coaching_notes: • Timing the Run – The centre forward should time their runs well, attacking the box at the right moment to meet the cross. The key is to anticipate the delivery and adjust the run accordingly to ensure they are in the correct position for the finish.• Finishing Techniques – The forward should focus on a variety of finishes, including volleys, headers, and one-touch finishes, depending on the type of cross. Encouraging the forward to use both feet and their head will improve their overall finishing skills in various situations.• Conditioning Focus – As the forward transitions from one end to the other, maintaining high intensity is crucial. They should push themselves to keep the pace up while maintaining proper technique. Conditioning is an integral part of this practice, so the forward should work to recover quickly and prepare for the next finish.• Focus on Accuracy – While finishing under pressure, accuracy should take precedence over power. The forward should aim to place the ball in the corners of the goal, either side of the goalkeeper, ensuring a higher chance of scoring.
progression_one: Increasing the DistanceTo further challenge the forward’s conditioning and finishing ability, increase the distance the forward must travel between each finish. This will require them to work harder to get into position and execute the finish while maintaining speed and focus.Focus: Improving stamina and focus during high-intensity actions.
progression_two: Randomized CrossesIntroduce more unpredictability by randomizing which player will cross the ball. This forces the forward to adjust their positioning on the move, ensuring they stay alert and react quickly to different types of deliveries.Focus: Adapting to varying cross types and maintaining focus in chaotic situations.

title: Sydney Recovery & 1v1
instructions_setup: This 1v1 drill starts with a 4-player attacking combination. While this combination is ongoing, a single defender should make a recovery run into the box from the wide area. As the 4-player combination concludes, the final player will attack the goal in a 1v1 scenario. The defender must recover at pace, as the practice will be run as a 1v0 if they don't recover in time.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Movement – The attacking players should focus on timing their combination passes to create space for the final attacker. They must ensure quick, accurate passes and support the player on the ball to increase the chances of success.• Defender’s Recovery – The recovering defender should focus on sprinting at full intensity to reach the box in time to make a defensive intervention. Encourage them to stay goal-side and position themselves to make a challenge as soon as they arrive.• Finishing under Pressure – The final attacker should be encouraged to attack the goal with confidence, using quick, precise movements to beat the defender. They should focus on staying calm and making a well-placed shot, particularly when faced with a 1v0 situation.• Decision-Making – The attacker should assess whether to finish with a shot, dribble around the goalkeeper, or use other tricks, depending on how much time they have before the defender recovers. Being decisive in the final phase is crucial.
progression_one: Add More DefendersIntroduce a second defender to increase the difficulty of the 1v1 scenario, requiring the attacker to make quicker decisions or attempt a more complex move to break through.Focus: Improving finishing under pressure when facing multiple defenders.
progression_two: Limited Touches for AttackersLimit the number of touches each attacker can take during the combination play to increase the intensity and focus on quick decision-making and sharp execution.Focus: Increasing the speed of play and improving quick passing and finishing.

title: Tokyo Build Up Possession
instructions_setup: This possession practice is designed to develop structured build-up play under pressure. The setup includes two centre backs locked on the bottom line, two full backs locked on the touchlines, two attacking midfielders locked on the top line, and one floating midfielder who operates freely inside the grid. This creates a 7v3 scenario, with three defenders applying pressure and attempting to force turnovers.The aim for the possession team is to retain the ball through patient circulation, intelligent movement and well-timed positional adjustments. The defending team can score into any of the four mini goals placed around the outside if they regain possession, encouraging realistic transition moments. Mannequins are positioned across the lines to prevent flat, horizontal “square passes” and to force players to drop off, open passing lanes and adopt better angles during build-up.
coaching_notes: • Create Angles, Not Lines: Encourage players to avoid standing flat and instead move off mannequins to open diagonals and provide clearer passing options.• Role Clarity in Possession: Reinforce centre backs building calmly, full backs offering width, attacking mids providing height, and the floating midfielder linking play.• Receiving on the Half Turn: Coach players to position their body to play forward when possible, helping the team progress through the thirds.• Defensive Pressure Awareness: Highlight the importance of scanning before receiving to avoid being pressed from blindside positions.
progression_one: Two-Touch Minimum for Possession Team:All possession players must take at least two touches—one to control, one to play. This increases the emphasis on the quality and direction of the first touch and encourages better preparation for the next action.Focus: Enhances first-touch control, passing accuracy and composure in build-up.

title: Tokyo Counter & Recovery
instructions_setup: This counter-attacking practice begins with a defender playing a pass into two attackers positioned ahead of them. As soon as the ball is served, the two attackers break forward and attempt to exploit the temporary overload in a 2v1 situation. Their objective is to attack at pace, combine quickly and finish before defensive support arrives.A recovering defender starts five metres behind the attackers and must sprint back to prevent the counter-attack from becoming an easy overload. Their aim is to recover into a good defensive line, create a 2v2 as quickly as possible and delay or stop the attack. The practice creates repeated scenarios of fast transition play, decision-making under pressure and defensive recovery habits.
coaching_notes: • Attack With Speed: Encourage the attackers to drive forward aggressively, using sharp passes and decisive movement to take advantage of the momentary 2v1.• Commit the Lone Defender: Reinforce the importance of drawing the defender before releasing the pass to maximise the overload.• Recovery Sprint Quality: Coach the recovering defender to sprint at full intensity, then enter with control to re-balance the phase.• Timing and End Product: Highlight quick decision-making—attackers should recognise when to release early, when to dribble and when to finish.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit to Score:Give the attackers a 4–5 second window to create and take a shot before the recovering defender arrives. This increases the urgency and raises the tempo of the counter-attack.Focus: Encourages rapid decision-making and clinical execution before pressure arrives.
progression_two: Recovery Defender Starts Closer:Reduce the starting distance of the recovering defender to 2–3 metres behind the attackers. This increases the challenge and forces attackers to combine much faster.Focus: Develops speed of play, adaptability and tighter execution under early pressure.

title: Tokyo Finishing Under Pressure
instructions_setup: This finishing practice is designed to create realistic pressure moments inside the final third. Play begins with a defender serving a pass into the first attacker. Immediately after releasing the ball, the defender must sprint back to recover into position. The first attacker then sets or plays a pass into the second attacker, who must take their touch forward and attempt to finish quickly.The practice can be run in two variations. In the 1v1 version, only the second attacker engages the recovering defender, working to finish under direct pressure. In the 2v1 version, the first attacker joins the phase after playing the initial pass, creating a numerical advantage and allowing for combinations before the finish. Both options emphasise speed, timing and composure when finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quality of the Set Pass: Encourage the first attacker to cushion the set into the second attacker’s path, enabling a forward touch and clean finish.• Forward Touch and Body Shape: Reinforce that the second attacker should take their first touch into space and open their body to finish early.• Defender’s Recovery Line: Coach the defender to sprint with intent, recover centrally and angle their approach to narrow the finishing angle.• Composure Under Pressure: Highlight calm final actions—attackers should stay balanced and make quick decisions as the defender arrives.
progression_one: Limit the Number of Touches:Allow the second attacker no more than two touches before finishing. This increases demand on first-touch quality and quick decision-making.Focus: Improves sharpness in front of goal and execution under pressure.
progression_two: Defender Starts Closer or Further Back:Adjust the defender’s starting distance depending on ability or desired intensity. Closer starting points increase pressure quickly, while further distances create more time for attackers to execute.Focus: Develops adaptability and realism in both attacking and defensive behaviours.

title: Tokyo Rondo Gauntlet
instructions_setup: This practice, known as the Rondo Gauntlet, is designed to combine conditioning demands with high-intensity defensive pressing. Three small rondo grids are set up in a line. Each grid contains three possession players, creating a 3v2 scenario whenever defenders enter. Two defenders begin in the first grid and must attempt to win possession as quickly as possible.Once the defenders force a turnover in the first grid, they must sprint immediately into the second grid and repeat the press. After regaining possession there, they transition into the third grid to complete the final 3v2. The sequence is continuous and physically demanding, challenging the defenders’ work rate, coordination and pressing habits, while the possession players focus on quick combinations and evasion.
coaching_notes: • High-Intensity Pressing: Encourage defenders to enter each grid at sprint speed, close distances quickly and work together to force predictable errors.• Quick Ball Circulation: Reinforce fast, sharp passing from the possession players to move the ball away from pressure and maintain control.• Transition Speed: Coach defenders to react instantly after each regain—accelerating into the next grid without hesitation.• Body Shape and Angles: Highlight curved pressing runs to screen passes and cut off central options, improving pressing efficiency.
progression_one: Time Limit Per Grid:Give the defenders a strict time window (e.g., 6 seconds) to win possession in each grid. Failure resets the rep. This raises intensity and sharpens pressing decisions.Focus: Improves urgency, anticipation and defensive coordination.
progression_two: Touch Limit for Possession Players:Introduce a two-touch maximum inside all grids. This increases tempo, forces sharper movement and makes the defensive press more realistic.Focus: Develops quick combinations, better support angles and rapid ball circulation.

title: Tokyo Wide Combination & Finish
instructions_setup: This finishing practice begins with a three-player wide combination designed to create a crossing opportunity. The wide unit can vary their patterns—using overlaps, underlaps or quick 1–2s—to beat the mannequin or defender and deliver a cross. After combining, two attackers make forward runs into the box, attacking different finishing zones as the cross is delivered.Once the first finish is completed, the attacker who did not take the shot immediately turns to receive a pass from the coach. They must take their touch forward and finish into the opposite goal, creating a second finishing action under minimal pressure. The practice provides repeated opportunities to work on wide-area combinations, timing of box entries and quick transitions between finishing moments.Once the first finish is completed, the attacker who did not take the shot immediately turns to receive a pass from the coach. They must take their touch forward and finish into the opposite goal, creating a second finishing action under minimal pressure. The practice provides repeated opportunities to work on wide-area combinations, timing of box entries and quick transitions between finishing moments.
coaching_notes: • Variety in Wide Combinations: Encourage overlapping, underlapping and bounce passes to keep the patterns unpredictable and game realistic.• Timing of Box Entries: Coach the attackers to stagger their runs—front zone, back-post, and cutback areas—to maximise finishing options.• Quality of Final Delivery: Reinforce accurate, purposeful crosses with the correct pace, height and angle to match the attackers’ movement.• Quick Reset for Second Finish: Highlight the importance of the supporting attacker reacting instantly to receive from the coach and finish cleanly.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender on the Cross:Introduce a defender who applies light pressure to the crosser. This forces more precise execution of the delivery and encourages better timing from the attackers.Focus: Improves delivery accuracy, movement coordination and realism.
progression_two: Add a Recovering Defender for the Second Shot:Allow a recovering defender to pressure the attacker receiving from the coach. This increases demand on touch, speed and composure for the second finish.Focus: Enhances finishing under pressure and quick decision-making.

title: Tottenham 3 Team Possession & Progression
instructions_setup: This possession-based practice involves three teams of three players, along with two neutral joker players who remain in the central grid. Play begins with a 3v1 rondo in one of the end zones. After completing five consecutive passes, the objective is to progress play through the central grid by combining with the jokers, then switch play into the opposite end zone for another 3v1. If the defending team wins possession in the central area, they can break and score into one of two horizontally-placed mini goals. If they regain the ball in an outer grid, they must connect with a teammate inside the central zone.
coaching_notes: • Passing Angles – Players must constantly adjust their positioning to create forward-facing angles that allow smooth connection through the jokers and into the next zone.• Transition Movement – Central jokers and wide players must react instantly during possession changes, either repositioning to offer support or reacting defensively to prevent counters.• Ball Speed – All passes, especially those through the central grid, should be played with pace and accuracy to exploit openings before defenders can reset.• Defensive Triggers – Defenders should press on visual cues like poor touches, telegraphed passes, or hesitation to increase their chances of regaining possession and countering quickly.
progression_one: One-Touch Limit for JokersRestrict the jokers to one-touch passes when linking play between grids.Focus: Increases demand on timing, positioning, and pass quality from the outside players during transitions.
progression_two: Live Pressure in Central GridAllow one defender to enter the central zone and apply pressure while the ball is transitioning through.Focus: Develops composure, scanning, and quick decision-making under realistic central pressure conditions.

title: Tottenham 3rd Man Finishing
instructions_setup: This finishing practice focuses on 3rd man attacking combinations, giving players plenty of opportunities to finish. The centre forward will play a set pass to a teammate before making a sharp movement around a mannequin. After the movement, the centre forward will receive a cut-back pass and finish on goal.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the Set Pass – The centre forward should play the initial set pass with good weight and timing, ensuring that the receiving player can control the ball and move it forward towards the final action.• Sharp Movement – After playing the set pass, the centre forward must make a sharp, purposeful movement around the mannequin. This should be a quick, decisive change of direction, simulating a real game situation where the CF needs to shake off the defender and create space.• Receiving the Cut-Back – The centre forward should focus on timing their movement to meet the ball at the right moment, using their body to shield the defender and create space to finish cleanly.• Finishing with Composure – Once the centre forward receives the cut-back, they should focus on finishing with composure, whether it’s a first-time shot or a controlled touch followed by a finish. Encourage different types of finishes based on the situation, such as low drives or chips.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender who starts at a distance but pressures the centre forward during their sharp movement. The defender will attempt to make the centre forward's cut-back more challenging by closing space or influencing the shot.Focus: Adds pressure to the movement and finish, encouraging the centre forward to remain composed under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Vary the PassChange the set pass to a more dynamic ball, such as a lofted or diagonal pass, requiring the centre forward to adjust their movement and touch before completing the combination.Focus: Develops the centre forward's ability to adapt to different types of passes and still execute the 3rd man combination effectively in varied situations.

title: Tottenham 3v3 Conditioning
instructions_setup: This drill combines conditioning with small-sided gameplay to encourage high-intensity work and quick transitions. Play begins with players sprinting across the area and around the poles positioned ahead of them. The sprinting phase is designed to get players moving at maximum speed and focus on conditioning.Once the players complete the sprint around the poles, the game transitions into a live 3v3 format, where the aim is to score a goal. After each goal, teams reset to their original positions, complete another sprint, and the winning team from the previous game receives the ball to start the next round.
coaching_notes: • Maximize Sprinting Effort: Ensure players are sprinting at full intensity, focusing on their speed and quick recovery between phases of play.• Transition Quickly into Play: After completing the sprint, players must immediately transition into the 3v3 match, focusing on fast decision-making and sharp movements.• Recovery and Re-focus: Encourage players to focus on their recovery and re-adjustment before the next sprint. This helps them maintain energy and composure for the following game.• Maintain High Intensity in the Game: In the 3v3 phase, players must continue to work hard, applying pressure, creating space, and using their conditioning to maintain intensity throughout the drill.
progression_one: Add More Players:Increase the game size to a 4v4 or 5v5 format to encourage more team play and tactical awareness while still including the conditioning sprint.Focus: This increases endurance and requires players to think strategically while managing their energy levels.
progression_two: Add Time Constraints:Limit the time each team has to score to increase urgency, ensuring that players work at a high tempo throughout both the sprinting and the game phases.Focus: This encourages players to stay focused on both their physical performance and their ability to execute under pressure.

title: Tottenham Finishing In Behind
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, the focus is on creating and finishing goal-scoring opportunities from wide positions. The winger starts with the ball on the flank and plays a short pass backward to the midfielder, positioned centrally. The midfielder then clips a ball over the defensive line for the attacking player who has made a timed run in behind. The attacker has the option to finish with a header, volley, or controlled touch, depending on the delivery and timing of their run.This drill helps improve timing, awareness, and finishing techniques under realistic match conditions.
coaching_notes: • Winger’s Passing Accuracy: The winger must ensure the pass is accurate, allowing the midfielder to easily receive and deliver the ball over the top. A well-timed and precise pass is essential for the attacker's success.• Midfielder’s Timing and Delivery: The midfielder should focus on timing their pass and delivering it with the right weight and height to match the attacker’s run. The ball must be clipped over the defensive line to allow the attacker to stay onside.• Attacker’s Run and Timing: The attacker should focus on making their run just as the pass is being played, timing it to stay onside and be in a prime position to receive the ball in stride. The run should be direct and quick.• Finishing Variety: The attacker must be prepared to finish using various techniques, such as a header, volley, or controlled touch and finish, depending on the ball's delivery and where they are when receiving it.
progression_one: Add Pressure:Introduce a defender to apply light pressure on the attacking player after the ball is played over the top. The attacker must still focus on the run and finishing technique while dealing with the pressure.Focus: This progression adds an element of decision-making under pressure, mimicking real match situations.
progression_two: Multiple Attacking Runs:Increase the number of attacking players in the drill, allowing for different options for the midfielder to pass to. The attacker can now choose from a wider variety of runs and finishing techniques.Focus: This adds complexity and encourages decision-making on the ball while enhancing teamwork and communication.

title: Tottenham Overlapping CM
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a central midfielder receiving the ball and executing an overlapping run. As the midfielder moves into the attacking zone, they deliver a cross into the box aimed at two attackers. The attackers position themselves to make runs into the box, looking to time their movements for the cross. The focus is on the timing of the overlap and the quality of the cross, ensuring both attackers can make effective runs toward the ball.During the unopposed phase, players should focus on quick, fluid movement, and maintaining proper spacing to allow the attacking midfielder and the attackers to connect with the ball. The central midfielder should work on timing their overlap with the ball progression while ensuring the cross is accurate and delivered with the right pace for the attackers to finish.
coaching_notes: • Timing the Overlap: The central midfielder should time their run so they are in position to cross when the attackers are ready to attack the ball. Proper timing and awareness are essential.• Crossing Technique: Emphasize the quality of the cross. The ball should be delivered with the right amount of pace and precision, aiming for the attackers’ preferred areas.• Movement of Attackers: Attackers should make runs into the box that create options for the cross, ensuring they adjust their position based on where the cross is coming from.• Communication: Encourage players to communicate throughout the pattern. Attackers should give signals for where they want the ball played, and the midfielder should be aware of these cues to provide the best service.
progression_one: Add Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders who apply light pressure to the central midfielder and attackers as they execute the overlapping run and cross. The attackers must still focus on the timing and quality of their runs and finishing, but now with mild pressure.Focus: Helps attackers maintain focus on their runs and finishing under slightly more challenging conditions.
progression_two: Add Finishing Option for Central MidfielderAllow the central midfielder the option to either cross or take a shot themselves if the angle is right. This gives the midfielder a chance to be more dynamic and adds a decision-making element to their run.Focus: Develops versatility in the midfielder's decision-making and encourages attackers to stay alert for both the cross and potential shot.

title: Tottenham Reactions Warm Up
instructions_setup: This warm-up and reaction drill focuses on improving agility, quick directional changes, and mental alertness. Players are positioned on the central line, bouncing lightly on their toes to stay agile. On the coach's whistle, players must quickly spin 180 degrees to face the opposite direction. At any point, the coach can call out a color, and the players must react instantly, sprinting across the end line where the corresponding colored cone is located.This drill helps develop reaction time, agility, and concentration under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Reaction Time: Players should focus on reacting as quickly as possible to the coach's whistle and color call. The quicker they react, the more they’ll develop the ability to change direction swiftly.• Agility and Balance: While bouncing on their toes, players should maintain a low center of gravity for better balance and faster acceleration when the whistle blows.• Spinning Technique: The 180-degree spin should be sharp and controlled. Players should avoid losing their balance when turning and ensure they can quickly change direction.• Sprint with Purpose: Once the color is called, players must sprint decisively towards the correct cone. Encourage quick acceleration and strong, purposeful strides to simulate match situations.
progression_one: Add Dribbling Element:Introduce a ball to the drill, where players must dribble to the designated color cone instead of sprinting. This progression incorporates ball control under pressure.Focus: This progression challenges players to maintain focus while managing the ball during reactive situations, improving both technical skills and reaction time.
progression_two: Increase Reaction Speed:Reduce the time between the coach's whistle and the color call. Players must react even faster to the color call and sprint to the cone in a shorter time.Focus: This progression enhances the players' ability to make faster decisions, improving their reaction time and readiness in a real-game scenario.

title: Tottenham Rondo to Finishing Centrally
instructions_setup: This semi-opposed drill features a 4v2 central rondo positioned just outside the penalty area. The aim is for the team in possession to complete five consecutive passes before playing into a centre forward, who is shadow marked by the coach. The forward is restricted to two touches to control and finish. If the defenders win possession during the rondo, they transition quickly to attack either of the two mini goals placed beyond the grid. Players rotate roles throughout to ensure balanced repetition and varied service into the striker.
coaching_notes: • Quality of Pass – Passes into the forward should be firm, accurate, and timed to exploit the forward’s movement and two-touch limit.• Forward Movement – The centre forward must stay alert, using subtle movements to create space and receive under pressure from the shadow defender.• Compactness in Possession – The four players should keep tight spacing and circulate the ball quickly to stretch the two defenders and open passing lanes.• Transition Mentality – The defending pair must switch quickly from defending to attacking upon winning possession, targeting space beyond the rondo grid.
progression_one: Active Defender on the ForwardReplace the shadow-marking coach with a live defender to apply realistic pressure on the centre forward.Focus: Tests the forward’s ability to receive and finish quickly under live defensive pressure.
progression_two: One-Touch FinishingLimit the centre forward to one-touch finishes after receiving the ball.Focus: Improves timing, anticipation, and striking technique under tight constraints.

title: Tottenham Wide Combinations & Crossing
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing drill allows players to develop their ability to cross the ball after making positive forward runs in wider areas. The crossers should work on a mixture of low, driven, or floated crosses throughout the practice. As a progression, place several mini goals as targets instead of one big goal, which adds an element of decision-making to the practice and replicates multiple runners into the box.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing – The wide players must focus on making positive, forward runs into space. The timing of these runs should allow them to meet the ball in stride, ensuring they can either take a touch or cross with minimal delay.• Crossing Techniques – Encourage the crossers to vary their crosses. Low, driven crosses should be used for players making near-post runs, while floated crosses are ideal for players arriving at the far post or for crosses to the back of the box.• Decision-Making – Players should make quick decisions on the type of cross based on the position of the attacking players. Knowing when to deliver a driven ball versus when to float a cross will increase the effectiveness of their crossing.• Target Focus – With the mini goals placed as targets, the crossers should focus on targeting the space between them rather than aiming for a single large goal. This requires improved accuracy and judgment in delivering crosses based on the movement of the runners.
progression_one: Mini Goals as TargetsInstead of one big goal, use several mini goals as targets. This forces players to make better decisions about where to place their crosses, adding complexity to the practice as they aim for specific areas.Focus: Developing accuracy in crossing and improving decision-making under realistic game conditions.
progression_two: Multiple Runners into the BoxAdd multiple runners into the box, replicating a game scenario with several attacking players arriving at different times. The crossers must now assess the best delivery for each type of run, increasing the pressure and decision-making challenge.Focus: Improving the timing and placement of crosses based on the movements of multiple runners into the box.

title: Toulouse Attacking 2v1
instructions_setup: Play begins with a pass from a central player into one of two wide stations — left or right — alternating each repetition. After the initial pass, two attackers combine to create a 2v1 situation against a single recovering defender. The attackers are encouraged to use creative movements such as overlaps, underlaps, and quick one-two combinations to break down the defender and create a clear scoring opportunity.Each station has a small goal or goalkeeper, so players must adapt based on the side of play and make quick decisions in tight spaces. The focus is on intelligent movement, timing, and variety in how the attackers combine to exploit the overload.
coaching_notes: • Variety of Combinations – Encourage players to experiment with overlaps, underlaps, and 1-2s to unbalance the defender and open up shooting opportunities.• Timing of Movement – Emphasize precise timing of supporting runs to avoid being too early or too late, especially when linking up in wide areas.• Communication – Attackers should use verbal or visual cues to coordinate movements and improve the flow of the combination.• Defender Position Scanning – Players must scan quickly before receiving to assess the defender's positioning and select the best combination option.
progression_one: Defender Starts Closer to the PlayMove the defender’s starting position closer to the combination area to reduce attacker time and force faster execution of overlaps or one-touch passes.Focus:Sharpens attacker decision-making under pressure and encourages quicker, more decisive passing combinations in tight spaces.
progression_two: Add Recovery Defender From Central AreaIntroduce a second defender who starts deeper and recovers toward goal as the 2v1 begins, adding urgency for attackers to combine and finish early.Focus:Promotes fast, purposeful attacking play and improves attackers' ability to recognize when to combine vs go direct with pressure increasing.

title: Toulouse Counter & Build Up
instructions_setup: The drill begins with a 3v1 counter-attack in a central grid. The three attackers aim to score against the lone defender, using quick movement and passing to break through. Two additional defenders are positioned 5 yards behind the grid and can join the defensive phase once the attackers have completed the first phase, aiming to create a 3v3 scenario. The counter-attack phase is short, with the attackers looking to finish quickly while the single defender tries to delay or win the ball.Once the first phase ends, a second ball is played into the defenders and goalkeeper, who are tasked with building out of the back and attempting to score in two mini goals positioned at the ends of the grid. The three players who were part of the counter-attack now transition to defense, looking to prevent the build-up and stop the attacking team from scoring. The second phase focuses on transitioning quickly from attack to defense, with defenders aiming to regain possession and stop the attacking build-up.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transition to Attack: Encourage the 3 attacking players to move quickly and decisively, utilizing speed and creativity to break down the single defender in the first phase.• Defensive Awareness: The 2 recovering defenders must react swiftly, using effective positioning and communication to try and make it a 3v3 before the attacker's finish.• Building from the Back: When the defenders and goalkeeper are in possession, they should focus on building from the back with short, quick passes, ensuring they use the full width of the grid to create space.• Transition to Defense: As the counter attackers transition into defenders, they must remain disciplined, focus on positioning, and communicate effectively to prevent the build-up and block passing lanes.
progression_one: Add Time PressureIntroduce a time limit for the first phase of the counter-attack (e.g., 15 seconds). If the attackers don’t score in that time, the phase is considered over.Focus: Increases intensity, forcing players to make faster decisions and transition quickly.
progression_two: Add Pressing Triggers for DefendersOnce the ball is served into the defensive phase (second phase), the defending players must press the ball within 5 seconds of possession, applying pressure on the goalkeeper and defenders as they build out.Focus: Encourages quicker, more aggressive defending during the transition and promotes fast-paced defensive decisions.

title: Toulouse Long Ball Mastery Warm Up
instructions_setup: In this long ball mastery warm-up, players will work on developing set passes and combination play from long balls. Two players are positioned at the top and bottom of the practice area, with two central players positioned closely together in the middle. The ball carrier at the top will play a long, high ball to the furthest central player, who must control the ball with one touch and then allow the second central player to play the ball forwards. The practice then repeats from top to bottom.This warm-up emphasizes clean ball control, first touch under pressure, and quick combination play to transition the ball effectively over longer distances.
coaching_notes: • Ball Control: The central players must focus on their first touch to control the ball cleanly and allow for a smooth progression of play. Encourage players to use the inside of their foot to cushion the ball and direct it toward the second player.• Timing of Passes: The ball carrier at the top must time their long pass accurately to allow the central players to move into position for the knockdown. The receiving central player should position themselves in anticipation of the ball and be ready to control it cleanly.• Combination Play: The second central player must be aware of the knockdown and look to play a quick pass forward. This encourages fluid combination play and the ability to shift from defense to attack with minimal touches.• Communication: Encourage verbal and non-verbal communication between players to coordinate the timing of the passes and movement. Clear communication will help ensure the drill runs smoothly and players are in sync.
progression_one: Add Defenders:Introduce one or two defenders who can apply light pressure to the central players receiving the ball. This will encourage the attacking players to maintain their composure and increase the quality of their first touch under pressure.Focus: Improves the ability to control the ball while under pressure and make effective passes despite defensive presence.

title: Toulouse Technical Passing & Receiving
instructions_setup: In this technical passing practice, players work the ball around a square using a variety of 1-2 combinations. After each pass, the player follows their pass to the next station, promoting constant movement and positional rotation.The focus is on developing quick, accurate passing, sharp movement off the ball, and clean execution of one-touch combinations under minimal pressure.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Support Runs – Players must anticipate the return pass and move early enough to support the 1-2 combination without overrunning or being late.• Body Position on Receive – Encourage receiving players to open up their body and angle themselves appropriately to play and move fluidly around the square.• Pass Weight and Accuracy – Emphasize firm, accurate passes into feet and on the correct foot to keep the rhythm and flow of the practice high.• Communication and Tempo – Verbal cues and eye contact should be consistent, with players working at a sharp tempo to mimic match-speed combinations.
progression_one: Introduce Opposite Foot Only PassingRequire all players to complete the entire sequence using their weaker foot only, increasing difficulty and technical focus.Focus:Builds confidence, balance, and passing quality on the weaker side while maintaining speed and precision under self-imposed pressure.

title: Trondheim 2v2 Dribble Through
instructions_setup: In this 2+1v2+1 drill, play begins with a 2v2 battle in a central grid. Each team is supported by a neutral player positioned on their end line ahead of the grid, who acts as a free player when their team is in possession, creating a 3v2 numerical advantage. The primary objective for each team is to use effective dribbling and combination play to navigate through either of the two gates positioned on the left and right sides of their respective end line.This setup encourages quick decision-making, exploiting overloads, and sharp dribbling skills under pressure while emphasizing spatial awareness and teamwork to unlock defensive structures.
coaching_notes: • Encourage effective use of the neutral player to create overloads – Players should quickly identify and utilize the numerical advantage by combining with the neutral for easier gate entries.• Stress sharp dribbling skills and timing when attacking gates – Attacking players must use controlled touches and sudden changes of pace or direction to beat defenders.• Promote defensive communication and compactness – Defenders should stay organized, communicate constantly, and anticipate passes to prevent attackers from exploiting the gates.• Highlight quick transitions between offense and defense – Players must react swiftly when possession changes to either defend or attack the gates effectively.
progression_one: Limit Touches to 2 Per PlayerImpose a two-touch maximum to increase tempo and force faster decision-making, encouraging sharper passing and quicker ball control under pressure.Focus: Develops technical sharpness, speed of play, and encourages players to think and act quickly in tight situations.
progression_two: Add a Time Limit to ScoreTeams must complete the gate dribble and score within a limited timeframe (e.g., 10 seconds) after gaining possession, increasing urgency and pressure in attack phases.Focus: Builds intensity, enhances quick transition play, and forces players to make faster decisions while maintaining control.

title: Trondheim 3 Phase Possession
instructions_setup: This is a progressive possession drill designed to replicate game-realistic build-up under increasing pressure. Play begins with a 4v2 rondo in a tight central grid, focusing on sharp passing, movement, and supporting angles. Once the team in possession completes a set number of passes or a successful trigger, they break out into a 5v3 phase that expands the playing area and includes wider options.After maintaining possession in the 5v3, the drill expands again into a full 7v5 possession game across a small-sided pitch. The 7 includes 2 goalkeepers who can be used as outlets or to recycle play. If the team of 5 wins the ball in this final phase, they can counter and score into either of the two main goals. The transitions between phases test composure, awareness, and decision-making under pressure as numerical advantages reduce.
