coaching_notes: • Encourage constant scanning before receiving – Players must read pressure, identify space, and make quicker decisions based on visual cues to avoid unnecessary turnovers or forced errors.• Emphasise quality of the first touch – It should set up the next action efficiently while avoiding pressure and maintaining tempo, especially under tight, high-pressure conditions.• Reinforce body shape when receiving – Players should receive on the half-turn with hips open to switch or progress play more easily, allowing them to exploit space in either direction.• Use the goalkeepers to recycle intelligently – Goalkeepers should remain calm and offer safe outlets that help shift or reset play with purpose, encouraging wider pitch usage and controlled tempo.
progression_one: Limited Touch Rondo PhasesReduce touches in both the 4v2 and 5v3 phases to 2-touch or 1-touch play, forcing quicker decisions and improving passing tempo under tighter time constraints.Focus: Develops speed of play, technical execution, and fast support angles under controlled pressure environments.
progression_two: Time-Limited Final PhaseAdd a 10–12 second time limit to score in the 7v5 phase. If the team fails to score or loses possession, play resets to the 4v2. Defending team gains a point for each successful stop.Focus: Encourages urgency, structured penetration, and intelligent final-third decision-making against defensive overloads.

title: Trondheim Back to Goal 1v1
instructions_setup: This is a dynamic 1v1 drill focused on attacking with purpose and recovering to defend. The practice begins with the defender dribbling toward the two mini goals at the top end of the grid and playing a firm pass into either mini goal. Simultaneously, the attacker dribbles up the opposite side and plays a quick 1-2 combination with a supporting player before turning sharply.After their respective movements, the attacker immediately drives forward and attempts to score into either of the mini goals. The defender, after passing into the goal, must quickly recover and defend 1v1. This practice helps develop recovery speed, sharp changes of direction, and creative attacking decisions under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Stress the importance of defensive recovery runs – Defenders must react quickly, angle their run effectively, and regain compact positioning to delay the attacker.• Encourage aggressive forward play from attackers – Attackers should drive at the defender with controlled speed, using changes of direction and body feints to unbalance them.• Reinforce quality of the 1-2 combination – The initial wall pass should be played firmly and accurately to maintain tempo and allow a smooth turn and attack.• Highlight finishing decision under pressure – Attackers should scan early, select the best mini goal, and execute a composed finish despite recovering pressure from the defender.
progression_one: Touch Restriction Before 1v1Limit the attacker to two touches after receiving the 1-2 before they must engage the defender 1v1 and attempt to score.Focus: Increases speed of execution and demands tighter control and quicker decision-making.
progression_two: Add a Recovery IncentiveAward a point to defenders if they win the ball or force the attacker to miss the mini goals within 5 seconds of the 1v1 phase starting.Focus: Encourages urgent recovery runs and competitive defending while motivating attackers to be decisive and efficient.

title: Trondheim Double 1v0 Into 1v1
instructions_setup: Play begins with 2 players positioned centrally who each receive a precise pass from a teammate. After controlling the ball, they turn quickly and sprint toward opposite ends of the grid to score in their respective mini goals. This first phase emphasizes quick ball control, sharp turns, and accurate finishing under light pressure, helping develop spatial awareness and quick decision-making in tight spaces.Once both players have completed their initial finishes, a second ball is played into the grid to start a highly competitive 1v1 duel between them. This phase focuses on attacking and defending skills in a realistic scenario, challenging players to use dribbling, positioning, and finishing techniques under intense pressure from their opponent.
coaching_notes: • Stress quick, controlled first touches to enable rapid turning and acceleration – This helps players create space and maintain attacking momentum effectively, even under intense game pressure and tight marking.• Encourage players to use feints and body positioning in 1v1s – To deceive defenders, create clear shooting opportunities, and gain an advantage by manipulating defensive reactions.• Remind defenders to maintain low, balanced stances and stay patient before committing – This allows better reaction to attacker’s moves, reduces chances of being beaten, and improves defensive timing significantly.• Emphasize composure and accuracy when finishing in tight spaces – Players should focus on precision to consistently score under pressure, considering both placement and power of their shots.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit for First PhaseIntroduce a strict time limit for players to receive and finish in the first phase, encouraging faster decision-making and sharp execution.Focus: Develops speed of play, urgency, and mental sharpness under match-like conditions.

title: Trondheim End to End Transition
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on quick attacking and immediate defensive transition. It begins with a 1v1 duel in the top half of the grid where the attacker aims to score or beat the defender. As soon as the play concludes, the attacker must rapidly recover and transition to defend in a new 1v1 situation taking place in the bottom half of the grid. This simulates real-game demands of switching roles instantly from attack to defense.The challenge tests both players’ fitness, reaction speed, and tactical awareness while emphasizing mental sharpness during fast-paced transitions between offense and defense.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize explosive sprinting and recovery speed – Attacker must quickly shift mindset from attacking to defending and recover position rapidly to prevent scoring.• Encourage controlled but aggressive defensive positioning – Defenders should maintain low body shape and use angles to delay the attacker while staying balanced for quick reactions.• Stress decision-making under fatigue – Players must stay composed and make smart choices despite physical tiredness caused by repeated sprints and role changes.• Promote communication and awareness of space – Both players should scan constantly to anticipate opponent’s moves and adjust positioning effectively during transitions.
progression_one: Add a Touch LimitLimit players to a maximum of two touches per possession in both 1v1 phases, encouraging quicker decisions, sharper technique, and higher game realism.Focus: Enhances technical execution speed, quick thinking, and improves ball control and passing accuracy under pressure.

title: Trondheim Low Block Progression
instructions_setup: In this low block penetration drill, two attacking players look to move the ball quickly in order to manipulate and shift three defenders who are protecting a central line. The defenders are tasked with staying compact, denying passing lanes, and blocking direct access to the striker positioned behind them.The attacking pair must work at tempo, using movement, disguise, and ball speed to create an opening. Once a gap is found, they must play a penetrative pass through or around the block into the striker, who receives behind the defenders. If successful, the striker finishes unopposed on goal. The focus is on patience, timing, and execution when facing a structured low block.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise ball speed and disguise in possession – Attackers must move the ball sharply with minimal touches and use subtle body movements to shift the block.• Reinforce compact positioning and lateral movement for defenders – Defenders should remain disciplined, slide as a unit, and communicate to prevent line-splitting passes.• Focus on the striker's timing and movement – Striker should stay alert, constantly adjust positioning, and show for the ball at the right moment to receive cleanly.• Encourage patience and creativity in possession – Attackers must not force the play but use clever angles, feints, and changes in rhythm to open a passing lane.
progression_one: Limit Time in PossessionAllow the attacking pair only 8 seconds to break the block and find the striker behind the defensive line. Start the timer as soon as the first pass is made.Focus: Forces quick decision-making, promotes faster ball circulation, and simulates real pressure scenarios with urgency and composure under time constraints.
progression_two: Add a Pressing Defender on the StrikerInclude a recovering defender who pressures the striker immediately upon receiving the ball behind the line. This defender starts 5 yards away and closes down at speed.Focus: Tests the striker’s ability to control under pressure, receive on the half-turn, and finish quickly while adapting to defensive pressure.

title: Trondheim Opposed Attacking Patterns
instructions_setup: In this practice, 5 attackers work through a variety of unopposed passing combinations outside the penalty box to develop sharp movement and precise ball control. These combinations focus on creating space, timing runs, and rehearsing attacking patterns to open defensive gaps effectively. The initial phase allows attackers to build rhythm and chemistry without pressure.Once the ball enters the penalty box, 2 defenders become active and apply immediate pressure to defend the area. The defenders must organize themselves to block passing lanes and challenge the 2 or 3 attackers trying to penetrate and score, emphasizing defensive positioning and timely interceptions under realistic match conditions.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize quick, accurate passing during unopposed phases – This helps attackers maintain possession and create quality scoring opportunities with good tempo and precision.• Stress effective movement off the ball to create passing lanes – Players should use sharp runs and positioning to open space and confuse defenders.• Defenders must communicate clearly and maintain compact shape – To efficiently cover dangerous areas and close down attackers with teamwork and anticipation.• Encourage defenders to delay and force attackers wide inside the box – Applying pressure while guiding attackers away from the central scoring zones.
progression_one: Add a Third Defender in the BoxIntroduce a third defender inside the box to increase defensive pressure, requiring attackers to make quicker decisions and sharper movements.Focus: Improves attackers’ creativity under pressure and defenders’ coordination and communication.
progression_two: Limit Attacking Team to Two TouchesRestrict attackers to a maximum of two touches during the unopposed passing phase to speed up play and simulate higher game intensity.Focus: Develops quick thinking, sharp technical skills, and faster attacking transitions into the box.

title: Trondheim Recovery 1v1 Into 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill begins with a 1v1 phase where a defender passes to an attacker on the left side of the grid before immediately applying pressure to prevent a goal-scoring opportunity. The focus is on quick reactions, individual defending, and forcing poor decisions or rushed shots from the attacker.After the first phase ends (either with a goal or a defensive stop), the opposite defender on the right side plays a pass into a second attacker. This begins the second phase — a 2v2 — as the original attacker and defender stay involved. The emphasis now shifts to defending as a pair and making decisions based on the positioning of teammates and attackers.
coaching_notes: • Stress intensity in the recovery run – Defenders must sprint quickly after the pass, close the space immediately, and apply intelligent pressure to reduce shooting angles.• Reinforce timing and angle of defensive approach – Defenders should bend their run to force attackers wide, staying low and balanced to delay or block shots.• Encourage awareness during transition between phases – Defenders and attackers need to quickly adapt as the situation shifts to 2v2, adjusting positions and roles on the fly.• Promote communication and defensive shape in 2v2 – Defenders must talk constantly, stay compact, and avoid getting split while covering space and tracking runners.
progression_one: Add a Recovery Line for DefendersAdd a line 5 yards behind each defender. They must sprint around it before engaging the attacker. This adds a recovery element and realism to the initial 1v1 duel.Focus: Emphasises physical recovery speed, defensive transition, and the ability to recover ground before engaging attackers in realistic defensive situations.
progression_two: Add a Support Pass Option for AttackersIntroduce a neutral support player behind the play that attackers can use once in the 2v2 phase to create overloads or play bounce passes.Focus: Develops decision-making, third-player movement, and encourages attackers to combine intelligently when under pressure in tight areas.

title: Turin Finish The Attack
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 5v4 inside a central playing area. The team of five attackers aims to break down the defensive four by circulating the ball at high tempo, using quick combinations and sharp movement to create gaps through the middle or find opportunities to play around the defensive block. Two additional attacking players are positioned in wide channels, offering an outlet to progress the attack if central penetration is not possible.The attacking team can score by breaking through centrally or by finding one of the wide players and progressing the attack towards goal. Once the ball has moved beyond the central grid, the attackers play the phase out to a finish. If the defensive team wins possession and secures control, they can transition quickly and score into any of the three mini goals around the outside. This encourages realistic defensive transitions and rewards clean regains.
coaching_notes: • Speed of Circulation: Encourage the attacking team to move the ball quickly to disrupt the defensive shape and force defenders to constantly adjust.• Play Through or Around: Coach players to recognise central gaps early but also identify moments to bounce wide and progress through the wide players if the middle is compact.• Supporting Angles: Reinforce the need for constant movement off the ball—showing between lines, rotating positions and creating passing lanes to maintain flow.• Defensive Transition: Highlight the importance of reacting instantly if the ball is lost—delay the counter, protect the middle and prevent quick finishes into the mini goals.
progression_one: Touch Limit for Central Attackers:Apply a two-touch limit inside the central grid to increase the speed of decision-making and force sharper combinations.Focus: Raises tempo, improves quick support play and encourages faster ball movement.
progression_two: Allow Wide Players to Join After First Wide Pass:Once the ball is played into a wide channel player, allow that wide player to break into the central space and join the attack. This creates dynamic overloads and provides more finishing options.Focus: Develops timing, third-man runs and more unpredictable attacking patterns.

title: Turin Finishing Overloaded
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 3v2 attacking overload in a central area. The three attackers aim to combine quickly, commit defenders and create a finishing opportunity before the defensive pair can delay or force mistakes. Once the first phase is completed through a goal, save or turnover, the coach immediately initiates the second phase.In phase two, the ball is played out to a wide player who can drive down the wing unopposed and deliver a cross into the box for the same three attackers. However, the defensive team has full-backs positioned to prevent or block the cross, meaning the winger must choose the right moment, angle and delivery technique. The attackers then attempt to finish from the cross, while defenders react and try to stop the second wave.
coaching_notes: • Exploit the Overload Early: Encourage the central attackers to combine at speed—using third-man runs, quick passing and movement to take advantage of the 3v2.• Quality of Final Pass: Reinforce the importance of timing and weight of the final ball before the shot in phase one.• Crossing Precision: Coach the winger to recognise the defender’s positioning and deliver crosses with accuracy, disguise or varied height to beat the full-back.• Box Movement: Emphasise coordinated movements from the three attackers—front-post, back-post and second-phase positions to increase finishing options.
progression_one: Add a Recovery Defender Into the Box:Allow one central defender from phase one to recover and defend the cross in phase two. This increases realism and forces attackers to adjust their timing and movement inside the box.Focus: Improves decision-making and finishing under increased defensive pressure.
progression_two: Limit Time Before the Cross:Give the wide player a 2–3 second limit to deliver the cross once they receive the ball. This forces quicker execution and more realistic tempo against full-back pressure.Focus: Enhances crossing speed, delivery quality and attacking anticipation.

title: Turin Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: This practice uses two rondo grids with a middle transition zone and four teams of four players. Two teams begin in possession, one in each rondo grid, while the other two teams start in the central zone as defenders. The practice runs continuously for a set time period to create high-intensity pressing and repeated transition efforts.Each defending team sends two players into their assigned rondo grid (top or bottom) to press in a 4v2 situation and attempt to win possession. Once they win the ball or force a turnover, both defenders must sprint out of the grid and return to the middle zone. Their two resting teammates then immediately sprint into the same grid to take over the press. This pressing cycle repeats non-stop, creating a physically demanding exercise that blends technical quality with high-energy defensive work.
coaching_notes: • High Tempo Possession: Encourage the possession teams to play quickly with crisp one- or two-touch passing to escape pressure and maintain control.• Pressing Intensity: Reinforce the need for defenders to enter the grid at full speed, close distances quickly and work together to force predictable mistakes.• Quick Transitions: Highlight the importance of sprinting out of the grid immediately after a regain and triggering the next pair to enter, maintaining continuous flow.• Support Positions: Coach possession players to constantly adjust angles and distance to keep the ball moving efficiently and avoid getting boxed in.
progression_one: Touch Limit for Possession Team:Introduce a two-touch limit inside each rondo. This forces quicker thinking, sharper ball movement and increased physical demands due to faster tempo.Focus: Improves decision-making speed, tempo of play and technical quality under pressure.
progression_two: Scoring System for Defenders:Award defenders a point for each clean regain within a set time (e.g., within 5 seconds of entering). This motivates coordinated pressing and more aggressive defensive actions.Focus: Develops collective pressing behaviours, anticipation and defensive work ethic.

title: Turin Receiving Under Pressure
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on receiving under pressure with realistic timing and movement patterns. Play begins with the attacker making a sharp run toward a mannequin before checking off at an angle to create space. As they move away from the mannequin, a supporting player plays a pass into their path. The attacker must receive cleanly, take their touch forward and attempt to finish into the mini goal.As soon as the pass is released, a recovering defender sprints from behind to apply immediate pressure on the receiver. Their aim is to close the distance quickly, disrupt the attacker’s first touch and prevent the shot. This creates a game-realistic scenario where attackers must receive on the move, protect the ball and stay composed under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Check Movement: Encourage the attacker to check off the mannequin with tempo, using the movement to create separation before receiving.• First Touch Direction: Reinforce taking the touch forward and into space, setting up the finish while protecting the ball from the recovering defender.• Body Positioning: Coach players to scan early, open their hips and receive on the half-turn to maintain forward momentum.• Composure Under Pressure: Highlight staying calm during the finish—attackers should focus on clean execution despite the defender closing down.
progression_one: Add a Touch Limit Before Shooting:Limit the attacker to two touches before finishing. This demands a cleaner first touch and quicker preparation for the shot.Focus: Sharpens first-touch quality and improves speed of decision-making.
progression_two: Adjust the Defender’s Starting Distance:Bring the recovering defender closer or further away depending on ability level. This increases or decreases the intensity and forces the attacker to adapt their movement and timing.Focus: Develops adaptability, receiving awareness and real-game pressure handling.

title: Turin Wide Progression to Finish
instructions_setup: This practice begins with a 3v1 rondo in the first wide-area grid. The attacking trio must work the ball quickly, keeping possession under pressure and completing five passes before they are allowed to progress. Once the pass count is reached, the attackers can break into the second wide grid and immediately continue with another 3v1, again aiming to complete five passes against the single defender.After successfully completing both rondos, the attackers can exit the wide channel and play into a final unopposed phase. From here, one of the wide players drives forward and delivers a cross into the box, where two attackers position themselves to finish. This sequence links wide-area progression, technical possession play and final-third end product.
coaching_notes: • Tempo in Tight Spaces: Encourage quick, sharp passing in both rondo grids to maintain control and keep the defender moving.• Supporting Angles: Coach the attackers to adjust their positioning constantly—opening passing lanes, creating triangles and supporting the ball-carrier.• Timing the Breakout: Highlight the need for coordinated movement when exiting each rondo so players enter the next phase cleanly and with purpose.• Quality of Final Ball: Reinforce accurate crossing technique and ensure the two attackers attack different finishing zones inside the box.
progression_one: Reduce the Pass Count:Lower the required passes from five to three before progressing to the next grid. This speeds up the tempo and increases the demand for quicker combinations.Focus: Improves urgency, quicker support play and faster transitions between phases.
progression_two: Add a Recovering Defender Into the Final Phase:Allow a defender from the second rondo grid to recover into the box during the crossing phase. This adds pressure on both the crosser and finishers, increasing realism.Focus: Enhances crossing precision, movement timing and finishing under defensive pressure.

title: Valletta 2 Zone Build Up
instructions_setup: This practice is organised across two connected zones with identical structures. In each zone, the possession team consists of four outfield players plus one goalkeeper, creating a 5v2 against two pressing defenders. Both zones operate simultaneously. The objective for the possession teams is to retain the ball under pressure while looking to score into any of the four mini goals positioned centrally between the two zones.The possession teams can score in two ways. They are awarded two points for scoring into a mini goal from their own zone, or one point for successfully switching play across the grid into the opposite possession zone. The defending players must prioritise protecting the mini goals while also pressing to regain possession. If the defenders win the ball, they are encouraged to attack quickly and score immediately, reinforcing realistic transition behaviours.
coaching_notes: • Scanning and Decision-Making: Encourage players to constantly scan both their own zone and the opposite zone to recognise when to secure possession and when to switch play.• Goalkeeper Involvement: Reinforce the use of the goalkeeper as a key build-up player to create overloads and improve circulation under pressure.• Speed of Circulation: Highlight the importance of moving the ball quickly to draw defenders out and open passing lanes into the mini goals or across zones.• Defensive Priorities: Coach defenders to protect central spaces first, screen passes into mini goals, and then press with control when triggers appear.
progression_one: Touch Limit for Possession Teams:Apply a two-touch limit for all outfield players in possession. This increases the speed of ball circulation and forces quicker decisions in both zones.Focus: Improves tempo, scanning behaviour and technical efficiency under pressure.
progression_two: Allow One Defender to Press Across Zones:Permit one defender to recover or press into the opposite zone after a switch. This reduces time on the ball for the receiving team and increases realism.Focus: Develops quicker ball movement, awareness of pressure and sharper positioning after switches of play.

title: Valletta Finishing Into 2v1
instructions_setup: This practice begins with an unopposed finishing action. Play starts with a pass played into an attacker positioned near a mannequin. The attacker must receive, turn sharply around the mannequin and finish on goal with speed and composure. This phase focuses on quick receiving, body shape and clean execution in front of goal.As soon as the finish is completed, that same attacker must immediately transition into a defensive role to face a live 2v1 against two new attackers. The defending player must delay, protect the central space and attempt to prevent a shot. After the 2v1 phase is complete, the teams swap roles and repeat the sequence, ensuring all players experience both the unopposed finishing action and the defensive transition into an overloaded scenario.
coaching_notes: • Sharp Turn and Finish: Encourage attackers to open their body on the turn, take their first touch forward and finish with minimal delay.• Immediate Transition Reaction: Reinforce the need for instant mindset change—attack to defend with urgency and defensive intent.• 2v1 Defending Principles: Coach the recovering defender to delay, angle their run to show wide and protect central spaces.• Attacking Decision-Making: Highlight the importance of committing the defender in the 2v1 and releasing the pass at the right moment.
progression_one: Add a Time Limit on the Unopposed Finish:Introduce a 3–4 second window from receiving the ball to getting the shot away. This increases urgency and replicates realistic match pressure.Focus: Improves speed of execution and finishing under time pressure.
progression_two: Allow the Defender to Counter After Winning Possession:If the recovering defender wins the ball in the 2v1 phase, allow them to counter and score into a small target goal or dribble through a gate.Focus: Develops realistic transition behaviours and defensive motivation.

title: Valletta Penetrating Between
instructions_setup: This possession practice is set up as a 7v3 rondo with a central target area. The seven attacking players aim to retain possession under pressure while also looking to penetrate between the three defenders. Four mini goals are positioned back-to-back in the centre of the grid, providing clear targets for vertical penetration.The attackers are rewarded with one point for completing a designated number of passes and two points for successfully breaking defensive lines and scoring through any of the central mini goals. The three defenders work as a unit to screen passes, protect the central targets and apply coordinated pressure to force turnovers.
coaching_notes: • Play Between the Lines: Encourage attackers to recognise moments when defenders are disconnected and disguise penetrative passes through the block.• Patience vs Penetration: Reinforce the importance of circulating the ball with purpose—drawing defenders out before threading passes in behind or between.• Body Shape to Receive Forward: Coach players to open up their hips on reception, allowing them to play forward quickly once space appears.• Defensive Compactness: Highlight the need for the three defenders to stay close and connected to prevent split passes.
progression_one: Touch Limit for Possession Team:Apply a two-touch limit for the seven attackers. This increases tempo and demands sharper movement and quicker combinations to create penetration opportunities.Focus: Improves speed of play, awareness and technical efficiency.
progression_two: Allow Defenders to Score on Regain:If the defenders win the ball, allow them to score into two small target goals outside the grid. This adds a transition element and rewards aggressive, coordinated pressing.Focus: Develops defensive transition mindset and purposeful regains.

title: Valletta Pressing Forwards & Finish
instructions_setup: This practice combines repeated pressing actions with a competitive finishing outcome. Play begins with two defending players sprinting into a central grid to press in a 2v4 rondo. Their objective is to work together to regain possession against the four attackers through coordinated pressing, pressing triggers and compact movement.Once the two defenders successfully win possession, they immediately split into two separate smaller grids, each now defending in a 1v3 rondo. They must again attempt to regain the ball individually under fatigue. After winning possession for the second time, each player exits their grid and receives a pass from a coach to finish first time against a goalkeeper. The practice creates a physically demanding pressing sequence followed by a composed end product under fatigue.
coaching_notes: • Pressing Triggers and Angles: Encourage players to press on poor touches, slow passes and when play is forced wide, using curved runs to block passing lanes.• Defensive Work Rate: Reinforce the importance of relentless effort, quick recovery steps and immediate re-engagement during all pressing phases.• Composure Under Fatigue: Coach players to stay calm in front of goal after intense physical effort, focusing on clean contact and placement.• Transition Speed: Highlight rapid movement between each phase—central press, split press and finishing—to keep intensity and realism high.
progression_one: Time Limit to Regain Possession:Add a 6–8 second time window in each rondo for defenders to win the ball. If they fail, the phase restarts. This sharpens pressing speed and collective reactions.Focus: Improves pressing urgency, defensive decision-making and physical output.

title: Valletta Technical Passing
instructions_setup: This technical passing practice is set up as a high-tempo warm-up using two balls simultaneously to maximise repetition and engagement. Players are positioned around the outside of the grid and work through a series of short, sharp passing patterns, constantly receiving and releasing the ball under light pressure. The use of two balls increases scanning demands and keeps players fully alert throughout.The objective is to circulate both balls at speed while maintaining technical quality, rhythm and accuracy. Players must adjust their body shape to receive on the move, play with minimal touches where possible and remain aware of both passing sequences at all times. The practice is ideal for activating technical sharpness at the start of a session.
coaching_notes: • Body Shape to Receive: Encourage players to open up when receiving so they can play forward quickly with their first touch.• Passing Quality: Reinforce firm, accurate passes into the correct foot based on the receiver’s body position.• Scanning and Awareness: Highlight the need for constant head movement due to the presence of two balls operating at the same time.• Tempo and Rhythm: Emphasise maintaining a high speed of movement while staying composed and technically clean.
progression_one: Mandatory Two-Touch Play:All players must now take a minimum of two touches on every reception—one to control and one to pass. This forces players to focus on the quality and direction of the first touch before executing the next pass, rather than rushing the action.Focus: Improves first-touch quality, ball control under tempo, and accuracy of the follow-up pass.

title: Vienna #9 Finish & Link Up
instructions_setup: In this unopposed finishing drill, the centre forward works through two distinct phases to develop shooting accuracy and passing precision. In Phase 1, the centre forward can shoot into either of the two main goals, each guarded by a goalkeeper, within a 30x30 yard small-sided pitch. This phase encourages quick decision-making and composure in front of goal, simulating realistic scoring opportunities under minimal pressure.In Phase 2, the centre forward transitions to a passing task where they must deliver the ball into one of four colour-coded mini goals positioned in each corner of the grid. Players receive a predetermined passing instruction to play into the correct mini goal, reinforcing spatial awareness, accuracy, and controlled passing under match-like conditions.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, decisive shooting during Phase 1 – The centre forward should maintain composure and choose the best goal to exploit the goalkeeper’s positioning.• Stress accuracy and technique in shooting – Controlled, well-placed shots improve scoring efficiency from different angles and distances.• Emphasise correct identification and execution of the pass to the designated mini goal – The player must quickly process instructions and adjust body positioning accordingly.• Reinforce smooth transition between shooting and passing phases – Maintaining focus and intensity through both phases maximises training effectiveness.
progression_one: Add passive goalkeeper movementGoalkeepers perform light lateral movements to increase challenge – This encourages the centre forward to refine shot placement and adapt quickly to changing keeper positions.Focus: Improves shot accuracy and decision-making under variable goalkeeper pressure.
progression_two: Introduce time constraints for passing phaseLimit the time allowed to pass into the correct mini goal after shooting – This develops faster cognitive processing, technical execution, and game-speed decision-making.Focus: Enhances speed of play, technical precision, and mental sharpness under time pressure.

title: Vienna Build Up & Recovery Defending
instructions_setup: This drill begins with two defenders advancing up the grid to receive a pass each from the attackers. The defenders focus on controlling the ball under light pressure before playing a composed, accurate pass into their respective unopposed mini goals. This phase prioritizes ball control, timing, and precise delivery to maintain possession and build confidence in the build-up play.Immediately after completing their passes, the drill transitions quickly as the two attackers launch a fast break, attempting to score on goal. The defenders must execute sharp inside recovery runs to reorganize defensively and defend the ensuing 2v2 attack. This demands quick reactions, strong communication, and coordinated defensive positioning to close down space and delay the attackers. The attackers, meanwhile, must exploit any defensive hesitation with clever movement, quick decision-making, and clinical finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise precise and controlled passing from defenders into mini goals – Players should focus on technique, weight, and timing of passes to maintain possession and accuracy.• Stress the importance of sharp and aggressive recovery runs by defenders – Defenders need to anticipate attackers’ movements and close down space quickly to reduce scoring chances.• Encourage attackers to exploit the transition phase with quick, incisive attacking play – Effective communication and movement off the ball will create opportunities in the 2v2 attack.• Reinforce defensive shape and teamwork during the 2v2 defensive phase – Defenders must communicate effectively, cover for each other, and delay attackers’ progression patiently.
progression_one: Limit defenders to two touches when passing into mini goalsRestrict defenders to a maximum of two touches in the build-up phase to increase pressure and improve speed of play.Focus: Develops quicker decision-making, enhanced technical skill, and encourages sharper, more effective passing under pressure.
progression_two: Introduce a passive attacker during the defenders’ build-up phaseAdd a passive attacker who applies light pressure on defenders during their passes to mini goals, increasing difficulty and promoting composure under pressure.Focus: Improves defenders’ ball control and composure, sharpens passing accuracy, and better prepares players for realistic game pressure.

title: Vienna Continuous 2v2s
instructions_setup: Set on a 30x36 yard small-sided pitch, this dynamic drill features continuous 2v2 attacking phases played end to end. Two attackers work together to break down the defense and score in either the top or bottom goal. Meanwhile, two defenders are assigned to defend the top goal and two others defend the bottom goal continuously, maintaining defensive shape and pressure.Outside the grid, two additional attackers provide service by playing balls into the active attackers inside the pitch. As soon as the attacking pair fails to score or loses possession, they immediately switch roles with the defending team, keeping the drill fast-paced and conditioning-focused.
coaching_notes: • Encourage attackers to use quick combination play and movement to create scoring chances – Effective communication and timing between attackers are essential to break down well-organized defenses.• Stress disciplined defensive positioning for defenders protecting each goal – Defenders must maintain shape, anticipate attacker runs, and close down passing lanes promptly.• Emphasise quick transitions between attack and defense during switches – Players need to mentally and physically reset rapidly to maintain high intensity throughout the drill.• Reinforce accurate and well-timed service from outside attackers – Precise delivery is crucial to allow attackers inside the grid to control and exploit scoring opportunities effectively.
progression_one: Limit attackers to two touches maximumRestrict attackers to two touches per possession to increase pace, force quicker decisions, and improve technical sharpness under pressure.Focus: Develops rapid technical execution, sharper decision-making, and improved teamwork during fast transitions.

title: Vienna Double Ended 2v1s
instructions_setup: This energetic 2v1 drill features two consecutive attacking phases played in opposite directions. The session begins with two attackers working together to outplay a single defender and score in one of two mini goals positioned wide on the pitch. Immediately after completing this phase, players quickly turn around and transition into a second 2v1 attacking scenario going the opposite way, this time aiming to score in the main goal.The drill develops quick attacking combinations, sharp decision-making, and rapid transitional awareness while challenging defenders to maintain positioning and defensive discipline under continuous pressure.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick combination play between attackers – Players must use sharp passing, movement, and communication to exploit numerical advantage effectively.• Stress the importance of defensive positioning in 1v2 situations – Defenders need to anticipate passes, maintain balance, and delay attackers to reduce scoring chances.• Emphasise rapid transition and awareness between phases – Players should quickly reset mentally and physically to maintain intensity and sharpness in both attacking directions.• Reinforce accuracy and composure when finishing into different-sized goals – Attackers must adjust technique and power according to goal size and distance.
progression_one: Limit attackers to two touches maximumRestrict attackers to a maximum of two touches during each 2v1 phase to speed up play and increase pressure on decision-making.Focus: Develops faster technical execution, sharper vision, and improved teamwork under tighter possession constraints.
progression_two: Add a passive defender to the second 2v1 phaseIntroduce a passive defender providing light pressure in the second attacking transition to increase difficulty for attackers and encourage better ball control.Focus: Improves composure under pressure, decision-making in tight spaces, and encourages attackers to shield and protect the ball more effectively.

title: Vienna Fitness & Conditioning
instructions_setup: This fitness and conditioning drill combines high-intensity sprinting with technical passing and quick changes of direction. The player begins by sprinting towards a designated mini goal to deliver a precise pass, emphasizing accuracy under fatigue. Immediately after passing, the player completes a fast sprint up and around a pole, focusing on agility and sharp directional change.Following the pole sprint, the player receives a second ball from a coach or teammate and executes a second pass into a different mini goal. This sequence challenges cardiovascular endurance, explosive speed, and technical skill under physical stress, simulating realistic game demands.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise maximal sprint effort to develop explosive speed – Players should push their pace during each sprint to build conditioning, power, and improve overall game intensity.• Encourage accuracy and weight of passes despite fatigue – Precision in passing under physical pressure replicates real-game scenarios requiring quick, clean technique.• Stress sharp, controlled turns around the pole – Maintaining balance and body control reduces injury risk and enhances rapid change of direction ability.• Reinforce quick mental focus during ball reception – Players must prepare immediately for the second pass while recovering from high-intensity sprinting and turning.
progression_one: Add a time limit for completing the full sequenceSet a strict time target for sprinting, passing, and turning – This encourages players to perform with greater intensity and efficiency.Focus: Develops anaerobic endurance, technical sharpness, and the ability to perform under timed pressure, simulating high-tempo match situations.

title: Vienna Switching Play Rondo
instructions_setup: This technical rondo focuses on switching the point of attack quickly and effectively across two grids. The drill starts with a 4v2 rondo in one grid where the attacking team maintains possession against two defenders. To progress play, attackers must switch the ball to the opposite grid by either penetrating the central line—guarded by the two defending players—or by switching play around the central line to two wide players positioned in boxes on the far side. These wide players are part of the opposite grid, creating a dynamic interplay between both areas.The drill develops quick decision-making, accurate passing under pressure, spatial awareness, and the ability to switch play efficiently to exploit defensive weaknesses.
coaching_notes: • Stress quick, precise passing to maintain possession and exploit switching opportunities – Players must use sharp vision and technique to break the defensive lines effectively.• Encourage defenders to anticipate and guard the central line tightly – Defenders need to communicate and position well to cut off penetrating passes and force wider switches.• Emphasise timing and communication when switching play to wide players – Attackers must coordinate runs and passes to exploit space on the opposite grid efficiently.• Reinforce body positioning and first touch quality when receiving the ball in tight spaces – Players should prepare to quickly control and redirect the ball to keep possession flowing.
progression_one: Limit attackers to two touches maximumRestrict attackers to two touches to increase the speed of play, forcing quicker decisions and more accurate passing under pressure.Focus: Enhances technical precision, faster decision-making, and sharper awareness in high-pressure possession scenarios.

title: Vienna Technical Defending Into 2v2
instructions_setup: This technical defending practice begins with two central defenders defending against two separate, unopposed crosses—one delivered from the right wing and one from the left wing. The initial phase allows the defenders to focus solely on positioning, timing, and aerial duels without pressure, helping them perfect their technique in dealing with wide crosses into the box.After successfully managing both crosses, the drill transitions into a 2v2 defensive phase where the two central defenders face two attackers aiming to score in the main goal. This phase challenges the defenders to apply their positioning skills under live pressure, emphasizing communication, coordination, and defensive shape in a realistic attacking scenario.
coaching_notes: • Stress the importance of balanced positioning during the crosses – Defenders should maintain compactness, communicate clearly, and time their jumps to effectively neutralize aerial threats.• Encourage correct body orientation to anticipate the flight of the ball – This allows defenders to react quickly and clear crosses efficiently.• Emphasise communication and coordination in the 2v2 phase – Defenders must work as a unit, covering space and supporting each other to deny scoring opportunities.• Reinforce controlled aggression and timing when challenging attackers – Well-timed tackles and interceptions reduce risks and maintain defensive solidity.
progression_one: Add passive pressure on crossesIntroduce light pressure on the crosses from attackers positioned near the wings – This forces defenders to adjust positioning and timing more dynamically.Focus: Enhances aerial duel technique and adaptability under mild pressure, encouraging quicker reactions and improved decision-making in contested situations.
progression_two: Increase attacker numbers in 2v2 phaseAdd a third attacker to create a 2v3 situation, increasing defensive complexity – Defenders must communicate effectively and prioritize marking and zonal coverage.Focus: Develops defensive resilience, decision-making, teamwork under numerical disadvantage, and improves spatial awareness while managing increased offensive threats.

title: Vienna Transitions Under Pressure
instructions_setup: This dynamic 1v1 drill focuses on rapid attacking transitions followed by immediate defensive recovery. Players start by attacking and shooting on goal, and immediately after their shot, they transition quickly to defend against the next attacker who sprints towards the opposite goal to score. The defending player’s primary objective is to apply maximum pressure on the attacker in transition, forcing hurried decisions and minimizing scoring chances.This drill develops quick shifts between attacking and defending roles, enhancing players’ fitness, awareness, and tactical discipline. It simulates real-game scenarios where players must instantly switch mindsets and react quickly to changing situations on the field.
coaching_notes: • Stress the importance of explosive reaction immediately after shooting – Players must quickly transition mindset and sprint back to close down the next attacker effectively.• Encourage aggressive but controlled pressure on the attacker – Defenders should close down space quickly without compromising balance or risking fouls.• Emphasise body positioning to force attackers away from goal – Defenders should angle their approach to shepherd attackers into less dangerous areas.• Reinforce communication and awareness of the game flow – Players need to anticipate transitions and position themselves optimally for quick defensive actions.
progression_one: Reduce recovery time between phasesShorten the rest or recovery period between attacking and defensive transitions – This increases physical demand and simulates high-tempo match conditions.Focus: Improves players’ stamina, reaction speed, and ability to sustain high-intensity defensive pressure throughout the game.

title: Villareal 2v2s & Transition
instructions_setup: In this continuous 2v2 transitional attacking drill, two players attack against two defenders aiming to score into either of two mini goals positioned ahead. Once the attacking duo completes their attempt—whether scoring or losing possession—they must immediately transition by turning and defending against the next pair of incoming attackers. This cycle repeats continuously, creating a fast-paced, high-intensity environment that demands quick decision-making and sharp transitions.The drill focuses on developing rapid attacking combinations, defensive recovery, and seamless transition between roles. Players improve fitness, awareness, and the ability to perform under sustained pressure in a game-like setting.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, decisive attacking passes and movement – Attackers should combine swiftly and use sharp runs to create scoring opportunities before defenders adjust.• Stress rapid transition mentality between attacking and defending – Players must switch mindset instantly, reacting quickly to change roles and maintain intensity throughout the drill.• Emphasize communication and spatial awareness for defenders – Defenders need to organize quickly, mark tightly, and anticipate attacker movements to disrupt scoring chances.• Reinforce composure and accuracy when finishing – Attackers should focus on controlled, precise shots to maximize scoring chances even under immediate pressure.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player to Support AttackersIntroduce a neutral player who always supports the attacking team, creating a 3v2 scenario that forces defenders to communicate and adapt quicker.Focus: Improves attackers’ passing options, quick decision-making, and defenders’ organizational skills under increased pressure and overload situations.
progression_two: Restrict Touches for AttackersLimit attackers to a maximum of two touches per possession to increase tempo and encourage sharper technical skills during attacks and transitions.Focus: Enhances technical control, quick thinking, and decision-making speed, promoting a faster and more game-realistic attacking rhythm.

title: Villareal Continuous 1v1s
instructions_setup: This continuous 1v1 drill features two teams positioned on opposite sides of the grid: one team occupies the bottom and right sides, while the other occupies the left and top sides. The first team attacks horizontally across the grid in a 1v1 to score in a mini goal. Once the attack is complete, the other team immediately attacks vertically 1v1 toward their own mini goal.The drill promotes quick transitions between attack and defense, challenging players to win duels under pressure and adapt rapidly to changing angles of attack. The constant switching keeps intensity high and encourages sharp decision-making and conditioning.
coaching_notes: • Encourage explosive first touches and sharp turns – Players must control the ball efficiently and quickly create separation from their opponent with clever movement and agility.• Demand aggressive but controlled dribbling in tight spaces – Attacking players should use feints, changes of pace, and body positioning to beat defenders while maintaining possession.• Reinforce defensive anticipation and positioning – Defenders need to stay balanced, anticipate attacker’s moves early, and use angles to force mistakes or regain possession.• Emphasize quick recovery and readiness after each duel – Both attackers and defenders must stay mentally alert, preparing immediately for the next challenge to maintain drill rhythm and intensity.
progression_one: Add a 5-Second Time Limit to ScoreAttackers must attempt to score within 5 seconds of starting their run, increasing urgency and forcing quicker decision-making and execution under pressure.Focus: Improves speed of thought and action, pushing players to be decisive and clinical in tight timeframes with rapid reaction to defender’s positioning.

title: Villareal Passing Game Warm-Up
instructions_setup: This is a fast-paced, fun warm-up game that promotes awareness, transition speed, and passing accuracy. Two teams compete, with one team starting as defenders, positioned in front of two mini goals. The attacking team looks to pass into either of the mini goals to score while the defenders attempt to block the ball using only their feet or legs — no diving or hands allowed.As soon as a successful pass is made into one of the goals, the passer must immediately sprint to become a defender, and the previous defender quickly joins their team and prepares to receive the next ball. This creates a continuous cycle of attacking and defending roles, sharpening reactions and transition focus.
coaching_notes: • Encourage sharp, snappy passes into mini goals – Players must strike the ball with intent and accuracy while disguising direction and staying composed under pressure.• Demand high communication and quick trigger scanning – Ensure players alert teammates of their movements, check passing lanes early, and decide where to play before receiving.• Reinforce intensity and reaction speed in transition moments – After scoring or losing the ball, players must immediately switch roles with urgency and sprint to defend.• Ensure defenders stay balanced and mobile when blocking – Defenders should use lateral footwork, keep their knees bent, and react instinctively to close down goal angles quickly.
progression_one: Add a 5-Second Scoring LimitAttacking team must attempt to score within 5 seconds of receiving the ball, increasing pace and forcing quick decisions under pressure.Focus: Trains fast decision-making and forces players to create quick solutions in tight time frames with added urgency and increased mental sharpness.

title: Villareal SAQ & 1v1
instructions_setup: This high-energy 1v1 race combines speed, coordination, and technical dribbling under pressure. Two players begin side by side at the base of an SAQ ladder. On the coach’s signal, both players race through their ladders using quick feet and controlled movement. Once clear, they sprint laterally to collect a ball placed ahead of them on the side.After collecting the ball, players immediately dribble through a line of three cones set diagonally in front of them, encouraging close control and body movement. Once through the cones, they attempt to pass cleanly into a mini goal at the end of their lane. The first player to score earns a point for their team.This competitive format builds intensity, improves foot speed, and develops technical composure under physical fatigue.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize sharp, accurate footwork through the ladder – Players must stay light on their toes, focusing on rhythm and control throughout the pattern.• Encourage powerful, lateral sprinting after the ladder – Players should drive forward aggressively and stay low to accelerate efficiently into the ball pick-up.• Promote close, controlled touches through the cones – Use both feet when dribbling and keep the ball tight to the body while changing direction.• Stress calm, composed finishes into the mini goal – Even in a race, players should stay focused on accuracy and weight of pass when finishing.
progression_one: Add a Final Sprint After the PassOnce players pass into the mini goal, they must complete a short 5m sprint to a finish cone to fully complete the round.Focus: Reinforce full intensity through to the end of the task, improving work rate and recovery speed after technical actions.

title: Villareal SAQ Warm Up
instructions_setup: This dynamic warm-up drill focuses on crisp passing, explosive footwork, and individual ball control. Players begin by playing a firm pass into a teammate, executing a 1-2 combination, then immediately sprinting forward into an SAQ ladder to work on quick feet and coordination.After completing the ladder, they receive the ball back from their partner and perform a skill move (e.g., step-over, scissors, or feint) to beat a mannequin. They then dribble into space before returning to the start. The practice develops tempo, technical sharpness, and movement efficiency in a game-relevant context.
coaching_notes: • Focus on crisp, accurate passing in the 1-2 – Players should punch passes with proper weight, scan before receiving, and open their body for a clean return under light pressure.• Promote light, controlled footwork through the ladders – Keep heads up, arms relaxed, and concentrate on rhythm and speed of movement to mimic sharp directional changes seen in games.• Encourage explosive reception after the ladder exit – Players must be prepared to receive at pace, shift their body to control instantly, and transition into the next action without delay.• Stress creativity and confidence when beating the mannequin – Use a skill move with speed and intent, maintain close control, and accelerate past the mannequin with purpose into space.
progression_one: Use a Moving Server for Return PassInstead of a static pass returner, the server moves laterally after the first pass, forcing the player to adjust angles and foot positioning.Focus: Improves awareness and timing of movement after the pass, sharpening real-game passing dynamics, reactions, and scanning under pressure.

title: Villareal Wide Progression Into Finish
instructions_setup: In this wide progression drill, the attacking team begins with possession inside a 15x15 yard grid located in the wide zone. Their objective is to skillfully progress the ball past two defenders positioned to block their advance. Once the attackers successfully bypass the defenders, they are allowed to deliver a cross into a single attacker positioned centrally for an unopposed finish on goal.This drill emphasizes wide play development, encouraging quick combinations, effective use of space, and accurate crossing. It also develops attackers’ timing and finishing skills in a controlled, yet game-realistic scenario.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, precise passing and smart movement – Players must keep ball control tight while using sharp combinations to beat defenders effectively and create clear crossing lanes.• Stress awareness and timing of runs into the box – Attackers should time their runs perfectly to meet the cross, maximizing scoring opportunities with well-coordinated movement.• Emphasize accuracy and quality of crosses – Crosses should be delivered with the right pace and placement to allow the attacker an easy, unopposed finish.• Reinforce defensive pressure and compactness – Defenders need to maintain close marking and communicate effectively to prevent easy ball progression and crossing opportunities.
progression_one: Add a Second Attacker to the FinishIntroduce a second attacker making a simultaneous run into the box to create more dynamic finishing options and force defenders to make quick decisions.Focus: Enhances attacker’s timing, spatial awareness, and decision-making under pressure while encouraging defenders to adjust marking and communication rapidly.
progression_two: Limit Crossers to One Touch DeliveryRequire players crossing the ball to deliver their pass with one touch, increasing the pace and challenge of execution in the wide zone.Focus: Develops quick decision-making, technical precision, and sharp timing for both crossers and attackers, simulating high-pressure game scenarios.

title: Villareal Y-Passing Into Score
instructions_setup: This Y-shaped passing pattern is designed to activate players through clean combination play and structured movement. Players begin at the base of the Y, making a sharp pass into one of the wide arms, where short combinations are played to simulate midfield passing movement and third-man runs.Rather than recycling the ball back to the start, the final player in the sequence plays a firm pass into a mini goal. They then jog or sprint back to the base, collect a new ball, and the sequence repeats. This continuous cycle develops rhythm, accuracy, and end-product focus within the warm-up phase.
coaching_notes: • Encourage sharp, snappy passes across the Y shape – Players must pass with correct weight and direction, opening their body to support the next movement phase consistently.• Demand high communication and quick trigger scanning – Ensure players check shoulders early, communicate next actions, and are aware of where to play before receiving.• Reinforce timing and angles of movement throughout pattern – Off-ball players should arrive on time to receive and position themselves at optimal angles for smooth combinations.• Ensure final pass into goal is clean and accurate – Players must treat the pass like a finish, striking with precision, focus, and awareness of the goal’s position.
progression_one: Add a Passive Defender in Front of Mini GoalA passive defender stands between the final passer and the mini goal, forcing a curved pass or disguised delivery.Focus: Encourages creativity, composure, and precision on the final ball, simulating real matchplay passing lanes and defender movement.

title: Villarreal SAQ Race & Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving speed, agility, and finishing under pressure. Play starts with two players competing head-to-head in a SAQ (Speed, Agility, and Quickness) race. The first player to reach the ball will then transition into an unopposed finishing scenario. The second player must quickly react, recover, and sprint backwards to their designated pole before getting ready for the next round.The drill improves reaction times, acceleration, and the ability to finish under pressure after a competitive race.
coaching_notes: • Quick Acceleration: Emphasize the importance of explosive acceleration as soon as the whistle is blown, focusing on the initial burst of speed to get to the ball first.• Reactivity and Recovery: The second player must react quickly and use proper running technique to recover fast to their designated pole, maintaining focus throughout the drill.• Finishing with Composure: The player who wins the race should focus on staying composed while finishing, even after a competitive sprint. Encourage calmness when taking the shot.• Efficient Footwork: In the SAQ race, players should focus on short, quick steps to optimize their speed and make sure they maintain balance and control when changing direction.
progression_one: Add Pressure to the Finish:After the race, introduce a defender who applies pressure as the player finishes, forcing the player to make a quick decision and take the shot under pressure.Focus: This progression simulates game-like situations, where players need to focus on finishing while under competitive pressure from an opponent.
progression_two: Increase Sprint Distance:Increase the distance in the SAQ race, forcing players to sustain their sprint over a longer distance before transitioning to the finish.Focus: This progression challenges players to maintain speed and composure throughout a longer sprint, helping them build endurance while maintaining a high level of performance.

title: Vitesse 2 Team Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill focuses on quick passing combinations and finishing under minimal pressure. The setup consists of two 18-yard boxes with two goals positioned opposite each other. One team will shoot into one goal, while the other team will shoot into the opposite goal. Each team has a player positioned on the center line who plays a 1-2 combination with the shooter, who then becomes the player on the center line after completing their finish.The drill emphasizes timing, communication, and finishing accuracy after receiving a well-timed pass.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing: Players should focus on making accurate and quick passes during the 1-2 combination. Ensure that the player receiving the ball on the center line times their movement well to meet the pass and create a clean shooting opportunity.• Composed Finishing: After receiving the ball from the center line, the shooter should remain composed and focus on their technique when finishing, whether it's with a volley, header, or controlled finish.• Fluid Movement: The shooter should maintain fluid movement, immediately transitioning to the center line after their shot. This quick change ensures constant activity and keeps the drill moving at a high pace.• Proper Follow-Through: Emphasize the importance of a proper follow-through after the shot. Players should finish with their head over the ball, ensuring clean contact and accuracy when striking.
progression_one: Add a Defender:Introduce a defender in the shooting area, challenging the shooter to finish under minimal pressure while maintaining focus on the 1-2 combination.Focus: This progression simulates match scenarios, where players must react quickly to pass and finish under slightly more realistic pressure.
progression_two: Vary the Passing Angle:Vary the angles from which the center line player delivers the pass, encouraging the shooter to adapt their positioning and movement to receive and finish from different situations.Focus: This progression helps players become more versatile in their finishing ability, preparing them for a variety of in-game scenarios where they might need to adjust their positioning.

title: Vitesse Back 3 Build Up Patterns
instructions_setup: This unopposed passing and movement drill is designed to replicate build-up patterns within a back 3 formation. The setup includes 8 stations, shaped to reflect typical positions of a back 3 and supporting midfielders/wing-backs, arranged in a mirrored pattern.Two balls are active simultaneously, each starting at opposite ends of the grid and moving through the same passing sequence but in opposite directions. The practice is continuous and flows without the ball leaving the designated area.The focus is on executing a variety of build-up patterns commonly used by teams operating with a back three—ranging from switches across the back line to vertical passes into midfield and wide overloads.
coaching_notes: • Body Shape & Scanning: Players must open up and receive side-on, scanning the next passing option before the ball arrives.• Tempo & Rhythm: Encourage a consistent tempo and clean technique with every pass and movement—timing and precision are key.• Communication: Even though unopposed, demand clear communication, including verbal cues and hand gestures to mimic game-like build-up scenarios.
progression_one: Add a Passive Pressing Trigger:Introduce a floating passive defender who moves slowly within the grid to simulate light pressing pressure or passing lane denial.Players must now scan, adjust angles, and play around the passive obstacle.Focus: Develops awareness, angle creation, and subtle decision-making adjustments under minimal pressure.

title: Vitesse Double Phase Overload
instructions_setup: This double-phase overloaded drill helps improve attacking combinations and finishing under pressure. The first phase begins with 3 attackers trying to score into one of two mini goals while being defended by 2 players. The attackers should focus on creating space through quick passes and movement to break down the defense and score.Once the first phase is complete, one of the attackers transitions to the wide channel. They receive a pass from the coach and now face a new 3v2 situation, aiming to score in the main goal. The drill emphasizes quick decision-making and fluid transitions between the two phases, with attackers constantly shifting their roles.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision-Making: Attackers should make quick decisions in both phases, choosing whether to take a shot, pass, or dribble based on the defenders’ positioning and movement.• Creating Space: The attackers should focus on making runs that stretch the defensive shape, creating space for their teammates to exploit in both phases of the drill.• Effective Combinations: Encourage the attackers to use short, quick combinations in both phases. This can help break down the defenders and create more goal-scoring opportunities.• Composed Finishing: In both phases, players should remain calm and composed when shooting, ensuring they choose the right technique (e.g., placing the ball in the corner) to increase the chances of scoring.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the Wide Channel:Introduce an additional defender into the wide channel for the second phase. This increases the pressure and forces the attackers to be more precise in their decision-making and movement.Focus: This progression challenges attackers to create a 3v2 overload in tighter spaces, improving their ability to break down more compact defensive setups.
progression_two: Limit Time for First Phase:Limit the amount of time attackers have to complete the first phase, encouraging quicker, more dynamic play with fewer touches and faster decisions.Focus: This progression focuses on improving the speed of decision-making and execution, simulating match situations where attackers must respond quickly to create goal-scoring chances.

title: Vitesse Finishing the Attack 2v2
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on switching play quickly and creating goal-scoring opportunities from wide areas. Play starts with an unopposed switch from the winger to the central midfielder, who then passes it back out to the winger. The winger will then deliver a cross into the box, where a 2v2 situation unfolds as the two attacking players attempt to finish the ball into the goal.After each rep, the players quickly swap ends and repeat the process in the opposite goal, simulating game-like transitions and improving both crossing accuracy and finishing under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick and Accurate Passing: Focus on quick, precise passing when switching play from the winger to the central midfielder and back. The speed and accuracy of the ball movement are crucial for breaking down the defense.• Timing the Cross: The winger must time the cross perfectly, ensuring that the ball is delivered into the path of the attackers making their runs. Focus on crossing with both pace and accuracy to allow attackers to finish under less pressure.• Movement in the Box: The attackers need to time their runs into the box and look to exploit space created by the cross. Good timing and positioning are key to getting on the end of the ball.• Composed Finishing: Attackers should remain calm and composed when finishing the cross, choosing the best technique based on the situation, such as a volley, header, or controlled finish.
progression_one: Add a Defender to the 2v2:Introduce a defender into the 2v2 scenario, increasing the pressure on the attackers and forcing them to make quicker decisions in the box.Focus: This progression works on decision-making and the ability to finish under pressure with defensive pressure in the box.

title: Vitesse Passing Patterns
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on improving passing accuracy, movement, and ball control through quick and efficient combinations. The practice is set up with 4 balls working simultaneously on a rectangular grid, with players positioned at the corners of the grid. Each player will pass to the next player in the sequence and follow their pass to the next corner, ensuring continuous movement and passing.Players work on short, sharp passes and quick combinations to move the ball from corner to corner. The drill emphasizes the importance of good first touches, precise passing, and supporting runs after every pass.
coaching_notes: • Accurate Passing: Focus on making crisp, accurate passes to teammates, ensuring that the ball reaches its intended target with the correct weight and timing.• Quick Movement: Players must always follow their pass and immediately make a supporting run to the next corner. Timing and positioning are key to maintaining fluid movement.• First Touch: Encourage players to take a positive first touch that sets them up for the next pass, helping the flow of the drill remain smooth and fast.• Communication: Players should communicate with each other to ensure they are aware of when to pass and when to move into the correct position for the next combination.
progression_one: Introduce One-Touch Passing:Players are now restricted to using only one touch for each pass. This increases the tempo of the drill and forces players to be more decisive and efficient with their touches.Focus: This progression helps improve quick decision-making and technical execution under pressure.

title: Vitesse Possession & Build Up
instructions_setup: This drill simulates a build-up phase under pressure, where a team of 5 players in possession must work to progress the ball across zones while being pressed by 2 defenders. The key focus is on maintaining possession and breaking the press to advance play forward. The two pressing players aim to stop any forward progression and, if they win possession, quickly transition to attack to score.The practice area is a small-sided pitch with two goals and two goalkeepers. The pitch is split horizontally, with two defenders positioned in each zone. The goalkeepers are part of the possession team, aiding in the build-up play.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement: Players in possession should focus on quick, precise passing and constant movement to create space and evade the pressing players. Quick decision-making is essential to avoid being caught under pressure.• Support Play: Players should always provide support to the ball carrier by offering passing lanes and options to ensure that possession is retained, even under pressure from the defenders.• Communication: Constant verbal and non-verbal communication is necessary to alert teammates to the defensive pressure and to coordinate quick passes or switches to open up new angles for progression.• Defensive Pressure: Pressing players should work on closing down passing lanes, staying compact, and forcing the ball carrier into a situation where they are unable to progress forward.
progression_one: Increase Pressing Intensity:The pressing team can now apply more intense pressure, with defenders allowed to close down more aggressively, forcing the possession team to work on playing quicker passes under higher pressure.Focus: This progression improves players' ability to maintain possession and execute quick passes under more intense pressing conditions.

title: Vitesse Protecting Possession
instructions_setup: In this drill, players work on deceiving the opposition with quick changes in direction, body feints, and double movements. The goal is to lose the defender and create space in order to receive a pass from one of the two players positioned on the outside of the grid. Players must constantly work on their footwork and timing to ensure they are in the right position to receive the ball.To progress the drill, return passes should be made with one touch, emphasizing quick decision-making and ball control. However, as players become more comfortable, they can be encouraged to take 2-3 touches, which adds an element of possession protection and a chance to manipulate the ball under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Quick Movements and Body Feints: Players should focus on using body feints and explosive movements to deceive their defender, making it difficult for them to anticipate where the ball will go.• Create Space: The key is to use the quick movements to create enough space for the pass. Players should make sure their positioning allows them to receive the ball cleanly from the outside players.• First Touch: Encourage players to use a quick, controlled first touch to set them up for the next action, especially when the ball is passed to them under pressure.• Protecting Possession: As players progress to 2-3 touches, they need to work on protecting the ball for a short period, shielding it from the defender and looking for options to play the ball forward or maintain possession.
progression_one: Incorporate a 1v1 Scenario:After receiving the ball, players must immediately attempt to beat a defender in a 1v1 situation. This forces the player to think about how to use deception both when receiving and when transitioning into an attack.Focus: This progression adds an element of decision-making after receiving the ball, improving a player's ability to use quick movements to beat defenders.

title: Vitesse Transition Breakout
instructions_setup: This large-sided counter-attacking drill is designed to help a team develop its ability to transition quickly from deep positions. Play begins with a deep player (starting outside the opposition's defensive half) dribbling into the field and looking to play a forward pass to initiate a counter-attack. The attacking team is overloaded 4v2, giving them a numerical advantage to create a goal-scoring opportunity.After the first phase of the attack concludes, whether through a goal or the ball going dead, a new phase starts in the opposite direction, allowing both teams to practice defending and attacking during transitions.
coaching_notes: • Quick Transitions: Focus on the speed at which the deep player transitions the ball forward. The quicker the ball is played, the more effective the counter-attack will be, catching the opposition off balance.• Numerical Overload: Emphasize the use of the overload (4v2) to create spaces and quick, decisive movements. Players should be encouraged to move the ball quickly and exploit any gaps in the defense.• Finishing: When in the attacking phase, encourage players to get shots off quickly and make good decisions in front of goal, whether that's a pass, a cross, or a direct shot.• Defensive Recovery: The defenders must focus on quickly recovering into the defensive half. The transition from attack to defense can often happen quickly in counter-attacking drills, so defenders must be alert and ready to handle the overload.
progression_one: Add Defenders to the Build-Up:To make the drill more challenging, add one or two additional defenders in the initial phase to delay the counter-attack and force the attacking team to be more patient and precise in their decision-making.Focus: This progression focuses on how the attacking team deals with a more organized defensive structure and still looks to exploit the overload in transition.
progression_two: Restrict the Time to Attack:Limit the time the attacking team has to progress the ball and finish. This can be done by implementing a timer or a set number of passes. This restriction forces quicker decisions and helps develop the ability to score under pressure.Focus: This progression emphasizes fast decision-making, reducing the time to set up and finish attacks.

title: Wales 2v1 Into 3v2 Transition
