instructions_setup: In this practice, play begins with a 2v1 attacking scenario where the two attackers work together to score in the main goal against a single defender. The attackers must use quick combinations and smart movement to create scoring chances while the defender focuses on closing space and disrupting the attack.Once the initial phase ends, the lone defender quickly transitions by running into the next zone to receive a pass from the coach. In this second zone, a 2v2 battle unfolds, creating a 3v2 situation overall. This progression challenges players to adapt rapidly from defense to attack and maintain high intensity throughout continuous play.
coaching_notes: • Encourage sharp, quick passing between attackers – Players must keep the ball moving fast to exploit numerical advantage and create clear scoring opportunities.• Stress defender communication and positioning – The defender should stay alert, anticipate attacker runs, and work to delay or block passing lanes effectively.• Emphasize rapid transition from defense to attack – Players need to switch mindset and roles quickly, maintaining intensity and awareness during phase changes.• Reinforce effective movement off the ball – Attackers and defenders should use smart positioning and timing to create space or close down opponents efficiently.
progression_one: Add a Neutral PlayerIntroduce a neutral player who always plays with the attacking team, increasing attacking options and encouraging quicker passing decisions.Focus: Enhance attacking creativity and overloads, improving player awareness and decision-making under pressure.

title: Wales 3v2 Into 4v3 Counter
instructions_setup: In this drill, play begins with a 3v2 attacking phase inside the grid where the three attackers work together to create scoring chances against two defenders. The attackers should focus on quick, precise passing and intelligent movement to exploit the numerical advantage and find space to attack.After the first phase ends, two wide players enter the grid with a ball to attack the opposite end in a 4v3 scenario. The original 3 attackers from the first phase must quickly transition into defenders to stop the new attackers, creating a dynamic shift that tests players’ ability to switch roles and maintain intensity throughout continuous play.
coaching_notes: • Encourage sharp, dynamic passing to exploit the 3v2 advantage – Players must maintain good body positioning and quick ball circulation to break down the defense effectively.• Stress defenders’ communication and coordinated positioning – Defenders should stay compact, anticipate passes, and apply pressure together to limit attackers’ options.• Emphasize quick transition from attack to defense – Players must react immediately to role changes, staying mentally and physically prepared for defensive duties.• Reinforce off-the-ball movement and spatial awareness – Attackers should use clever runs to create space while defenders must close passing lanes and mark tightly.
progression_one: Add a Neutral Player for AttackersAdd a neutral player who always supports the attacking team in both phases, increasing passing options and encouraging quicker decision-making and movement.Focus: Boost attacking creativity and overloads, enhancing players’ ability to read the game and make smart choices under pressure.
progression_two: Touch RestrictionLimit attackers to a maximum of two touches in both the 3v2 and 4v3 phases to encourage faster play and improved ball control under pressure.Focus: Develop technical precision and speed of execution, fostering quick thinking and sharper passing in tight spaces.

title: Wales Central Build vs 4-4-2
instructions_setup: In this drill, one goalkeeper and five players work together to progress the ball into any of the three mini goals positioned around the grid. They face intense pressure from four defenders arranged in a 2-2 pressing shape that replicates the central pressing structure often seen in a 4-4-2 defensive setup. The attacking team must focus on quick, precise passing and smart positioning to break through this compact press.The drill challenges players to maintain composure under pressure and encourages intelligent movement off the ball to create passing lanes. The goalkeeper plays an important role in initiating play and providing safe passing options, while the attackers must use a combination of short and long passes to exploit gaps and find the mini goals.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick, accurate passing to evade pressure – Players should keep their heads up, use correct weight on passes, and maintain sharp ball circulation to break down the press effectively.• Demand constant communication and coordinated team shape – Players must work together to create angles and support, ensuring the press is stretched and bypassed.• Reinforce the goalkeeper’s role as a key playmaker – The keeper should remain alert, distribute accurately, and help maintain possession under pressure.• Stress intelligent off-the-ball movement to create space – Players need to time runs well and position themselves to offer multiple passing options under tight pressing.
progression_one: Add a Neutral MidfielderInclude a neutral midfielder who supports the attacking team in maintaining possession and creating overloads against the press.Focus: Encourage creativity in build-up play, improve combination passing, and develop better spatial awareness to exploit pressing gaps.

title: Wales Continuous 4v2
instructions_setup: Play starts with 4 players attacking in a 4v2 setup on one side of the grid, working to create a goal-scoring opportunity. The attacking team looks to score by combining and exploiting the space, while the defending team aims to prevent a shot on goal. If the attackers manage to get a shot off or score, they quickly return to the central line and switch to the opposite side to begin a new 4v2.The defending team’s goal is to win possession and then transition quickly to the opposite side by switching play and becoming the new attacking team. The drill focuses on attacking movement, quick transitions, and defensive pressure.
coaching_notes: • Attacking Runs: Encourage attackers to make intelligent runs into space to create passing options. Timing of the runs is crucial to breaking down the defense.• Defensive Shape: Defenders should maintain a compact shape and communicate well to limit the attacking team's options. Quick pressure on the ball is essential to forcing mistakes.• Quick Transition: Once possession is won, the defending team should look to switch the play quickly and create an overload in the opposite 4v2. Speed in transition is key to exploiting the attacking team while they are disorganized.• Finishing: The attackers should be encouraged to take shots early and make quick decisions in front of goal. Focus on quality of finishing and making the most of goal-scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Add Additional Defenders:To increase the difficulty, add an extra defender to the defensive team (making it 4v3). This challenges the attacking team to be more creative and precise in their passing and movement.Focus: The added defender forces the attacking team to be quicker and more efficient in their play, testing their ability to find space and make accurate passes.
progression_two: Limit the Number of Passes:Impose a limit on the number of passes the attacking team can make before taking a shot. This progression emphasizes quick decision-making and finishing under pressure.Focus: This restriction forces attackers to think faster, focusing on efficiency and precision in the build-up play.

title: Wales Finishing Under Pressure 2v2
instructions_setup: In this finishing under pressure drill, play starts with a pass between teammates where the receiving player must quickly turn and shoot while facing intense pressure from two recovering defenders closing down rapidly. The attacker needs to maintain composure and technique despite tight defensive pressure to create a clear scoring opportunity.Immediately after the shot, the two recovering defenders transition into attackers and quickly launch an attack against the opposite goal in a fast-paced 2v2 scenario. This continuous flow trains players to finish under pressure and seamlessly switch roles between defense and attack, simulating realistic game transitions.
coaching_notes: • Stress quick, controlled first touches to enable rapid turning and acceleration – This helps players create space and maintain attacking momentum effectively, even under intense defensive pressure.• Encourage players to use feints and body positioning in tight 1v1s – To deceive defenders, create clear shooting lanes, and gain an advantage by manipulating defensive reactions.• Remind defenders to maintain low, balanced stances and stay patient before committing – This allows better reaction to attacker’s moves, reducing chances of being beaten, and improves defensive timing significantly.• Emphasize composure and accuracy when finishing in tight spaces – Players should focus on precision to consistently score under pressure, balancing placement and shot power carefully.
progression_one: Defenders Start Further BackPosition recovering defenders further from the attackers at the start, increasing attackers’ time and space to finish but requiring defenders to close down quickly.Focus: Improves attackers’ spatial awareness and decision-making while enhancing defenders’ recovery speed and pressing efficiency.
progression_two: Add Touch Limit on AttackersLimit attackers to a maximum of two touches before shooting to increase pace and force quicker decision-making under pressure.Focus: Develops technical sharpness, quick thinking, and composure during high-pressure finishing situations.

title: Wales Overlapping Passing
instructions_setup: In this unopposed passing and mastery drill, players form a circle with one player positioned in the middle with the ball. The ball carrier will pass to an outside player, who then passes to the player on their right. After making the pass, the outside player will overlap, receive the ball back, and become the new inside player. The original inside player then moves to take the place of the outside player.This drill encourages precise passing, timing of movements, and improving technical skills in a dynamic and fluid pattern. It allows players to practice passing accuracy, receiving, and overlapping movements while staying engaged in the activity.
coaching_notes: • Passing Precision: Emphasize the importance of accurate and well-timed passes. The ball should be played firmly but at the correct pace to ensure smooth transitions.• Timing of the Overlap: The overlapping player must time their run to perfection, ensuring they are in the right position to receive the return pass.• Receiving on the Move: Encourage players to receive the ball on the move, using their first touch to set themselves up for the next pass.• Quick Transitions: Once the pass is made, the inside player must transition quickly into the outside role, while the outside player moves into the center, ensuring fluidity and minimal downtime.
progression_one: Add a Second Ball:Introduce a second ball into the drill, with another set of players passing in the opposite direction. This progression increases the intensity and improves players' ability to maintain focus and control under more pressure.Focus: Players must keep their concentration high and make quicker decisions, while maintaining control and accuracy with multiple passes happening simultaneously.
progression_two: Add Movement with No Ball:To increase the intensity, ask the players to perform a certain movement (e.g., a quick sprint or a change of direction) before they pass the ball. This variation enhances the drill's fitness aspect and simulates real-game scenarios where players are constantly moving.Focus: This progression encourages players to incorporate more dynamic movements into their passing, improving their agility, fitness, and awareness.

title: Wales Possession Transfer
instructions_setup: In this practice, there are three teams of 4 players, plus 2 bounce players positioned on either side of the two grids. The team in possession will have a 5v2 overload and must complete 5 passes before attempting to switch play.Once they complete the 5 passes and successfully switch play, two new defenders positioned at the poles must sprint into the new zone and work to win possession of the ball. The emphasis is on quick ball circulation, awareness, and transitioning between zones under pressure.
coaching_notes: • Ball Circulation: Ensure that players are focused on quick, accurate passing to maintain possession under pressure. Encourage them to move into space to receive the ball and create passing options.• Timing of the Switch: Players must be patient and wait for the right moment to switch play. Emphasize timing the switch when the defense is stretched, making it harder for defenders to press effectively.• Defensive Awareness: Defenders sprinting into the new zone must immediately engage and anticipate the attacking team's next move. They should close down space and limit passing lanes to win the ball back quickly.• Quick Transition: Once the switch is made, the attacking team must quickly adapt and shift their focus to the new zone. The defending players must be agile and ready to press immediately.
progression_one: Increase Passing Requirement:Increase the number of passes to 7 before the team is allowed to switch play. This progression forces players to be more patient and maintain possession for a longer period before switching.Focus: The emphasis is on retaining possession for longer periods while ensuring that players remain composed under pressure and execute accurate passes.
progression_two: Add Conditional Passing:Introduce a rule where one player must always receive the ball with a one-touch pass. This progression encourages players to improve their first-touch control, speed up the game, and adapt to quicker decision-making under pressure.Focus: Improving passing speed and decision-making under pressure, while developing technical skills for controlling and distributing the ball quickly.

title: Wales Unopposed Finish Into 3v2 Recovery
instructions_setup: In this drill, play begins with an attacker receiving a pass from a coach positioned behind the goal for an unopposed finishing opportunity. The attacker focuses on composure and technique to execute a clean and accurate finish. Immediately after the finish, the attacker must quickly transition into a defensive role as a 3v2 plus 1 neutral player phase begins in the opposite direction. The attacker aims to recover quickly to restore balance and help their team defend effectively.This practice develops sharp shooting skills under controlled conditions and reinforces rapid defensive transition awareness. Players are challenged to switch mindset instantly from attacking to defending, enhancing their physical and mental responsiveness during match-like scenarios.
coaching_notes: • Encourage focused, composed finishing under pressure – Players should concentrate on striking with accuracy and calmness, simulating game-intensity situations.• Demand immediate mental and physical transition after finishing – Players must quickly switch from attack to defense, recognizing their defensive responsibilities.• Reinforce communication and teamwork during defensive recovery – Players should coordinate with teammates and use effective communication to maintain defensive shape.• Stress awareness of numerical balance in transition phases – Players need to track opponents and adjust positioning to help regain equal defensive numbers quickly.
progression_one: Add Time Pressure on FinishIntroduce a time limit for the attacker to finish, increasing urgency and simulating tight game scenarios.Focus: Improve quick decision-making and shooting accuracy under increased pressure to mimic real match intensity.

title: Warsaw Compact Combos & Finishing
instructions_setup: This drill is designed to improve team possession under pressure and quick transition into attack. The practice takes place in a 20x35 yard grid with a goal positioned at each end. The possession team consists of 4 outfield players plus 2 goalkeepers and 1 neutral player, creating a numerical advantage of 7 players maintaining ball control against 4 pressing opponents. The possession team’s primary task is to retain the ball by using effective passing, movement, and support play.If the pressing team manages to win the ball cleanly, they immediately transition into attack and attempt to score in either of the two main goals at opposite ends of the grid. This creates a realistic game scenario where players must be alert in possession and prepare quickly to defend or attack based on the turnover.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Quick, Accurate Passing and Smart Movement – Encourage players to maintain sharp passing angles and constant movement to support possession under pressure.• Promote Effective Communication Among Possession Team – Players must talk actively to organize and anticipate pressing movements, improving overall team cohesion.• Stress Awareness and Immediate Transition After Losing Possession – Possession players should quickly shift mindset from offense to defense to delay or prevent counterattacks.• Encourage Aggressive Pressing and Fast Counterattacks – The pressing team must work as a unit to win the ball quickly and transition with speed to exploit the goals effectively.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Possession PlayersIntroduce a two-touch maximum for the possession team to increase pressure and improve quick decision-making.Focus: Enhances technical precision and rapid ball circulation under tighter constraints, improving possession speed.

title: Warsaw Continuous Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: This high-intensity rondo drill is set up using three connected 15x15 yard grids, each occupied by teams of six players. The drill focuses on fitness, quick reactions, and possession skills under pressure. At the coach’s whistle, two players from the first grid sprint into the second grid to press and attempt to win possession in a challenging 2v6 situation. Their goal is to disrupt the larger possession team and regain the ball quickly.Once these two players successfully win possession in the second grid, two players from the second grid then immediately sprint into the third grid to repeat the same pressing and winning scenario. Following this, two players from the third grid will run into the first grid to continue the cycle. This rotation maintains continuous movement, combining cardiovascular fitness with sharp decision-making and technical ability in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Explosive and Quick Transitions Between Grids – Players must sprint rapidly and be mentally prepared to switch roles from possession to pressing instantly.• Stress Communication and Awareness During Rotations – Effective verbal and non-verbal cues will help players anticipate the timing and positioning of incoming attackers.• Promote High-Intensity Pressing with Controlled Aggression – While pressing hard, players need to maintain discipline to avoid fouls and maintain effective pressure.• Focus on Maintaining Possession Under Intense Pressure – Possession teams should use quick, precise passing and smart body positioning to withstand the 2v6 challenge.
progression_one: Reduce Recovery Time Between RotationsShorten the rest or pause between rotations to increase fitness demands and test players' endurance.Focus: Builds greater aerobic capacity and mental resilience by minimizing recovery and encouraging sustained high effort.
progression_two: Limit Touches for Possession TeamsImplement a maximum of two touches per possession player to increase technical difficulty and decision speed.Focus: Enhances quick ball control and sharp passing under intense pressure, improving technical and tactical sharpness during fitness work.

title: Warsaw Double 1v1s
instructions_setup: This drill is set up on a 30x36 yard pitch with two main goals, each guarded by a goalkeeper. Teams are divided with two players positioned on the left side and two players on the right side of the grid. The drill begins with simple passing across the grid between teammates, establishing possession and connection before the competitive phase starts.Once the initial pass is played, a 1v1 attacking and defending phase immediately begins on each side. The player who made the pass now quickly transitions to defend the teammate receiving the ball, resulting in two simultaneous 1v1 battles. This dynamic setup challenges players to react swiftly both offensively and defensively while working under pressure in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Quick Transition Between Attacking and Defending Roles – Players must rapidly switch mindset and positioning from passer to defender to maintain intensity and effectiveness during 1v1 duels.• Encourage Sharp, Controlled Dribbling and Ball Manipulation in Tight Spaces – Attackers should use close control and change of pace or direction to create separation and scoring opportunities.• Focus on Defenders’ Anticipation and Positioning to Limit Attacking Options – Defenders need to read the attacker’s moves early and position themselves to block passing lanes and shooting angles.• Promote Communication and Awareness to Manage Simultaneous 1v1s Effectively – Players should stay alert to both their duel and the overall game context to optimize decision-making and spatial awareness.
progression_one: Allow Defenders to Support Each Other Post TransitionPermit defenders to briefly support their teammate in the adjacent 1v1 by double-teaming before settling back, increasing defensive complexity and encouraging teamwork.Focus: Develops coordinated defensive strategies and communication under pressure, fostering better collective defending in 1v1 situations.

title: Warsaw Finishing From Cutbacks
instructions_setup: This drill develops players’ ability to switch the ball quickly and accurately from one side of the penalty area to the other, encouraging good ball circulation and creating space in wide areas. Players work on maintaining possession with crisp passing, focusing on moving the ball from side to side outside the box to manipulate defensive shape and open passing lanes.The final pass is a penetrative through ball played into a winger on the opposite side, who immediately delivers a first-time cut-back cross into the half space. Attackers time their runs to exploit this space and receive the cut-back for an unopposed finish inside the box. This practice sharpens the timing and execution of attacking runs and crossing, improving the ability to create and finish goal-scoring chances from wide positions.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Quick, Accurate Switching of Play to Create Space – Players must focus on crisp, well-weighted passes combined with clear communication to effectively shift the defense and open passing lanes.• Stress Precision and Timing of the Penetrative Pass Behind Defenders – The final through ball must be perfectly weighted and timed to allow the winger to receive the ball in stride and maintain attacking momentum.• Promote First-Time Cut-Back Crosses with Proper Weight and Accuracy – The winger’s delivery needs to be fast, precise, and measured to catch defenders off guard and create clear goal-scoring opportunities.• Focus on Well-Timed Runs Into the Half Space by Attackers – Attackers should coordinate their movements carefully to exploit the space created by the switch and arrive in the optimal position to finish confidently.
progression_one: Include a Second Attacker for Near-Post OptionsAdd a second attacker making near-post runs, creating multiple crossing options and forcing the winger to read the defense and choose the best delivery.Focus: Enhances attacking creativity, increases finishing variations, and encourages precise reading of defensive positioning for optimal crossing choices.

title: Warsaw Penetrate to Finish
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on attacking combinations around the penalty area with the aim of developing sharp, quick interplay to create clear scoring opportunities. Players will work together to execute purposeful passing sequences and movement patterns to break down the defense before finishing in the main goal against a goalkeeper, honing their timing and precision in the final third.The drill then immediately transitions to a second phase starting from behind the goalkeeper’s goal, where players quickly build play upfield with quick passing and movement. This phase culminates in a penetrative pass into one of two mini goals, encouraging players to improve their vision and accuracy in delivering decisive final passes under match-like tempo.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Sharp, Quick Combinations in Tight Spaces to Break Defenses – Players must focus on clean first touches and rapid decision-making to maintain rhythm and outmaneuver defenders effectively.• Encourage Awareness and Movement Off the Ball to Create Passing Lanes – Intelligent positioning and timely runs are crucial for opening space and supporting teammates during the attacking phase.• Stress Composure and Accuracy in Finishing Against the Goalkeeper – Players should maintain calm under pressure to execute precise and confident shots on target.• Promote Quick Transition and Intelligent Passing from Behind the Goal – The second phase requires sharp vision and timing to release accurate penetrative passes to the mini goals quickly.
progression_one: Alternate Starting Sides Behind the GoalSwitch the starting position behind the goalkeeper’s goal to the opposite side to challenge players’ adaptability and encourage using both feet and varied passing angles.Focus: Develops versatility in attack, improves weak foot passing and finishing, and sharpens spatial awareness across different field orientations.

title: Warsaw Recovery Defending 1v1
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on the attacker receiving a pass just outside the box and making a forward run into the box with the objective of scoring. The attacker is immediately pressured by a recovering defender who must sprint around two poles positioned before the box. The defender’s challenge is to complete this high-intensity recovery run quickly enough to close down the attacker and engage in a 1v1 duel inside the box. This setup develops the attacker’s ability to manage pressure and finish under duress while improving the defender’s recovery speed and timing.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize Explosive First Touch and Acceleration by the Attacker – The attacker’s ability to control the pass and accelerate quickly can create crucial separation before defensive pressure arrives.• Encourage Defenders to Maintain High Intensity on Recovery Runs – Defenders should push their pace around the poles to close down the attacker as fast as possible while maintaining balance.• Promote Decision-Making in Tight 1v1 Situations – Both attacker and defender must make quick, intelligent choices to beat their opponent or prevent a goal.• Focus on Composure and Precision in Finishing Under Pressure – Attackers need to stay calm and select their shot carefully to convert despite the defender’s close presence.
progression_one: Introduce a Passive Second DefenderAdd a second defender who starts passive but can join the 1v1 if the first defender delays recovery.Focus: Improves attacker’s ability to handle layered defensive pressure and decision-making in more complex scenarios.

title: Warsaw Switching Play to Create
instructions_setup: This drill focuses on developing fluid attacking combinations in wide areas, emphasizing quick interplay and effective switching of play. Three players will work together in a wide zone, combining through quick passes and movement to create space and destabilize the defense. After establishing the combination, the attacking team switches the ball rapidly to the opposite wide area to exploit space and prepare for a crossing opportunity.Once the ball is switched, the wide player delivers a cross into the box where three attackers coordinate their runs to finish the move unopposed. The drill encourages timing, communication, and precise execution of combination play and crossing to create high-quality scoring chances.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Sharp, Accurate Passing and Quick Combinations – Focus on crisp passes and fluid movement to break down defensive lines effectively.• Stress the Importance of Effective Switching of Play – Players must recognize moments to switch the ball quickly to exploit the opposite wide area’s space.• Promote Well-Timed Runs into the Box for Crossing Opportunities – Attackers should coordinate their runs precisely to meet the cross in optimal scoring positions.• Focus on Controlled and Confident Finishing Techniques – Emphasize composure and technique in unopposed finishing to maximize scoring chances.
progression_one: Add Passive Defenders to Apply Light PressureIntroduce passive defenders in wide areas to increase decision-making speed and passing accuracy under mild pressure.Focus: Improves player awareness and precision while maintaining the attacking pattern under slightly increased defensive pressure.

title: Warsaw Wide Rotation Patterns
instructions_setup: This practice focuses on developing fluid rotations and combinations between the full back, winger, and central midfielder, replicating realistic scenarios for playing out from the back. Players work on coordinated movements and quick passing exchanges to create space and progress the ball effectively through the wide and central areas.By emphasizing varied combination patterns, the drill encourages players to understand positioning, timing, and communication to unlock defenses. This enhances their ability to manipulate opponents and maintain possession under minimal pressure, setting a foundation for more complex attacking sequences.
coaching_notes: • Encourage Precise and Confident Passing to Maintain Possession – Accurate, well-weighted passes help keep the ball moving smoothly and reduce turnover risks during rotations.• Focus on Coordinated Movement and Timing to Create Passing Angles – Players should time their runs and rotations carefully to open space and offer clear passing options for teammates.• Promote Communication Between Players to Enhance Understanding – Constant verbal and non-verbal cues improve coordination and help anticipate each other’s intentions.• Stress Patience and Awareness to Exploit Defensive Gaps – Players must read the play and delay when necessary to draw defenders out of position and create better attacking opportunities.
progression_one: Introduce Passive Defensive PressureAdd light, passive defensive pressure to challenge players to execute rotations and passes under slight opposition, encouraging sharper decision-making and quicker ball movement.Focus: Develops composure and precision when facing defensive disruption, improving players’ ability to maintain control and create space in pressured situations.

title: Watford 352 Rondo
instructions_setup: This rondo breaks a 352 formation down into specific zones, where the possession team will play 4v2 or 3v2. The #6 is required to slide horizontally to work across both of the bottom 2 zones, while the #10 can be allowed to slide vertically to create 4v2's. The practice transitions into a 6v3 centrally if the pressing team manages to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Horizontal Movement of the #6 – The #6 should focus on covering both bottom zones by sliding horizontally. Encourage them to read the game and identify when they should move to create overloads and support the possession game.• Vertical Movement of the #10 – The #10 must focus on creating overloads by sliding vertically. This movement is essential to breaking defensive lines and offering a passing option. The #10 should look for opportunities to create 4v2 situations in the top zones.• Pressing and Anticipation – The pressing team should focus on cutting off passing lanes and forcing the possession team into difficult areas. They must remain compact and organized, aiming to regain possession quickly and transition into an attacking scenario.• Creating Overloads – The attacking team needs to focus on combining passes quickly to maintain possession. By moving the ball around and working together, they can create spaces for a 4v2 or 3v2 in the key zones of the field.
progression_one: Reduced Grid SizeReduce the size of the grid to increase the intensity of the rondo, forcing players to make quicker decisions and pass the ball faster.Focus: Speed of passing and decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Counter-Attack OptionAllow the pressing team to counter-attack immediately if they win possession, transitioning from the 6v3 central overload into a fast attack. The defending team must recover quickly to prevent a successful counter.Focus: Fast counter-attacking and quick defensive recovery.

title: Watford Build the Attack
instructions_setup: This build-up practice focuses on developing a team's ability to progress play against an opposition midfield 3. The central defenders (#5 and #4) and the centre forward (#9) are unopposed, while the players inside the central grid are opposed. The team building up must focus on breaking lines through passing, dribbling, and quick combinations, aiming to score into either of the two mini goals. The 3 pressing defenders (reds) attempt to win possession and then quickly transition to attack by scoring into any of the mini goals directly ahead of them. The two defenders (#5 and #4) can step in to protect the mini goals after losing possession.
coaching_notes: • Breaking Lines – Encourage players to make penetrating passes, dribbles, and runs that break through the opposition midfield. The central defenders (#5 and #4) should look for opportunities to play direct passes or use the centre forward (#9) as a focal point to progress the ball forward.• Quick Combinations – Stress the importance of quick combinations between the central defenders and the centre forward to create space and disorganize the opposition midfield. Players must work together to maintain fluidity and increase the speed of play to move the ball past the opposition press effectively.• Decision-Making Under Pressure – The team building up should be taught to make quick decisions while under pressure from the 3 pressing defenders. This includes knowing when to play simple passes, when to dribble, and when to combine with teammates to break the opposition's lines.• Defensive Transition – When the opposition wins possession, emphasize the defensive transition of the central defenders (#5 and #4). These defenders should immediately step in to block shots or prevent counter-attacks, using their positioning and awareness to help protect the mini goals.
progression_one: Limit Time to BuildIntroduce a time limit for the team to complete the build-up and break the lines. This will increase the intensity of the drill, forcing the team to make faster decisions and execute quicker passes, simulating game-like pressure.Focus: Improve decision-making and speed of play under time constraints.
progression_two: Add More DefendersIntroduce an additional defender or two into the midfield grid to increase pressure on the team building up. The added defenders will make it harder to progress the ball, requiring the team to make more creative decisions and use effective combination play to break through.Focus: Improve the ability to break through a more compact and organized defensive midfield.

title: Watford Combo & Finishing
instructions_setup: Set up two 18-yard boxes facing each other with a goal and goalkeeper at either end, creating a small-sided game-style pitch. Each goalkeeper starts the practice by passing into a group of three central players positioned in front of them. There are two mirrored groups of three players, one for each goalkeeper.The three central players work together using quick, fluid, one-touch combinations to break forward and finish into the goal opposite to where the ball was served from. The emphasis is on movement, awareness, and clinical end product following fast build-up play.
coaching_notes: • Encourage the receiving player to set a firm, clean first touch that invites the next combination pass immediately.• Focus on sharp one-touch play, clever angles, and intelligent supporting runs to create space within tight areas.• Demand quality final passes into shooting positions, with players timing their movement to strike the ball cleanly.• Reinforce constant communication and visual scanning between players to anticipate the next action under pressure.• Highlight the importance of quick recovery and resetting after finishing to maintain the flow and tempo of the practice.
progression_one: Introduce Passive DefendersAdd a passive defender between each group of three to apply light pressure and force quicker combinations under realistic conditions.Focus: Improving ball speed, decision-making, and player movement to operate effectively under limited time and space.
progression_two: Transition After ShotAfter a shot is taken, the shooter must immediately sprint and pressure the goalkeeper about to start the next repetition.Focus: Building a transition mentality, encouraging quick recovery, and adding intensity to both attacking and defensive actions.

title: Watford Mastery Warm Up Game
instructions_setup: Each team has 4 balls per round, with both players having 2 balls each. The teams must attempt to score with as many of the 4 balls as possible by using turns, skills, and fast dribbles to create space. The 2 defending players must attempt to match the runs and movements of the dribbling players and protect their mini goals. Once Team A has used all 4 balls, the teams will rotate, and Team B will attempt to score as the attacking team.
coaching_notes: • Skill Application – Emphasize the use of quick turns, feints, and dribbling skills to break past defenders and create space. Players should be encouraged to get creative with their ball control and take on defenders when possible.• Defensive Positioning – Defenders should focus on staying compact and positioning themselves to force attackers wide or into less dangerous areas. They must avoid ball-watching and track the attackers' movements closely.• Decision-Making – Attackers need to be decisive with their dribbles, deciding quickly when to use a skill move or make a pass. Encourage players to keep their heads up and scan for space or opportunities to exploit.• Teamwork – Both attacking and defending teams should work closely together. Attackers should communicate and set up passing lanes, while defenders should communicate to prevent attackers from creating clear goal-scoring chances.
progression_one: Additional DefendersIntroduce a third defender to increase the difficulty for the attacking team. The attackers will now have to work together even more efficiently to create space and avoid being crowded out.Focus: Improving teamwork and individual skill under pressure.
progression_two: Limited TimeIntroduce a time limit for each attacking phase (e.g., 30 seconds per round). The attacking team must score as many goals as possible within this time, encouraging fast-paced decision-making and execution.Focus: Enhancing the speed of attack and decision-making under time pressure.

title: Watford Overloaded SSG
instructions_setup: This small sided game features a continuous 4v2 practice in a tight space, with the addition of an offside line. The attacking players (4) must make well-timed runs and movements to receive the ball in front of goal, avoiding the offside line while looking for scoring opportunities.If the attacking team scores, they will continue play with a new ball. However, if they fail to score, the attacking players will switch to become the defending team. Two players will defend, and the other two players will position themselves off the field to maintain the flow of the game.
coaching_notes: • Timing of Runs: Attackers must be aware of the offside line and time their runs accordingly. Encourage players to make quick, direct runs into space while staying onside.• Ball Movement: Quick and accurate passing is crucial to create space for attackers. The player in possession must be decisive, looking for opportunities to play a through ball or quick pass into space.• Defensive Positioning: Defenders must work together to limit attacking space, stay compact, and communicate effectively. When switching to defense, they should immediately organize themselves and block passing lanes.• Transition Speed: After a failed attack, emphasize the importance of quickly transitioning between attack and defense. Defenders must be quick to press and regain possession, while attackers should be ready to make runs again once they get the ball.
progression_one: Introduce Time Limit:Add a time limit (e.g., 20 seconds) for the attacking team to score. This will encourage faster decision-making and increase the intensity of the practice.Focus: Speed of play, timing of runs, and quick decision-making under pressure.
progression_two: Add More Defenders:Introduce a second defending pair (2v4) for a brief period, increasing the challenge for the attacking team. This progression will force attackers to be even more precise with their movements and passing.Focus: Improving attacking play under pressure, with emphasis on maintaining composure and working as a team to create scoring chances.

title: Watford Technical Passing
instructions_setup: In a 20x20 yard grid, two teams of 4 players each have their own ball and direction of play. One team works horizontally (left to right), while the other works vertically (top to bottom). Each team has two target players positioned on their respective end lines, with the remaining two players moving freely inside the grid.The objective for each team is to work the ball from one end to the other, using their target players and central roamers in continuous passing combinations. Players are encouraged to use movement, rotation, and awareness to maintain possession and progress play in their designated direction while coexisting with the other team in the same space.
coaching_notes: • Directional Awareness – Players must scan constantly to recognize teammates’ positions and target zones relative to their direction of play.• Sharp Movement After Pass – Encourage players to move into new supporting positions immediately after releasing the ball to maintain fluidity and options.• Rotational Support – Inside players should rotate between high and low positions, offering dynamic angles to link the play between end line players.• Composure in Crowded Space – With two balls in play, reinforce control, communication, and spatial awareness to minimize collisions and maintain purpose.
progression_one: One-Touch to Target PlayerRestrict the final pass into the target player to one touch only, forcing quicker decisions and cleaner buildup play through the central roamers.Focus:Improves technical precision and movement timing in tight areas while demanding better communication and awareness.
progression_two: Neutral Player Support in the GridAdd one neutral player inside the grid who can support both teams, creating overloads and encouraging quick combination play in traffic.Focus:Enhances use of the extra player to create space and improve tempo, while increasing decision-making under dual-team interference.

title: Watford Technical Warm Up & SAQ
instructions_setup: This technical warm-up focuses on developing players' ability to play one-touch passes while maintaining balance and body positioning. Players will execute one-touch passes before immediately moving and touching the cone placed horizontally to them. This drill enhances quick decision-making, technical precision, and movement off the ball.
coaching_notes: • One-Touch Passing – Emphasize the importance of making clean and precise one-touch passes. Encourage players to focus on the weight and accuracy of each pass, ensuring they complete the pass with minimal time spent on the ball.• Balance and Body Positioning – Remind players to maintain proper body posture and balance when receiving and playing the ball. Players should keep their bodies low and stable to maintain control and execute efficient one-touch passes.• Movement After Pass – Ensure players quickly move to the cone horizontally after each pass, focusing on sharp, purposeful movement. This will improve players' ability to read the game and react to passing options quickly.• Timing and Rhythm – Encourage players to maintain a good rhythm with their passing and movement, focusing on timing their actions to ensure smooth transitions between passes and movements to the cone.
progression_one: Add a DefenderIntroduce a passive defender to apply pressure on the player receiving the ball, forcing them to make quicker decisions when playing the one-touch pass. This will increase the intensity and challenge players' ability to maintain composure under pressure.Focus: Improve one-touch passing and balance while handling defensive pressure.
progression_two: Increase the DistanceIncrease the distance between the cones and players to challenge their passing accuracy over a longer range. This forces players to refine their passing technique and maintain control while moving at a higher intensity.Focus: Develop the ability to make accurate one-touch passes over longer distances while maintaining balance and body control.

title: West Ham Finish The Attack
instructions_setup: In this drill, players will work on quick combinations and finishing in and around the goal area. The practice is set up with 3v3 play centrally, with 3 bounce players positioned around the outside of the area. The team in possession can use the bounce players for support, but these players are limited to 1 touch and cannot score. The focus of the drill is to move the ball quickly, break down the defense with fast passes and combination play, and finish with high accuracy in the attacking third.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations – Emphasize the use of fast, sharp passes between teammates in central areas to break down the defense. The attackers should look to link up with bounce players to switch the point of attack and create goal-scoring opportunities.• Movement and Timing – Players should focus on making well-timed runs to receive the ball in space. Encourage attacking players to make diagonal and overlapping runs, pulling defenders out of position and creating more opportunities to finish.• Finishing Under Pressure – The attackers should be encouraged to finish quickly and with composure. Challenge them to make accurate, decisive shots on goal, using both feet when possible, while under pressure from defenders.• Utilizing Bounce Players – Encourage the players in possession to use the bounce players wisely to maintain possession and stretch the defense. The bounce players should be used to reset play or switch the point of attack, creating space and new passing angles for the attackers.
progression_one: Add Defender Pressure on Bounce PlayersAdd a defender to pressure the bounce players, forcing the attacking team to make quicker decisions and improving their ability to play under pressure.Focus:Improves decision-making, speed of play, and composure under pressure.
progression_two: Add Extra Attacker in Final PhaseAdd a fourth attacker in the final phase to increase the attacking overload and give more options to finish the attack, forcing defenders to cope with more attacking threats.Focus:Encourages team coordination and movement to exploit defensive weaknesses, improving finishing in crowded situations.

title: West Ham Mannequin Rondo
instructions_setup: In this 4v1 rondo, the aim is to develop penetrative passes for the possession team and interceptions for the defender. The 4 players in possession must complete 'x' number of passes before attempting to hit the central mannequin with a pass. The defender, who is in the middle of the rondo, must work to prevent the pass to the mannequin by intercepting or disrupting the flow of play. This drill encourages both quick ball movement and defensive anticipation.
coaching_notes: • Penetrative Passing – Encourage the players in possession to look for penetrative passes that break lines and push the ball into dangerous areas. Players should avoid square or backward passes unless necessary and always look for the opportunity to play forward, either through the lines or into the space.• Passing Combinations – The attacking team should focus on quick, dynamic combinations to outplay the defender. Use wall passes, 1-2s, and movement off the ball to create new angles and maintain possession. The focus should be on moving the ball as fast as possible to create a passing lane to the mannequin.• Defensive Anticipation – The single defender in the middle should focus on reading the play and anticipating passes. Encourage the defender to track the ball and the movement of the players, looking for opportunities to intercept the pass to the mannequin. The defender must stay close to the ball while remaining aware of the passing options.• Pressure on the Mannequin – Once a pass is played to the mannequin, the defending player should immediately work to pressure the passer and challenge the receiving player. This adds an extra level of realism to the practice, simulating the final phase of breaking down a defensive block and forcing players to make precise passes under pressure.
progression_one: Add More DefendersAdd a second defender to the middle, creating a 4v2 scenario. This increases the difficulty and forces the possession players to work harder to find the penetrative pass and break down the defense.Focus:Improves decision-making under pressure and passing accuracy in tight spaces.
progression_two: Reduce Number of PassesReduce the number of passes required before attempting to hit the mannequin, forcing the players in possession to play quicker and be more decisive in their passing choices.Focus:Enhances speed of play and quick thinking when under pressure.

title: Wolves 3rd Man Into 1v1
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a 3rd man passing combination that leads to an attacking player receiving the ball and immediately competing in a 1v1 against a defender. The attacker aims to score, while the defender's objective is to win possession of the ball and then dribble through the central gate to score a point.
coaching_notes: • Timing of the 3rd Man Pass – Emphasize the timing and movement of the third man. The pass should be played at the right moment to allow the receiver to attack quickly and use the defender’s positioning to their advantage. The third man must make a well-timed run to open up space and create an effective attacking opportunity.• 1v1 Attack – When attacking in the 1v1 scenario, encourage the player to dribble with purpose and take on the defender with confidence. Attackers should focus on using a variety of moves, like feints or changes of direction, to unbalance the defender and create space to shoot or pass.• Defensive Pressure – Defenders should focus on staying goal-side of the attacker and force them into less dangerous areas. The defender must be aggressive in closing down the attacker, using good body positioning to block the path to goal while waiting for the right moment to win the ball.• Transition After Possession – Once the defender wins the ball, they must immediately transition into attack mode and dribble through the central gate. This transition requires the defender to be sharp, using quick decision-making and exploiting the space to earn a point for their team.
progression_one: Add a Second DefenderIntroduce a second defender to the 1v1 scenario. This forces the attacker to make quicker decisions, and the defenders must work together to contain the attacker and regain possession.Focus:Improves attackers' ability to make decisions quickly under pressure and enhances defenders' ability to work in pairs.
progression_two: Limit the Number of Touches for the AttackerLimit the number of touches the attacker can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches). This will force them to make quicker decisions and improve the speed of their attacks.Focus:

title: Wolves Breakout Rondo
instructions_setup: The practice begins with a 4v2 rondo inside a central grid. The 4 players in possession must retain the ball, completing a set number of passes. If the 2 defensive players win possession, the 4 outside players become live, and a 6v4 is played out inside a larger grid. The attacking team must then look to create space and progress the ball through the larger grid to maintain possession and look for scoring opportunities, while the defending team aims to regain possession.
coaching_notes: • Quick Passing and Movement – Encourage the players in possession to move the ball quickly and look for angles to break through the defensive lines. Quick, one-touch passing, and movement off the ball are key to maintaining possession and progressing the ball through the grid.• Defensive Awareness – The defenders should focus on pressuring the ball while maintaining their defensive shape. They should work together to trap the ball and create turnovers, making sure they cover passing lanes and anticipate where the ball will go next.• Transition Play – Once possession is won, the transition from defense to attack must be fast and decisive. The defending players who win possession must immediately look to exploit the larger grid by transitioning quickly to create a numerical advantage and put pressure on the opposing team.• Communication and Spatial Awareness – Both attacking and defending teams must communicate constantly to adjust positioning and respond to changes in the play. Players should be aware of their teammates’ positioning and always be looking for open spaces to receive or distribute the ball.
progression_one: Increase the Number of DefendersIncrease the number of defenders in the central grid to make it more difficult for the attacking team to retain possession. This will force the attackers to play with greater precision and increase the intensity of the practice.Focus:Improves the ability to retain possession under pressure and develop quick decision-making in tight spaces.
progression_two: Limit the Number of TouchesLimit the number of touches the players can take while in possession. This will force them to move the ball quicker, increasing the tempo and requiring more precise passes and movement.Focus:Enhances passing speed and decision-making in high-pressure situations, encouraging players to think and act quickly.

title: Wolves Continuous Finishing
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice takes place in the size of two 18-yard boxes. There are two goals and two goalkeepers positioned in each goal. A player in the middle acts as the link between the two teams, playing a 1-2 combination pass to receive the ball and finish into the goal. After completing a finish, the player then quickly transitions to the opposite side to receive the ball and repeat the process. This practice focuses on continuous movement and finishing under minimal pressure.
coaching_notes: • Movement and Timing – Players should focus on their movement off the ball, ensuring they are in the right position to receive the pass and finish with minimal delay. The timing of the runs should align with the player playing the 1-2 pass to ensure the ball is delivered at the right moment for an accurate finish.• Finishing Technique – Encourage a variety of finishing techniques, such as side-foot, instep drive, or placement shots, depending on the situation. Emphasize composure and accuracy when finishing in front of goal, ensuring the ball is placed in the most effective area.• Quick Transitions – After completing the finish, players should focus on quickly transitioning to the opposite side of the field to maintain the flow of the practice. Quick movement between each phase ensures the tempo of the practice remains high.• Goalkeeper Awareness – Goalkeepers should be ready to adjust quickly to the angle of the shot and focus on positioning themselves well to save the shots. They should track the ball and anticipate where the shots are likely to come from based on the angle of the pass and the player's run.
progression_one: Add Pressure to the Finishing PlayerIntroduce a passive defender to apply light pressure on the player receiving the ball and preparing to finish. This will help simulate a more realistic game scenario and encourage better decision-making when shooting under slight pressure.Focus:Improves finishing under pressure and enhances decision-making when shooting at goal.
progression_two: Limit Touches for the Finishing PlayerLimit the number of touches the finishing player can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches). This increases the urgency of the practice and encourages players to finish more quickly and decisively.Focus:Enhances quick thinking and sharpens finishing accuracy when under time constraints.

title: Wolves Directional Possession
instructions_setup: Play starts with one of the players on the end lines playing a pass into the center. Teams are playing 2v2 centrally, with the goal of progressing the ball from end line to end line. The attacking team earns points by successfully passing the ball from one end line to the other while maintaining possession against the defending team. The defending team aims to regain possession and prevent the ball from reaching the opposite end line.
coaching_notes: • Positional Awareness – Encourage players to maintain good spacing and positional awareness while in possession. They should use the width of the area to stretch the defenders and create more passing options, making it easier to progress the ball forward.• Quick Decision-Making – Players should focus on making quick decisions when receiving the ball. They should assess whether to dribble, pass, or hold possession based on the positioning of teammates and defenders, using fast ball circulation to break down defensive pressure.• Defensive Pressure and Transition – Defenders should work on pressuring the ball carrier quickly while covering passing lanes. Once possession is regained, they must transition quickly to exploit the attacking end line and score points for their team.• Communication – Strong verbal and non-verbal communication between teammates is vital. Players should talk to each other to create passing lanes, provide support for the ball carrier, and ensure they are prepared to transition when possession changes.
progression_one: Add a Third DefenderAdd a third defender in the middle to increase the defensive pressure. This will force the attacking team to be more creative with their passes and work harder to create space.Focus:Enhances creativity in possession and forces quick passing under defensive pressure.
progression_two: Limit TouchesLimit the number of touches a player can take (e.g., 2 or 3 touches). This will increase the tempo of the game and encourage players to think faster and move the ball with greater precision.Focus:Improves passing speed, decision-making, and reduces unnecessary holding of the ball.

title: Wolves Free Kick Routine
instructions_setup: This unopposed free kick routine drill is designed to help players rehearse and refine various attacking free kick patterns from wide or central areas. The team will focus on the key components of a successful set-piece routine including delivery, movement, and timing. Players will position themselves according to the selected routine (e.g., near post runs, edge of the box setups, far post overloads) and execute planned movements without opposition.The free kick taker will deliver the ball into a designated area, aiming for the appropriate target zone based on the play design. Meanwhile, attacking players will make synchronized runs to either meet the delivery or create decoy movements to free up teammates. This unopposed format allows the team to work on precise timing and technical execution without the distraction of defenders.
coaching_notes: • Run Timing & Synchronization:Attackers must time their runs perfectly in relation to the free kick taker’s delivery. Runs should be coordinated so that the ball is met at the optimal point, with staggered timing to create different attacking options.• Varied Movements:Players should rehearse a variety of runs including curved runs, late arrivals at the far post, and quick darts into central zones. Decoy runs and quick direction changes are essential to unsettle defenders in real match scenarios.• Delivery Execution:The free kick taker should focus on consistent and accurate delivery, using different techniques such as whipped, floated, or driven balls based on the routine. The quality of the ball into the target area is crucial to the success of the routine.• Role Clarity:Ensure every player knows their specific job in the routine — whether it’s to attack the ball, screen a defender, make a decoy run, or be in position for a second ball. Clarity in roles improves execution and reduces hesitation.• Communication:Strong verbal and non-verbal communication is essential between the free kick taker and the runners. Agreed cues or signals should trigger the movement so that everyone is synced to the delivery.
progression_one: Add Light Pressure from DefendersIntroduce passive defenders to lightly mark the runners and challenge aerially. Their role is to track movements and apply mild resistance without aggressively disrupting play.Focus: This adds realism and forces the attacking team to fine-tune timing and positioning under game-like conditions while still maintaining the structure of the routine.

title: Wolves Hexagonal SSG
instructions_setup: This small-sided game is played with 3v3 centrally, with 2 bounce players for each team positioned along two sides of a hexagon in the attacking half. The central players must use the bounce teammates for quick passing combinations, allowing them to create space and generate goalscoring opportunities. The bounce players are limited to one touch and can only pass to players in central areas.
coaching_notes: • Quick Combinations – Emphasize the importance of using the bounce players for quick attacking combinations. The central players should focus on playing one- or two-touch passes to maintain the rhythm of the attack and exploit spaces in the defensive structure.• Movement off the Ball – Encourage players to move quickly off the ball to create passing angles and give their teammates options. This movement will enable them to receive passes in stride and make decisions faster, increasing the effectiveness of the attack.• Exploiting Space – The bounce players are critical in creating space for the central attackers. Encourage the players to recognize when and where they can move to pull defenders out of position, allowing their team to progress the ball and open up chances for a goal.• Defensive Awareness – Defenders should remain aware of the space behind them and be quick to track runs from the central attackers and bounce players. They must work together to close down space and prevent the attacking team from exploiting open areas.
progression_one: Limit Touches for Bounce PlayersLimit the number of touches the bounce players can take (e.g., 1 or 2 touches). This encourages faster play and challenges the attacking team to think and move more quickly.Focus:Improves tempo and increases the intensity of the game.
progression_two: Add a Defender on the Bounce PlayerIntroduce a defender to pressure one of the bounce players. This adds an element of defensive pressure to the practice, forcing the attacking team to work harder to maintain possession and create space.Focus:Enhances attacking decision-making and ability to play under pressure.

title: Zagreb Breaking Lines Build Up
instructions_setup: This unopposed build-up practice focuses on the relationship between the defensive midfielder (DM) and the forward player. The DM works on movements to receive the ball while the forward focuses on creating space and screening the ball into central areas. The DM's objective is to move out of the shadow of the forward, receiving the ball and progressing it forward into more attacking positions.
coaching_notes: • Movement off the Ball – The DM should focus on making dynamic movements to lose the forward’s shadow and create an angle to receive the ball. Encourage the DM to vary their movement to pull defenders out of position, either checking back or making a run into space to receive the ball.• Screening and Link-Up Play – The forward player’s role is crucial in screening the ball into central areas and creating space for the DM. Encourage the forward to work on shielding the ball, making it easier for the DM to receive a pass and progress the play effectively. Good link-up play between the two is key to breaking the opposition’s lines.• Timing and Awareness – Both players must have good timing to ensure the DM receives the ball in a space where they can progress it forward without pressure. The forward needs to be aware of the position of both the ball and the defenders, ensuring they provide an effective screen at the right time.• Passing Precision – The DM should focus on the precision of the pass when receiving the ball from the forward. The ball must be played with the right weight and angle so the DM can either control and progress or pass it on to the next phase of play.
progression_one: Add Defenders for PressureIntroduce a single passive defender to pressure the DM after they receive the ball. This forces the DM to make quicker decisions and handle defensive pressure in their build-up.Focus:Develops the ability to receive and distribute under pressure, improving decision-making in real match situations.
progression_two: Involve More Players in the Build-UpIntroduce additional players to join the practice and work on creating triangles and passing lanes. This will replicate a more game-like situation where the DM and forward need to involve other teammates for effective build-up play.Focus:Improves team coordination and the ability to play through multiple passing channels.

title: Zagreb One to One Coaching Activity
instructions_setup: This unopposed full back drill focuses on receiving high balls, carrying forward, and making passing decisions in the final third. The full back starts in a wide position and receives a high ball dropped into their zone. After controlling the ball, they drive forward with a few touches before passing into one of two mini goals. One mini goal represents a pass down the line to the winger, and the other simulates a pass inside to a central midfielder.
coaching_notes: • Judge Flight and Position Body Early – Move into position and adjust body shape early to deal cleanly with the high ball.• Use First Touch to Set Forward Drive – Cushion the ball into space to flow into the next action and gain momentum forward.• Lift Head Quickly to Scan Passing Options – Be aware of space and the two target options as you drive forward.• Time and Angle Final Pass with Intent – Deliver a sharp, accurate pass that replicates match tempo and direction to winger or CM.

title: Zagreb Recycle & Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing practice simulates the ball being recycled from the wide areas back into central attacking zones. The sequence begins with a winger passing back to a deeper player, who then plays an inside pass to a player positioned on the edge of the penalty area. That player then finishes from range.Three poles are set on the penalty area line: one near the side, one at the 90-degree angle, and one near the top, forming a triangular reference to guide positioning and passing angles.
coaching_notes: • Accurate Recycle Passing – Emphasize crisp, well-weighted backward and inside passes to maintain attacking momentum.• Body Positioning to Shoot – The finisher should open up their body to strike quickly and cleanly on the first touch or with minimal preparation.• Timing of Runs – The player on the edge of the box must time their arrival to meet the ball under optimal shooting conditions.• Variety in Finishing – Encourage different finishing techniques such as driven shots, curled efforts, or controlled placement to replicate game-like scenarios.
progression_one: One-Touch Finishing OnlyRequire the player on the edge to finish with one touch immediately upon receiving the inside pass, increasing decision-making speed and positional awareness.Focus:Develops sharper spatial awareness, quicker technical execution, and readiness for high-tempo match situations.
progression_two: Passive Defensive PressureIntroduce a passive defender applying light pressure near the edge of the penalty area, forcing quicker control and shooting under pressure.Focus:Enhances composure, improves rapid decision-making, and simulates realistic shooting pressure from defenders.

title: Zagreb Rondo with Transfer Zone
instructions_setup: Set up a rondo grid divided vertically into three zones: top, middle, and bottom. The top and bottom zones have structured possession play with defenders applying pressure. The middle zone acts as a free play transfer zone, where players have more freedom to dribble, pass, or combine to progress the ball through under pressure.Players in the middle zone face significant pressure but are encouraged to use creativity and quick decision-making to either carry the ball forward or find passing options to connect the top and bottom zones. The overall aim is to maintain possession and progress the ball vertically through the three zones with fluid ball circulation and movement.
coaching_notes: • Use of Space in Middle Zone – Encourage players to exploit the freer, more open middle zone by dribbling or quick passing to break lines under pressure.• Body Positioning – Players in all zones should position themselves to receive with an open body to maximize vision and passing options.• Support and Movement – Continuous off-ball movement is key to create passing lanes, especially around the middle zone where pressure is highest.• Decision Making Under Pressure – Players must quickly assess whether to dribble, pass short, or switch play to maintain possession and progress vertically.
progression_one: Limit Touches in the Middle ZoneIntroduce a 2-touch maximum rule in the middle zone to speed up play and encourage sharper passing and quicker decisions under pressure.Focus:Improves technical precision and rapid decision-making when pressured in transitional areas.

title: Zagreb SAQ & 1v1
instructions_setup: The practice begins when the coach calls out two colours. The two players must sprint to the coloured poles corresponding to the coach’s call. Once the players complete the sprint, they will then compete in a 1v1 situation in the central area. The coach does not give preference to either player, so the ball will be passed into the middle, and the player who completes the SAQ part (sprinting to the poles) the quickest will get to the ball first. The players can score into either of the mini goals, adding variety and challenge to the 1v1 situation.
coaching_notes: • Explosive Speed – Focus on the explosive acceleration required when sprinting to the poles. Players should concentrate on pushing off quickly and efficiently to gain the advantage in the 1v1 phase. Encourage quick starts and fast direction changes during the sprint phase.• 1v1 Decision Making – When engaging in the 1v1, players should work on quick decision-making: whether to take on the defender with a dribble, use a skill move, or take an early shot on goal. Encourage players to read the defender's body positioning and attack or shield the ball accordingly.• Finishing Under Pressure – The 1v1 scenario should include pressure situations where players are forced to make quick decisions under pressure. Whether the defender is closing down space or the player is in a tight angle, focus on finishing quickly and efficiently to get a shot off.• Recovery and Resilience – After the 1v1 phase, players must quickly recover and transition to be ready for the next round. Encourage them to maintain their intensity and remain focused after completing each phase of the practice, emphasizing the importance of mental and physical resilience throughout.
progression_one: Add More GoalsIntroduce additional mini goals or cones to encourage more creativity in the 1v1 phase, requiring the attacking player to choose which goal to attack, creating more decision-making opportunities.Focus:Improves decision-making under pressure and encourages attacking players to be more versatile.
progression_two: Add a Defending RestrictionLimit the defender’s actions (e.g., no tackles or only allow them to block or jockey), forcing the attacker to focus on finishing or creating space in other ways, such as taking a shot or passing.Focus:Helps attackers work on finishing under less pressure, allowing them to refine their shooting and placement.

title: Zagreb Switching Play & Fitness Rondos
instructions_setup: Two grids are set up on opposite sides of the pitch. Teams play 4v4 with one neutral player (making it 5v4 in favor of the team in possession). The team in possession aims to complete 5 consecutive passes before switching the ball quickly to the opposite grid. Upon the switch, the defending team must sprint across the pitch to close down and defend the new ball location. If the defending team wins possession and switches play back, the original attacking team immediately transitions to defend and must sprint across to close down.
coaching_notes: • Quick Decision Making – Players must recognize the right moment to switch play quickly to exploit space and unbalance defenders, improving anticipation and awareness.• Transition Speed – Emphasize rapid attacking to defending transition with high-intensity sprinting across the pitch to simulate real-game counter-press scenarios.• Communication – Encourage vocal coordination to organize defensive shifts, alert teammates to switches, and maintain defensive shape effectively.• Positional Awareness – Teach players to maintain compactness in defense and create effective passing triangles when in possession for better ball retention.
progression_one: Limit TouchesRestrict players to a maximum of two touches before passing, increasing pressure to think and act faster during possession and transition.Focus:Improves speed of play, control under pressure, and faster decision-making in tight spaces under real-game conditions.
progression_two: Add a Second Neutral PlayerIncrease to two neutral players supporting the team in possession, encouraging more complex passing patterns and quicker ball circulation.Focus:Enhances passing options, off-the-ball movement, and teamwork under dynamic and physically demanding conditions.

title: Zagreb Technical Passing & Receiving
instructions_setup: In this technical receiving drill, two players begin on opposite sides of a central square. On the coach’s signal, both players move into the square simultaneously to receive a pass from a feeder positioned outside. The focus is on receiving the ball cleanly on the move, taking a positive first touch, and turning away from pressure before passing to a new player on the opposite side.This drill emphasizes scanning, body orientation, and the ability to receive, turn, and play forward with efficiency. It is ideal as a warm-up or technical activation, promoting repeated, high-quality repetitions of receiving under light directional pressure.
coaching_notes: • Body Orientation – Players should arrive with an open body shape, ready to receive on the half-turn and transition quickly into the next pass.• Scanning Before Receiving – Encourage players to scan their surroundings prior to receiving, allowing better decision-making and spatial awareness.• First Touch Direction – The initial touch should take the player into space or towards their next action, rather than stopping the ball dead.• Pass Execution – Focus on clean, accurate passes off both feet with appropriate weight and timing to maintain tempo and rhythm across the grid.
progression_one: Passive Defender Inside SquareAdd a passive defender in the square who applies light pressure, encouraging players to use feints, shielding, or quick turns to evade pressure before passing.Focus:Improves composure on the ball, close control in tight areas, and confidence turning away from light pressure realistically.
progression_two: One-Touch Passing After TurnOnce players turn, challenge them to deliver their return pass with only one touch, demanding quicker processing and sharper body positioning.Focus:Develops sharper footwork, faster technical execution, and a greater awareness of space and timing under tighter constraints.

title: Zurich #6 Technical
instructions_setup: This technical activation focuses on the number 6’s ability to receive the ball under control and quickly link play through effective passing combinations. Players work within a compact grid where the number 6 receives passes from different angles, faces varying directional pressures, and connects with teammates through one- or two-touch combinations. The drill develops first touch, vision, and quick decision-making to simulate the pivotal role of the number 6 in transitioning play from defense to attack.The drill encourages multi-directional receiving, body positioning to open passing lanes, and precise execution of short passing sequences. This structured yet fluid environment helps build the number 6’s confidence and technical sharpness for controlling tempo and maintaining possession in tight spaces.
coaching_notes: • Encourage the number 6 to receive with an open body shape – This allows quick scanning of the field, immediate identification of passing options, and better awareness of opponents’ positions.• Stress crisp, accurate passing combined with quick first touches – This maintains possession rhythm, speeds up team transitions, and reduces the chance of losing the ball under pressure.• Emphasise communication and anticipation of teammates’ movement – This promotes seamless timing, fluid combinations, and helps the number 6 create passing triangles effectively.• Reinforce composure under directional pressure – The number 6 should stay calm, focused, and controlled to make efficient decisions even when closely marked by opponents.
progression_one: Increase tempo and reduce touchesIncrease the pace of the drill and limit the number 6 to a maximum of two touches per possession – This pushes for faster decision-making and cleaner, more precise passing under game-speed conditions.Focus: Enhances speed of play, technical accuracy, and mental sharpness under limited touches.
progression_two: Add passive defensive pressureIntroduce a passive defender applying light pressure on the number 6 as they receive and connect – This encourages sharper ball control, quicker decisions, and better shielding under mild pressure.Focus: Receiving and playing under pressure with improved composure and technique.

title: Zurich 2v1s Into Double 1v1
instructions_setup: This is a high-intensity 2v1 into double 1v1 transition practice. The drill begins with two attackers combining to score against a single defender in the main goal.
