The focus is on decision-making in overloads, movement off the ball, and exploiting space in advanced areas of the pitch.Once the 2v1 phase ends, two defenders positioned behind the main goal immediately sprint forward with a new ball. Each looks to drive and finish into one of the two mini goals, while the original two attackers must transition quickly and defend both 1v1 scenarios, reacting instantly from attack to defence.
coaching_notes: • Emphasise quick, purposeful combinations to take advantage of the 2v1 – Encourage precise timing, sharp movement, angles, and weight of pass to break defensive lines effectively and finish quickly.• Focus on fast mental transition from attacking to defensive mindset – Players must recover urgently, scan the pitch, track runners, and engage opponents without hesitation or delay.• Promote sharp, controlled 1v1 defending under physical fatigue – Defenders should stay compact, time tackles well, show attackers away from goal, and delay forward momentum with intelligent positioning.• Encourage sprint recovery runs with good scanning and communication – Players must identify central and wide threats early, work together vocally, and protect both mini goals using high defensive effort.
progression_one: Introduce time limits in both attacking and recovery phasesImpose a 5-second time limit to score in the 2v1, and 6 seconds for defenders to counter and finish in mini goals. This forces quicker decisions and more explosive transitions.Focus: Develops urgency, mental sharpness, and physical commitment during high-speed transitional moments under time constraints and pressure.
progression_two: Require a combination before defenders can shoot in mini goalsThe two counter-attacking defenders must combine with a pass before shooting. This demands coordination and reduces predictability during the counter phase.Focus: Reinforces teamwork, delayed attacking decisions, and improves timing and support runs when transitioning from defence to attack quickly and effectively.

title: Zurich 3 Team 4v2 Rondos
instructions_setup: This is a competitive 3-team rondo practice using two adjacent 10x10 yard grids placed side by side. Two teams of four players each operate inside their own grid, aiming to retain possession through short, sharp passing sequences. The third team defends by sending two players into each grid, creating a 4v2 scenario in both spaces. Four mini goals are positioned outside the grids—two on each side—to reward successful defensive transitions.If a defender wins possession and scores into one of the mini goals, their team rotates roles with the team that lost the ball in that specific grid. This creates a continuous cycle of attacking, defending, and transitioning under pressure, helping players develop spatial awareness, pressing coordination, and ball retention skills at pace.
coaching_notes: • Encourage pressing defenders to stay compact and communicate to close passing angles – Cohesion and timing are essential to force errors in tight spaces and create scoring chances.• Focus on sharp, one- or two-touch passing from possession teams – Speed of circulation helps break pressing lines and maintain control under pressure with good ball tempo.• Remind players to quickly reset their shape after possession turnovers – Transitioning immediately improves realism and builds reaction-based awareness in game-relevant scenarios.• Promote quick decision-making and confident finishing when defenders win the ball – Players must capitalize on chances to score and switch roles swiftly after turnovers.
progression_one: Limit touches to one or two in possessionRestricting touch count forces possession teams to play with urgency and accuracy while working under pressure from two active defenders.Focus: Enhances tempo, technical speed, composure, and quick ball circulation under constant pressure.
progression_two: Allow defenders to switch between gridsGive defending players freedom to rotate or switch grids mid-round, increasing unpredictability and forcing possession teams to stay alert and adaptive.Focus: Improves scanning, spatial awareness, and adaptability while increasing defensive coordination and tactical alertness.

title: Zurich Dribble to Combination Finish
instructions_setup: This unopposed finishing drill begins with the attacker dribbling through a set of poles, focusing on close control, agility, and quick changes of direction. After completing the dribble, the attacker participates in a quick four-player combination sequence designed to simulate game-like passing patterns and movement around the defensive line. The combination culminates in a precise through ball played between the defenders, allowing the attacker to make a timed run and finish unopposed at goal.The drill emphasizes technical control during dribbling, sharp passing, timing of runs, and clinical finishing under ideal conditions to build confidence and execution in the final third.
coaching_notes: • Focus on tight ball control and quick footwork while dribbling through poles – Precision here builds the technical foundation needed for successful attacking play.• Emphasize crisp, accurate passing and smart movement in the combination sequence – Players must maintain tempo and sharp decision-making to replicate realistic attacking patterns.• Stress the timing and weight of the through ball to perfectly split the defensive line – Well-executed passes create clear scoring opportunities and stretch the defense effectively.• Encourage confident, composed finishing with varied techniques once through on goal – Composure underpins consistent goal-scoring ability in match situations.
progression_one: Add a passive defender tracking the attacker’s runIntroduce light defensive pressure to increase realism and challenge the attacker’s decision-making and composure when finishing.Focus: Develops attacking sharpness and finishing accuracy under mild pressure while maintaining technical quality.
progression_two: Limit touches during combination play to two per playerRestrict touches to increase tempo and force quicker passing and movement, enhancing game-speed decision-making and execution.Focus: Sharpens technical precision and accelerates attacking rhythm to better simulate match intensity and speed.

title: Zurich Multi-Directional 1v1s
instructions_setup: This dynamic drill features two distinct 1v1 phases designed to test players' attacking and defensive skills under varied directional pressures. The first phase involves a horizontal 1v1 contest across the penalty area, with four mini goals positioned two on each side of the penalty box, encouraging quick decision-making and precise finishing into small targets.Immediately following the initial phase, players transition into a vertical 1v1 within the penalty area, aiming to score in the main goal. This shift challenges players to adapt their approach quickly, emphasizing agility, body positioning, and sharp finishing under realistic game conditions.
coaching_notes: • Encourage quick reactions and sharp changes of direction in horizontal 1v1s – Players must use feints and body positioning to create space and beat defenders effectively.• Emphasise accuracy and composure when finishing into small mini goals – Controlled, well-weighted shots improve goal-scoring chances from tight angles and limited space.• Promote fast mental and physical transition between horizontal and vertical phases – Players need to reset their focus and adjust movement patterns to succeed in the second attacking scenario.• Stress the importance of balanced defensive positioning during vertical 1v1s – Defenders should stay low, anticipate attackers’ moves, and delay shots to reduce scoring opportunities.
progression_one: Add a touch limit in both 1v1 phasesRestrict players to a maximum of two touches per possession, forcing quicker decisions, cleaner technique, and enhanced game-like pressure in both attacking and defending moments.Focus: Develops technical precision, speed of execution, and mental sharpness under restricted touch conditions in tight spaces.

title: Zurich React & Finish Into 1v1
instructions_setup: This is a high-intensity reactions and 1v1 drill designed to simulate quick transitions between phases of play. Two players start by sprinting across the grid and playing a ball into a mini goal, testing their reaction speed, awareness, and technical quality. Immediately after this initial phase, they must spin and react quickly as the coach plays a new ball into the grid, sparking a live 1v1 duel.The drill is designed to sharpen players' transitional speed, agility, and mindset—quickly shifting from a technical action into a competitive 1v1 situation that demands both physical and mental sharpness.
coaching_notes: • Highlight the importance of explosive reactions and intensity in the sprint – Quick transitions simulate match demands and raise overall engagement levels early in the drill.• Emphasize clean technique and focus when playing into the mini goal – Accuracy and control should remain consistent even at high speeds and under fatigue.• Promote sharp directional changes when transitioning into the 1v1 – Efficient body movement helps players recover quickly and engage in the duel effectively.• Encourage creativity and confidence on the ball during the 1v1 – Players should use feints, changes of pace, and direct play to create an advantage.
progression_one: Increase distance before turning for 1v1Extend the initial sprint or angle it diagonally to make the recovery and 1v1 more physically demanding, replicating realistic recovery movements.Focus: Improves recovery speed, fitness under pressure, and sharpens 1v1 engagement from varied distances and angles.

title: Zurich Recovery 3v2s
instructions_setup: This 3v2 counter-attacking drill begins with an attacker playing a precise pass down the grid to two teammates positioned ahead near the attacking third. Once the ball is received, the initial passer must drop back quickly to get onside, creating a dynamic 3v2 attacking scenario inside a defined grid. Meanwhile, two defenders start off the grid and must sprint around a pole placed outside the playing area to recover and enter the grid live, simulating realistic recovery runs under intense match pressure.The drill focuses on rapid transitions, timing of runs, and exploiting numerical advantages in attack. Defenders work on quick recovery and positioning to disrupt the counter-attack before it develops fully.
coaching_notes: • Emphasize precise timing of the initial pass and off-the-ball runs – Coordinated movement creates space and maximizes attacking opportunities quickly and effectively under pressure.• Encourage attackers to maintain high tempo and sharp passing under pressure – Fast ball movement is crucial to exploit defensive disorganization during intense counter-attacks.• Stress defenders’ sprint intensity and positioning when making recovery runs – Effective recovery delays or stops attacks, greatly improving defensive resilience and team organization.• Highlight communication between attackers to coordinate overlapping and support runs – Clear verbal and non-verbal cues enhance attacking cohesion, decision-making, and overall team fluidity.
progression_one: Add a third defender joining the recovery runsIncrease defensive pressure by introducing a third defender who also makes a recovery sprint, making the attacking phase more challenging and realistic.Focus: Improves attackers’ decision-making under heavier pressure and promotes sharper offensive tactics with increased complexity.
progression_two: Restrict attackers to two touches maximumLimit touches to increase speed and precision in the counter-attack, encouraging quicker ball control and faster attacking moves under pressure.Focus: Enhances technical sharpness and rapid decision-making during fast transitional play, improving overall attacking efficiency.

title: Zurich Runs In Behind Technical
instructions_setup: This is an unopposed technical activation passing practice designed to focus on timing of runs, movement coordination, and passing accuracy. Players begin by circulating the ball across the grid before playing a well-timed pass between mannequins to simulate breaking the defensive line.The receiving player must time their run to remain onside while still breaking through the defensive shape at speed. After receiving, they finish into a mini goal, simulating a game-like attacking sequence that emphasizes decision-making and movement off the ball.
coaching_notes: • Ensure players scan before passing to recognize best moment to release – This improves visual awareness and prevents rushed or mistimed forward passes.• Focus on correct weight and angle of pass through mannequins – This helps simulate splitting defenders with game-relevant diagonal through balls into key areas.• Encourage receiving players to arc their runs to remain onside – Sharp curved movements help mimic realistic attacking runs behind a defensive back line.• Promote clean, composed finishing into mini goals after timed runs – The end product must reflect control, timing, and purpose under light game pressure.
progression_one: Add a passive defender near the mannequinsIntroduce a passive defender positioned between the mannequins to make timing and execution more game realistic and force precise execution of the pass.Focus: Sharpens timing, awareness of space, and encourages disguise in the final pass release.
